incident_description: There is a potential deadly issue with the plastic grill burner knobs on the Weber Summit Grill .  The burner knobs operate to turn the gas on and off for each burner.  3 of the 6 knobs have cracked on our grill,  so they no longer work to turn the gas on or off for the burner, they simply spin freely without turning the gas flame up or down, on or off.  It becomes a deadly issue if the knob DOES work to turn the gas on, but then the knob cracks after turning it on and will not work to turn the gas off and therefore the gas could accumulate in the grill and create an explosion hurting or killing someone.  This product should be made of some type of metal that will not crack like the current plastic knobs.  Weber offered to send new burner knobs, but that does not solve the issue since the new ones are also made of plastic.  I am very concerned someone is going to get seriously hurt or killed by a gas explosion from failing (cracked) burner knobs.
justification: Gas accumulation due to non-functional knobs poses a high risk of explosion, potentially leading to death.

incident_description:
A company out of [REDACTED] (temporary fencing) that are meant to protect the public from being injured or killed around job-sites, pools, trenches, lakes, waterways, and other hazardous areas. However their design is aimed at reducing costs in lieu of public safety. Currently ASTM F 3342-19 does not define what is considered safe. Instead it ASTM F 3342-19 Section 1.6 states in part:
1.6 - This standard does not purport to address all of the safety concerns, if any, associated with its use. It is the responsibility of the user of this standard to establish appropriate safety, health, and environmental practices and determine the applicability of regulatory limitations prior to use. In other words leaving the definition of a safe fence up to BOCA.
Rental companies and contractors are unknowingly purchasing safety products and installing them in hazardous locations with the presumption that they have been tested to be safe. Master Halco, the largest manufacturer and distributor of fence systems in the USA, has taken it a step further, buy actually advertising that the product is safe. However when I spoke to Master Halco's legal department disclaimed the product as being safe in areas in-which it was not originally intended - hazardous areas. Injuries and deaths have occurred in connection with safety fences that did not meet BOCA. [REDACTED]
justification: Injuries have occurred due to safety fences not meeting BOCA standards in hazardous areas.

incident_description:
On July 17th, we purchased a Ryobi electric mower that came with two 40V battery packs and a charger. We did as told and made sure the batteries were not stored on the charger and kept inside at room temperature and await from moisture or high humidity. After the first use, both batteries would no longer charge. We contacted Ryobi and received two replacement batteries but they didn't ask for the batteries back or suggest there was anything concerning to them going into "sleep mode." Fast forward to October 27th. I happened to walk past our storage room and found it was filled with smoke and smelled horrible. One of the Ryobi batteries had melted a hole in the casing and was spewing smoke/fumes everywhere.  My husband grabbed our woodstove gloves, got the battery out of the house, and called the fire department. 

The fire department came out and checked out the whole house and confirmed the smoke and fumes were from the battery melting a hole. They used equipment to aerate the house so that we could get our pets and ourselves back into the house and advised us to run fans to continue airing out the melted plastic odor. They also recommended that we contact Home Depot and Ryobi, which I did, but Home Depot has yet to return our message and Ryobi passed us off to a safety group who have yet to get in touch.

As both battery packs that came with the mower were defective, the fire department told us to get the batteries into heavy-duty [REDACTED] bags, a box, and wrap that box in a heavy-duty trash bag. They told us where we need to bring them to ensure they're properly recycled and handled from this point on.
justification: Battery meltdown and smoke emission caused potential injury and property damage.

incident_description:
Rubbermaid model 1800001 Slide-Lid Shed. The shed is intended to allow the user to slide the roof backwards into an open position or forward into a closed position. When in the forward/closed position, the user is supposed to be able to close the two front doors to seal the shed. As currently designed, this operation is unsafe and exposes the user to pinch hazards:
The shed roof is inadequately supported, so the peak of the roof sags below the top of the doors. To close the shed, the user must manually lift the peak of the roof while closing the doors, then release the roof onto the doors. It is very difficult to perform this operation without pinching the user's fingers between the roof and door.

The mechanical design of the shed is inadequate. The roof is attached to two flexible walls. There is no horizontal cross-support to prevent the walls from bowing outwards, which causes the roof to sag.

I tried to report this safety issue to Rubbermaid on Sep-10 and again on Sep-26. I have received no response.

Amazon reviews indicate that a large percentage of users have encountered this issue, noting that manual manipulation of the roof height is necessary to close the doors.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B007KL9PBW/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1
justification: The design flaw exposes users to a high likelihood of finger pinching injuries.

incident_description:
I am writing regarding the Toro cordless leaf blower, product number 51820.

I have used it problem free for almost two years until the week of 8/8/2022. When holding down a ÃÂturbo boostÃÂ button the blower has, one IÃÂve used many times before, it began to lightly shock my thumb. I read that humid conditions can lead to static shocks with leaf blowers so I stopped using it and tried later in the week, and it did the same thing any time I used the turbo boost button.  Something was malfunctioning or defective, so I followed the manufacturers guidelines for an item under warranty and took it to a certified service dealership. After 2.5 weeks I got the blower back, was told that there was nothing wrong with the product, that plastic is not capable of conducting electricity so they are certain I could not have been shocked, and that it was likely static due to weather conditions which is outside of their control. I tried the product again when I got home and once again was shocked every time I tested the turbo boost.

I called Toro customer service to discuss the issue, and lack of service provided for a defective product that is capable of causing harm, and after 20 minutes of describing the issue with the product, the means in which it was handled by their service team, and options available, the only other option available was to try a different service dealer. I tried one more authorized service dealership for Toro and was called the following day to be told they do not service electrical motors. I tried leaving a review on the Toro website to explain what has happened with this product, the way it delivers a shock, the difficulties obtaining service with the unit still under warranty, and the lack of options available or care provided by the Toro customer service line, but my post was moderated and deleted. I tried calling Toro again, and the only option once more was to take it to a dealer. 

I decided to report this product, as I believe that it is capable of causing bodily harm by way of a wiring defect that can shock the user, and Toro has shown no care or interest in resolving the matter.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (shock) and the likelihood of it happening again is high as the issue persists despite multiple attempts to resolve it.

incident_description:
Purchased a GOSUN FUSION Hybrid Solar Oven.  The Electrical function of the product is a FIRE HAZARD and unsafe after 3 uses.  The supplied cord does not make intimate contact with the receptical on the tray.  This oven pulls up to 15amp @12v and the plug melts within 3 uses due to the resistance found in the poor connection.  The first cord was replaced by the manufacturer, but they fail to reply to my followup email with my safety concerns:  " hanks for the replacement, what do you mean about cooking? Most everything takes at least an hour to cook with the electric, and sun for that matter.  Is this not engineered to be safely used to cook food to a safe temperature with electric? perhaps a more robust connector like a standard c13 & c14 plugs should have been used.

So if it takes more than an hour to cook most anything with either sun or electric, how is this a useful oven to cook with it's HYBRID function?

If another one melts out, you should source another cable with a higher rated connection and a more solid connection.."

So they replaced the cord and it too melts within 3 uses of only 40min each.  The tray filling and cooking directions are followed and still this happens.  This is a significant fire hazard as it is an oven that would be in use for long period of time unsupervised indoors.
justification: The oven's electrical function poses a high likelihood of fire hazard due to poor cord connection, despite manufacturer's replacement.

incident_description: I purchased an outdoor mist cooling system on 07/15/2022 from Mistcooling.com. The product has 110VAC electricity in the same enclosure as a 250 psi water pump. The manufacturer did not insulate against water spraying on the electrical connections; nor did they provide a circuit breaker or GFI of any type. It turns out that - on my system - the connector that supplies water from the user's garden hose water supply to the 110VAC pump is leaking water under pressure right next to the pump and the solenoid that activates when the pump is turned on. This design will cause a serious injury or perhaps death due to electrical shock when the user steps in the water puddle caused by the leak to turn on or off the pump.
justification: Water leak under pressure near electrical connections poses a high risk of injury due to electrical shock.

incident_description:
I have a John Deere 2025 R Compact Tractor with a front end loader and 4 wheel drive. I was spreading dirt on my property with the 2025 R and this tractor is 11 months old, and garage-kept and not used through the winter months. 

While using my tractor the front wheel came completely off of the tractor with the front end loader full of dirt. The Tractor almost flipped completely over. My body lunged forward with the seat belt on and jerked my low back so hard that my back is injured. I am having constant pain in my lower back. 

The Dealer refused to repair my tractor. Now can you just imagine if I was loading my tractor on to the trailer and the wheel came off. Or going 8 mph cutting grass and a wheel comes off. Please read this very carefully because in the John Deere reviews this has happened before on the same tractor. One review stated the 2025 R was 13 days old and the front wheel came off. John Deere repaired this tractor and 11 days later the same front wheel came off a second time. Please consider this an unsafe design due to their recommendations to retorque every so many days months and hours. No one ever has to retorque bolts on automobiles unless removed. This design is unsafe because the wheel can come off at any given time. The wheel is mounted with bolts into a threaded hole opposite of any normal wheel, such as a car or truck and many other tractors have threaded studs you put the wheel on and then install a nut. 

I am injured and my new tractor is damaged at the cost of $3500.00 and I have 5 year extended warranty Bumper to Bumper coverage that was refused to repair and only 11 months old. This is a $24000.00 tractor with a unsafe wheel application that needs immediate attention before someone
gets killed.
justification: The incident resulted in a back injury and could have been catastrophic if the tractor had flipped completely over.

incident_description: Traeger Tailgater Grill (TFB30LVB) catches fire.  We have had a number of fires in this grill.  The most recent was 16-April-2022.  As instructed in the past the grill was thoroughly cleaned.  08-May-2022 the grill was started up for a test, without food, completely clean.  Within 30 minutes there was a loud "pop" sound, an explosion inside the grill.  The grill was shut down, allowed to cool, and again cleaned.  I restarted the grill, this time with separate temperature sensors.  First: the temperature readings by the built-in Traeger sensor were found to be wildly inaccurate, occasionally over 50 degrees off.  Second: the temperature control was found to be erratic.  Third: even with the grill set for a low temperature (225 degrees) the temperature soared past 500 degrees.  Given these findings the cause of the fires and explosion are now clearly evident.  The electronic controls are malfunctioning and the safety interlocks (if there are any) are not working.
justification: Multiple incidents of fire and explosion, with clear evidence of malfunctioning electronic controls and safety interlocks.

incident_description:
Product used was a Troy-Bilt Wood Chipper model number 24A-414B766.  Impeller is mounted with four flail assemblies.  Flails are secured to impeller through a combination of a spring pin and retaining clip.  One flail came loose during operation of wood chipper and was tossed about inside the unit until the engine was stopped when the flail jammed the impeller from spinning.  Upon inspecting the impeller, discovered retaining clip was missing on all four flail assemblies and three of four spring pins were missing.  Fortunately, no injuries. incident_description:
Item: Coleman Dual-Fuel Camping Stove, Model 424

Background: This is the second Model 424 stove received directly from Coleman as a replacement for the initially purchased stove, ordered from Amazon on May 3, 2021 delivered on May 5, 2021, that was also defective.

Summary of Problem:

During a recent camping trip, October 10-16, 2021, the Coleman stove would produce a ÃÂpuffingÃÂ sound that extinguished the burner flame.  This would normally occur when the flame was set to the low to medium range.  This required constant relighting of the burner.  At one point, on the second day, when relighting burner, the entire stove was engulfed in flames, reaching nearly two feet in height. Since this happened when under my camping canopy, I immediately removed the fuel tank, closed the stove lid and, with pot holders, physically tossed the stove away from my camp site.  It continued burning until the fuel had completed burned out.

Since early in my camping trip, once the stove had cooled, I reinstalled the fuel tank to determine if the stove was still operable. After approximately 10-minutes of operation I noticed that the table it was sitting on was wet with fuel that was leaking from the fuel tank. Obviously, I quickly turned off the burner.  What I found was the indentation on the fuel tank, where the generator assembly is attached to the tank, was filled with fuel and spilling over onto the table. Investigating the generator connections, I found that I could tighten the coupling near the fuel knob an additional ÃÂ½ turn and the coupling from the long generator tube another ÃÂ¼ turn. (Labelled picture available) This action stopped the leak. Regardless of evidently stopping the leak, I decided not to use the stove any further during this trip.

When this stove caught fire, it was under my camping canopy which was adjacent to my tent. This fire could very easily have resulted in an over $600.00 loss of equipment. Of course, this property damage is of little consequence when considering that I may have been severely burned when tossing the stove away from my campsite.

On 10/27/2021 I filed complaint to Coleman Consumer Service via the Coleman website and, through an automated receipt message, was assigned the reference number of [REDACTED]. As of 12/08/2021, 42-days after my initial submission, Coleman has yet to respond.  Therefore, I feel that I have no other choice but to bring this issue to your attention.

Without a doubt, due to either manufacturing or quality control problems, this defect is a safety issue that should be investigated before someone is seriously injured using Coleman Model 424 Dual-Fuel stove.
justification: The stove's design flaw caused a significant fire, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description: About 2 weeks ago I purchased a new Ryobi cordless lawn power head model # RY40009VNM serial # LT21086N120328 from my local Home Depot in bundle model # RY40290VNM . The first day I ran the power head I used several different Ryobi-made and approved attachments including an edger, blower, weed trimmer, and a pole saw. After about 40 minutes of use, the palms of my hands began to sweat a little - not dripping with sweat but slightly damp. I then began feeling sharp and painful shocks in my right hand (trigger hand) when gripping the trigger of the power head at full throttle. The first couple of shocks were so startling I jerked my hand away from the trigger and nearly dropped the entire tool. This power head runs on 40V batteries. With a little experimentation, I discovered I could run the power head without getting shocked if I held the trigger grip with my thumb and trigger finger being careful not to grip the rubber overmold near the recessed steel screws holding it together. Apparently, the shock is passing through these steel screw heads into the palm of my sweaty hand. I do not know why these screws are energized. Perhaps this a manufacturing defect (wire to the trigger assembly pierced by one of the screws) or a design flaw that is causing current to leak from the trigger/grip assembly. I do not know. I called Ryobi support and they promised to forward this report to their product safety department. I was told I would be contacted by safety directly. It has been a week since contacting them, and they have not reached out.

incident_description: My Masterbuilt slow smoker stopped working.  I found that it had tripped the gfci breaker on the outlet feeding it.  When I tested the power cord to the smoker with a multimeter, I found the the live and neutral power terminals were shorted to ground.  I opened the smoker and saw melted wires.  The internal wires to the electrical heating element have high temperature insulation, but the wires on the electrical cord powering the smoker do not.  The insulation had melted and the wires were shorted together and to the housing.  I contacted Masterbuilt customer service twice and only received one response stating the the smoke temperature  emanating from the smoker is less than 105ÃÂ°C.  They did not address the real problem that the power cable is held against the heating element with zip ties, causing the insulation to fail.  Their power cord insulation is the incorrect type for this high temperature application and poses a shock hazard to the user once melted through.  NEC table 400.4 states that thermoset insulation should be used for heater elements which this insulation is definitely not.  It seems to be thermoplastic from the way it melts.  Additionally, the use of this cable violates NEC article 310.15(A)(3) that states that the insulated conductor's temperature rating may not be exceeded.
justification: The melted wires pose a significant shock hazard, increasing the likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
We purchased a Cuisinart Twin Oaks combination pellet/gas grill at the beginning of the summer.  We used the pellet side for a few small smokes. On our first 3+ hour smoke we had our first hopper fire once our food was completed. At the conclusion of cooking, we came inside and began eating.  I noticed a small amount of smoke coming from the hopper but the manual said this was ÃÂnormalÃÂ.  When the smoke began getting thicker I checked on the smoker. Fire had consumed interior of the hopper.  I extinguished the fire and began looking for what I did wrong. After rereading the manual and doing some research I found that this was a common problem with the grill. A [REDACTED] video described a similar situation to what I believe happened in my grill.  I contacted Cuisinart customer service to voice my concerns. After much back and forth, I was told that fires are not covered under the warranty and that my issue could not be reproduced. As the grill could no longer be returned to Walmart, I purchased the necessary replacement parts. I continued to monitor my grill closely and follow the instructions from the manual in addition to the recommendations provided via email.  Since the initial replacement I have had two more hopper fires that I have been able to extinguish before damage to the grill.  After continued emails, cuisinart continues to claim this can not be reproduced.

The main issue comes from the fire pot not emptying when the clean out mechanism is used. If the grill sits for a period of time without use, particularly in a humid climate, the ash hardens and does not drop into the removal tray. When the ash remains, when one would think itÃÂs empty, the ash accumulates until pellets in the auger catch fire.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the common issue with the grill's fire pot not emptying.

incident_description: I have a Ryobi 40 volt blower.  The battery/charger exploded while it was being charged
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not common for batteries to explode during charging.

incident_description: New Troy Bilt mower model TB100 with a Briggs and Stratton 500 series 140cc engine.  Eleven hours of use,  engine oil started spraying out of the  air filter box,  engine and mower deck begin to be covered with oil,  while the engine was burning oil smoke.
justification: Oil spraying from the air filter box indicates a potential engine failure, which could lead to an incident but unlikely to cause injury.

incident_description: Webber BBQ grill was being used to cook food when flame erupted from a burner control knob. The customer immediately shut off the propane tank and then blew out the flames.  The fire resulted in the control knob being melted.  This event could have easily resulted in burns to the fingers or hand.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a flame eruption, posing a potential burn risk.

incident_description: My wife was using the Black & Decker trimmer LST140C and pieces of line were being automatically fed at the wrong time and being cut off and striking her in the legs. It has happened 4 different times and leaves up to 1 inch cuts on her legs. I have complained to Black & Decker twice but they just offer a new product. The last 2 that we have used have done the exact same thing. They want to keep sending me new ones instead of addressing a very serious and dangerous problem with their auto feed system.

incident_description:
The BBQ I own, the fire box that hold the briquettes is metal and has burned through exposing the insulation.  So now the briquettes that are glowing and a fan blowing the heat into the bbq has the chance of insulation going into the cook area.  I've contacted Masterbuilt about this issue with the gravity feed smoker/BBQ and so far just getting the run-around.  So basically the insulation is in the fire box.  I'm not sure how safe this is, but I needed to bring this to  someone's attention as Masterbuilt is just saying this is normal.

justification: While no immediate injury has been reported, the exposed insulation in the fire box poses a potential fire hazard and could lead to property damage or injury if not addressed.

justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is high as evidenced by the ease of finding a video of the same event.

incident_description: Troybily electric leaf blower . Fan came apart in pieces came thru body of blower hitting my wife in the abdomen area and striking a glass pane on a heater/fireplace  in garage shattering front glass.
justification: The fan coming apart and striking the glass pane indicates a malfunction, making this a possible occurrence.

incident_description: Lawnmower got engine fire
justification: While engine fires on lawnmowers are possible, they are not common and typically do not result in injuries.

incident_description: Product caught fire.  Returned for exchange second caught fire first time I used it
justification: The product catching fire twice in a short period indicates a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I was just operating my 80 volt Kobalt mower on some dewey grass which naturally plugged up the inside of the mower deck. I turned it on its left side and used my garden hose to spray out the clumped grass. I was using my hands to help clear out the grass when the blades started turning and immediately hit full RPMs for a couple of seconds then stopped.Fortunately, I pulled my hand out quick enough to not lose my hand or any fingers. I really couldn't believe it and made sure nothing was affecting the power button or safety bar. I stood back and continued to spray the inside the deck and it started up again and again. Perhaps the water from the hose shorted out something that bypassed the start button. When I righted the mower it operated normally. I have not seen this issue elsewhere but am truly amazed this could happen. I will post this elsewhere and hope it will get some attention before someone else is not as lucky as I was.
justification: Injury occurred when blades started unexpectedly while hand was clearing grass.

incident_description: The rear wheel bolts on the wheel  spacers sheared off and the rear wheel began to come off the tractor axle. There were only two of the 6 bolts holding the tire/rim on the tractor. The tractor only has 20 hours on it.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident could have led to a loss of control of the tractor, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description: My Masterbuilt Electric Smoker started on its own for some unknown amount of time while it was covered and powered off.  Once it was noticed overheating, removed cover, unplugged unit, and noted seals melted, plastic warped, electronics non-functioning, decorative cover scorched.  Unplugged unit to turn off.  After letting unit cool down, plugged back in, observed unit again in runaway temp mode, display and controls were non functioning.  Attempted to reach Masterbuilt customer service and filled out on-line report including pictures.  They appear not interested in investigating their product and attempting to understand if this a serious issue.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' at severity level 2.

incident_description: We purchased a SunJoe mower from Amazon.  We charged it and used it once.  Then we charged it again over night.  The next morning I left for work but my wife was home with our toddler.  She smelled ozone and went into the garage.  About that time the fire alarm went off and she saw the mower smoking by the gas tank of our SUV.  She pushed it outside and went to get the fire extinguisher and it exploded, hitting her in the ankle with debris.  She sprayed it down but the battery is inside and it exploded a second time, fortunately in the driveway.  She then had to get the hose and hose it down.

incident_description: We have a RainBird ESP-M sprinkler controller that exploded and caught fire on our garage wall. The door and front panel were found over 20 feet away from the unit attached to the wall. The fire extinguished itself, and did not cause additional damage to the garage structure. incident_description: Brand new Weber Barbecue caught fire during first use.

incident_description:
Masrerbuilt Model CM7P smoker.

incident_description: I was cutting grass on my 60" Ariens zero turn mower for about one hour without incident and stopped to take a break. incident_description:

incident_description: In July I decided to use our new Feit headlamps that we had purchased from Costco (https://www.costco.com/feit-rechargeable-led-headlamp%2C-2-pack.product.100526075.html). incident_description:
I bought a Weber Spirit 320 gas grill around 2009. Almost immediately a green mold showed up on the stainless cooking grill and the flavor bars. It took Weber almost a year to replace them. THe mold immediately returned on the replacement parts.

Meanwhile the aluminum box warped out of shape, and the stainless steel inside the lid started crumbling to scale, often falling on the food being cooked.

The grease catcher tray on the bottom rusted off, so now it falls down into the grill base.

The bottom has rusted through, and the legs are rusted and failing.

We just rebuilt our deck, and are afraid to use this product on our new $25,000 deck.

I have a 30 and 40 year old Weber when they were still made in USA that are both in better and safer condition than this piece of junk.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant damage to the grill and potential property damage to the new deck, making it an incident with no injury but notable impact.

incident_description: I purchased and had installed by an electrician, a Utilitech motion activated security light model number 6222B-PIR24.   The item was installed on January 9th, 2019.  Sometime between July 23rd 2021 and July 25th 2021,  the  motion lights stayed on continuously until the product caught fire and melted, destroying the fixture and blackening five sheets of aluminum siding.  An electrician verified today August 3rd, 2021, that the wiring is properly installed, the product is defective.
justification: The product's defect led to continuous operation and eventual fire, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: While edging sidewalk with a MTD Trimmer Plus 720E edger the plastic debris shield separated from the cutting head leaving blade exposed.  Product used for only the third time.  No injuries incurred.

incident_description: Was mowing the grass, got off of mower to put air in a truck tire and mower motor caught fire melting the motor and hood before it was put out.
justification: Although there was an incident (motor catching fire), there were no injuries reported.

justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the potential for harm is high due to the unexpected wheel detachment.

incident_description: I preheated my new Weber Go- Anywhere grill for 5 minutes, when I lifted the lid to place my food I noticed the handle was overly warm. Cooked for 3 minutes and lifted the lid again to flip my food. The lid was what I would call hot. Cooked for an addition 2 minutes and dropped the lid due to the pain in my hand.

COULD NOT PUT IT OUT WITH DIRT AND HAD TO CALL THE FIRE DEPARTMENT TO PUT IT OUT. IT WAS A TOTAL LOSS. APPEARED TO FROM A FUEL LINE.

A week after setup, we were filling mulch behind the edging and the edging kept tipping over due to a poor design on the stake peaks(tips of the points that were supposed to secure product into the ground). On June 2 my oldest son tripped over the edging, the edging became dislodged due to it's poor design, product flipped around and impalled him in the shin. Fortunately, only bandages were needed as opposed to stitches. I reached out to Suncast right away to report and ask for refund since I couldn't find receipt. They responded and denied product being unsafe and a refund--I didn't have my receipt. I included both pictures/proof of ownership to them but no receipt. I retain their emails to me

On 7/4/21, I read the instructions which stated to use care and the gloves they provided, as there were sharp edges, and began to assemble the shed.  I did as the instructions recommended.  I noticed that there were razor-sharp edges on all parts.  I was very careful, but wondered why any product would be sold with parts like this.  I picked up a side panel, carefully, and although wearing gloves, my hand was sliced open by the flat inside of the panel.  A metal v-shaped part had popped up against the flat side, and cut the palm of my hand open.  My hand began to bleed profusely, even through several large towels.  My sister  took me to the emergency room, where they diagnosed a deep tissue wound.

incident_description: Fan blade broke apart in several pieces exiting the blower end of the unit
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but could have caused property damage, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

I was afraid gas tank might fall onto the hot motor and explode.  He called the company also, they would not send him the replacement parts.

incident_description: I just purchased a Husqavarna Z254f. This is a large zero turn mover and I expected to be able to add the rollover protection. They offer many models and it seems all their other models have this option. The part number for the kit is 539115163. I am now told the part is discontinued and is not going to be replaced. incident_description:
The 'trailing shield' on my mower fell off and was chopped to bits on my mower... only 4 months after the 2 year warranty expired. The guard exists to prevent rocks, etc. from coming out from under the mower and hitting the operator. In several decades of using mowers this has never happened to me before.

incident_description: The grill was purchased the day after Christmas. We waited to assemble it until the summer, when it would be needed. After several uses, we noticed this problem. It has had very little use for it to catch fire like this. When using grill, it catches fire violently.  The entire bottom of the whole grill was on fire. incident_description: One of two motion-activated solar powered security lights caught fire.  The units were mounted on the rain gutter on the side of our home.  The fire caused the battery door to melt and the battery fell out burning the grass.   This occurred at approximately 3:15 PM.  My wife saw the smoke and alerted me. incident_description:
We recently had a fire that I believe may have been caused by an out of place burner deflector on this grill. The grill was estimated to be 1 month old prior to the fire and had only been used 1-3 times prior to this fire. During my investigation, I did not find any other ignition sources that may have contributed to the fire.

We were called to a grill on fire on a deck that was connected to a single-family home. My engine company was the first to arrive. I found fire blowing from the relief valve of the propane tank connected to this grill. The fire from the relief valve was impinging on the the deck railing and communication lines running from the backyard power pole to the house. We extinguished the fire using a dry chemical fire extinguisher and cooled the railing and communication lines using a garden hose from the house. 

The homeowner stated the grill was approximately 1 month old and that they had used it 1-3 times, with no issues, prior to this fire. The person who started the grill stated it was heating up for only a couple of minutes when he returned outside and saw the fire near the propane tank. 

During my investigation, I found no other nearby ignition sources. There was a plastic handle grill scraper that was melted and laying on the floor of the deck, to the left of the propane tank. The scraper was directly below the hooks on the grill shelf that are intended to be used to hang accessories. The only other items to be damaged during this fire were the deck railing, communication lines, and the scorch marks on the left side of the grill and underside of the shelf. This area of the grill is where the propane tank was installed. 

I examined the grill and found it to be relatively clean with a minimal amount of burn food debris and grease on the inside bottom of the grill. I found the left burner heat deflector to be out of place. The deflector was still above the burner but was positioned slightly right of the burner and was rotated slightly in a clockwise position. This position would have deflected some of the heat from the burner towards the left side of the grill and towards a manufactured hole on the left side of the grill that was only a few inches away from the propane tank valve and the pressure relief valve on the tank. 

When I asked the person who started the grill about the position of the burner deflector, he was unsure what position the deflector was in prior to starting the grill. I asked the fire personnel who assisted in the extinguishment and overhaul of the scene if they moved the deflector or if they thought their extinguishment efforts may have moved the deflector. They believed their efforts had very low impact, if any, on the integrity of the grill or the items within it, and do not think the deflector was moved as a result. 

While I cannot state with absolute certainty that the position of the burner heat deflector caused this fire, I did not find any other ignition sources that could have caused this fire. I do believe it is possible that the heat deflector position along with the location of the manufactured hole in the grill side, and the location of the propane tank (fuel source), could have combined to cause this fire. I believe more testing of this product is necessary to ensure this issue does not happen again.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the fire posed a significant risk due to its proximity to communication lines and a power pole, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
On Saturday night, May 22, 2021 the Fairfield Fire Department responded to a reported propane grill explosion at [REDACTED]. 

According to the homeowner [REDACTED] who is also the owner of the grill and the individual who reported the incident, he had just finished cooking his burgers and went inside to dine with his family.  He heard a loud ÃÂwooshÃÂ and saw flames in the back yard.  He evacuated his family from the house to the neighbors across the street.  When he was safely across the street he looked back and observed the size of the fire increase exponentially.  ÃÂAll of a sudden it got really big.ÃÂ
  
[REDACTED] recalled that he shut off the burners by closing the burner control valves but did not close the tank valve because the tank was located inside the grill cabinet and that it was too hot to turn it off.  He usually waited for the grill to cool down before closing the tank valve. 

Fairfield Fire Engine 1 arrived on scene and reported heavy fire in the back of the house visible from the street front.  Size up revealed a large gas grill had exploded in the rear yard, the relief valve from the 20 lb. propane cylinder supplying the grill had functioned, and a liquid propane fueled fire was burning from the tank which had fallen on itÃÂs side.  Exposures included the fence, a large bush, the garage, patio furniture, and the house. 

Engine 1 crew stretched an 1 ÃÂ¾ hose line to knock down the fire, cool exposures, and redirect the venting propane from the dwelling.  After the tank was cooled firefighters righted the tank, standing it upright on itÃÂs base.  As the tank was cooled and the internal pressure dropped the relief valve reset and the leak stopped.  The tank valve was closed and the tank stabilized.  

The tank was examined and determined sound and safe for travel.  It was transported to the Fairfield Fire Training Center for safekeeping.  Initial investigation revealed that this grill was recalled by the manufacture in 2008 and 2009 for a design defect that resulted in fires similar to the one we experienced Saturday night. 

The grill was secured by the Fairfield Fire Department and transported to the Fire Training Center for safekeeping.  A fire and explosion investigation was performed, evidence collected was photographed, documented, and is currently being stored at the Fire Training Center.

Asst. Chief [REDACTED] DFM was the incident commander and also the investigating officer for this explosion.  Chief [REDACTED] is a certified fire marshal and fire investigator and has completed the FBI post blast investigation program.
justification: No injuries reported, but a significant fire occurred due to a recalled grill's design defect.

incident_description: I [REDACTED] planned to cook a chicken on my Jenn-Air grill (model 720-0063-lp, 2004) using the rotisserie capability. After putting the chicken on the grill rotisserie unit, I turned it on and put a pan underneath to catch the drippings.  I then turned on the rotisserie heating element at the back of the unit, and turned on the rotisserie motor to ensure it rotated correctly with the heat turned on.  After watching it for a few minutes, I closed the cover.  In about 10 minutes, I glanced over to see the grill and saw that it had caught on fire at the area where the plastic button is to ignite the rotisserie. The fire also burned the gas hose that goes to the lp tank, as well as the wire that goes from the rotisserie igniter button to the rotisserie heating element.  I feel very lucky that I saw the fire before it burned completely through the hose to the lp tank.  It might have caused an explosion or significantly larger fire.  I have pictures of the grill after the fire and fragments of the burned pieces.  I sustained some minor burns to my fingers trying to stop the fire before it spread, but just put them in water for awhile.

incident_description:
Caller reported that the Lawn roller detached and fortunately was stopped by a tree in his yard.  The attachment broke causing the incident.  Caller feels that this is a faulty design.  The company was contacted and the rep advised that if a sharp turn is taken the incident will occur.

Caller contacted the retailer and he was provided with replacement clips which have a better design.

Caller feels that this product is unsafe and should be reported before consumers are seriously harmed.
 
I purchased a 50 gallon lawn roller and put it together as per instructions.  I used the roller for aproximately 30 to 40 minutes when the drum became detached from the towing frame and rolled out of control thru my yard striking a tree which stopped it. When inspecting what happened, I found that the "D" clips that hold the drum to the towing frame had broken causing the drum to detach from the frame. This drum, when full of water, weighs about 400 pounds. Had it not hit the tree it would have ended up in my neighbors yard possibly causing damage or hurting someone.
I called Home Depot where I purchased it and the Outdoor manager told me he would give better replacement clips or a refund whatever I prefer. I got the new clips and compared them to the damaged original clips and found the new clips where made of a hardened material not cheap soft metal that comes with the roller. I used the roller for about an hour after using the new clips and had no further problems.

I called the company who makes the roller and explained what happened and the representative  I spoke with defended the product saying they have never had any problems before and she told me that if you take too sharp of a turn with the roller this kind of incident may happen. When I asked where in the instructions it says that, she could not tell me because it is not there. I said if you know of this, why don't you put it in the instructions, And again she defended the product.	This attitude is what prompted me to contact the CPSC. This roller will eventually hurt someone if this problem is not addressed.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage or harm to others, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
I was using my MacKissic Mighty Mac LSC chipper shredder to reduce my pruning of a forcithia bush on my property. As I was shredding the trimmings, the Mighty Mac began to vibrate quite vigorously, the engine cut off, and the flywheel continued to spin for about a minute when it ran out of energy.

Looking to see why the machine stopped running, I was shocked to see a softball sized hole on the side of the engine on the side opposite to where I was standing. Please see the attached images.

Had I been standing on the opposite side of the Mighty Mac, I would have had serious injury to my legs from the shrapnel of the engine at a minimum.

I have used a variety of yard equipment for the last 20 years maintaining several properties with both new and used machines. I have never seen such a catastrophic failure of an engine. Looking at the metal where the hole was blown in the engine, the grain pattern suggests metal fatigue as the reason for failure. I have a [REDACTED] chainsaw from the late 1980s, that still starts quickly and reliably cuts wood.

Working as a biomedical engineer at a local hospital supporting a variety of medical equipment, I find it unconscionable to sell a piece of equipment that could fail in such a hazardous state. Especially since this is a wood chipper that chips up to 2.5ÃÂ limbs, one would expect a higher level of engineering to prevent such a failures knowing the forces involved.

I am thoroughly disappointed that I have purchased one of these Mighty Macs knowing that reliability, safety, and robustness of design was not part of the design process for this piece of equipment. At this point, I am just thankful that I was not injured by this catastrophe engine failure.
justification: The engine's catastrophic failure and expulsion of shrapnel could have caused serious leg injuries if the user was standing on the opposite side.

There were a couple of times that the button to turn on the flashlight accidentally got bumped and turned the flash light on when it was in my pocket.  I quickly noticed the warmth coming from the flash light.  It was a burning sensation to the skin, through the clothing, but did not cause a burn that needed to seek medical attention.  Yesterday when I had the flashlight in my back pocket on my jeans, once again the flashlight got turned on.  As I was sitting in the chair I started to smell something burning.  I quickly reached for the flashlight and it was extremely hot and I could smell something was burnt.  I looked the flashlight over and it appeared to be fine.  I mentioned it to my husband.  When I got home later in the evening my husband noticed a burn spot on the t-shirt I was wearing exactly above the pocket I had the flashlight in.  The flashlight burned a hole in my tshirt.  I have reached out to the manufacturer and received a fairly generic response of sorry you are not happy with the product. incident_description: Operating a Kubota farm tractor and was mowing a flat grass pasture with a Land Pride, Model RCR1260, 12 Series, 60 inch rotary cutter when the tail wheel assembly that holds the wheel broke off.  It broke at a portion of the assembly where welding could previously be seen.  I notified the dealer, [REDACTED] in [REDACTED], MS where the cutter was purchased on 05/02/2019.  The owner of the dealership made mention that these cutters are known to have bad welds and that he did not like Land Pride products but that is what they are stuck with since they are affiliated with Kubota now.  I had insurance with Kubota Finance but the deductible was $250 so I will be buying a replacement part for $140.  This is a potentially hazardous issue in that the tail wheel assembly can break, cause the wheel to come off, and cause the rotary cutter to be dropped and scalp the ground below.  This, in turn, could possibly cause potential hazards were the blade to be flung out from underneath the rotary cutter.  The operator of the tractor may not know the wheel has come off until they make their turn and notice scalped grass where they had just been cutting.  I had observed the portion that broke prior to it breaking.  It always had a welding that looked unprofessional, almost bubbly.  Paint seemed to deteriorate at that weld location faster than it did anywhere else on the cutter. It just never looked like a "finished product" from the factory.  And I stored it under a covered barn, out of the elements.  I still have the broken assembly if CPSC would like to collect it in their investigation.  I also have digital photographs.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage and potential safety hazards, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
kobalt 80v kmp6080-06 Mower.  The  self propelled on-off paddle switch  does not return home.   The mower self propelled mechanism is turned on by pushing the paddle down.  The mower then moves forward under power from the rear wheels.  The paddle is released to stop forward motion.....but the paddle does not return home as it should and mower continues moving forward.  The mower will continue to move forward unless the operator reaches behind the paddle and pushes it home, or physically restrains the mower.   Since the Operator  will be surprised the mower doesnt stop upon paddle release, they will likely continue  to grip the handle to hold the mower  back.  This action prevents the blade stop from deenergizing the motor and stopping the blade motion, thereby potentially endangering anyone close to, and in the path of, the mower in forward motion.
A broken return spring is likely responsible for the paddle not returning to home.
Kobalt Customer Service had no repair parts or guidance for troubleshooting and repair available.   Owner was told to return the mower for a replacement or refund at LOWES
justification: The mower's failure to stop upon paddle release could lead to injuries, as the operator may struggle to control it and the blades remain energized.

incident_description: Pellet smoker grill caught fire. I've been in discussions with the smoker grill company about the failure of design and manufacturing of the product which has been completely manufactured in China and shipped perhaps without any oversight from them and only becoming aware of a possible problem after a great deal of failures/fires. They have only admitted that the replacement parts that failed are on back order and that they underestimated the amount of these parts that will need to be replaced. As a retired engineer and the lack of the product manufacturer to service the product I and many others have had to perform service on these products. I found the cause of the failure/fire to be the fan/auger motor assembly. The assembly motors that are found to be in these grills are not the assemblies that are outlined in their own wiring diagram. The failed units are with only one wiring terminal to operate the pellet auger feed system and none for the cooling fan on the assembly which possibly leaves the cooling fan inoperable or insufficient which leads to overheating and failure/fire of the product. They refuse to discuss my findings  or even listen to the fact that the motor they keep saying is in it in fact is not the motor in the product. I've even sent pictures showing this to be true. They have only expressed that they need a  great deal of replacement motor assemblies but thats where the discussion ends.  My findings and their refusal to talk about this is in my professional opinion is a clear attempt to stonewall for liability and or safety recall reasons.  In my professional career I worked directly with liability concerns as an engineer and their reactions and denials to answer my questions reflect nothing more than a coverup of perhaps thousands of defective/dangerous units.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of similar incidents is high due to widespread use of the defective product and manufacturer's refusal to address the issue.

I then tried to start  the engine and  I could not pull the starter handle/cord because it seemed like it was seized. I also heard a lot of gurgling but thought nothing of it. The next day I thought I'd try again and rechecked the oil and to my surprise gas came out the oil fill hole. So now I guess the gurgling was the gas somehow leaking into the oil.

I found this site where I see Kohler has had a recall on these engines. This engine was built on Mar 8, 2018 and just missed the recall, however I feel this engine should be covered as well, as obviously something is terribly wrong. 

The Specification is: SH265 - 3011
Serial#: 4906714408

Thank you for your help with this problem engine.

[REDACTED]

incident_description:
Earlier this year a bought a Columbia riding lawn mower,model #13BPA1KS897. This riding mower has the gasoline fill tube directly over the left side foot rest. On 2 occasions gasoline has spilled out of the gas tank onto my foot to the extent that it soaked my shoe and sock as well as my pant leg.
The first time it happened I thought that I had not secured the cap so I read the instructions and re secured the cap with three clicks. It continued to leak, I reread the instructions and learned that it was overfilled with the gasoline in the fill tube so I lowered the level of gasoline and continued using the mower. The second incident which occurred yesterday happened after I filled the tank with the level below the fill tube. I thought I had secured the cap as it clicked. Apparently it was not secure and it leaked over my shoe and the foot rest  as I was using the mower. 
The location and design of the gasoline tank and the fill tube is inherently dangerous, a potential lethal outcome could have occurred had the gasoline ignited. When one secures a gasoline cap it is expected the fill tube will not leak outside the tank especially with a vehicle that rides rough causing gasoline to slosh around its tank.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the repeated gasoline leaks pose a significant risk of injury or fire, making it an incident with high likelihood.

incident_description:
I sustained a significant injury, losing two toes, while operating the "Hyper Tough 20" Side Discharge Push Mower with Briggs and Stratton Engine."  Due to the defective design or defective parts of this mower, my foot is permanently disfigured.  

I purchased the mower roughly one year ago, and had used the mower several times over the course of the past year without any issues.  The incident occurred when I was operating the mower on July 11, 2020.  I was using the mower in the typical fashion to mow my small, flat yard.  As I was pushing the mower through a clump of grass or weeds, the mower's handle suddenly collapsed away from me.  As the mower folded forward, I was propelled forward onto my right foot, which became caught under the mower and mangled by the blades.  The blades chopped off half of my big toe, and the entirety of my second toe.  I fortunately had the mental and physical capacity to make it in to my house and call 911, as I was home alone at the time of the accident.  

Because the paramedics were unable to locate my toes when they arrived, the surgeon was unable to reattach them.  While the sutures on my foot are nearly healed, I can no longer walk without a strong limp.  The injury has interfered with my ability to perform my job and my ability to carry out basic everyday functions including driving, dressing, running, and bathing.  I also suffered a tremendous amount of trauma and emotional suffering as a result of the accident.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (loss of two toes) and significant long-term impact, and the likelihood of such a defect causing an accident is high given the mower's history and the specific circumstances.

incident_description:
On or about June 5, 2020 I purchased a Cuisinart 3-1 5-burner grill from Walmart in Delavan, WI. The unit had been fully assembled by Walmart. The advertised price was $347 plus tax which I paid in cash. A Walmart employee named  -------helped load the unit into my vehicle.

I spent the next several days trying to absorb all the warnings and instructions contained in the Cuisinart Grill Operator booklet. I also stapled the purchase receipt into that booklet.

On June 9, 2020 I returned a propane tank to the Clinton, WI grocery store because it was malfunctioning in that it was not producing any gas. The store owner/mgr [REDACTED] provided me with a replacement tank. Both tanks were furnished by the [REDACTED]. Because it was starting to rain from the hurricane Cristobal which was just entering our area, I had the grill about 2-3ft. in the garage. I set the tank on the tray underneath the grill and connected it to the grill regulator. A soap test on the newly connected tank did not indicate any leak.

The new tank produced gas and all 5 burners on my grill ignited immediately.
The side burner, however, would not ignite. Per the instruction booklet, I proceeded to let the grill burn for 10ÃÂ15 minutes. There was no obvious sign of any problem. I periodically checked the temperature of the grill on the closed lid thermometer and it eventually reached 500 degree+/-. At about
12 minutes, I decided to shut it down by turning off the tank valve first...
per the instructions. When I bent down, I saw yellow flames quietly burning in the area of the tank connection to the grill hose. I attempted to turn off the tank valve but it was burning hot.

I ran to the house to get oven mitts but by the time I returned, there was now a roaring jet of orange flame under the grill. I tried repeatedly to turn off the valve which required about 15-20 rotation attempts.  But when I succeeded, a new jet of flame blew out of the valve and the grill was fully involved in flames. I then managed to pull the grill out into the driveway and again ran to the house to call the [REDACTED] Fire Dept. By this time there was a loud siren sound coming from the tank which my wife heard from inside the house. She thought it was a tornado warning. I told her not to worry ÃÂ it was just a propane tank fixing to explode.
It was now pouring rain. The fire dept. arrived and decided to spray water on the grill while they let the tank burn out from a distance. The chief in charge was [REDACTED NAME] who took my information for his report. As he talked to me in the garage, he asked if I was hurt because he could smell burnt human hair. I then realized I had burned my right arm and there was some pain.

I went to the Walmart store in Delavan on 6/10/2020 and after some difficulty, conveyed this information at 9:55 a.m. to ÃÂ[REDACTED]ÃÂ who said he was the assistant mgr. The booklet including my cash receipt had been sitting on the grill and most of it was consumed in the fire. I showed him my small bag of charred remains and he stated he could look up the purchase in their system. I gave him my contact information and said he might want to contact Cuisinart but he said we should wait for the fire report. He identified [REDACTED] as the actual store manager but said he wasnÃÂt there.

I now have the fire report.
justification: Injury occurred due to flames from a propane leak, and the incident was likely due to improper shutdown procedure and a malfunctioning propane tank.

incident_description: Re: Troybilt Pony 42" riding lawn mower purchased from Home Depot.  Mower is equipped with only a single clutch-brake pedal (not two separate drive/gas and brake pedals).  When mower is in motion it remains in motion until the clutch-brake pedal is depressed - similar to cruise control on an automobile. If the clutch-brake pedal become obstructed, is caught on an object, or if for any other reason the operator cannot depress the clutch-brake pedal, the machine will remain in motion with blades engaged.  This situation occurred on 7/21/20 when the clutch-brake became entangled in a child's swing, which prevented the clutch-brake pedal from being engaged to stop the machine.  As a result, the machine continued in forward motion while entangled in the swing chain, raising the front end of the mower off the ground, spinning the mower 90 degrees left and crashing the mower into the swing set frame and finally a tree which was sufficient to stop the mower until it could be turned off.  If the mower had the 'normal' configuration of two separate drive and brake pedals, the operator could have simply removed their foot from the drive pedal and the machine would have stopped without the need to engage the brake. In the dual pedal configuration, the operator must actively and continuously engage the drive pedal for the machine to move.  Without such engagement, the machine automatically comes to a stop. In the case of the Troybuilt Pony 42" the opposite is the case - the machine will by default move forward (or reverse) at the 'cruise' speed setting until the clutch-brake is engaged. Of secondary concern, there have been several prior instances where the clutch-brake engages rapidly, particularly at higher speed settings, causing the mower to lurch forward.  In other cases, the clutch-brake does not engage. In my opinion as an engineer and safety professional in the construction industry for more than 30 years, this is a potentially dangerous product.
justification: The mower's single clutch-brake pedal design increases the likelihood of incidents, as demonstrated by the swing entanglement event.

incident_description:
This documents serves to capture an incident that occurred on Saturday, April 4th in 2020 with a Propane smoker from Masterbuilt.  The product I was using was the MPS 230S Propane Smoker.
On the evening of April 4th, at approximately 6:30 PM MT, the brisket and pork butt I was smoking  was taken off the smoker and into the house to rest the meat.
When I came back outside to close the smoker down, I re-opened the area of the smoker body where the meats are cooked.  Just as I was moving to close the door to to shut off the gas to extinguish the flame, the "Water Tray", which was filled with drippings from the meat that was just cooked, apparently sloshed slightly.  This cause some drippings to fall down onto the flame directly below, which was covered only with the Wood tray, which also is made to burn wood during the process.  This ignited and send a larger flame and caught the entire "Water Tray" on fire, which erupted into a very large flame and enveloped my entire face.  
I threw myself back away from the flame swatting to put it out and try to keep it from my face.  The grill, which was positioned 9 feet behind me and was not on at the time, broke my fall.  My wife, [REDACTED], was in the kitchen at the time and saw the eruption of flame and immediately came outside to see what was happening.
The entire smoker was instantly on fire.  My reaction next is probably what saved the entire situation from getting completely out of hand.  I moved toward the tank and shut the valve to stop the flow of propane gas.  I, then, removed the line and took the tank away from the smoker while the smoker was still fully engulfed.
My wife helped me get the entire flame out from the smoker after we took both the wood tray and grease pan out of the smoker completely.  We put a large pan lid from our kitchen on both trays in order to extinguish the flames, as we knew grease fires cannot be put out with water.  So, I know we did the absolute right things to get the situation under control.
Next, because she is a medical professional, she took me upstairs to look at the burns closely.  In her professional opinion, and because of the Covid-19 illness that was rampant during this time, she put some burn gel (aloe) over the areas that appeared affected, specifically the nose, cheeks and lips.  She applied it very liberally to help slow the burn process.  Since it was so late on a Saturday night, she thought it would be best to avoid the visit to the ER(again, because of Covid), unless symptoms got significantly worse.  So, we agreed we would monitor the burns carefully.  All went well, and when Monday morning approached,  I called my doctor as soon as the office opened and got an appointment for that afternoon.
My doctor agreed it was a really good call to not visit the ER and that everything [REDACTED] did worked wonders and prevented further damage to my face.
My doctor, then, prescribed some better face cream(Silver Sulfadiazine) with antibiotic and soothing properties to intensify the healing process.  
In the week I have been taking the cream it has improved the appearance significantly.  I am still in some pain from it, but it has come a long way, so far, and I hope the healing continues for it.
While my physical appearance has healed, there are lingering feelings on my nose and lips that I was told may take more than a year to fully heal, so time will tell on those.
My analysis of the product is that it is seriously flawed in 2 critical areas.  
First, the "Water Tray" is not deep enough to hold enough of the drippings that fall into it during the cooking process.    
Second, there is nothing to prevent or divert any drippings from the tray from reaching the flame below and causing it to ignite into such a monstrous fireball.
My situation is one that is only able to be shared because of how I reacted at the moment the flame erupted.  And, because I have more than 20 years of smoking experience, I was more prepared than most people would have been in this situation.  My exposure to the flame would have been significantly different with a much more catastrophic end result had I not reacted as fast as I did.
I truly don't want another person to have to endure the trauma this incident has caused me.  
And, again, my nose and lips will continue to heal, I hope, so I will eventually be fine from this incident.  
I am still very outraged at this incident and wish to have it resolved as soon as possible.  The company, Masterbuilt, has not offered an acceptable agreement on it, and they seem to be more concerned about my signing a form agreeing not to sue them.  They offered to replace it with a similar product to the cost of what I paid, excluding tax.  But, the features on the product they offered are the same, so I fear it could potentially happen again.
I have, since, purchased a new propane smoker from a different company, which is much safer and has a much larger "Water Tray" and has shields the trays below to deflect anything that may potentially fall toward the direction of the flame.    
I have disposed of the old smoker, so it is no longer in my possession.  The old one was unusable because of the amount of damage it suffered in the fire to the inside walls.
I would like this product investigated for the safety benefit, and I wish to have them pay me a reasonable amount for the suffering I've endured from using the product and trying to reason with them with no success.
justification: Injury occurred due to flames engulfing the user's face, with potential for more severe outcomes if not for the user's quick reaction.

While the rest of the grill is consumer assembled, I had conducted a leak test on the initial use with no problems found. The grill was purchased 2/29/20 and assembled on 3/1/20. Between that date and final use on 6/7/20, the grill was used maybe 10 or 12 times. It was garage kept and cleaned including the grease tray when not in use.

The grill was a DynoGlo model DGP483CRP serial number 194BFA1189.

I have contacted the parent company of DynoGlo with no response yet. Contact was made on 6/21/20 via their online web form.

I put the fire out with a fire extinguisher kept in my garage. Unfortunately after putting out the fire, leaking gas could clearly be heard and smelt. While attempting to shut off the propane tank, I burned my right thumb and two fingers as the tank was still very hot. I finally shut off the gas by using an oven mitt.

While I was able to return the grill to the store I purchased it at, I have pictures of everything.
justification: Injury occurred due to gas leak from a factory-assembled part, despite initial leak test.

incident_description:
On May 23, 2020, I purchased Arnold Multi-Tool
Item #526356 Model #490-240-0009 , a plastic stop valve for use on a riding mower from the Lowe's Home
Improvement store in Bee Cave, Texas. This product's manufacturer is Arnold Products, apparently a division or
subsidiary of MTD Products (mtdproducts.com).
Today (June 4, 2020), I installed the valve for it's intended an advertised use, on a 1/4-inch ID gas line between the
gas tank and the carburetor of my riding lawnmower. After mowing the lawn and parking the lawnmower, I noticed
a growing pool of gasoline below the valve on my garage floor, and discovered that the "guts" were missing,
leaving just the black housing, and allowing gasoline to flow unimpeded out of the line. Approximately three
gallons from the full tank was discharged, onto my lawn, and onto my garage floor and onto the area of the hot
engine exhaust. No injury or damage to property occurred (though I am not sure that damage to landscaping
would have shown up by now). Oh, and Home Depot refused to issue a refund without my entering their store,
which is ill-advised because of my medical condition and risk factors for Covid 19. My concern is that it could have
--- and may have already -- turned out a lot worse for somebody else. I am willing to provide the remains of the
defective valve to the CPSC (the guts are lost in my lawn) or the manufacturer for inspection and to address this
apparent defect.
justification: Gasoline leak due to missing internal parts of the valve could have caused a fire or explosion, posing a significant risk.

incident_description:
"Rome" Brand Pie Iron.Manufacturer Code:  "Rome's #1605 Pie Iron Double Cast iron"  SKU # 29794-16059

Usage:  Pie Iron has two sections which fold over each other to hold a sandwich while the entire utensil is placed over a camp fire.  The cast iron sections had supported by two 24" metal handles.  The handles are supposed to be attached by roller pins press-fitted through holes in the cast iron to secure than handles.  The handles must support the iron as it is lifted out of the campfire, since the iron is red-hot from the camp fire.

One set of handles was unsecured, the roller pins were not installed during manufacture.  The other handle set was secured by roller pins but those pins were of a size which did not permit a solid press fit to secure the handle.

While lifting the iron from the campfire, one handle immediately detached out of the capture hole and the heavy iron rotated around the other handle.  This caused the iron to open and one side of the red-hot iron dropped onto the ground, very close to the foot of the person cooking over the fire.

This is a very dangerous manufacturing defect; post-manufacture quality control should have caught this deficiency.
justification: The incident resulted in a near-miss injury, with the red-hot iron nearly touching the person's foot, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is almost certain given the manufacturing defects and the nature of the product's use.

The box was unopened, everything inside had never been used (all bags sealed with original tape; all items unassembled and no dirt; no parts bags opened). The string trimmer is battery operated and comes with a battery and a battery charging base. The charging base has a manufacturing defect in the electrical plug causing neutral prong to be askew and pointing out at an odd angle. This was not bent after manufacturing but was bent first and then molded into the black plastic of a standard two-prong electrical plug.

I contacted GreenWorks customer service and they refused to replace it since I bought it on eBay. I explained it could be a safety issue and that the item was CSA listed and that they should take this opportunity to understand whether other consumers were affected. The tech refused and again stated their policy that they would not replace the dangerous part.

I did not attempt to plug it into my outlet but other customers may have tried to use it anyway which could represent an electrical safety issue (such as a short circuit) which could cause electroshock to a person or fire damage to property.
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the defect poses a high likelihood of electrical hazards, such as electric shock or fire, if used.

I attempted to call customer service for Craftsman and after five calls, I finally got someone to attempt to answer my question about the functioning of the chain brake.  their only response was to return it to the store at which i purchased it. incident_description:
When using a Toro Recycler Lawn Mower Model 20334 powered by a Briggs & Stratton 163 cc engine the fuel cap loosened and fell from the safety tether which is meant to hold it and prevent it falling. In this case it failed to stop the cap from falling and was shattered by the mower's operating blade and explosively propelled the hard plastic pieces in numerous directions with some rebounding off an adjacent wall and striking the operator's arm, fortunately without serious injury.

Initially the owner, myself, believed it was a fluke and located the correct replacement cap, a Genuine Briggs & Stratton Model 594061 Fuel Cap on Amazon.com and provided through the Briggs & Stratton Store. It matched the original item exactly and seemed secure when it was installed. After several minutes the fuel cap again fell to the ground and fortunately was not hit. Upon inspecting the unit the safety tether no longer secured the cap and fit the perimeter of the cap loosely, not securely as it had upon installation.

Upon investigating it appeared the tether expanded in the heat of a 85 degree day and would no longer hold the cap safely. The mower was left overnight in the garage and the next day the tether appeared to hold. Operating it cautiously under cooler conditions and inspecting the tether after several minutes revealed the cap was not being held securely. It is assumed just the heat of an operating engine allows the tether to fail.
justification: Although no serious injury occurred, the incident resulted in the fuel cap being propelled by the mower's blade, posing a potential hazard.

incident_description:
I was finishing mowing my lawn with my John Deere Z445 zero turn lawn mower near dark and noticed a glowing ember and flame from the right panel (a fender).  The source of the fire was the right side light of a dealer installed BM23575 lighting kit.  The light fixture can pivot when it encounters shrubs, as I believe happened in this case.  Apparently, the wiring or contacts of the bulb shorted and overheated.  The bulb melted its way out of the housing and fell against the plastic fender panel causing it to melt, overheat and produce a flame.  I turned the light switch off and the flame abated.

This may be a design defect as John Deere fender panels used to be metal and the lights encased in a housing.  The fact that the lights can pivot and the wiring flexes allows the possibility that an electrical short is likely to occur over time.  The 'outrigger' positioning of the lights leads to the likelihood that they will come in contact with evergreens and bushes in normal use.  I can understand that plastic fenders won't rust and are less expensive, but the lights need to be in a housing for protection.

This right fender panel includes the gas cap and though most people would turn off the mower or the lights as I did, potential contact with gasoline spillage is a possibility.

I would have thought this series of events to be very unlikely, until it happened to me in very normal operation.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire on a lawn mower, posing a potential risk to the user and property.

Instructions are to screw the propane canister to the regulator and then insert & rotate regulator into the grill burner.

Batteries were charged fully and stored in warm condition. Unit has not been abused or dropped. At no point was the unit opened or altered from the original manufacturing.

The parking lot surface was sandy and aslightly uneven, some bumping of the unit as it was operated. Unit was pushed through heavy snow but not set to clear too difficult snow/ice conditions. incident_description:
This is a safety notification. I am also in contact with the manufacturer - YTL International Inc. 

CountryLine 25 ton log splitter Purchased at Tractor Supply Company

Yesterday (2/23/20) I was using the log splitter to split logs from a felled tree. I transported the log splitter to the tree by towing it there. The logs were a little heavy so after consulting the instruction manual I decided to place the log splitter in a vertical orientation. I had never used the product in this way before.

"To split wood in the vertical position, release the pin on the beam latch located near the
front end of the beam. Tilt the beam up until the foot plate is sitting squarely on the ground and the log splitter is stable."

When I placed the beam vertically I could see that the foot plate was a little off the ground so I moved the splitter slightly to adjust it. When I moved the tongue of the splitter I leaned over it to move it, but the I-beam came crashing down on my back. The I-beam only locks in the down/horizontal position and not the vertical one and it is unstable in the upright position and even the slightest movement will cause it to come crashing down. The beam is very heavy and it has bruised my back and ribs and when it knocked me to the ground I broke my finger. 

I was hurt by this accident, but I could easily have been killed. 

The manufacturer still sells this product through Tractor Supply Company and there should be a warning at a minimum that the beam is unstable when it is upright. The product needs a locking mechanism to safely keep the beam upright. 

Please take appropriate action to warn customers of this danger.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (broken finger, bruised back and ribs), and the unstable vertical position of the beam, which is not locked, increases the likelihood of similar accidents.

incident_description: When using a Black & Decker Electric String Trimmer (Model BESTE620) there are two handles, a pistol grip controlling handle at the back and a loop handle closer to the trimming head. The button is a toothed cylinder that when not depressed grips teeth on the inner rim of the loop handle attachment. During use the loop handle would disconnect from the toothed button allowing the loop handle to rotate back and consequently dropping the trimmer motor and head to the ground. These events appeared to happen randomly. After several incidents use of the trimmer was terminated for concern that the rapidly spinning trimmer string spool head could cause damage especially if it were to separate from the main part of the trimmer. I arrived home, after leaving for approximately one hour, to a house full of smoke and my dogs coughing. The fire was extinguished and I notified the Fire Marshalls, the installer, and the distributor of the stove. I also called Thelin the following day but they would not discuss the incident and said I should speak to the distributor. I asked for the name of the person at Thelin, and she disconnected the call.
