After looking at the stove, the distributore was instructed by the manufacturer to pull the stove from my home.

The gas hose was burned through on our arrival with fire burning freely under the grill. The grill was a Weber three burner.
justification: No injuries or deaths reported, but the incident caused property damage and had the potential for escalation due to the gas bottle involvement.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he was using his leaf blower for approximately fifteen minutes when a burning rubber smell was emitted and the unit burst into flames by the engine. The flames were so hot that they melted through the metal of his extension cord. The consumer dropped the leaf blower on his driveway and immediately put out the flames. The consumer inhaled black smoke but was feeling better the next day.

The consumer has contacted the manufacturer thirteen times in the last two years because, after having explained the situation and being informed he would receive a replacement unit an extension cord, they have not honored their word.

The consumer states that the unit was used, on average, twelve times per year for about fifteen to thirty minutes.

The consumer plans on keeping his leaf blower for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident resulted in the consumer inhaling black smoke, indicating an injury.

incident_description:

~09/28/2019 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer via their online form explaining the situation however he has yet to hear from them. Soon after the consumer purchased his unit he also contacted the Manufacturer via their online form but never received a response either.

The consumer states that he uses his unit every two weeks for approximately one hour during the warmer months.

The consumer plans on keeping his lawn mower for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The bar not disengaging poses a potential injury risk, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description:

When the consumer was finished, he put his lawn mower away but noticed, the second time he went to use it, that the unit had no fuel in it. The consumer proceeded to add fuel and cut his grass, again smelling gas all the while. When finished, the consumer inspected his unit and noticed that it was leaking gas from the two front-bolts the gas tank is mounted to the frame on.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer (Case Number: [REDACTED]) and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him that there was no assistance they could provide free of charge thus the five-gallon, plastic gas tank needed for his machine would cost him 189.99$.

The consumer states that the unit is used thirty to forty times per year for approximately two hours each use.

The consumer plans on keeping the lawn mower for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: Potential for injury due to gas leak, but no immediate harm reported.

incident_description:
On August 29 I cooked two salmon fillets on my new Traeger Silverton grill from Costco. This was the second time that I used this grill, I cooked the same items a week prior without a problem. I put the grill on "smoke" for about an hour, then turned it up to 350 degrees for the final 15 minutes of cook time. About 10 minutes after turning it up, I could see smoke pouring from the grill and heard noises coming from it. I opened the lid and flames were shooting out several feet. I shut the lid and turned the grill off, but it was still on fire. I opened the lid again pulled the salmon out, I had about 15 guests at my home and people were screaming. The fire eventually extinguished.
     The next several weeks were spent with innumerable calls to Traeger, they were completely unphased regarding the description of the fire. They finally agreed to replace this grill with an identical one, (after first offering to just replace the "burnt" parts, but truly did not care about the REASON the fire happened in the first place. So I then called and spoke with the Costco rep for Traeger, [REDACTED] (Sept 23, 2019) and described the grill fire.  This resulted in a call the following day from [REDACTED] in the Escalation Department at Traeger. I spent about an hour on the phone with him, taking the Pellet grill apart and texting photos of the burnt parts. I was naive in believing that they would be honest, but this was just a ploy to lay blame elsewhere. [REDACTED] decided that the fire was my fault and there was no defect in the grill design. He told me that the aluminum foil on the drip pan had a wrinkle in it, and that the aluminum drip liner (supplied by Traeger), had a wrinkle or fold which caused the fish grease to pool and catch on fire. First of all, the aluminum drip liner was so badly burned from the fire and was so distorted and charred as a result, there was no way to determine just how it was installed. The steel grill topper that I use for fish was also distorted and bent from the high heat of the fire, that was how hot it was. The tiny "wrinkle" in the aluminum foil could not have been the cause, so absurd! [REDACTED] (Traeger) sent [REDACTED] (Costco) an email essentially letting him know of his results. 
     I spoke with both [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] today (Oct 7, 2019), they are both happy to put the cause of the fire on the wrinkle in the aluminum foil and liner creating the pooling of grease which ultimately caused the fire. How absurd!
     Here is what I know:
1) I have had a Traeger grill for about 5 years and have cooked this same item on it hundreds of times without incident, I am not new to this. I've lined the drip pan with heavy aluminum foil for years without incident, wrinkles and all. 
2) I do believe that the fire WAS caused by the pooling of grease, as there was no grease flowing into the little grease bucket. But this was not a result of the little wrinkle in the aluminum foil, rather, it is a direct result of the angle (or lack of angle) on the drip pan itself.  When comparing the drip pan on the new grill as compared with my old Traeger grill, the pans sit at a completely different angle. The drip pan on the new grill is almost completely flat, there is hardly an angle to it at all. On the old grill, however, there is a distinct and visible angle to the drip tray allowing any grease to freely flow into the drip bucket and preventing the "pooling" of grease, thus preventing a fire. 
3) When I discussed my concerns with both Costco ([REDACTED]) and Traeger ([REDACTED) today, they were in denial and were both confident they had no responsibility. The "fix" for this defect is so easy, but imagine contacting every consumer that purchased this item for a retrofit repair to the grill....it is so much easier for them to deny there is a problem. My concern is that unsuspecting customers are currently subject to personal injury, property damage, or fatal injury as a result of this defective product.
4) Traeger was happy to send me another grill. After my first conversation with [REDACTED], he claimed that the Silverton had undergone some design changes and that I would not have a problem with the new grill. I had a handyman come out two days ago to put it together for me, and when I saw that it was identical to the one I currently have, I decided to send it back to Traeger. The freight company just picked it up a few minutes ago, and the driver told me he picks these up all the time because people are complaining that they catch on fire.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage and distress to guests, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I purchased these plant hanging pulleys to hang hanging baskets of flowers in my home.  The concept of this product is to allow potted plants and baskets up to 15 kg to be hung up high, but then be pulled down for watering2 Pack Plant Hook Pulley, Retractable Plant Hanger Easy Reach Hanging Flower Basket for Garden Baskets Pots and Birds Feeder Hang High up and Pull Down to Water Or Feed and care, then lifted back up into position for proper display, whereupon the mechanism will match, securely holding the plant until it is time to water it again.

I purchased 6 of these items from a seller on Amazon.com.  Here is the link:  2 Pack Plant Hook Pulley, Retractable Plant Hanger Easy Reach Hanging Flower Basket for Garden Baskets Pots and Birds Feeder Hang High up and Pull Down to Water Or Feed (2) https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07QSZQXVN/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_api_i_Z6NJDbY27J0V8

Within the first 15 minutes of use, 3 of the mechanisms failed without warning while holding stationary 9kg baskets.  This resulted in the baskets plummeting straight down to the end of the cord.  At the end of the suspending cord, the cord separated from the internal pulley mechanism, allowing the basket to continue falling until it impacted the floor.  The impact force was sufficient in one case to result in the breakage of the high impact hanging pot.

Had a child or pet been playing on the floor beneath the falling basket, in my opinion as a physician, serious bodily injury would have been a definite possibility, especially if the victim were struck on the head.
justification: The mechanism failure could have resulted in serious bodily injury, especially to a child or pet playing beneath.

In addition, the same part resulted in a minor cut (equivalent to a ÃÂpaper cutÃÂ) moments later during in the opposite hand (right hand, thumb).

incident_description:
MTD brand lawn mower adapter, which is a metal piece that is used to hold the lawn mower blade to the shaft of the lawn mower's engine, cracks apart while the engine is running, causing the lawn mower blade to fall off.  No injuries were sustained.  However, given that when the product fails, the the spinning blade falls off of the lawn mower, injuries are likely.

All three times, the blade came off the mower.

The part number is 753-0588 (blade adapter) for MTD brand lawn mower model no. 11A-428Q088.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the recurring failure of the blade adapter causing the blade to fall off poses a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
We recently purchased  a John Deere Z535M 62 inch zero turn mower. My wife had a minor accident while mowing. The mower started to roll backwards on a small hill. She went to hit the foot brake and there was no foot brake. She rolled backwards off a  low retaining wall. Lucky she wasn't hurt or the machine damaged. We know older John Deere zero turn have foot brakes. We thought all riding lawn mowers had foot brakes. 

Even the online owner's manual says not do mow up and down hill. Apparently they are aware there is no way to stop on a hill. 

We did not receive an owners manual from the manufacturer. We contacted them three week ago and have yet to receive the manual that we were promised.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have been severe due to the lack of foot brake on a hill, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Internal fuel line connections come apart during normal use, spraying gasoline inside the motor case (in potential direct contact with electrical spark and hot muffler, causing an immediate fire hazard) and also spilling on operator's hands and into the environment. This tool uses a primer bulb for starting. Two sections of fuel line are attached to small tubes on the primer bulb, relying only on friction and the rubber fuel line's normal elasticity to hold them in place; no clamps of any kind are used. This is an inherent design flaw: fuel-line connections in a confined environment subjected to high temperatures should be secured better. One of these lines leads from the fuel tank to the primer bulb; the second from the primer bulb to the carburetor. When the primer bulb is pressed (according to manufacturer's instructions for a cold start) it exerts pressure on the second of those fuel lines. That pressure pops the fuel line off the connecting tube, spilling gasoline into the case. I was able to cut off the end of that out-going line, which had apparently become enlarged, and achieve a somewhat more secure fit. But then after using the saw for just a few minutes, the second (incoming) fuel line spontaneously popped off, spraying a dangerous quantity of gasoline into the case and onto my hands. When the motor is turned off, the heat of the engine and muffler causes the spilled fuel inside the engine case to smoke.
I have had this saw exactly one year. I bought it in September 2018 immediately after Hurricane Florence and used it for post-storm cleanup for the next few months. It has been in storage since late 2018. Immediately on my attempting to re-start it this month (September 2019) I discovered this problem with the fuel lines. Also, I note from the serial number plate that this saw was manufactured in September 2015, almost three years before it was sold. It may have been in Home Depot's inventory all that time, to be offered for sale on short notice in the aftermath of natural disasters. It was in a large temporary display of chain saws at my nearest Home Depot store as soon as it opened when the hurricane had passed.
justification: The inherent design flaw of the fuel lines, combined with the high temperatures and pressure, caused the lines to pop off, leading to a spill and immediate fire hazard, resulting in potential injury.

Wondering if this incident has happened before to any other Snapper owner with the rear wheel breaking off of the axle.

According to Snapper it was said if the Snapper Service Center felt the failure was due to a defect they can obtain assistance from Snapper for the cost of repair to the mower. If they do not find an issue the dealer would bill me for the repair. CRM:[REDACTED]

I would assume that the Snapper Service Center would charge me for the time to inspect the axle and wheel, I do feel that the Snapper Service Center should remove the axle install a new axle and wheel at the expense of the Snapper, (Briggs & Stratton) Company and ship both the damaged axle and wheel to the Snapper, (Briggs & Stratton) Company as this should not have happened unless there was a problem/defect with the axle.

I feel that the Snapper Company, (Briggs & Stratton) should either repair my lawn mower at their expense, replace my lawn mower with the same type of lawn mower or reimburse my money of $796.82 which includes MA State Tax. I do not expect this to happen, but it should. 

There was a Three (3) year warranty on this lawn mower, had it for 4 years, 4 months.
You may release my name and contact information to the product manufacturer, this Lawn Mower was not a safe product for me to have owned.

On 20 August 2019, my Toro 51978 Gas Trimmer had a metal fatigue failure that broke the upper shaft assembly, causing a loss of control of the trimmer head.  The upper shaft and lower shaft assemblies provide the mechanical support for the engine and trimmer head, and these shaft assemblies also contain the driveshaft from the engine that drives the trimmer head.

No injuries occurred.
justification: The incident resulted in a loss of control of the trimmer head but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
A standalone "Sunsetter" motorized awning has a short-circuit grounding problem.  When the motor gets wet a ground surge occurs causing the electrical connection to short.  This can trip a breaker or Ground Fault interrupter.  This occurs even when the motor is not in use only connected to house outlets.


In my case I found the outlets in my garage shut down including power to a refrigerator.  I assume any motor designated for outdoor use should be waterproof or at least protected from getting wet.  Sunsetter ignored my request for an upgrade to solve this problem.


If for some reason the circuit breaker does not switch off current could flow and heat up the wiring.   


I recently got a safety upgrade concerning bungi clips used to hold down the awning cover.  The government seemed to find this to be dangerous, but ignored the problem described here.
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the incident has caused power outages, potentially leading to spoilage of perishable goods.

incident_description:
Husband was putting pre-cooked ribs on the grill when grease dripped off the rack of ribs while he was placing them on the grill. That grease ignited into flames as he was moving the ribs onto the grill, ran up toward the ribs and his hand, and also down into the grill.

While it was scary that the grease burned up toward him, that is not the complaint. The complaint is that when the grease dripped into the grill, it ran right out the bottom of the grill body, and directly onto the gas hose and LP tank in the cabinet of the grill.

He then had flames in the grill itself as well as on the gas line and LP tank. He tried to close the lid on the grill to snuff the flames, but there is a huge gap where the lid and the body meet, as well as several large gaps at the bottom of the grill body. These let in tons of air, and fed the fire instead of snuffing it.

Worse still, he had to get into the grill with fire coming from everywhere, to turn off the valve on the LP tank and disconnect the hose. This was made even more dangerous, because the LP tank is physically clamped into the cabinet, so he had to unscrew those clamps before he could move the tank to safety. - All with flaming grease dripping down onto the rubber gas hose and LP tank, and my husband.

This all seems very wrong. We've owned maybe 6 or more gas grills over our 30 year marriage, and none were built like this, or would have EVER had a dangerous situation like this arise.

This could easily have burned down our house, seriously injured my husband, and even destroyed our truck. Totally unacceptable for a Walmart purchase.
justification: The incident involved direct contact with flames and potential exposure to hazardous fumes, posing a high risk of injury.

He said the gas tank is made up of 2 plastic pieces that is glued together and over a period of time the tank begins to leak at the seam. He first noticed his gas tank leaking in June of 2017 and he said the issue has become worse with the tank leaking each time it is filled with gas.

He also noted that the replacement tanks have a different design with only one piece of plastic and he believes this is due to the firm knowing the defect with the tank.

The unit is used twice a month from march to November

incident_description:
Product: "Lunar Bowl Fire Table" by ELEMENTI, product # OFG101LP (propane fueled fire pit)

I ordered this fire pit through Amazon and it was delivered to my home.  It did not light using the ignitor, despite several attempts following the manual's lighting instructions. As I indicated to ELEMENTI, "IGNITION CLICKING HEARD AND PROPANE FLOWING, BUT UNIT FAILS TO FLAME. "

They responded by sending a second unit.  This had the same problem, as it did not flame in the fire pit following the lighting instructions.  I could hear the ignitor clicking, but it would not light.  I allowed the propane to dissipate as suggested in the manual, and then repeated this again, also as suggested in the manual, but it would not light. I then followed the alternative directions in the manual to light the fire pit using a handheld lighter. I was able to get the fire ring to light this way, but shortly after lighting it, a fireball exploded.  My son and I were seated next to it on the couch, and the fire appeared to come mostly from underneath the unit and caused burns to our legs.  It seared off the hair on our lower legs and resulted in second degree burns, mostly to my son's lower left leg and foot, and a smaller second degree burn to my right lower leg. The burns to my son's leg were treated in the Emergency Room at Rhode Island Hospital.

I had a fire pit/ gas service professional examine both fire pits afterwards and he detected heavy leaking propane from the air mixer (venturi) device underneath each unit. He reported them both to be unsafe and condemned them for use. Since the same issue involved BOTH units, from same part, I am concerned that there is a manufacturing design or part failure/defect.  Out of concern for others, I contacted Amazon and ELEMENTI, to let them know, as I am concerned there may be other units with the same propane leaking air mixer part and potential for injury to others.
justification: Second degree burns to both individuals, with one requiring ER treatment, indicates a severe incident.

incident_description:
My neighbor purchased an Ever Brite Black Motion Activated Outdoor Integrated with 24 White Solar Light.  He screwed this light into his fence.  That night, I walked by and the sensor activated.  The light blasted me in the eyes and caused considerable eye pain and even more severe psychological pain.

This light is a 5000K color temperature LED light that has no place in a civil society.  It is a weapon, not a light.  This light needs to be recalled and removed from the market.  It is a hazard!
justification: The light's high intensity and motion activation caused temporary blindness and significant psychological distress.

incident_description: I had just assembled the Akorn Kamado smoker/grill by Char Griller and wanted to move it. Before lifting the handle, I saw the warning label by the handle that indicates not to move the kamado grill if the latch is not attached. I thought I had secured the latch but I did not. I then proceeded to lift the handle and move the kamado/grill. The kamado/grill immediately tipped over spilling out the cast iron grill which hit my leg and landed on my foot. Luckily I had just put the kamado together but if I had used the kamado, then it would have been filled with hot coals and the cast iron grill would also be hot.

Direct sunlight on the failed product is estimated at approximately 8-10 hours because of mature trees, landscaping and other structures in the neighborhood. When [REDACTED] returned home during the afternoon hours, she found that one of the solar lights had been melted, the grass around it blackened, and a small spot on the wood deck that burned but did not sustain combustion. But received little help or information from the office.

incident_description:
A gas grill, sold by Sears, under model number 139.01566310 contains a defectively manufactured part, "Drip tray Assembly", part # CH3017361.  This part is a piece of shaped galvanized stainless steel, acting to catch grease/fat drippings from food during cooking. It also provides a thermal barrier between the burners and the LP tank.  Unfortunately, this part, through no fault of the consumer, or lack of maintenance, rusts away and disintegrates, allowing the flame from the burner to be unobstructed within inches of the LP tank. 
Sears has been made aware of this defect, and the grill has been the subject of a class action. 
However, Sears refuses to provide a replacement part, or to have a replacement part manufactured to address this defect. 
When I open the lid of my grill, I can see my LP tank, and have stopped using the grill. The bottom frame of the grill, below the firebox is enclosed so, even the slightest leak of propane, or an improperly tightened hose would result in a catastrophic explosion, due to this failed part. 
When I attempted to order the part from Sears, the order was taken, money was paid, but Sears had no intention of fulfilling the order - I eventually received a refund. However, Sears does not plan to address the safety issue with this grill.
justification: The defect could lead to a propane leak and subsequent explosion, posing a high likelihood of an incident with no injuries.

incident_description:
Incident 1:
November 23, 2018
Using new Westendorf front end loader in normal manner. Removable bucket safety latches failed. Loader bucket fell in operators lap, breaking femur bone. Operator required femur surgery.

Incident 2:
July 2, 2019
Using same Westendorf front end loader. Loader is rated to lift 3000 pounds. Actual load = 2300 pounds. Loader king pins sheared on both sides, load fell to ground, and safety latches failed once again.

Incident 3:
July 30, 2019
Using same Westendorf front end loader. Safety latches failed again, bucket fell off loader. I had previously added safety chains to prevent bucket from falling onto operator again.

Incident 1 was reported to Manufacturer. Unacceptable response from Manufacturer. Incident 2 reported to Manufacturer. Manufacturer provided replacement king pins. Operator still un recovered from previous indecent and unable to repair front end loader with parts supplied by Manufacturer.

This Westendorf front end loader, obviously, has multiple safety problems. (multiple safety latch failures and load capacity issues) Operator is fortunate that one or more of above incidents has not resulted in death.
justification: Multiple safety latch failures and load capacity issues have led to injuries, making another incident likely.

incident_description:
We have a Troy-Bilt mower with a Briggs-Stratton engine.  It is about 4 years old. My spouse was mowing the lawn when the engine began to smoke and almost immediately (~1 second) afterwards, shot a ~5 cm piece of metal out of the engine through the engine housing.  The metal appears to have broken off from the engine.

We have maintained this product per the manufacturer's specifications.  Although it is out of warranty, we do not feel that exploding is part of the expected or safe function of a mower.  

I have pictures of the damage but was unable to upload them.
justification: The engine's unexpected failure and expulsion of metal, though not causing injury, indicates a significant safety issue.

incident_description:
Product: Eureka Sprie camp stove
One year old

Regulator failed and allowed high pressure LP gas to the burners 

Video on my facebook page 

https://www.facebook.com/[REDACTED/
justification: The regulator failure could have led to a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Consumer reported that the battery in the flashlight apparently overheated and exploded while the flashlight was charging in a wall outlet.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (flashlight explosion) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur frequently due to safety measures in modern electronics.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her riding lawnmower just purchased May 31st, 2019.
With the first use on the day of purchase the unit was not cranking over easily and she noticed fuel shooting out from exhaust port.
She contacted the retailer who told  her that he would be more concerned if it was diesel fuel and she should just be sure to remove the key when not in use.
Once she spoke with him and started mowing with it and this particular problem seemed to solve itself until the day of the incident being reported.
Sometime around June 25th, 2019 after mowing and putting the mower in her garage. she turned it off and removed key then the alarm on the unit began sounding loudly, she checked the unit traced it to the starter but when she attempted to start it again it was dead.
Alarm was still sounding, starter was very hot.
She disconnected the battery, however she remembered verbiage from the manual that instructed to remove spark plug wires first which she did then began disconnecting the battery, however it sparked and the motor started turning over.
She pushed the unit out of her garage.
She now cannot disconnect the battery because it is sparking causing the motor to continue trying to turn over.
With the wires disconnected it will not run but does continue to crank as if beginning to run.
She contacted the place of purchase to advise them that she had a safety issue going on but the person she was speaking with asked whether she had an extended warranty.
She asked the representative when she could get it in to him but she states that he told her that it was first come, first serve at which time she said her thought was that the word "safety hazard" was not understood. 
The consumer called the manufacturer, she spoke in depth with their technician who provided her with case# [REDACTED] contact# 800-227-3798
She is reporting this unit as a severe fire and burn hazard and that no safety feature worked to prevent this.
(1)  Seat safety switch.  Did not work.
(2)  Having to depress the break to start.  Did not work.
(3)  Key out of ignition.  Did not work.
(4)  No fuse blew
There are no injuries being reported
The manufacturer was contacted multiple times
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a severe fire and burn hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a high likelihood of occurrence (4) given the repeated issues and safety features that failed to prevent it.

incident_description:
In August 2017, I purchased a Saber 3-Burner Cast Black Grill. During the weekend of August 11, 2018, when I attempted to light the grill, it burst into flames and exploded. We called the fire department, and the grill was left inoperable. I reported the issue to Saber, and they promptly sent a representative to pickup the grill and provide a new one. (Saber Case # [REDACTED])

This past weekend, on July 27, 2019, I went to light the grill that Saber provided in return for the defective grill in August 2018--and the same thing happened. A loud explosion, a fireball, and all of the grills were displaced when I attempted to light the grill. I called Saber to report the issue again; they declined to provide a refund, and explained that the issue is a "delayed ignition" issue which can be addressed by simply cleaning out the burners. 

There is a real safety issue with these grills. The two issues I have experienced in the last two years are identical to the issue described in the 2017 recall of Saber Grills, although neither one of the Saber Grills I used were within the scope of the recall. 

I requested a refund from Saber Grills, but they declined to provide a refund. They stated that any refund must come from the dealer where I purchased the grill. This grill, however, came directly from the manufacturer.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the grill's repeated explosions pose a significant safety risk.

incident_description:
Please see the email correspondence with the company.

I am concerned about two defects that I noticed in an LP gas replacement burner manufactured by GrillPro/Broil. King/Onward Manufacturing Company Limited. 

1.  The gaskets provided deteriorate within a few weeks of use to the point where they crack, break apart, and cause gaps that could allow gas to escape thereby allowing for the possibility of the gas to be ignited and flames to occur in the areas of the grill where they are not intended and may cause fire or explosion.

2.  The burner is intended for heating separately controlled sides of a grill.  However, I have received three of these  replacement burners over the course of less than two months and all three have had the same defect. The seperating divider within the burner, between the two halves, has large gaps that allow gas to pass from one side to the other when only one side is intended to be lit. Due to the proximity of the gas escaping to the flame on the intended lit side the escaping gas is ignited and either stays lit on the unintended side also or it ignites then goes out then reignites cyclically as the gas accumulates. The user may not expect the other side to be hot causing an accident.
justification: Potential for fire or explosion due to gas leaks, posing a significant risk of property damage and injury.

incident_description: Greenworks Lawnmower Twin Force 40 Volt Lithium Max Lawnmower. I took it outside to start mowing my lawn and it suddenly made a weird noise, after approximately 30 seconds, the lawnmower stopped and then I noticed it was on fire. I used a fire extinguisher to put it out, but it no longer works.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the lawnmower catching fire is a significant incident, and while not common, it's possible given the sudden malfunction and ignition.

incident_description:
KitchenAid 710-0003 Natural Gas Hose and Regulator for Gas Grill Conversion

I have had TWO of these develop gas leaks and create small fires at the place where the hose goes into the fitting which connects it to the grill body.  This is not part of the grill itself, it is part of the natural gas conversion kit.

The first one actually burned through the natural gas hose, the second I found while doing a check and noticed it had developed a small flame coming out of it.
justification: Two incidents of gas leaks and small fires occurred, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
My Hitachi Trimmer is CG22EAB SLP the Issue is that it gets very hot. I normally use it the turn it off too cool, 
then Finish trimming
justification: The trimmer overheating could potentially cause burns, hence an incident with no injury.

incident_description: On 7/12/2019, at approximately 10:30 pm, my wife noticed that our back deck was on fire.  In the process of putting out the fire, we discovered that our Kobalt 40v Lawn Mower was on fire and subsequently caught our back deck on fire.  We stored the lawn mower just under the deck while not in use.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of it happening again is possible due to the proximity of the lawn mower to the deck.

incident_description:
Electric lawnmower deadman's switch and safety switch no longer operate properly -- mower starts when neither is pressed!

I was mowing, and released the deadman's switch in order to move something in the yard to mow around it. The mower started slowing down, and then sped up, rapidly reaching full speed. Engaging and disengaging the deadman's switch did nothing, and now, whenever it is plugged in, the blade starts spinning even if you are not touching the mower.

Ordinarily, a side switch must be pressed, and then the deadman's switch pullbar pulled back, before the motor turns on. I've had this mower for 5 years as my sole mower, so I've used it quite a lot.

I looked at reviews on Amazon (where I purchased it), and although others have had problems like catching on fire or just failing to run, I have not seen anyone else mention this particular safety issue, of the safety mechanisms failing.
justification: The mower's safety features failing could lead to an incident, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
While mowing my yard with a John Deere E130 Riding Lawn Mower purchased from Lowes in Tyler, Tx. on June 29, 2019, the mower caught on fire. Within a matter of minutes, the entire mower was consumed with flames. I'm lucky I saw the flames and got off in time. The wind was blowing and the fire spread. Luckily though, no one was hurt, and I got the flames extinguished in the pasture that kept the fire from spreading and jumping the road that would have contacted other people's domiciles. I had already called the Baxter Volunteer Fire Dept. They sprayed water on the mower that completed its extinguishing. The fireman completed a report for which I have a copy as well as pictures and videos of the fire.

I suspect that the muffler emitted a spark onto the dry grass which quickly caught fire. The mower's muffler is very low to the ground and does not have a spark arrestor. My old John Deere LX188 has a spark arrestor around the muffler to prevent this type of incident.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the potential for property damage and spread of fire was high due to the dry grass and wind.

incident_description: I own a Toro brand self propelled mower with a Briggs and Stratton 7.25 Hp engine (model #128M02-0001) manufactured in October 2012.  The fuel cap is one of three that were used on this model and is a 1/4 turn model ( 957C 591003).  I have just ordered my third fuel cap due to the failure of the cap and the prodigious leaking of raw gasoline that results.  The cap is the only one of the three for this engine that is unvented, relying on air to come in through where the threads should be.  This is a significant safety hazard and the manufacturer, Briggs and Stratton, should be required to replace the cap on all remaining models.
justification: While no incidents have been reported, the unvented fuel cap design poses a significant risk of fuel leaks, which could potentially lead to fires or explosions.

incident_description:
When mowing my lawn, my Husqvarna engine blew up. Product# 960450004 Model# YTH20K46SN# 072108A012551

The engine block totally broke into 2 pieces.  The explosion was so big the head light covers out.
My biggest concern is that the gas line disconnected and it could have been much worse if it caught fire.

Kohler Spec NO PS-SV6-00-0024
SN# 3817610553

I've tried contacting Husqvarna and [REDACTED] engines with no success.
justification: The engine explosion caused property damage but no injuries, and while it could have been worse, it did not result in any injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Lawnmower would not start and smelled like electrical wires melting. I took it to someone to look at it and the wires and contacts were melted and burned.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning lawnmower with melted wires, posing a potential fire hazard but no immediate injury.

incident_description: Regarding our LM2102SP, there is a potentially dangerous concern with the self-propel feature.  If you pull the mower backwards, the rear wheels can lock up, then suddenly release, causing the mower to lurch backwards.  If a person were to have this happen with the blade turning, it is possible for the mower to: 1) cause the operator to stumble, 2) the mower to be pulled over a body part and 3) cause personal injury.  In my mind, the fix is to correct the situation that can cause the self-propel system to engage without any throttle being applied such that the wheels will always turn freely in either direction, unless the operator is using the self-propel feature.
justification: The incident description details a real risk of injury, with the mower potentially causing the operator to stumble or be pulled over, leading to personal injury.

incident_description:
I acquired this leaf blower as an item I received for cleaning out a neighbors garage in 2015.
I have used it regularly on my driveway and street in front of my home along with the back patio. Today I cut my front lawn as usual, I edged and trimmed afterwards. Then I blow off the driveway and street gutter. I completed the driveway and all of the gutter except the last 2 feet or so. As I was swinging the blower in a sweeping motion left to right and back left again as I always do, it seemed to explode in my hands. It sounded like a large handgun going off in my hand. Then I immediately felt this intense pain in my leg. I would say it felt like I was shot, but I never have been, but I imagine it is pretty close to the feeling. I dropped the blower immediately on the ground and looked at my leg, then around to see if anybody else had heard the noise. A neighbor was out with her kids in a small pool and was looking at me as if she heard the noise. The blower was still powered up and I immediately went to the cord and unplugged it, not sure exactly what had happened. I looked for smoke from an electrical fire, but there was none. I then picked up the blower and a piece came sliding out a large hole in the side of the casing, and something else was rattling around inside the blower. There was another large hole on the other side of the casing. I had no idea what had just happened, but now my leg was really hurting. I couldn't understand why the thing exploded the way it did. I went in and examined my leg. A large welt started to form on my upper thigh. The welt was about the same height as my testicles. If this machine would have exploded one second sooner, the injury would have directly been to my testicles. I cannot imagine what that would have felt like, but I guess I would probably not be here typing this report, as it probably would have sent me to the E.R, at the hospital! I am still thanking God that piece of "plastic shrapnel" did not neuter me! Although I may not be in physical pain shock, the thought keeps going through my mind of how close that came to my nuts, I still can't believe that machine exploded with such force and shattered two large holes on either side of the casing. The injury could have been devastating in just a split second. I came in and had to make dinner and feed our dogs and took a short nap. My leg had a large welt and a bruise on my thigh. I took several pictures after dinner. I have used that blower for years and never heard of a recall, but I did not buy it either.Nor did I know it was made in China. I had several other items from the garage I cleaned out and noticed they were from China and I sold those in a garage sale for just that reason. I had no idea this blower was on recall, or it was even made in China.  I tend to stay away from cheap products like this and now I will need to examine the rest of my tools for recalls and where they are manufactured. I am still in shock as to how close that came to blowing up my testicles and what that pain would have been like? It gives me chills!
justification: The leaf blower exploded unexpectedly, causing a significant injury to the user's leg, and could have caused severe injury to sensitive areas if it had occurred a moment earlier.

incident_description:
Dear Amazon, a few days ago my wife purchased some bug zappers from Amazon. Upon first use, one of the metal plug pins broke off when removing the unit from a wall outlet, leaving the pin protruding from the wall. As that metal is at a potential of 120V AC, there is a risk that a user could touch it when pulling the unit away from the wall or when attempting to remove the part that has broken off. Please see attached a photo of the failed device and a warning sheet from the NY State occupational health office. I am an Electrical Engineer with professional registration and experience in the US and EU, so have a reasonable basis for my concern.
The seller seems to believe that as the voltage generated inside the unit is low, it is safe, which is not correct. The seller also continues to list the product, and it is annotated as ÃÂAmazonÃÂs ChoiceÃÂ for its vendor. I saw at least two warnings from other purchasers after a brief scan of recent reviews for this product.
For my part, I wrote to the seller, also alerted Amazon in my replies which I understand are monitored by you, and I separately wrote to your CIS email below. As I have not heard back from Amazon, please acknowledge receipt of this message, which is copied to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission.
Feel free to call me if I can be of any further assistance. My phone number is below.
Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in no injury but has the potential to cause electrical shock, making it an incident with a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased three (3) "Headlamp Led Flashlight Waterproof Hard Hat Light, Rechargeable 18650 headlight" from Amazon and produced by Hai-electronic for Christmas 2018. I gave one to my mother [REDACTED] and the other to my friend [REDACTED].

On 6/29/2019 @ approx 1020pm EST [REDACTED] placed his " Headlamp Flashlight Headlight Rechargeable 18650 headlight" on the charger. 10-15 min later the headlamp exploded and caught fire. After extinguishing the fire it was found that parts of the two batteries had blasted through a cabinet and into the wall of the home. The second battery hit and detonated in the couch less than three feet from [REDACTED] wife and stepson, throwing battery acid and noxious fumes into the air and causing both material damage and possible health issues as the house was now filled with toxic smoke. Fortunately, [REDACTED] was a former paramedic and was able to evacuate his family shortly after the event and then ventilated the house. He contacted me to warn me of the possible danger and I have stopped using the headlamps since. I contacted Amazon to apprise them of the issue and was issued a credit for the item and told that it would be investigated for a possible recall.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage and potential health issues due to battery acid and toxic smoke, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high as the incident occurred shortly after charging and involved a product defect.

incident_description: I own a Char-Broil 6 burner grill that caught on fire when in use. The grease from the hamburgers has nowhere to drain. This could have resulted in a deadly accident as it uses propane gas to operate.
justification: The grill's design flaw in grease drainage, combined with the use of flammable propane gas, makes a fire highly likely.

incident_description: The mower was purchased from Lowe's in 2014.  It was model # KM2040X-6,  item # 506586.  It spontaneously combusted and caught my house on fire.
justification: The mower spontaneously combusted, causing a house fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that his one year old BBQ grill caught fire Inside the housing where the knobs are located when he turned the knob on to use the grill, then propane leaked into the housing area causing all of the knobs to be extremely hot due to the housing behind them being on fire.
The fire was extinguished with water.
The caller's left hand was slightly burned, however he is reporting no injury.  Customer service was very slow to return email.
justification: Injury occurred due to hot knobs caused by propane leak and fire, but not severe enough for death.

incident_description: We purchased this grill in May 2018 and used it throughout the summer season without a hitch. We loved it. It was great. During the winter months, we had it stored in the garage. Memorial Day weekend this year (2019) we brought it out of the garage, thoroughly cleaned it inside and out and began using it again this season. IÃÂd say between last summer and this May/June we have used the grill maybe 20-25 times total. This past weekend, my husband was preheating the grill and within 5 minutes we smelled an awful burning smell. We opened up the grill and flames were everywhere. It was totally on fire. After turning off all the burners, we closed the lid to try to have the fire burn itself out. Nope. That didnÃÂt work. Flames began shooting out the bottom of the grill (where the drip pan is). Keep in mind, the drip pan had been changed out the night prior. There was ZERO grease in it. This was not a grease fire. After a minute of panic that the entire unit was going to catch flames and light the propane tank on fire, we opened up the lid and doused the entire grill in baking soda. THANK GOD it put the whole fire out. The inside of the grill is destroyed. The cookbox is melted in several locations and melted to the drip pan. The flavorizor bars are destroyed and look like they are disintegrating and rusty now. The cooking grates are peeling and rusty looking. The entire grill except for the stand and propane tank are RUINED.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, with the grill being ruined.

incident_description:
First use just out of the box of a Coleman Camping Grill/Stove+, followed directions for setup an d how to line bottom to ease cleanup.  Cooked food on skewers, removed cooked food and turned off gas supply.  When I went after dinner to clean up I discovered that the burner tube and the cooking grate had melted into a metal and aluminum glob.  The burner tube was completely destroyed and the center portions of the cooking grate/grill was totally melted.

Concern is twofold: 1) Coleman camping products should be reliable; 2)  If I had not turned off the propane gas supply before the meltdown the product failure could have caused injury from burning or possible explosion of the pressurized gas supply tank or, at a minimum, could have caused a fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the product failure could have led to burns or an explosion if the gas supply hadn't been turned off.

incident_description:
The Briggs & Stratton engine model # 104M050072F1 is deficient in design.  The fuel cap cannot be secured tightly, resulting in the cap coming off when the lawn mower is in use.  Gasoline splashes onto a hot engine directly adjacent to a now wide open gasoline tank.  I do not know if any fires have resulted from this condition, but it would be surprising if there have not been.

I have attempted to express my concerns with Briggs & Stratton, only to be told that my machine's warranty would be handled by a dealer.  I am not concerned about the price of a replacement cap.  I am concerned about the safety of the product.
justification: The design flaw poses a high risk of injury due to potential gasoline fires.

incident_description: I have a John Deere D-110 riding lawn mower. I was driving down a small embankment and the brakes failed completely and I was unable to stop the machine using the brake pedal or parking brake. The machine stopped when it ran into a fence. I think the linkage on the braking system failed. Earlier models of this machine were recalled due to linkage failure.  I think this machine should have been included in the recall.  I contacted John Deere and they said it was  not their problem.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the complete brake failure poses a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: Fan exploded shooting out shrapnel and hitting my son with some force 30' away.
justification: Injury occurred due to shrapnel hitting the son, but no fatality reported.

incident_description:
I am writing to inform you, that there is a safety issue with the Lowes Utilitech submersible sump pump.

The pump exploded and caught fire.  I heard a very load explosion type noise and could not find the source. A half hour later the smoke alarm went off and I found the sump pump to be on fire with a three inch flame and was put out with a fire extinguisher. The sump pit was full enough of water where the pump could have activated.  The middle section of the pump was broken from the inside out for 360 degrees. The electrical wiring was blown off the pump.   Photos available.

Application:  The pump was used to pump water from a home iron filter.  This filter is cycled every other day and discharges about 30-40 gallons per cycle.  It uses soda ash which lowers the PH of the water (It does not use salt).  The only other water source is from a dehumidifier.    The pump was installed correctly including the vent hole.  The pump has about a 8 ft head.
justification: The pump explosion and fire caused no injuries, but the incident could have resulted in property damage and potential hazards if not detected promptly.

incident_description:
Submitter says that while the product was in use, flames randomly shoot up very high. Callers son tried to put the flames out quickly. Scared of the gas tank underneath the product igniting. In order to put the flames out had to turn the gas off. No injuries. 

Caller believes this product is a fire hazard. BECAUSE THE BURNER TUBE RUSTED & SPLIT. I BELIEVE THE METAL WAS DEFECTIVE.
justification: The incident involved a fire, but no injuries were reported, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is high due to the identified defective metal.

incident_description:
(06/15/2015) The consumer lost the tip of his finger in the log splitter. The consumer was trying to get a piece of wood out of the log tray. He got his finger caught between the log and the inside of the wood tray.

The consumer stated that the way the product is made is defective.

The consumer had to go to the emergency room so that they could stop the bleeding. His doctor has scheduled amputation on part of his finger.
justification: Injury occurred due to product design defect, with potential for recurrence.

incident_description:
On Saturday 6/2/ 2019 I was setting up my smoker. I heated it up to brush the grates before putting
food in. When I turned around the entire this was ablaze
The heat melted the bottom of the grill and burned through the propane line.
My first thought was to turn off the grill at the knob. However, the cheap plastic knob melted off leaving only a red hot stem
 Had I not had the sense to kill the propane I could have easily blown up the house.
This is a MAJOR DESIGN DEFECT .
This is extremely DANGEROUS


I contacted Masterbuilt who attempted to blame me for the issue. A quick scan of the internet shows that other consumers have had the EXACT same issue. The cheap flooring buckles in the heat exposing the propane line to direct flame.

The smoker is currently in my garage available for inspection. Masterbuilt declined to look at it and replied without ever seeing the grill.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the number of reported similar incidents.

incident_description:
On July 1, 2018, I bought a Weber Spirit E210, 2-burner BBQ at Ace Hardware in Jackson, Wyoming.	For a variety of reasons, including the fact I have a larger, [REDACTED]grill, I did not used it very often. However, whenever I did use it to BBQ a whole chicken, grease seeped everywhere, and as the grease ran down its sides, it dripped onto, and burned, my deck. (I am enclosing 4 photographs .) Last summer, I was preoccupied with other matters, stopped using the grill, and did not contact Weber or the CPSC.

As we got prepared for this summer season, we thoroughly cleaned the grill. But when I BBQed another whole chicken, I had the same result - grease went everywhere . So, we cleaned it again, this time getting it as clean as it was when it was "brand-spanking new." Then I grilled another whole chicken, and again, lots of grease ran down its sides, and dripped onto my deck.

Accordingly, I called Weber's customer service line. The representative asked for photographs; I sent the ones attached hereto, and after he looked at them, he called and said, "when you BBQ fatty things, that will happen; it is normal and to be expected."

I responded: First, there wasn't much fat on any of those chickens, as I always remove the fat before BBQing.	WAY MORE IMPORTANT : Weber should not manufacture a BBQ that gushes grease when someone grills a chicken - I suspect, one of the most commonly grilled items .

Because I was taken aback at his response; I asked to speak to his supervisor and was transferred to her. She essentially said the same thing he had.

When I asked to speak to her supervisor, she said her supervisor had left for the day but would call me the next morning . She didn't!

It took a week before she finally called. When she did, she agreed there was a problem and said she would ship me a replacement unit, which has a slightly newer design, I said that would probably work and went to Ace to see how the new model differed from mine. The newer model has two wheels - mine has four and I need four - so I told her I would pay the difference and upgrade to the next model (a [REDACTED]), and that's what I did.
 
When I told the Customer Service Manager, she told me she would arrange tor Ace to refund my purchase price, pick up my Spirit, and destroy it.	I was shocked and said, 11 DESTROY IT! Don't you want to inspect it and see why it leaks grease?" "No," she replied.

My Spirit (and perhaps others) is extremely dangerous and I cannot believe Weber doesn't want to inspect it and figure out why so much grease escapes. Maybe it wasn't assembled properly (that was done by Ace), perhaps it has a faulty part, etc .? But SIGNIFICANTLY MORE WORRISOME : why does Weber want it to be destroyed without inspecting it? ASAP, NO LESS!

As an aside : two weeks ago, we had some young families and their kids over for dinner, and although I used the larger [REDACTED to BBQ, I realized those kids could easily have been seriously burned if I had been using the Spirit and they touched it.  Consequently, I contacted you.

I hope the Consumer Product Safety Commission will look into this matter - indeed, inspect the Spirit and determine if mine is the only one with an issue or if all 2-burner E210s need to be recalled.

Thanks,
[REDACTED]
justification: Grease dripping onto the deck could potentially cause a fire, posing a risk to individuals, especially children, who might touch the grill.

incident_description: This product is not weatherproof as it claims to be.  The same day these were placed outside a heavy rain came through and caused 2 of these fixture to blow a circuit and fry the outdoor outlet.  Water had pooled in the base of the lampholder.  Not safe.
justification: Heavy rain caused a circuit to blow and fry the outdoor outlet, posing a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
Charbroil grill2go x200 purchased approximately  May 25 2019 returned to retailer approximately  2 weeks later
2 major problems both concerning the regulator control

1. The grill, on low, would run over 600 degrees with no food inside, no grease fire, all from gas source

2. After weeks of ownership the fuel began bypassing the control valve on the regulator. This led to fuel flowing into the grill with the odor of gas (propane scent) noticeable 30 feet away. This occurred when the grill was turned to lock which is an extension of the off position. Fuel bypassed the control valve into the burner which had not been lit yet and was unattended and assumed off for 15 minutes. All fuel components were checked at for leaks at time of connection and none were detected, meaning the failure occurred after the grill was inspected to be safe within minutes of the failure. After failure fuel was only noticeable as coming from the brass nozzle that is inserted into the burner with the valve confirmed again as still off AND locked.  Valve was never handled with more than ÃÂfingertipÃÂ force and regulator never dropped or subjected to any damaging force since purchased.

3. Charbroil customer service advised of issue and questioned if there was another revision to the regulator.  Was advised that there were 2 revisions. CS advised that they could not trace by manufacture date code nor serial number what revision grill was equipped with when failure occurred.

4. Not wanting another regulator that may have the exact problem, grill was returned for exchange of different model.  Grill was purchased and returned to LoweÃÂs in Port Richey, FL. LoweÃÂs web page for the product shows reviewers making frequent complaints of overheating on low and other regulator related problems. Seemingly these are the only complaints about this product.

5. I am reporting this because I had adverted catastrophe with it is apparently far from isolated
justification: The grill's design flaws, overheating on low and fuel bypassing the control valve, pose a high likelihood of causing a fire or explosion, which could lead to injuries or even death.

incident_description:
Back in 2012 (appx) i received a letter from Kawasaki announcing the recall. I attempted to find a dealer at that time that was willing to perform the recall but no dealer within a 100 mile radius was willing to do the service work or provide a replacement tank so that I could do my own recall. At the time I was not having an issue so I stopped trying to find someone to replace the fuel tank. 
In 2018, the fuel tank began seeping fuel and I discontinued use. In an attempt to repair the recalled fuel tank myself, I tried to purchase a new tank but the tank is discontinued and is no longer available.
What recourse do I have now in an attempt to repair this product?
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident (fuel tank seepage) did occur, and the likelihood of it happening again, given the discontinued tank, is possible.

incident_description: I have a Toro 18" gas trimmer and the rubber stopper on the gas tank that is the fuel line and primer, leaks terribly. Called Toro, and while it's not under a recall, its very dangerous, and I can no longer use the trimmer. Called Toro to see if I can get a replacement (under warranty). They recommended checking their website. They do not offer replacement gas tanks for this trimmer online. Checked with a Toro dealer, and they don't carry parts. I guess this is a throw away machine. Sad because of the money I paid for it. However, it is unsafe, and I'm sure other homeowners face the possibility of a leaking tank as well...fire hazard.
justification: Leaking gas from the trimmer poses a significant fire hazard, although no injuries have been reported.

incident_description: Upon finishing mowing our yard with our cub cadet mower, it backfired and the engine caught on fire. The entire mower erupted in flames within a minute or two. We were unable to extinguish the flames and the mower burned down to its frame. It is a complete loss.   The lawn mower came with a three year warranty and should have been covered, however Mtd products representative requested that we file a claim with our homeowners insurance.   Our deductible is too high, therefore we could not file a claim with our insurance
justification: The mower catching fire and burning down is an incident with no reported injuries, and while it's possible, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
I was using my Honda HRX2175VKA when I must have hit a rock in the yard and I heard a loud crack. There was no damage visible at the time. I recently was changing the oil and sharpening the blade so had the mower on its side and observed that the deck/shroud next to the blade was cracked and had a quarter size hole in it. The rock/object must have been propelled through the deck and caused the hole. 

This struck me as a safety hazard as the integrity of the plastic material had been compromised. As the mower deck has a lifetime warranty, I took the mower first to Home Depot, where it was reviewed and deemed to be damaged by "abuse". I contacted Honda customer service and inquired about the damage being covered under lifetime warranty and if hitting a rock in the yard would be considered abusive use. I was advised to take it to another shop and was also contacted by a senior account specialist who advised he didn't think hitting a rock was abuse. 

I took it in to the shop, had it reviewed, and was told this time that the damage was due to an impact so was wasn't covered by warranty. From this, I am to assume that the Honda plastic deck material is not designed to stop rocks from penetrating and being ejected. My particular rock impact went away from me while mowing. Some other consumer may not be so lucky and will catch a speeding object in the lower extremities or will impact someone further away. 

I believe that the plastic material used by Honda is unsafe and should be recalled and not used again.
justification: While no immediate injury occurred, the potential for future incidents due to compromised mower deck integrity is high.

incident_description: I own a Hustler brand of zero turn mower, a Raptor SD.  The design of the fuel tank is such that once initially filled, after a minute or so, the tank is no longer full to the top as the fuel has migrated to an air pocket at the top of the tank and started filling it.  You can repeat this process one or two times, adding additional fuel and then the tank is actually 100% full.  However, the evaporative emission system employed on this mower will then siphon out a large amount of fuel out of the fuel tank and dump all of this fuel on the floor beneath the mower through the vent on the system.  It is a large amount of fuel.  It is fortunate that I do not have a gas hot water heater in my garage as the fumes from this large amount of fuel would certainly have ignited inside the closed garage. Dumping of the fuel is not readily noticed after filling the tank, but apparently starts some minutes later, after leaving the area.  This needs a design remedy asap before a fire does happen with one of these mowers.
justification: Fuel dumping is likely to occur after refilling, posing a fire risk in enclosed spaces like garages.

incident_description:
Echo PB-265LN Backpack Leaf Blower fuel line detaches from unit when running due to vibration and spills gasoline down my back which can be a fire and personal injury risk.

There is a tube that runs from the gas tank to the bulb pump.  On the 2nd season this tube began detaching.  It is just slid in to each side and is not fastened well and may be cut too short.  It becomes detached when engine is running.  I have fastened with a mini clamp to hold in place but that no longer is holding.

When calling Echo they say there is no recall on the model even though I see a recall for the exact issue on the same model without the L on the end of the model number.  When looking at the pictures it is the same design and issue.
justification: Fuel line detachment while running poses a high risk of personal injury and fire.

incident_description:
CHAR-BROIL OUTDOOR GAS GRILL.  Model # 463446015.  Serial # Upon request.
Does not have adequate bottom deflector to funnel grease from grill to catch pan thereby causing extreme fire within unit.
Have cleaned unit AFTER EACH USE, of any and all possible grease buildup and halfway through the next cooking process, grill again becomes engulfed in flames causing food to be ruined and minor skin burn to hands and forearms.
justification: Injury occurred due to flames engulfing the grill, despite regular cleaning.

incident_description:

While pulling the rope the motor backed fired and pulled the rope backwards causing the injury to the submitters wrist.  Strained wrist.

Submitter believes this product is a safety concern.

incident_description: I was using your blower today here in Northern Cal and it delivered me numerous shocks though my trigger finger. The shocks would only happen when my thumb was used to press the turbo button. They happen every-time I pushed the turbo button. The shocks were mildly strong and the first one forced me to drop the blower but subsequent expected shocks were not strong enough to force me to drop the blower. The weather today was warm, dry and sunny with humidity levels about 20%. My blower is not damaged in any way and is clean/maintained.  I believe you should be aware of this situation.
justification: Repeated electric shocks, though mild, caused injury to the user's finger, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The product is a griller /smoker brand name "char-griller akorn" 
While lifting the lid of the grill while in use, the heavy  lid suddenly separated from the grill body and fell to the ground. This caused my forearm to contact the hot grill surface.
justification: The lid suddenly separated, causing contact with the hot grill surface, resulting in an injury.

incident_description: I was blowing leaves off our wooden deck and left the blower outside. Our neighbor noticed the deck was on fire at 1am and called 911 and woke us up.  The fire dept determined the fire was caused by the leaf blower.   The damage was extensive and we are fortunate the neighbor saw it or it would have burned our home as well.
justification: The fire was caused by a common household item left unattended, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Safety Issue
I purchased 2 Bell Outdoor portable metal spike lights SL101B from Home Depot. I accidentally GOT SHOCKED as soon as I touched one of those lights when it was wet. 
It might be affected by irrigation and water dripped inside.
For safety concern, I tried to look it up on UL website and see if it is a listed safety products. Unfortunately the website does not show any information about this specific item, neither the product itself has UL control number. 
In my opinion, this may be a fake UL certified product that and must be spotted by CPSC and retailers.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (shock) and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the product's lack of UL certification and the consumer's exposure to water.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting the unit for posing a fire hazard.

She turned on all four burners and placed the food on the grill. A few minutes later, the second burner from the left side fell onto the ash tray and the fire continued to emit from the burner. She immediately turned the four burner knobs to the "Off" position and shut off the gas tank valve. 
She said the fire stopped a few minutes later. 

She indicated that the burner box eroded and this allowed the burner to fall onto the ash tray. The ash tray sits right above the gas tank and she is concerned that another incident could lead to a huge fire or explosion. 

She believes the unit is defective and the parts should not erode after 2 years. She indicated that the unit has been used about 30 times. 

She contacted the firm (800-549-4505) to report the incident but she was told that she had to contact another department to report the matter because they could not assist. She was repeatedly referred to different departments and each Rep. that she spoke to gave her another number to call because they could not assist. She was provided the following numbers:
(800-469-4663) (800-697-3277) (800-349-4358) (800-659-7026)
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard with potential for serious harm, making it likely to recur given the defective unit.

incident_description: I engaged the blades on my Craftsman Pro 26 HP 54" Desk Garden Tractor (Model 917986451) and a blade shot out form under the mowing deck and across the street.  No one was injured.  Upon inspection, the Easy Blade assembly failed.
justification: While no one was injured, the incident involved a blade shooting out from under the mowing deck, posing a potential hazard.

incident_description:
Went out to grill lunch.  My Weber grill would not ignite I went to open the door and reached my hand to check The tank and flames shot out at me.  I donÃÂt remember much after that. My left side of my face and arm were burned. The ER said I was lucky that I was so quick to get away from the flames. 

I must note that I contacted Weber a few times in the past two years about issues with the igniter. There must be something up with it. Please look into this. I do not want someone else to be injured.

incident_description:
(05/25/2019) The consumer stated that he had been using the product for about 30-40 minutes, when it blew up. An object blew out of the housing and hit the consumer on his hip causing lacerations.

No medical attention was required.
justification: Injury occurred but no medical attention was required, indicating a possible occurrence.

incident_description: I was using my electric Makita chainsaw to trim some trees and discovered that I was unable to turn off the saw. I was not injured, but it continues to turn on automatically upon being plugged in. I am only able to turn it off by removing it from the power source and feel that this poses an inherent risk to the user.
justification: The chainsaw's automatic on feature poses a risk of unintended operation, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description: My D155 John Deere caught on fire in my Garage at 3:30 am it destroyed my home while we were sleeping in the home on May 18,2019. Whom do I get answers for this issue
justification: Fire destroyed the home while occupants were sleeping, resulting in potential loss of life.

incident_description: A local citizen stopped by one of our fire stations with this product to let us know that it had "exploded" and caught a near by bush on fire. One of our on-duty Captains took a few pictures (attached) to document the concern. It appears that the solar battery overheated and ruptured causing the nearby vegetation to catch fire.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burnt bush) but no injuries, and while it's possible for solar batteries to overheat, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: I was mowing a lawn using the Hustler Super Z mower with at Kawasaki FXT00V-CS08-R motor on it and the motor began to shoot flames out of the exhaust and the engine caught on fire and under the exhaust the rubber wheel on the mower was engulfed with flames as well at the same time. justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a fire on a lawn mower, which could have escalated if not quickly extinguished.

incident_description:
