The propane leaks from the regulator and fire comes out where the regulator connects to the stove.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the propane leak and fire from the regulator pose a potential risk of injury.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his spouse experienced similar problem of  recall [REDACTED] with the leaf blower. Hazard: The plastic fan inside the electrical blowers can break, causing the fan blades to be discharged from either end of the blower tube. This poses a laceration hazard.

He stated that his spouse was using the unit when the incident occurred, the broken fan blades discharged causing her to received bruises on upper right leg, no medical attention was received.
The company was contacted and he was advised that they would pick up the blower and provide a replacement which he feels that might be covering up the evidence.  He is concerned that the company is aware of the problem but not addressing the safety of the product.
justification: Injury occurred due to fan blades being discharged, and similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description:
There is, in my opinion, a strong risk of personal injury using a Havahart model 1085animal trap.


 Shame on me for trusting this Havahart trap. They have been in business for years. They had a good reputation until now. The trap consists of 3 different size holes: 1x7/8, 1/2x7/8, AND a 1x2. Now there are 2 columns of the later size running down each side right below the handle on top. Note the attached picture of my latest capture. It was able to extend its reach for 6". There is a trough dug out of the dirt along the bottom corner. Would you really want to put this on your deck? Grass would eventually recover in a week or so. Concrete would be best. Unfortunately, I don't have any.
   But wait that's not all. I don't kill the critter. I figure he's just trying to make a living like the rest of us. I take them on a 4-5 mile trip to release.
 So this trap probably weighs about 10 pounds. Say the coon weighs 20-25 pounds. Since the geniuses place the largest openings right below the handle, one then has to hold the 30-35 pounds straight out from your side,  don't forget it has at least a 6" reach. Walk that way for 75 feet, then lift it up int your vehicle. I do have to get back to the gym.
  One more dandy little tidbit is they advertise proudly how there are no sharp edges inside the trap so it's safe for the animal. My question is what about my leg?
justification: The trap's design, with large openings near the handle, increases the risk of user injury when handling a trapped animal.

incident_description:
Ryobi battery  Jet Fan Blowers 
Hazard: The plastic fan inside the blower broke causing the fan blades to be discharged from either end of the blower tube, posing a laceration hazard. This shot shards of heavy plastic out the end when it exploded  this is the same as the recall already on other products they sell.Recall Number: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration hazard due to the discharge of fan blades, indicating a potential for injury.

incident_description:
One of the two blades on my Toro Timemaster lawn mower snapped in half during routine lawn mowing. Replaced both blades with new blades purchased at the dealer where I purchased the mower, and within two weeks one of the new blades snapped in half during routine lawn mowing. 

I notice there was a recall back in 2013 for this very same issue (recall #14-046), and I don't ever recall my dealer telling me they fixed the issue during yearly service of my mower. Apparently not because two blades have broken on the mower in the last two weeks.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the repeated blade failure indicates a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: While trying to park a 2019 bad boy 42 inch mower on my patio.Because speed,brake ,forward,reverse is controlled by two hand held levers.Accidentally tapping one lever forward caused mower to jump forward and destroy an aluminum awning support. These mowers should be required to have a separate foot brake and  speed control for the transmission.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an accident happening is possible given the mower's control design.

incident_description:
I was blowing leaves off the paved driveway and my electric Troy Bilt leaf blower exploded. The leaf blower was less than one year old. It suddenly exploded with a deafening explosion  It blew off a piece of plastic housing that we have been unable to find. Also, the internal propeller blew out. (See photo).  
I researched online to find answers to why this happened and found this news item from 2013 in Houston describing the identical incident.  It was fortunate that I was not hit by the projectile as was the woman in this news item.

Had I not found this news item I would have thrown the blower away and bought a new gas blower instead. However, now I realize this is is a faulty design of the Troy Bilt leaf blower and want to protect future consumers of this product. 


https://www.click2houston.com/consumer/leaf-blower-explodes-in-houston-womans-hand_20151124024147709
justification: Although no injuries occurred this time, the identical incident in 2013 resulted in a woman being hit by a projectile, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: On 5/22/2019 I was preparing to mow our lawn with our Craftsman Pro Lawn Tractor (model # 917986451, made by [REDACTED]).  As I engaged the blades, one of the the Easy Blade holders (Part #580954003) failed, resulting in one of the mower blades being thrown from under the mower, landing about 25 feet from the machine.  The mower has been used multiple times this spring and showed no signs of an issue - the incident happened without warning.  There were no injuries.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a mower blade being thrown, posing a potential hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: Masterbuilt smoker serial #AD111411 started on fire. Hose connecting to smoker temperature know came off/melted off causing fire. The was second time using the product.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case. The likelihood is 'possible' as it happened twice with the same product.

incident_description: Using the Chicago 14" chain saw and the saw would not stop running even after releasing the ON trigger.  Had to unplug the chainsaw to make it stop.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury but could have led to one if the saw couldn't be stopped.

incident_description:
My Toro Time-master 30 inch mower started to vibrate, shake and broke one of the mower blades.
 I undid the plastic cover and found out the gear that drives the blade had become out of shape and slipped on it's shaft causing the blades to go out of time and collide.
justification: The mower blade broke, causing the mower to malfunction but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the riding mower is emitting overwhelming fumes that gets all over the user.  She stated that after using she has to shower to rid herself of the toxic fumes.  This problem has been ongoing since purchase. She believes she is inhaling CO which is poisonous. 

The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised to contact the dealer since the unit was under warranty, the dealer advised her that they contacted the company for instructions on fixing the problem but they were not given any, however, they are working to find a solution.   She contacted the manufacturer again and they advised of what the dealer had related to her, they informed her that there was nothing they could do for her.
justification: The incident has been ongoing since purchase, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
This report is for a 2011 Husqvarna LGT24K54-24047 riding lawn mower. This mower has a plastic 4 gallon gas tank which is cracking and leaking. The tank is clearly disintegrating and the mower  cannot be used. Husqvarna, per my phone call with their customer service line today 04/29/2019, was pleasant but unwilling to offer any assistance. 

This is a serious safety hazard for anyone filling or starting this tractor. Any source of ignition would result in a probable injury.

The part number for this gas tank has been changed twice, indicating to me that Husqvarna is aware at some level that they have knowledge that this is a failed and defective product.

Husqvarna should recall and repair the tractors effected.
justification: Leaking gas tank poses a high likelihood of injury due to potential ignition sources.

incident_description: My Char-Broil outdoor propane gas grill caught fire due to a defect in design and materials. There is a metal plated attached to the bottom of the firebox (in which the burners are placed). That plate is made of thin metal and is not removable for cleaning. Most drippings flow to the center into an opening and to a can that can be attached for catching grease. The metal plate corroded and formed a circular hole allowing grease to flow onto the PROPANE TANK and exterior grill base and floor. EVEN WITH REGULAR CLEANING THAT GREASE CANNOT BE REMOVED. IT CAUGHT FIRE - AND COULD HAVE INJURED ME AND EXPLODED THE PROPANE TANK. I EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE AND WAS ABLE TO PREVENT A DISASTER.
justification: The grill's design flaw, allowing grease to accumulate and ignite, poses a high likelihood of reoccurrence despite regular cleaning.

incident_description:

After examining the grill grates I discovered they were de-laminating, the metal shards ranged in size from very small to very large. If these shards were to be ingested it could pose a serious health issue. Your attention in this matter will be greatly appreciated. Thank you, [REDACTED] 

PS. I can provide pictures 
or some actual shards if requested.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that a couple of times now his wife has received shocks when she turns on their leaf blower. The consumerÃÂs wife turns the unit off when this happens so they are not aware of the shocks are persistent while the leaf blower is in use.

The consumer notes that they have tried various cords on the unit but it does not fix the problem.

The consumer plans on keeping his unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the persistent shocks pose a risk of injury, making it an incident with potential harm.

incident_description:
Purchased a chainsaw from a manufacturer thru Alibaba.  Aside from not working the chainsaw did not have a chain brake or noise reduction:

Title 29 of the Code of Federal
Regulations


1910.266(e)(1)(ii)(E)
Chain brakes and nose shielding devices, to assure that they are in place and function properly;

More detailed info:
1910.266(e)(2)(i)
Each chain saw placed into initial service after the effective date of this section shall be equipped with a chain brake and shall otherwise meet the requirements of the ANSI B175.1-1991 "Safety Requirements for Gasoline-Powered Chain Saws", which is incorporated by reference as specified in Sec. 1910.6. Each chain saw placed into service before the effective date of this section shall be equipped with a protective device that minimizes chain-saw kickback. No chain-saw kickback device shall be removed or otherwise disabled.
justification: The chainsaw lacked a chain brake and noise reduction, violating CFR Title 29, increasing likelihood of injury.

incident_description: STOK Quattro gas grill caught fire shortly after being lit to cook and almost burned the house down. Fire appeared to be coming from underneath and completely engulfed the entire unit.
justification: The grill caught fire shortly after use, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence, and while no injuries were reported, the incident could have caused significant property damage.

incident_description:
Purchased a now discontinued product from a Sears Outlet, an All Power snow blower, manufactured, I think, by JDNA products Model no. APSB 055E , 21-inch 196cc, 4-stroke. I didn't have a use for it the first winter because we didn't have that much snow.

Would like refund of money I paid to Sears, and product removed from my home.
justification: The product is discontinued and poses a fire hazard, making it likely that it could cause an incident.

incident_description: On 2 occasions in 2018 and 1 in 2019 my Charbroil Tru Infrared model 463335115 had blown up in my face. It appears that the grilling surface has small slits to allow grease to drain through and after a couple of uses those slits get clogged up, then the propane gas collects underneath the grilling surface so when you push the igniter the grill explodes. The only way to clean the burnt on grease is to use a drill and a wire wheel to unclog the slits/holes and the grill stays unclogged for only a couple of uses.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (face burns) due to the grill exploding, and it has occurred multiple times (2018 and 2019) with the same model.

incident_description:
In March of 2017 I purchased a barbecue cover from Kmart (Kenmore Elite - # 40339). I had purchased their product in the past and it did not last very long so I bought the most durable one they had. I did not use my grill more than 2 or 3 times in 2017 and 2 or 3 more times in 2018. The last time I removed the cover I noticed that it emitted a cloud of dust. Just recently I noticed that there was a tear in one of the corners - probably from the wind. Since the cover had a warranty of 5 years, I went to take photos of the tear for purposes of getting a refund. After taking the photos (attached) I noticed that my fingers were covered in a white powder / dust which concerned me. I then located the box which stated that the cover was made from polyester which is a plastic and coated with PVC (polyvinyl chloride) which is another form of plastic. I than went online to research and learn if PVC was toxic (I try to refrain from buying products made in China whenever possible - they paint our children's toys with lead based paint and put anti-freeze in our toothpaste).

It didn't take long to find out that PVC is indeed very toxic. 

After a little over a year of slight use, this product began to decompose emitting a poisonous dust. I do not want to breath it in - I don't want it on my cloths and I definitely don't want it anywhere near my food. When I tried to contact Kenmoore (several times - 866-872-7442 - the # on the box the cover came in) no one answered and no returned my call for several weeks. When someone finally did get back to me she said that she could not issue me a refund and that she was only authorized to send me a replacement. I explained to her that the cover was made out of a toxic material and I did not want a similar one that was destined to decompose and emit a poisonous dust just as the one I already have. This is a bad product and never should have been put on the market to begin with. Please help me get my money back so that I can purchase a BBQ cover that won't kill me - and this product should be taken off the market asap.
justification: While no immediate harm was reported, the incident highlights a potential health risk due to the toxic decomposition of the product.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting the unit for posing an injury hazard. He indicated that the unit does not shut off when the hand lever is released.

He used the unit to plow snow from his driveway and when he released the hand lever the impeller did not stop. He indicated that the unit is supposed to shut off when the hand lever is released. The unit continued to move on its own down the driveway. He said he was able to stop it before it could injure a person. 

He contacted the firm and reported the incident. He was told to take the unit to a local repair dealer for inspection but he hasnÃÂt been able to because of the weather. 

He indicated that this was his third time using the unit. Now every time he turns the unit on the unit keeps running after the hand lever is released and he has concerns with using it.
justification: The unit's failure to shut off when the hand lever is released poses a significant risk of injury.

incident_description: Hello I bought a gasoline powered post hole digger from [REDACTED] item number 6062 250 they say to store it with gasoline in the tank and following their directions  with the gas additive in it. I soon found out that if you do this the gas tank will explode because of improper venting of the tank. If it wouldÃÂve done this while running it wouldÃÂve been a huge fireball. The fuel tank of this model should be recalled or taken off the market I have tried to contact them and so far they have not gotten back to me and it has been months.
justification: The incident did not result in injury, but the likelihood of an explosion is high due to improper venting of the gas tank.

incident_description: I have a Cooper solar light that started a fire on my house during the night. This happened on the early morning hours of 2/10/19. I bought the light from Home Depot about one year ago. I own two of the lights and have since removed both. I have pictures of the damages.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in property damage, making it a level 2 severity. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 'possible' given that the product was used as intended and the incident happened once.

incident_description:
(11/07/2018) The consumer stated that there is a design issuer with the product. The bolt that holds the hydraulic cylinder and the splitting wedge bent and broke, which is a safety concern. The consumer stated that the same thing happened about a week ago.

(11/07/2018) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that there is a replacement part that he can get at a cost to him. He was also advised that the issue has been know to the firm since 2004.
justification: The incident has occurred before, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
We just purchased a gas fire pit, model FW-R32TMFP on 10/31/18.  When I inspected it for leaks before use, I noticed that the white heat shield (on the underside, below the lava rocks) had a crack in it.  I contacted the manufacturer, Foremost Groups, Inc, of East Hanover NJ, and they agreed to send out a replacement fire pit.  

On 12/22/18, we used the new fire pit for the first time.  Within a few minutes of use, we heard a loud pop.  When I inspected the unit the next morning, I observed a crack in the heat shield, similar to on the first unit.

I'm concerned that this unit is unsafe as 2 in a row have had cracked heat shields.
justification: Two consecutive units from the same manufacturer exhibited the same defect, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and potential safety hazard.

incident_description: I have a recalled snow thrower.  Model #DB7659-22. I would like the repair kit and instructions to install.    My unit does not throw snow  the auger seems to not spin fast enough to throw snow and clogs.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning snow thrower, which could potentially cause injury if not handled properly, but no immediate harm has been reported.

incident_description:
My John Deere riding lawnmower caught fire a couple of minutes after it was turned off and completely burned up.
The engine had approximately 90 hours on it. I used it for about 45 minutes before taking a break. I contacted John
Deere and sent them pictures of the burned up mower. The John Deere legal team responded by contending it was
up to me to hire someone to prove it was their fault.
Fortunately I had parked the mower in my driveway. If I had parked it in my garage it probably would have resulted
in a major house fire.
I don't understand why a product "fire" is being treated as a trivial incident
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in a major house fire if the mower was parked in the garage instead of the driveway.

incident_description: We bought a John Deere D105 from Lowe's.  It has blown off the spring cover for the transmission three times, causing the mower to not move.  The metal part flies out and could injure anyone standing near the mower or in the line of where it explodes off to.
justification: The incident has occurred multiple times, with a metal part flying off, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: On Feb. 12, 2019 my 78 year old mother went into her garage, plugged in a Weed Eater brand electric leaf blower to blow the driveway off. She plugged the unit in, turned on the power switch on the leaf blower and it literally exploded in her hands causing lacerations and trauma to her right hand. She quickly went to her doctor who referred her to have x rays done at a nearby imaging facility. The doctor thought the hand could be broken due to the extent of the swelling and bruising. My mother followed all the safety precautions. The unit is stored in a dry, closed indoor storage room off the garage when not in use. She was not using an extension cord or anything out of the ordinary. The fan wheel of the blower burst through the side of the blower, shattering the plastic motor housing. The fan blade struck my mother in the hand causing bruising bleeding and swelling.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (lacerations, trauma, bruising, and swelling) but no death, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the age of the equipment and lack of maintenance history.

incident_description: Reflection Isles Community automatic electric gateway struck multiple vehicles. Gate way is apparently SB325 non-compliant. Posted on transponder receiver is notice of possible malfunction due to radio or microwave interference.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible due to the non-compliant gate and potential interference.

incident_description:
Fuel leaks from the carburetor throat and drips on the floor when it is not running. Diagnosed as the float needle not sealing so I purchased a carburetor overhaul kit and replaced all the seals and gaskets, as well as the float and float needle. Fuel is still leaking, the float needle and the needle seat are in perfect condition (examined both with a 10x magnifier). The float needle that had been removed was also in serviceable condition, the needle seat is not replaceable but looks perfect.

The carburetor float and the float needle are moving freely, no binding or problems.

I contacted the manufacturer and because this model was not under recall they determined it was not their problem. It is no longer under warranty as it was purchased in late 2016 by the original owner, used that winter then stored properly (fuel drained and oil was changed) before the owner passed away. If the defect was noticed before I cannot ask, the widow (wife's cousin) was not using it and gave it to us.
justification: Fuel leak, though not causing injury, poses a fire hazard and could lead to property damage.

incident_description: I received this unit as a gift. ("Yankee Swap"@ work, unknown giver, no receipt) On 1st use, the unit made a sharp "crack" type noise, but continued to work. It was then noticed that the base of this device had bubbled up, and a burnt odor was noticed .This unit is a GRANITE brand  small panini press, Model# YD205, ITEM # GKA-CG100 . Made in China.  I promptly disposed of this unit.  I did take 3 photos of this unit, and the damage to it.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to the bubbling base and burnt odor, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I had purchased a King Pellet Stove in September or 2018, at Tractor Supply Co, the stove was installed in October of 2018 oer manufacturers instructions using the recommended ventilation kit purchased also at Tractor Supply.
Upon initial start of the unit , it had what was expected as a "burn in" period where you could expect  the burn off smell of a paint etc in a new heating product.
However, this unit shut down and failed to eject the smoke contained in the unit and smoke emitted into the basement area of my home. Also the unit burned extremely dirty leaving large deposits of unburned pellets and residue.
I also explained the unit was feeding pellets too fast,
I had made a call the following business day to the customer service number provided in the owners manual. I had an extremely hard time talking to a representative, and you do not know if you are actually talking to a technical agent or not, after spending hours both calling and texting messages. These issues were brought up in a BBB complaint, filed in November 2018.
Customer service personnel instructed me to make adjustments on the control panel, the unit (once I got a hold of one, and would not tell me if they were "technical" support or customer) in which resulted in the unit again burning off excess smoke filling my basement again with smoke, again many calls made back and once someone got back to me I explained the issues, not burning correctly( sent them pictures and videos of what was happening and the installation, also feeding too many pellets, again they gave me adjustment to make and finally it got to where the unit just filled and over filled the pellet bowl and would not light, and the one time it did an extremely large fire inside with all the pellets and I shutdown unit,
In the mean time the customer service representative stated they would first send me a new blower unit, now this is brand new barely 3 bags of pellets through it, and another stated they would send an ignition card, both times I explained how would I know how to install these, and they said to you-tube it!
I reminded them that in their instruction manual it specifically states to NEVER try to repair or replace any parts of the stove unless instructions for doing so are in the manual, in which  they are not.
This is stated twice in the manual, first page and page 17., thus contradicting their safety instructions.
I reached an exchange agreement with Tractor Supply since I was outside their 30 day return policy as well as filing a BBB complaint against the company which they said they would send me 300.00 for my trouble, in which they never did, again it smoked my house twice, and I had to pay for an install and uninstall, and another install!
Also my local Tractor supply stated they had several of the same units exchanged for the same reasons!
Representative did not respond to my question after that and have not responded to my calls or text.
justification: The incident resulted in smoke emission into the home, causing discomfort and potential health risks, but no physical injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This caller purchased rat traps around June 25th or June 26th, 2018 from retailer in [REDACTED] then came home and began setting them the next day.
One of them snapped right after he set it and when he inspected it he saw that the staples were not set deeply enough for it to work properly.
He set another trap that snapped while he was setting it and just missed his head as it went flying past it.
He is reporting these traps as a severe injury hazard and would ask that CPSC inspect and recall them.
There are no injuries being reported 
He reported these incidents to the manufacturer who is sending him three more rat traps.
He states that the store where he purchased his has seven more of these defective traps and that other stores are also selling them which could result in someone being severely injured and he is asking that the stores become notified and told to remove them from the shelves.

Caller asked that a note be placed advising that ACE Distributing should be contacted immediately and advised to inspect then remove any of these rat traps still on the shelves.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved multiple traps snapping unexpectedly, posing a high likelihood of injury to the user or others.

incident_description: On my last use the one of wheels that holds belt totally blew in 2 pieces and was not even three months old
justification: The wheel breaking into pieces could have caused injury but did not, and the likelihood of such an event happening again is possible.

incident_description:
I purchased a Poulan Pro PR4218 18-inch gas chainsaw on 12/9/2017.  I used the device on 12/10/2017.  The second time I used the device was on 8/11/2018.   The chainsaw's SKU number is 967063901.  The Serial# is 17262N501386-1.  The second time I used it, I noticed that the chain turns at idle with the blade brake engaged and without a hand on the trigger.

I made Husqvarna aware of this safety issue.  They asked me to send the chainsaw to their facility in Charlotte, NC, which I did.  They claim that the chainsaw is malfunctioning due to operator error.  They are claiming that I used the chainsaw at full throtle with the blade brake engaged.  In fact, I don't believe that it is even possible.  If it is then the product is extremely dangerous and should be recalled.  The owner's manual for the Poulan Pro PR3816 / PR4218  states that is designed according to ANSI standard B175.1-2012.  I dispute their evaluation that I used the chainsaw incorrectly.  I'm convinced it is dangerous.  They offered to send me a reconditioned chainsaw with no warranty.  I refused their offer, and am still working towards a resolution.  I asked them to return the chainsaw to me, or destroy it.  I am concerned about this safety issue, and don't want the chainsaw refurbished and resold to an unsuspecting consumer.

Please do not hesitate to contact me at [REDACTED]  if you need any additional information.
justification: Potential injury due to unexpected chain movement, as the chainsaw's blade brake engaged without the trigger being pressed.

incident_description:
Philips Indoor Smoke-less Grill plus Bonus Cleaning Tool, HD6371/98 is sold by amazon.com and manufactured by Philips. I purchased one here: [REDACTED]

This product comes with a bonus item: cleaning tool, which is a sharp knife to scrape the barbecue griddle. This knife is not covered and is simply taped to the product on the inside with the blade completely exposed. While putting my hand in the retail box the knife went right through my finger. This knife cannot be seen from the outside and consumers have no way of knowing.
justification: Exposed blade of the cleaning tool caused injury upon first contact, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
We had a light snow today and I took out my Toro electric leaf blower model 51586 to clear the snow off of my car.  I've done this many times and it works great.  I plugged it in, turned it on and second later it violently exploded with a very loud bang.  The impeller came apart and ripped through the blower housing.  Parts of the housing and impeller hit me in the chest and face.  Fortunately I was wearing a ski mask, winter coat and glasses and was not injured.  

I had purchased the blower from Home Depot around 2001.  I was not aware this model had been recalled in 2007.  The potential for injury in this type of product failure is very high and I feel that Toro should have done more to alert customers of the recall. The recall section on their web site does not list this recall.
justification: Although no injuries occurred this time, the violent explosion and potential for injury make this a serious incident.

incident_description:
The Hitachi leaf blower was being used following instructions.  The first step is to prime the unit.  Upon priming the unit, fuel began to gush out of the gas tank, covering various items nearby - the floor, clothes, etc.

Had an attempt been made to start the unit, the sparks may have ignited the leaking fuel.

Reaching out to the corporation, along with additional research, seems to yield that this is a common problem and design flaw.
justification: Fuel gushing out of the tank could have easily ignited if the unit was started, posing a significant fire risk.

incident_description:
I went to start my 2016 electric start Toro Snowmaster 824 QXE Snow Thrower for the first time this winter.  It did not start on the first try so I pushed the primer button again before pressing the starter.  When I pressed the starter flames shot out in the carburetor are and continued burning. I had to move the machine away from the garage and tried to snuff out the flames with snow.  I was finally able to get the flames out after 5 minutes or more and after parts of the ignition area were melted.

Last winter when I put gas in it for winter the gas all leaked out.  The dealer took it in for service but said they could not find anything wrong.  It worked okay for the rest of the winter.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage or injury due to the fire.

incident_description:
Ryobi 18v blower fan exploded sending parts flying out. Son was hit but not injured.
Model P2108 from Home Depot 
SN EU16284D150565
justification: Although an incident occurred with the blower fan exploding, no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I bought three solar rechargeable lanterns through an ff from Science Of Skill website and one didn't work at all but the one that concerns me is the one I had plugged in to charge, it blew up. The whole top blew off of it and the battery blew apart throwing a black sooty material all around the lantern. When I reported this to Steel River (the company that has their logo on the lantern) they told me that I had already received a refund from Science Of Skill company but they didn't address the dangers of their product, So I thought it would be best to report it to you so others know of the hazards this product can produce
justification: The incident resulted in property damage and potential injury, as the lantern exploded and scattered sooty material.

incident_description: My electric leaf blower exploded in use. Plastic pieces hit my leg. I was wearing sweatpants and was punctured and bruised by the sharp plastic. I went to the manufacturer's website and found this product has been recalled. I was not aware of the recall as I had moved during that time.
justification: Injury occurred due to recalled product's malfunction, likelihood is possible given the product's history.

incident_description: While driving my 2013 John Deere, D-105, the transmission failed as I was transitioning from the road to my lawn, causing me to be in the middle of the road without the ability to move.  Fortunately there was no traffic at the time, and I was able to push the mower off to the side until the equipment could be diagnosed and repaired.   I believe the transmission issue to be a bad design and consistent with other D-105 transmission recalls.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the mower's transmission failure caused a road hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting the unit for posing a laceration hazard. 

While he used the unit the mulch blade shattered and metal pieces flew everywhere. He had been using the unit for approximately 30 minutes, prior to the incident. He was not injured but fears he could have been and believes the unit should be recalled. 

He took the unit apart and examined it. He believes the blade broke in half and he found holes on the exterior of the housing. He indicated that the motor still runs.

He contacted the retailer's customer service and informed them of the incident. He was told that his unit is not recalled and they no longer offer parts for the unit.

The submitter purchased the unit used about three weeks ago and he said he has used it for about 30 - 40 hours. 

He said he cleaned the engine after he purchased the unit. He said the reseller used the unit a handful of times.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a laceration hazard due to a shattered blade, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Severity Level 2). The likelihood is 'Possible' (Likelihood 3) as the unit had been used for a significant duration (30-40 hours) before the incident, indicating a potential design flaw.

incident_description: Ariens Platinum 30 snow blower, model 921029, leaks gasoline when the fuel valve is turned on.  Possible fire hazard.  The snow blower is about 4 years old.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to gasoline leak, but no immediate injury reported.

incident_description:
This product is a replacement carburetor for a riding mower with an 18.5 HP [REDACTED] engine. It is advertised as a "Nikki" brand carburetor, as is the OEM item. Upon installation, the engine started and ran fine for a short time, then the engine died, and refused to restart. The battery died, so I left the mower for the day and charged the battery. Upon returning the next day, gasoline was seen to be dripping from the muffler of the engine, and the entire contents of the fuel tank had been drained. The oil dipstick indicated higher than normal levels of liquid in the crankcase. Several days passed and I again filled the fuel tank, and fuel began to drip from the carburetor itself. 

This is the URL for the item and seller it was purchased from: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B074KDKM7Z/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1
justification: Fuel leakage and engine failure indicate a high likelihood of future incidents, but no injuries reported.

incident_description: After replacing the propane gas tank, I turned it on, using all the burners to heat it up and clean it before my wife had her cub scout group cook on it.  I went inside the house for about 5 minutes to get the grill cleaner and when I came back out I saw fire under the far right burner knob.  I immediately turned off the supply and then the burners.  I then noticed the far right burner handle was on the ground.  I picked it up... it was hot and it had partially melted.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the partial melting of the burner handle indicates a potential hazard.

incident_description:
The New Flexon hose when used (October 17 & 18 2018) at 7 am & again at 7pm for 70 minutes, attached to water
supply (drinking water supply for our condo) on a recently seeded lawn (seeded on Sept 15 2018, killed the new
grass in the same location as the water was sprinkled. Please note using this hose to water the lawn for 2 days, the
lawn showed definite signs of some sort of burning. We suspect the hose because that was the only physical
method that distributed the burned pattern on the new grass. We have complained to Amazon and they have sent
us a new hose which we have not used. Inspecting this hose by smell one can detect a very high degree of some
sort of chemical residue emitting from the hose. We have discontinued using the Flexon hose. Note that we live
adjacent to the [REDACTED] river in [REDACTED] and using this hose we now have inadvertently polluted the
ground next to the river. We feel Flexon if it is found that the Flexon hose was the cause of the contamination, that
they should be held responsible to clean up and repair the damage.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to the lawn and potential river pollution, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Troy-Bilt Pony Lawn Tractor. 42ÃÂ deck 15.5 hp
We purchased the Troy-Bilt Pony from LoweÃÂs in April, 2014. In September 2018 two of the 3 seat adjustment knobs fell off unbeknownst to us until the next time I went to use the mower. One of the plastic pieces into which the knob is screwed went up into the seat itself. 
I sat on the seat and applied the brake before turning the key. The seat swiveled around. While turning the steering wheel or applying the brake the seat would swivel. If the remaining one knob had fallen off while I was mowing I could have lost control of the mower causing a crash and injury to myself. I could have fallen off the mower also. Who knows what would have happened if I had fallen off with the seat. If the two knobs that did fall out had done so while I was mowing I could have lost control at that time. If my husband had not been able to repair the seat by getting the plastic screw piece back into the seat (not as easy thing to do) and buying new seat adjustment knobs at a local hardware store we would be unsafe using this mower. I feel this mower should be recalled before someone is seriously injured. Thank you.
justification: The incident could have resulted in injury or loss of control of the mower, as the seat adjustment knobs falling off made the seat unstable while in use.

incident_description:
I was mowing my lawn with a Kobal KM2040X-06 electric lawnmower. The mower was operating loudly for a bit, and then began to smoke. I shut the mower off and turned it over to find two spots within the unit from which smoke was emanating. I discontinued use of mower.

Note that the mower has had issues over the summer with increased noise - it will randomly increase in volume, as though something is wrong, and then quiet back down to the expected noise level after a few minutes. This appears randomly - it is not associated with areas of mowing that are difficult, or strenuous, to the unit. The mower has not emitted smoke prior to this incident.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the mower emitting smoke indicates a malfunction that could escalate to more severe issues, making it an incident but not yet at a severe level.

incident_description: I have a problem in bending over, I was using this device to pick up my shoes of the floor. when I attempted to take the shoes out with my hand, the spring end sliced my knuckle on my left hand. I have two devices just like this one and they are not sharp. This one I just bought last week, the metal is sharp on the edges. It appears to have been stamped out and not smoothed down, the edges are like Knife Blades !
justification: Sharp edges on the new device caused a knuckle cut, making injury likely in future use.

incident_description: I had been using the blower for about 15 minutes clearing my driveway of acorns.  I turned blower off and moved under my house (it is built up one story on pilings) to blow off some leaves from the parking area.  I then turned blower back on and turned power up to full blast.  About two seconds after doing this the blower exploded.  The fan/impeller blade disintegrated and blew out the right rear (the five o'clock position) of the casing.  Parts of the red casing and gray blade were blown some thirty feet away.  Fortunately I was holding the blower with my right hand as I was turning the power up and the force of the blast missed hitting me.  But if I had had the blower in my left hand (as I often do when using it) I would have been hit in the groin area and upper leg and would have suffered very serious injuries.  My wife was about twenty feet away from me when this happened and a piece of the casing just missed her.  If one of my small grandchildren had been present he might well have been hit in the face.  This blower is only about three years old.  It is used about ten times a year at my home.  It was not used in any commercial manner.  I was very lucky not to have suffered any physical injury but someone else could get really get hurt.  (Obviously, I'm pretty shook up!)
justification: The blower's explosion could have caused serious injuries, as demonstrated by the force of the blast and the distance debris was propelled.

incident_description: I had purchased a perfect flame model gcs3318 bbq at Costco and have only used it a few times a year tonight I was cooking a tri tip roast and the bbq caught fire, melted parts of the bbq the utensils in the drawer and dripped melted metal on my porch. It took awhile to get out I finally got the propane tank disconnected from the burning gas grill and got the fire out. This bbq has been thouroughly cleaned after each use and did not have build up or anything in it. It was so scary and dangerous I had my grandchildren here who are all toddlers and could not believe this happened. I had the bbq on Medium heat and had been keeping an eye on it. I donÃÂt understand how this could have happened
justification: Injury could have occurred due to the intense fire and melted metal, and it was possible given the presence of toddlers.

incident_description:
I purchased a battery operated strobe light from Walmart.  It is made by Gemmy Industries Corp.  Identification numbers on the product are, #64085 & SW0418.  It says "batch-sw001, Xiamen, China.

The product comes with batteries, three of them, already installed.  I turned the light on and put it in our upstairs attic window.  It ran for a day or more until the batteries ran out.  

I changed the batteries, two on one side, and one on the other, following the indicated "+" and "-" signs.  It did not seem to work well, so I decided to put different batteries in.  All batteries were brand new.  The first battery installed, on the "two-battery" side was so hot, I could not hold it.  This happened in only about 3 to 5 minutes.

Since these were cheap batteries from the Dollar Store, I decided to buy Energizer batteries and try again.  The same thing happened.  The first battery on the "two-battery" side became very hot in the first sixty seconds, too hot to hold.  

I feel this is a dangerous product that many may not know about.  I don't know why the original batteries, already installed did not react this way.

NOTE:  I was "extremely" careful to follow the "+" and "-" signs when installing the batteries.
justification: Batteries overheated and became too hot to hold within minutes, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I was storing my Cub Cadet lawn mower in the garage and noticed that there was a bad smell of gas throughout the garage. After investigation, I noticed that it was coming from the underside of the gas tank around a gasket that had broken down on my Cub Cadet zero turn s48 lawn mower.
I found a recall (11-733) on the same model between January and March of 2011. When I called the manufacturer, they said that my mower was made before those dates and therefore the recall did not apply. I feel like this is a manufacturing defect that is indicative of the same problem mentioned in the recall. Here is my serial number:
[REDACTED]
justification: Potential gas leak due to a manufacturing defect in the gas tank gasket, which could lead to an incident but unlikely to cause injury.

incident_description: I have a snow blower made by Amerisun. I got a recall notice of a bolt that comes loose and i the consumer needed to tighten. I did such and proceeded to run the snow blower. I cranked and came on but never shuts off. Its got an on and off switch and a key to remove for safety and shut off. Neither worked and had to let the gas run out. A bolt did come also flying off and its now a safety hazard because it cant be turned off. I luckily only filled it with a tiny bit of gas.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in a safety hazard due to the snow blower not shutting off, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Upon using my remington outlaw chainsaw . I had a quite a bit of gas leak on my hand it also back fired and flamed out
justification: Gas leak and backfire resulted in injury, but not death, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is possible.

incident_description:
This 60  year old consumer is reporting that he had been using his electric grass blower September 21st, 2018 for approximately 5 or 10 minutes in the evening to blow grass off the patio and the lawn mower when he looked down and saw that the blower was on fire 
He dropped it and immediately unplugged it.
He did not notice any warning odors or sparks.
No injuries being reported
He is reporting this product as a fire injury hazard and would like to see it recalled.
The consumer contacted the manufacturer September 21st, 2018 and created case#[REDACTED] with their representative who advised him that they would contact him in two weeks.
It has now been over three weeks and he has heard nothing.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of the blower catching fire poses a significant risk, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario with a 'possible' likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Put together a Target Fire Pit by the letter of the instructions.  Lit it on fire and after 10 minutes of use, heard several large cracks followed by several hot "lava rocks" shooting from the interior of the pit across the deck.  This thing is a bomb.  No doubt they would cause injury if someone was standing there.
justification: Lava rocks shooting across the deck pose a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: Turned on blower and the orange plastic fan inside broke into pieces.  Some of the pieces flew out into the air and onto the ground.  We purchased it on May 29, 2017 at Home Depot along with an extended warranty but was told it is still under the manufacturer's warranty.  I have called Ryobi's Lawn and Garden Service line twice-on Sept 10, [REDEACTED] filed a safety report and on Sept 20, [REDACTED] again filed a 2nd safety report.  I was told both times that someone would contact me back in 7-14 days for a replacement blower BUT NOBODY HAS CALLED BACK.  The reference number I was given is [REDACTED].
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (broken fan) but no injuries, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is possible given the product's failure and lack of resolution from the manufacturer.

incident_description:
Ryobi 18V Battery powered blower. Model P2108 Purchased at Home Depot 

turned on Blower and it sounded like a small explosion - The fan blades literally shredded, throwing parts in all directions at least 20 feet away.  The incident is identical to the incident that prompted the recall on the Ryobi Electric blowers and caused injuries.

incident_description:
Hi,

I am the owner of a new Heatolator Cab50 wood pellet stove. When this issue occurred, I had only burned two bags of pellets in the stove since it was installed.  

To summarize the issue. I walked into my house to find the smoke alarm going off and the house smelling of smoke. I immediately went to where the pellet stove was located and could see that there was an issue with the stove. What I found was the electric igniter that is used to ignite the wood pellets was stuck on. There were no pellets in the fire pot and the thermostat was not calling for heat. 

Because the igniter was stuck on for apparently a long time all the metal in the stove was glowing red hot causing the stove to overheat and fill the room with smoke. 

I tried to shut down the stove down but was not able to, apparently the safety features built into the stove had failed preventing me from shutting down the stove. I was forced to unplug the stove to stop it from burning. After a few minutes I plugged it in again and the same issues occurred.
  
There is clearly a failure in the safety mechanism in this product and I was just fortunate enough to have come home in time before I had a major fire in my house. I strongly believe the manufacture should recall these stoves and correct this safety issue before more issues like this occur.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The stuck igniter and failed safety features led to a house filling with smoke, posing a high risk of injury or property damage.

incident_description:
On 03/12/2012 my husband and I bought a Husqvarna riding lawn mower. It had issues from the beginning. Many times when you would start it, it would spit and sputter and throw out black smoke. If you let it do this for about 3-4 minutes, it would come out of it. Occasionally, it would do this while you were mowing, You would have to stop and let it spit and sputter until it was done, and then it would run fine. We took the lawn mower in to a repair shop several times, only to be told there was nothing wrong with it. 

On 10/3/2018, I mowed my yard. I had to stop and pick something up in the yard. I turned the mower off, got off and picked up my mums. When I got back on the mower, it wouldn't start. This was not the first time this had happened. Most of the time, I would sit on the mower and wait it out because after a few minutes it would start. This day, I decided to go inside and check the time and get me something to drink. I came inside and grabbed a cup to put ice in and I heard a big BOOM! I thought someone had hit something such as a telephone pole because it was so loud. I looked out and my mower was engulfed in flames. Flames were 20-25 feet in the air. I had neighbors stop by because they thought my house was on fire, because the flames were so tall and the smoke was so black. Thank goodness, I didn't stay on the mower. It would have killed me. It just so happened it quit at the end of my driveway. Otherwise, if I had parked by my house, or in my garage, they too would have caught fire. On 10/4/2018, I called Husqvarna and reported what happened. They had me send pictures and were supposed to get back with me, which they never did. The gentleman I spoke with told me it wasn't under warranty since it was 6 years old. Regardless of the age, it should not have blown up like it did. I have since called them back 2 more times. Each time I am promised a callback, but they never call back. I still have the burned up mower sitting in my yard.
justification: The mower's spontaneous combustion resulted in a severe fire, posing a high likelihood of fatality.

The second incident occurred when I had plates lying on the accessory near the inner edge - the exhaust heat from the propane burners causes the plates to become very hot and I received first degree burns when attempting to pick up the plates.

This is a very serious safety issue that I brought to the attention of the manufacturer via email on August 10, 2018.  The manufacturer dismissed and did not address my safety concerns.

    https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HL-hOO3GoOQ

This incident scared the living daylights out of me.  If any body part or animal had been in the vicinity of that blade, it would have been sliced to ribbons.

It appears from my experience and that of the person who posted on YouTube that water on bottom of the mower can override the mower's safety lockouts.  This is a VERY dangerous product that has an extremely high potential of causing traumatic injury.
justification: The mower started unexpectedly while being cleaned, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
On 9/29/18 i was grilling dinner on my Kenmore Elite 600 series grill.   However the flames were really high on the 4 end burners & more so on the end then in the middle of the burner even when turning back to low.     The next morning on 9/30/18 I cleaned the grill and notice the the firebox has a hole that rusted through right next to where you ignite the burner.    I contacted Sears by phone and the said I would have to have a service man come and look at it but it would cost $99.    

The grill was purchased in 6/18/15 but we did not receive it until late July.    I have the original packaging sticker and warranty that has 10/25 year warranty on parts.    This stick said the firebox stated on sticker "porcelain coated firebox".    The firebox should not wrought away.

After getting service repair man from Sears, he came out on 9/30/18 to look at grill charge me $99 that had to be paid then and gave me estimate for $452 to repair firebox that they say is not covered.

I did not repair and started investigating Kenmore Gas Elite grills on line and found that over 12-15 were in class action lawsuit that were handled by the [REDACTED] law firm and sears /kenmore had defective grills that caused firebox tray to corrode prematurely exposing the propane tank and hose connections to grills burners, potential creating a safety hazard.

I have sent a report and filed a copy of my info to the lawfirm.   In the suit on March 13, 2017 sears had to pay the cost for repairs and reimburse customers but not all the kenmore grills were recalled,   This started back December 2015 the same year I purchased my grill.   

Sears knew or should  have known that the grills are defective, not fit for their intended purpose, and unsafe to use as intended.  Sears routing failed to repair grills when the firebox defect manifests, and that owners of the affected kenmore grills had to spend around 300 per repair.   

I had a gas oven blow up in my face over 15 years ago and had 1st, 2nd and third degree burns on my face.   I do not need a gas grill that has an open hole and corroding above the propane tank to explode again in my face...
justification: The grill's firebox rusted through, exposing the propane tank and hose connections, posing a high risk of explosion and severe injury.

incident_description: I bought a Blackstone model 1560 36 inch stainless steel grill from Home Depot and used it first time on 6/30/18. It was scary and a big mess. Lucky I didn't burn the house down or get burned. This has a front trough that fills with hot grease that runs to the right and into an inadequately small catch container. Much of my oil ran out of the container, on to the deck and hot grease just went everywhere. The trough has a hole in the end of it and the grease runs out and turns back under, mostly misses the catch basin and ends up running all over. Next and worse, the consumer is then working over this big tray of hot grease with open flames a short distance away, right under the trough. If it were to  drip over the side, the whole thing catches fire. This is a HUGE fire danger. And since that trough isn't flat on the one I got, the center fills up and holds hot grease. No offense but this design is flat out dangerous. I've seen ads on TV that show a newer and safer designed unit that has a rear exit for grease with a one inch steel wall in front. But that's not what home Depot and many others are selling. I talked with Home Depot and their only solution is to return it. I told them its dangerous. We will be looking to obtain the model with the newer safer rear grease exit. But what about all those unsafe units out there?? I have tried to contact Blackstone but get no response either by email or phone.
justification: The grill's design allows hot grease to overflow and potentially ignite, posing a high likelihood of an incident.

incident_description:
Daily, I plug the blower into the electric outlet in the garage to blow debris out of the garage and driveway.  On this occasion, while the blower was on, I placed my hand underneath to support the blower while also holding it from the handle.  The plastic covering over the impeller fan cracked and my middle finger was sucked into the impeller.  Blood splattered all over the garage floor and I dropped the blower and ran into the house to run my finger under the faucet and put pressure on the wound.  The blood would not stop.  I grabbed the phone to call my roommate to meet me at the emergency room.  

My middle finger on the left hand was fractured as well as two major tendons completely severed.  Surgery was required to repair the finger with a pin inserted to stabilize it for three months.  I also sustained nerve and tissue damage and the finger is non-functioning.  Two hand specialists, a trauma surgeon, and an occupational therapist are attempting to restore movement in that finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury, with two major tendons severed and a fractured finger, making it a '3' on the severity scale. The likelihood of this occurring again is 'possible' given the regular use of the blower and the unique way it was handled this time.

incident_description:
I purchased a Yardworks Fireman's Nozzle, model 274-292 for my home garden hose. I had it maybe a month and used it several times. Having unhooked my garden hose from my outside house spigot because I was going to use it to spray down a driveway I was going to sealcoat  at a different location than my house, I transported the nozzle and hose in my work van. 
  
After I turned the water on from the spigot at the new location, I reached for the nozzle to turn it on to spray and before I could, the inner brass core shot out and landed so far away I couldn't find it in the grass. At first, I thought the hose had burst from the popping sound, but realized the brass inner core that actually moves in and out from the nozzle frame, was missing. I examined it and it looked as if it was the failure of the plastic that broke on the inside that I guess the brass fitting is connected to, which I have a picture of. Looks like plastic but maybe zinc or some type of metal. Either way, it was jagged and the failure occurred there.  

I took it back to Menards in Golden Valley Minnesota, today, and exchanged it for a new one. Having looked at the boxes of these nozzles, there were some from 2017 and 2018. I also told the manager on duty about it and also the Returns Customer gal about what happened so Yardworks could be informed. If a person or a child had been standing in front of it when it shot out, injury would have occurred because I couldn't even locate it on the driveway, which means it shot somewhere into the grass all the way across a 16 foot wide driveway. 
I'm also, leery about using the new one since this happened, and exchanged it so I could get the correct model number, etc.. Menards has the broken Fireman's Nozzle the Customer Service gal marked it and was going to give it to the Hardware manager to inform.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the potential for injury was high due to the projectile nature of the failure.

Thinking not much of it in 2017 I purchased another  model TB635EC from the same store.   Upon unboxing it and getting ready to start it, the kick out spurs that are on the metal flywheel broke on the first pull.  So I returned this to the store and they replaced it with another from stock.    Most recently the first week of June 2017 I was using the 3rd Troybilt unit Troybilt item # 41ADZ63C766, Model TB635EC, S/N 1C157DD1012, which is about 1 year old.  When using this most recent one at full throttle, the metal flywheel broke apart immediately stopping the weed eater.   Luckily no metal fragments or parts exploded from the plastic shroud.    These models are inherently dangerous due to the location of the motor and flywheel being close to the operators side.  This began last season, I ordered the steering parts ( bearing, gear plate and gear) and replaced them. The mower is only 4-5 years old and this seemed early to have to replaced steering components. Actually I have never heard of anyone having to replaced steering gears on lawn mowers of any age. However this seemed to work throughout the winter and early spring. About 9 months later as the mowing season began it started again. 

I called Cub Cadet to check on recalls or service bulletins. I was told there was a recall and was given  a case [REDACTED] along with a list of service centers. I called the first four dealers multiple times to get in for repair, no one seemed to want to work on it, even the dealer I bought the machine from who has a good reputation for service after the sale.  I called the fifth dealer who did make the repair but told me it was not under recall and they just tighten the bolts. I brought it home and the same thing is happening the first time I used it after the repair, but the steering is the worse than it has ever been. I called Cub Cadet and this time they said there was a recall for the power steering but only if it was still under warranty. incident_description:
Weber Genesis gas (propane grill) started up and within 5 minutes of operation the hose just downstream of the regular failed and propane was coming from the hose. The fire continued for several minutes until a small extinguisher was used to extinguish and get close enough to the valve so it could be shut off.

The concern is the flexible hose and regulator are attached to a metal pipe that feeds the ignitors. The rubber hose is in a area that is subject to thermal damage from other metal parts below the grill box. Newer models I understand are separated from the grill box by a piece of sheet metal and some distance. Realistically there's no easy way to shut off the gas since its also located right by the connection to the grill.

Of course the manufacture initially suggested  it was probably the gasket on the propane container and also said they didn't like those propane tanks with the gauges on the outside. Turns out both were ok.
Then they suggested it was a grease fire that caused it, but I doubt that as well. 
The location of the hose and regulator are to close to the heat source are of combustible construction and potential problems are endless. Bad design that was incorporated  now
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is high due to the grill's poor design and proximity of the hose and regulator to heat sources.

incident_description:
My father in law and myself both purchased Honda self propelled rotary mowers 4 and 3 years ago respectively.  We have both been fans of Honda products for many years.  After purchasing these mowers, we noticed they were of lesser quality than previous mowers.  Most notably. The rear drive wheels would periodically lock up after the clutch was released.  This made mowing very difficult.  In he summer of 2017, I searched the Internet where many Honda owners reported similar problems.  Some sites recommended methods of repair.  No information was available in my online searches from Honda.  I attempted a repair and after reassembly the drive belt fell off.  After further work, I got that back on but the wheels still would not roll backwards.  Out of frustration, I went to the Honda Power Equipment site and filed a complaint that provided model number, serial number and summary of the problem.  I never recieved a reply, but a Honda ÃÂRobotÃÂ continued to send be satisfaction surveys to which I responded that I had not recieved an answer.

This summer the belt fell off again and I was just fed up.  I took the machine back to the Honda Dealer from which I purchased it and explained it was the third mower I had purchased from them and it was of far lesser Quality.  I felt I had paid a premium for a ÃÂbest in classÃÂ mower and instead was provided a Walmart quality machine.  The service manager said there may be a service bulletin that covered my machines problem and might be repaired at no cost.  After about three or for weeks he called me and said it was repaired at no cost by Honda.   My wife picked up the machine and stopped by my father in laws house.  When she told him the story, she called the Honda dealer and was told she had to bring it in to see if it was a affected machine, it could not be done over the phone.  After she brought my mower home the belt promptly fell off and the wheels would not roll backwards.  I took both mowers back to the dealer for service.  At that time I wAs given a copy of a service bulletin first issued in February 2017, affecting 3 modern numbers and a range of serial numbers.  It indicates the rear wheel bushings may be undersize and cause the symptoms I describe.  It also says if the mower is under warranty it should be repaired and if out of warranty may be repaired based on goodwill consideration.  the Honda dealer must contact Honda Corporate to recieve good will consideration.

The Honda Dealer presented a positive report that Honda repaired at no cost.  In reality they knew of a design/manufacturing error before my complaint in 2017 and had not made any effort to publicize this problem so affected owners could have them repaired.  Most owners cannot or will not borrow a truck to return a mower that is out of warranty, they will instead fight the mower by dragging it backwards or lifting the back of the machine.

At first I was angry because Honda benifitted financially at the initial sale and appeared to make the service notice ÃÂsecretÃÂ so other owners would not know.  As I thought about it more, I realized that lifting the mower to pull it backwards defeated the foot guard and significantly lessened discharge protection.  I contacted Honda again and suggested they recall the affected machines or at least make the service bulletin public on the Internet with searchable words.  They responded that they fixed my mower and provide service bulletins to dealers as a form of engineering assistance.  In reality I think they have covered up this problem since they have to provide new parts and pay the dealer for 3/4 hour of labor.

Finally, earlier this year my father in law had a cardiac event while mowing.  One can question the wisdom of an 83 year old man mowing his lawn.  I am sure his wife would not have let him had she known how difficult the units are to use.

I have a copy of the service bulletin if you need it.  I hope you can convince Honda to make itÃÂs service bulletins public and/or recall these machines since serious injury could occur.  It also makes me wonde how many other similar problems Honda has covered up.

If you need any additional information, please call.

Best

justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant inconvenience and frustration, with multiple trips to the dealer and failed repair attempts.

incident_description:
I was heating the grill yesterday (May 13, 2018) to cook a Mother's Day dinner for my wife and mother-in-law.  When I looked outside to check temperature, I saw dark smoke billowing from the grill and also could see flames in the undercarriage of the grill, far below the burners.  I was very concerned that the propane tank might ignite or explode.  I grabbed a fire extinguisher (dry chemical) and sprayed the front of the closed grill, then around the side.  I was then able to reach and turn off the four burner controls on the front of the grill.  The fire in the undercarriage (below the burners, above the propane tank) kept re-igniting.  After giving it a big blast from the fire extinguisher, I was able to manually turn off the valve to the propane tank to the fuel line.  I blasted it again with the extinguisher and waited a couple minutes before I went to disconnect the fuel line from the propane tank.  When I started to unscrew the fuel line, it fell to the side - the fuel line had been completely severed.  

My belief is that the fuel line was touching a hot part of the grill and that it ruptured and caught fire, spewing propane into the lower part of the grill.

incident_description: I filled a Gardenline one-gallon multi-purpose spray tank with one gallon of weed killer mix, took it to the driveway in front of my garage, and pumped 3-4 times to begin to pressurize it. I heard a loud boom and the entire front of the tank opened up and blew the fluid all over the driveway. I was wearing shorts, and some of the fluid went on my boots and legs. I immediately washed it off my legs and then cleaned up as best I could. Fortunately, I was wearing glasses, a mask, and gloves, or else some of the spray could have gotten in my eyes. If the back of the tank had blown out, the fluid would have gone all over me and into my garage. If I had been able to pressurize the tank fully and had been carrying it and spraying at the time of the blowout, the situation could have been even worse. I inspected the tank and took pictures that I will attach. The plastic appears not to be of sufficient thickness and quality to hold the pressure needed to be a safe and dependable spray tank. I purchased the tank at Aldi in North Port, FL, 4/27/2016 as an extra sprayer. I have two much older one-gallon tanks that have performed well and safely. I have used the Gardenline sprayer only a few times for very light duty. It has never suffered any damage or abuse before the incident but has been stored in my shed where I keep the others. The tank had no apparent hole or crack in it before the incident or it would not have held sufficient pressure to blow up.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the potential for serious harm was high due to the tank's failure, and the likelihood of a similar event happening again is likely given the tank's poor quality.

incident_description: My electric mower started spontaneously and without warning. I tipped the mower on its side to clear away already wet grass under the deck and was using water from a garden hose; I had not removed the battery yet. The blade went to full speed only inches from my hands. I had to place the mower back on its wheels and pull out the battery to get it to stop. I reinserted the battery and the motor started again without having to pull back the bail lever and/or press the safety lock-out button as usually required. I repeated this several times with the same result. The red safety key next to the battery was the only other way to stop the mower motor. I have a 572 MB video of this process. The mower is relatively new; purchased in June of 2017 and used about 6 times. Each use consumed only 1 indicator bar on the battery. That is about 20 minutes of run time x 6 total use. A warning in the manual says not to expose mower to water to "reduce the risk of electric shock" but does not mention unexpected or spontaneous starting of the motor. It also states to remove the battery before cleaning but again does not warn about unexpected or spontaneous starting. I am certain others will do exactly as I did and will suffer permanent injuries. This is a major safety issue and should be addressed. I checked the mower today and it appears to have returned to normal. It is obvious now that the water somehow got into somewhere it should not have. I was not injured and am not asking for compensation of any sort. This was truly a "Close Call" for me, a couple of inches would have change my life forever. You can be sure I will pull the battery at the drop of a hat from now on.
justification: The mower's spontaneous ignition, despite safety measures, poses a high likelihood of injury to others.

incident_description:
On Saturday April 14th my son was grilling hot dogs using Expert Grill Instant Lighting Charcoal which we believe may have led to him having a seizure.  He cooked with this product around 1-2 P.M. at his grandmotherÃÂs house across the street from mine.  I returned home from work around 6 p.m. and as I walked to her house I noticed a strong odor that smelled like fireworks, particularly the black snake fireworks that came in a small tablet and when lit would grow into an ash snake.  This odor was coming from the grill that was used 4 hours earlier.  I asked my son, daughter and their mother if they noticed the strong smell and they agreed it didnÃÂt smell like charcoal normally does.  With the exception of my son everybody was inside while the charcoal was being lit but did notice the smell after the food was done and they came outside.  A couple of people, including my daughter, stated that the food had an odd taste but didnÃÂt think much more of it.  A hot dog was prepared for me and later as I got it out of the fridge and re heated in the microwave I could smell the odd odor once again and after taking a bite I even tasted it on the food so I threw it away.  I asked them what kind of charcoal was used and if they found anything odd about it when they opened the bag and they commented that the coals went up in flames extremely quick unlike other charcoal that takes a little time to light and a couple of minutes to be fully engulfed.
Early the next morning my son had a violent seizure that required a call to 911 with an ambulance transport to the hospital. He had a blood and urine test to rule out drugs plus two brain scans to look for physical problems.  He was then transported to another hospital where he was given an MRI and EEG with these tests requiring him to stay in the hospital overnight.  All of the tests came back negative and he was released the following day though per Virginia law he cannot drive for six months.  The neurologist said though they ruled out drugs, brain tumors and any other physical issue but could have been an external source that triggered the seizure.  After we returned home from the hospital I started thinking about what could have caused this and the first thing that came to mind was the charcoal.  Since charcoal doesnÃÂt seem to list the ingredients I found out the ingredient that causes the same unique smell from the coals he cooked with and the black snake fireworks, what I found was a chemical named Naphthalene which is known to cause seizures.  My son was grilling on a small table top grille that was placed on the carport next to his chair.  He was sitting next to it during the entire time the coals were burning in addition to being the one that cooked the food so he had maximum exposure to the fumes.  I purchased an identical bag of this charcoal the day after returning from the hospital and what I found was the typical smell charcoal has in addition to it taking a bit of time to light unlike the bag he used. This appears to possibly be isolated to the first bag of charcoal.  Though all of the coals were used there is enough small fragments left in the bottom of the bag that hopefully can be tested for Naphthalene or other dangerous chemicals that can cause seizures.  Please advise me on how to get this tested and the direction I need to proceed in.
justification: Son experienced a violent seizure and required hospitalization, likely due to exposure to Naphthalene in the charcoal.

I purchased a Char-Broil GRILL2GO X200.  Model number 12401734 from Camping World.  This order was dated 13 Sept 2016.  

This grill is a table-top grill and is used and stored in my Recreational Vehicle (RV).  I started a trip in the RV on 12 May 2018 and I noticed the odor of Propane gas in the vehicle.  I checked the vehicle LP gas system and found no problem.  I assumed the odor was from my starting the refrigerator.  Later that night at my first stop when I opened the basement compartment where the Grill is stored, the odor was very strong.  Inspection revealed that the Grill gas regulator valve was leaking.  It can not be completely turned off.  I checked with Char-Broil and discovered the valve type on my unit has been replaced with a redesigned valve, but it was not available.  I called the help desk and the gentleman said I would have to call the company as ask for a replacement.  He gave me the new part number.  I did that, and now a new valve is supposedly enroute to me.  I will be charged for the new valve plus shipping.

There has been no recall on this potentially explosive safety hazard.  I hope this alert will have some postiive effect.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a propane gas leak from a defective grill regulator valve, posing a significant safety hazard.
