I had two lacerations on my neck which thankfully did not do serious damage, instead just bled for 10 to 15 min. The big chunk of fan that hit my shoulder created a softball size bruise because it busted one of the veins that runs across my deltoid. It also busted the skin and bled a little through my shirt. I am blessed because I realize this could have been much worse, especially soo close to my head and eyes. I have a handful of pics to go with my claim, my wife was standing 4 feet away when it happened and she thought I some how got electrocuted when she heard the Big Bang and I dropped the blower and jumped away.

This has caused me great trauma, time and concern during a holiday weekend, that was supposed to be relaxing!
justification: The product's unexpected explosion caused injuries and significant property damage, indicating a high severity level. The company's admission of previous incidents suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I am writing to notify you of a malfunction with a Tomcat wooden rat snap trap that caused me to suffer a serious eye  injury.
Monday June 6th just before 2pm, in my home, a set trap was about 10 feet away from me when the hammer tripped but not due to the trigger arm operating normally. 
Instead, the small metal U-shaped staple that holds the trigger arm came loose from the wooden base, which triggered the trap and shot the staple straight into my right eye. The trigger arm went flying in another direction; the trap basically blew up sending metal pieces flying around the room. It was a shocking, painful, and traumatic event in which I suffered deep lacerations to my inner eyelid, lacerations to my cornea, and damage to my pupil and globe. I lost vision completely.
After being seen at the nearest hospital they transferred me to another hospital with more advanced equipment and an optometry specialist.
He performed emergency surgery to repair the cuts in my eye, and I will have stitches in my eyeball for a few more weeks. At that time, we'll know how much of my vision will fully return. 
As we look closer at the trap, we are surprised to realize how insecure that staple is, it would be so much safer if it was longer and hammered down on the backside to secure it from coming loose and airborne with all the pressure of the springs behind it. 
My Father in Law has said that he's also had that u-shaped nail come out of a Tomcat trap before but he never found where it flew to, thankfully he was not injured like I was. I'm so interested to know if other consumers of this product have had that staple come loose, if so I hope that like my Father In Law that they were not hit directly with the staple, or the metal arm.
I had no idea that these traps were capable of turning into projectile weapons, I'm still in shock this happened and feel so lucky that it wasn't one of my four children in the room who had been hit. I'm extremely concerned that there is a pretty major design flaw or hardware quality problem that could be easily fixed so the Tomcat trap works as intended. 
I'm very concerned for the safety of other families, children and pets who are unknowingly in danger while using these traps.
As a consumer that trusted this product I would like to request a recall of these traps, until a safety modification to secure that staple has been made. 
I'd also like to suggest more safety warnings on the label, recommending safety glasses being worn while in proximity to a set trap would be a good idea. 
I have reported the incident and details of my injury to Tomcat, and requested a recall of their product. I believe the Tomcat company is taking my request seriously, but I wanted to report it to other sources as well.
justification: The incident resulted in serious eye injuries, and the loose staple design flaw was previously experienced by the victim's father-in-law, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a Sears snow blower in October 2017, during it's 1st use in January, I noticed gas on the driveway.  I looked for any loose hoses but could not find any during the next 2 months I would siphon gas after each use from the gas tank because I didn't want the gas leaking in my garage.  In February I called sears for a warranty repair on the gas tank and chute control mechanism (the chute stopped working).  The repair technician arrived and replaced the chute mechanism & confirmed it was the gas tank that was leaking (from a seam).  He said I need a new gas tank & one will be delivered to my house in a few days.  I received a call (on 3/28) indicating the replacement tank is not available and sears cannot tell me when it will arrive and they will not schedule a service technician until a gas tank is available.  I was told whenever it does arrive, to please call and they will send someone out to replace it.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a gas leak, posing a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: New from box, assembled product in vacuum mulcher configuration.  Within one minute of first operation received a substantial shock in my index finger that shot up to my elbow.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (substantial shock) to the user's index finger, extending up to the elbow, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: While using my snow blower this past winter, the unit got stuck in drive.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning snow blower, which is a common occurrence, but did not result in any injuries.

incident_description: Using the leaf blower to blow grass cuttings off driveway holding in my right hand. All of a sudden it literally exploded in my hand. The bang was loud enough to have my right ear lose hearing for a few seconds. A plastic piece was flown out on the driveway that definitely could have hurt someone or me if I was holding in my left hand. The entire side of the blower is cracked open leaving a big hole from the piece from the inside blew out.
justification: The incident resulted in a loss of hearing temporarily and a potential hazard was created by the flying debris, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
"Dirty Hands" 28 Ton Gas Log Splitter:

Log Splitter hydraulic pump high pressure hose blew apart spraying hydraulic oil all over the machine, the operator, the nearby deck railings and the surrounding lawn area.

Log splitter engine had only been running for a few minutes before the hose failure. Otherwise, the hydraulic oil could have ignited causing severe personal injury to operator i.e. burns and fire to surrounding combustible material i.e. my home.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in severe burns and property damage if the hydraulic oil had ignited.

incident_description: I own a John Deere ztrak I bought April 2017. Last week I got off the mower while in park and the mower belly off however unbeknown to me I never realized that the blades donÃÂt stop even when in off positio and when I got off the blades hit something and flew up and hit my hand cause a small cut and bruising to my finger.  I believe this isnÃÂt very safe and that the blades should have a break when you cut it off.
justification: Blades did not stop when the mower was turned off, causing injury.

incident_description: I own a Black and Decker Hedge Trimmer Model TR016. Everytime I use it, I push the trigger to start the trimmer, but when I release the trigger the trimmer doesn't stop. I have checked numerous times to make sure the trigger lock isn't on, so it isn't the trigger lock that is causing the issue. There have been many times I have used this trimmer, have released the trigger that powers the trimmer, and have set the trimmer down on the ground, and the trimmer continues to run, even though I released the power trigger many seconds previous. I have had this trimmer for several years, and didn't know there was such a site to report unsafe products, or I would have reported it years ago. This is a very unsafe product, since the release of the power trigger doesn't stop the trimmer from running.
justification: The trimmer's failure to stop when the trigger is released poses a high likelihood of injury, as demonstrated by the user's repeated experiences.

incident_description: Two days ago I filled my Greenwood Two Gallon Garden Sprayer with weed killer.  Sold by Harbor Freight..  I primed it three or four times and it exploded in my face.  I was completely saturated in noxious weed killer.  After a shower I then investigated the sprayer.  The protective base was blown off and I found a long slit on the bottom edge of the sprayer.  My son gave me this sprayer last year.  It was used once and stored in the garden shed.  I have used sprayers for years and never had anything like this happen.
justification: The sprayer's failure to withstand priming resulted in an injury, making it a possible occurrence given the age and infrequent use of the sprayer.

incident_description:
I was riding the mower from the edge of the concrete drive up about 8 inch grass incline and the mower went like I was a tractor in a tractor pull, 2x.
It then tipped over to the right and fell and threw me off
justification: The mower tipping over and throwing the rider off resulted in an injury, making it a 'possible' occurrence.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her spouse was operating the zero turn tractor when it caught on fire.   She stated that he had turned it off while using it to talk to her and when he tried to start it  up again it started to emit flames from the engine compartment.  She stated that the flames were contained with water.  She stated that the unit was in use for approximately 45 mins to an hour before the incident occurred.

Caller stated that the retailer was contacted about the incident.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller checked to see if the tractor had any recalls on it but there were no recalls on model or serial number.  She is concerned that this tractor is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a significant fire.

incident_description:
i have a cub cadet riding lawn mower purchased april 2012.   2 weeks ago, the hydrostatic transmission failed, causing the mower to go freewheeling down a small incline in my lawn.  the brake pedal did nothing to stop mower. i am handicapped so my son mows my lawn for me. after an hour, my son tried mower again and exact same problem reoccurred.    i told him to shut it off and he towed it to my garage      as i was researching cub cadet repairs on the internet, i learned there was a safety recall for my mower's transmission problem. when i checked mower model and serial numbers,
date of manufacture, and transmission model and serial numbers, it appears my mower and transmission were made just after your recall manufacture dates.  IS IT POSSIBLE YOUR RECALL ISN'T BROAD ENOUGH? my mower otherwise is in perfect condition and maintained well above cub cadet's
maintenance schedules  my mower is :
Cub Cadet LTX 1050 model 13WQ91AP056    serial 1K231H30284  manufactured 11\ 2011
Hydro-Gear transmission model 618-0319   serial 1243H30306

PLEASE HELP ME!
Thank You,
[REDACTED]
justification: The mower's transmission failure, causing it to freewheel, poses a high likelihood of injury given the incident's recurrence and the user's disability.

incident_description: The switch/trigger failed and when the Chainsaw is plugged in to power, the Chainsaw runs at full speed.  It can not be shut down until power is removed.  The saw guard was still on however it was tossed approximately 10 feet and the chain impacted the driveway and came off the guide.
justification: The chainsaw running at full speed with the guard off and chain impacting the driveway poses a high risk of injury.

incident_description: Several years ago I purchased a very expensive (over $3,000) outdoor gas grill from Capital Cooking Equipment. The dials on the front to turn on the gas and control the temperature get so hot that I have actually burnt my fingers so have to wear insulated gloves. In fact they get so hot that they have burnt out the automatic igniters and even melted the plastic which shows that gas is flowing. I have contacted the company several times about this but they refuse to do anything.
justification: The grill's dials reaching dangerously high temperatures, causing burns and damaging components, indicates a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: I was using a Husqvarna YTA24V48 mower while having the mower in reverse backing down a hill the transmission went into a neutral position or failed causing it to free wheel out of control and rolled over injuring my leg .
justification: Injury occurred due to mower losing control and rolling over, likelihood is possible given the mower's reverse operation on a hill.

incident_description:
Re: Ryobi Leaf Blower: Model RY42102, Serial Number EU15522N170419
My Ryobi Leaf Blower exploded and ejected orange plastic fragments under high velocity, some of which hit me in the eye.
The primary disintegrated component *appears* to be the impeller but that's a guess. There is more than one type of plastic mixed into the pile.
justification: High velocity plastic fragments hit user in the eye, resulting in injury.

incident_description: Burned top of left hand twice while turning off propane gas tank.  The top of my hand hits the bottom of the fire pan. No protection from hot pan.
justification: Injury occurred due to direct contact with a hot surface, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
Was preparing to use electric chain saw to remove 4 small trees in my yard.

Plugged in the saw and squeezed the power trigger to confirm everything was ready and working properly. The saw started running and did not stop when I released the trigger. I squeezed the trigger several times trying to get the saw to shut off but in continued to run. I carefully placed the saw on the ground keeping the moving chain from touching anything. I then delicately unplugged the saw keeping the moving chain from touching anything.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage or injury if the saw hadn't been safely placed and unplugged.

incident_description: On 10/28/14 while operating a Harbor Freight, Chicago Electric, Electric Chainsaw, the chain saw did not shut off properly.  The chain continued to rotate around the motor and bar after I let go of the button.  The chainsaw hit a branch and caused the chainsaw to kickback and hit my left, thus cutting the 5th digit on my left hand requiring a trip to [REDACTED] Emergency Room and stitches.  The chainsaw was supported in my right hand at the time.  There is a scar on my left hand from the incident.
justification: Injury occurred due to chainsaw not shutting off properly, leading to kickback and cut on left hand.

incident_description:
I was cooking on my Broil King Signet grill  (Onward Mfg, Ontario Canada) when I noticed that the base of the grill, which is made of flammable plastic parts, had caught fire. The entire area around the gas tank was in flames.  I was able to extinguish the flames from a distance using a garden hose. , but th grill was destroyed

 I have safely used gas grills for over 40 years.  I note that this mfg had a recall in 2008 because of  afire and burn hazard. Constructing a grill from parts that can catch fire near the gas tank should not be allowed.
justification: The grill's flammable plastic parts near the gas tank caught fire, leading to a significant incident but no injuries, given the user's quick response with a garden hose.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore gas grill m# 148.20125510 S# RBTN015226  purchased 5/1/16, after assembly grill caught on fire at first lighting due to bad hose fitting, which melted wires.  No injury's, called phone number in owners manual and they sent out a new part. Grill had worked great since then.  2/21/18 Last night noticed large flame coming from under heat diffusers.  lifted grates and diffusers, found stainless steel burners had rotted and cracked in less then 2 years. also found that the main body of the grill had rusted away in the back where burners are secured. The burners are under a 10year warranty so  I called  the 800 number 1-844-553-6667 and was told they could sell me the parts. When I explained that the burners were under a 10 year warranty he said they can only sell the burners for 55.00 each(4) and that I would have to take it up with the store that I bought it at. Also gave me a quote on the main body of the grill which is not under warranty at 367.00.  Now granted its not under warranty but it still should not rust away to the point that I cant get new burners and install and secure them. After a few very frustrating phone calls with them I started to look else where for parts for it to no avail.  But found quite a few negative reviews for this grill and other Kenmore grills for similar issues. Also there is a class action lawsuit for other Kenmore grills, and after reading about that, this grill model probably should have been included.  This could have resulted in a fire,burn or death. especially if the burner had fallen since the locking piece in the back has rotted away in less than 2 years
justification: The grill's rapid deterioration and previous fire incident indicate a high likelihood of future incidents, potentially leading to injuries or worse.

incident_description: I was blowing leaves when suddenly the blower made a clattering noise. I immediately stopped blowing leaves. I observed that the fan inside the leaf blower had come apart with the fan blades all broken off and flying out the back of the leaf blower. I feel very fortunate that none of the plastic pieces struck or injured me.
justification: Although the incident resulted in damage to the leaf blower, no injuries were sustained.

incident_description: FIRE/EXSPLOSION - of Lawnmower on April 24, 2018. My husband went to get the garbage cans (two) and parked the mower and came inside our home. Approx. 10-15 min later he heard the dogs barking and looked outside and the mower was on fire. He yells to me to call 911 as he runs outside, unhooked our dog who was near by, run back inside and grabbed the keys to my dads car to move it and by the time he got back outside the lawnmower explodes, throwing debris on him and the car keeping him from opening the door. This caused the top of the mower to be expelled onto the cars left bumper which engulfs into flames as the mower had a full tank of gas. My husband gets the water hose to start fighting the fire. As we wait for the Fire Department, I move our other vehicle, dog, try and get my husband to move back from this extremely dangerous fire. The wind was blowing for strong this day and every time I tried to get close to him the wind would change and I would get black smoke in my face. We start hearing Fire trucks, they pass by my house. I freak out, thinking they missed our house and call 911 back only to be told they where dispatched to another location. (We live about 1 mile from the Fire Station) The car explodes and my husband goes down, I am really freaking out now (he had a stroke in 2012 so I was scared something was wrong with him) but he  gets back up and continues to try and save our house from this fire. Another Fire Truck goes by, then another... the car explodes again and again. Finally a Fire Truck pulls in and helps my husband put out this fire and he is ok only exhausted. He has PTSD and is now having nightmares about this issue over and over again, seeing his funeral. Seeing his family live without him. He is in therapy trying to work through this horrible experience we are just glad he was not on the lawnmower when it decided to catch fire/explode. I found out after the fact the company has similar "FIRE ISSUES/RECALLS" that we where unaware of on the exact same model of lawnmower. We purchased the mower new in 2013. Place of purchase: Elberta Hardware, Elberta AL 36530 / Make: Cub Cadet Model: XLT 1050 - the recall is on the Cub Cadet website for a fuel filter on the engine.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the individual trying to control the fire, with multiple explosions and exposure to intense heat and smoke.

incident_description:
The submitter said he was riding the unit when the gearbox locked and he could not put the unit in neutral. The submitter said he had a similar incident occur again and during the second incident the unit ran into his motorcycle.

The submitter contacted the firm and notified them of the incident. The submitter was told that his unit was not included in recall # 17-227. The submitter spoke with a supervisor and she told him that they could not assist with a free repair or inspection.

The submitter believes his unit should be included in the recall.
justification: Although no injury was reported, the potential for harm is high as the unit malfunctioned twice, leading to a collision with the motorcycle.

incident_description:
Casa Pura Interlocking Acacia Wooden Tiles - Sold thru Amazon.com and sold by Iconik Direct

Acacia wood tiles plastic interlocking back deteriorates causing wood to collapse underfoot more than 1/4 inch creating a trip hazard.  Plastic deteriorated in aprozmately 1 1/2 year.  Tile collapsed and I tripped but luckily no injuries.  I've now inspected multiple tiles and found they are likewise deteriorating.

I notified Amazon of the safety concern.  They instructed me to notify Iconik Direct

Tiles were purchased May 8, 2016 (online thru Amazon.com).  Tiles were installed sometime June 2016.

incident_description: I purchased an All Power America snowblower in Winter 2013.  It is the same unit which appears as recalled on your website SB044P.  The unit worked until late last year.  When I attempted to start the unit last month (December 2017) the unit would not start.  After pulling the cord repeatedly, the gasoline came rapidly pouring out the back of the engine.  Every time I pulled the cord since, more fuel is ejected from the rear of the engine.  (Because there was no ignition, the fuel did not start on fire and there was no engine fire.)
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fuel leak, posing a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: Purchased a Vogelzang Pellet Stove model vg5790 in January 2016.  Since then the auger sheared off, pins sheared and then the igniter went out causing us to have to manually light the pellet stove, then the blower went out. Called the manufacturer and was told to CUT a extension cord and use the wires to direct connect wires to live 110 wires to auger motor to check. How smart and safe is this.  I went one to vogelzang international corp on Facebook and others are having the same issues and told the same things. I was also told it was because I'm burning Pellets well it's a pellet stove that's what you are supposed to burn right?  Prior to this happening my home filled up with smoke and flames were high in the pellet stove and I unplugged the stove and it kept going. This pellet stoves are defective and unsafe. Along with technical support telling people to cut extension cords and directly connecting live wires!!!  These need to be recalled and the company needs to make things right with consumers.
justification: Multiple safety issues and dangerous advice from manufacturer.

incident_description:
I purchased a Akron CharGriller back in June 2017 from Lowes in Stafford.

I have written the company previously regarding this grill.  The wooded handle cracked and I requested a new one.

On December 4, 2017, I decided to Chargill and smoke some meat.  As I went to load my grill the entire top came off.  The bolts that fasten to the grill completely failed.  This is a safety issue.  The lid cover came completely off and it weighs at least 20+ pounds or more.  The grill can't be safely operated and lid .  It seems like when the grill lid  and bottom gets hot the lid would not stay upright. The metal fails and the lid completely  falls back and becomes paraell or  flushed with the grill grate level or hits the ground. (take your pick)  Once I open the lid it completely came off and fell upright on the deck. The whole grill could have flip with the coals lit and everything could been set a blaze.

I continue to cook my food but I had to lift the hot lid and place it down on the ground.  During the operation I know was at risk of catching my deck on fire because I had to reach over the top of the grill.   I had to place lid on my deck each time I wanted to load the charcoal, wood chips, turn the meat and remove the meat.  The lid is heavy and hot.  I could have burned myself.

I requested Chargriller replace the whole grill and they refused too.  I would like a recall notice to be served for this grill.   The  bottom metal has overheated and failed.  The bolts are either not heat resistant or they aren't the proper length.   Here is the model number MODEL 06719

Here is the serial number. 19032092c.  


I don't know how this happen.  My grill is covered and I treat it pretty good plus it is only 6 months old.

I have contacted Chargriller as well at this email address:  

service@chargriller.com


I paid over $300.00 for this grill and it has turned out to be a lemon and a fire hazard.

 I need an entire replacement grill at this point or refund.
justification: The grill's lid completely detached, posing a high risk of injury or fire, and the issue is likely to recur given the design flaw.

incident_description:
The submitter said he powered the chainsaw to check if it worked and when he went to power it off the chainsaw would not shut off. The submitter said the turn off switch failed and he had to use the manual choke to shut it off. 

The submitter said he has checked it a few times during the past 2 months and each time the chainsaw fails to shut off.

The submitter contacted the retailer, Sears and notified them of the safety hazard. The submitter was informed that the chainsaw is not recalled and they could not assist him.

The submitter noticed that the chainsaw was made by MTD and he may contact the firm to notify them.

The submitter believes the chainsaw is unsafe and should be investigated.

Please note
It appears that saw chips from using the saw got into the kill switch, preventing the switch from functioning properly - Switch is not enclosed Dangerous design flaw as, all it take is on wood chip to render the kill switch inoperative
justification: The chainsaw failing to shut off poses a high likelihood of injury, as demonstrated by the submitter's repeated experiences.

incident_description:
(12/23/2017) The consumer was using the unit to blow leaves. After about 15 minutes, the unit made a little noise then broke apart. A piece of the propeller broke through the side of the housing and hit his elbow. 

The consumer was not injured.

The consumer contacted the firm around the first part of January. He was advised that a $75 check and a release form would be sent to him. He was also asked to return the blower to the place of purchase.

(02/02/2018) A representative from the place of purchase contacted the consumer. The representative stated that he was advised to take a picture of the unit and also destroy the unit.

The consumer stated that he had already taken a picture of the blower and did not return it to the place of purchase.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a product failure that could have caused injury, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' case with a 'possible' likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
Blade broke off on blower impeller and was projected at high speed out of the blower, hitting my hand, causing significant bruising and bleeding.

I am an engineer with NASA and am good at diagnosing failures.  My theory is that using the blower as a yard vacuum over the years has sucked up debris that damaged the impeller blades.
justification: Injury occurred due to debris damaging impeller blades over time, making this incident likely.

incident_description: On Tuesday Nov 14, 2017 mt father was helping to prepare my snowblower that is stored at his house over the summer by inflating the tires that had gone flat.  He took the tires to the local gas station to use their inflator.  The tire exploded.  The explosion propelled the rim/tire cutting his hand and thrusting the rim down onto his foot.  He then fell to the ground from the explosion and the tire came to rest 200 feet away from the explosion.  We are lucky the tire/rim did not catch him in the forehead.  The force of the rim on his foot cut through his leather shoe, gashed the top of his foot that is still not fully healed and fractured his toes in 3 places, . The gash was so wide they could not stitch it it closed so my parents have been forced to change the dressing on the foot regularly to prevent infection and promote healing.  My parents had to purchase a walker to assist him with his balance as he could not place pressure on his foot/toe. We are fortunate that by chance his sister was at the same gas station pumping gas saw/heard what happened and was able to contact my mom and take him to the local urgent care. Upon the physicians reviewing my dad's injuries it was determined that he needed more care for his foot than they could provide so an ambulance was dispatched to take him to the local hospital for emergency care.  The doctors at the emergency care were considering the use of pins in the toe but the location of the injuries would not allow that so them had to immobilize his foot.  He has not been able to get around. My dad actually felt bad that he ruined the tire and rim and actually apologized to me for the accident. It was not until I started researching replacement tires for the Craftsman 4-cycle 3 speed snow blower model number 247.88255 and tire part number 634-0232A from the owners manual did I realize it was not his fault.  This is a known issue and the faulty product has produced horrible injuries to my dad. His suffering is not just from pain, but also anguish in my elderly parents having to provide this extra care for is healing and the cost financially for his care.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries, including a gash on the foot, fractured toes, and required extensive medical care, but did not result in death.

incident_description:
(10/19/2017) The submitter stated that the consumer,[REDACTED], had been mowing the lawn for about an hour when he smelled smoke.   He looked around to see where the smoke was coming from. The smoke was coming from the back of the mower. [REDACTED] got off of the unit and saw flames below the seat of the unit. With help from the neighbors, he was able to put the fire out. Also, the fire department came out and made sure that the fire was completely out.

No one was injured.

(11/01/2017) The submitter contacted the firm who requested pictures. The submitter sent pictures to the firm but did not get a response.

(11/06/2017) The submitter contacted the firm again, but the person that she needed to talk to was not available. She left a message for the person but did not receive a call.

(11/07/2017) The submitter contacted the firm again and was advised to contact her home owner's insurance.
justification: While the incident resulted in no injuries, the potential for property damage was high due to a fire on a lawn mower.

incident_description: My Ever Brite solar powered motion light caught fire last night and burned part of my shed.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while solar-powered lights can malfunction, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a BYBLIGHT 42 LED Solar Flag Pole Light with 2 Brightness Level on Amazon.com.  I set the light onto a recycling container to charge it before putting up on the flagpole. The light has two brightness settings and I did not want to have to take the pole down because I did not get it switched on, or it was too dim. 

The light exploded and caught fire and charred the lid to the recycling container.
justification: The light exploding and catching fire, though damaging property, did not result in any injuries.

incident_description: Traeger Tailgater wood pellet smoker grill does not hold temperature.  If the flame goes out or temp goes low the grill continues to feed pellets into the grill.  Once this happens the pot where the pellets burn become over filled and then hot ash reegyntes the pellets causing extreme temperatures and at a final point the excessive smoke in the grill will Egnyte and blow the lid open from the heat and pressure.  It is only a matter of time before this grill causes serious damage or death.  This is not user error, the grill simply does not posses the proper safety features to prevent this from happening.
justification: The grill's design flaw can lead to extreme temperatures and explosions, posing a high risk of death.

incident_description:
I received a Toro Power Clear 180, model 38282 as a Christmas present in 2009.  It has serial number 310022796.  I was able to use it the first winter, however in December 2010, I found a gas leak.  The Toro dealer handled it under warranty but made no mention of a recall.  The product worked that winter but would not start the following winter of 2012.  After paying for a tune-up, the next leak was found in December 2013.  I paid 139.47 in January of 2014 to get that taken care of.  In December, 2016 the leak returned.  I paid $254.18 to have the problem resolved and all necessary maintenance.  

It is now December and when I added fuel to get the blower going for the first snow fall, there was an immediate leak.  While looking for a way to get the leak fixed, I found the notice of recall from 2010.  While I do not object to paying for a tune-up when needed, I do believe that I am entitled to have a product that does not continually leak and endanger me and my family.  

It is possible some of the work done previously was done under the auspices of the recallI, but if that were the case, then whatever the problem was has not been properly and permanently fixed as evidenced by the multiple recurrences of the problem.  It is disturbing that supposedly authorized Toro dealers are incapable of properly dealing with this problem.

Your assistance in getting this matter resolved properly and promptly will be appreciated.
justification: Multiple gas leaks pose a significant fire hazard, though no injuries have been reported.

incident_description: I purchased a clip-on battery operated light from Dream Tent for my 4 year old nephew.  This light clips on a fabric dream tent that is installed over pillow area of child's mattress.  When I received the light, it did not turn on.  When I checked the batteries, the batteries were do hot that they burnt my palm.  I treated the burn with salve.  I went out bought new batteries and installed them, before I could complete screwing the back cover back on light, the new batteries became extremely hot.  Hotter than the original batteries.  All the batteries were LR44 x 3.  I believe this product is an extreme fire hazard, especially when considered that it is intended to be installed in a fabric tent over a sleeping toddler.
justification: Burn injury occurred due to excessively hot batteries, and the product's design poses a high likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description: On Tuesday, October 31, I was using my 2009 Cub Cadet 1040 LTX mower to cut my yard one final time for the season.  After cutting my yard, I parked my mower in our garage.  I then went to get my truck from the street.  As I was backing my truck into the garage I looked in rear view mirror and noticed the my mower engine was completely engulfed in flames!  After putting the fire out I noticed that the exhaust manifold had broken loose and had to have been rattling around while I was cutting and the when I stopped the mower the hot exhaust manifold sparked the fire.  The damage to the engine is extensive.  The plastic shell around the engine is melted, the spindle is melted onto the engine, the spark plug hose and hose hose leading from the exhaust to the air filter has disintegrated.  The spark plug is melted into the engine and the exhaust manifold is resting on the inside of the engine.  The oil stained the mower and my garage floor and the hood of the mower is now burned and black
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the extensive damage to the mower and garage, along with the potential for escalation, warrants a severity level of 2.

incident_description: While mowing with my John Deere D105 rider the mower would not stop when I let off the gas pedal, and as soon as I take my foot off the brake it starts to move forward on it own.(It should not move unless the gas pedal is pushed.) Also the transmission will not shift into neutral or reverse. I checked on line an there is a recall for the D105, I looked for my Vin #[REDACTED] I could not find it on the list, but I will say my experience today really scared me and I feel this mater should be looked into, I am glad it happened to me and not my wife, or one of my grandchildren...
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm if the rider had been operated by someone less experienced.

incident_description: I was using the Toro leaf blower per recommended instructions. My hair was tied back, and I had a hat on.  The blower inlets sucked in my hat and hair, hitting me in the head resulting in a concussion and 5 staples, significant hair loss and neck injury as well. The unit was flush to my head, the fire department had to be called to open the unit so I could obtain medical attention.There was no safety feature on this unit to disengage the motor when a foreign object enters, nor did it have a safety feature for automatic shut off. The unit continued to run and hit me in the head until my son came to unplugg the unit during the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, staples, hair loss, and neck injury, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 as it's possible, given the lack of safety features and user's reliance on instructions.

incident_description: When I use the John Deere D105 the transmission slips out of gear and it take off. If your not careful you can loose control of it.
justification: The transmission slipping out of gear and the lawn mower taking off could lead to property damage or loss of control, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting a solar LED light manufactured by manufacturer in Fairfield, NJ, 1 that she purchased around May or June 2017 from where she believes was Shop-co in Manistique, MI.  
The Insurance 
She had the light sticking on her screen door to provide additional light.
She said that Sunday, September 10, 2017 a young man driving past her home with his wife stopped, knocked on her window and informed her that her porch was on fire.
He asked if she had a fire extinguisher but settled for the garden hose to extinguish the fire.
The fire department verified that the fire had been extinguished completely.
There are no injuries being reported
She has not at this time contacted the manufacturer but she does intend to contact them.
justification: Fire occurred but was extinguished before any injuries, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
I PURCHASED THIS CHAR-BROIL TRU INFRRED GRILL ON JULY 30, 2017; 
MODEL # 15601900 PATIO BISTRO 240
THE GRILL BLEW UP IN THE PROCESS OF LIGHTING IT.  THESE GRILLS WERE RECALLED IN 2013 AND 2015 FOR THE SAME REASON.
I TURNED ON THE GAS WITH THE COVER OPENED SET THE DIAL WITH THE TEMPERATURE AND PUSHED THE ELECTRONIC IGNITOR WHEN DID NOT LIGHT IMMEDIATELY TURNED GRILL OFF AND IT BLEW UP.  THIS IS THE EXACT INCIDENT IN THE RECALL.  CHAR-BROIL OFFERED TO SEND ME THE REPLACEMENT PARTS BUT I WILL NOT FEEL SAFE USING THE GRILL.  SINCE I PURCHASED IT 5 MTHS AGO REQUESTED A MONEY REFUND. CHAR-BROIL REFUSED ONLY TO SEND REPLACEMENT PARTS. BECAUSE OF MY EXPERIENCE WITH THIS GRILL I DO NOT WANT AND WILL NOT USE IT AGAIN.
MY HAIR DID GET SINGED AND EYE BROWS.  THIS COULD HAVE BEEN MUCH SERIOUS.
AS A CONSUMER PLEASE INVESTIGATE THIS ISSUE FOR PUBLIC SAFETY.

incident_description:
Twice this has occurred when less that 525 hours on it.  Left wheel with all lugs came out.  Had to call JD , 2014 JD 4044 r tractor.  Has happen again.  This tractor was shipped from, La., to Al.
once arrive in Alabama they stated done an inspection.  When got home with the tractor  a few days
later wheel on left side came off.  They came and got the tractor, then  had to go over local office to corporate to get it fixed.  Once I got the tractor to the dealer- ship I had them to air tight the front
wheels and then they found the right wheels  were extremely loose and they were tighten also as well as the back wheels. 

The left wheel has came out again!   This must be a safety issue here somehow? How would it keep doing this with just bushing hogging.

The front wheel left side came off the rim on county hwy as I was going to turn into my brother in laws
drive way to get the tractor off the Road.. Wheel coming off could cause wreck of tractor and injury the person driving and/or killing people on side of road.  This second time bushing on level land the left wheel came off.
justification: The incident has occurred multiple times, with the most recent causing the tractor to veer off the road, posing a high risk of injury to the driver and others.

incident_description:
I recently purchased an Ariens Platinum 24 SHO Snow Blower with EFI.  The unit contains a 7.2 Volt Battery that is either Lithium or Nickel Cadmium. The leads on the battery are defective and the plastic plug came off with no effort and exposed the two leads which shorted out.  The pins for the leads are defective and are not secured correctly.  From what I've been told this is NOT an isolated issue to my snow blower. Within 20 inches (estimate ) is the gas tank.  I store my snow blower in my garage and or shed. My concern is that the spark from the short can start a fire from nearby stored gas or spilled gasoline.


BTW.  The Dealer is terrific.  They took back the unit understanding that gravity of the issue and exchanged it for another unit without EFI.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to exposed battery leads near gasoline storage.

incident_description: My Ryobi 8 Amp Electric Jet Fan Blower motor blades shattered. The orange fan blades exploded and were expelled out of the back intake and front of the blower upon use, along with parts of the internal framework. I was not aware that this product was under recall. I had used it successfully until this occurred.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant failure of the product with blades and internal parts being expelled, indicating a possible design or manufacturing defect.

incident_description: I purchased my blower at Lowes on May 29, 2017.  I noticed in the instruction manual that it is best to use low or no ethanol fuel.  I purchased no ethanol fuel specifically for my new blower.  I have used it 10 to 15 times to blow grass clippings from my driveway and sidewalk.  It has been easy to start and use.  On October 29th, when priming, fuel squirted up from the fuel tank.  Upon inspection, I noticed that the clear fuel line appeared to be dissolved where it meets up with the plug to the fuel tank.  Had the engine started, this could have posed a fire risk resulting in a burn or worse.   IÃÂve used lawn equipment all my life, this is the first time that I have seen something like this on equipment that is less than 6 months old with low use. This appears to be manufacturing / part defect.   Doing some quick online research, many others are experiencing the same issue with this model.
justification: Fuel line dissolution could have caused a fuel leak and subsequent fire, posing a burn risk.

incident_description: Batteries blew up while charging. Charging time was about 2 hours. I did notice the battery life was getting shorter and shorter each use.
justification: Batteries exploding while charging indicates a potential hazard, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description:
Gas tank too close to flames caused facial burns.  Replacement parts not available as company out of business
Would like replacement calls due with recall but paying for them not an option.
Called Grille Parts Onward Grilles, [REDACTED] told toss grille out.  Grille seldom used but have returned the new cover.  Grille can't be used until repaired.

incident_description:
Char-Broil Silver 4-Burner Liquid Propane Gas Grill with 1 Side Burner Model # 463344116
The all four burners are just an inch above where grease collects.  I am a light user of this grill and have grease fires about every month.  The fires last well over five minutes; I have become an expert of putting them out using baking soda. I thoroughly clean the grill after every grease fire.  This grill can hold up to 15 burgers easy at a time but I get grease fires every month cooking dinner for two twice a week. Please help remove this product from families homes before damage and loss of life occurs.
justification: Frequent grease fires pose a significant risk of property damage and potential injury.

incident_description:
While using a Toro Leaf Blower for about 15 minutes I began to smell an electrical overheat aroma.  Before I could turn the Blower off, Smoke bellowed from the electric motor and the blower plug began to melt.  The product was a Toro Super Blower / Vacuum, model 51618  S/N 316103305.  I had purchased the product in November 2016.  Numerous calls to Toro failed to result in any service being done.

I feel this blower is internally defective and should be investigated.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk with electrical overheating and melting of the blower plug.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her battery operated Blower because the fan blades inside spontaneously broke Thursday, September 21, 2017 sending pieces of it our of the back and just a couple of small pieces out of the front.
She purchased this blower around the Autumn of 2016 from a home supply store in Sun City Center, Florida.
There is a piece of the fan still in the blower that she said sounds like a kaleidoscope.
She is reporting this incident as an injury, laceration and potential blinding hazard.
There were no injuries with this particular incident.
She contacted the manufacturer's Customer Service  Office who verified that they would replace the piece broken free of charge.
justification: While no injuries were reported in this specific incident, the potential for injury (laceration, blinding hazard) exists due to the spontaneous fan blade breakage.

incident_description: Ryobi 8amp Jet Fan Blower Model RY42102 impeller blades shattered and ejected a few seconds into use resulting in minor leg scratches and a million tiny pieces of red plastic strewn across my driveway. Returned to mfg, per CPSC recall for replacement. Mfg had failed to replace more than 8 weeks after return, offers no estimate of when they will replace (despite fact that replacement model is in stock at retail outlets), and offers no alternative, such as refund or coupon for replacement unit.
justification: Injury occurred due to impeller blades shattering, and the likelihood is possible given the product's recall and manufacturing delay.

incident_description:
(03/2017) The consumer stated that he was on the tractor. The tractor had ben running for about five minutes when the front of the unit caught on fire under the hood. The consumer tried to put it out with his gloved hand but had to dump water on the hood to put the fire out.

No injuries.

(08/2017) The consumer contacted MTD. He was advised that nothing could be done.
justification: Fire under the hood of a tractor is a possible occurrence, causing no injuries in this case.

incident_description:
In November of 2017 I purchased a Toro 518 ZR snowblower. Since purchase the machine has leaked gasoline three times.
The first time, an authorized dealer attempted to fix the machine, a few days later, a gas leak was discovered again. The dealer confirmed again that this was from the carburetor. The dealer took almost three weeks to obtain a part from Toro but could not and as a result they grabbed a part from a new machine in a box and used that part. That machine was returned to me on December 28th. Now, the machine is rapidly leaking gas from the same area again. I am going to call Toro tomorrow to request a refund or an exchange to a different model machine.
justification: Gas leak incidents have occurred multiple times despite dealer's attempts to repair, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a snowblower from my neighbor.  It is a Yard Machines model #: 31A-3BAD700.
Serial #: 1J185I10210. 000001.  The tires were flat. I tried inflating with a hand pump but was not sucessful. On Oct 2 I removed the wheels and took it to an auto shop, (Excellent Auto).  When they were working to inflate I heard an explosion.  Two people came running out with their hands badly cut and bleeding.  They told me to leave because they needed to get to the emergency room because the wheel had exploded.  I was very upset and talked to a person that said he thought there was a recall involving snowblowers.  I went on-line and found the MTD hotline and called.  They indicated there was a recall and took my information. They said they will send me a repair kit.  I told them that two people were injured.  They said they would have to file an incident report themselves.  Today, I gave the phone # and my case number to the shop owner who was hurt. His name is [REDACTED]. Phone : [REDACTED].  I feel terrible about this and felt I should report this incident.
My case #  with MTD is: [REDACTED].

incident_description: (06/12/2017) The consumer was getting ready to grill.  I lite the grill checked the flame, there was no flame.  Turned the grill valves off and went to change the propane tank.  I didn't turn the valve off all the way on the propane tank off all the way and started to remove the hose from the grill to the propane tank.  The propane started to come out of the hose and did not stop even when the hose was disconnected from the propane tank.  The fumes from the propane tank built up and exploded in my face.  The propane tank had fumes coming out so the fumes where lite so it was like a torch.  I ran inside and my wife came out with the fire extinguisher and put the fire out.  My wife the dragged the propane tank that had propane tank still coming out to the yard away from the grill and the house.  I went to the local hospital (New Britain_ CT) where the had me transported to the burn center in Bridge Port, CT.  I received 2nd degree burns on my left side of my chest, 3 fingers, on my left hand, the palm on my right hand, my left ear, and on my neck.  I need to go to the wound center for multiple appointments after this accident.
