incident_description:
I am writing to let you know about a dangerous product I purchased from my local Tractor Supply store. The product is a County Line 25 ton log splitter, manufacgturerd by YTL international. The product had a few assembly issues including a loose wheel but I was able to resolve this.  The real reason for my letter is to inform you that the design of the tongue is defective and is likely to cause a substantial risk of injury to customers.  This design is unreasonably hazardous and dangerous, and I would suggest TSC consider recalling this product immediately and updating the design.  I know it is unsafe because I nearly lost part of my finger when the tongue collapsed and caught the tip of my finger in the unit.  Please see the picture I included.  I was simply try to lift the tongue stand up so I could move the log splitter.  The unit was not running, it was on level ground.  As you can see from your website there are no safety or pinch point decals on the folding tongue.  The described method to ÃÂkickÃÂ the tongue stand up is counter intuitive to any similar design on the market, and frankly it does not work.

Upon being injured by this product I called the consumer help line at 1-888-376-9601.  It rang for 2 minutes without answer, I hung up.  I called again later and again, no answer.  Finally, after a third call, I got through and was told there was nothing to report since the product was not malfunctioning.  I tried to get some product liability insurance information on the manufacture, YTL but was told they could not provide it.  Upon learning the manufacture was a company called YTL international and not TSC itself I learned that they have had recalls on product in the recent past.  Including a dry wall lift that was recalled by the cpsc.  

I have contacted the store and the manufacturer without a response to date.
justification: The defective tongue design caused a severe injury, and the likelihood of this happening again is high given the product's design flaws and lack of safety warnings.

incident_description: I had an Everbrite solar light on my deck that exploded and burst into flames burning the deck.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur frequently due to the rarity of solar lights exploding.

incident_description: I purchased a fire pit from Amazon in December 2015 for a house that was being renovated.  We began using it in the summer of 2017.  The description of the firepit said it had a stone base.  As the firepit got hot, pieces began to shoot off of the product.  They appeared to be plaster, not stone
justification: Pieces shooting off the fire pit could cause property damage or minor injuries.

incident_description: Caller is reporting that the hose burst and was leaking water all over the place.  He has had 2 incidents with 2 different hoses, however, when he contacted the company they were not willing to assist him.   He was referred to contact CPSC and report it from the State Attorney General's office.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of a hose bursting and leaking water could lead to property damage or slip hazards, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This riding mower is a fire hazard.  Even the Owners' Manual contains a warning that debri (leaves, grasses) can accumulate around its muffler and catch fire.  

I purchased this mower from a Lowes Home Improvement store approximately 6 years ago and, in addition to using it to mow grass, I used it each fall to mulch leaves in our yard.  After mowing and mulching, and prior to parking it in our garage, I would leave it sit in our driveway while I blew grass and leaves from our sidewalks and driveway.  During this time, I frequently noticed smoke rising from under the mower's hood and that grass and leaves accumulated next to the muffler were catching fire.  Because of this experience, after each mulching job was complete, I'd use a gas powered blower to clear debris from the muffler area and elsewhere.

This process worked fine until June 4th of this year (2017).  After mowing the yard, I again parked the Troy Bilt Pony in the driveway while I cleared our sidewalks, driveway, and mower of debris which takes about 10 minutes.  Then I restarted the mower and drove it into the garage.  I noticed no smoke or fumes prior to parking it, but noticed the mower softly backfired when I started it up.  Approximately 10 minutes after parking it, my wife went into the garage and found flames coming from under the mower hood.  Fortunately, we were able to pull the mower out of the garage and into our driveway prior to the fire speading.  The fire totaled the mower and caused about $10,000 of smoke damage to our home.  Due to my clearing out debris from around the muffler, I'm convinced the fire was caused by something other than the muffler.

I was curious as to whether other owners of Troy Bilt Ponys had similar experiences, and found a video on the web of an owner who also had his Pony destroyed by fire after a noticeable backfire.

I recommend this mower be recalled or other remedy enacted.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the repeated instances of smoke and fire, as well as similar experiences reported by other owners.

incident_description: I was doing prep for hurricane Irma and checked my flashlight to see what type of batteries it uses. Saw it was "c" batteries and I clicked it on and off to see if it was working or if I needed to replace them. The flashlight didn't come on so I put it down and decided I needed new batteries. A few minutes later I thought I should test the batteries to see if they were really dead or if maybe something was wrong with the flashlight. I picked it up and the flashlight was burning hot!  It's all metal. I quickly unscrewed the cap and dumped the batteries out onto the counter top and they were also burning hot!  Good thing I only left this for a few minutes and didn't leave to go to the store. I don't know how hot it would have become and if it would have started a fire. A piece of plastic inside near the bulb appears to be melted but I do not know if that's normal for this flashlight or not. I saw someone else reported the exact same incident on 5/15/2013 with you so I figured I should report it also since I don't see an active recall.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to overheating batteries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: The Tragger pellet grill I have was not running properly. After looking around for a minute, I discovered the problem. There is a fan on the bottom of the unit the fan and had a wasp nest built around it. While brushing away the nest I was electrocuted. I believe that this is a major design failure. The fan and motor are exposed and in no way covered. the fan and the motor sit about 2 feet off the ground the perfect height for a child to get hurt. I was hoping that they had a fix for this and when to the store and looked at some new  Tragger grills. They still are manufacturing the with out any cover.
justification: Exposed fan and motor at child-reachable height increases likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
The plastic fan inside my Ryobi Cordless Jet Fan Blower, Mod. P2108, Ser No. EU 16192D150206
broke, which caused the fan blades to be discharged from the front end of the blower tube. Luckily, no-one was near when this failure occurred.

I've contacted Ryobi Customer Service and filed a warranty claim. They in turn have forwarded the claim to the Ryobi "Safety" Dept who are supposed to handle the claim.

I'm contacting the CPSC because the same circumstances have resulted in the recall of a similar
Ryobi blower. The Ryobi [REDACTED], Mod [REDACTED] has been recalled, 
Recall No. [REDACTED]. The reason given in the CSPC recall notice is: " The plastic fan inside the electric blowers can break causing the fan blades to be discharged from either end of the blower tube.
This poses a laceration hazard."
justification: Although no injury occurred this time, the potential for laceration hazard is high due to the similarity of the incident to a recalled product with the same issue.

incident_description:
On 8/28/17 our solar motion light caught on fire.62 LED Solar Light, Perfectday 62 LED Outdoor Wireless Solar Powered Motion Sensor Light Ponds Accent Lighting Decor Lamp with Three Intelligent Modes
Sold by: FINY PRODUCTS

It caught on fire while mounted under our gutter then fell to the flower bed and caught a rose bush on fire.
justification: Although the incident caused a fire, no injuries were reported, and the damage was limited to property.

incident_description: I am reporting an unsafe barbecue, " Porta-Chef 120 made by Broil King". It has no real grease drainage system. It stores grease in the bottom of the barbecue base, near the flame, until the grease reaches a depth of 1/4" with an approx. area of 135 sq inches. After it has reached this level it drips all over the floor. However, multiple times the grease has caught fire. It is a very ferocious fire and difficult to put out. If used near a building or an apartment it could easily start a fire. I was using this in 90 degree weather and it happened three times in a row. I stopped using it after I realized what was going on. Each fire was progressively worse than the last as the grease level increased.
justification: The barbecue's lack of grease drainage system leads to frequent grease fires, posing a high risk of property damage.

incident_description: I was mowing uphill and suddenly for no reason lost power to move forward and brakes also failed.  The lawn tractor and I both ended up in the trees/brush line at the bottom of hill.  Thankfully not the creek that is just past the trees. After getting it towed out and into the shop they say the transaxle is broke. My mower is a Cub Cadet SLTX 1054 model # 13WK92AK010, Serial #1F180H60078.  The transaxle #618-04270B and the transaxle serial number is 0161H10033.  It does not appear to be on the recall list, but it is near the same time of manufacture and resulted in the same incident that other models were recalled for.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident could have been severe if the tractor had rolled into the creek.

incident_description: Gaspro propane gas grill regulator failed and started leaking after 2 uses. Potentially explosive condition.
justification: The grill regulator failed after minimal use, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and posing a significant safety hazard.

incident_description: The "Everbrite Solar Light" attached to my house exploded and caught fire, catching a portion of my house on fire!
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is rated as 'possible' given the unexpected nature of the product failure.

incident_description:
The Craftsman gas chainsaw overheats and sparks are created while cutting wood.  There is the gas supply just above the sparks and the chain oil dripping out just below the sparks.   I do not believe this chainsaw that has been recalled is safe.

This same model chainsaw has been recalled due to fire hazards, however the serial number of this saw is not within the dates of recall.  This Craftsman saw was manufactured on July 1st according to the serial number while the recall included all saws through June.
justification: Sparks from the overheating chainsaw could ignite the nearby gas supply and chain oil, posing a high risk of fire.

incident_description:
I OWN A SCAG TIGER CAT RIDING MOWER.  I HAS DEVELOPED NUMEROUS LEAKS IN THE LEFT SIDE MOLDED PLASTIC GAS TANK.  THE RIGHT SIDE TANK IS OF A DIFFERENT MOLD AND IS FINE.
THE TANK, IN MY OPINION, WAS MADE OF FAULTY PLASTIC OR A FAULTY MOLDING PROCESS.  THERE ARE SMALL PINHOLE LEAKS AND SEEPS IN THE TANK , ESPECIALLY AT THE SEAM THAT ATTACHES THE TOP AND BOTTOM HALVES OF TANK.  IT IS A FIRE HAZARD.  I ONLY USE THE NON LEAKING RIGHT SIDE TANK NOW.  IF YOU LOOK INSIDE THE EMPTY TANK YOU CAN SEE PLACES WHERE THE PLASTIC IS NO LONGER PROPER.  THE INNER PLASTIC IS FAILING AND AND ALLOWING THE OUTER PLASTIC TO DEVELOP LEAKS AND SEEPS.  

I CONTACTED OEM AND HE SAYS NO RECALL ON THIS ITEM AND SUGGESTED I CONTACT THE DEALER I BOUGHT IT FROM. I HAVE DONE OTHER AND THEY SAY THEY WILL NOT REPLACE THE TANK.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the persistent leaks in the gas tank pose a significant fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: We use our grill frequently and have used other smoker style grills. This traeger catches on fire extremely easily. We always have the grill cleaned and only use the appropriate pellets. While cooking the temp suddenly rises and then the inside of the grill is on fire and billowing black smoke. I have read many reports of this happening to others as well. It is something with this specific brand/model that makes it more prone to catching on fire.
justification: The grill's propensity to catch fire easily, as evidenced by numerous reports, poses a significant risk of property damage and potential injury.

incident_description: I was blowing leaves on our patio with the Weed Eater WB160. I had been using it no more than 5 minutes when it exploded inches from my thigh. There were no indications of what was about to happen, no strange smells, sounds or appearance. There was a deafening shotgun sound and the internal pieces were expelled out the sides of the plastic housing and directly into my right leg. After the initial shock of the sound, the blower was still running, making a high pitched whirring sound, even though almost all of the green plastic housing was obliterated. I immediately unplugged the unit from the wall and called my husband over for help. He promptly took photographs of the blower, the adjacent pieces and my leg. Upon inspection my right leg was bleeding, had several abrasions and a contusion about the size of a football. We left right away for the ER to make sure nothing more was wrong.
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected explosion of the Weed Eater, making the occurrence 'possible' rather than 'rare' or 'unlikely'.

incident_description:
Raven Mower engine cam shaft blew up at church picnic. This mower has had several issues since replacement of original.
I purchased my original Raven in 2014, after less than a year, the generator portion of the MPV stopped working. At that time Denver Global Products (DGP) replaced the mower with a new one. Then at the beginning of 2016, the mowing deck stop working, I called DGP and found out that there was a recall on the deck at the end of 2015 and failed to contact me. They sent me a new mower deck mid-year 2016 after several attempts to contact them. Fast forward to this year. At the beginning of the mowing season, I had to "charge" my Raven so that I could mow, after several attempts to contact them due to voicemail issues or being on hold for an hour, they finally sent someone out. The tech was able to diagnose that the batteries had failed and that they needed to be replaced. They were changed on Aug 15, 2017. 6 days later, I was able to mow and the mower started cutting off on its own and would restart with no problems. This happened 4 times, then front right wheel came off the mower, WHILE I was mowing. I called for a replacement wheel and after several minutes they agreed to replace it. When I finally got the new wheel, I was finally able to mow again on Aug 28. Everything seemed to be going smoothly, until the mower started cutting off again in mid-mow. This happened 4 times, then on the 5th time the mower would not restart. I called and email DGP about what had happened, and they said they would get a tech out in 2 weeks. Since I had a Church picnic coming up on Labor Day and had no mower that would work, I had to borrow one to get the mowing done. At the picnic, several of the guys had heard me talk about the Raven and how much I had enjoyed the product asked to look at it. I showed them the features and they were impressed with the set-up. I attempt to start the Raven and low and behold it started. One of the guys said that it is sounding like a diesel engine, and said that it might be the cam rods. As soon as he said that the top of the engine blew off and several pieces flew 20' away and almost hit the kids that were playing nearby. One gentleman got hit on the forehead and is ok. Oil spew out all over the place onto our clothes and on my siding. I am absolutely shocked, but glad that no one was seriously hurt. 

I have email the above information to DGP and have not received any email back from them. I finally called and talked to [REDACTED], and she said that the engine is out of warranty and that I can buy a new engine to put in, but still hasn't emailed me.

 I am totally frustrated and actually scared of this machine. Plus, I want people to know that this could happen to someone else as well
justification: Engine explosion resulted in minor injury to a bystander, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents given the history of mower failures.

incident_description: Consumer got a burned hand after turning off a gas fire pit.  Consumer states that there is no warning in the manual, that the fire pit needs to cool off before touching it safely.  There is not much room between cylinder gas valve and bottom of tray.  In addition, there is no mention of tightening the bolts during assembly.
justification: Consumer suffered a burn injury due to lack of safety warnings and insufficient cooling time before handling.

incident_description: PREMATURE FAILURE OF BELT GUARD.  Actual in-use time was 35 - 40 hours.  Belt guard (TroyBilt part #: 781-0427-0637) broke.  Both flanges separated from the body of the guard leaving the drive belt exposed.   The flanges are an integral part of the guard and are the means of holding the guard in place over the drive belt.  It appears that a very sharp bend was used at the point where the flanges protrude from the guard.  This sharp bend could not tolerate the constant vibration of the edger and failed allowing the body of the guard to separate from the flanges.  This item is one of the prime safety features of this product and needs to be more durable.  Judging by the number of belt guards available on [REDACTED], this seems to be a high failure item not only on this unit but others also.
justification: The belt guard's failure exposed the drive belt, posing a high likelihood of injury due to the guard's primary safety role and the prevalence of similar failures.

incident_description:
On July 11, 2017 I folded  down the handle  on the mower and put it into my [REDACTED].   When  I went to unload the mower and started to move it out  of the vehicle by hand, the mower started while still  inside the vehicle.  I was finally able to shut it off by moving the blade control bar. Fortunately I was not injured and there was no damage to the vehicle.

Here is what happens :  When the  mower handle is folded down,  the start push button comes directly in contact with the wheel height adjustment lever on the left front wheel.  The height adjustment lever was in the third slot( rotated clockwise).  This direct contact depresses the electric start button, and with any slight movement of the blade control bar, the mower starts automatically.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm due to the mower starting unexpectedly while being unloaded.

incident_description: I was using a Troy-Bilt Leaf Blower. The impeller broke and exploded through the outer shell of the leaf blower. The shrapnel hit me on the stomach, chest and neck causing lacerations. The neck laceration could have been life threatening had it been deeper and cut my jugular vain. A video of the incident was captured by my security system.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations, with a neck wound potentially life-threatening if deeper.

incident_description:
When using Craftsman Leaf Blower model 138.74899  Serial number "SET0780152  03/19/14" suddenly the blower caught fire with huge orange fireball and the blower 2 print plug and the cord got burnt. This was in dry sunny weather about 50F temperatures. Very scary experience. So I looked up and seems there is a recall for the same reason but my serial number mentioned above was not included and should be. 

I just made a call to the The Craftsman brand hotline toll-free at 888-266-7096 but they are trying to weasel out saying my blower is not included even though model 138.74899 is included my serial number falls out of range. Also I used good quality single 3 prong orange extension cord of AWG16 3/C 1.31mm2 cord they are trying to find some reason and asked for photos that I have sent them. Request to please expand the recall as this is a dangerous product that can harm US citizens.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the recall for similar models and the user's experience.

incident_description: The RYOBI JET FAN BLOWER MODEL #RY25AXB has an adjustable strap that can be used one of two ways - it can either be used over the shoulder or cross body.  It allows for you to adjust the length to the operators height and musculature.  I have had the product for one year and have used the shoulder harness/strap on several occasions and usually used it cross body.  The last time I used the product, I simply used the strap as a shoulder strap and I am glad I did.   When I was working in the yard, the tail end of the adjustable shoulder strap got caught in the intake and sheered the leaf blower right off my arm causing lacerations to my hand between my index finger and thumb.  The engine immediately shut off however, had I used it as a cross body strap I could have easily been strangled when the piece got tangled in the intake.  I am lucky that I only suffered lacerations.   I was told that I would get a call from the safety team as well as a supervisor on Monday (today) and never got one.  I called and explained what happened and was told it would take 3-5days for someone to contact me instead of the call expected on Monday.  Someone finally contacted me on Monday at 4pm when I was not available.  There doesn't seem to be much concern on the part of the manufacturer to resolve the issue so I found this website and hope to get the word out.  This could have ended up much worse had I used the strap as a cross body strap instead of simply over my shoulder.
justification: The strap's design flaw, allowing it to get caught in the intake, led to severe lacerations and could have resulted in strangulation if used cross-body.

incident_description:
On Monday July 3, 2017 at 13:39 ours [REDACTED] received a 911 call form [REDACTED] of [REDACTED] reporting a building fire at [REDACTED]. I arrived as the first firefighter on scene and was the Incident commander for this fire. The fire was almost completely extinguished by [REDACTED], also of [REDACTED] using a garden hose. Upon my arrival I observed a small smoldering fire on the patio next to [REDACTED] with flame damage to the exterior south facing wall. The door to the house was locked and no one appeared to be home. Firefighter's used a ladder to access a second floor window and confirmed there were no occupants. Firefighter's also confirmed that fire damage was limited to the exterior, overhaul was completed and suppression crews were dismissed.
According to the [REDACTED], this property is a 1,892 square foot, three story, wood frame home with vinyl siding built in 1992.
I walked clockwise around the entire building and noted there to be no other signs of fire. The area of origin was located on the patio adjacent to the stairs and along the south facing wall of the home. I then focused on the area of origin and found the melted remains of a plastic patio chair with what appeared to be an electronic device welded to the remains of the chair. There were two transformer plugs on the ground in front of the fire area. The neighbor from [REDACTED], Mr.[REDACTED] reported to me that he heard a loud pop from outside his home and shortly after became aware of the fire when a neighbor alerted him.
[REDACTED] of [REDACTED] says, saw a fire up against the side and to the left of the door to number [REDACTED]. After seeing the fire, Ms. [REDACTED] said she alerted the [REDACTED] to the fire. Mrs. [REDACTED] said she called 911 to report the fire while Mr. [REDACTED] used a garden hose attached to [REDACTED] to extinguish the fire. Mr. [REDACTED] said he removed the transformer plugs from the outlet located in the exterior
justification: No injuries were reported, and the fire was quickly extinguished with minor property damage.

incident_description: 3 months ago we bought a Char-Broil Advantage 4 burner gas grill.  This grill is a fire hazard! We just replaced a grill we'd had for 8 years with this one. We have had several raging fires in it ( we NEVER had a fire in our last grill, ever). After the first time, we cleaned the grill thoroughly and according to instructions-- I'd only cooked on it 5x at that point, so we were surprised to need to. Then we had another fire. Another cleaning. So on. Last night we had ANOTHER FIRE, one that required a fire extinguisher, it was the first cook since I last cleaned it. The grill was spotless when I started the burgers, but the flame is just positioned too close to the bottom and the grease drainage is woefully inadequate; grease collected while I cooked and erupted in flames. My husband used to be a firefighter and he can't believe this design hasn't been recalled! I now see SO MANY reviews online with the same complaint. I called the company and after submitting photos they claim it was my fault because there was too much grease in the bottom of the grill.  The only great in the grill was the grease from the burgers I'd been cooking-- I had JUST cleaned it.  Plus, I've only cooked on the grill a dozen or so times, and I've cleaned it several.  CharBroil created a product that will catch fire if ther is any grease-- which is woefully inadequate for a BBQ grill!   I guess the company is waiting for a tragedy or a lawsuit before changing anything.
justification: Multiple instances of fire, even after thorough cleaning, indicate a high likelihood of reoccurrence with potential for injury.

incident_description:
We purchased a Toro Recycler Mower last year from Home Depot. Right away we noticed mulch, rocks and grass flying out at us from a gap in between the mower and the clippings bag. We notified Toro immediately. They were aware of problem saying a "few" customers experienced this problem. Their repair was a small foam piece that stuck on to the catcher opening and closed the gap between the mower and the bag. 

This worked moderately well for a few months, but when the foam compressed, the rocks, mulch and grass came shooting out at us again whenever the mower was in operation. The clippings bag also shoots out grass clippings and dust. It appears as though the weave of the clippings bag is not tight enough, there are numerous holes in the material that allows unacceptable amounts of clippings and dust to be blown out at the user. Its unbearable to use the mower without a mask and eye protection. 

Toro will not refund our purchase price and take back the defective and dangerous mower. 

We feel this mower should be recalled since their only solution is to send out another foam piece which is temporary at best and does not address the defective clippings bag. 

We have seen problems with the Toro recycler mower in the past year that lead to a recall with the blade. We feel this is another issue that warrants a recall on the Toro Recycler Mower.
justification: The incident involves repeated exposure to debris and dust, posing a potential injury risk, and Toro's awareness of the issue and limited response indicates a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I was riding my lawnmower down a hill from my doublewide to my older house and the mower began to increase in speed just like it went out of gear. It sped up and would not slow down. I was able to steer the mower to safety but since then the transmission will not hardly pull at all, especially when it gets warm. I saw a recall on it but serial number was not listed in the numbers. My lawnmower is a John Deere D105, serial # 1GXD105EKGG705963, purchased at Lowes in Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia. I bought it April, 2016
justification: Although the incident resulted in no injuries, the potential for harm was high due to the lawnmower's sudden acceleration and loss of control, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a CharGriller Dual Gas/Charcoal Grill on 8/19/17 from a local Wal-Mart Store.  On October 14, 2017, my husband and I were getting ready to grill hamburgers and turned the grill on low; a few moments later we noticed a funny smell coming from our grill.   He looked at the grill and before the grill even had the burgers on it, it had gotten hot enough to melt the knobs off of the grill, melt the paint off of the grill and melt the hood on the gas side of the grill.  We immediately cut the grill off.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the grill malfunctioned severely, causing significant damage within a short period of use.

incident_description:
Sears Craftsman lawn mower blade adaptor safety issue.

The "star" adaptor has sheared off on 2 of the OEM adaptors I have bought as replacements which eventually ruined my 12 year old mower with same part.

I bought a new Craftsman 37820 163cc 22ÃÂ Rear Wheel Drive 3-in-1 Lawn Mower with High Rear Wheels on July 12, 2017.  I used it twice and on the second use the blade adaptor "star" sheared off and my blade kept spinning after I stopped the mower.  I have a 50 x 100 yard, not much to mow!

I do have pictures of the defective adaptor part #:
Sintergy 581851501

There are numerous reviews on AMAZON.COM about this defective, unsafe product:
Craftsman 581473301 Blade Adapter
https://www.amazon.com/Craftsman-581473301-Blade-Adapter/dp/B002ESAHGS?tag=vs-home-convert-amazon-20

Thank you.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (mower) but no injuries, and there are multiple reports of the same issue, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: The Troy Bilt mower model TB 320 has a defective gas cap. Whenever full or near full with gas, the gasoline leaks from the cap onto the mower deck. I've had the cap replaced, but the replacement also leaks. This is most pronounced when mowing on a hill. It is both an environmental danger and a fire danger.
justification: Gasoline leakage poses both environmental and fire hazards, making it likely to cause an incident.

incident_description:
The consumer was in the kitchen looking out the back window when he noticed smoke. The consumer went to his back porch and noticed that one of the wall lamps was on fire. The porch steps and the grass below the steps also caught fire from the lamp. The consumer put the fire out with water. 

The consumer states that the lamps were located on two supporting posts: one at the top and one at the bottom of the steps; the latter was the one that exploded.

05/28/2017 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer via e-mail explaining the situation. He has yet to receive a response.

The consumer states the wall lamps came on every night for two to three minutes when they detected motion however the consumer noticed that sometimes they would stay on for hours.

The consumer plans on keeping the wall lamp for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire that could have escalated, making it an incident with potential for injury.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Products Safety Commission:

On July 5th I sent Ryobi Tools the following email:

Tonight July 5, 2017 my wife was operating our Ryobi One+ 18-Volt Lithium-Ion Cordless Jet Fan Leaf Blower (Model # P2108, Serial # EU16291D080162) that we bought at Home Depot in October of 2016 when the orange plastic fan inside the unit disintegrated into pieces which discharged through the housing and the electric motor started smoking. My wife immediately threw it down and ran. To say the least, she was shaken up, but fortunately not seriously injured. I have been a New Jersey attorney for over 35 years and can tell you this is definitely a defective product - for the exact same reasons as the electric one you previously recalled (MODEL [REDACTED]). You are on Notice, and this defective product should be recalled immediately before anyone gets injured by flying fan pieces or the electric motor catching fire or lithium battery exploding as a result. I just called this in to your 800-860-4050 # (Refer to Customer # [REDACTED]) and your representative told me to take it to a repair center in Somerville or Bound Brook be repaired. That is not acceptable! For the same reasons as you'll see below with your other recall, I demand a replacement; or a full refund for our cost of the blower, the 2 lithium batteries, and the battery charger.

See Recall Date: March 2, 2017, Recall Number: [REDACTED], One World Technologies Recalls Electric Blowers Due to Laceration Hazard. But I now see that they were being recalled for the same defect.

"Hazard: The plastic fan inside the blower can break causing the fan blades to be discharged from either end of the blower tube, posing a laceration hazard. 
Remedy: Replace 
Consumers should immediately stop using the recalled electric blowers and contact One World Technologies, Inc. for a free replacement."

_______________________________

Because this defect has already caused personal injuries in their electric cord model of the exact same design,  and because IÃÂm receiving no response, I have called Ryobi numerous times only to be told by their Customer Service people that my complaint is at the Products Safety Department in a stack of complaints and will be tended to on an ÃÂas received basis which should be in 10 to 14 business daysÃÂ.  They refused to escalate it nor allow me to talk to anyone in their Safety Department.  This is irresponsible and outrageous.  I ask that you folks contact them and request that they recall this product before more people get injured.  

Thank you.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a product malfunction that could have caused lacerations, matching the hazard described in the previous recall.

incident_description:
I purchased a char broil grill from Lowes, model number 463625217, a few months ago. Within 2 weeks, the ignitor was no longer functioning. I contacted Char broil and replacement parts were mailed to me with no instructions.

I watched a few "You Tubes" on how to change ignitor and completed the process on my grill without difficulty.  I went to turn grill on, and smoke began to come out from under where the replaced ignitor box was located, and then, flames began pouring out from where the ignitor box was located. 
I was trying to turn gas valve off of tank, but flames were preventing me from doing so. Finally, I was able to reach in to the tank and close the gas valve. The fire ceased.
justification: The incident resulted in a fire, which could have caused injury.

incident_description: I own a john Deere 100 series lawn tractor bought it new at Lowe's the problem with the tractor is that the steering has broken several times since I have own this tractor and is very dangerous when mowing and  the steering fails. I have repaired the tractor twice and it breaks only after one summers use.
justification: Steering failure is likely to occur again given the history of repeated repairs.

incident_description: I made the modification to the Husqvarna Grass Trimmer per instructions and parts received from Husqvarna.  The gas leak still continues.  I will take the 122c to a dealer for repairs.
justification: While no injury was reported, the persistent gas leak poses a potential hazard, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

incident_description:
Model gr2210601-mm-00
Serial number  313161000575533


The grill was assembled by sams clubs associates when we purchased it.   We have had repeated issues with getting the grill to start and remain lit.   We have had two incidents that the grill has emitted a fireball of flames when attempting to light it.   The last incident involved my husband sustaining sever burns on his face and hands. 1st and 2nd degree burns.     The last fire caused two of the knobs to melt, after the grill actually caught on fire.   We had to use a fire extinguisher to put out the flames.  
Item that were damaged:

2 control knob bezel. Part number 8
1 grill body-hose regulator assembly. Part number 4v
2 control knob/side burner control knob. Part number 9
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns (1st and 2nd degree) to the husband, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Craftsman 20-In. Hedger Trimmer, Model Number 900.794410 had defective switch that appears not to work.  But, when I touched the cutter bar with the trigger switch in the "Off" position, it suddenly turned on.  This resulted in badly lacerated fingers.  The switch was completely Off with nothing touching it.  I've been able to safely test repeat the incident.    

The On / Off switch and safety does not turn the machine or On or Off.   It appears to be non-working.  However, if you touch the cutter bar it suddenly turns On.  

Other safety reports mention the switch has a problem of always being "On", but the cutter runs as soon as plugged in.  In my case, it may be similar but touching the cutter bar causes some other short to complete the circuit then turning it On.  This is especially dangerous as it is likely a person will want to inspect the bar with the unit Off (not realizing doing so will turn the cutter on).
justification: The defective switch caused the cutter to turn on unexpectedly when the user touched the bar, leading to lacerated fingers.

incident_description: Lawnmower caught on fire and burned up while mowing grass.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (lawnmower) but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
On Saturday morning the submitter's husband was mowing the lawn and noticed that the light was on the ground completely melted. The submitter's husband noticed a circular scorch mark on the grass and a foot long scorch mark on the side of the shed. The submitter indicated that it rained on Friday. 

The submitter indicated that the light was installed approximately 2 months ago.

The submitter plans to contact the firm to notify them of the incident.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the melted light and scorch marks indicate a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: The gasoline cap is a quarter turn type. The cap comes off while the machine is running resulting in gasoline spilling onto the engine. This has occurred several times.
justification: The incident has occurred several times, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I received an email from the US Consumer Product Safety Commission regarding the Cordless Electric Lawn Mowers Recalled Due to Fire Hazard; Made by Hongkong Sun Rise Trading. I purchased one of these mowers August 23rd, 2014 which falls in the date range for the recall. I am concerned at the potential fire hazard that this mower presents. At the time that I received that recall, I had not yet used the mower this season. During the first time using this mower, it remained very hot for much longer than it should have. I removed the battery in an effort to cool the unit down.
justification: While no injury occurred, the mower's excessive heat and potential fire hazard pose a significant risk.

incident_description:
LED Headlamp with rechargeable batteries purchased from Amazon exploded into flames when being charged. The explosion sent intensely hot material around the room causing multiple fires where the hot pieces landed. The unit has OUTERDO RJ-3000 printed on the larger light and has two smaller lights adjacent to the larger center light. It is listed on Amazon as manufactured by EOTO. Amazon list an identical LED Headlamp manufactured by Harugo. Both these lights look identical with the same features.

I was very lucky to have seen and put the fires out before spreading to the entire home!
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident could have caused significant property damage if not contained.

incident_description: My Energizer plug-in rechargeable flashlight caught fire, while plugged into the wall, in my garage. I was home at the time, was able to extinguish the fire fairly quickly, preventing it from becoming a major incident.
justification: Although the flashlight caught fire, no injuries were reported, and the incident was contained quickly.

incident_description: Front rims of Sears Lawn tractor split apart causing loss of stearing. First time I almost went into a fence. Riding mower was only 16 hours old. Second time the other rim disenegrated while mowing and also could not turn and went out into traffic. This second time occurred after approximately 30 hours. Material thickness of rim is too thin. Someone is going to get seriously hurt or killed because when it happens you cannot steer. I can provide pictures of Rims. Craftsman lawn tractor Model number 917-203921.
justification: Rims disintegrating twice in less than 30 hours of use, with potential for loss of control and injury.

incident_description: My son got that lantern for his birthday on March 2017. Since he had it the batteries kept popping out in the compartment that is secured by a screw. We had to unscrew the lid every time to fix the batteries, we changed batteries often and still kept popping out. One night my son told me that his lantern was getting hot, when I touched the bottom of it (where the batteries are located, ) it felt really hot, so I asked my husband to give it a look. He opened the battery compartment and one of the batteries was melted and the other 3 were hot. The lantern was not on when the incident happened.
justification: Batteries popping out frequently and lantern getting hot indicate a high likelihood of a similar incident recurring.

incident_description: American Tool Exchange item 94002 portable butane stove was used as a camp stove. Have used previously without issue. On first use on recent camping trip the stove appeared to ignite normally and with frying pan in place suddenly was consumed in a ball of fire. Was able to unload fuel canister while burning. Stove is no longer usable. I disassembled pressure regulator and found a metal part that should have been attached to the rubber diaphragm became detached resulting in a large hole in the rubber diaphragm allowing butane to vent into the butane canister storage compartment.
justification: The stove's malfunction due to a detached metal part caused a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
08/18/2017
Consumer stated he was using his riding lawnmower for about an hour cutting 4 acres of grass. He stated he became stuck in between a tree in the yard and the back wall of his home. He stated he was unable to shift gear from forward to reverse, so he powered off riding lawnmower using the key in the ignition to off position. He stated when he got off riding lawnmower he bruised/cut his right lower leg. He stated he went to the rear of lawnmower to pull transmission release lever, so he could remove lawnmower away from tree and his home. He said this is the first time this has happened. He feels this a design flaw with Tough Torque transmission and a safety hazard.
justification: Injury occurred due to user's inability to shift gears, indicating a possible design flaw in the transmission.

incident_description: I purchased the Flex Able Hose from Walmart in Huntington Beach, CA Talbert Ave  I attached a sprayer nozzle to the hose and turned on the water in my front yard.  The hose started to fill with water when the green fabric that is on the outside of the hose tore from the plastic fitting and started to fill with water like a long water balloon.  When I saw that, I bent down to turn off the water at the spigot when the balloon exploded in my face burning and cutting my right cheek to my chin and my left upper cheek bone.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the face, indicating a severity level of 3, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the unexpected failure of the hose.

incident_description:
Last month, when starting the lawnmower the cast-metal blade adapter (Part no. 748-0377C),  which orients the blade on the engine shaft, broke sending a piece of the adapter's collar into the blade flinging it out from under mower. In other words, a cast metal part that holds the blade to the lawn mower engine became a piece of shrapnel. 

The lawn mower is an 11-year old, Series 420 walk-behind, gas-powered, rotary mower with a 21 inch blade that is manufactured by MTD LLC (Model No. 11A429R729  S/N IC281I11486). 

While the adapter is subject to a lot of stress, the cast part must have had a defect for it to break. I have saved the original part as well as high resolution pictures.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident could have caused harm if someone was nearby when the blade was flung out.

incident_description:
In March 2016 I purchased a Stok BBQ grill from Tool Direct a retailer for company owned products such as Ryobi Tools, [REDACTED] among others from an outlet at [REDACTED].
The  grill, still in warranty and used very little and taken extremely good care of exploded causing $14,500.00 damage to my home , burns to my face, arms, forearms, and top of my head.
I contacted the Arkansas State Police Capt [REDACTED] and an investigator was dispatched to my home . The results were to be found the fire was a defective fuel regulator burning though the fuel supply line from the propane that caused a massive fire with force under pressure,
I contacted Stok Grills A me. [REDACTED] concluded to his findings that the fire was caused by either a defective fuel supply line of operator error.
I learned Stok Grill recalled over 40,000 grills in 2012 2013. They states there were over 500 events that caused no injuries or property damage.
justification: Injuries were sustained due to a defective fuel regulator, as confirmed by the Arkansas State Police.

incident_description:
I have a Cub Cadet lawnmower that I purchased 2 years ago that was brand new at the time. Well today when I was done cutting grass I shut it off and the engine burst into flames in which I was able to contain and extinguish the fire before any major damage to my home but sustained injuries on my hand to include blisters and lacerations. So far after trying to contact the manufacturer I have been unsuccessful due to being transferred from department to different department. The lawnmower in question is a cub cadet xt1, 46 inch deck with a Koehler 22hp engine.

It appears that the current company in question does not have a concern in assisting me and I am looking at having to get the media as well as a lawyer to assist me in resolving this matter.
justification: Injuries sustained (blisters and lacerations) warrant a severity level of 3, and the likelihood of such an event occurring (engine burst into flames) is possible, hence a likelihood of 3.

incident_description:
The Gold Armour charger does not use an isolated supply.  Instead, one of the battery terminals has a direct path to the mains through a fuse and a diode as illustrated with the hand drawn circuit.  The other side is not isolated either.  Interestingly, it does not matter which way the plug is inserted, so even if it had a polarized plug, it would not be any safer, for up to 160VDC is present on the battery terminals regardless of orientation. 

I discovered this by inserting the battery while standing barefoot on a concrete floor.  I then measured 160 volts DC from the battery terminals relative to ground.
justification: Direct path to mains and lack of isolation pose a high risk of electric shock, as demonstrated by the incident.

incident_description:
I purchased an outside Weber summit s 670 grill from Lowes on 05-25-2016 after using the grill for 3 months I start having issues with the roatesty motor and the burners will go out and come back on. At one point grill start making loud bang noises.
I have contacted the Weber and emailed, I communicated with coustomer service representative [REDACTED]. He said that he will ship the replacement parts to the local repair shop. I have contacted the independent contractor and have them look at the grill. I was told the fault is with the main gas flow tubing abs no matter what it will cause the issues. I have requested to have the grill replaced, I was told that Weber will not replace the grill.
I'm reaching out to see if I can get any help and have people aware of the issues I have been facing.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning grill, causing inconvenience and potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that he experienced similar problems with his backpack blower as recall #12-118.  Hazard: The fuel line between the fuel tank and carburetor could have been damaged during assembly leading to fuel leakage, posing a fire hazard.

The caller had no problems with this riding motor until Monday, June 12, 2017 after She had been cutting grass around 30 to 45 minutes then parked it, walked away from it then realized when she glanced back at it that it was in flames.
She was able to push the riding mower away from the buildings it was parked near.
She did have to visit her chiropractor the following day for pain in her arms, knees, back and neck.
She did contact the manufacturer June 15, 2017 and they referred her to CPSC.

I was using my leaf blower to blow off my back porch. I don't have a lot of strength because I am going through chemo therapy- my arms were tired so I rested the blower against my left leg. The blower exploded- it happened to be the part that was up against my leg that busted/blew up and shot fire and plastic. I threw it down and ran away from it. It was shooting tiny plastic pieces everywhere and making loud noises for about a minute before it finally shut off. 
Thankfully I didn't have to get stitches and it was no worse than it was. Unfortunately, it takes me a while to heal due to my current fight with cancer...now I'm having to baby a huge place on my upper thigh.

The flame keeps going out and because you can't see through the metal plates I can't tell if it;'s still lit or not?  When I check to see if the gas is still ignited by clicking the igniter, the gas explodes and pop's the iron plates up into the air. I have tried resetting the gas regulator and when that didn't work I even replaced the regulator, but my flame is still cutting out while still letting out gas and making a very dangerous situation.

incident_description: I was using my Nexgrill (model # 720-0864) gas grill to make dinner just now.  I set the heat to low and went in the house to cut vegetables.  I came out 5 minutes later to check the grill and it was SCORCHING hot.  I was barefoot and noticed the cement in front of it was hot, the patio chair near it was hot, the flowers along the fence behind it were hot.  I opened the grill lid and the flame was low where I had set it but the heat was unbearable.  The cooking grates were light gray instead of their normal dark black. The inside of the lid was burned as well as the front and sides of the outside of the lid.  I knew I had to immediately turn off the gas under the grill and the nozzle of the gas tank was hot! I hurt my hand but had to turn off the gas so the thing didn't blow up!  I've never seen such a thing in my whole life and I've been grilling on gas grills for almost 20 years.  The temperature gage on the grill was all the way over to the right even though I had the flame set on low! I am absolutely shocked - I could have been seriously injured or killed just now trying to grill our dinner.  Thank God I didn't pull the grill near my house or car.  I have pictures of the charred grill if you need them. Someone needs to document this and contact Nexgrill before someone gets hurt or killed.

incident_description: My husband had cooked on our Blue Ember barbecue, model number FG50069.  He finished cooking, turned the burners and the propane tank off, and went inside to eat dinner with our two sons.  Approximately 15-20 minutes after turning the grill off, he heard a strange noise outside on our patio.  Upon inspection, he found the grill and propane tank on fire from an apparent explosion.  A second explosion followed while he was trying to put the fire out, which resulted in a fire that has likely caused the complete loss of our home and most of our belongings.  He received small burns to his ear as well, and miscellaneous abrasions and bruises resulting from trying to fight the fire with a garden hose while awaiting the arrival of the fire department.  There is a recall for this grill, for which we never received notification.  Several other incidents involving injuries and loss of property are noted in the comments of various articles regarding this recall.
justification: Injury occurred due to explosions while attempting to extinguish the fire, despite no initial injuries.

While cutting the grass the lawn mower was working fine.  After I finished mowing the lawn I went to clean the lawn mower and I notice a bolt had fallen out.  The bolt fell from  the right side cutting blade which has two blades one on the left and one on the right.  The right side had fallen out of the housing then I notice that another bolt had fallen off.

I mailed the warranty card in when I purchased the lawnmower back in May of 2016.  Hopefully you got my warranty card.  I want to know what can I do to get my lawnmower fixed or replaced since this is a recall product and safety hazard.

Thank you
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a recalled lawnmower with loose bolts, posing a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
I am writing today with a report of a product sold to consumers which I believe is quite unsafe.  My opinion is based on my Electrical Engineering training (B.S. with honors, Pennsylvania EIT certification on the way to PE status), as well as common sense. 

A few years ago, I visited LowesÃÂ hardware store in Homestead, PA and purchased an ETL- and UL-listed Portfolio (LowesÃÂ-owned brand) outdoor wall lantern, item #253849.  This contained within it a UL-listed 2SW9 Lampholder (socket base) stamped with the code ÃÂE230757 JHE26 JINHAI ZHEJIANGÃÂ rated for 250V, 660W.  On the first occasion when I needed to change the bulb (very recently, because I used a CFL), I attempted to unscrew the bulb from the socket.  I then found that whatever was supposed to hold the socket in place was not really there.  Thus, when I twisted the bulb, it twisted not just the base of the bulb but the socket it was in and the multi-stranded wires that fed the socket.  The twisting force in the multi-stranded wires leading to the socket caused the weak insulation to strip off.   Some of the now-exposed strands from supply and return lines were then able to arc/short directly.  That part of the unit exploded in a shower of sparks.  Fortunately, an AFCI breaker cut the power on the circuit pretty quickly.  

I also took some close-up photos of where the twisting caused insulation to be removed, the most illustrative of which are attached, or provide the product itself. 

The design and manufacturing of this unit appears to have been very unsafe, with the item posing a serious fire hazard.   This report is not a post-mortem investigation following a serious fire or personal injury/death, but it is easy to see how such an outcome could have resulted, and may be the outcome in other cases (past or future).   I encourage you to take corrective action in order to protect other customers from these negative outcomes.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in a serious fire, posing a significant risk to users.

incident_description: I had a "Ever Brite" solar light mounted on my deck for a few months. Yesterday, while at work, my neighbor called and told me there was popping coming from my yard. When he looked over there was a fire on the corner of my deck. He jumped the fence and put out the fire with a blanket. It seems as if the battery in the solar light exploded and cause the fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire could have spread and caused property damage, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The ignitor system had stopped working on my gas grill. I removed the heat distribution plates over the gas burners to clean the ignitor contacts and noticed that the horizontal gas distribution tube had rusted through and was cracked. I shut off the main gas line and removed it. Large pieces of the tube fell off the assembly.

I have ordered a new part and am glad that I discovered this as it would have caused a gas leak in the grill and possibly an explosion. I have reported it because there is a chance that other consumers are using the same grill with the same safety issues.
justification: Although no immediate harm occurred, the incident could have led to a gas leak and potential explosion, hence the severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This consumer was using his electric leaf blower to blow leaves out from under his hood when there was a large bang sound then a kick feeling then the nozzle fell off the end of the blower and went into the engine compartment of his vehicle.
There are twelve veins and when he opened the blower he saw that one had blown off.
He was not injured.
He is reporting this incident as an injury hazard.  
The nozzle could have gone outward or upward depending upon thrust or position and injured the user or persons standing nearby.
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer and said that he may contact them.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved a high-energy projectile (nozzle) that could have caused harm, making it an incident with potential injury.

incident_description: This is an electric Homelite blower vacuum Model UT42120.  It already has a different recall,  but wanted to add that the brass on the plugin came off and stuck in my extension cord and I could not dig it out, so had to throw away a brand new extension cord. incident_description:
This is an electric BBQ powered by an electric 110 volt wall outlet. The on/Off switch is not in any way prevented from turning on by the usual Push In (indent) method used for example in an electric range. The knob moves freely from its off position to any one of 5 power numbers simply by turning the knob.
The plastic weather cover which is made by Char-Broil for this unit upon placing it over the BBQ invariably will turn the unit on. A red light behind the knob indicating that the unit is on is thus concealed. The BBQ will ignite the cover and thus create a fire. We have the unit placed on a porch on the second floor of a condominium. If we had not noticed this problem and thus avoided it by always unplugging the unit after use I'm confident we would have experienced a serious fire.
justification: The BBQ's design flaw, where the cover can turn it on and conceal the power indicator, increases the likelihood of an incident, potentially leading to a serious fire.
