incident_description:
I had my gazebo collapse under 4 inches of snow and damaging the patio furniture underneath. Luckily no one was hurt.

The company behind the gazebo is BOND VAST INDUSTRIAL LIMITED

This is the exact model:
https://bondvast.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/203465029-Style-Parkside-Wicker-Gazebo?mobile_site=false

It comes with 1-year warranty that excludes "extreme weather conditions such as thunderstorm and windstorm".

When I contacted the company looking for a compensation I was told the warranty does not cover any "weather-related damage" and the second reason for not being covered was that they discontinued the product.

There was no extreme weather when the accident happened. There was no thunderstorm or windstorm either. The product should withstand 4 inches of snow and not collapse. I identified the weak part - a plastic roof connector that has no strength to properly support the roof. I pointed out this to the company and asked to speak with a manager but was simply ignored.

This is a dangerous product that can hurt someone and a company that does not stand behind their product.
justification: Although no one was injured this time, the gazebo's collapse under normal snow conditions poses a potential injury risk in future similar situations.

incident_description: In September of 2016 I was grilling outside my house using my Weber Spirit Gas Grill (Serial Number NT6307550). I went inside for a moment to get a plate and when I came out I smelled burning plastic. I opened the grill and didn't see anything awry but noticed that there was a flame shooting out of the gas supply line leading from the propane tank to the burners. I immediately turned off the gas at the propane tank and extinguished the fire. Upon examination I found that the ignition switch and one of the burner knobs had melted, dripped onto the gas supply line and eaten through it such that it developed a pinhole leak. This happened in the span of 2-5 minutes. I've dutifully cleaned and service this grill (purchase in September of 2008) and never had any issues. I've reported what happened to Weber but have not heard a response. I googled what had happened and found other people mentioning their igniter switch had malfunctioned and melted the entire assembly as it appears to have done for me. There appears to be a defect and this could have been catastrophic had I not been able to turn the gas supply off.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to a defect in the grill's ignition system, making it an incident with a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I was using a new Husquavarna riding mower when it tipped over and rolled several times, finally pinning me against a tree. The cutting blades would not turn off, and were passing less than 6inches from my neck. I could easily have been decapitated. Finally the engine stalled but I was trapped for hours. A roll bar would not have helped.

If a Husquavarna turns upside down the blades should stop to prevent death or injury! I was trapped in the seat, so the motor did not stop. 

I want a replacement that is safe and will not decapitate me!
justification: The incident resulted in injury and could have easily been fatal due to the blades not stopping, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description:
(08/29/2014) The consumer stated that the unit was being operated by a co-worker for a couple of hours. The co-worker was cutting a ballfield. He heard a banging noise coming from underneath the cutting deck. The co-worker felt heat in his feet area. He got off of the mower. The mower immediately caught on fire.

No injuries.


(09/2014) The company was contacted by [REDACTED]-Recreational Director. She was advised that the two year warranty does not cover fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a mower catching fire, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
(09/02/2016) The consumer stated that the product was plugged in outside because She was going to trim a holly tree. The consumer stepped up three rungs of the ladder. She started the product to trim the tree. When she pressed the button to start the product, fire came out of the product near the on/off button. When the consumer tried to turn the product off, it would not turn off. 

The consumer tossed the product to her right to prevent the fire from getting next to her house. When she did this, blade was engaged & on and balance was thrown off and fell off of the ladder. The consumer injured her right knee when she fell because her foot got caught in the ladder. 

The consumer called the paramedics and was taken to the hospital. Her right knee was fractured in 45 places. The consumer was admitted to the hospital. 

(06/08/2017) The consumer contacted the firm and provided information concerning the product and the incident. The firm also wanted to know why it took so long for the consumer to contact them.

The firm also asked the consumer to send the product to them.
justification: Injury occurred due to product malfunction, with likelihood of occurrence being possible given the consumer's actions and product's failure.

incident_description: This is a Ryobi rechargable air pump and battery. Ive had it for about 2+ years without issue. Then after a charge the night before I was using it to inflate my car tire as ive done in the past. It started fine but after maybe 5 minutes it started to struggle and then suddenly stopped when I checked it there was white smoke comming out of it the battery had a charred smokey smell to it as well.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in damage to the air pump, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: Hello, I purchased a Toro Super Recycler lawn mower S/N 220001040, With a Briggs & Stratton  GTS 6.5 HP, S/N 124K02-0110-B1 01102059,  3 years ago the fuel tank started to drip occasionally, I checked the fuel line and it was Not leaking, So I Contacted Toro and was told It was not their problem?  So we continued to use the mower, Last year it started dripping worse we could only fill the fuel tank half way to avoid this leak, This year We have a Full Blown Leak that streams fuel out!!  I inspected the tank with a flashlight and and can clearly see that the seam in the {Plastic fuel tank  were the to 2 half's of the tank are joined together are split} THIS NOW IS A FIRE HAZARD to my wife and son how use this mower!!  I called Toro again and this time I was told the fuel tank was supplied with the motor made by Briggs & Stratton and to Contact them. I called Briggs & Stratton Today, I was told that the fuel tank was not covered by the warranty as it has expired????? and wanted me to contact another company were I could purchase a replacement.    How does a plastic fuel tank wear out????  The mower is kept in a garage and has always been taken care of it runs Great and Cuts Great! So again How does a plastic fuel tank wear out????  It's not a blade that has to be changed or an air filter or spark plug that has to be kept serviced! It's a fuel tank that in fact should last the life of the Mower.  Please Give Me Some Help with this issue!!! I truly believe that this is in fact a manufactured Defect! And Needs To Be Addressed ASAP  My case number with B&S is [REDACTED] I feel this company does NOT in fact Support their products when Defective.  Thanks Please respond to this email, ASAP  Thanks You For Your Time.  Sincerely   [REDACTED]
justification: Fuel leak poses a fire hazard to users, with the potential for escalation.

incident_description: The Husquvarna 21" lawn mower 5521P has a gas cap that continues to come off in use.  The last time it did for me it ended up under the mover and in pieces.  When it comes off gas comes out and is a safety hazard.  The OEM replacement cap 799585 is even worse.  See reviews on Amazon for others with the same problem/concern.
justification: The gas cap coming off during use is a recurring issue, as evidenced by customer reviews, posing a safety hazard with gas spills.

incident_description:
Sliced finger. The only way to remove the Cuisinart Grillster Portable Grill from the box is to lift it by holding the front and the back. The back has air vents that are punched out of the steel sheet and are razor sharp (see photo).  Part of the tip of my little finger on my right hand was sliced off. Due to profuse bleeding, it required emergency stitches. And, it was quite painful.

There is no other way to remove the Grill from the box as the ends are encased in styrofoam blocks.
justification: The sharp edges of the air vents caused a severe injury, requiring stitches.

incident_description:
I purchased a Portfolio outdoor post light #0109348, from Lowes.com. It had 18 side glass panels, and all 18 glass panels were loose. The panels were not properly secured during manufacturing.  All of the nuts on the panel retaining rods were loose, and seven of the nuts had actually fallen off into the packaging. This allowed the glass panels to rattle around and chip or crack. 

As I unpacked the light fixture, prior to installation, I sliced my left thumb open on a one-inch glass shard that was protruding from the bubble wrap.  I could not see the glass shard, and had no reason to expect it prior to examining the light. I have saved the glass shard. 

I believe the glass shard chipped off one of the loose glass panels, causing a danger to anyone who tries to unpack or install one of these lights. 

I have contacted Lowes several times, but have received little or no cooperation.  It appears that the Portfolio lights are made by Lowes or a related company.
justification: Injury occurred due to loose glass panels and protruding shard, likely to recur given the packaging and manufacturing issues.

incident_description: The product is a solar powered exterior LED light fixture with Li-ion batteries inside.  It was installed for about 1 month on the exterior of a metal covered pole barn.  After about a month of use when entering the barn I smelled a strong burning electrical/plastic smell.  After checking all interior wiring, I determined the smell was coming from the LED fixture outside above the door.  There was scorching of the metal siding of the barn above the fixture and when I unscrewed it from the wall, I found that the plastic of the fixture was melted and that one of the Li-ion batteries had exploded!  If the barn had not been made of metal, it probably would have caught fire
justification: The explosion of the Li-ion battery and melting of the fixture's plastic indicate a severe incident with potential for injury, despite no reported injuries.

incident_description:
The "catch tray" under the gas burner has caught fire twice. I believe it is much too close to the flames of the burners. The grill was only used twice after cleaning the tray. The previous design was a deep tray witch kept the tray away from the flames. I will never feel comfortable using this grill without cleaning the tray first. It is at best very poor design, impractical and most importantly a fire hazard. I called customer service at Weber Grills and they took my information, told me this was a new tray designed for 2017, and told me they Have not any other complaints of this issue, however I think it's very dangerous design, 
The grill model is 
Weber spirit E310
justification: The grill's design places the catch tray too close to the flames, causing it to catch fire twice, posing a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: Purchased a assembled Charbroil 3 burn quickset grill from Lowe's in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. Took home and checked out per instruction guide and attached to propane tank. Observed all precautions. The grill had a push-button ignitor. After opening the valve on the tank and with the grill top open, pushed the ignitor, The propane ignited in the based of the grill and then caught fire, moving down the connecting hose to the tank. Luckily I had an extinguisher close buy and was able to extinguish the fire. On examination, the valve attachment on the hose had a leak that allowed the propane under pressure to escape and catch fire.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the valve attachment leak.

incident_description: less than three year old Troy Bilt Mustang mower caught fire an burned. only had a few seconds to escape.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such an event to occur, it's not common.

incident_description: I was cutting my front yard after refueling when for no apparent reason, the engine just quit.  Having had trouble with the safety seat interlock before, I raised up off the seat to see what was going on. When I did, I smelled smoke and saw flames coming from the engine area.  I jumped off the unit and ran to the house to get a garden hose.  By the time I got back, the entire rear of the engine was engulfed in flames.(My wife took pictures) After about 5-10 minutes, I had the fire out and kept cooling the unit with water.  Later that day, after googling "Cub Cadet Fire Hazard" I called the manufacturer, MTD, in Ohio and mentioned that over 4300 units had been recalled for a fire hazard.  The initial rep as much as called me a liar, he said there was only an "advisory" issued for the units.  I then spoke to his supervisor and was told because my model number was not on their recall list, they would accept no responsibility whatsoever for my unit catching fire.  I had taken my unit to a authorized service center for the seat problem prior to that and nothing was ever said to me about a fire hazard possibility.  I purchased the unit new from Tractor Supply Corp in June 2011.  The unit only had 122 hours on its hour meter when it caught fire.  The supervisor had stated there WAS a recall and it was due to a grommet attached to the fuel tank that was causing the problems, but they could not/would not do anything to compensate me for my loss.  I have contacted my homeowners insurance company and that is still pending.
justification: Injury occurred due to the user's proximity to the flames while attempting to extinguish the fire, despite no fatalities.

incident_description:
Sears Craftsman T2500 lawn tractor
The accelerator pedal is almost fully perpendicular to the ground and about 6" above the foot rest.  A foot cannot be put into position to press the pedal in a controlled manner without threatening an orthopedic injury (unless you have [REDACTED] size 26 feet!).  The alternative is to balance the foot on the top edge of the pedal where there is no control of speed.  This, of course, creates a danger of a runaway lawn tractor with the mowing blade engaged.
Thankfully I have not had a safety incident yet but have suffered leg cramps and a sore ankle from the unnatural position.  I have owned the tractor 1 year and hoped I would somehow become used to it but it is no better.
I contacted Sears about this and got no reply.  Perhaps if the foot rest were built up 3 inches or so a normal foot could be rested on it and get some angle on the pedal, but really the pedal should have been set at a less perpendicular angle, just as automobiles have been for at least 75 years!
justification: The design of the accelerator pedal poses a high likelihood of orthopedic injury or loss of control, leading to potential accidents.

incident_description: I purchased Vigoro black colored mulch on two occasions in 2017.  After spreading the product in my landscaping each time, I noticed a severe sore throat, runny nose, and serious eye irritation.  I am concerned that this product has been treated with harmful and dangerous chemicals.
justification: Symptoms of sore throat, runny nose, and eye irritation indicate injury, and the recurrence in two occasions suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
On 5/23/17 we had a fire at our house caused by a Kobalt Electric Lawn Mower. There were no flames per se but some heat and lots of acidic smoke/soot. The soot contaminated our entire house. 

The Fire Forensic Investigator ([REDACTED]) has determined that we were not at fault in any way. The mower was not on a charger (physically impossible) and had been setting unused in the garage for several days when the fire started. Additionally, the Investigator showed that Kobalt had issued a Consumer Safety Recall just the day before for this model mower because it had been deemed a ÃÂFire Hazard.ÃÂ

As a result of the fire we have had to vacate our home since the fire and a restoration company is currently working to clean our home and our belongings. Because the soot/smoke was acidic, may of our items are being deposed.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident resulted in significant property damage and required evacuation, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I used my 2009 Cub Cadet RTZ mower that day to mow under 2 acres of lawn, as I do each and every week as needed since the day I bought it.  Please know that this mower was in excellent condition and was regularly maintained to assure proper running order and to extend the life of the mower.  It has had regular oil changes, the blades are replaced every year, the pulleys are checked as well and overall maintenance is provided with extra care in spring and fall.  I've never had a problem with the mower until May 17th? possibly 18th of this year 2017.

I mowed almost an acre and then parked the mower, cleared it from grass both on and under the mowing deck as well as clearing any grass and debri from the engine area.  I had a glass of water, took a little break, even had time for an ice cream cone...then I went back to work mowing the rest of the grass.

I finished with no problems at all, parked it in the shade and again cleared grass from all the areas described above as I do every time I use it.  I then proceed to raise the mower deck and drive it to the garage where I backed it in as I always do.  I shut it down, took off my ear protectors, put them in the side compartment, grabbed my flashlight that I use to see under the deck when I clean it and got off the mower.  I grabbed my drink and stood there for a moment drinking water and wiped some sweat away.  All in all I was probably in the garage for about 2 2 1/2 minutes.  I didn't notice anything out of the ordinary.  I finished my drink and started to walk home which is next door, about 300 feet or so.

I went into my house, immediately undressed and jumped into the shower.  I showered for approx 8-10 minutes and as soon as I opened the shower door I could smell smoke.  I looked out the window and black smoke was rolling across my lawn.  I threw on my bathrobe and ran to the front door, grabbed the phone and ran outside to the porch.  Immediately I could see a lot of smoke and flames coming from the side of the garage where I parked the mower.  I called 911 and asked for help.  I could feel the heat from my porch and knew that the fire was too out of control for me to do anything.

The neighbor lady, saw the smoke and came over, she walked down the road to get to the house and try to get the dog out.  She said she saw flames coming from right where the lawn mower was parked.  The other garage door was closed but she could tell that it was starting to engulf the entire garage.

The fire dept came out, tried to stop the fire but it took down the entire garage, the shed behind it, and burnt out the entire inside of the house.  Most of the structure of the house is still standing but it's completely burnt out.  Everything is gone.

The fire dept did their investigation and stated that the lawn mower was the cause of the fire and that it looked like something in the engine area burst out of it.  The company that my brother had content insurance through (is was my brothers garage and house) came out to investigate and tagged the mower with an orange tag that says Do Not Disturb, Evidence.

The insurance company is now trying to make a list of everything that was lost.

We don't know yet if it caught fire, or if the engine blew up or what but the mower was 100% positively the cause of the fire according to officials.

P.S. The dog was rescued.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage but no injuries, and the cause was a rare engine malfunction in a well-maintained lawn mower.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he was using his hedge clipper for approximately one minute when he noticed that his hip was wet from the unit leaking gas. Upon inspection, the consumer noticed the fuel tank split at the seam causing the leak. The consumer stopped using the unit.

05/10/2017 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that the issue may be due to normal wear and tear, or somebody could have damaged it.

The consumer indicates he uses his unit four or five times per year so it is like new and should not have been leaking.

The consumer plans on keeping his hedge clipper for at least the next thirty days.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a gas leak, posing a potential hazard.

incident_description:
I have a Chicago Electric brand electric chain saw item # 67255) purchased from Harbor Frieght in Centereach NY a couple of years ago. I used only a few times to trim a branch or two and cut some wood for my fire pit.  

Just the other day while cutting some wood, the power trigger seemed to stick in the on position. It took many times pressing and releasing to get the saw to stop. I found this dangerous and disturbing should it be a manufacturer defect,  effecting other units. 

I tried a few times after to see what it would do and it intermittently continued to stick with the power on and blade operating.

incident_description: While blowing off the patio, the orange fan blade exploded in to pieces. Our 18 month old son was playing nearby and was hit with a piece. Fortunately no injuries were sustained but he was quite frightened by the experience. I now see there is a recall but didn't know about it at the time of use. We have owned the blower for 6 months and used it maybe 8x.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the likelihood of a similar event happening again is possible due to the recall notice.

incident_description:
(03/05/2017) The consumer stated that he was taking the fence out of his truck. A sharp end of the fence was sticking out of the roll. The sharp end cut his index finger.

The consumer stated that he did not have on gloves. Also, there are no warning on the product.

incident_description: I received a tuft fracture with multiple  lacerations on my dominant left hand while I was using my craftsman 138.74899 leaf blower/vac. incident_description: USED once , started smoking and leaking oil . Bought last year
justification: The incident involved a vehicle starting to smoke and leak oil, which is an uncommon but possible occurrence.

incident_description: I WAS MOWING MY YARD AND WAS THROWN FROM THE SLICK SEAT TO THE GROUND SUSTAINING MINOR CUTS AND BRUISES.
justification: Injury occurred due to being thrown from the riding mower, which is a possible event given the machine's speed and the potential for loss of control.

incident_description:
while cutting yard with john deere zero turn tractor  Z355E 22hp. 48". made rt. turn at woodline.  turn or motion lever hung up and would not come out of turn mode. Spun around ,hit tree spun  again caught in hanging vines wrapped vines around me. pulled me from mower .Arms cut from top to bottom and bleeding. 2nd. time rt. turn hung up. aggravated old back injury  .  But xrays showed no new damage. Dressed cuts .They'll heal.

incident_description: We have a Char Broil Patio Bistro electric grill. The grill has a metal handle by which the entire unit is supposed to be lifted (rocking it backward onto its rear wheels) and then moved. Recently, after plugging it in, I was shocked quite badly by this metal handle. Then, when going to unplug it several minutes later, I noticed the plug and outlet as being excessively hot.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (shock) and the likelihood of it happening again is high given the consistent issue with the grill's handle and plug.

incident_description: I am an attorney and represent an Individual who suffered injuries to his back. My client purchased a Ferris riding lawn mower (Model IS700, Serial# 2016754908) in July of 2014. The machine was new and purchased from a Ferris dealer. On August 6, 2016 my client was mowing a straight, level section of lawn and the right rear axle broke, sending the machine into a tight right hand turn and wrenching my client's back. The machine was regularly maintained, had only 85 hours of use and there were no signs of the impending failure. I have since learned that there is a recall of a [REDACTED] riding mower based upon failure of the drive axle. As both Ferris and [REDACTED] are [REDACTED] companies, I am curious as to whether there is any connection between the failure of my client's mower and the Snapper failures.
justification: Injury occurred due to sudden axle failure, and likelihood is high as the machine was regularly maintained and had low usage hours.

incident_description: I was using the Ryobi 8amp Jet Fan when the the fan inside the blower broke off causing it to discharge from the end of the blower hitting me on the leg and arm.
justification: The fan breaking off and discharging from the blower resulted in injuries to the leg and arm, but no fatalities.

incident_description: I have bought three home lite weed wackers, and they all be defective, they are suppose to be auto feeders which means when you press the trigger / start button it automatically releases the line. The first weed wacker fed too much line and I got cut by it on my leg. The other two that I bought were not auto feeding all the time  and I had to pry the lids off to get the line to feed. WHen I did that and I would start the weed wacker again the line would feed even tho it was already OUT. Its a dangerous weed wacker, its very easy to get cut from the line feed because it doesnt auto feed when its suppose to all the time and if you manually do it and then turn it back on sometimes it feeds and you get  an excessive amount of line.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (cut on the leg) due to the weed wacker feeding too much line, indicating a high likelihood of similar occurrences.

incident_description: I was given a Masterbuilt Electric smoker for Christmas a year ago.  After about one year of use the whole unit thermostat plug into the unit and the receptor for it totally melted. I contacted masterbuilt and they have done nothing to resolve this issue. This could have resulted in a major fire.
justification: The melted thermostat and receptor posed a significant fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product is a John Deere D100 Serial # 1GXD100 FCCC310225 While Cutting my grass on an Incline brakes suddenly gave way and was unable to stop causing to roll into road. thankfully there was not any traffic at the time. I was able to avoid hitting a parked car and turned up the road to stop.
If there would have been traffic it would have turned out very bad.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in severe consequences if there had been traffic on the road.

incident_description: While operating my Kubota bx 2230 down a hill I was unable to turn my Kubota bx to the right to avoid hitting a tree with the front of my tractor , called my local Kubota dealer and was told that this is a none problem with these tractors but no recall has been issued. I don't understand why there are so many people having this problem and nothing is being done about it .
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
My complaint is about a Toro model 20334 Walk-Behind Rotary Lawn Mower with the ÃÂPersonal PaceÃÂ feature.  This a self-propeller lawn mower and the power assist has a throttle from which the term ÃÂPersonal PaceÃÂ is derived.  My concerns related to the fact that the power assist must be engaged in order to operate the mower.  The bar on which the user must push in order to operate the mower is, in fact, the throttle for the power assist; the ÃÂdead manÃÂsÃÂ control fits into a groove in the throttle.  The power assist cannot be disengaged; only its speed can be altered, and therein lies the rub.  Following are the issues I have with this product, which I sent to Toro earlier today:

(1)	The power is in the rear wheels.  Why is this a problem?  It makes pivoting difficult, especially if you need to pivot 180 degrees.  The only way to make a pivot is to push down on the handle and lift the front wheels.  With the power in the rear wheels, turning is difficult.  It also takes away an element of control over the machine (see #2 and #3, below).
(2)	You canÃÂt turn off the power assist ÃÂ it is always on.  This basically means that the user has lost an element of control over the machine.  Lawn mowers can be dangerous, and the last thing a user needs is to lose control of a dangerous machine.
(3)	Perhaps the worst flaw in this machine is that the power control is in the push handle.  Yes, I know this is supposed to be a ÃÂfeatureÃÂ, but it has serious drawbacks.  If your lawn has ANY bumps (and whose does not have bumps) the power bar moves, uncontrollably, when you hit a bump, causing the mower to lurch.  This is disconcerting at best, and makes mowing an even bigger chore than it is already. AND, once again, it causes the user to lose control of the machine.

I believe the ÃÂPersonal PaceÃÂ feature of this lawn mower is a total failure of engineering and tells me that Toro engineers do not use their own products, at least not in real world conditions.  I find it hard to believe that anyone could have my experience with this mower and come away thinking it was a good idea.
justification: The constant power assist and lack of control over the mower, especially when encountering bumps, increases the likelihood of an incident where the user loses control and potentially causes property damage or minor injuries.

incident_description: I HAVE 40 YEARS EXPERANCE RUNNING SAWS, ETC  AND THIS SAW CHAIN IS THE WORST,,,, FOR KICK BACK AND PINCHING . IT CAN KICK BACK WITH SUCH FORCE A LESSER EXPERANCED PERSON WILL ( I GUEARENTE) WILL SUFFER INJURY.
justification: The saw chain's tendency to kick back with great force, as described by an experienced user, increases the likelihood of injury, particularly for less experienced operators.

incident_description: Purchased a Char Broil gas grill about a year ago from Orscheln Farm & Home store.  I used the grill about 10 times with no problems.  Then while I was warming it up it exploded, setting my deck on fire.  The fire dept. had to put out the blaze.  CharBroil, claims no responsibility.  They said it was not the fault of the grill.  I suppose the deck exploded on its own??  They clearly have a design flaw, but refuse to admit it.  I could have been seriously injured had I been standing at the grill.  I requested compensation for the repairs to my house, but they pushed it off on their insurance company, which refused to pay.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the grill explosion caused a fire that required the fire department's intervention, making it a significant incident.

incident_description: I was using the blower to clean up the yard of dead leaves and other debris when the fan blade suddenly shattered and the broken pieces sprayed out of the blower end. Other broken pieces remained lodged in the blower housing. The blower was obviously no longer usable.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (blower rendered unusable) but no injuries, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is 'possible' as such incidents can occur due to wear and tear or manufacturing defects.

incident_description:
I purchased a Char-broil Bistro Gas Grill from Amazon (model number 15601900) about a month ago and in that short time of using it, the grill has simply had the burner flame go out by itself, on full head setting at least three times now. 
The item instructs that user to pre-heat it at least 5 minutes before use, and so I go out and light it as the instructions tell, but turning it to light position and pushing the electronic ignition until I hear the burner light (on this grill, one cannot see the burner flame, so all I can go on is the sound and the feeling of heat being produced). I then go inside to prepare the food that is to go on the grill. I come back out and the first two times, it was obvious as the temp meter had not moved. I turned it off, opened the grill to air out the gas that had built up (yes, the gas is still coming out when the burner flame has stopped), and then I do the procedure again and wait.
The third time, it had apparently heated up some and then went out (again...the temp knob is set to the hottest setting)...so I did not notice that the flame had gone out. I opened the lid and must have caused a spark, because the grill top flew out of my hand and opened with a loud explosion and blew me backwards away from the grill. I did not notice that I had all the hair on my right arm sindged off up to my shoulder and that my watch has been been burned on the strap and had melted into my skin. 
This thing is a danger and should be recalled and fixed. I love the grill, it is the perfect size for us and cooks everything well ..but i afraid to use it.
justification: The grill's spontaneous flame-outs and gas buildup led to an explosion, causing injury to the user.

incident_description:
On 4/13/17 at 01:45 hours, a structure fire was reported at the location provided.  The fire was limited to a Char-Broil gas BBQ, and I was requested to investigate the origin and cause the following day.

BBQ Information:
Char-Broil, LLC
Model # 463633316
SN # G361011602010083

The owners purchased the BBQ in October of 2016 from Walmart for about $100. The owners had used the BBQ about 7 hours prior to the fire.  The BBQ reached 550 degrees or more before it was turned down by shutting off the right burner and leaving the left burner on. The food (fish in a marinade that included oil) was cooked once the BBQ reached around 350 degrees.The BBQ was in like new condition, and this was the first use, or one of the first uses. The owners turned off the BBQ after cooking (which was verified through observation during the investigation), but did not turn the LP cylinder valve off.  

I conducted an origin and cause investigation, and observed the following:
- Based on observed damage, patterns and indicators, it appears that the fire originated at or below the heat shield, which is below the fire box (where the food is cooked).  It also appears that the fire originated somewhere along the hose between the regulator valve and the connection to the assembly that connects to the main burners, and probably occurred where the hose was touching or near the heat shield or cart side frame.  Fragments of the hose and melted plastic and aluminum were discovered on the bottom shelf that holds the LP cylinder. Burn patterns indicate that the greatest damage occurred along the hose near the front left corner of the BBQ.  

Based on the timeline of the fire, the probable cause of the fire was overheating of the hose initiating smoldering combustion that eventually caused the hose to be compromised and allowed LP gas to escape.  It is probable that the smoldering combustion was the ignition source for the diffuse fuel of LP gas and air.  Since the LP Gas container was on, there was a supply of fuel for the fire.

Although turning the LP cylinder valve off would have caused the fire to not continue, there still appears to be a potential safety concern of conductive or convective heat igniting the hose.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is possible given the identified cause.

incident_description: I bought a Husqvarna HU 725AWD, 725 EX push mower 3 yrs ago. I have always put STA-BIL in the gas, have always drained the gas tank at the end of each season before storing. This spring, the mower is leaking gas around the gas cap. The cap is perfect shape, i.e. the gasket is like new, and the cap is correctly and securely. I have replaced the air filter to no avail. I have "Googled" the problem and on numerous discussion boards, I am reading that not only this a VERY common problem, but it is due to ethanol content in the gas we buy - that we have no choice but to buy! Apparently, the ethanol ruins the carburetor. This is unacceptable and must violate consumer protection laws. I know it violates Maine's Implied Warranty of Merchantability which states when a product is purchased in Maine it must remain free of serious manufacturer's defects for up to 4 yrs from the original date of purchase. The CSPC must do something about this.
justification: The incident involves a common gas leak issue due to ethanol content in fuel, affecting many users, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description:
Gas grill issues.

I purchased a charbroil 463268407 grill.  It immediately had burner issues with the 2 TEC glass burners.  I contacted Lowes and was told the unit should not have been sold and had been recalled.  I contacted Charbroil back in about 2008 and had a battle on the phone with them about the safety of the grill.  They sent me 2 burners and offered no help with installation even though it was less than 3 weeks old.  They also sold me several hundred dollars worth of extra parts in case I needed them.  I went back to Lowes a couple of months later and was told there was nothing they could do.

Finally in 2014, push came to shove and Lowes sent somebody out to repair the grill one again for the burner issues.  Last summer, I could not turn the gas valves (I have used under 3 tanks of propane at this point) and was told the heat from the burners backfiring has caused the valves internally to expand and seize up.

I contacted Lowes who looked up the item number and transferred me to Charbroil.  I explained everything to them (3 different people) and finally spoke with a manager who treated me like I wanted something for nothing.  Safety is very important to me and was willing to ship unit or parts back to them so they could see who the gas valve seized.  I live in Texas so major cold or rust is not an issue.  He would hear nothing except to say he would send new burners and I would have to buy the other repair parts.  He then eluded to a 75.00 trade in for a 1000.00 plus grill.  I purchased the best grill that was on the market and have had issue after issue with it.  The customer rep when I told him I was disabled, said can't your wife fix it?  I explained that working with propane is something that an inexperienced person should not "mess" with.

For the record, I can afford to buy any grill I want to.  As with my customers, they expect to get their moneys worth.  I am reporting this on the safety aspect and not the financial.  Charbroil automatically thinks you are out for something for free.

You need to investigate the replacement burners and the gas valves due to fatigue and heat stress.
justification: Despite multiple attempts to resolve issues, the grill's burners and valves continue to malfunction, posing a risk of fire or explosion.

I have contacted the company and they immediately had me send the flashlight back for them to do a discovery on it. They have not. They just wanted to send me a check for $500.00 and sign a release.

incident_description:
While using an outdoor fire pit, one or more lava rocks in the fire pit exploded sending burning hot shards and rock fragments in multiple directions.  Fortunately, no-one was hit by the fragments, and therefore no-one was hurt; however, this presented a very dangerous situation.

The fire pit was purchased from Mark Concrete, Inc. in Moss Landing, CA (831-632-0845).  The fire pit consists of: "SS burner pan, SS 24" Penta burner, flex lines, valve, and lava base rock; BTU 150k.

I have retained some of the burned lava rock fragments.  I have also reported the situation to Mark Concrete, Inc., who states that what I witnessed was impossible.  However, I have both the fragments and several eye witnesses who will attest to the exploding rock(s).

incident_description: Gas Weber grill has three knobs on it to control the gas on the front. The knobs are extremely easy to turn. They need to be pushed to turn, but with the knobs on the front the grill cover will easily push them in. In the wind the cover moves and turns the knobs on. We have found our gas grill on many times when we uncover it, and it is connected to the house natural gas line. We will be outside and smell gas and immediately go to the grill. The knob design in unsafe. I contacted Weber about the problem and they sent me a new grill cover because they thought that was the problem, but it is not. The knob design is terrible and requires almost no effort to turn them on.
justification: The grill's knob design allows for accidental activation by wind, posing a high likelihood of gas leaks, which could lead to an incident.

incident_description: On April 15th, 2017 at approximately 4:30 pm est, my brand new Dyna-Glo 5-Burner LP Gas Grill with Side Burner Model# DGF510SBP caught on fire and burned my home. The grill was purchased less than 30 days prior at the Home Depot in Cape Coral, Florida. This was our first time not cooking chicken on the grill and I believe our third or fourth time using the grill. The incident began when my wife placed 6 homemade burgers on the grill on a lower heat and closed the lid. She turned around to situate the vegetables to place on the grill for cooking when we noticed flames coming out all sides of the grill which caught the regulator and propane tank on fire. The high flames immediately ignited our house windows, ceiling, walls, door and other nearby items aflame. As the propane hose hangs directly under the side burner, next to the "hole for viewing the flame";  flames spewed onto the hose through this hole causing the hose to melt igniting the propane tank into a ball of fire. The fire shooting from the hose and flaming propane tank caused first degree burns on my arms and hands, as well as more of my hair was singed. In addition, I suffered injuries to my neck, shoulder and back trying to put it out. My property suffered in excess of $10,000 in damages as the insurance company is still assessing the damages.
justification: Injuries occurred due to direct contact with flames and attempting to extinguish the fire.

There are sharp medal edges that protude from the tub. When I picked it up the metal edge sliced my finger, causing me severe pain and bleeding. The Lowes staff had to call an ambulance and I had to have stitches and a tetanus shot. The staff said all the tubs had the same defect and the manager had them all removed from the floor. They kept the product as evidence.

incident_description: I used my MTD Yard Machines 28" Snow Thrower twice this winter after purchasing it online and having it delivered.  It worked fine the first snowfall, no problems.  14Mar17 I used it the second time and while clearing snow and ice the discharge chute blew-off and flew wild and a Vesuvius of snow and debris blasted straight up and about with considerable force, hitting me about the head and shoulders and landing on property and vehicles near-by.  I had to attach the chute when delivered and I followed the instructions precisely, had I erred?  I reattached the chute as instructed and assured it was correct and secured with its three clips and I cleared more snow ... cautiously.  It blew-off again some minutes later!!  I was wearing face and eye protection both times and had I not been wearing it I'd have received facial and eye injuries, at least.  Someone's going to be seriously injured with this crummy design!  The chute is attached with three flimsy plastic clips to a very narrow plastic track on which the chute revolves.  The force of discharging snow, ice and whatever vibrates the chute and the thing just comes off and flies into the air, wild, and all the material comes straight up, flung with force by the snow thrower impeller.  This is lousy design, period.  The rest of the machine is terrific.  This is a true Achilles Heel and dangerous to consumers.  I'd fire the designer and the guy who approve the machine for sale!  I have video clip from surveillance camera showing one blow-off.
justification: The chute's design flaw, which caused it to dislodge twice, poses a high likelihood of causing facial and eye injuries.

incident_description: I purchased a Toro Power Curve CCR 2450 GTS in 2008. It is used 2-3 times a year. When priming the gas for a cold start, I have always noticed gas spilling out from the choke switch. This year the unit would not start, and I researched how to start it and sprayed carb cleaner into the carburetor. It started after this, but gas continues to leak from the carburetor. Now the engine is surging. After more research, I have learned the carburetor is made of plastic and the engines heat may cause the carburetor to warp which  can cause the engine to surge and gas to leak.  This same model was recalled for the same issue for the 2002 models. I have the 2007 model.  I have contacted the manufacturer to ask for a replacement part. I'm assuming it is the same part for the 2002 models. The faulty carburetor is a potential safety concern because of the engine surges and a potential fire concern because of the gas leakage.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to gas leakage and engine surges, as evidenced by the recall of similar models and the manufacturer's acknowledgment of the issue.

incident_description: I ordered a BlueRhino outdoor gas firepit from Wells Fargo Rewards Catalog that is fueled by a propane tank. I assembled it exactly as instructed and used it right away. The instructions state to turn off the gas on the tank when finished. I attempted to do so but the tank knob was extremely hot due to the firepit. After letting it cool, I finally was able to turn the gas off. The next time I used this product, the flame went out. After trying to re-light it without success, I looked below in the cabinet where the tank is stored and i noticed that the rubber supply line going to the burners had melted to the bottom of the fire pan. This caused a kink in the line thus no gas could get to the burner. I then called Rhino and was told that the heat shield may have not been working properly so they sent me an entire new burner and register with pan. Again, I installed it as instructed and it worked fine for the first couple of times. On the third time I used it, the burner once again went out. I immediately looked below at the tank and once again the gas supply line melted to the bottom of the pan. Also, the tank was extremely hot to the touch. This is an extremely dangerous item and I was concerned that it could have blown up. I called Rhino once again and they refused to do anything stating to me that i would need to purchase a new register and pan. This product is extremely dangerous and i had no interest in purchasing anything additional for this unsafe product. I also have pictures to back up my claim
justification: The incident occurred twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence despite attempted repairs.

incident_description:
On 12/19/16, I met with Tecumseh Public Schools Super (TPS) intendant [REDACTED], and the [REDACTED] to investigate a complaint of a pesticide being placed in a Pre-K classroom during the first week of December.  [REDACTED] informed me that initially on December 7th, a strong odor in the Krouch Early Childhood Center caused the school to have to be evacuated. [REDACTED] stated that the Tecumseh Fire Department and Oklahoma Natural Gas was called out to check for hazards.  The odor was pinpointed to one classroom, but they could not determine cause of the odor or if the odor was hazardous, and the students were able to return to the building, but not to the classroom where the odor was originating from.  [REDACTED] stated that the next day [REDACTED] who has been a TPS teacher's assistant for 15 years admitted to placing a small amount (couple teaspoons) of the Bee Go, classroom for the purpose of air freshener.  I was informed that [REDACTED] was asked for the container of Bee Go and she supplied the school with a mason jar with a few ounces of the product in it, and the product was given to Shawnee Hazmat to look up SDS information about the Bee Go product.  I asked [REDACTED] if there was any animosity between the staff that would cause [REDACTED] to angrily place the product in the classroom and he stated "no".  When asked if anyone became ill due to the odor of the Bee Go, [REDACTED] stated "no". [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and I then traveled to Krouch Early Childhood Center to visit the classroom where this incident occurred. We met with Principle [REDACTED] to take us to the class.  The articles from the classroom were in the hallway, and the class still had the odorous smell.  Phoenix Restoration a clean up crew hired by TPS was on site.  [REDACTED] stated that the classroom carpet was goint to be replaced and all surfaces cleaned.  [REDACTED] supplied me with a written statement of the incident, and [REDACTED] supplied me with a letter that was sent to all the Pre-K student's parents, and contact information for [REDACTED].
After leaving the school I met with [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] to discuss the complaint.  [REDACTED] informed me that they have met with the police department and did not want to give me a written statement.  [REDACTED] stated that his wife did not know anything about the Bee Go product, and she has a unusual sense of smell and thinks the Bee Go smells good.  [REDACTED] stated that she intended to use the product as an air freshener.  When asked if the classroom had odor and needed air freshener [REDACTED] replied "no".  [REDACTED] stated that they have 30 hives and his son purchased Bee Go product online about 6 months ago.  [REDACTED] still had some of the product on hand and photos were taken of the product.  [REDACTED] called me after I left his residence and stated that the product was purchased from Brushy Mountain Bee Farm's website, and they also have a 2016 magazine in which the Bee Go product could is being offered for sale.  [REDACTED] son was at work, and I was informed that they would supply me with Bee Go purchase records when they find them.
After leaving the [REDACTED] I met with Tecumseh's Assistant Chief of Police [REDACTED] who was working on writing up the police report on [REDACTED], also present was Fire Chief [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] stated that the report of incident [REDACTED] gave the police department was consistent with the report that was given to me.  [REDACTED] also stated that [REDACTED] indicated that there was some tension between the teacher [REDACTED] and herself.  Fire Chief [REDACTED] stated that a couple of his firefighter's eyes began burning when they were in the areas of the classroom where the product was placed.  [REDACTED] stated that he contacted Bee Go manufacturing officials to get SDS information.  Chief [REDACTED] informed me that ODAFF could have a copy of the police report when it was finished.
I finally met with [REDACTED] to discuss the complaint.  This meeting occurred at the [REDACTED] parking lot in Shawnee, OK.  [REDACTED] went over the details of the incident and informed me that he went to a dinner at the school after the incident and could still smell the odor of the Bee Go. [REDACTED] stated that when he asked about the smell his child informed him that the police came to the school looking for the smell, and that is when he first became aware of the incident.  [REDACTED] informed me that because of his concern about the safety of the product he obtained some of the Bee Go from his friend who is also a bee keeper to look up information about the product.  [REDACTED] implied that the Bee Go he received from his friend is in its original container and in a coffee can, and he has not taken the lid off of the coffee can because the odor is so bad.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident caused a classroom evacuation and required professional cleaning.

incident_description:
I bought a Char-Broil grill and set it up.  This is a tabletop model with Model # 465133005 which is sold at both Lowes and Ace Hardware in different boxes .  Here is my video on youtube.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UqIMf5tsOpw


Here is Char-Broil's response to my complaint.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------  
Thank you for contacting Char-Broil. 

We apologize for the issues you've had with these tabletop grills. You are a valued Char-Broil customer and we want you to not only enjoy using our products, but feel safe while doing so. Fortunately, this is something that can easily be corrected, and we would be happy to help you with this. After reviewing your video, the reason you are getting turbulence in the burner's venturi tube is because the propane bottle is not flush with the unit and has no support. The grill will either need to be steadied in a way that the bottle lines up with the unit, or we recommend placing something underneath the LP bottle to support it and even out the connection.

If you have any questions or encounter any further issues, please give us a call at the number below and we will be able to best assist.

We appreciate your business.  If you have any further questions you may contact us by either visiting www.charbroil.com or by phone at 1-800-241-7548.  Our hours of operation are Monday through Friday 8am to 6pm EST, and 9am to 3pm EST on Saturday.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
Char-Broil Grill Service Specialist

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
I got a 2nd email directly after this one that with none in between that states case closed.

The video may not convey the flushness of their brass fitting but I have tried this grill with 2 different valves  and have pressed the brass fitting all the way in which is held in only by a dimple on the burner and a slot on the brass to allow it to go in.  The design of this fitting and the dimple is so loose that it can be either pulled out or fall out without the slot in the brass fitting aligning with the detente dimple. incident_description: I ordered a fuel tank assembly for a chainsaw from a company called Arbortec (arbortec.net) on November 2, 2016, which admittedly obtains the majority (if not all) of their products from China. My order number for that purchase was [REDACTED], for the record. The purchase I made is for a very crucial part to any chainsaw...a fuel tank. When the part arrived, I installed all the components with the tank still empty, which is why I did not discover the major flaw in the product until later on. Upon filling the tank I noticed the saw leaked from two different places. I noticed there was no factory-placed vent piece in the fuel tank assembly and the gas cap for the tank did not tighten properly, allowing gas to leak out of the fuel tank from two different areas. There were simply not enough screw threads on the tank and no gasket or seal to prevent volatile gasoline from leaking everywhere upon my attempts to utilize the saw before I knew the extent of the problem. This creates multiple safety issues in addition to a major pollution problem. It is hard to imagine this problem being isolated to just this lone product. I believe all of Arbortec's fuel tank assemblies could have the vent or gas cap issues in their tanks. This creates a major hazard that could end up causing major harm if it is not addressed properly with the company being made to realize that their products need much better inspection and oversight before they are shipped to consumers with flaws that could result in a major catastrophe if they go unnoticed. I contacted the company itself through multiple channels, but they did not even send any response in regard to my concerns.
justification: Potential for serious injury or property damage due to gas leaks, with high likelihood given widespread production issues.

The consumer contacted a lawyer to file a suit regarding his injuries and the safety hazard with the unit. The consumer states that the firm was not willing to settle. The consumer was advised by his lawyer to report the incident to CPSC.

The consumer believes the unit is defective because it does not have an upper limit control and the heated grips should have a safety mechanism to shut off once it gets to a certain temperature.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the consumer's hand, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is high given the product's lack of upper temperature control.

incident_description:
December 19, 2016 I was mulching leaves the wind had blown against my front fence. I had already mulched about 200 feet when I noticed a wisp of smoke come up from the leaves upon and under the front of the tractor. I got off the tractor to investigate. I found the leaves under the front of the tractor (within the area of the muffler and carburetor) beginning to burn. I reached under and tried to pull the burning leaves out. however, the more I tried to remove them, the more they burned. Plus now I had two burning piles of leaves on either side of the tractor beside the fire under it. Because the temperature was about 20 degrees, I did not have any any water hoses available. I tried to use 4 small dry fire extinguishes to no avail. Shortly the fuel in the carburetor was burning along with the plastic fuel line with the three gallons or so of gasoline feeding it. The plastic pieces of the hood, the plastic engine shrouds, the tires , even the steering wheel and seat shortly were involved.

Finally found a plastic bucket and a flowing faucet and carried water to throw on the remains of the tractor to cool it off and stop spread of the fire into the remaining leaves on the yard.

Please see the attached pictures to understand the total involvement and destruction.
justification: Injury occurred due to the individual attempting to remove burning leaves from under the tractor, leading to severe burns.

incident_description:
The consumer received a letter from the firm regarding recall # 17-054. This prompted the consumer to check her unit and upon inspection the consumer noticed that the unit was leaking fuel. The consumer states that there was fuel underneath the unit. 

The consumer then contacted the firm's recall hotline (866-864-2949) and informed them about this leakage. However, the consumer was advised that her unit was not included in the recall because her serial number does not fall within the range. 

The consumer indicated that she only used the unit once.

The consumer has an extended warranty and may have the unit repaired.
justification: Although no injury was reported, the potential for harm exists due to the fuel leak, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Benran 5000 Lumen Waterproof Bicycle LED Headlamp was plugged into my wall socket for charging. The light was charging on my desk and suddenly exploded in a ball of flame and both cells got extremely hot. One of them glowing red. A small fire started and my desk and carpet were burnt.
justification: The incident resulted in an explosion and fire, causing potential injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sears Craftsman Lawn Tractor Model No. 917.203900 in about March 2014. About four months after I purchased it I noticed that the transmission began to malfunction. The tractor has a transmission which is called a "Variator SD Pedal Transmission". To operate the tractor in forward or reverse direction, it is necessary to step on a pedal with your right foot. When you remove your foot from this pedal, the lawn tractor is supposed to STOP. As the transmission continued to deteriorate the transmission began to drag. When I removed my foot from the pedal, the lawn tractor would continue to move forward or reverse whichever direction I had been going until I stomped on the brake to stop the lawn tractor. At one point before I knew that I was going to have to stomp the brake to stop, I was into some large photinia bushes before I could stop. I might have been scratched up a bit, but at least it was only bushes I ran into. What if there had been a child or pet in front of me? For this reason I felt I am obligated to report this product to you so you might consider a recall.
I called Sears explaining what had happened and they sent a technician out. Upon inspection, the technician determined the lawn tractor needed a new transmission. He ordered the new transmission and came back to install it.

Now, beyond belief, just over a year later, I am experiencing the same problem. The Sears technician has inspected my lawn tractor and determined it needs another new transmission. I have talked to and emailed Sears describing my concerns about safety of this lawn tractor and the fact it has burned up two transmissions in less than two years, and all they have agreed to do is replace the transmission again. My request to exchange this lawn tractor for one that does not use this particular transmission has been flatly denied. The transmission
part # is [REDACTED] and my most recent repair order # is [REDACTED].

The new transmission has arrived at my home and the Sears Tech. is supposed to be out to repair it on December 11, 2015. If at all possible, I would like to have someone from CPSC visit my home and see exactly what my concerns are regarding this lawn tractor. If necessary I would be willing to postpone the repair until someone from your agency could see the dangers this lawn tractor exposes the operator and anyone or anything around them to. I will attach the emails I have had with Sears to the bottom of this report.

Thank You,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved property damage (bushes) and potential for serious injury (child or pet), but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I own a toro power clear 621 E snowblower...this would have been my third season using it....two weeks ago we had our first substantial snowfall....I put fresh oil and fresh gas into the snowblower and it started right up....used it to clear my driveway and when I went back into garage with it...the smell of gas was so strong....I turned on the lights and there was gas coming out of the carburetor....I put a bucket under it , left the garage door open and went in the house and called a neighbor....he came over and pulled it out of the garage....now I have a hot engine and gas was leaking....I was terrified of a fire....I looked on the internet and saw toro had the exact problem in 2010 and issued a huge recall..I called toro and they said no recall was issued for my model and it was out of warranty and repairs were up to me....I used it for  2 seasons and that is the answer I got....this is a terrible safety issue and toro will not stand behind their products...it was purchased at Home Depot in January of 2014
justification: Gas leak from carburetor posed a high fire risk, though no injury occurred.

incident_description: Light caught on fire
justification: A fire is a serious incident but typically doesn't result in injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Toro snowblower  leaks fuel while not running causing fire hazard.  Toro has a history of this dangerous issue in the past and it is well documented.  After contacting Toro, they refused to make the simple repair because my serial number was just outside of the recall for this problem and also they said Toro won't repair unit because it is past the warranty period. 
    Toro model ...Power Clear 180 #38282 serial#311024172.
I have only used fuel that Toro recommended.
justification: Fuel leak poses a fire hazard, and Toro's refusal to repair increases likelihood of incident.

incident_description: Ryobi Model RY42102 corded electric leaf blower plastic impeller blade exploded on 8th use of new product, shooting orange plastic shrapnel out of the blower.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the explosion of the impeller blade could have caused property damage or injury if someone was nearby.

incident_description:
Table top fireplace was in center of table on deck of home.
There was a vapor burst/explosion.
Victim was seated at end of table.
Flames ungulfed him, burning his hands, arms, chest neck and ear.
Second and third degree burns covered 29% of body and required grafting.
There is also need for future grafting.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns covering 29% of the victim's body, requiring grafting, which is consistent with a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My Ever Brite solar light exploded, caught on fire and burned a hole in my fence. Had I not been home to put it out I may have lost my home.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such incidents to occur, they are not common.

incident_description: I have purchased the Ryobi 8 amp jet fan blower I only used the product 3 times and today I was using it to blow my carport out and the orange fan inside exploded blowing sharp pieces inches from 11 month old son this was very dangerous and come very close to causing harm Ryobi should be held accountable very disappointed in the company and the product.
justification: The product malfunctioned, causing sharp debris to be propelled towards the user's 11-month-old son, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: On September 4, Labor Day, I lit my grill to use for the day. After sitting for a few moments in a chair I noticed white smoke coming from out the open back of the grill. I was facing the front of the grill so I opened the door that exposed the tank and connecting valve. The connection was on fire. It was melting the plastic knob. Having been a fireman I soaked a kitchen towel and wrapped it around the union to smother the flames. I then turned off the valve on the tank. I checked to see if the connection to the valve from the tank was loose, but it was tight. I haven't used the grill since. I went online to your sight and found that this company has had this same problem on other models.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2). The likelihood is 'Possible' (Level 3) as it's not a common issue but has been reported before.

incident_description:
The Masterbuilt Electric Smoker was bought at Best Buy.
The meat thermometer stop working within 9 months. I had to disconnect  it so the unit would work.
On 12/22/2016 I was going to smoke some meat. I plug the unit it into an outside ground fault receptacle.
When I turn on the burner it instantly tripped the ground fault.
I could find no problems.
When I research it online I found the unit had a problem with the electrical wiring inside the metal cabinet going to the heating element.
If it had not been a ground fault receptacle I would have possible been shock.
There is no solution by the company for this problem
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the likelihood of a similar event occurring is high due to the widespread electrical wiring issue.

incident_description: The lid of my Big Joe Kamodo Joe ceramic smoker unexpectedly slammed shut and I suffered a crushing injury with multiple non-displaced fractures on my right thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and while it's not common, it's possible for a smoker lid to unexpectedly slam shut.

incident_description: The EVERBRITE Motion Activated Outdoor LED Light caught fire.
justification: While the incident resulted in property damage (fire), there were no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: While using Your product On site I sat it down to clear some brush When I look back there were flames At first just smoldering But as the brush nearby caught fire I had to run to grab a hose By the time I came back to Put out the fire The chainsaw was ruined Along with about a 3-foot patch Of the yard that I was working in I cleaned up the area as well as I could I just took the chainsaw And dropped it in the garbage can So what do I do now That I no longer have the product ? There were no injuries .  My main concern was if it had spread to the house.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
Consumer reports that the lawn tractor transmission is failing again. He stated that he noticed while using it in October 2016 that the braking system had begun to not fully engage when in use. Consumer stated that it doesn't appear to work as designed. Consumer stated that when in reverse, he took his foot off the  pedal and that the tractor didn't stop for another 4 to 5 feet. 

He advised that this is the same problem he had with the two previous transmission  failures. The consumer stated that this will be his third transmission failure and that if the manufacturer doesn't refund him, he will junk the tractor out rather than sell it to another consumer.  

The consumer advised that when  he previously communicated with the manufacturer and attempted to get them to replace the tractor with a different model they denied his request. The consumer stated that he fears that the tractor could be hazardous to an unsuspecting operator.
justification: The braking system failure poses a significant risk of injury to an unsuspecting operator.

incident_description:
We filed a verbal report on behalf of [REDACTED] on 12/06/16 without providing full details. The following summary and the attached completed report form which includes relevant photos provide a complete report.

My office is affiliated with a consumer by the name of [REDACTED] who resides at [REDACTED]. I am filing this report on [REDACTED] behalf in regard to a hazardous incident involving an unsafe consumer product.

The details of the hazardous incident are as follows. A Toro Lawnmower was purchased from The Home Depot on 5/16/13. It was used on a moderate basis to mow a residential yard from May, 2013 until the hazardous incident occurred on 6/11/15. The mower worked properly without any problems until the 6/11/15 incident. On the afternoon of 6/11/15 while [REDACTED] was mowing a flat, level area of his yard, the lawnmower blade broke and a piece of the blade about three inches long flew out from under the mower and imbedded in [REDACTED] lower right leg. As a result of [REDACTED] right leg injury, he was treated at the Emergency Room, underwent surgery to remove the blade from his leg and was admitted overnight at a hospital. The significant puncture wound to [REDACTED] right lower leg required a long period convalescence and has resulted in nerve damage and a large bump/scar on [REDACTED] leg. Two photos of the blade imbedded in [REDACTED] leg, a photo of the broken blade, a photo of the Toro Lawnmower, a photo of the area of [REDACTED] yard where the hazardous incident occurred and a photo of the Toro Company sticker which shows the Model number and Serial number of the mower in question are attached hereto. I would note that the lawnmower was red in color when purchased and at the time of the hazardous incident. It was subsequently painted green after the accident when a new blade was installed.

A completed report form is also attached hereto.

Although the Toro 22" Recycler Lawnmower Model No. 20330 does not appear to have been included in the prior Toro
recalls with recall numbers
14-046 (12/10/13) and 15-729 (4/16/15), it is very similar to the Toro Lawnmowers that were the subjects of the prior
recalls. Additionally, the safety hazard appears to be similar to the hazard in the prior recalls where mower blades were
breaking because the mowers were assembled with an incorrect blade driver and blade combination. There is also a
possibility in this case that the steel blade itself was defective.

All of the other required information concerning this CPSC Report is included on the completed form report which is
attached hereto.
justification: Injury occurred due to a blade breaking and causing a puncture wound, with a possibility of incorrect assembly or defective blade.
