incident_description:
The consumer used the unit to mow his lawn and the leaves. After approximately 15 minutes of use, the consumer noticed smoke emitting from the front of the unit, near the hood. The consumer assumed it was an issue with the belt because it has been replaced every year. The consumer got off the unit. As he opened the hood flames went up about 6 ft. high. The consumer indicated that the leaves and grass nearby caught fire. The consumer indicated that the unit is almost completely burned and not operable. The consumer believes the leaves or grass that were underneath the unit caught fire and caused the gas tank to melt. The consumer indicated that the gas tank was full.

The consumer used a fire extinguisher to put out the fire.

The consumer has read multiple reports online of similar incidents. 

The consumer contacted the firm to inform them about the safety hazard and the incident. The consumer was told that they could not assist because they already warn consumers about this hazard in the manual. The consumer has now realized a statement in the manual that warns about grass, leaves or debris under the unit causing a fire hazard. The consumer does not understand how a product that is meant to mow a lawn would have such warning.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the consumer's actions and the product's warning.

incident_description: The 5.11 Light For Life was sitting in the charger, charging. I went to pull the flashlight from the charger, the light was melted on to the charger.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the melting of the flashlight onto the charger indicates a malfunction that could have caused injury if not noticed.

incident_description:
My Honda snow blower model HS928 has intermittently leaked gasoline.
It already has a recall for my serial number.
I will call Honda to have it fixed.
justification: Although no injury has been reported, the recurring gasoline leak poses a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
In November 2016, I took delivery of a wood pellet stove from a Home Depot Store in San Diego, CA, with order Nr. C53809356. This stove is made by US Stove Co., model Wiseway #GW1949.
When I fired it up on Nov.27,2016 the stove worked fine for three hours, but then suddenly emitted heavy smoke.
I closed the hopper, but the stove can not be shut off - it has to burn through the supply in the chute. It kept smoldering for 90 min., filling my house with heavy smoke. 
When I inspected it later, the fire had apparently reversed course and burned up the chute in direction of the hopper.
I notified Home Depot and US Stove Co. but got no answer as to how this incident could be avoided.

Conclusion: Had I not been present and closed the hopper, the fire would have burned and ignited close to 
50 lbs. of pellets, causing considerable damages.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' level 2 severity.

incident_description:
Toro Model 38282 snowblower
Serial # 311018859

Gas leak from the carburetor.
justification: Gas leak from the carburetor poses a risk of fire or explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My Toro snow blower (Power Clear 421Q E) was first recalled in 2011 under campaign due to gas leaking from the carburetor.  The snow blower was repaired by an authorized Toro dealer on 1/24/2012.  The issue has returned on 12/10/2016 and the replaced carburetor again leaked out gas causing a fire hazard in my garage.  The gas ran down the carburetor and pooled on the garage floor creating a fire hazard for possible ignition by any flame source.

Toro know that all gas made causes a problem with their design still continues to make the same product design.  This design is unsafe no matter how many times it is repaired and causes a fire hazard.  I do not want to risk having a snow blower leaking gas at my residence.  All these snow blowers with these designs should immediately stop being sold until the design can be corrected to stop the leaks. Toro should voluntarily buy back the defective machines and/or replace with a true safe design.  At a minimum Toro should be required to add a gas shut off valve into the design as a fail safe if they continue to be incompetent to correct the design flaw.
justification: Gas leak from the snow blower has already occurred twice, with the most recent incident resulting in a fire hazard.

incident_description:
I was using a Hitachi 23.9cc 2-stroke gas powered blower model RB24EAP blowing leafs off my patio.  The problem with this product occurred when the nut and washer holding the white blower wheel came off.  I removed the cover and replaced the washer and nut but it happened a second time after only 2 hours of intermittent operation.  The danger this could result in is the nut and/or washer come flying out of the slotted cover and strike anyone standing close by.
The nut and washer should be of some kind of locking washer/nut to prevent it from coming lose during operation.
justification: The incident occurred twice in a short period, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: After mowing lawn for about one hour, I parked my lawn mower in my new shed. After about 10-15 minutes, I noticed thick black smoke pouring out from the shed. Upon going to the shed, the front of the mower was completely engulfed in flames. I was able to quickly drag the mower out of the shed where it was completely destroyed.
justification: While unlikely, it's possible for a lawn mower to overheat and catch fire after recent use, especially in an enclosed space like a shed.

incident_description: The Craftman leaf blower Model 30376 ,2 speed started on fire. I had only used it 5 times before and used it to blow leaves away from the door. I had not even used 15 minutes when smoke and sparks were coming out of the plug in. Burned up my new extension cord that I  just bought it when I bought the leaf blower , and burned my hand (not bad enough to seek emergency care). This is not the first time I have had trouble with this model. The first leaf blower I got in April got stuck on high and could not get it to switch off unless unplugged. So sent back and got the second one bought in March. This one burned my hand and could have started a bigger fire as I was in the middle of dry leaves. I finally got the people to take this one back and they will refund us the money, they said. I am terribly sad with the quality that Craft man is putting out. I see 2 other models have been recalled and money refunded. I will not be replacing again with a Craftman.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the potential for a larger fire was high due to the dry leaves present.

incident_description: I had cooked steaks on the grill approximately 5pm on the evening the fire happened. When finished cooking, I closed the lid and the top and bottom vents. I had turned the gas off before I started cooking the steaks. I went to put the grill up approximately 8pm after it had cooled, but noticed a flame from the vent hose hole between the gas regulator and the grill. I moved the regulator knob to make sure it was all the way off. It was turned off all the way. I opened the valve to try to close the valve again. When I opened the valve again, it blew the flame into the grill. The grill was apparently full of propane from the regulator leaking by. Large flame and explosion. Blew the lid off. Burned me. Burned my house.
justification: The incident resulted in burns, indicating severity level 3, and the likelihood was high due to the propane leak and subsequent explosion.

incident_description:
The consumer states that after about a year of owning his lawn mower, his transmission cooling fan quit working. The dealership informed him that he needed to pay out-of-pocket since this was not considered part of the transmission but quit working due to normal wear-and-tear. Five hours after the transmission cooling fan was fixed, it quit working again. The consumer took the unit back to another dealership and this time they said it was covered under the lawn mower's warranty. The consumer contacted the Manufacturer about this issue; his claim number is [REDACTED].

The consumer indicates that after approximately thirty seconds of going up a hill, the mower quits moving.

11/2014 (Approximately) - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that they could not assist him since the unit was out of warranty and not included in a recall.

04/15/2015 (Approximately) - After having used the unit for approximately one hour, the consumer reached down to check the fluid level in the transaxle and burned his right hand with said transaxle; his injury was treated at home.

The consumer states that prior to ceasing use of the unit in April 2015 after his injury, he used it approximately once weekly for about one hour. The consumer plans on keeping the unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The consumer suffered a burn injury due to the mower's transaxle overheating, making the likelihood of recurrence high.

incident_description: I was using my lawn mower to mulch leaves.  The leaves built up under the mower and near the engine.  They caught fire from the heat of the engine exhaust pipe.  The fire spread to a pile of leaves on the ground under the lawn mower, and on leaves that had accumulated on top of the mower deck.  I was unable to easily put the fire out.  I backed away from the leaves on the ground, and they continued to burn.  There were still leaves up against the engine exhaust and on the mower deck that continued to burn.  The fire was too big to easily put out, but I was able to do so by using a garden hose.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire that could have escalated, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her 20" 40volt Lithium Battery operated cordless lawnmower  purchased from Amazon July 12th, 2016.

The caller received the lawnmower July 15th, 2016 she charged the batteries but didn't attempt to use the mower until August 2nd, 2016 when she put the batteries in both areas (One is storage) then put safety key in and turned it on but the mower began smoking and emitting a smoky odor.

She moved it to a non grassy area at which point she noted that there was plastic melted in an area that appeared to be in the center over the motor then she saw flames three or four inches high and growing, she called emergency or the fire department then noted that the flames were three to four feet high with loud noises and the wind blowing fire to the right of the mower.

There are no injuries being reported.

The South Whidbey Fire Department has pictures of the flames while the consumer has only pictures of the aftermath.

She contacted the .com where she purchased the mower and they refunded the callers monies and she also contacted the manufacturer who apologized for the inconvenience but then referred to their service center.
justification: No injuries were reported despite the mower catching fire, indicating a low severity level, while the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the delay in use and the mower's age.

incident_description:
Briggs & Stratton 699374 Fuel Tank
Above part on Briggs & Stratton lawn mower engine cracks and leaks gasoline.  Recurring problem with this part and the plastic Briggs & Stratton fuel tanks leaking gasoline.
justification: Fuel tank leakage poses a fire hazard, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
My Craftsman lawn mower model 247.374320 with Kohler engine model XT675-2044 leaks gas where the gas cap meets the gas tank. Gasoline pools on the mower deck posing a fire hazard and leaks onto the lawn which is an environmental concern. Others have reported this same issue according to Sears' Parts Direct website:
http://www.searspartsdirect.com/partsdirect/part-model/Poulan-Parts/Grass-Line-Trimmer-Parts/Repair-Maintenance/Questions-Answers/Leaking-gas-cap-247374320-Craftsman-Mowe/Model-PP330TYPE1/1324/1503820/399002?modelNumber=PP330TYPE1
justification: Gasoline leakage poses a fire hazard and environmental concern, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
I have a Briggs and Stratton 625e model 120000 Quantum 625 series engine on a Poulan lawn mower. The gas cap leaks. I replaced it with a new Briggs and Stratton gas cap part number 799585 that is identical to the original on the mower at a cost of $12.97. I never fill above the bottom of the fuel tank neck. It still leaks allowing gasoline to seep over the side of the mower. The engine model and type number is 122MO2-1619-F1. Date of purchase is 3-12-2014. The model number is 122MO21619.

I sent an inquiry via e-mail to Briggs and Stratton and was advised they could not help me and referred me to an authorized Briggs and Stratton dealer. I visited with them and showed them the gas cap and explained the problem. They acknowledged it is a problem and had no solution. They agreed the gas cap is a poor product design in that the O ring fails to seal allowing gasoline to leak out of the cap when the engine is vibrating. Their only suggestion was to maybe put a small rubber band under the O ring to tighten the seal.

I feel the leaking gasoline creates a safety as well a a hazmat problem and that Briggs and Stratton needs to address the issue and design a fix as well as offer a free replacement to current Briggs and Stratton Owners.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the consistent gasoline leakage poses a significant fire hazard and environmental risk.

incident_description:
This is a Toro 51956 Gas String Trimmer. The engine head leaks gas when it is either hung for storage, or placed vertically on the ground.

I bought this during late 2013. I had owned the trimmer and the engine head for a few months, and would usually store it flat on the ground. Later, I decided to hang it on a hook on my garage wall the following year. That's when I noticed a strong smell of gas the following day. Upon examination, I noticed a puddle of the oil+gasoline mixture on the floor directly under the unit.

I tried hanging it in different orientations, but it appeared to make no difference. Initially I thought that the gas cap may have been loose, but tightening it also made no difference. I tested it further by making sure that the level of gas in the tank was below the cap while it was hanging. The gas still leaked out from somewhere.

The unit is used fairly rarely - maybe 5-6 times per year - and is used and stored with no possibility of damage to the unit, it's gas tank, pipes, etc. 

I have decided to file this report because I see that an identical problem has been reported, yet no recall has been issued as per Toro's website.
justification: Gas leak occurred consistently when stored in multiple orientations, posing a fire hazard.

incident_description: We purchased a Char-Broil Hybrid Gas Grill Model #463750914, Serial #G3121713120222227 approximately 2 years ago.  This season, the lid began peeling on the inside.  Upon further evaluation, it is PAINT peeling off and dropping into our food.  I contacted the company who offered us a new lid for $4.95 which I did have them send to us.  They insist they do not paint the inside of the lid and claim it is carbon build up.  When the new lid arrived, it is confirmed that the inside lid is indeed coated in black enamel paint.  As most of us know, sheet metal does not come out of the factory with black & red enamel paint on it.  I have pictures and will hold the old lid & the new lid until I am contacted by you.  This product should be recalled and consumers should be reimbursed for the cost of it.  I can only hope that we, and anyone else, has not ingested the peeled paint from the lid.
justification: Paint peeling into food poses a health risk, though no injuries reported yet.

I decided to do further inverstigation on line and discovered the recall and reports of the hazards of this product. The unit that I have (model 20200, S/N 313005420) is part of the recall list. I would like to thank Toro for intentionally not notifying me of the dangers of this product. I informed my neighbor of this situation and he will be inititating a lawsuit against Toro. incident_description:
The gas cap on my lawn mower easily comes off when rubbing against bushes or other brush, spilling gas onto the mower while in operation which could cause an explosion or fire.  My mower information follows:  Briggs & Stratton lawn mower engine model # B&S 300E 125CC , serial # 1505205484786.  

The gas cap is a plastic quarter-turn tab type.  i.e., there are no threads.  It comes off very easily.  When mowing under bushes, the cap or the plastic strap that attaches the cap to the mower will catch in the bush or brush causing the cap to come loose.  If it does not come off immediately, it will vibrate off within a few minutes.  This has happened to me many times.  At first I did not know why the cap was coming off.  Then I noticed it rubbing against a bush and could see the cap turn when that happened.

The above comments are facts.  My opinion is that the cap is cheaply made and does not have enough tension to keep it in place.  I have several other gas yard machines, most of which have threaded gas caps which tighten very well and would never come off when touching an object.  The one other machine that has a quarter turn tab cap is made out of metal and has a tension spring which makes it very hard to take off and would not come off when rubbing against something.

In summary, I feel that this cap is cheaply made, very dangerous, and needs to be recalled/discontinued.

I called Briggs & Stratton to voice my concern.  They basically blew me off, saying that they would include my concern on a list to presented to some committee and probably would never be acted upon.

I hope that you can exert some pressure on the Briggs & Stratton people to fix this problem/recall the mower with this type of cap and discontinue production of it on new units.

Let me know, if you need further information from me.

Thank you.
justification: The gas cap's design flaw, easily dislodged by bushes, poses a high likelihood of causing an incident with potential fire or explosion.

incident_description: I was mowing my lawn when the mower died, I waited a few seconds then started it and mowed a couple of strips. Just as I was getting off the mower my friend yelled to me it was on fire. I got the fire extinguisher and my friend ran for the water hose. But not before the damage was done. My seat was on fire and the whole right side of the mower was in flames. I contacted Troy Bilt to inform them of the incident and the safety hazard the mower poses. The mower is a Troy Bilt Mustang Series RZT and has less then 50 hours of riding time, it wasn't even ready for the first oil change. The warranty department didn't care of the hazard it posed because it was subject to a fire so there was nothing they could do.I informed them it wasn't subjected to a fire it was the subject of the fire and that myself or one of my family members could have been seriously injured or even killed. I thought they would take this seriously but they said everything was great from their end and they had no recalls or safety hazards to report. I asked them to investigate the matter and they may need to have a safety recall. I informed them that the product was defective and they were going to be getting more cases for this matter and just hope that no one dies from this. It caught fire at the ignition area where you put the key in. I don't know if they messed this up in manufacturing or what but this is a very serious fire hazard and some one needs to investigate this.  We took very good care of the mower we paid  $3072 for it and only got to use it one full season. As you can see in the following pictures 4,5&6 the wiring was still in tact and the key was still in the ignition. I hope someone takes this serious before its to late.      Thank You
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard, with the mower catching fire at the ignition area.

The second time I mowed with it I was putting it up in the barn and I noticed dust rising and I park it on a rubber mat and it cut the mat. The blades were still turning even with the PTO disengaged. The next time I mowed I noticed that sometimes when I would disengage the PTO the blades were still turning and then I lifted the deck and the blades fully engaged even when the PTO lever was in OFF position.
I called the service dept. and they sent a repairman out 9/16/16. He told me that when dirt and grass get on the mower deck it can keep the brake from fully engaging. So he cleaned it off and it worked. The next time I mowed the same ting happened. This is a lawnmower that is suppose to cut grass and normally grass and dirt are going to get on the deck. So is a person suppose to do??
I went to Craftsman website and sent them a complaint 9/20/16 and still have not heard anything. 
If someone is unaware of this problem and gets off the mower or if a child or pet ran up to someone on the mower and they believed the blades where disengaged, it could have terrible results.

I got a phone call from my neighbor who told me to come outside because my tractor was on fire.  When I got outside, the fire was about eight feet high and was fed by the gasoline.  I melted the siding on my house to a height of about fifteen feet.  The LTX1045 is a 2011 model and I see other mowers of MTD manufacture have had a gas leak problem.

incident_description:
I was mowing the lawn as usual (3rd gear) when the gas tank caught fire and burned up the back of the mower.  I had been mowing for about 30 minutes before the fire broke out.  The engine was not involved and was not damaged.   It appears there was a leak in either the gas tank or fuel line from the tank and something in the rear end was hot enough to ignite the gas.  The gas tank was about half full when the fire started.  I did not notice a gas smell when I started the engine and there was no indication of a gas leak on the floor where the mower was kept.

The gas tank and all plastic in the rear was melted, the fiberglass body in the rear was damaged as was the seat and the transmission is now locked up.  My right leg was slightly burned (did not require going to a Dr.) but it could have been worse if I had not smelled gas fumes just before the fire broke out.

The mower was purchased new on March 30, 2010 and the hour meter shows 71 hours of use.  The last use of the mower before the fire was about two weeks and there were no problems then.  The mower has not required any repairs since it was purchased - only routine oil and oil filter change and air filter replacement.
justification: Injury occurred due to gas leak and subsequent fire, which could have been worse if not for the timely detection of gas fumes.

incident_description: I purchased the Ace sprayer as a backup for the sprayer I was using.  It was purchased a year or 2 ago but is still being sold by the company.  It is sold under the Ace name as well as the manufacturer.  This product is a safety hazard.  It is used to spray weed killers which should not come in contact with the person using it.  This is impossible with the design of this product.  There is no release valve.  The top is unscrewed to release the pressure in it.  When the top is unscrewed the contents of the tank spray up at your face.  There is no way to avoid this.  They instruct the user to turn the tank to the side to unscrew it but it still sprays in your face.  With this design it would have to be upside down but then of course it would leak out of the top.  I tried releasing the wok-shaped top several times using water and was sprayed in my face and upper body every time.  My old tank sprayer manufactured by [REDACTED] also, had a top lid that completely covers the top opening of the tank.  When the pressure is released by opening the top the air sprays down due to the lid.  This is the only way it should be allowed to be manufactured.  I've enclosed a picture of the new cork-type lid.
justification: The design of the Ace sprayer causes contents to spray directly into the user's face upon pressure release, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
Fuel leaks from the filler cap on the engine. The filler neck on the tank is oval shaped. I replaced the gas cap which helped for a short time but it is leaking fuel again. I contacted the manufacturer of the lawn mower, Lawn Boy, who told me to stop using the mower and to contact Kohler, the engine manufacturer. I have tried to contact Kohler but received no response. 

The oval shaped filler neck is a defect in manufacturing. The gas cap will not seal properly. This not only is a fire hazard, but is also an environmental problem. Kohler needs to come up with a proper solution as simply replacing the cap has not worked.
justification: Fuel leak due to manufacturing defect poses a high likelihood of fire hazard, with potential environmental impact.

incident_description: Craftsman lawn mower 247.374320 serial number 1F203K10571with Kohler engine developed excessive fuel cap leak after 2 years, now 3 years old.  Sears parts say to replace with new cap assembly ($16 with shipping) but it did not fix problem.  Filler and cap are poorly designed and failure is a fire safety and emissions issue.  If mower has more than 1/4 tank of fuel as much as several ounces of fuel will leak out the fill cap and the filler neck down onto the mower deck during use.  Sears parts chat agent says no incidents, then said issues with high heat or sun exposure.  I live in Michigan, the mower is stored in an insolated garage, I only mow in the evening and only during the day occasionally when it is cool out in Spring and Fall.  Google 247.374320 to see numerous other consumer complaints on the Sears parts web site.
justification: Fuel leak poses fire risk, especially with full tank, despite user's precautions.

incident_description:
My Honda HRT216SDA lawn mower fuel tank has cracked and is leaking fuel continually. I visited the Honda parts
dealer and they refused to give me a replacement tank when I showed them your recall notice. I had no choice but
to purchase a used fuel tank.

In April 2000 (#00ÃÂ·095) CPSC issued a recall of Honda lawn mowers for fuel tanks with seams that can split or crack.
The recalled mowers have an engine serial number between 1128495 and 1438098. My Honda HRT216SDA
lawn mower is 1613389, has been leaking fuel from a crack where the two plastic pieces are welded together. lf I
only fill the fuel tank below the weld it does not leak. My serial number is beyond the recall notice, so the Honda
dealer refuses to issue a replacement part. I am notifying CPSC so that the recall may be properly extended to cover
all similar lawn mowers
[REDACTED]
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the continuous fuel leak poses a fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: The lamp fell apart after just few hours of operation and led elements got exposed, it started to spark and make sparkling noise.
justification: The lamp falling apart and exposing live elements, though not causing injury, poses a significant risk of fire or electric shock.

incident_description:
(08/02/2016) The consumer stated that he was cooking on the grill. He went inside for a few minutes. About 10 minutes later he looked out and saw flames on the top lid. 

The consumer went outside and shut the gas on the product. The consumer was able to blow the fire out.

(08/04/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. He was advised to send photos. The photos were sent to [REDACTED]. The consumer did not receive a response.

The consumer was cooking on this brand new BBQ a steak right in front of a kitchen window that looks out over the porch along the front of his house. He went inside to prepare the rest of his meal. He could see small flare ups from grease dripping on the burner cover. About 8 to 10 minutes he noticed a fire that did not look like a grease flare up. He went out to get a better look and that's when he notice the back of the BBQ lid was on fire. He turned the propane gas valve off but the fire did not go out. He was able to put it out by just blowing on it. He removed his steak and that's when he realized the BBQ lid had burned on the inside and continued up the lid to the top on the outside.
The consumer had to send the BBQ to Suntech Parts and Service Inc. of Canada to get a complete cash refund.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire on a new BBQ, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I purchased 3 Energizer/Eveready Rechargeable LED Lights/Flashlights Model #RCCHFNM from a local Virginia Walmart. The first failure was the red LED charge light failed to illuminate. The second failure was the product became hot to the touch when plugged into the wall socket. The final failure was the noticing the melted plastic case in the same spot on all 3 lights. The risk of fire hazard prevents me from further use of the product. The product is still for sale at my local Walmart. I have notified Underwriters Laboratory and Energizer about this issue.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to overheating, despite no reported injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer said that the handle gets extremely hot when the grill is in use.  The handle is made of a hollow stainless steel and it is not insulated from the stainless steel top.  The consumer nearly burned his hand, but let go of the handle in enough time to prevent any injuries.

7/25/16:  The consumer called the mfr. and told their rep. ([REDACTED], last name unknown) about his concerns.  The consumer was placed on hold and when [REDACTED] returned, he informed the consumer that the grill was designed that way.  He suggested that the consumer use grill gloves to prevent any injuries.  The consumer informed him that he would contact the CPSC about his concerns.

*  The consumer used the grill once, but he was cooking hot dogs, it didn't get that hot.
*  His daughter used the grill and mentioned how hot the handle got, but was not injured.
*  The consumer's son used the grill and nearly burned his hand on the handle.

The consumer believes that this situation could lead to a burn hazard.
justification: The grill's design allows the handle to get extremely hot, posing a burn risk despite the consumer's quick reflexes.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his electric lawnmower with 48 volt battery purchased sometime in 2015 and that he believes has a defect causing safety hazards with battery or charger.

When the 48 volt battery went out on him the first time within the first year the manufacturer replaced both the battery and the charger.

After approximately nine months the battery stopped working and when the caller picked it up battery acid leaked on his right hand and right thigh due to it leaking and causing a couple of mall blisters.

The caller treated himself stating no need for physician.

The caller contacted the manufacturer but states that they are not polite of cooperable.

He has asked that this lawnmower become recalled.
justification: Injury occurred due to battery acid leakage, though not severe enough for medical attention.

incident_description: Using a splitting maul purchased at Harbor Freight new earlier in the day, I had taken one swing without issue.  On the second swing the 8 lbs. head on the splitting maul broke off of the shaft.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to equipment but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur on the first use of a new tool.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting the fire caused by his riding lawnmower and his 15 year old son's burn injury to his right arm and hand. 
He purchased this unit from Pratts Lawncare Missouri sometime in 2010.

He had no problems with the unit until Wednesday, July 20th, 2016 when his 15 year old son was on riding lawnmower.

The 15 year old had been using the lawnmower for approximately one hour when he stopped the mower, turned it off then decided to check the fuel level when the gasoline erupted throwing gasoline all over the young man and then burst into flames.

The callers son dropped to the ground and rolled away from the unit.

The fire department informed the caller that most likely when the gasoline hit the engine of the lawnmower it instantly caused it to catch fire.

The caller's son was taken from the scene of the fire in an ambulance to Phelps County Regional Medical Center Emergency in Rolla, MO where he was diagnosed with second degree burns from the back of his thumb up his arm to his armpit.

He was referred to Mercy Hospital Burn Center.

He was seen again at Mercy Hospital in St. Louis, MO on Thursday, July 21st, 2016 in the High Level Burn Center/Burn Clinic where he began his treatments for the burns.

The callers are reporting this incident as a sever fire, burn hazard.

This riding lawnmower is recalled with release# 11-733 which the caller had no knowledge about.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident resulted in a 15-year-old sustaining second-degree burns, and the likelihood of such a fuel-related incident is high given the recalled lawnmower.

incident_description: sears craftsman lawn mower with briggs and Stratton motor has a fuel leak developing on the plastic seam. next to the hot muffler definitely a fire and safety hazard. B&S will not replace the tank. I read online many customers having the same issue complaints. I wonder how many have been injured or killed. how many homes burnt down because of this defect. we all have the same issue the plastic fuel tank seams start leaking fuel. if they admit a problem they would be libel for injuries and damages to property. therefore they deny all complaints!
justification: Fuel leak near hot muffler poses a high risk of fire, though no injuries or deaths have been explicitly mentioned.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his propane gas grill that he purchased from a retailer in Minnesota around November 2010 time frame.
He had no problems with this grill until around July 1st, 2016 when he placed his food on the grill then went inside to prepare other portions of the meal.
After just a few moments he looked out of his window and saw that the grill was on fire with flames close to two feet high coming from the back of the grill.
He immediately dialed 911 for the fire department who arrived in no longer than two to three minutes and checked the grill because the fire had extinguished itself.
The smell of the propane leaking from the grill was still quite strong.
The fire department firemen separated the tank from the grill and couldn't get the knob on top of the tank to turn off so the removed the grill and tank separately away from the caller's home.
There  are no injuries being reported.
The caller did contact the manufacturer July 21st, 2016 to ask if they would inspect the grill and repair it at their cost but they declined that offer and advised the caller that any inspection/repair would be at his expense.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire and propane leak, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her ride on lawnmower purchased from retailer June 13th, 2013 in Virginia.
The unit was delivered the same day but when the caller was driving it while cutting grass on her and her husband's one acre property the gears slipped from fifth to seventh gear and shot the lawnmower up through the yard.
She & her husband returned to Lowe's to complain and they were advised to return the lawnmower after being also advised by the delivery person that these models were being returned every day.
However they kept the unit instead of returning it.
During the week of July 18th, 2016 she was riding on the mower when she felt the seat jiggle, she turned the key off and when she got off she noticed that the seat had come loose and come off.
Friday, July 22nd, 2016 she had been cutting grass when the deck spending that hold the blade fell off onto ground.  She said it tore her yard up.
There are no injuries being reported.
She contacted the manufacturer July 26th, 2016 1 (800) 828-5500 and spoke with representative (she didn't obtain his name), he advised her to take it to Buena Vista to have it repaired, 6 miles from her home.
The 72 year old caller said that the store gave her repair places 100 miles away from her home.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the recurring issues with the lawnmower, including gear slippage, seat detachment, and blade deck falling off, indicate a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: I purchased Ryobi lawn mower model RY40108 and received it on 8/9/2016. After using the mower and spraying it off, I stored it in my garage.  I was having problems making it turn on.  After removing the ÃÂStart keyÃÂ and putting it back in, the mower started running without the ÃÂbailÃÂ safety release or the ÃÂstart buttonÃÂ being pressed.  The mower ran for approximately 30 seconds without the ÃÂbailÃÂ bar safely release being held down. This bail bar is the bar that is designed to stop the mower as soon as it is released. See video of the incident submitted.

incident_description:
While mowing the yard my nephew saw smoke coming from the top of the mower. He got off & turned it off when it then burst into flames. My wife tried to put it out with water but it got too hot. It started shooting flames & a neighbor put it out with a fire extinguisher. It totally destroyed the mower. It has 1 back tire that doesn't appear to be damaged. I've enclosed numerous pictures of the tractor & ground right where it burned. John Deere's response, without examining the tractor, was he was mowing with the deck too low & debris flew into hot components, & the claim was denied. (continued on seperate page)
(continued)
As I explained to their (John Deere's) representative this could not be plausible. If the front tires were not melted off, as well as the deck wheel, the deck would be raised several inches. Also the debris would exit the shoot to the side or would travel the opposite direction of travel if they came from outside of the deck. There would be no hot components on the rear of the tractor and it was not mowing in reverse. It also shows the position of the deck adjustment handle in the puctures. We have always mowed in the positions marked on the indicator, in the suggested spot. This being said, if the fire was caused by debris on hot components then the safety issue would be the debris access to these hot components. It is my belief that this may have been an electrical fire. A portion of the battery (as seen in the photo) was separated & quite a distance from the rest of it. As of this date I have not been able to get the manufacturer or their 3rd party to examine the tractor even with me offering to transport it back to the merchant or authorized repair facility.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in significant property damage, with the mower being completely destroyed.

incident_description: On April 20, 2016 around 5:30 p.m. I was using a recently purchased gas grill from the Home Depot (Make and Model: Nexgrill #720-0830H).  Upon removing the food from the grill, I went inside the house to place the cooked food in the kitchen.  Moments later a jet engine sound rang out from the porch area of the house.  I immediately went to the area where I saw the grill emitting flames.  I attempted to pull the grill out the door of the porch area when the grill exploded burning my head, face, neck and arms.  Fire department and ambulance reported to the scene.  I was transported to the hospital burn unit.  I have found multiple complaints and issues regarding the design of the grill that have been reported online.  It has been banned in Canada.  It is still available for purchase at the Home Depot.  Please take this product off the market before another familyÃÂs life is changed forever or even worse, lives are needlessly ended.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns, and the grill's known design flaws increase the likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:

Lawn Boy lawn mower
  - Filled with regular gas
  - While moving it onto the lawn, the hidden plastic gas tank ruptured spilling most of the tank of gas on the mower and dry lawn.  
  - Had I not noticed a strong smell of gas and checked for a problem, starting the lawn mower could have sparked the gas fumes resulting in injury and fire
  - Found out online that Lawn Boy had recalled this model of lawn mower - describing the exact product safety problem I encountered - a sudden rupture of gas tank spilling gas

Model number 10247 Lawn Boy Mower - they need to recall the entire series and replace the gas tank before someone is seriously injured.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his zero turn rider lawnmower purchased from Sears in Dodge City, Kansas during the Fall of 2014.

The caller had no problems with this mower until the evening of Saturday, July 9th, 2016 when he was mowing after taking breaks between mowing his five acre property.

He had taken a break of around two hours, went back to the mower and began working again, there were no indications that there was any problem with the unit, no noise, no bad odor etc., however after only thirty minutes he felt the heat from flames due to the mower catching fire.

He did smell something but it was not a bad odor and though maybe someone was grilling.

He measured the area using gasoline leaks, burn marks on the grass beginning 15 feet from the turn, to 63 feet to where he realized that it was on fire.

He immediately got off the mower & rushed to his house to contact the fire department to extinguish the approximately seven foot high flames.  The lawnmower is burned beyond repair.

He calculated that riding about 5 miles per hour that would be approximately 10 seconds from the time the leaking began until the time it burst into flames.

He is reporting this incident as severe fire, burn and explosion hazard.

There are no injuries to report.

He did contact the retailer July 11th, 2016 but he believes he may have gotten the runaround.

He contacted the manufacturer July 12th, 2016 and spoke with [REDACTED] at 1 (800) 659-5917 where he was transferred to her.

She assisted the caller with completing a report and said he would be contacted.

Caller checked with Great Bend, it's Sears Store.  He look at new Zero turn mowers.  the gas tank is made with real light gauge plastic.  He could push in the tank. which is not protected with any thing. from the tank to the wheels of mower.

He believes something hit the gas tank rupturing it, causing the fire,
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a severe fire hazard due to a gas tank rupture, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I purchased a GreenThumb Pumpless Pro multi-purpose sprayer about a month ago.  I've used it 3 times, and on 2 occasions, the hose detached from the spray wand, dousing me with the contents (an insecticide mix).  Because the valve is in the spray wand, once the hose detaches from the spray wand, there is no way to shut off the flow of the liquid insecticide mix until all the pressure is released.

The hose is only held onto the wand by a friction fit (there is no hose clamp) and no pressure regulator on the sprayer, so failure of this kind is unavoidable and inevitable.

Given the types of toxic chemicals typically applied with a garden sprayer, this product is incredibly dangerous and should be recalled immediately.
justification: The product's design flaw, lack of a hose clamp and pressure regulator, makes detachment and exposure to toxic chemicals likely, resulting in potential injury.

incident_description:
Our Char Broil gas bbq almost caused our house to burn down. 

I had lit the grill and gone inside to retrieve the food.
Apparently holes developed in the metal tube connecting the rubber gas line to the burners. 
There is evidence of charring under the grill, so flames must have been coming out of the
tube. It appears that those flames  melted the gas line, then ignited the gas flowing out of the severed gas line. (It must have been flames, not just heat from the bbq, otherwise the gas wouldn't have ignited.)
The propane bottle, unrestrained by the gas line fell over.  The lit gas line acted like a flame thrower, hurling flames at our house. Fortunately it had rained so the house was wet and we were able to grab a fire extinguisher and put this out. What a disaster.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in significant property damage or injuries due to the gas line igniting and flames reaching the house.

incident_description: I have a John Deere LA 135 lawnmower that the fuel tank has cracked. This lawnmower is very well maintained and is kept sheltered. I purchased this lawnmower for $1950.00 in 2009. I have had trouble with the carburetor as well, this may be sue to the crack in the fuel tank.
justification: While the lawnmower is well-maintained, the cracked fuel tank and previous carburetor issues suggest a possible future incident.

incident_description:
I purchased a Jetboil Flash Personal Cooking System (Blue Desert color) from Backcountry.com on May 29, 2016. I noticed there was  a very strong plastic smell to it when I received the product, but the seller assured me it is common with new stoves. I did not attempt to use the stove until a camping trip on July 17, 2016. On July 17, 2016, I put cold water into the Jetboil cup and attached it to the Jetboil burner that is attached to Jetboil fuel canister. I made sure that the burner is at the lowest setting and pressed the igniter button that is supposed to automatically ignite the stove. 

What happened instead is I saw the whole stove go up in flames. I could not touch the stove or attempt to disconnect the fuel canister due to extremely high temperature and used whatever water I had at the campsite to put out the fire. Upon examination of the damage, I noticed that the igniter button completely melted off, plastic stand that the burner is attached to sustained substantial damage, and there was some damage to the wooden picnic table.  Upon first use, the whole plastic burner bottom went up in flames when I pressed the igniter. This sort of malfunction is a major safety issue, especially if I did not have access to water at the campsite (which is common on camping trips), the fire could ultimately lead to fuel canister explosion. 

I contacted the manufacturer Jetboil via email describing an incident and attaching photos of the damage but have received no response. Jetboil has previously recalled some of their product and it appears to be another instance of brand new stoves not being properly tested before being put on the market.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the severe fire and potential for fuel canister explosion pose a significant risk.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that is gas grill has a leaky valve, he replaced the valve but in the process of using the grill approximately few mins later, he heard a sputtering noise and then the grill caught on fire.  He contacted the fire department who came out and contained the fire.  There was a fire report submitted.  He returned the grill to the retailer for a refund.

(6/2016)  The manufacturer was contacted through email/ voicemail but there was no response as yet. 

Caller feels that this grill is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description: Using new propane grill for about the 6th time. Flames inside the grill increased rapidly. Shut off regulator but the fire continued at a slower rate. Had to shut off tank valve to shut down grill. Upon checking the regulator continued to pass gas when shut off and rapidly passed gas when turned on.
justification: The grill's regulator failed to shut off properly, leading to a persistent fire and potential injury.

incident_description:
(6/22/16 Estimated) The consumer indicated that he had used the grill for approximately 30 minutes, when he noticed the temperature dropped so he turned the control knob to the off position, and then shut off the gas tank valve. The consumer then unscrewed the regulator and heard a puff of gas come from the tank. Immediately after the consumer states that he saw a flash and a minor explosion from the gas. The consumer was an outpatient at Carlisle Regional Medical Center emergency room located at 361 Alexander Spring Rd, Carlisle, PA 17015. The consumer sustained first degree burns on his face and right hand. The consumer sustained second degree burns on his left hand and redness similar to a sun burn on both his arms. The Doctor told the consumer that when liquid propane gas ignites it can cause redness similar to a sun burn.

(7/1/16) The consumer contacted the firm (888-317-7642) and informed them of the incident. The consumer states the Rep. [REDACTED] told him that the regulator was defective and caused the explosion. The consumer was then transferred to another Rep. [REDACTED] (800-469-4663) to purchase a new regulator. The consumer believes gas was trapped in the regulator and in the tank which lead to the explosion. 

The consumer states that he has changed the gas tank multiple times over the years and never an incident. The consumer believes the incident could have been prevented if he would have waited for the grill to cool down. The consumer believes the firm should put a warning on the grill and on the manual advising consumers to wait for the grill to cool down to room temperature before replacing the gas tank. 

The consumer received the grill as a gift about 10-12 years ago.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (first and second degree burns) but no fatalities, and the likelihood of a similar occurrence is possible given the consumer's actions and the grill's design.

incident_description:
Abbreviated version - the longer version I just wrote did not save - frustrating!

I'm the original owners of a craftsman model 917-286450 lawn tractor DSG 6500). I've owned the machine for approximately 4-5 years and keep it in excellent working order. A few weeks ago while mowing my lawn in the early cool morning, I  noticed a burning smell and soon noticed that the motor had caught fire.  Within seconds the machine was burning uncontrollably.  I quickly jumped off the machine unharmed and raced for a nearby water hose.  I became increasing concerned about the machine exploding and injury me and/or my kids who can running with curiosity.  Potentially just as alarming was the possibly of a huge grass fire threatening all the residences along the periphery of our property. incident_description:
I am a fire investigator for the State of Maine Fire Marshal's Office. On 04/12 I investigated a fire involving a 4-burner Master Forge (Lowes) gas grill. The investigation revealed that the grill had blown over in a heavy wind storm. When this particular grill falls on its control knob side, the knobs and electric igniter are in contact with the ground at the same time. This grill fell over on concrete with the tank valve still on. The grill slid across the concrete in the wind causing all four knobs to turn on as the igniter was firing. This caused ignition of the LP gas. Luckily the grill was lying on the concrete patio and the fire did not spread to an adjacent structure. I just wanted to make you aware of this as I was able to duplicate the event my first try. 

Mod#1010048

Ser#101CWIG0048119281

Office of the State Fire Marshal
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: Although the incident resulted in a fire, it did not spread to adjacent structures and no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My Weber Genesis 310 CNG gas grill supply line caught fire on Sunday. The grill was completely destroyed and minor damage occurred to my home. The grill was not in use at the time and had not been in use for roughly 36 hours. 

As you can see, the grease is empty, the cookbox is relatively clean, and the origin of the fire is very clearly on the outside at the gas line. You can also see the melted wheel on the left side, which indicates the gas hose where it was near the ground was on fire. 

This is a defective gas line that seems to have started leaking underneath the cover. The combustion pattern is consistent with a gas accumulation under the cover below the velcro constraints beneath the side shelves. Splay patterns and flame spread are consistent with a fire point of ignition to the rear of the grill and in the gas line on the outside of the cabinet but roughly 2' from the supply line on the house. 

Weber states the supply line leaking from the center of the line was due to being left under pressure. The line, however, is designed to maintain pressure. ASTM standard indicates it should handle 105 psi for 10,000 service hours. The gas in my house is 0.26psi and the grill was installed approx. 8,900 hours prior. The line is installed per code and is a butyl core line, wrapped in corrugated steel, and covered in polyethylene. This is a clear defect. A storm was in the area, so ground static was high at the time. Weber states that this is an "act of nature", but a gas line that's not leaking won't ignite even under direct flame impingement.

The product is unsafe and Weber refuses to either honor the warranty, replace the grill, or deal with the problem.

Photos: https://www.dropbox.com/sh/nn6l4io51goc8mn/AADgo6u8PFblRxr6k2L8rSPra?dl=0
justification: The grill was destroyed, causing minor home damage, but no injuries were reported.

When I drive to put the mower in my shed, a mat I had on the ground was shred up by the moving blades. This is a dangerous situation.
justification: Blades turning on unexpectedly when adjusting height, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Scotts 18879 Lopping Shear about 1 month ago.
I used it less than 100 times on materials within its size and type of material range as shown by the manufacturer: "Branches less than 2 inches in diameter".
On the last use the steel lopping tab broke off and whizzed past my ear.
It missed my eyes by less than 6 inches.
If it had hit my eye I would have probably been blinded in that eye.
There was no unusual force or twisting that was ever used on the lopping shear.
On examination the broken area on the lopping shear showed very heavy "crystallization and snapped off cleanly.
I am an engineer and to me this is a clear indication of bad heat treating.
The lopping tab itself is also very small and thin.
This is a very unsafe product and could easily have caused me a serious injury.
justification: The lopping shear broke suddenly due to poor heat treatment, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
02/10/2016 - The consumer dropped off two tires to have tubes installed in them and have them pumped to 30 p.s.i., as specified on the tires. The consumer indicates that the tires are originally tubeless but their bead had broken off.

02/11/2016 - The consumer went to the repair shop to pick up the tires. The Store Manager, [REDACTED], brought the wheels out and placed them on the countertop. As they were talking, approximately two minutes later, one of the tires blew up in front of them. The Store Manager got hit with shards on his chest, receiving bruises about the size of a silver dollar coin; they have yet to heal completely.

The consumer indicates that the wheels are plastic, and believes this is what may have caused the problem.
justification: Injury occurred due to tire explosion, likelihood is possible given the unusual circumstances of the tires.

incident_description:
On Monday, May 9, 2016, I plugged in my Worx 24 Amp "Power Tank" rechargeable (lead acid type) battery (for a lawnmower) in for recharging.  I have owned this product since September, 2013.  It normally takes several hours to charge.

In any event, on this date (5/9/16), after a few hours of charging, it began to give off a TERRIBLE odor and become VERY hot.  In fact, the odor permeated my entire home.  I quickly realized the battery was overheating.

I cannot understand why this would happen.  The battery has never been dropped, subjected to any trauma, or abused in any way.  Later, on May 10th, I did some online research indicating that the odor was caused by Hydrogen Sulfide gas, which is poisonous and explosive.  This gas leaks from lead acid batteries when they overheat. I consider myself lucky to not have burned my house down and/or suffered grievous injury.  Please have Worx this obviously dangerous product.  

I have already replaced the lawnmower with a fully corded, electric type.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a dangerous gas leak from an overheating battery, posing a significant risk to the user and their property.

incident_description: I was mowing the yard with the rear bagger attached as directed by the instruction manual. The mower is a self propelled mower.As I turned the mower to start back along the previous swath that I had just mowed, the rear bagger detached from the mower. The steel rod on the right side of the rear bagger lacerated my right leg between my knee and ankle.

incident_description:
Lawn mower was being used in its normal manner.. 
Blade came off of the mower and landed behind the mower in the space between the mower and the operator. Engine was still running. 
Shut down the engine and turned the mower on its side. Found that the bolt that holds the blade in place was loose but still in the motor shaft.
Found that the blade could be put back on without removing the bolt as the bolt head was approximately the same size as the hole in the blade.

The consumer was able to contain the fire with a garden hose.   The Fencer had a plastic coating which melted  and over a time of exposure caused the incident.  He stated that he researched online and noticed that they were other complaints of this product.  The consumer has the product.

Respondent feels that this is a fire hazard which should be reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on 4/7/16, he was mowing the lawn for about 1-1.5 hours. The tractor stalled so he turned the ignition key off. 

The consumer noticed flames coming form the front left of the tractor. The consumer got off the tractor and opened the hood. The consumer saw flames near the carburetor and hot exhaust muffler. The consumer tried to extinguish the flames with some green lawn clippings. That slowed down the flames but did not extinguish them.

The consumer thought to turn off the gasoline at the tank but there were no valves to turn it off. The consumer watched as the flames grew larger and move towards the gas tank. The plastic gas tank melted from the flames. The gasoline in the tank ignited. 

The only thing the consumer could do was water it with garden hose. This again only slowed down the flames but not extinguish them.

The whole tractor is burnt. Repair is not possible on the unit.

The consumer went on the firm's website and saw to report the issue to CPSC.


The consumer stated that nothing hit the tractor and there were no foreign objects that got into the tractor. Before the tractor completely burnt, the consumer noticed that there were some rubber gasoline lines at the carburetor, near the muffler. The consumer believes that the rubber lines failed and spilled gasoline onto the muffler which ignited the gasoline.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the failure of rubber gasoline lines.

incident_description:
I bought an outdoor BBQ kitchen from Tropicana Outdoor Living Company and had it installed by their installers.
The kitchen top came off its footing with the winds we had two months ago. Luckily I was home to tight it down during the rain storm to prevent it from flying off to my neighbors' yard and possibly causing property damage and/or Injury to personnel. Enclosed are pictures of the top and screws used to attach the footing. I'm no engineer, but the size of the top overhang and footing are bad designs. This product should have never been on the market as designed; I was expecting a stronger footing design. Use of a metal plate with bolts would make a big different in the strength of the footing with a smaller top overhang. Notified the company of the Incident, talked to a person named [REDACTED], he stated that the design was safe and that the company's Installation team simply did not installed It correctly, maybe due to the installation team fatigue. I check with Amerimax engineering for specifications on size of overhang for the amount of spacing between posts for the patio top Installed by Tropicana 
Outdoor living installers and it specifies it should be no longer than 25% of post spacing (2 feet). Top installed has an overhang of over six feet, way beyond specs provided by Amerimax engineering and presents an extreme safety Issue and should no longer be on the market. Enclosed are Amerlmax engineering specifications. In addition, this company sale their products at home shows throughout Southern California. Yes, I would like to get reimbursed for the faulty product I bought from Tropicana Outdoor living Company, but most important is the unsafe condition that could exist out in the public in Southern California due to design of this product and faulty installation.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in property damage or injury due to the top's improper design and installation.

incident_description: This grill has igniter problems. The flame is unstable and the gas builds up below the burner grate. This causes an explosion when restarting. This has happened 2 times now. The grill pan was blown at least 2 feet in the air and the fireball was at least that large. I contacted Charbroil after the first explosion to find repair parts for the igniter. They were no help and couldn't tell me what parts to order. The gas tank placement is also unsafe, I burned my arm 2 weeks ago when turning off the gas. I now have a scar from the burn. These are immediate issues that need to be addressed. The grill all has rust problems with the grease pan and the grill grate. The igniter malfunctioned within the first 10 uses, the grill pan rusted within a couple of months along with the grease pan.

incident_description:
I spoke to [REDACTED] by telephone.  Mr. [REDACTED] told me that he was attempting to light a Weber gas barbecue grill on the deck and had just connected a new propane tank to the grill.  Mr. [REDACTED] stated that he did not hear any sounds indicating a gas leak after opening the valve of the cylinder.  He attempted to light the grill with the built-in igniter but was unsuccessful.  He knelt down in front of the grill and opened the cabinet doors to check the connections.  While he was kneeling in front of the grill, he opened a burner valve and pushed the igniter button.  He stated that the grill ÃÂblew up in his face.ÃÂ  Mr. [REDACTED] stated that he had owned the grill for approximately 1 ÃÂ½ years, and had no previous problems with it.  

After consideration of data collected for fire cause determination, and using the overall methodology by applying the scientific method as discussed in the 2014 edition of ÃÂNFPA 921- Guide for Fire and Explosion Investigation,ÃÂ it is my opinion that the fire originated in the barbecue grill on the exterior deck on the east side of the structure.  The ignition source for the fire was a spark from the electronic igniter on the grill.  The first fuel ignited was uncontained flammable gas (propane) from a source other than normally intended at the burner, possibly due to a leak or improper connection at or near the container or piping.  The factors that brought the ignition source and the first fuel ignited together were the unintentional actions of a person or persons.  Using these elements, the classification of fire cause is ACCIDENTAL.
justification: Injury occurred due to an explosion caused by a gas leak, likely due to improper connection or leak, which is highly probable given the actions taken.

incident_description:
My Toro snowblower was recalled in 2010 for gas leaking from the carborator.  After several times having it fixed, it still leaks raw gas again into my garage after sitting just 16 days after it's last use.  the dealer explained that all manufactureres make the same parts in China involving a needle to stop the gas from flowing.  There is a design issue when using gas with ethanol, which is 95% of all gas sold.  The gas has corrosive effects on the carborator and needle causing sticking and the gas flows onto the floor of the garage where the snow blower is sitting.  The gas ran down and out under the garage door, creating a fire hazard for anyone walking by with a match, cigarette, etc.  
Toro (and othe manufacturues apparently) blame the gas producers for making gas with ethanol which has various side effects such as this.  Toro knowing that all gas made causes a problem with their design still continues to make the same design ignoring the issue and blaming the gas refineries.
This design is unsafe, regardless of how many times it is repaired and causes a fire hazard.  I can't risk having the snow blower leaking gas into my residence so the dealer offered to buy it from me for $75 which I then sold to him.  All these snow blowers with these designs should immediately stop being sold until either the design can be changed to stop the leaks or the gas is changed to not cause the issues.
justification: Gas leak from the snowblower poses a fire hazard, potentially leading to an incident but no injuries.

incident_description:
See attached detailed description of need for replacement of rear wiring harness after 47.5 hours of use for a D110
John Deere Tractor (riding lawnmower)

RE: Replacement of rear wiring harness after 48 hours of use for a D110 John Deere Tractor (riding lawnmower)

In September 2015, I left my John Deere tractor for service at a local John Deere service center, which included correcting the sparking, backfiring, and the machine subsequently shutting down. I was subsequently informed by JD that the rear wiring harness needed replacement.

I was amazed that a wiring harness needed replacement after only 48 hours of use and subsequently went and looked under the mower tractor at the JD service place. The inspection revealed that the wiring harness was drooping low due to a push tab, which held the wiring harness to the mower deck had come loose. Photograph 1 shows the replaced wiring harness with the tab attached to the wiring harness. When the tractor is placed in the mowing mode, the tractor vibrates which could have caused the tab to come loose. I opine that the loosened wiring harness was damaged by the drive belt for the mower and the insulation was stripped from 2 wires (Photographs 3&4) in the wiring harness, causing sparking, backfiring and ultimately shutdown.

The local service center replaced the wiring harness but I was required to pay l/3 of the cost in order to get my machine back. I informed the staff I would pursue the 1/3 reimbursement with their headquarters, since I believe it is a safety issue that should be addressed at no cost despite the tractor being out the warranty period. No reimbursement occurred.

The above description, in my opinion is a significant safety concern, since the sparking, back firing of the damaged wire is close to rear fuel tank. The wiring harness under the mower deck is held to the mower deck by only one push tab and the wires under the mower deck are not enclosed in a protective shroud.

I have the actual replaced wiring harness as shown in Photograph 2, which can be furnished to the CPSC upon request. The replaced wiring harness better shows the stripped wires.
justification: Potential sparking and backfiring near the fuel tank poses a fire risk, though no injuries or fatalities have been reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Husqvarna produced Sears Craftsman Lawn tractor from Sears in April of 2015: Model Number 917.986410, Serial Number  021715A007147.

The tractor was used through the summer and fall of 2015 to maintain our 1.5 acre yard, and accumulated approximately 35 hours of use as measured by the installed hour meter.

The tractor began to develop a problem with sticking in forward gear late in the mowing season.  Sometimes it would just keep moving forward until the reverse pedal was lightly tapped or the brake applied and then the tractor would come out of gear and stop.  At first the problem seemed random and infrequent, but it later became apparent that the issue was degenerative in nature and becoming quite severe.  It finally got to the point where the tractor would stay in forward or reverse with the operatorÃÂs foot off of the pedal, and that the tractor would not stop moving in either direction even when the left brake was applied.  The only way to make the tractor stop was to repeatedly, and sometimes desperately toggle back and forth between the forward and reverse pedals until the tractor stopped moving.  The tractor does have a cruise control installed on the unit, but in all cases where the tractor was stuck in gear it was checked, and it all cases it was not active.
Obviously, this caused issues with operating the tractor and on several occasions it drove me into low hanging branches on trees and bushes in the yard.  My injuries were slight consisting of only scratches to the face and arms.  I always wear eye protection while mowing.

I called Sears service and requested that the tractor be repaired under warranty, since it was less than 1 year old.  The earliest service date was late December and the tractor was idled until it could be repaired.  In late December the service technician inspected the tractor and rapidly came to the conclusion that the transaxle was sticking.  He explained that the newer ÃÂplasticÃÂ transaxles could not be repaired and had to be replaced as a unit.  A replacement part was ordered.

The same technician returned in mid January to affect the repair.  He replaced the transaxle and showed it to my wife explaining that the shaft had rusted, and that when the shaft rusted it caused the transaxle to lock up.  He asked her if I had ever washed the tractor.  She explained that I had washed it several times using the clean out port on the mower deck and the clean out adapter included with the tractor from the factory, and that I had cleaned it out in accordance with the OwnerÃÂs Manual.  He explained that you should never wash the tractor regardless of what the manual said because the shaft would rust, the axle lock up and the tractor would stick in gear just as it had done.  He then related several stories to her of other tractors he had worked on with the same problem, and the same root cause.  Relating about how other owners were similarly injured.  The tractor should only be cleaned using a leaf blower and that it should never be allowed to get wet.

Clearly the tractor has a design flaw and fails in an unsafe manner.  Inherent in its use is the fact that it will get wet, from cleaning, from rain, from dew, or just from the wet grass clippings.  The device should be able to withstand repeat moderate wetting without any failure, let alone a failure that keeps the tractor in gear even when the operatorÃÂs foot is removed from the pedal.  And if moderate wettings cause failure, than the failure should be a safe failure where the tractor ceases to operate rather than remaining in gear, endangering the operator.  From my cursory inspection of the parts, it would appear that the problem could have been solved by about a dimeÃÂs worth of chrome or Zinc-chromate plating on the shaft.   Any rust resistant coating would have substantially reduced the probability of the failure mode.  The failure mode is completely predictable and testable given the speed at which my tractor rusted and failed with only very moderate use and wettings.  The defect, which seems to be relatively prevalent in the field according to the service technician, should have been easily observed in product usage testing and could have been avoided and corrected by proper material usage.   
[REDACTED]
justification: Injuries occurred due to the tractor's transaxle sticking in gear, causing it to move uncontrollably and collide with low hanging branches.

incident_description:
On January 17,  2016  Purchased a Ryobi PRUNER ATTACHMENT - MODEL RY15520  from Home Depot store #[REDACTED].

On January 24, 2016, I used the attachment with a [REDACTED] 4 cycle engine, designed to allow various attachment tools.  According to the HomeDepot web site:  "This pole saw attachment can be used with Ryobi, [REDACTED] and other universal brand fit power heads and trimmers."

The attachment comes with a strap hanger that the manual says to attach to the power head end of the shaft. It also comes with a shoulder strap which is then connected to the strap hanger with a snap clip.

The shoulder strap is made from nylon webbing and sewn together connected with some steel rings and nylon-plastic adjustment sliders. 

The manual implies to make sure to use this shoulder strap as a safety measure. 

From the manual: 

"When operating this unit, you must wear a shoulder strap
to support the unit. If your unit does not have a strap
hanger installed on the power head shaft, use the following
instructions to install the hanger.
? Pull strap hanger apart and place over power head end
of shaft; position near the upper knob.
? Install bolt and lock nut. Tighten nut securely.
NOTE: Check for tightness before each use to avoid
serious injury or product damage.
? Place shoulder strap over your left shoulder and attach
shoulder strap clip to strap hanger. Adjust by sliding the
front clip up or down.
NOTE: When properly adjusted, the power head should
be supported by the shoulder strap about hip level."

The first time I used this tool, I used it for about 45 minutes and then the shoulder strap fell apart and stopped supporting the weight of the power head and attachment. 

The combined weight of the power head and the attachment stressed and deflected a metal ring that holds two parts of the strap together.  The nylon part of the strap was then able slip out of the ring where a gap in the ring had opened up.  I did not get hurt, but feel I could have been.  I stopped using the product. 

In my opinion, this created a substantial safety hazard since the user of the product can suddenly and without warning have to support the full weight of the product with their hands and arms when the strap comes apart.  This unexpected shift in what carries the weight can result in injury in various ways:  At the least may be muscle strain in hands and arms.  At the most, an unbalance situation could occur where the user might fall and come into contact with the pole saw chain while under power.  (Like falling on a chain saw.)

I called Ryobi  Customer Service at 1-800-525-2579 on January 29, 2016 at about 11:30am Central Time to express my concerns. They offered to replace the strap.  I asked if there had been an improvement of tensile or deflection strength to the connecting ring that failed.   They said no, it would be the same strap.

I also asked if they wanted to take my name and number so that I might be kept informed about what they intended to do about this potential safety issue. They did not want my contact information. All they said was that they would pass along my description of the problem to the appropriate personnel.  It was at that point I decided to file this report and to decided to not keep the product. 

I will be returning the entire product to Home Depot for a refund as I can no longer trust the product.
justification: The strap failure could have caused the user to suddenly bear the full weight of the tool, potentially leading to muscle strain or a fall, posing a risk of serious injury.

Consumer stated that his snow thrower has a failure defect.  While pulling the cord to start the unit it broke and he fell to the ground.  He contacted the retailer and he was advised that a service technician would be sent out , however, when the service technician came out (11/2015) he was advised that there was a charge.  He advised him that the retailer informed him that there was no charge for the visit.  He was contacted later that the unit was no longer out of warranty and he would have to order the parts.
