The product was purchased at Lowes in 2914.  The model # is BV5600.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken finger, requiring stitches, and the likelihood of the cover coming off during use is high, as evidenced by the user's experience.

incident_description: On July 31, 2015, there was delivered a Black and Decker (UPC 885911221450)19 in. 36-Volt Self-Propelled Cordless Electric Mower with Removable Battery to my address. I tried it out and found its mowing performance to be acceptable.  A few days later, I decided to store it by taking advantage of a function advertised for this model, the handle that folds up for better storage. The metal handles consist of two pieces each, one of which has a pin or bolt in the middle, the other a corresponding hole. To disengage the pin and fold the handle, one turns a knob located on the handle a quarter-turn, grips the handle pieces and pries them apart. Once the pins are disengaged, the handle can be folded in half, the pins popped back into place, and the knob reset to lock the handle. I managed to disengage the pins and fold the handles. I re-engaged the pin on one side and turned my attention to the other. The instructions warn the user to be careful during this procedure not to "pinch" ones finger between the handle and the plate, so I was being careful when I did this. When I went to pry the handle piece in order to pop the second pin back into the hole, the considerable tension created by the force required in the maneuver propelled my index finger between the two handle pieces, shearing off a piece from the side of my finger. It's been two weeks and my finger is still trying to heal. Frankly, I could easily have lost the finger. I feel this incident should have been anticipated by normal testing and that it is a product defect (engineering/design). I am keeping the mower because of the difficulty in returning it and because I need something to mow my lawn.  I will not be using the foldable handle function, however, as soon as I figure out how I can re-extend the handles to mow the lawn without taking off a piece of me. This device should be investigated for this danger. Perhaps they could devise a simple tool to do the job rather than manual force.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, and the likelihood of it happening again is high given the design flaw and lack of safety measures.

incident_description: I own a John Deere D-series tractor.  I filled the gas tank with gasoline after I used it and the next morning the gas was all over the deck of the mower and floor of the garage.  I thought maybe I made a mistake so I filled it again to find the gas was leaking from a hairline fracture in the tank.  There is no evidence of impact on the tank it looks as if it just failed on the parting line of the tank.  I contacted John Deere and they told me that this is not a safety issue unless "I got burnt using the product".   I completely disagree.  The likelihood that the gasoline would ignite is extremely high given the amount and location of the leak.
justification: Gasoline leaked extensively, posing a high risk of ignition and potential fire.

incident_description:
The product is a "Dura Rib Pocket Hose", made in China by Telebrands, Inc of Fairfield, NJ (telebrands.com, and sold by Rite-Aid stores. (Mine is from Rite-Aid of Highland Park, NJ - 332 Raritan Ave, Highland Park, NJ 08904).

The first time I attached the hose to a spigot and nozzle and turned on the water, (removing their supplied valved adapter as per instructions), the hose failed explosively. The end of the hose flew off  and the torn hose began to flail uncontrollably (due to its soft construction) spraying water everywhere.

Of greatest concern is the force with which the hose end flew off, carrying the attached nozzle. It could have caused serious injury had it hit someone.
justification: The hose's explosive failure and the force with which the nozzle was propelled pose a high likelihood of causing injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated he was using the grill to cook some hamburgers. 

He stated that the way the grill is designed, the propane gas tank hangs over the table where the grill sits. 

The consumer moved the burgers to the side where the tank is located. The consumer stated that the grill flipped off of the table. As the grill was falling, the consumer grabbed onto the propane gas tank. The consumer stated that the tank came loose and caused a large flame (about 2-2.5 ft). 

The consumer stated that there is a safety hazard with the way the grill is designed.

The consumer will also contact the manf and inform them about the issue. 

The consumer notified the manufacturer of the incident.  Their response was that the tank could be turned at an angle so it rests on the table however fuel efficiency might be negatively affected.

They further stated that the design meets all safety standards and no further action would be taken.

The simple solution would be to make the legs of the grill long enough to allow the tank to remain vertical while sitting fully on the table.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a large flame, posing a significant risk of injury if it were to happen again.

incident_description: LED BATTERY OPERATED LIGHT identified as PT Power with bar code 0 39564 10132 8 and W2464 (V2) when powered by 3 each [REDACTED] batteries - after about 10 minutes operation became too hot to hold.  Examination shows interior plastic melted with a hole formed between the battery compartment and the circuit board.  Material surrounding the LEDs is deformed and cracked.  Sticky fluid has oozed into the battery compartment (melted plastic?  chemical from battery?)  Seems like this was headed for a Lithium fed fire?
justification: Potential for severe injury due to high heat and melted plastic, but no immediate threat of death or injury reported.

incident_description: Getting ready to cut grass. Drove John Deere toward cutting area and mower ended up in fence and consumer on grass with broken arm.  Consumer doesn't remember what happened but told his granddaughter in the ER that the mower lurched.  Now says he doesn't remember what happened.
justification: Injury occurred due to mower lurching, likelihood is possible as consumer doesn't remember the incident clearly.

incident_description: I have been using the Tele Brands Pocket Hose Ultra since the end of March 2015. Last week, I turned the hose on to water my plants and the hose immediately "exploded", squirting gusts of water in 3 separate locations. The water force was very strong, and started spraying water everywhere. I could not control the hose! Had a child been near this could have been very dangerous. I have followed the directions, always turned the water off when I was done and completely drained the hose out, kept out of sun, etc.
justification: The hose 'exploded' unexpectedly, causing water to spray in multiple directions, posing a potential injury risk if a child had been nearby.

incident_description:
Sears Model # 24737432 - 21" Lawn Mower

Regardless of how carefully I secure the gas cap, and no matter how carefully I check it, gas leaks out of the gas tank - from the cap - during operation.  
This has been a problem since I purchased the mower in July 2013, but I continued to try to secure the gas cap to remedy the situation.  The gas leaks out and pools on the mower deck and is a fire hazard due to the proximity to the ignition and exhaust systems.
justification: Gas leak from the mower's cap during operation poses a fire hazard due to proximity to ignition and exhaust systems.

incident_description: I was mowing with my Troy Bilt TB200 self propelled lawn mower.  The gas cap on this mower is exposed and high on the engine.  It also does not fit tightly and is easily loosened.  While mowing around and under shrubs, the slightest contact between the gas cab and branches will cause it to loosen and fall off.  This leaves the gas tank opening completely exposed and raw gas will spill out onto the hot engine and mower.  I feel this is a serious fire and safety hazard and some sort of redesigned gas cap or secondary lock needs to be available.  I am afraid to use this mower until this issue is resolved.
justification: Gas spillage onto hot engine poses a high likelihood of fire, though no injuries reported yet.

incident_description:
On 8/26/2006 I purchased a Jenn-Air Stainless Steel Propane Gas Grill from Lowes in Lake Ozark, Missouri. The Item Number is 18852 Model 720-0163 Serial Number DG-002 034610. Last fall when we went out to use the grill my wife said the grill smelled like gas. I checked out the grill with all the burners and valves in the off position we could still smell gas. We shut off the main gas valve and the valve to the BBQ as we were going to Florida for the winter. This spring when we came back I disassembled the grill checking all the hoses and fittings as well as individual gas valves on the BBQ with soap and water. I found one of the Main gas valves to one of the burners leaking propane, while in the off position. This unit has never been damaged or misused. In my 67 years I have never had a BBQ gas valve just start leaking. I believe you may have a very serious safety issue with the gas valves on this unit. Hopefully this will help before any damage (fire or explosion) or injury can be caused by this faulty item. 

As of right now I have been waiting over six weeks for another part (main Gas Valve) I ordered from nex-grill on June 15, 2015 and the date is now July 27, 2015. As of today they are telling the parts are still on Back order and they don't expect to receive them until September.
justification: Potential gas leak in the off position, indicating a high likelihood of incident.

incident_description: Weber Grill Model SP-310.  When grilling and lid is open, user can easily burn hand when reaching to close the lid. I have burned my hand twice since purchasing this grill a month ago.  I owned a previous Weber grill (Genesis 1000) which was designed so that the handle extended sufficiently beyond and below the lid, and the user would grab the handle without touching the hot lid. This problem on the newer SP-310 model could be fixed by Weber engineering by designing a replacement handle which would extend lower over the lid, allowing the user to grab the handle without touching the lid.  I strongly hope that Weber will either recall this and similar models, or provide a revised handle that users can self-install to prevent burns. (Weber customer service informed me that their manual states that users should wear over mitts when using the grill, which is an unreasonable expectation and precaution).
justification: The grill's design causes frequent burns, with the user reporting two incidents in a month.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the trimmer while in operation the bottom (plastic plate that is used for the strings) broke off and became a projectile.   He stated that he was hit in on the right leg with the object and he received a minor bruise.  No medical attention was received.  The Part#3410176A-1.


(7/13) He contacted the retailer and he was referred to the manufacturer which he was then transferred through 5 different departments but no one was unable to assist him.


Caller stated that he feels that this trimmer is a safety hazard and should be reported. 

The submitter added he found out theirs is an updated part. The submitter also noted he has "somewhere" in his house the two broken pieces that attach to the area where the spool goes in.
justification: Injury occurred due to a projectile from a broken trimmer part, with a possible recurrence given the caller's difficulty in getting assistance.

incident_description:
I purchased a Dolmar backpack blower on November 19th, 2013. The concern has been what seems to be a faulty switch on the trigger handle and intermittently sends a shock through the trigger handle assembly. The blower often runs flawlessly, but then sometimes it acts like it is shorting out and trying to turn off. It sends a shock pulse through my arm, even if I have gloves on when this acts up.

I have taken it in to 2 separate Dolmar dealers to see if they can solve this safety hazard while it is still under warranty. I have also made numerous attempts to contact Dolmar with little to no response. After numerous attempts they responded saying: 

"From the issue described below, the problem is static discharge from dust particles being drawn into the volute case and the discharge point of the static electricity is the screw in the on/off switch. Our factory created an anti static belt sold for the blowers as an accessory, the belt works well when limited amounts of debris/dust is being drawn in."

This is clearly a known defect that the manufacturer should repair under warranty and may need to issue a recall. The shock hazard is significant enough to inflict pain even when wearing gloves to avoid the shock.
justification: The incident involves electric shocks, which can cause injury, and the likelihood is high as it occurs intermittently despite the user's precautions.

incident_description: Recently I was using the blower to sweep my backyard when I started to smell smoke.  I looked around thinking it was something nearby but nothing.  The smell persisted so I looked at the blower and could see it smoking.  I immediately stopped using it and when I attempted to remove the extension cord it was melted onto the prong.
justification: Smoke and melted extension cord indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I bought this leaf blower to blow the leaves and cobwebs from my tiny townhouse patio. After a half dozen uses it began to get very, very hot when I'd use it. I knew something was wrong but it was designed in a way not to be taken apart. A use or two later, smoke came out of the plastic housing and it stopped working. It didn't burn me or hurt anyone. I threw it out having only spent $43.48 on it.  
Amazon Order Summary
Item(s) Subtotal: $39.98
Shipping & Handling: $13.24
Super Saver Discount: -$13.24
Total before tax: $39.98
Estimated tax to be collected: $3.50
Grand Total: $43.48
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident of the leaf blower overheating and smoking poses a potential risk for future users.

incident_description:
On 07/02/15 (approximately) while the consumer was using the lawn tractor he noticed that the lawn tractor slowed down and then spontaneously went full speed. However, the consumer did not change speed or move the gas pedal. The consumer had been on the lawn tractor for an hour before the incident occurred. The consumer turned the lawn tractor "off" and waited for about an hour for the lawn tractor to cool down. When the consumer tried to use the lawn tractor again he noticed that the lawn tractor was still doing the same thing. The consumer decided to turn the unit off. The following day the consumer used the lawn mower and noticed that the lawn tractor still jolted while being used. The consumer states the lawn tractor jolts more frequently and the issue has become worse. The consumer has noticed this occur while he drives the lawn tractor at any speed. The consumer normally uses the lawn tractor at full speed. 

On 07/09/15 the consumer contacted the firm (888-848-6038) and informed them of the issue with the lawn tractor. The consumer spoke with a firm rep (name unknown) and was told that the lawn tractor was not recalled. 

The consumer has reviewed recall # 12-132 and believes the lawn tractor should be included in recall # 12-132.
justification: The lawn tractor's unpredictable speed changes pose a significant risk of injury, as demonstrated by the consumer's repeated experiences.

incident_description: Purchased flashlight new on 7-25-2015.  Installed 3 new [REDACTED] C-cell batteries purchased along with the flashlight.  Flashlight has 'high' and 'low' intensity settings along with a couple of strobe settings.  Turning the flashlight on and selecting brightness or strobe is done through a press and release tail switch.  There is no tactile or visual feedback from the switch regarding whether the flashlight is 'on' or what mode it is in.  On 'low', the flashlight performed as expected.  When on 'high', the flashlight would go out after a few seconds.  Clicking the switch to return to the 'off' setting and clicking again would turn the flashlight back on for a few more seconds then it would go off again.  I repeated this cycle several times.  Eventually I decided that I wanted to find out whether the flashlight would come back on after shutting itself off if left alone for a period of time.  I turned the flashlight on in the 'high' setting and laid it on my desk.  I got distracted and several minutes later when I went to pick up the flashlight it was burning hot - Far too hot for me to hold it.  I don't know whether alkaline batteries can explode but I was afraid they might.  I went and got safety goggles and several rags.  I wrapped the rags around the flashlight to try to contain whatever might happen and slowly unscrewed the flashlight's tail cap to remove the batteries.  The flashlight and the batteries eventually cooled down to room temperature.  I am concerned that this flashlight posed a risk of bodily injury in the form of burns and a risk of a house fire.
justification: The flashlight overheating and burning hot, posing a risk of burns, indicates a severe injury potential.

incident_description: After using the product for a brief time, I smelled burning plastic.  I immediately turned off the blower and could tell the odor was coming from inside the engine compartment.  I let it cool down and put it away.  The following week I used it again.  I again smelled burning plastic.  I assumed that because it was new the plastic smell was from that.  After a brief time, I saw smoke come from inside the motor and it caught fire a short time later.  I immediately unplugged it and set it on the driveway and covered it was a blanket I had in the garage.  I threw the item in the trash the following week.
justification: The incident resulted in a fire, which could have caused injury if not quickly contained.

incident_description: I purchased a Husqvarna string trimmer model 223L. During the normal process of using the product, my forearm was constantly being burned by the exhaust/muffler. I went to the Husqvarna web site and there is a customer forum which lists several customers that are having the same problem. One response from Husqvarna basically said, quit "it wasn't designed as an arm rest". I can assure you, it's not a matter of resting your arm on the trimmer, it naturally comes in contact with the muffler/exhaust area as you move the trimmer.
justification: The incident resulted in burns, indicating severity level 3, and the widespread customer reports suggest a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
Dangerously Hot Glass-Reinforced Nylon Lid Handle - Weber Smokey Joe 14" Charcoal Grill

In September 2014, I bought a new Weber Smokey Joe 14" basic model to replace a 20-year old one as I was moving out-of-state. I was using the new one for the past few months without a problem. However, I recently bought the Weber coal Chimney Starter and tried it 2 nights ago. The coals heated up very quickly and I grilled meat with the lid off. Then I put slices of bread w/cheese on top on the grill and put the lid on for no more than one minute (to melt the cheese on the bread). When I went to take off the lid, the handle was so hot that I burned my hand and instinctively flung the grill cover away. It could have hit my feet/legs and I could have had serious burns. 

I've written to Weber about this on their company website.  However, I received their response today saying "Sorry to hear about that accident you had with your grill...The use of a heat-resistant BBQ mitt or glove is recommended when operating the grill.  These warnings are outlined in the owner's manual for your grill." 

Following Weber's response, I have accessed several websites to read consumer complaints about this product and this same issue of the overheated handle has been noted since 2010.  How can the company continue to ignore this?  

Please note:  I also own the Original Series large Weber kettle grill that my family received from [REDACTED] in 1976.  Importantly, this original grill has a wooden handle.  I continue to use this 40-year old grill and have never had an issue with burning my hands on the handle.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burned hand) and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the numerous consumer complaints since 2010.

incident_description: handle broke when cutting and squezed my finger realy hard.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and while it's unlikely to happen with a new, functioning handle, it's possible with a defective one.

incident_description: On 5/9/2015 the hose from the propane tank melted with fire coming from the end of it.  This is a grill with an oven attached.This is a serious design defect that would place the hose next to sufficient heat to do this.  Please issue a recall for these grills so that no one else has such a risk of damage.  I was fortunate enough to get the gas turned off before more damage occurred but the oven area of the grill is melted and it is unusable in under 20 months of use.
justification: The grill's design defect caused a fire, leading to property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: Before staring my tractor I opened up the air cleaner and checked under the hood for any nests or any other foreign material. My Cub Cadet Lawn Tractor model LTX 1045 was purchased new in 2009'  I was running the tractor when I smelled and saw black and white oily smoke coming from the left front in the area of the carburetor.  Next I saw burst of flame. I stopped the tractor and lifted the hood. Fire burst around the plastic air cleaner assembly  on the carburetor.  Everything was starting to melt so I moved a safe distance away in case of an explosion as the gas began feeding the flames through a melted hose.  Soon the entire tractor was engulfed in flames and burned to the ground. I live in a rural area and did not have a cell phone with me so no help arrived.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of such an event occurring again is high given the age of the tractor and lack of regular maintenance.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the gasoline is overflowing into the air filter of the unit. The consumer stated that this issue has been occurring since 6/25/15.

The consumer stated that he has had the unit repaired three times through Sears. The consumer stated that he had the unit repaired because the engine isn't working properly. The consumer stated that Sears replaced the carburetor twice. 

The consumer stated that he had a technician out on 6/25/15 to install the carburetor. The consumer stated that the technician had to drain the gasoline twice. The consumer was notified by the technician that if the ignition/start key is left to the "on" position, it allows the gasoline to flow. The consumer believes that this is an unusual process and a safety hazard.

The consumer stated that he has open flames in his house and is worried that the gasoline fumes that are permeating through his house could cause fire hazards. The unit is located in his garage. 

The consumer's unit is covered under repair protection until 06/12/16.
justification: Gasoline overflowing into air filter and potential gasoline fumes in the house pose a fire hazard, though no injuries reported yet.

incident_description:
(06/19/2015) The consumer stated that her husband had been mowing grass for 30 min. prior to mowing around the horse trailer when reversing mower at trailer, he noticed  flames coming from the engine which is right behind the seat. Her husband immediately jumped off the mower. The fire department was called. They came and put the fire out. It appeared to have been an engine fire.

No injuries.
justification: Engine fire occurred but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We recently purchased from our local Austin, TX Lakeline Target store a pre-assembled, floor model of a 32" Threshold Fire Column in the Garden section, retailing at $129.99. It is Store Item Number (DPCI) 009-07-0769 and Online Number: 16538881.

It came pre-assembled as a demo model and we googled and found the instructions online before using it. Before using I even checked the Target website that had the following two comments pasted below.

http://www.target.com/p/threshold-fire-column/-/A-16538881?lnk=rec|pdp|viewed_viewed|pdpv1

I read the userÃÂs  comments/warning about holding the ignition before starting the gas,  this didnÃÂt seem to help.   The directions didnÃÂt seem to indicate this, either. 
 
After about two seconds of holding down the ignition we had a large fireball that came out of the fire column and ended up with non-serious burns on my fingers.  
 
IÃÂve operated gas grills for years and havenÃÂt ever seen anything like this.   It is a very dangerous product and I did contact the Retailer to express my concern of an unsafe product. 

To date, I have not received a response from Target, though I contacted them on Sunday, July 12.

IÃÂm wondering if Target has had other complaints about this product in addition to the comments on their website. I believe it merits further investigation.
justification: Customer suffered non-serious burns due to unexpected fireball, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her riding lawn mower exploded in her shed.  It was completely powered it off after using it and approximately 20 mins later there was an explosion, smoke was emitting from the shed.  Caller stated that she used her water hose to contain the fire that took sometime because it developed under the hood of the unit.  Caller stated that she did not notice any fuel leaks from the unit.

 5/11 Caller stated that she contacted the manufacturer and a agent was sent out about a week later, they took pictures of the incident, and she was informed that the manufacturer would be in touch with her.

Caller feels that this lawn mower is extremely unsafe and should be reported.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (severity level 2). The likelihood is 'possible' (3) as the cause was not immediately apparent and required investigation.

incident_description:
During the second use of my CH3 chipper the machine caught on fire and sustained damage to the belt and engine area.    

I first used the chipper on 5/8/2015 for about 2.5 hours chipping branches on my property.  During this use the machine operated flawlessly.  On my second use of the chipper on 5/13/2015 I had been chipping branches for about 2 hours.  The chipper had been operating normally throughout the time I was working.  The machine was running while I used my chainsaw to cut some branches I was going to feed into the machine.   After cutting the branches I turned my attention back to the chipper and saw flames coming from under the belt guard.  I immediately went to the chipper and turned the engine off.  I attempted to smother the flames with some dirt, but was unable to get any dirt under the belt guard, and having no tools to remove the belt guard I tipped the machine on it's side in an attempt reduce the available air, hoping this would smother the flame which was steadily increasing in size.  The flames became so large that the air filter/fuel shut off also caught on fire.  At this point I was fearful that the chipper would explode (almost a full tank of gas).   Fortunately I was able to douse the flames with a bucket of water prior to a catastrophic explosive event occurring.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage and posed a potential risk of explosion.

incident_description:
2009 Cub Cadet LTX-1045 lawn tractor, 20 HP Kohler engine (SV600) caught fire and mower was destroyed.  Fire broke out after I put mower in shed after mowing.  Smelled burning plastic, rushed to shed and pulled mower out, extinguished fire.  No personal injury, no structural damage to shed (which is attached to garage which is attached to house).  Smoke damage to shed.
Notified Kohler and Cub Cadet.  Cub Cadet stated that mower was out of warranty, for me to contact my homeowner's insurance co.
justification: Fire caused no injuries or deaths, but resulted in significant property damage (destroyed mower, smoke damage to shed).

incident_description: I'm inquiring about a product we own: a Ryobi Model RY14110A 48 volt 20-inch self-propelled lawnmower (Serial# BMP0780024). Our batteries weren't charging and my husband pulled them out. They are bulging and look dangerous. I started researching the internet including Home Depot where we bought it, as they are a Ryobi distributor. Many people on the reviews complained about their batteries not holding a charge, some posted pictures of the bulging, and others stated their batteries leaked acid in the garage. Supposedly a poor charger was the cause but Ryobi didn't contact us. The reviewers also said that Ryobi Customer Service hasn't been helpful, but a Ryobi Facebook e-mail address was. My husband e-mailed them today and they weren't helpful and told him to call Ryobi Customer Service. My husband called Ryobi Customer Service and they basically said since our lawnmower was built in 2011 that we are out of warranty. However, we were never notified of a recall and I don't see one on this website, either. Many reviewers bought new batteries but they just stopped working due to the malfunctioning charger which was causing the batteries to go bad. Some of the Home Depot reviewers had Ryobi reply on the website and suggest they buy a different Ryobi lithium model--even thought they had already spent $400-$500 on this model, plus any battery replacements at $129 a crack. Aren't companies supposed to replace defunct products/issue a recall? Reviewers commented that there was a recall but hardly anyone (including us) knew about this. I put the bulging batteries in a box in our cool basement. With temperatures hitting 90 degrees this weekend, I didn't want to risk an incident in our garage due to overheating. However, I also don't want to get rid of the evidence in case someone wants to see it. I took pictures but the bulging doesn't show as well in the pictures. Please advise if there is an investigation regarding this product and/or the battery charger. Thank you.
justification: Bulging batteries pose a fire risk, as evidenced by reviewer reports of battery leaks and overheating.

incident_description:
The gas tank has a very slow fuel leak due to cracks that appear to be the result of a manufacturing defect.  Since the machine is kept indoors, this leak is a fire or explosion hazard aggravated by the fact that it took several weeks to find it.  The leaking cracks are at the bottom of the gas tank; but, at the top of the tank, there is a set of cracks similar to those at the bottom.  The attached pictures show those top cracks where you can see how easy it is for gasoline to leak out if those cracks are at the bottom.  This defect should be corrected as soon as possible and in the meantime other users of this product should be warned to look for fuel leaks especially if they detect gasoline odor coming from the machine in an enclosed area.  Approximately a week ago (early July 2015), I contacted Husqvarna at 704-597-5000 where a spoke with a person called [REDACTED].  I asked [REDACTED] to report this hazard through his internal channels but he did not sound interested at all

NOTE:  Sorry, no pictures.  Your form did not rallow me to attach anything when I pressed the "Add Files" button but I can provide them by other means if you need them.
justification: The fuel leak, if not addressed, could lead to a fire or explosion, posing a significant risk to users.

incident_description:
I have a John Deere Lawn Tractor, serial number 1GXD100EPCC328347.
It has the same problem described in the recall release #11-325 where the blade brake does not engage and the blade continues to spin.

THe brake pad came off the support bracket, and it no longer applied force to the pulley.

I think that this safety recall #11-325 should be expanded to cover the later serial numbers, and that John Deere should consider a redesign of the product to stop this from happening.
justification: Although no injury has been reported, the incident could lead to serious harm if not addressed, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: My son was burned on his left arm and side while mowing.  The gas cap blew off spraying him with gasoline then igniting.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burns) and the description suggests a high likelihood of similar occurrences due to the nature of the task (mowing) and the volatile substance involved (gasoline).

incident_description: I purchased a "pocket hose" on 4/28/15 and while using it on 5/31/15 it exploded and the fabric part separated from the metal parts. A metal bolt inside the spigot attachment flew across the deck, one part went off the deck and another was blown across the deck. Had any of these parts hit me in the face or eye, I would have sustained a serious injury. I am going to mail or attempt to attach a photo showing the various parts as well as the fabric crinkle hose itself.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious injury if the metal parts had struck the user's face or eye.

incident_description:
Brinkmann Gas grill 4 burner; NINGBO Wanan RS 329 pressure regulator
Upon trying to light my grill, it just about exploded; flames shot out everywhere, I singed my hair and burned my finger trying to reach in to turn off the main valve at the tank.

Upon thinking and very careful testing, I figure the valve is defective and the pressure regulation functions are non-existent, i.e. straight pass-through of unregulated/uncontrolled LP gas to the burners.
justification: Injury occurred due to defective pressure regulator causing uncontrolled gas flow and flames.

incident_description:
While using a string trimmer, my forearm touched a hot spot on a metal plate of the engine and I suffered a burn (see photo).

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn), and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur frequently given proper safety precautions.

incident_description:
On Friday, July 3, 2015, I was using my Troy Bilt TB195BV electric leaf blower to clear grass and leaves from my back patio. About 15 minutes into using the leaf blower, the unit exploded in my hands shooting shards of plastic and parts of the engine and unit across the patio while simultaneously hitting me and the side of the house. 

I was struck in the stomach, groin and thigh, which caused bruising and minor lacerations to my stomach, right below my belly button.  

The Troy Bilt TB195BV unit was purchased at Lowes in Arlington Heights, IL on April 30, 2010.  

Product Information: 
Troy Bilt Electric Leaf Blower
Model: TB195BV
Serial Number (S):
justification: The incident resulted in minor lacerations and bruising, and the likelihood of such an event occurring during the use of an electric leaf blower is possible.

incident_description: Several years ago, we received a secondhand Toro Super Recycler GTS XL 6.0 HP lawnmower my father-in-law purchased at a garage sale. Since we have a perfectly good lawnmower already, this 2nd mower mostly sat in the garage & was only used a few times. It has not been used in 1-2 years at least. Today, my teenaged son was moving the mower to retrieve a couple scooters (things had been moved around because we just had to replace our garage door). When he unfolded the handle there was a very loud popping sound, like a backfire (the engine was not turned on), & the portion of the mower where the air filter & gastank is burst into flames. He doused the fire w/water. There was very little gas in the tank. We feel very fortunate there wasn't an explosion.
justification: While no one was injured, the incident could have resulted in property damage or injury due to the unexpected fire.

incident_description:
My electric hedge trimmer was being used to trim shrubs at my home and I took a break.  During the break the hedge trimmer started operating itself.  I heard the sound and went near the hedge trimmer and found a burnt smell as well.  After disconnecting the trimmer I found the smell still persisted. Upon removing the screws to see what had burnt, I found the black on-off switch that gets pressed when you hold down plastic on button is burnt.

If the trimmer were inside it could have caused a fire in the house/garage.
justification: The hedge trimmer operating on its own and emitting a burnt smell indicates a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or damage were reported.

incident_description: When operating this [weed trimmer], the hot exhaust blows onto my right forearm. It burns the skin just below the elbow
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the description mentions it happening 'just below the elbow', indicating a repeated or common occurrence.

incident_description:
Ariens mower model A20VA46
Serial number 041614A008790

Purchase date approximately 4/14 (mower is registered with Ariens).
Approximately 6/28/14 transmission was replaced by Boyd Tire & Appliance, Clover SC under warranty as it was defective.  Attempting to utilize reverse pedal mower jerks into reverse.  Then when in reverse attempting to depress forward pedal, mower jerks violently into forward cauing potential loss of control by operator.
At this time 5/21/15 the replaced transmission is exibiting same problems.  Will not go into reverse without hitting reverse pedal very hard.  Then will not go forward when depressing forward pedal unless hit hard, then jerks into forward motion making it difficult to control mower.
justification: The recurring transmission issues could lead to loss of control, potentially causing an incident.

incident_description: Purchased an Earthquake model# 600050v trimmer mower. Mower came assembled in the box. As soon as gasoline was added to the tank, it rapidly leaked out of the air filter area of the motor creating a fire hazard.
justification: Gasoline leaked rapidly from the mower, creating a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Pacific Hydrostar gas powered 2" clear water pump from Harbor Freight Tools in Corpus Christi, Texas.  I set it up according to manufacturer's instructions (add oil, gasoline, prime pump, and start).  I filled the gasoline tank with a quart of fuel, and started the pump.  It ran fine for about 15 minutes and then quit.  I checked the motor and then the gas tank, noting that it was empty.  Puzzled, I refilled the tank, and started it again.  It stopped again after ten or so minutes of operation.  Again, the fuel tank was empty.  I then realized the tank had a leak and fuel had spread across the surface of the water I was trying to pump out of our yard.  I checked the tank and fuel lines for obvious leaks, but they run from beneath the tank to the carburetor without any area of access or observation.  I could see an inline fuel filter but no obvious leaks.  The engine exhaust is immediately adjacent to the carburetor/air filter assembly so I decided not to tinker with it any further out of fear of either a fire or explosion and returned the pump to the store for a refund.  They were told both of the problem and this report.
justification: Potential for fire or explosion due to fuel leak, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
I was rolling my 26 1/2 inch Weber Kettle grill and it collapsed to the ground.  The supports that hold the legs to the grill had rusted away.  I bought the grill  4/8/14 and it fell apart 6/1/15   They said they had never heard of this happenng before at Weber. 

This grill also had a issue with the leg falling out of the same little supprt bracket that rusted out when I first got the grill. Weber sent a new leg kit.  I did a google search and other people have had this same problem.  Some using screws to secure the legs in so they do not fall out of the support bracket the legs attach 2.
justification: The grill collapsing due to rusted supports caused no injuries but could have, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

incident_description:
Using chain saw to cut wood.

Chain saw has an on / off trigger saw  AND an safety interlock switch.

The safety interlock switch is a slide switch which must be postioned and
held in the on position in order to activate the on/off trigger switch.

Cutting wood.  When wood was cut I released both the trigger switch ( should have
turned off imediately)  AND the interlock switch.  The chainsaw stayed ON and knocked
wood scratching left shin.  So I disconnected it from the power source.

The chain saw is not turning off via the switch.  When it is plugged back in... it will
start again.... I'm assuming on off switch is defective.

Okay.. this is slightly really dangerous when a device requiring use of both hands
does not turn off and requires user to disconnect from power source while holding
device with one hand.   Chain saws are pretty dangerous.
justification: Injury occurred due to defective on/off switch, making the chainsaw not turn off when the trigger was released, and it continued to operate when disconnected from the power source.

incident_description: Mowing grass when mower started on fire
justification: While rare, grass fires during mowing can occur due to equipment malfunction.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on 6/4/15 he sent a letter to the retailer (Attn: [REDACTED]) regarding the safety hazard with his Power Lever Tree Pruner. 

The consumer stated that the product malfunctioned while he was using it to cut a tree branch. The consumer stated that the pruner came apart at the connector that joins the two poles. It came apart at the lower end of the connector that is factory made tight. The cutting pole end that contains the saw blade came down with great force onto his left arm (bicep area) causing severe pain and bruising. The back of the saw teeth hit his arm. The consumer stated that if the cutting edge of the blade would have hit him, then he could have suffered a deep cut. 

The consumer added to please be advised that on 6/11/15, he went to the doctor complaining of pain and bruising and a large knot at the location where the blade end of the 14 feet power lever tree pruner hit his left arm in the bicep area. The consumer noted the diagnosis was contusion and hematoma at said area...he then went for an ultrasound on the same day to look for blood clots.

The consumer also noted after reviewing the report he noticed two items that should be corrected: 1) It is an injury to his left arm in the bicep area, and 2) His last name is spelled Capria, not Catria. 

The consumer also added he was notified o 6/10/15 by the insurance carrier of Home Depot that he would start an investigation...The rep, [REDACTED], asked him several questions and he sent the rep several pictures that are on his cell phone.  The consumer noted he enclosed the report and letter he sent Home Depot on 6/04/15.  The consumer stated he will try to send his cell phone pictures to the website: clearinghouse@CPSC.gov.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (contusion and hematoma) and could have been more severe if the cutting edge of the blade had hit the consumer.

incident_description: I bought a Cub Cadet SLTX 1054 lawn tractor from Home Depot in May of 2010, all was well until last year, after my son stopped cutting grass because it was getting dark he parked the tractor in our barn and the next morning when he went out to finish cutting there was a pool of oil and gas under the tractor.  We called a repair shop and they picked up the tractor and had to replace the carburetor because something had broken inside allowing fuel to leak into the engine crankcase. Now one year later we are having the same issue, fuel leaking into a hot engine crankcase seems like a serious safety issue to me on a product that is not very old?
justification: The incident has occurred twice in a short period, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I used my Masterbuilt Electric Smoker Model #20072612 for the first time. I loaded the wood chips into the chamber, inserted it into the smoker as directed and turned to drop them. A few minutes later I smelled fire. I looked and the inside of my smoker where the chamber was caught on fire. The smoker was smoking and shaking. I immediately turned off the smoker, unplugged the smoker, and put out the fire. It appears that the interior of this smoker is defective and the smoker chips did not drop where they should off but instead dropped on the burners and caught fire. I will never use this smoker again although it is almost new. I was traumatized by this incident.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage and could have escalated to a more severe outcome.

incident_description: I have a gas griddle from Blackstone BLACKSTONE GRIDDLE COOKING STATION -Mfg# 1554.  I purchased the item in March of 2015 and received in April 2015.   I used it in April 2015 and noticed the top part of the grill was warped in the grease V edge.  There is a grease V edge that in the middle of the grill  on the end that the oil collects and gets hot enough to snap and pop and get on anyone using it.  It also runs over the edge and can get on your feet with hot oil.  I contacted Blackstone right after the first time using it and sent them pictures and everything.  They pretty much told me that is the way the item is and deal with it by making sure you push the grease to the end as much as possible.  Even told me to put something under the left wheels to make it lean enough to run out quickly so it doesn't pool in the V.  If you only cook a few things on it its okay cause you can keep up.  Well we used it this weekend and had 12 hamburgers on it.  This grill can easily fit 12 hamburgers with plenty of room to spare as its 36" wide.  Well the grease was staying right in the V like before right up to the lip and every time you tried to push it to the grip tray it would come over and splat on the ground.  If this items   V drip edge was flat and not warped I could see it probably being okay.  But after contacting blackstone again they will do nothing about it and state that is the way it should be.  I was burned on the leg and foot back in April when I first used it and on 6/7/15 with the leg.
justification: The warped grease V edge on the grill causes hot oil to splatter, leading to burns, as evidenced by the user's experience.

incident_description:
Purchased Toro time master 20200 walk behind mower. Gas tank now sprays gasoline all over engine.
Fire and explosion hazard. Called Toro referred to Briggs who refers to local dealer site as they will not send parts to consumer.  


gas tank was not overfilled had air space at top unable to determine if cap or tank is cause.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to gasoline leakage, but no injuries reported.

incident_description: I own a Cub Cadet [Weed Trimmer]. Model BC490. Item 41ad490c912 sn [REDACTED] It has a plastic gasoline tank and cap. The cap started leaking. I went to Cub Cadet and had the cap replaced. It still leaks. Quite a bit in fact. It is quite a fire hazard. When I replaced the cap with another cap from my handheld blower from another manufacturer; it didn't leak. So as best I can tell it is a cap defect.
justification: Although no injuries have occurred, the significant gasoline leak poses a high fire hazard, making it an incident with a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his lawnmower purchased 15 - 20 years ago.
He noticed that he smelled gasoline lightly as he rode when cutting grass and when stopped, however through out the years he has become more aware of the odor and then became aware of dripping of gas over the past three years.
Around Springtime of 2014 he noticed that the gasoline dripping was increasing and he began calling for assistance but dealer in Russellville, AR advised him that there was nothing he could do to help him.
He then contacted the manufacturer who advised him to contact the dealer.
He contacted one in Dardanelle, AR where mower was purchased  but this one was out of business.

There are no injuries being reported - Thank goodness the consumer doesn't smoke
This caller is asking for a new fuel tank because he took his apart May 11th, 2015 but states that he was surprised to see what appeared to be epoxy around the seams and cracks outside the seams that he states had to be placed there at factory because he had never opened it before this day.
justification: No injuries reported despite gasoline leakage, but potential fire hazard exists.

incident_description: Fuel tank (plastic) leaking gasoline from inside of the tank thru the bolt area.  Will cause an explosion or fire.
justification: Gasoline leak from the fuel tank poses a high likelihood of fire or explosion, but the incident description does not mention any injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I was pre-heating my propane gas grill prior to use. I left for a few minutes to get the meat. When I returned there were flames and black smoke rolling out from under the grill lid. I turned off the burner valves to no avail. I opened the enclosed cabinet where the gas tank is stored and saw a jet of flame coming from the area of the connection between the regulator hose and the main gas manifold. I closed the tank valve and extinguished the flames. The next day I could see that the spark igniter unit was burned and melted, the on-off switch for the grill light was melted and had dripped onto the deck, the gas regulator hose was circumferentially burned and melted and the main gas manifold tube had perforated with rust and corrosion. This last seemed to be the source of the gas leak which ignited from the burner flame. I believe that the gas regulator hose was moments from burning through and allowing gas to flow freely from the tank. The grill is kept on a wooden deck next to the house.
justification: Injury was possible due to the proximity of the gas leak to the igniter and the potential for the hose to rupture, leading to a larger fire.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he was putting air in his snow thrower and the rim exploded.  He stated that the plastic rim became a projectile and caused injury to his left hand.  He went to the Richmond University Hospital where he was treated and sent home for follow up.

Caller stated that he experienced similar problems of Recall#07-003.  If the snow thrower's tires are over-inflated, the plastic wheel rims can burst, posing a risk of lacerations and fractures.

Caller stated that he knows his product is recalled but has not contact them as yet but will do so later.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the caller's experience aligns with the known risk of over-inflation in the recalled product.

incident_description: Several years ago my garage had burned and the insurance sent a replacement trimmer the my damaged one, the unit they sent me was the Grasshog XP model GH1000 trimmer/edger. I did not realize there had been a recall on it the until the other day when I was looking to purchase a replacement spool and found articles on the internet of injuries caused by this piece of equipment. While I have no sustained any injuries myself, the spool and spool cover of the unit have come off in use, as well as the pieces of the trimmer string. Is there some sort of exchange or refund? I don't really want to be using a dangerous unit.
justification: While no injuries were personally sustained, the incident description mentions several instances of parts coming off during use, indicating a potential for injury.

incident_description: I was using my Homelite leaf blower to blow the leaves out of my landscape rock in my backyard. My right hand was holding the handle, but I began to lose my grip. I went to use my left hand to stabilize the blower while my right hand got a better grip on the handle. When I placed my left hand on the underside of the blower the plastic guard covering the intake fan broke off. My middle finger on my left hand fell into the fan and I experienced severe injury. I had my neighbor across the street take me to the ER at St. Mary's Hospital. My nail was torn off, the distal phalange bone was broken in several areas, and the soft tissue to the tip of my finger was shredded requiring approximately eleven stitches. I have found pieces of the plastic strewn about my yard. I have been referred to see an orthopedic surgeon and a physical therapy center. I have been under their care since the incident.
justification: Injury occurred due to equipment failure, not a common occurrence but possible given the age and use of the leaf blower.

incident_description: I ordered and received a PockeTech 48 Inch High Limb Chain Saw from Amazon.com. The product came with a rope, a chain with sharp teeth on both sides, and a throwing bag. I attempted to use it to remove a high limb.  The throwing bag is made of tough fabric and worked well. The chain saw itself works well too. The rope, however, failed. It is attached to the chain with a crimped metal connection. The crimped metal connection on mine came apart while I was sawing. As I was pulling on the rope at the time the crimped connection failed, the end of the rope with the crimp sped towards my hand and inflicted a painful cut.
justification: The rope's crimped metal connection failing and causing a cut to the user's hand indicates a severe injury.

incident_description: Was smoking some jerky and shortly after turning the smoker on the chips in the pan flamed up. I immediately opened the door and extinguished it with a water bottle.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (severity level 2). The likelihood is 'possible' (3) as it required specific conditions and user action.

incident_description:
This caller purchased the first lawn mower from the church after it was given to them by the first owner. 
He purchased the mower sometime in 2010 with no significant problems until sometime around the end of March or beginning of April 2015 when he noticed a gas leak.
The gas was leaking from a seam where the hose goes to the carburetor and was running to the frame by the drive belt.
The drive belt becomes hot when tractor is in use which has caused the consumer to report this mower as a fire hazard,
There are no injuries to be reported 
The consumer contacted the manufacturer sometime in April 2015
Product2 _ Lawn mower was purchased by caller from widow of first owner between 2010 and 2011.
He had no problems with this mower until May 7th, 2015 when he started it then noticed that it was leaking from a seam where the hose goes to the carburetor and was running to the frame by the drive belt.
He is reporting this lawn mower as a fire hazard with the same reasoning as with the first lawn mower.
There are no injuries being reported
He has not contacted the manufacturer for this second lawn mower because he states that when he contacted them for the first mower he was informed that the parts had been discontinued.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the gas leak and potential fire hazard pose a significant risk.

incident_description:
Hustler X-one commercial grade Zero Turn Mower.  Gas tank Vent seal split leaking and spraying fuel on driver and Motor.
  This seal was replaced by dealer in 2012 under a previous recall.
 I reported this event to Dealer and they said it wasn't a covered fix by Warranty or the safety recall.
 They would sell me the part and I could repair it myself.   There was no damage from use to this mower prior to this incident, it has only 80 hours of use since purchased and only at my home. 
 
This is a very real Fire and safety hazard and obviously a defect in materials and/or Design.
justification: Fuel spraying on driver and motor poses a high likelihood of ignition, leading to an incident but no injury.

incident_description:
Fiesta Grill called "Blue Ember" purchased 05/28/2009 from Home Depot. It was a clearance item assuming it was left over stock from the year prior. Our climate May is spring time thus assuming the product was a floor model for 2008. The exact amount is $419.04.

Last year a fire occurred where the rubber gas hose lit along with the interior and inside the base where the propane tank sits. After purchasing another rubber hose, I learned these grills were recalled. At that time I could not locate the serial number. My model no. is FG50069.

05/14/2015 I contacted the manufacturer by phone. Received an email to send pics. 
05/15/2015 I emailed [REDACTED](using [REDACTED]) by submitting pics. Prior to researching the day of purchase I incorrectly guessed the purchase took place in August of 2009.
05/15/2015 [REDACTED] emails me stating my grill is not within the grill does not fall within the 2006-2008 recall range. 
05/15/2015 I placed a call to the CPSC (you) and spoke to a lady who is in the process of forwarding my contact info and subject matter to another department. 

Knowing the fire is identical to multiple grills that were recalled, I firmly believe this $800.00 product purchase in May of 2009 should fall within the guidelines of both recalls (or extended) and a safety kit should be sent promptly.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of a fire occurring due to a recalled grill poses a significant risk of injury if it were to happen again.

incident_description: The 5-gallon gas tank on the Craftsman GT5000 (model #917.276071, serial number 05314B002776) garden tractor has deteriorated and developed cracks in the top.  As a result, gasoline vapors continually escape from the tank and create an explosive environment in any enclosed space where the tractor is parked.  There is a health risk as well from inhaling gasoline fumes when working in the garage where the tractor is stored.  Sears no longer sells a replacement part for this tractor's gas tank so we're stuck with a potentially dangerous product.
justification: Gasoline vapors create an explosive environment and pose a health risk from inhaling fumes, but no immediate injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description: I was using my smoker for the first time and "seasoning" the smoker like the instructions tell you to. I walked inside the house while the smoker was outside warming up and reaching temperature. My wife and I heard a loud bang like something slammed into the house and I ran outside to see what happened. The smoker's door had blown open and was bent at the hinge on the bottom. No one was injured but the items case and door was damaged slightly.
justification: The smoker's door blew open and was damaged, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Masterbuilt Model 20070512 40-Inch Smoker with Viewing Window and RF RemoteControl  

I purchased this product  November 13th, 2013 - I was smoking turkey and chicken for the holidays -  the unit had been smoking a while and all seemed to be going well - until a fire shot out the right side of the smoker - the entire inside was on fire -I WAS IN A PANIC MODE -It was a huge fire.  I am elderly and thought I must have done something wrong.   I closed the air hole off to suffocate the fire. It took the fire 15 or more minutes to burn out. The unit smoked the entire patio - I  let it cool and cleaned the unit - put the cover on it and placed in the garage, where it has sat now for 2 years.  I am afraid to use it, and felt robbed.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage and could have escalated, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his noticed that his tractor was leaking gas sometime in March.  He stated that he was awakened in the middle of the night to an overwhelming gas odor and discovered that most of the fuel had leaked onto the garage floor.  This seems that it could have sparked and caused a fire.  The manufacturer was contacted and the rep informed him that they were unaware of any recalls and informed him to contact a dealer close to him.  He directed the agent to the agency's website in accordance to Alert #02-517.  Although his model and serial number is not affected he is experiencing the same problem.


Caller stated that he contacted the dealer and he advised him that he was having a safety issue and would get back to him about the matter.  4/2015 He stated that he waited for about 2 weeks and called again.  He spoke to another rep at the dealer and he was informed that he would get in touch with Supervisor and then contact him.  He has not heard from anyone since.


Caller feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be included in a recall.
justification: While no injury or fire occurred, the incident involved a significant gas leak onto the garage floor, posing a high likelihood of ignition and subsequent fire.

incident_description:
I purchased a new Snapper rider last year and it has been nothing but a problem since I got it.
I believe it is totally unsafe and should be recalled.  After the first few cuts the seat slid and I
fell off of the mower.  I lifted it to discover the seat bolts unattached and laying loose.  The
rider sounds creaky when you are driving it like a 100 year old box spring.  The mower stops
when the steering wheel is turned and then lunges forward.  I have pulled my back several time because of these lunges and had to stop mowing due to the pain to rest and finish another day. The front wheels of the mower are cambered outward by design. There has been a screeching sound that comes from under the mower and the Dealer's repair man told  me this is a problem with all new Snapper riders.  I have had it in for repair twice before for this problem already.  When it happened a third time grease came pouring out of the rear axle onto the rim.  My "NEW" Snapper is currently being repaired at the Dealer's a third time for this problem as I write this and the dealer has advised me that he has contacted the manufacturer concerning this recurring problem.
justification: Multiple injuries reported due to seat malfunction and mower lunging, with recurring axle grease leakage.

incident_description:
I was using my Black & Decker CM1640 16-Inch 40-volt Cordless Mower yesterday, and when I released the red handle for blade engage/disengage the mower did not stop, but kept running (spinning the blade).  The only way I could get it to stop was removed the key or remove the battery.   When I reinserted the key, the blade would immediately start spinning, with my depressing the start button and holding down the bladed engage/disengage handle.  No injury occurred as I noticed the problem and acted cautiously. However, that red handle is the primary safety feature of the mower and is required to stop the blade when released.

Note: I've had the mower for almost a year, and this was the first time this occurred.  

I contacted Black & Decker who indicated I should bring it in for warranty service.  I suggested to them that they should file a report with the CPSC, but they declined.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the primary safety feature of the mower failed, posing a potential hazard.

incident_description:
2005 Craftsman Husqvarna Riding Lawn Mower, model# 917.276360 with serial# 
On Monday, April 27th, 2015 this caller was using a leaf collection product being towed by her riding lawnmower, after approximately two and one half hours on and off time she turned off.

She dumped the leaves and then got back on the lawnmower, turned it on heard a backfire, saw smoke so turned it back off.

She then saw flames and the lawnmower started back up again by itself.

She got off the lawnmower then her husband took a stick and pushed the wires away from the battery in an attempt to get it to turn off.

The lawnmower then stopped running.

She and her husband, a neighbor and her son used fire extinguishers to extinguish the flame.

She has pictures that she will attach when returning this report, the lawnmower is totaled.

The caller and her husband have ordered a new riding mower from the same manufacturer and retailer.  She would like to ask for some relief in the pricing of this ride on mower.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident resulted in significant property damage (totaled lawnmower).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he fully charged the battery before first use. The consumer used the product for the first time without any problems. 

After use, the consumer charged the battery overnight so he can use the product again the next day.

The consumer went to use the product again the next day. The consumer used it for about 2 minutes and received a shock on his right arm that went up to his elbow. The consumer suffered from some initial pain on his arm that eventually went away. The consumer was holding the leaf blower from the handle. 

The consumer stated that after receiving the shock, the leaf blower stopped working. The consumer stated that the battery shows full charge.

The consumer has taken the battery out few times and tried to use the leaf blower but it does not turn on.

The consumer stated that he contacted the # on the box for the distributor (LG  Solutions: 1-888-356-2258) and was on hold for 42 minutes before being able to speak to anyone. The consumer was informed to take the product back to the retailer for an exchange. The consumer stated that he would like to receive a refund instead.

The consumer will try to hold on to the product if possible.
justification: The consumer experienced an injury (shock and pain) while using the product, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: I have a Ryobi 40V cordless blower (Model # RY40411).  When I was done using it, I put it away in an outdoor closet.  About 10 minutes later, I heard a exhaust type of noise inside my house.  After a few minutes of trying to identify the source of the noise, it became apparent that the blower started on its own.  As I went outside to investigate, the noise stopped.  I then opened my closet door and discovered that the Ryobi was on fire.
justification: The blower starting on its own and catching fire poses a risk of property damage and potential injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
10/15/2014 - The consumer plugged the extension cord to the wall and the leaf blower to the extension cord. Approximately thirty minutes later, the consumer smelled smoke around him. When he looked to the ground, he noticed that there was flames where the leaf blower connected to the extension cord. 

The consumer turned off the leaf blower and unplugged the extension cord from the wall. 

The consumer put the leaf blower away and threw away the extension cord as it had melted. He indicates that he had to use a plumbing wrench to separate the extension cord and the leaf blower cord as they had welded together due to the fire.

The consumer indicates that he had owned the extension cord for at least ten years and never had any incidents with it prior to using it with the leaf blower. The consumer had used the extension cord with hedge trimmers, leaf blowers, vacuums, etc. and never experienced issues so he is certain the problem was the left blower by Homelite. 

The consumer never used the leaf blower again.

The consumer indicates that he checked online to see if his unit had been recalled and his model is not included in any recall. 

The consumer believes this product poses a safety and fire hazard. The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer does not plan on contacting the manufacturer but does intend on returning the product to its place of purchase. 

The consumer plans on purchasing a different leaf blower.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a fire caused by a faulty leaf blower, making it an incident with potential for injury.

incident_description: The lawn mower is very hard to start pulling at least 10 times and when cutting gas leaks out of the gas cap very scary and that's the reason I'm writing
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning lawn mower that is difficult to start and leaks gas, posing a potential fire hazard but no immediate injury reported.

incident_description: I have purchased two Toro 22 inch recycler mowers from Home Depot. #1 was purchased in 2013 and #2 was purchased in 2014. Both mowers developed significant fuel leaks around the fuel cap after one season of use. #1 was taken to a repair center in the summer of 2014 and required a new fuel tank. The repair center stated that the was a defect on the tank where the fuel cap screwed on. It took approximately one month to repair due to the tank being on back order. incident_description:

02/15/2015 The consumer's 18-month-old nephew put his hand in the gate and all of a sudden, his hand went completely through the gate and created a hole in it. They also informed the consumer that they would replace the unit but that the consumers would indeed have to pay for the shipping. 

The consumer called the manufacturer again and spoke to the owner, [REDACTED]. The consumer then spoke to another one of the other owners, [REDACTED], because she was unsatisfied with how they were handling the issue. The consumer contacted the manufacturer again and asked for their insurance information because they wanted to file a claim. incident_description:
Product: Toro 17 inch String Trimmer.  Purchased 10/07/13 at Home Depot
Model no.:  51956
SN: 312000006

Problem:  Unit developed a significant gas leak which was only detected after a short period of operation.

The product had been hanging in an unheated garage over the winter in Denton, TX.  It was hanging in such a manner as to be protected from damage.

Upon using the string trimmer I noticed a gas leak because gas was being splashed on my legs.  The trimmer had not shown any signs of leaking while it was hanging in the garage.  It was hanging in the normal operating position with the gas cap pointing up.

The gas leak is coming from one of the two small exit tubes located near the top of the gas tank.  I determined this by cleaning all the gas residue off the surface of the tank, checking the o-ring seal on the gas cap for any foreign objects that might create a leak and starting to place a short strip of paper napkin next to any potential leak site (gas cap, exit tubes, seal between the two halves of the plastic tank). 

I inverted the machine so the gas cap was pointing down.  I removed the air filter cover to have better access to the exit tubes.  I started to place the paper napkin strips around the two exit tubes when I noticed a significant amount of gas leaking from the tank from around where the tubes penetrated the tank.  I did not apply any pressure to the tank but simply allowed gravity (and internal vapor pressure) to work.  The leak is significant.

The reason the machine did not leak while hanging in the garage is the exit lines were above the level of the gas in the tank and the tank was upright.  Had it been hanging upside down I am sure it would have leaked.

There was no evidence of damage to either of the exit tubes.  There was no indication they had been pulled or otherwise disturbed.  The seal must be on the inside of the tank because there is no evidence of one when viewed from the exterior.

The exit tubes are shielded from the body of the motor by a heavy paper (?) shield.  The exhaust is directly below the leaking tubes but is also shielded by the paper barrier.

The unit did not ignite while I was using it and I had no indication gas had been splashed on to any hot parts.  The vibration and continual re-positioning of the machine while in use splattered gas droplets all over, however.

Had I not been wearing shorts I would not have felt the gas falling on my leg and would have continued to use the trimmer since the motor is held behind you.

Friday, April 10, 2015. I have determined the cause of the gas leak in this report. The exit gas tube from the trimmer gas tank is a "pressed fit" through the tank wall. The compressed tube is expected to be the seal. Over time (less than 2 years in this case) the tube hardens reducing the tube's pressure on the hole in the tank. It no longer forms a seal. This was demonstrated to me when I took it in for repair.
justification: Gas leak could have caused a fire or explosion, posing a significant risk.

incident_description:
I purchased the Primus Firehole 200 stove brand new from REI (Recreational Equipment Inc.)

I used the stove for cooking on three separate occasions. On the first occasion, the stove worked fine.

On the second and third occasions, I noticed the flame sputtering on both of the burners, indicating that they weren't receiving sufficient fuel.  On the fourth occasion, when attaching a propane fuel bottle, the gas immediately began leaking from inside the stove.  This was not a small leak, but a full-on flow of propane.  The smell of propane filled the air around me.

I immediately disconnected the fuel bottle from the hose attachment.  After disassembling the panel from the bottom of the stove, the cause was very clear.  The copper tube that carried the gas from the fuel source to the first burner had broken at the soldering point where it attached to the brass fitting that the rubber fuel hose connects to.  

This caused propane gas to spew into the interior of the stove unhindered when a propane bottle was connected to the hose.  Had I made an attempt to light the stove, it almost certainly would have resulted in an explosion.
justification: Potential for severe injury or death due to gas leak and risk of explosion.

On Friday, February 20th, 2015 the caller started the pellet stove, went to the other side of the house.
After approximately one half hour the caller smelled smoke and went to investigate, the lights of the control panel were all blinking and the stove was out.
Since there was no fire she decided to trouble shoot and re light the stove.
Approximately one half hour to one hour she smelled smoke again. 
She returned to the stove and found her bedroom where the stove was sitting engulfed in gray smoke but no fire again.
She continued to investigate and realized that the plastic compartment that hold the pellets had a hole in it and that the pellets had been sifting down into the motor like an hour glass.

This caller is reporting this as a severe safety hazard and is asking for her monies.to be returned for this product.and for her bedroom to be repainted at manufacturer expense.

The consumer provided photos and added: photo #1 - stove functioning properly; photo #2 - inside the hopper, still smoking pellets have poured down hole; photo #3 - after the fire was out, she removed the pellets and discovered the hopper floor had melted a huge hole; and photo #4 - left side-fire melted the insulation and wood placed in the window opening.
justification: Although no fire occurred, the incident involved significant smoke inhalation and potential for fire, posing a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description:

The smoldering hot metal showered onto the propane tank and hoses below. This could have been a life threatening situation for all of us. I shut off the burners. I could not shut off the propane tank valve because it was covered in shards of smoldering hot rusty sheet metal. I had to anxiously wait far away for it to cool so I could shut the valve. I cannot fathom why a grill would be designed so poorly. The metal between the actual flames and the fuel source is paper thing steel that rusts away in less than two years creating a potentially grave situation!!

My attempts to resolve this issue with Sears have been less than satisfactory. I am one of thousands of consumers experiencing this based on my own internet research. There needs to be a product-wide recall on these life threatening appliances.

Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in potential injury, as hot metal fell onto the propane tank, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the widespread issue with the grill's design.

incident_description:
On February 25,2015 I purchased a Black & Decker hand trowel from Walmart. I arrived home and a few hours later attempted to remove the product packaging that was affixed with a zip tie, a very tight, black zip tie. 
It was difficult to get the tip of the scissors up under the zip tie because it was excessively tight, so I stuck the pointed tip of the trowel down onto the driveway to get some leverage. The trowel was upright in my left hand and kitchen scissors were in my right, as I was attempting to get the tip of the scissors under the tie, my right hand slipped and smashed down onto the back edge of the trowel, the part most people would assume to be blunt, it wasnÃÂt. There was a crescent shaped divot out of the right side of the back of the trowel, and itÃÂs nearly razor sharp. That is exactly where my right forefinger smashed into, I pulled the trowel away and out of my finger, exposing what I thought looked like bone. I freaked out not understanding how this could of happened, I thought I had broken the trowel when I looked at the razor sharp divot.
Luckily I had neighbors who came to my rescue, they were as perplexed as I was as to why this trowel was like this. I understand now it is to remove roots and such, in a backward motion. My concern is it was not labeled to perform this function, not anywhere on the packaging, and the placement of product label obscured the sharp edge. I had no idea it was there. It is extremely dangerous and has caused me a lot of grief. I am a manager of a hair salon so my fingers are very important. I have not been able to work for 10 days now and am concerned because I don't have all the feeling in my finger back.
This product needs to be labeled differently and I wish we would ban zip ties!
justification: The trowel's sharp edge caused a significant injury, and while it's not common, it's possible given the product's design and lack of clear labeling.
