incident_description:
The Poulan chain saw model PP4620AVX  has a chain tightening system that locks the adjustment with a crank handle. This handle is loosened and the chain tension is adjusted, then the handle it tightened down. The problem arises in that the crank handle tightens only one bolt to secure the bar in position. Most chain saws use two nuts to secure the bar. The Poulan saw referenced has two studs through the bar just as most other models, but only one is used, the crank handle tightening the nut on the single stud used to secure the bar.

In use, the single nut is insufficient to secure the bar, and as a result, the chain is tight for a short time, then rapidly loses adjustment resulting in the chain flying off the bar while in use, if the loosening of the chain is not immediately noticed. At first I thought I was just not tightening the crank enough, but in talking with other Poulan owners, discovered that they were experiencing the same problem. The crank handle cannot be tightened enough to hold the bar in place.

In August of 2014, I addressed my concerns to the only address I could find for Poulan, at 
Poulan
335 Harris Corners Parkway, 
Charlotte, NC 28269

No reply was ever received.
justification: The design flaw in the Poulan chain saw model PP4620AVX, using only one bolt to secure the bar, increases the likelihood of the chain flying off while in use, posing a significant safety hazard.

The Chainbrake assembly of this chainsaw, which protects users from deadly kickback, is constructed of plastics parts which are in the direct path of hot exhaust gases from the muffler.  After only a few minutes of use the plastic begins to melt, degrading and eventually defeating the kickback protection of the assembly.  I have replaced the Chainbrake Assembly 3 times since I have owned this chainsaw.  The newly replaced part has signs of failure after only 15 minutes use.  The part need to be either; 
1, Manufactured of a more heat resistant material, or
2. Shielded from hot exhaust gases from the muffler, or
3. A re-designed muffler directing hot exhaust gases elsewhere.
justification: Melting plastic parts pose a high risk of injury due to kickback, as evidenced by repeated failures and short lifespan of the replacement parts.

incident_description:
I used the RidRite Advanced Electronic Pest Control System (Model RR303XL) to repel mice in my vacation condo in [REDACTED]. These devices are permanently plugged into an AC duplex outlet and operate continuously sending out ultrasound that supposedly repels pests.  After about 14 months of use, one of these devices caused a smoldering fire.  Two others elsewhere in the condo did not exhibit such behavior.  For reasons that are not clear, the defective device created a short circuit within it that caused a enough electrical amperage to be drawn to melt the plastic duplex outlet which the device was plugged into, melt the insulation of the hot wire lead connected to the outlet, and melt a portion of the plastic electrical box in which the outlet was mounted.  The device itself showed signs of excessive heat and melted plastic with brown discoloration near the electrical plug on the back side.  The melting of the electrical box led to a visible smoldering fire with smoke.  There was no flame at that point.  Prior to this event, for the period of a week clearly evident foul odor was noticed intermittently in the vicinity of the outlet (without evident smoke). Early on the source of the odor could not be determined, nor was there any evidence of smoke or fire.  After about a week in the condo, visible smoke was evident from the outlet.  Inspection revealed the electrical damage to the outlet itself, the associated wiring insulation, and the electrical box.  Had this not been detected and power disconnected, a fire might have resulted in the surrounding wooden paneling or support studs.

According to the manufacturer's information, this product is UL listed #3RR1.  The manufacturer is Lancer & Loader Group LLC, New York, NY 10016.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage and posed a potential fire risk, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Subject:	Electrical hazard finding
Area:		Consumer grade home improvement lighting
Product:	Defiant brand Motion Security Light 463 837 
Retailer:	The Home Depot
Problem:	Dangerously long screw results in contacting/cutting into wire insulation

	This lighting equipment was being installed on the outside of a garage using a metal weatherproof round junction box, 1 ÃÂ½ in deep.

From The Home Depot's website:
[REDACTED]

	The problem is with the hardware supplied with the Defiant Security Light. The main mounting screw, part ÃÂccÃÂ from the manual, is much too long and because it is positioned directly over the incoming 120V power wires, it cuts into the insulation while attaching the light to the box. The installer cannot know this has happened because it is now unseen. 
	In this particular installation the ungrounded hot wire and the ground wire were both damaged and shorted through the screw resulting in the metal round box to be energized (the ground lead was connected to the ground lug of the round box). The light still worked so no indication of a problem until the installer was applying sealant around the box and was shocked. See photos of the installation then the damaged insulation found afterward.

	The screw is 40mm long and has 25mm protruding into the box which is much too long, the screw should either be shorter by at least 10mm or offset so as not directly over the incoming wires ÃÂ or both.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (shock) due to a design flaw in the product, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the widespread use of such lights and the lack of awareness about the issue.

I have used this electric leaf blower/vacuum for several years to vacuum leaves around shrubs and other things in the landscape of my home.  This past weekend, while using the unit in the vacuum configuration, it picked up a stone (which is impossible to avoid when working around a large yard) and it THREW THE STONE THROUGH THE HOUSING OF THE UNIT AND INTO MY BODY AT HIGH SPEED.  The stone made a jagged hole about 1-2 inches across in the plastic body of the leaf blower - it went right through, and hit me in the hip. incident_description:
On Saturday 11/22/14, my 16 year old grandson was cutting our lawn and mulching up the last few leaves in the yard for the final time this season with our 2 year old Cub Cadet LTX1045 riding lawn tractor. He has used this lawn tractor for the past two years every week, so he is very familiar with how this mower operates.

When he was done cutting the grass, he parked the lawn tractor by the rear door to the house, shut it off, and went inside. Within less than a minute he was in the kitchen and happened to look out the window and observed light smoke coming from the front of the lawn tractor. He immediately went outside, pulled out the hydrostatic bypass rod to put the lawn tractor in freewheel mode, and then pushed the mower approximately 50 feet away from the house while yelling to my wife (who was outside in the yard at the time) that the mower was on fire. He also opened the hood to see what was burning. He observed a very small fire from somewhere underneath the front of the engine with light smoke coming from it.

The outside water was turned off for the winter, so my wife went inside and filled a pan of water, gave it to my grandson, and he threw it on the engine. It seemed to help a little, so they got more water and threw it on the engine. They then realized that the smoke was increasing and the small fire was not going out.

My grandson ran across the street to where I was visiting and told me that the lawnmower was on fire. I went with him immediately, and as we approached my house I told my grandson where the fire extinguishers were in the house and said to go in the front door and get them. As I came around the corner of the house and saw the lawnmower in the backyard, I could see that the flames were shooting 4 to 5 feet above the engine. My grandson came out the back door with the extinguishers. I took one from him and put out the fire with a short burst from the extinguisher - it was an A, B, C rated (chemical powder type) fire extinguisher.

All of the damage appears to be located on the front, middle, and top of the engine. Whatever plastic shrouds and wires that were in those areas are either burnt, melted, or unrecognizable. The fire didnÃÂt make it through into the gas tank, but a corner of the plastic gas tank is charred. The hood doesnÃÂt appear to be damaged because my grandson had opened it right away when he initially moved the lawnmower.

We are very thankful that my grandson saw the smoke when he did and was smart enough to put the tractor in freewheel mode and strong enough to be able to push the lawn tractor away from the house, otherwise it would have been a much worse situation if the house or gas grill (which was also right next to where he initially parked the lawn tractor) had caught fire.

We donÃÂt know what caused this fire. It was a cool day, the lawn tractor was not working hard at all, and there is no sign of a gas leak from the gas tank or the fuel filter. We changed the oil and filter early in the season and at that time we had thoroughly cleaned up any dirt between the engine cooling fins and on the engine itself, so there was no dirt accumulation on the engine. I also checked the oil level after the fire and it is full.

I will contact the manufacturer this week.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire that could have caused property damage or injuries if not quickly contained.

incident_description: Name = [REDACTED] Organization/Affiliation = self Daytime Phone = [REDACTED] E-mail address = [REDACTED] Message = I have recently discovered a potential hazardous condition with the Sunsetter "Oasis" Free Standing Awning. The self contained drive motor is subject to a ground fault if it gets wet. Sunsetter, Inc. is aware of this problem as indicated in its literature. Apparently the thermal sensor which is integral to the motor causes the actual fault. It is not necessary to operate the motor for the fault to occur. It just has to be plugged in to the outlet. This problem eventually goes away after the system dries out. In my case I had the awning plugged into a GFI protected outlet and was not aware that it failed until I noticed an odor coming from my spare refrigerator located in the garage and also connected to the same GFI circuit. This certainly makes for an unreliable circuit since other devices connected to the GFI sourced circuit will be turned off whenever the Awning connection fails. Sunsetter does recommend that their product is connected to a GFI outlet and they don't feel that they have a hazardous design problem. This assumes that the consumer is using an appropriate GFI protected circuit, but of course this cannot be guaranteed and the excited consumer may not have read all the instructions (many of which are found in extraneous fine print) and has plugged the unit into a non-protected circuit. This free standing "Oasis" product is relatively new and does not have the same protections as does the prior wall mounted units. The wall mounted units have a vinyl flap that protects the motor from moisture when the awning is rolled up and when rolled down most water rolls off the end of the awning. The free standing model has no built in vinyl flap and when open or closed is subject to water accumulating in the tubing which contains the motor. The consumer can buy an additional cover for the unit for use when it is unfurled, but this is very inconvenient to install each time the awning is closed up. You need a ladder to reach the top of the awning. In summary, this product can impact the reliability of household wiring and at worst present a hazardous shock condition. Sunsetter, Inc. should be encouraged to review their product design and come up with a way to protect this motor from outside elements. CPSC should be involved in encouraging and in approving the design change.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the potential for electrical shock due to a ground fault poses a significant risk, especially considering the product's newness and lack of widespread awareness about its design flaw.

Most noticeable in the morning after the garage was closed all night. I looked everywhere in the garage for leaking fuel.
Cars, lawn mowers, fuel storage, etc. I could not find where the fuel odor was coming from. 

After  a month of this odor I rechecked the mowers closely and found that the John Deere L111 fuel tank was seeping very slowly. The grass clippings were absorbing the seeping fuel so nothing was dripping onto the garage floor. The fuel vapors were filling the garage. I was lucky that the concentration was not sufficient to cause an explosion. I have since moved the tractor out of the house and I am considering my options to replace the leaking fuel tank. 

I contacted John Deere to see if there is a recall on the mowers with this tank style. They said no. I see on the CPSC web site that there have been recalls on leaking John Deere fuel tanks in the past.  

It is important to note that John Deere has changed the tank style for the replacement part. The old tank is a two piece seam tank. The replacement is a one piece no seam product. To me it is obvious John Deere is aware of the problem.  

I believe John Deere should replace the tank. 

Thank you.

[REDACTED]

He was able to open the garage door and as we were leaving the house we saw smoke spilling out of the garage and knew something was on fire. The cord going to the electrical panel was intact. We have an updated electrical service that was inspected and is in working order up to code. We would have expected the unit to short out and trip a breaker not get engulfed in flames. If we were not home or not have caught it as early as we did our home would have been a total loss. As you can imagine it was very scary for all of us and I don't disagree we were lucky but my family's safety is my number 1 priority. I would not want this to happen to another person. This product is dangerous and something needs to be done.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire in the garage, posing a high risk to the entire house and family.

incident_description:
On April 18, 2014 I purchased a gas grill from Sear's store located in Seaford Delaware a Kenmore Model#  720-0830A.  I used my grill over the next few weeks and had intermittent problems getting it to light. Sometimes it would light on the first attempt like you would normally expect and other times it took several attempts to get it to light.  On July 8, 2014 I attempted to light the grill at approximately 1850 hours. My first few attempts to get the grill lit were unsuccessful.  I tried several different burners thinking there may be a problem with one or two specific burners. I then took the regulator off of the LP gas tank, I remove the tank to feel it's weight. After verifying the tank was heavy and had plenty of fuel I reattach the regulator and install the tank in the grill.  I again attempted to light the grill and was unsuccessful.  I turned on several burners in an attempt to get fuel to the burners.  When I pressed the igniter a large ball of fire came out of the top of the grill (which was open) as well as the bottom of the grill (where the gas tank is stored).  I was blown back a bit.  Once I stood up I found I had sustained burns to my left leg, left arm, neck and face.  I was immediately taken to the emergency department at my local hospital.  From there I was transferred within the hour to a specialty burn care hospital in Baltimore, Johns Hopkins Bayview Hospital. I spent the next two days in the burn intensive care unit. I had sustained second-degree burns over 6% of my body.  After being discharged and recovering for the next few weeks I again attempted to use the grill.  My first attempt at using the grill after my recovery was successful. The grill lit just as anticipated and had no problems.  My second attempt at using the grill was unsuccessful and I again could not get it lit after multiple attempts using multiple different burners.  After being frustrated from spending $400 on a grill that I could never longer use I started looking for remedies.  I was strongly suspicious of the gas regulator being faulty.  My reason for the suspicion was the fact that at times when lighting it you could not even smell gas. I felt as though the regulator would not always pass fuel.  I purchased a new gas regulator and hose I installed it on the grill and I've now been using it for several weeks with no issues at all.  I strongly suspect the gas regulator has some type of defect. I contacted Sears and was transferred around amongst many departments finally landing in the recall department.  I spoke to a gentleman and told him my story I gave him the model number of my grill he responded with "yes your grill has a recall". The gentleman stated that parts would be sent out to my home and once I receive them to call the numbers provided and a technician would come out and replace the faulty parts.  I asked him to elaborate on the recall because I wanted to know if it was safe to use or what parts were involved in the recall. He stated he only had part numbers and had no further information, he then transferred me to the service department. I spoke to a very nice gentleman there that put the model number into the computer and then told me there was no recall and had no idea with the other gentleman was talking about. He did suggest that I contact the Consumer Product Safety Commission and file a report.  I simply don't want this to happen to anyone else.  I have retained the original gas regulator should your agency want it for testing purposes.  I would be happy to answer any questions or provide additional documentation such as receipt for the grill, medical records, and pictures of my injuries. Thank you for your time and looking into this matter.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns over 6% of the body, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of occurrence is rated 3 (Possible) as it happened once but could potentially recur due to the suspected faulty regulator.

incident_description: On August 17, 2014 I was mowing our field with our 2 year old Husqvarna YTH 2454 lawn tractor, with a [REDACTED] 24 HP engine, model 445677, Type 0176 E1, Code 060103YG.  After about an hour of mowing it suddenly stopped running as if the key had been turned off.  When I attempted to restart it about 2 pints of fuel leaked out of the hot muffler.  I could not see the leaking fuel because I was sitting on the tractor.  I found out later that it was also pumping fuel into the crankcase.  Fuel leaking trough the hot muffler could easily have caused a fire.  Fuel in the crankcase could also damage the engine. I contacted the dealer and spoke to a mechanic.  After discussing a few options he felt it was probably the fuel solenoid.  He mentioned he had seen the failure before.  I contacted [REDACTED] email help line.  After several emails their representative, even though I suggested the fuel solenoid as the problem, told me I needed to re-build the carburetor.  I went online to order [REDACTED] parts for the engine and discovered that the fuel solenoid had been discontinued and was no longer available.  I again spoke to the mechanic and he said he thought it was strange a part like that on a 2 year old engine, was no longer available without a safety recall.  The mechanic ordered the new replacement fuel solenoid and I after the solenoid and drained the fuel from the crankcase, the engine runs fine.   That amount of fuel leaking through the hot exhaust and muffler is a dangerous situation.  It could easily resulted in a fire. [REDACTED] n knows of this problem because it has discontinued the previous fuel solenoid.   This is a dangerous safety issue and the engines should be recalled and repaired.
justification: Fuel leaking from the hot muffler posed a high risk of fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
At approximatly 3 pm, I turned on my Weber gas grill to preheat for 30 minutes.  After 30 minutes, I heard a crash and went outside to investigate and found my grill tipped over and on fire.  After calling the fire department, the grill exploded, sending a ball of flames up the side of my house, setting the house on fire.  There were two explosions that followed.

After the fire was put out, I inspected the grill, finding that the bottom of the body of the grill had melted, which caused the grill to tip over in the first instance.  I note that the grill was two years old and clean.  Also, the grease pan had been replaced less than 8 weeks ago and the grill had undergone light use during that period.

Based on the manufacturers specifications, the grill body was made of aluminum, which has a melting point of 1400 degrees.  I stongly suspect that the body is not, in fact, made of aluminum, but rather tin which has a melting point of 500 degree.  There is no other explanation that I can descern since is it clear that it was the melting of the body that caused the grill to collapase and later igntire the propane tank.
justification: The incident resulted in a house fire with potential for fatalities, and while the likelihood of such a severe event is not high, it is possible given the grill's apparent material flaw.

The consumer stated that she had an issue with leakage in the hose. The consumer contacted the manf. The consumer was offered a free replacement hose assembly under warranty. 

The consumer ran into the same issue again in May 2014. The consumer purchased a new hose assembly from Ducane for approximately $30. The consumer stated that the hose assembly failed within few months (started leaking).

The consumer contacted Ducane with the issue. The consumer was sent a free replacement hose assembly with some other additional parts that she purchased. They informed her that they will test the assembly before they send it out. The consumer received this hose assembly around 7/25/14. 

The consumer stated that she put the new parts on along with the new hose assembly. The consumer stated that she used it once. The consumer stated then she heard leakage and tested it with soap water. The consumer stated that this assembly failed as well (started leaking).

The consumer contacted the manf and asked for her money back on the hose assembly purchase. The consumer was informed that she would receive her refund. The consumer believes that this assembly is hazardous and informed the manf to look into the issue.

The consumer purchased a new hose assembly from [REDACTED], made by [REDACTED] (made in Canada). The consumer stated that she has not had any issues with this assembly. The consumer stated that this assembly is made slightly different from the previous ones she had by Ducane/[REDACTED].
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the recurring leakage issue with the hose assembly poses a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Trimmer initially leaked gas at tank fuel line connection point and soaked my from pant leg with gasoline. Tank and its included fuel lines were subsequently replace  and leak re-occurred after short period of use.
NOTE: I attempted to include pics and my received e mails from manfacture but could not!
justification: Gasoline leak occurred twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: "Xhose" expandable garden hose was being used by my husband while my daughter was nearby and the hose suddenly exploded with great pressure and not only soaked her but the pressure from the water also hurt her face and scared her.
justification: The hose exploding with high pressure caused injury to the daughter's face, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood of this occurring is possible, given the unexpected nature of the incident.

incident_description:
Our Catalina outdoor fireplace is on a level cement deck.
we has just a couple of fires in it last summer then stored it away for the winter.
this summer we put a few small pieces of wood in and as the fire got going
two of the glass panels literally exploded shooting glass four to five 
feet surrounding the fireplace.
justification: Glass panels exploding and shooting glass up to five feet indicates a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I have a Husqvarna 128LD string trimmer.  The gas tank leaks at the cap.  The cap has never sealed correctly.

I called the company to see what could be done e.g. send me a replacement gas cap.  They said that it was a warranty matter, not a safety matter.  

Because I bought this item about a year ago, it is surely out of warranty.  But it's a safety issue, not a warranty issue.
justification: Leaking gas poses a fire hazard, though no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: While using (normal use) the Master Forge L3218 I bought in 2013 at Lowe's it suddenly burst into flames. The main burner burner hose melted causing massive fire. Lowe's assembled the bbq at the store. No on was seriously hurt.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant fire but no serious injuries, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario with a 'possible' likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I spy plastic bird feeder refracted the sunlight and caught my yard/ house on fire.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while possible, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: Single shoulder harness included with Stihl FS 90 R-Z (and other models) brushcutter/trimmer can detach unexpectedly resulting in the release of the powered brush cutter.   The clasp is poorly designed such that the "tongue" can move from side to side, leading to a potentially catastrophic release of the machine from its harness while it is running.
justification: The poorly designed clasp can unexpectedly release the running machine, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
On 7/21/14 the callerÃÂs wife was using the unit. She was blowing grass off of the lawn mower for about 2-3 minutes when the impeller broke and blew a hole on the side of the leaf blower. The caller's wife injured her right hand. 

She was holding the unit with her left hand. After she heard a loud noise coming from the unit she attempted to turn the unit off with her right hand. Her thumb bruised up and has a blood blister under her thumb nail. 

On 7/22/14 the caller contacted Troy-Bilt and explained the incident. He was informed that his unit had no recalls. He was transferred to a different department to file a report. Caller stated that while he was filing the report and after he provided the model number he was advised that his unit was under recall. He was advised to call CPSC for information and assistance.

There is a recall on Troy-Bilt Electric Leaf Blowers (recall# 14-151) with model# TB180B, item number 41BA180G966 and serial numbers ranging from S1D111XK0001 through S1F152XK2008.
The callerÃÂs unit does not fall under this recall.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and given the recall information, similar incidents are likely to occur with the same model.

incident_description:
May 17th 2014 this caller was riding on his rear engine riding lawnmower, he stopped to allow a woman walking with her baby to pass by when the frame snapped causing the engine to dropped downward stretching the clutch, gas etc. throwing the unit into high gear.

The consumer states that when the frame snapped the rear engine riding mower took off like a rocket ship almost causing caller to run over a lady with her baby.
This unit has not been used more than twenty hours total.

The caller is reporting this incident to alert the public of the safety issue for anyone riding the product or walking in front of it.

Caller states that he has a back injury after an on the job accident and he does believe that this incident has worsened the injury.

He has contacted the manufacturer but has received no assistance
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the caller, and the high likelihood is supported by the fact that the mower had been used for less than 20 hours and malfunctioned unexpectedly.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he just started using the leaf blower and the unit started emitting smoke from the plug for the extension cord.  This incident melted the electrical cord where the prongs were located.  There was also smoke emitting from the blower.  

6/22/14 The retailer was contacted and he was informed to file a complaint with the agency.  He feels that this leaf blower is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: Smoke and melted electrical cord indicate a potential fire hazard, making another incident likely.

incident_description: I was using my Homelite leaf blower to clean off my side walk after mowing the lawn and it caught fire. It was burning inside the motor Fire and smoke was coming out of the case. I unpluged it right away.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (leaf blower catching fire) but no injuries, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is 'possible' as it's not rare but also not an everyday occurrence.

incident_description:
On 7/28/2014 while grilling on my kenmore gas grill I was shocked to find the whole grill engulfed in flames. As I got closer to turn the knobs to the off position I smelled a rubber burning. To my surprise it was the gas hose connected to the propane tank that continued to burn. After trying to get everything shut down with having the fear of the whole tank exploding I took  the  chance and shut down the propane tank. The flames from the hose finally stopped burning. The complete firebox was completely crumbled to expose the propane tank and hose. Firebox was completely dicenegrated.  

Sears still sells this fire hazard  numerous similar complaints online
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the numerous similar complaints.

incident_description: I have a John Deere 2305 riding sub-compact residential tractor.  I was mowing and had a 48" brush hog attached to the rear PTO (shaft).  All of a sudden the tractor turned off, brush hog kept spinning and the tractor rolled in reverse uncontrollably.  Luckily, I was on a relatively flat surface so the tractor came to rest but the blade on the brush hog kept spinning.  When everything eventually stopped, I disconnected the PTO and inspected the tractor.  Not knowing much about them, I took it to a local Deere dealer who stated that the shaft / transmission was a known problem in this model and that John Deere had a design flaw.  The only was to "fix" it was to replace the entire transmission / gears / shaft with a new product.  Why was this not recalled if it is a known issue with a new / different part number with a different design to repair the problem.  This is dangerous and Deere should repair ALL tractors that exist with this issue.  So far, I can see from my research and information from Deere that ~ 300 + tractors have had this issue.  I contacted John Deere and they refuse to listen.  Please help.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm due to the tractor rolling uncontrollably with a spinning blade.

incident_description: Fire department dispatched to a lawn mower fire inside the garage. Crews arrived to find the lawn mower outside of the structure in the driveway.  The fire appeared to be out as by-standers had standard water hose spraying on the mower.  The mower still had heat & a small flame from under the chassis.  Crews checked on the homeowner & by-standers for any medical issues, all denied.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (severity level 2). The occurrence likelihood is 'possible' (3) as lawn mower fires can happen but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
I purchased a Jenn-Air Built-In Gas Grill Model # 750-0142 LoweÃÂs SKU # 168935. As I understand it, this grill was manufactured by NexGrill and sold under the Jenn-Air brand name. 

After replacing the steel rod cooking grids on at least three occasions, it has become apparent that there is a serious manufacturing defect in this portion of the product. 

What has me very concerned is how they are manufactured. The grids are advertised as Stainless Steel. I am no expert, however, it appears that they are actually made of steel rods that are then ÃÂdippedÃÂ with a stainless steel coating. The end result is that after about 4-6 months of normal usage the outer stainless steel coating begins to separate and razor sharp pieces of steel flake off of the grids. This is bad enough, however, even more dangerous is the fact that those razor sharp pieces stick to the food you are cooking, causing an extremely dangerous hazard should someone ingest or swallow a piece of this steel flake. I have photos to illustrate the issue visually if you would like me to send them to you.
justification: The incident involves a serious manufacturing defect that poses a high likelihood of injury due to ingestion of sharp steel flakes.

incident_description:
Product: ECHO Gasoline powered backpack blower Model PB-265L S/N P0931 2039 347

After about 6 hours of use, fuel was found to be leaking over and around the fuel tank, some leaking down onto my shirt.  Investigation showed that the fuel return line from the priming bulb to the top of the fuel tank had pulled out of its rubber fitting.
justification: Fuel leak caused potential injury due to contact with shirt.

incident_description:
7/6/14 - Consumer went to use the smoker.  It was plugged in but not on. When the consumer touched the door handle he received a slight tingle and when he touched the rack inside the unit he received a huge shock. Consumer states he received no medical attention. 

Consumer has used the unit for 6 months and has had no prior incidents. 

Consumer contacted the manufacture an hour prior to calling the  CPSC Hotline.   The manufactureÃÂs rep. advised the consumer to mail the label on the unit with the cord back to them and said he would receive a replacement box. Consumer will keep the rack and parts inside his current unit to reuse in his new unit. Consumer filed a report with the firm - case #170784. 

The consumerÃÂs unit appears to be included Recall # 13-241 - Masterbuilt Manufacturing Recalls Electric Smokers due to Fire Hazard. The hazard in the recall is the wood chip tray can fail to slide securely into the smoker, causing the wood to combust and the smokerÃÂs cabinet door to blow open, posing a fire hazard.

The consumer stated that he has not had any such problems that are noted in the recall.
justification: Consumer experienced an injury (shock) due to a malfunction in the smoker, despite the unit being recalled for a fire hazard issue.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his mower has the same hazard as recall #13-187.

The consumer stated that the pulley was rubbing against the fuel tank. The consumer stated that there was a slice/cut in the fuel tank. The consumer stated that he noticed the issue when the gas leaked from the tank.

The consumer stated that when he saw the recall, he contacted the manf. They informed him that his mower is not included in recall. They provided no further assistance.

The consumer contacted the dealer and reported the issue on 06/09/14. The dealer provided a new fuel tank on 06/13/14. 

The consumer stated that replacing the fuel tank does not eliminate the issue causing the fire hazard. The consumer stated that the pulley would still continue to rub against the fuel tank leading to the hazard.
justification: Although no injury has been reported, the potential for fire hazard due to the pulley rubbing against the fuel tank is high, as evidenced by the gas leak.

incident_description:
On 5 July 2014 I purchased a Better Homes and Garden table top grill model GBT1452W/BH14-101-009-05 at Walmart in Bemidji MN. On July 11 2014 I was using the grill in Wisconsin Dells WI when the screw connect between the burner and gas regulator became detached causing the gas control valve, regulator and propane tank to fall away from the burner. Raw propane was released to the atmosphere. Looking at the screw attachment I could see only a very small amount of soldier had held the screw attachment to the burner.

I exchanged the broken grill for the same make and model at the Walmart in Wisconsin Dells. The unit was assembled as instructed. The screw attachment again separated from the burner causing the gas control, regulator and propane tank to separate from the burner. Raw propane was released to the atmosphere. Again, looking at the screw attachment. only a small amount of soldier was visible.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant release of raw propane, posing a high risk of fire or explosion.

incident_description:
The consumer turned the blower to the "on" position and there was a tremendous loud noise and smaller pieces of broken plastic flew from the blowerÃÂs vent.  He immediately turned the blower off.

The hard, clear, plastic fan blade is located in the bottom of the assembly that is held in the hand and it disintegrated in this instance.  Some of the pieces hit the consumer's clothing, but he did not sustain any injury.  The large pieces of the fan blade remained inside the blower's housing.

At a later time, the consumer disassembled the blower for further examination.  He saw that in the mounting assembly, the area where the fan blade screws onto the motor was damaged.  The collar that goes on to the threaded brass fitting, which secures the screw for the fan's blade failed.  The consumer is not exactly sure, but this is what appears to have happened after he disassembled it.

The consumer conducted research on-line and was looking to see if he could find a replacement fan blade, but he found that parts were not available. 

6/30/2014 & 7/1/2014:  The consumer called the manufacturer and was directed to their authorized service center, but that is when he confirmed that parts are no longer available.

There is a date code on the batteries for the latter part of 2006.  The consumer is not sure if he received it in 2007, 2008 or later.

The consumerÃÂs main concern is that the pieces could fly out at a high velocity and injure someone severely depending upon where it hit them.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a significant failure of the blower's fan blade, which could have resulted in severe injury if pieces had hit the consumer's face or eyes.

incident_description: My Lawn Boy gas powered push mower just developed a leak in the gas tank, posing a fire hazard. I have Model #10247, Serial #8911875. Many other Lawn-Boy mowers with the same serial number (10247) have been recalled for this reason. I was told by Lawn-Boy that because my particular serial # was not part of the recall, I will have to pay for any repair. I also see that others have complained of the same problem with the same model/year mower from Lawn-Boy, so obviously the recall should be extended to include older models of 10247. I want Lawn-Boy to pair for the repair of the gas tank.
justification: The gas leak poses a fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury.

incident_description: We just bought our coleman road trip grill. We Cooked on it and after went to remove the water tray and put my had down and brushed my had against the hole opening for the burner and sliced my finger open. I had to go to urgent care. I receive a Tetanus shot and four stitches in my finger.  The edge is very sharp it is like a razor blade. I think a finished edge should be put on there so you don't cut yourself.
justification: Injury occurred due to sharp edge of the grill's water tray, and the likelihood is high as it's a design flaw that could easily happen again.

incident_description:
On or about May 5, 2014 I was mowing my lawn and a piece broke off the lawnmower and went flying and the blade became loose but did remain attached to the mower. The piece that broke is called a blade adapter and connects the the blade to the shaft. I took the piece of the blade adapter that remained on the mower to an authorized Husqvarna dealer and they said it broke because of a manufacturing defect. They also said that Husqvarna was not making the blade adapter as strong as they use to. I reported this incident to Husqvarna but there has been no follow-up by them so I am now reporting it to you.

No one was injured in this incident but someone could be severely hurt if the piece that broke off and went flying hit them.
justification: While no one was injured this time, the potential for injury is high due to the flying debris, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: My  Ariens snowblower which is less than three years old leaked gas onto the garage floor.  I took it outsiide and started it to use up any remaining gasoline.  After a short time, the engine shut off.  I went into the house and a few minutes later, the snowblower burst into flames.  The fire department was called.  Luckily no one was injured, but  my $1700 snowblower is ruined.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Severity Level 2). The likelihood of this occurrence is 'Possible' (Likelihood 3) given the age of the snowblower and the sequence of events.

incident_description: The X Hose Pro garden hose is dangerous.  I purchased this via the company's website a month ago.  I purchased 2-25 foot sections of hose.  Since then I have used the expandable hose according to instructions.  As of today both hoses have burst with a powerful force.  The fabric on the outside splits and the heavy balloon inside expands and bursts within a matter of seconds.  The second hose that burst this morning propelled the rubber into my window almost breaking it.  Imagine that rubber had hit someone in the eye.  This is a dangerous product that is being advertised and sold all over the country.
justification: The hoses bursting with force and propelling rubber debris poses a high risk of injury.

incident_description: Hand held sprayer (Stihl SG 10) came apart at seam while pressurized drenching operator with fungicide.
justification: The sprayer malfunctioned under pressure, leading to an injury from the fungicide.

incident_description:
(05/24/2014) The consumer stated there is a cradle that hold the log in position. The consumer stated that he went to split a piece of wood. The cradle and the log fell on his leg . He lost his balance and fell on top of the top of the log splitter. He chipped his teeth and a piece of wood flew in his eye.

The consumer went to see the eye doctor two days ago. He went to see the dentist three ago.

He is making an appointment to see a chiropractor. 

Enclosed pictures of log splitter wood cradle deck of log splitter. Picture of wood cradle bent on sides. Picture deck of log splitter where all four bolts stepped off cannot see two bolts broke and part of bolt still in log splitter purchased Lowes Lake City. Sales associate was awful in knowledge of unit. He said unit was commercial?  I asked him if he had boot for unit after five minutes looking he said he could not find boot he stated to home and copy it off the internet. I asked him about  the recommended [REDACTED] tell us 2m 32 hydraulic fluid he showed me wrong fluid and said we do not carry recommended [REDACTED] fluid I asked him why? no response had problem with cradle 15 hours use when cradle would say it would go into hydraulic hose.
justification: Injury occurred due to malfunctioning equipment, with likelihood of recurrence high given the lack of proper maintenance and knowledge of the sales associate.

incident_description: My husband was cooking burgers on our Char Broil Commercial Series Grill (Model number 463268806) that was connected to our gas line. He made eight burgers without incident and then placed eight more on the grill. Suddenly, flames became very large and would not extinguish. The fire had a different smell and red flames. We had to quickly disconnect from the gas line and smother the flames with baking soda. After the fire was out, it was obvious that the metal at the base of the grill had caught fire.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, making it an incident with no injury (severity level 2). The likelihood is high (4) as the fire was sudden, intense, and difficult to extinguish.

incident_description:
Rented a Krendl Blower model [REDACTED] from Menard's. Upon plugging it in, the 3way toggle switch blew flames when the switch was thrown.

Received another Krendl Blower model [REDACTED]. Was operating the unit for approximately 2 hours,when the house breaker was blown and the auger unit stopped working. Turned off the switches on the unit. Reset the breaker in the house. Upon turning the unit back on, flames shot out of the 3 way switch.

I contacted Krendl  manufacture and notified them of the issue. They started that it must have been abused and that is why the switch failed.
justification: The incident occurred twice with the same model, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Mantis tiller/cultivator leaks fuel.
justification: Fuel leak from Mantis tiller/cultivator could lead to property damage or fire, but unlikely to cause injury.

incident_description: bought a tornado tools cordless string trimmer....  assembled according to user manual...  the screws holding the guard to motor housing do NOT screw into anything...  first use guard flew off and was thrown by the string...  without guard secured to housing this is an unsafe product...
justification: The guard flying off during first use poses a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she experienced similar problems of Release #12-198 with her lantern.  Hazard: An electrical short circuit can occur in the lanterns' internal wiring, posing a risk of fire, burn and electric shock to consumers.  The lantern caught fire while in use.  She powered off the switch and the fire dissipated.  

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.  The product is part of the recall.

Consumer needed to add this incident to the database.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a high likelihood (4) as it's a recurring issue with the recalled product.

incident_description: The flashlight exploded on my 3 year old daughter as she held it watching cartoons. It burned her hand, arm, chest, face, and eyes. It made a huge laceration in her leg which required surgery. She was admitted to Brenner's children's hospital where she underwent multiple tests and procedures. The Light part of the flashlight went into her leg and back out and the compass "lid" part is lodged into my ceiling about 10 ft from where she was sitting when it exploded. If the light had been pointed at a different angle this could have been a tragedy. Something more needs to be done to get the word out on this recall, we were not aware of this recall until after all of this happened.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries, including burns and a laceration requiring surgery, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood is high given the widespread use of flashlights and the lack of awareness about the recall.

incident_description: I purchased two Bunny K Expandable Garden Hoses (50' each) online at Amazon.com (the seller was wachegenas storefront).  While I was watering my lawn and grandson's swing set a few weeks ago, the hose developed a balloon where the hose and nozzle connect and exploded within seconds. I had been holding the hose low and slightly away from my body because I had to move the swing, when, just by chance, I glanced down and to my lower right, I saw this balloon growing down the hose, within seconds of my noticing this balloon the hose exploded where the nozzle attaches to the hose and pieces of the hose hit my lower leg with such intensity that it immediately caused a large terrible bruise, that became swollen and black and blue instantaneously.  If my grandson, my 96 year old father or my two puppies had been nearby when this hose exploded, I have no doubt, the injuries would have been deadly.  I was not able to return these hoses because the companies return policy had expired; however, I would never use another expandable hose due to my recent experience and my fear of the harm this hose can produce. I have the hose, the pieces of rubber that exploded off the hose and hit my leg and the nozzle that I also purchased as recommended by the web site.
justification: The hose's sudden explosion and the force of the debris caused a significant injury, and the presence of others nearby could have led to severe harm.

incident_description: while using the packtite, we smelled something hot, I ran upstairs and found that it had overheated and caused the vinyl tiles on the bathroom floor to discolor and lift.  We have not used this product since because we feared it would cause a fire.  It was over $350 to protect us since we travel, but not worth losing our home over.
justification: The product overheated and caused damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Toro Power Clear 180 Snowthrower Model #38282 S/N 310024442, repaired 4-21-2011 for recall issued 7-14-2010 CPSC #10-299. Has hardly been used since the repair (was not used at all last year)
Snowthrower is again leaking raw gas from the carburetor and creates a huge fire hazard, this appears to be a common problem even with products repaired under the first recall
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the snowthrower's gas leak poses a significant fire hazard, making it an incident with potential for injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Toro 20383 in 2013.  After one season of normal residential use, the bolts holding the side discharge port cover came loose and fell out.  This caused the side discharge port cover to fall off, exposing the  spinning lawn mower blade.  It would be extremely easy for someone to injure their fingers, as there is a large open port on the side of the mower (approximately 5"x6").

A check of the parts list shows that there a no lock nuts (actually no nuts of any kind) holding the bolts in place.  They are just screwed into a metal bar and can easily come loose.

There a no directions in the owners manual instructing the user to periodically check the tightness of the the bolts
justification: The incident description details a real-world scenario where the bolts holding the side discharge port cover came loose, exposing the spinning lawn mower blade, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: I've owned this Weber Spirit Grill for about 5 years. Always kept it out of the weather and in good condition. A couple days ago we had just started grilling and got the grill up to temp and had just but burgers on it. We went to turn the burgers down and notice the gas flow control knobs were melted flat to the control panel. We took a look underneath and the valves under the knobs just above the propane tank were spewing in flames! the fire was right at the main propane supply hose to. Another minute or so and this could have been a lot bigger incident if we hadnt went to turn the temp down when we did because when the supply line burned through it would have taken the whole tank with it with my niece standing right next to it!! I looked it up and the same exact thing is happening to lots of these same grills. Once I saw that it was not a matter of seeking replacement parts to fix this grill that should have had another 5 years of life left at least. Me and my families safety is not worth it. I'll just buy a different brand.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to a design flaw in the grill, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: Used wood chipper for about 5 minutes it smoked then burst into flames
justification: The incident involved a machine malfunction (smoking then bursting into flames) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Honda Lawnmower, Model HRR2165VKA serial number MZCG-7811329
I had my Honda on the bench for service, I am an service tech.  I had to replace part number 76147-VG4-000 (cover roto stop) due to the fact that it had failed in many locations.  This is a circular metal part which is just below the engine but located on the under side of the cutting deck.  When replacing this part which was ordered from Honda and is an original part, I found that the actual cutting deck, where 4 bolts hold the motor to the frame had structural failures in all four mounting locations.  I found structural cracks and completely missing metal pieces of the cutting deck. This would have never been found unless the motor was pulled from the deck and the deck inspected.  As this structural failure hides very well and is difficult for a normal non technical person to identify.  A complete failure might cause a running engine with a spinning blade to completely  break free from the mower cutting deck and cause serious injury or death and or property damage.
justification: Structural failures in the cutting deck could cause the engine and blade to break free, leading to potential injury.

incident_description:
We ordered  Kay Home Products Hibachi Grill Model 30052.  Upon first use, the wooden handle for the grid-iron came loose because the metal tang/haft is way t too short.  Because the item was only warm at the time, no injury occurred; however, such an ill fitting handle is a burn hazard.  The tang/haft needs to be much longer to ensure proper seating and retention.

The 3rd time we used the hibachi, we bbq'd chicken, which took longer than the steak, and hamburgers we did the first two times.  I went indoors to get utensils and a pot holder.  I returned only moments later to discover that the shortness of the handle placed it too near a chicken-fat flaring charcoal.  The flimsy handle was badly  charred after only a very short period of time.  Again, this is a fire and burn hazard.  

Lastly, the leg brackets are so short, placing this hibachi on any item other than one made completely out of non-combustibles is likely to cause a fire or collapse of the stand on which it is placed.
justification: The ill-fitting handle and short leg brackets pose a recurring burn and fire hazard, as demonstrated by the charring incident.

incident_description:
I have been noticing a lot of waandering in the steering wheel.  This has been happening quite often.  But on June 16, 2014 and on June 21, 2014 while mowing the lawn and other times as well  this year I have seen the issue get a lot worse.  A couple of times I have pulled the tractor into the garage and almost hit the garage wall and 1 time I did run into the back of my SUV not being able to turn the whell properly.  
Luckily, I was not hurt, but if the steering on these tractors has a design flaw that will cause many people to experience steering failure, people could be hurt badly.

There is quite a bit of information at:
http://www.ssbtractor.com/wwwboard/view_all.cgi?bd=kubota&msg=8684

There needs to be a recall of all Kubota tractors with this faulty steering setup, and a safety replacement for all tractors experiencing the problem, with a NEW, properly engineered steering cylinder.
justification: While no injuries have been reported yet, the increasing frequency and severity of incidents, including near-misses and property damage, indicate a high likelihood of future injuries.

incident_description:
Re: Troy-Bilt Pony 42" riding mower  Mod No: 13WM77KS011

Purchased new at Lowe's Champaign, Il. on 05/07/2014

Safety Concern:

The 1.3 gal fuel container is a medium gauge polypropylene tank that sits exposed on a metal platform to the rear and directly above the engine. Tank is directly to the front of the driver.

Tank is secured to platform by just one medium size and strength nylon zip-tie. Tank wobbles when shaken by hand and more so when mower is driven. The nylon strap will be prone to deterioration and breaking from age, heat from the engine, and the constant flexing.

If the cap on the tank was to loosen, the fumes could easily ignite and ignite the fuel in the container. If the tank was to rupture or the nylon strap breaks, the tank will fall onto the engine.  If the tank is nearly full and ignites and/or explodes, the driver or anyone near will be immediately engulfed in gasoline and flames before they could react and safely escape.

I consider the fuel container and the location and method it is secured to be a hazard and a grave incident waiting to occur. I am also surprised that the material used and method and location secured passed ANY safety inspections.
justification: The exposed fuel tank secured by a single zip-tie poses a high risk of rupture or ignition, which could lead to severe burns or death.

Additionally, the screw was not the only failure here, as the pop button used to guide and keep attachments from rotating in powerhead shaft coupling while equipment is in operation also failed to retain attachment/stop attachment rotation, though I am certain this is if only a secondary safety assistance device. The head of polesaw attachment is undeniably similar in design, and functionality, and relative use, and relative danger, as to a chainsaw.
If the same would have happened with the high torque tiller head from the same product line, (another interchangeable attachment i own as well for this power head unit), I could almost certainly be missing a foot, or leg, or worse, as the torque generated by the transmission is immense in comparison. What makes this situation worse is that the Home Depot, where this was purchased, does not offer or carry a replacement part in store or online, nor were either of the 2 Home Depot stores I visited willing to even offer a replacement item, even though in one store a like/type would have been available from display stock (im looking for a 3 inch screw, not the whole piece of equipment and i explained such clearly and with sample in hand). The Home Depot is claiming that since the powerhead and its attachments were purchased beyond 30 days (I purchased these as well as 3 other attachments approximately a year ago, all are still operable) that the entire unit assembly with an odd, oversize design weighing approximately 15 pounds, would need to be mailed out for repair at a potential additional cost. What bothers me most here is that this is a craftsmanship/workmanship/materials issue and especially in the case of a safety/related item, should have no associated cost whatsoever, to with respect to modification or abuse. 
MY REQUEST: Require same/similar to MILSPEC materials standards and/or to require use of spring steel or other similar material with the same/similar strength characteristics to be utilized in the future manufacture of all like/type equipment, as there should never be a materials failure of a safety item manufactured for use on a power tool.

incident_description:
The product in question is a gasoline powered weed trimmer (power head).

I was preparing to use the unit for the first time this spring. It had been purged of fuel before storage in the fall.
I poured fuel into the tank and it immediately dribbled out rapidly. The leak was very conspicuous so I did not attempt to operate the unit. No injury occurred.

I am concerned that a less obvious leak would create a high risk of serious burn injury to an operator.

When in use, the operator wears a supporting strap across his torso, over the left shoulder while the power head is held at his right side. Gasoline dripping from the unit could easily fall on the operators clothing. If an operator needed to separate himself from a burning unit he would have to first lift the strap over his head and toss the unit before dealing with any burning clothing. I would not want to be in that situation!

After inspecting the unit to find the source of the leak I am concerned that this failure will be very common.

Two small plastic gas line tubes enter the gas tank through a hole in the tank wall. An elastomer (rubber?) grommet fills the hole in the tank, sealing to the gas line tubing and to the wall of the tank. The seal is effected by compression of the grommet into the hole in the wall of the tank and by compression of the gas line tubes where they penetrate the grommet.
Two failures occurred:
1.	The gas line tubing compression set (shrank) where it meets the grommet. The lines were loose in the grommet.
2.	The grommet shrank so that it is no longer compressed when seated in its hole in the tank wall.

Conversations with the nearest authorized service shop suggest that it is not a novel failure and that the manufacturer associates the failure with the use of alcohol blended gas. The operatorÃÂs manual specifically allows the use of automotive 10% alcohol fuel. ThatÃÂs what I have used.

 I have used the unit in accordance with manufacturerÃÂs instructions. This failure occurred two years after the unit was placed in service.

I think the failure I have observed will be common. It presents a significant risk of serious burn injury to the operator. It is a design defect (poor choice of materials for fuel system).
justification: Potential for serious burn injury due to fuel leaks, as demonstrated by the incident and confirmed by service shop conversations.

incident_description:
My Sears Craftsman Riding Lawn Tractor LTX1000, model # 917.272420, part # 184900  purchased in 2001 new from Sears and owned by me this entire time developed a leak in the gas tank.  The tank is plastic and it developed four small cracks at the corners of the tank just above  the mid line where the two sections are joined together.  The cracks appear to be caused by the stress of vibrations coming through the frame the tank attaches to.

As a result of the cracks, gasoline would slowly leak from the tank.  I discovered this because the mower was stored in a section of basement beneath my bedroom.  I went to bed one night smelling gasoline fumes.  I checked the mower the next day, but could not see any evidence of direct leakage (the cracks are partially hidden by the chassis and dirt that attached to the leaked gas).  When the problem continued after several mowings and refillings of the tank, I measured the tank level after filling it, then again when I mowed a week later - I could then see the level in the tank had dropped about an inch.  An internet search turned up other consumers with similar tank problems.  I removed the tank, cleaned it, and the cracks were immediately apparent.

I consider this to be a very serious issue because my mower (and other persons') are stowed in basements and garages.  Those areas often have hot water tanks.  If the gas leak created enough vapors, they could be ignited by the burner on the hot water tank.  In addition, if the crack opened rapidly while the mower was being operated, gasoline could leak around the engine and catch fire, causing serious harm to the operator.  If this was a car's gas tank leaking, I am sure regulatory agencies would be all over it.  There is no difference.  A gasoline leak is a gasoline leak.

I know parts wear out, but ones that are crucial to safety must either carry a warning to inspect them for failure or be recalled and replaced.  Inspecting a mower's gas tank is not something most people would even think about doing.  I certainly didn't.  My previous Sear riding mower lasted 25 years and its tank never leaked.

I contacted Sears for a replacement part and notified them of the situation.  They said they would take it seriously and gave me free shipping and 10% off a new tank.  Personally, I think they should issue a recall.  I have their email replies to my emails if you want them.

There is YouTube video posted by me showing the tank problem.  It is located at  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8dPxstHd-RI
justification: Potential for fire due to gasoline leak, posing risk to property and life, despite no immediate injuries reported.

incident_description:
My wife and I purchased and moved into our home in March 2012. The house was built in 2008/09 and we purchased it from the first owner. We had an independent home inspection done prior to moving in and everything checked out. A few months after moving in, we noticed that the majority of the composite deck boards were wavy/warped and bowed. I was able to track down who I thought was the original manufacturer through all of the build specs for the house. I did a quick Google search on the manufacturer - Louisiana Pacific "LP", and the first thing that came up on the search page was for a recall on my specific decking - for the exact same symptoms that I was experiencing (warping/bowing). I contacted "LP"'s claim line and they sent me a claim form. I filled it out in its entirety, and sent it back to them - along with a few pictures that they had requested. A few weeks later, I received a letter back from "LP" stating that "By the time my decking was manufactured, they were sold out to another company - "Fiber Composite" or "Fiberon". My home was built during a "transitional period" where it could have been either company the manufactured it. There is a special notch in the board that indicates that it was in fact manufactured by "Fiber Composite" or "Fiberon". As a consumer, I found it hard to believe that two different manufacturers would have the same warping issues with their decking. I called and spoke to someone at the claims center at "LP".. who stated that he had received numerous phone calls, claim forms and emails regarding defective decking manufactured by "Fiber Composite" or "Fiberon". The theory was that when "Fiber Composite" or "Fiberon" purchased the company from "LP", there was no recall, nor was there any indication of anything wrong with the way that the decking was being manufactured or materials used. They continued on with the same materials and manufacturing process as "LP" did. When they realized that there was an issue, they modified there product, but there was still some composite decking that was produced by "Fiber Composite" of "Fiberon" that was defective. 
When I contacted "Fiberon" to initiate a claim, they indicated to me that because I am not the original owner, nor do I have proof of purchase, that this would not be covered. That is absolutely ridiculous! This decking should have been recalled , just as the "LP" decking was. There is no logical reason why composite decking should be wavy and warped after 5 years. This is unsafe and unacceptable, regardless if you are the first owner or not. My next stop will be to contact the bbb, the attorney generals office and my attorney to inquire about starting a class action. I honestly don't have time to deal with this, but in this case.. I will make time. This is an unfair and unethical business practice and Fiberon needs to take full responsibility for it.
justification: The warping of the deck boards poses a tripping hazard, potentially leading to injuries.

My town home, built in 2009, has a sewer collection tank for sewage to be pumped up hill to the city sewer. The sump pump is made by Zoeller Pump Company (Model 270) in Kentucky and the pump had the date of May 2009 for installation. On March 31, 2014, the electrical part of the pump burned out and caused an explosion that blew the cover off the sewage collection tank. Not only was I unable to use the water or toilets in my house, it made an unsafe situation as the tank was exposed. The wires that go into the pump were exposed and frayed, the motor completely black and burned out. The cost for replacement, including plumber's labor was nearly $2,000.  Insurance does not cover this and the developer is long gone. 
A search of manufacturer's recall found Zoeller did indeed have sump pumps that had been recalled. When I called the manufacture to ask about it, the salesman was immediately defensive, evasive and quite rude. Instead of asking for the model number and looking up the recall, he argued and claimed it was not intended for sewage use (when it is called a "submersible sewage pump" on the spec sheet). Unfortunately, my plumber had to drive out 50 miles to find a replacement and used the same manufacturer. I would advise against using products from this company, as even though the model I own was not the one recalled, it is suspect. And more importantly, the customer service is negligible to abusive.
justification: Incident caused inconvenience and potential safety hazard, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Milliard 20" x 48" Seedling Heating Mat to warm the soil for my garden seeds and enhance germination.  After using the mat for several days, I noticed that the heating elements had burnt several holes in the insulation and had scorched the underlying shelf which fortunately was flame-resistant.

I thought this might be an isolated instance, but noticed today a product review in Amazon.com for the identical problem in a Milliard 20" x 20" mat. [http://www.amazon.com/Milliard-Durable-Waterproof-Seedling-Heat/product-reviews/B00CRJ10FQ/ref=dp_top_cm_cr_acr_txt?showViewpoints=1]

This seems to be a systemic issue with Milliard heating mats and could be a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
The flexible X-hose failed and exploded, tearing thru the inner and outer jacket.  My wife was watering the garden and was not injured.  However, if she were closer to the point of failure, it could have resulted in minor injuries.  The 50' X-Hose Pro was only 1 month old and not abused or altered from original manufacturer.  When the shut off valve was turned off, the hose swelled at a certain point and exploded.  The shut off valve is included and part of the product (not removable.)

Note:  I have had two other 25' X-Hoses that failed in the inner lining, but not exploded like the 50'.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the hose explosion posed a potential risk of minor injuries if the person was closer to the point of failure.

I purchased a Briggs and Stratton snow blower from Home Depot in 2012, it sat unused until yesterday (12/8/2013) when I proceeded to fill it with gasoline to remove snow from my driveway.  Which at the time I noticed a steady stream of fuel pouring from the plastic cover covering the carburetor, I removed the cover and could see the fuel dripping in a steady stream from the carburetor itself. Sometime during January 2012 I noticed the smell of gasoline in my garage. Over several days I isolated the source to be my Model L111 John Deere Lawn Tractor. Further investigation led to the determination that the plastic gas tank was leaking fuel. Approx 260 hours on the tractor.
This particular machine ( GXL111A051973 ) was purchased from The Home Depot on 7/10/2005.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wife stretched the hose out as instructed.

The consumer stated that his wife turned the water on and the hose blew into pieces. The consumer stated that the hose blew up in the middle. The consumer stated that the area where the hose blew up is shredded.

incident_description: Was using a Chicago 14" electric can saw - model 67255 - serial number - 369951233 - purchased from Harbor Freight in Green Bay, Wisconsin in February of 2013 to cut slightly oversized firewood into a size which would fit into my fireplace insert.  When I released the safety switch and trigger switch to shut the saw off it failed to shutdown.  The electrical connection next to the handle covers the connection and makes it extremely difficult to disconnect power.  It was 0 degrees out and the area where I was standing was surrounded by ice.  This prevented me from moving to a safe location and nearly impossible to remove the heavy glove from my left hand to disconnect the saw while holding the running saw safely in my right hand.  I contacted Tech support at Harbor Freight and was told to have the saw repaired and that they no longer carried replacement switches (saw is one year old and the model is currently on sale in their most recent flyer).  I received no indication that they are considering this to be a safety issue and that they will be taking follow-up action..
justification: Injury likely due to difficulty in disconnecting power in emergency situation.

incident_description: I purchased a outdoor patio heater at ACE hardware in Daleville, PA.  After bringing it home and assembling it per the instructions we began to use it.  Within a week we started having issues with the ignitor not working properly.  It was inconsistent as I would have to keep pressing it sometimes without lighting or wait them try again.  I was concerning with the accumulation of propane until it lit.  The patio heater has a tray for setting drinks on it while standing beneath it and we used it as such.  After a short time we observed metal pieces dropping on us and the tray.  Upon further inspection of the flame area I observed the mesh around the flame was melting and dropping pieces down on us, some of which were hot or could have dropped into our drinks.  I contacted AZ Patio Heaters http://www.azpatioheaters.com and spoke with someone named [REDACTED] there.  I explained the issue and forwarded pictures to review.  In the meantime, we observed that where the screen was missing a flame was protruding out the safety cover and burning the upper heat reflector cover, which could harm a rather tall person or someone standing on a stool.  I contacted AZ patio again and was told by [REDACTED] to remove the screen.  I was not comfortable rigging it because it still did not address the ignitor issue or the flame shooting out the side.  I contacted him a few more times with no response, so I called this morning and spoke to a management person.  He told me they were aware for a while of the issue (did they contact you?) and were telling consumers to remove the screen.  What effect that will have on windy days?  Will the flame shoot out the side and burn the flame reflector like mine?  Do you want inexperienced consumers trying to fix this item?  Next, he told me the he thought the flame was caused by the regulator, but could it be that it is from the missing screen that burned off?  Unknown.  Why was this not reported as a safety issue to you if they knew it was a problem for a while with hot metal pieces falling on people or possibly ending up in drinks and consuming?  I will be contacting consumer reports as well.
justification: Metal pieces falling from the heater pose a high risk of injury, as evidenced by the consumer's experience.

incident_description:
My Toro Power Clear 210R snow blower (Model 38587) has been leaking gasoline onto my garage floor,
repeatedly over the last month or so. I first noticed that it had a serious leak in January. It lost perhaps
1/3 tank of its gasoline/oil mix over a period of a couple weeks (or less, I cannot be sure) onto the
garage floor. There was a water puddle there the entire time from ice melt off my two cars that made it
hard to notice any gasoline residue though, of course, I smelled it. As soon as I realized that there was a
significant leak, I took the unit to the dealer where I had bought it. He recognized the problem
immediately, having seen this issue with other Toro units. (I since learned that Toro had a CPSCmandated
recall of a similar model in 2011. Online one finds that other Toro models have generated
essentially identical leak complaints as well.) The problem here was a sticking needle valve in the
carburetor; this allows gasoline to flow from the fuel tank to the carburetor inlet where it overflows and
runs onto the floor. They performed the [REDACTED]-recommended repair to the carburetor and then kept the
snow blower for a week to see that the leak had indeed stopped. After a few uses over the last few
weeks I again noticed a gasoline odor and confirmed that the unit was again leaking. I again took it to
the dealer (yesterday) and they cleaned the carburetor float and needle valve; this seemed to stop the
leak. However, I checked it overnight only to find that it is still leaking.

I have 30 years professional experience with fire safety issues and also have worked with CPSC
personnel on some fire issues. I recognize this problem as an imminent fire safety (or even explosion)
hazard when the unit is stored in an enclosed space, especially as in my case, an attached garage. I have
removed my snow blower from my garage and stored it outside. Also I have reported the problem to
Toro and I am awaiting their response
justification: Although no injuries have occurred, the repeated gasoline leaks pose a significant fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the blower vacuum has a failure, while using it approximately 30 seconds, her spouse held in it his hand and it began taking in his garment, then the plastic crate at the bottom of the unit broke which caused it to take in even more of the garment.  He then noticed that the electrical cord started to melt.  It was unplugged to prevent further damages.

The product is not part of a recall.
justification: Injury occurred when the blower vacuum malfunctioned and pulled in the user's garment, posing a high likelihood of recurrence given the previous incident.

incident_description:

product called metal landscape edging (usually a green color, 8' segments) regarding safety? The product is sold at
Lowe's and Home Depot and other landscaping companies. It is used by home owners and landscapers. The product is a
potential safety hazard with reported injuries to people and animals. Please refer to a medical paper "Metal lawn edging
and garden edging: The hidden knife?" by [REDACTED], MD and [REDACTED], MD in Pediatric Medical Care Vol. 17, No. 1, 2001.
The metal edging can disengage at its connections, typically has a projection higher than grade level, has sharp edges
and corners, has a high potential as a trip point in residential and commercial settings, especially at entrance walkways,
has caused serious injuries. I can provide a copy of the referenced medical paper if requested. Other information may be
available in the open literature. The desired outcome of your review of this product: Designated as a safety hazard,
