justification: The product has caused serious injuries as reported in a medical paper, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I have A Masterbuilt meat smoker it caught fire on 11/25/2012 I took pictures and sent them to Masterbuilt the called me to ask what happend when I returned the call I got no answer.11/20/2013 I emailed them back with pictures. I have found out 11000 smokers were recalled. My smoker caused damage to my porch and was very hard to put the fire out. I almost lost my life putting out the fire.

incident_description:
On November 30, ten minutes into mowing my yard, my John Deere D130 lawn tractor exploded.  The machine was nearly new (3 hours of use) and I was using as intended when suddenly I heard a "pop" sound and about 10 seconds later noticed flames shooting out from under the "hood", hearly burning my foot.  I ran from the machine and called the fire department who had to visit to extinguish the incenerated machine and a surrounding brush fire.  

Repeated calls both by myself and my attorney to Deere have met with the answer that I have to prove that I didn't deliberately start the fire in order to force a remedy.  No concern as to my welfare was expressed.  I file this in order to initiate an investigation into an obviously faulty product that could cause injury or death to a less agile individual.
justification: Injury occurred due to a sudden explosion of the lawn tractor, and the likelihood of such an event is high given the new condition of the machine and its intended use.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his spouse found acid leaking from the shear and he returned  it to the store (9/2013), he received a replacement and while he was charging it for 24 hours the same incident occurred.  The acid that had leaked was on his garage shelf and on the floor.

He contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that they were not aware of any incident with the product and would not offer any assistance.  He has since returned the product to the retailer.

Caller feels that this is a safety hazard and can cause harm to consumers.

The product is not affected by a recall.
justification: Acid leakage from the product occurred twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and posing a potential injury risk.

incident_description:
We bought a NEW Gas Grill and were using it for the FIRST time (we have had other grills for years.)
The grill spewed a LARGE flame, caught the tank on fire and melted the coupler around the tank.
We had to let the tank empty itself.

It has been looked at by engineers from the Tank company, Uhaul where the tank was inspected THE DAY OF THE INCIDENT and Brinkman, the manufacturer of the grill.

Brinkman has blamed the tank from day one, despite it passing inspection on two occasions.

They refuse to pay to reside our home, as the fire damaged it (It is a new home, just bought in May 2013)

They admitted the tank was neither overfilled, nor out of recertification - yet blame them and deny our claim without an explanation as to WHY it should be the tank's fault.

During inspection, by Brinkaman's OWN engineer, the regulator on the grill caught fire, and spewed flames.

Despite this obvious flaw, they refuse to acknowledge it and said the regulator on the grill (Made in China) is not significant.

THis is on tape, and was witnessed by myself, an engineer from Uhaul, and Brinkan's rep.

They refuse to give me the evidence nor any reports.

Brinkaman had a similar issue with other regulators and had to recall them for the same reason.

There is NO DOUBT from myself and Uhaul's engineers that this caught my home and the grill on fire, and it is a danger.

Please help us get this resolved, and these grills off the market!
justification: The grill caused a significant fire, damaging the home, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she saw this product advertised on tv. She is concerned for the safety of children because her father became Ill from the bacteria from the bird dropping. The consumer stated that he had a bird feeder on his window ledge on the outside of his home.

Who manufactures this product?  Have they taken Illness from Bacteria in bird droppings into account for safety? Again I request you to stop sell of this bird house and feeder for up close use for health safety of the young and elderly.  One Life is too many to lose to a silent killer!!!

I am a very concerned person who lived a night of anguish from a personal use of such an item. incident_description: On 10-03-11 I was in my backyard pulling weeds & trimming my rose bushes - went to move my cart 4 feet with the [lid] down - next thing I remember (I was knocked out) had to be hospitalized - severed muscle & skin over eye - eye brow & onto the temple area - plastic surgeon saved my eye & was able to after tune set my muscle to work - left with dry eye as my lid won't close properly.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his grill on January 10th, 2013, brought it home, put it together then he and a friend began grilling but after approximately ten minutes his friend who was cooking noticed that grease from the meat was dripping into the tray.
He also noticed that the slope in the middle of the drip tray is not manufactured to allow the drippings to drain quickly enough to prevent the accumulation of the flammable grease placing too closely to the burner assemblies and flames from the grill itself.
Ultimately the grease caught fire and in seconds it went from one small place to engulf the entire bottom of the grill.
All the burners were on low and the lid was on but the entire grill was in flames as high as twelve inches high.
His friend tried to reach the lid to open it and allow the flames to extinguish, however he was burned on his hands and face.
His hair was burned off and his skin looked like he had a sunburn but he did not go to the hospital or require medical attention other than the cream he placed on the areas himself.  His skin did heal well.

The caller brougt the new grill home and began cooking however the incident repeated exactly as the first incident had happened.
He had this time used only one burner, kept the lid open and a fire extinguisher beside him.
justification: Injury occurred due to grease fire, and likelihood is high as it happened twice with the same model grill.

The owners manual recommends outdoor air for combustion but to gain this outside air it would require that you drill an outside hole. THIS WAS DONE.

incident_description:
This fire pit has an extremely sharp edge to the bowl.  Simply running your finger along the edge can cause injury.   I accidentally walked into this fire pit, resulting in an ambulance ride to the hospital,10 stitches to one leg and 30 stitches to the other leg.  

Report Update: 11/27/2013
The pit had been put out that day, so I was unaccustomed to it being there and therefore not taking caution as to the path I was taking across the yard. As I was walking my dog accross the large yard, I kept glancing over my shoulder to watch her, which probably steered me off course a bit and into the path of the fire pit. It was about 9:00pm, but the pit was slightly illuminated from porch lights.
I WALKED into the firepit, where my left shin caught the edge. This was the horizontal wound to my left leg, requiring 10 stitches. When my left leg hit the edge, it caused me to fall forward over and onto the pit where my right leg came down on the edge. This caused the vertical wound, requiring 30 stitches. The wound to the right leg was very severe, going all the way down to the bone and muscle. As a result, I have some nerve damage and numbness.

Purchased this Toro 4221 QE snowblower 12/12/09. I had the recall repair work done on this Toro snowblower, 421 QE Power Clear 2/1/2011)Leaking gas). Carb repair work was needed again 1/14/2012 (Leaking gas).

This is the second time in 3 years this has happened. Toro should be made to recall these dangerous machines or give consumers rebates to purchaser new machines that DO NOT LEAK GAS ALL OVER GARAGE FLOORS ALL OVER THE USA.

incident_description:
Caller was using his shredder/grinder on November 30th, 2013 shredding his leaves from his 
200 feet wide x 75 feet deep yard.

Shredder was beside compost pile

Debris from leaf blower fell onto the muffler and then fell to the ground catching his [REDACTED] grass lawn on fire and the shredder/grinder on fire.

Caller's hand was burned while he was trying to put the fire out by beating it with the rake and his hands but treated himself by running cold water over the burning area.

Consumer contacted the manufacturer December 2nd, 2013, left message but has not received a response from them.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
Enclosed is the completed form you sent me. It would have been better if you had just sent me a blank
Word Document that I could have filled out rather than the enclosed partially filled out one that has the
numbers correct but no description of the actual problem I was reporting. The problem with this piece
of equipment in a nutshell is that by design, the broken up particles of leaves blow out both discharges
(one is the intended on and the other is designed for branch grinding). When this occurs airborne
particles fly all over the place and land on the muffler that is a basically rectangular box. The muffler has
a guard that keeps someone from getting terribly burned, but its open structure allows the airborne
leaves to float down and lay on its top. As my photo show, the leaves that are resting on the muffler are
in fact smoldering. It was smoldering leaves that blew off the muffler and landed on the lawn that
caused my lawn to catch on fire and my chipper grinder's plastic feed chute to catch on fire. I am not an
engineer but it would seem to me a simple fix on the engine would be a round muffler or an inverted "v"
type of guard so that nothing could rest on it. I don't think there is any simpler, cost effective fix that
Sears/Craftsman could make.

I would appreciate it if you would please let me know whether I should contact Sears again or whether I
should try something like hiring a lawyer in order to get my piece of equipment fixed.
Thank you for your assistance in this matter. My case was lucky because I was "on the spot" within a
minute of the fire starting, but if I had been in the front of my house raking leaves my entire backyard
could have been on fire and the there would have been a burnt down garage and fences as I would have
had to wait for the fire department to respond to a call. As it was, I was able to put the fires out with my
hands and the rack (plus buckets of water).
justification: Injury occurred when the caller burned his hand while trying to extinguish the fire, and the likelihood is high as the fire started due to a design flaw in the shredder.

incident_description:

Around 10:30pm, she heard the sound of glass breaking.  About one minute later she heard glass breaking again and went downstairs.  She saw flames emitting from the pellet stove.  It was still running.   She threw a pitcher of water on the fire then unplugged the unit.  

She evacuated her family.  She went back into the house to get her daughter's pet bunny.  She saw that the window sill was on fire.  She threw another pitcher of water at the window.  911 was called and emergency crews responded to the scene.

The two smoke alarms in the house did not sound because the batteries were dead.

The retail store was contacted and they reported that they no longer sell this product becasue there have been issues with it.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the history of issues with the product.

justification: While the consumer's interpretation could lead to an incident, the manual's instructions are likely misinterpreted, making an explosion or fire unlikely.

incident_description:
We bought a gas grill, Model Char-Broil Classic C-59G4-463252113, in June 2013. We used it three times.  On Dec. 5, 2013, we tried to use the barbecue (the fourth time.)  While cooking, the grill melted the middle knob, a wire inside the grill caught on fire and melted, and flames darted out  from the front of the grill through an opening in the front.

Char Broil called it a [REDACTED] fire and requested that we send photos, which we did.  The company refused to do anything but sell us a new knob and new wire.  They claimed that the fire was caused by an obstruction in a conduit (we removed the conduit and saw no obstruction) probably a spider web, they said.

This dangerous product should be removed from the market.

incident_description: This is my third winter with the Toro Power Clear 180 Snowthrower and when I went to use it, it wouldn't start.  However, I noticed that there seemed to be gas leaking from somewhere.  Upon further investigation, I found gas leaking from the carburetor.  Fortunately I stopped and investigated on the web for further information.  What I found was that this model has been recalled previously for the exact same issue.  I called Toro and they said they have no recalls on this particular model/serial number at this time.  I bought the snowblower right after the first recall and can't help but wonder if the store just happened to have some defective merchandise in stock still and didn't realize it.  I was instructed to take it to the nearest Toro dealer and they would determine if they could fix it and would decide if it should be covered or not.

incident_description: bought ariens 20E snow blower  model 939401  serial number 087832   Engine would not turn off even after turning off switch and pulling out emergency key.  Engine kept running.  Had to close choke and turn off fuel and let remaining fuel be used before it would shut off.  If I needed t oshut of in emergency it could not happen!

incident_description:

Each year thereafter, for a total of three times, we have had to take the snowblower in for repair for leaking gas.  It is now leaking gas for a fourth time.  Toro/Toro dealer has tried to repair the snowblower under warranty but it continues to leak gas even though they have replaced the carburetor each time.  I have noticed there has been a recall to a similar model.

incident_description: I was on my cub cadet LTX1045 tractor mowing my lawn.  About 10 minutes into the mow, I stopped to empty out my bagger.  Upon returning to the tractor, I saw a fire under the hood of the tractor through the louvers.  I opened up the hood and found the front portion of the engine on fire.  I quickly ran to the house to get the garden hose.  The size of the fire had increased in the minute it took to get the the hose over to the tractor.  The fire was burning very close to plastic gas tank.  I sprayed the hose on the fire for about 2- 3 minutes before I was able to extinguish the flames.  All of the plastic component on the engine were in full flame and melting.  The hood portion started to melt.  all the electrical wires melted and bare metal was exposed.  I was lucky that I had stopped to empty the bagger in a location where I could reach with a garden hose.  If I was any further away, the whole tractor would have been burned to the ground and gas tank may have exploded.  The tractor was less then 6 month old an only had 24 hours on the engine.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the severe engine fire posed a significant risk, with melting plastic components and exposed electrical wires, and could have led to a gas tank explosion if not extinguished.

incident_description:
Switch failed in the run position after 17 months. A year warranty on something that should last a but forever is not worth much.  Pump was running full time. Had  over 120 PSI in the system. The gauge was pegged  I am glad that the weak link in my pluming was in a unfinished space near a drain and not the pressure tank or in a wall upstairs. 
(The previous switch lasted 23 years. It failed when the diaphragm devolved a small leak and caused corrosion on one of the contacts resulting in no electrical connection.)
The cause of this switches failure is the part that rests against the diaphragm and transmits the force of the water pressure to the switch. It is a disk with two legs bent from the same piece of metal. Both of the legs are and has always be over bent. (>90 degrees) One is bent more than the other. This shows on the wear pattern of the contact points. Over time it the wear caused one of the legs to slid off it's contact point. With the legs at opposite sides of the diaphragm and the disk not engineered to move parallel with out bot legs in contact little (well less than half) of the pressure was transferred to the switch and the pump would not shut off. 
With most manufacturing defects if there is one most likely there are more produced at the same time. It is all so possible it has been found and corrected by now.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage and potential safety hazard due to high pressure and failed switch.

incident_description:
I wish to report a serious and potentially dangerous situation. I have been using both [REDACTED] and other high intensity LED flashlights with a belt sheath and I prefer to use [REDACTED] batteries because they donÃÂt corrode as with other batteries. 
On 15 November 2013 my 2 cell AA flashlight exploded shooting the lens and reflector out shattering the lens. Luckily no one was injured just shocked by the loud bang and flying debree.
I believe the problem is that  LEDs require far less voltage to operate than traditional light bulbs and this discharges batteries beyond the threshold of tipical ÃÂbad batteryÃÂ placing them into a unstable condition where now gasses are produced compared to older light bulbs that get to dim identifying time to replace batteries.  Most flashlights are sealed to prevent moisture from entering and under these conditions the gasses have nowhere to go and Bang it explodes.
I feel that LED flashlight need a sensor installed to prevent discharging batteries beyond there safety limits and a pressure relief valve installed to prevent dangerous gasses from building up inside the case. Or have Battery manufactures ensure that discharging batteries do not produce gasses!
The exploding of my flashlight had serious potential to injure someone, and since many of these sealed flashlights state suitable in hazardous environments a detonation like the one I had can cause an explosion of the hazardous material as well
justification: While no one was injured, the flashlight exploding and shooting debris could have caused injury, making it an incident with high likelihood of occurrence given the widespread use of LED flashlights.

incident_description: As reported to Canadian Standards Association (CSA Group) by an American Citizen - "I installed four of the fixtures I purchased online about 2 years ago. Since then 2 of the units stopped working. They have light sensors so they only come on at night. I suspected the problem was with the sensors. I took the units down yesterday and found out that the sensors had actually blown. There was black soot inside the fixture and actually a hole blown in the side of the sensor".

incident_description:
Chainsaw Poulan Pro, Model number PP4218AVX with keyless chain adjustment system. 

The keyless chain adjustment system has a design flow which does not hold the tension of the chain while cutting the wood. Properly adjusted chain gets loose in a matter of seconds while cutting wood which resulted in chain slipping off the chain bar and swinging right next to my hand. I had lots of luck that I was not injured. I have called the company and they refused to address this issue for me because the product was out of warranty. Instead they wanted to sell me an alternative cover with regular chain tensioning system. I think they need to inform other users about potential danger and  offer free of charge remedy. 

There are plenty of evidence of users affected by this problem on the internet. Below are a few comments form Amazon.com product review pages. I am not sure how many of the users realize that if the chains jumps out of the groove because it is too loose they can get seriously hurt.

"Chain Tension - This is an absolute engineering disaster. After some usage, my saw would not keep the chain tight. After an adjustment and a couple cuts of 6" limb or 1 cut of 12" or bigger, and I would need to readjust the chain tension."

"If I adjust the chain too tight it binds, too loose it fall off. There doesn't seem to be a correct adjustment (believe me, after putting the chain back on a few dozen times I have tried everything)."

"The idea of the chain adjustment actually being in the bar sounds great but its a real failure. It is either too tight or too loose, no in between."
justification: The design flaw of the keyless chain adjustment system can cause the chain to loosen and slip off, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she turned on the burners.  Smoke than emitted from the side vent underneath.  The right burner was melted with flames coming out of it.  She grabbed the fire extinguisher and put the flames out.  There was damage to the deck with scorch marks on it.  

The model number is on recall (Release #09-020) but the dates are not in range.

incident_description: I screwed a 50W ACE Hardware indoor/outdoor halogen floodlight bulb (product # 3067261) into a lamp socket to test it.  Immediately there was a flash and a small flame.  The socket in the lamp melted/burned, and the incident stopped only because the lamp was plugged into a power strip with a GFI switch.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the misuse of a high-wattage bulb in an unsuitable socket.

incident_description: I purchased a Pumpkin Torch at Wal-Mart for my kids on November 4.  It was bought at the WM on Shackleford Rd in Little Rock, AR.  I brought it home, replaced the batteries with new and handed it to my daughter.  A few minutes later she screamed and threw it down crying "That burned me" clutching her hand to her chest.  When I looked at it I saw melted plastic stuck to her hand.  The end of the toy had melted, the metal burning through the plastic.  I contacted WM repeatedly about it but have largely been ignored.  E-mails were not responded to and their FaceBook page just redirected me to report it elsewhere with no response there.  I know it was a seasonal toy, but I worry the same product is out there being remarketed for Christmas and another kid could get hurt!
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the child, and the product's defect (melted plastic, exposed metal) increases the likelihood of similar incidents occurring with other units of the same product.

incident_description:
The product is a portable gas grill manufactured by Kuuma Products/Camco Manufacturing, Inc.
This grill has a built in Pezio igniter which sometimes works, sometimes doesn't.   When it does function, it ignites propane at the burner.  When the lid is shut on the grill the flame is extinguished but the gas continues to build up inside the grill.  Only by looking at the temperature gauge (built in to the lid) can you determine that the flame is out (the temperature goes down).  After five minutes with the gas turned off,  the flame may be relit.  When opening the lid, you have access to an access hole to be used to relight the flame by sticking a lit match or utility lighter through the hole.  Residual gas still inside the burner area ignites all at once with a loud noise (whump) and a fireball which singes the hair on your arm.  This happens often while cooking.

Additionally, the wire which connects the Pezio igniter to the sparking head lies close enough to the flame that the insulation on the wire catches fire.  The operator cannot see this take place.  The insulation continues to burn until it reaches the ignitor button and then the plastic housing for the spark generator catches fire.  Again, the operator cannot see this happening while cooking.  After the gas is turned off and the cooking flame is extinguished there continues to be black smoke coming from the ignitor button area.  By inspecting the inside of the unit, I found the Pezio ignitor had burned into an unrecognizable black blob of plastic.  When I contacted the manufacturer to obtain a new ignitor, I explained what happened.  They sent me a new ignitor which I installed according to the directions provided.  After using the grill a few times, the second ignitor caught fire and melted.
justification: The grill's design flaw, allowing gas buildup and delayed ignition, poses a high risk of burns and injuries, as demonstrated by the repeated incidents.

incident_description:
Product: Chicago 14" Electric Chain Saw. Model 67255. Distributed by Harbor Freight Tools

This is the second saw I had. The first I had to exchange. There is a basic design flaw and the company doesn't want to acknowledge it. Thank God I haven't injured myself yet. 
Here is the problem: There is a front handle with guard (good); There is a lockout switch which slides forward. Below there is a trigger switch which slides forward. This combination is unsafe. The trigger switch should slide up or depress. This is the natural motion. When you push down on the front handle to cut, that removes pressure from the power switch and the saw stops as you try to cut. If you keep pressure on the power switch and handle at the same time, the saw will be pushed forward instead of down and fly free. The more you try to correct the problem, the greater chance of injury.
The only for this saw to function is to remove your hand from the front handle and place it near the other hand near the lockout switch. This will then allow the power switch to stay engaged. I tried that and the saw was all over the place but it cut without stopping. That is extremely dangerous so I stopped before I injured myself.
I have notified Harbor Freight Tools and they didn't seem to care. This tool needs to be recalled and have a proper purer switch installed.
justification: The design flaw increases the likelihood of injury, as demonstrated by the user's struggle to control the saw without removing their hand from the handle.

incident_description:
This involves the seat latch on a 2010 Simplicity Manufacturing Regent Riding Lawn Mower Model 2690575 (44" Deck with a B&S 22 HP motor).

The seat latch moves out of the user-adjustable notch when ascending or descending a slight grade. The movement of the seat moves to either of the extreme positions unexpectedly within a fraction of a second. The unexpected seat movement can cause the Operator to lose control of the mower, possibly causing an accident and/or injury to the Operator, bystanders, or property. The seat latch has been re-designed and is of an improper gauge of metal to properly hold the seat in the pre-determined position. 

This has happened on many occasions.

The manufacturer has been informed of the issue and has not offered remediation of the cause.
justification: The seat latch issue can cause unexpected seat movement, potentially leading to loss of control and injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the plastic on the bottom of the panini maker started to melt. The consumer stated that the heating element melted through the plastic. The product started to smoke and the consumer smelled burning. 

The consumer unplugged the product.

The consumer stated that the product was on for 2-3 minutes on medium heat before her husband smelled burning. 

The consumer stated that she spoke to the manf. They informed her that they have never had such a problem before. The manf informed her that this model has been discontinued. The manf offered the consumer discount towards a new purchase.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of the panini maker melting and smoking indicates a potential safety hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' at severity level 2.

incident_description:

The rear axle broke while mowing the lawn and then it leaned towards the left, lowering to the ground with the blade on.  She was able to power off the unit.  This incident caused her neck to be tilted a little and she took some Advil for the pain. No medical attention was needed.

The caller feels that the product is a safety hazard and should be reported.

incident_description:

incident_description: Childrens Spiderman projector flashlight purchased at Dollar Tree made by What Kids Want.  The flashlight has three different designs kids can place over end to project a design.  Takes two AA batteries.  Purchased today...and put two brand new [REDACTED] batteries inside it.  Used for literally minutes and got extremely hot.  Thankfully my four year old was smart enough to tell us.  We shut it off and opened it up to find it had melted the bottom battery.  The battery was too hot to even touch.  My child could have been burned.  It could have set something on fire if left on unattended.  Product is ages four and up.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using her lime green expanding water hose for the second time, the water hose exploded and became detached in 2 places. The consumer stated that she stretched the water hose out and had been using it for approximately 3-5 minutes before it exploded. She stated that she was completely wet and the water force knocked her glasses off her face. 

The consumer stated that she had her contacts on and the pressure of the water knocked her contact out of her left eye. The consumer stated that she could not see from her left eye and decided to go to Doctor [REDACTED] on 09/02/2013. She stated that he diagnose that the water pressure of the hose had pushed her contact to the back of her eye ball. 

The consumer stated that on 09/04/2013 she had to have surgery to remove the contact from the back on her left eye ball and put back in placed. The consumer stated that surgery took approximately 3 hours and she was then sent home. She stated that on 09/11/2013 she has a follow up appointment to see how her eye was doing after surgery. 

The consumer stated that she hasnÃÂt been able to check the damages to her glasses.

The consumer stated that there were no damages to her home structure. 

She stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious eye injury requiring surgery, classifying it as a '3 - Injury' on the severity scale. The likelihood is rated '4 - likely' as the consumer had been using the hose for only a short period before the incident occurred.

incident_description:
(8/3/13)  The consumer trimmed an area that contained landscaping rocks that were 1-1/2ÃÂ ÃÂ 2ÃÂ dia.  Some of the rocks were being thrown against the consumer, while she was using the trimmer.  Additionally, the trimmer kept re-threading itself during use.  The consumer continued to use the trimmer, but adjusted her stance so that she was further away from the trimmer.  The adjusted stance did not make a difference.  Large chunks of thread were being spewed from the trimmer, but the line was not clipping itself consistently.  She continued to use the trimmer and a large chunk of trimmer thread hit the consumerÃÂs left leg twice, in succession.  She received a cut on her left leg from the thread.  She has 3 scars that are staggered on her leg and she does not believe that they  will ever go away.  She has not seen a doctor and does not plan to.

(8/5/13)  The consumer called the manufacturer and shared her concerns with them.  Their rep. asked the consumer what she would like and indicated that they could replace the trimmer or give her a refund.   The consumer was told that a refund could take several weeks, so she opted for a replacement trimmer.  The mfr. sent the consumer and identical model trimmer and she returned the older trimmer back to them, at their expense.  The consumer also sent the additional spool of thread that she initially purchased to the mfr. along with the trimmer.    

The consumer was later told that the manufacturer could not test the trimmer using the original spool of thread that she included.  It is not known why they could not use it.  The consumer noted that she has scars on both legs from where the rocks and gravel hit her.

The consumer has a firm file: [REDACTED] associated with the report that she filed with the mfr.

incident_description:
I purchased two DAP Xhoses, 75', in September 2013.  The product ID is XHOSE75PROBG.  I purchased them because they were advertised as being stronger than the original Xhose.

I unpacked them and followed the directions before the first use.  One Xhose literally exploded within ten minutes of the first time I used it and the end connected to the water supply snapped around.  No one was near so there were no injuries.  The split in the outer black covering is 30 inches and a blue inner tube of 13 inches was blown out of the split.

The second Xhose failed the next day when the water supply had been turned off and the Xhose was retracting.  The outer cover did not split, but it appears the inner tube broke and water leaked out of the hose.

The DAP Xhose is an unsafe product.  The advertising for the product is false as the Xhose is not strong and failed upon the first use of them.
justification: Both hoses failed within days of use, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I am contacting you to report a safety issue with a Char-broil Quickset grill purchased from Lowe's.  The grill caught on fire after only the 2nd time of use.  It was clean and kept covered during unuse.  Went inside to get the meat to put on, and when I returned, flames were pouring out the front and sides.  I couldn't turn the grill off because the knobs had melted, disintegrated, and fallen off.  Heat was so hot it also melted the ignituion button.  The only way I was able to extinguish the fire enough to turn it off directly at the propane tank was by spraying water on it.  The grill is now unusable.  I am so glad I had pulled the grill two feet away from my house, because my 12 yr old was inside the adjoining room and I shudder to think what could have happened if the tank had exploded or the the house caught fire.  This grill is a safety hazard and needs to be removed from the market or recalled.  While checking online, I found over 100 similar incidents and complaints reported on Char-broil grills at http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/char-broil.html?page=2.  This company is being irresponsible by ignoring the multipe incidents and acting like it is consumer error.  This is only the small handful of people who reported the issues.  Many people do not report incidents.
justification: The grill caught fire on the 2nd use, with no apparent user error, indicating a high likelihood of reoccurrence.

incident_description:
Homelite chinsaw is used to trim dead branches form trees. Th chain(blade repeatedly disengaged from its track. This item is brand new. Even after reinstalling the chain, it continued to come loose.
On close examination, it was discovered that the drive spline is to short to hold the chain in place.
When I tried to report a probable safety issue to the company, customer support told me to take for repair and refused to let me speak to someone whoe might be able to correct the problem. Repairing the chain saw I purchased is not the difficulty, as I can simply return it to the store where I purchased
it
justification: The chain disengaging repeatedly poses a risk of injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased the Bel Air outdoor wall latern (part #253366) about two years ago. This light stopped working about a week ago so i took it down to figure out why it stopped working. After looking at the inside of the latern there appears to be a good amount of burn marks as if the latern had caught on fire. After googling the part number I found there was a safety recall from the company for the exact same thing. This item could have burned my house down!!!

incident_description:
The rubber hose from propane tank to gas valve melted, while the grill was in use.  

The consumer said that his wife had a problem starting the auto igniter on the grill.  She retrieved a 6" grill lighter and attempted to start the burners, but they would not work.  The consumer removed the propane tank and bought a new one and attached it to the grill.  The burner lit, but the flame was extremely low.  The consumer turned the grill off and inspected it.

He examined the grill and saw a hole in the hose connected to the propane tank and the gas valve.  The consumer discontinued use of the grill.  

(7/20/2013)  The consumer searched the Internet and saw Recall 10-099 and noticed that the problem was similar to what he experienced.

The consumer called the brand name company on 7/19/2013, but they were not open.  He reached the firm on 7/22/2013.  The firm's rep. (name unavailable) told the consumer that they did not make his particular grill and they referred him to Archway 800-723-8836.  The rep. at Archway told the consumer that his grill was "not" under recall, but as a 1 time curtsey, they would replace his hose with a new one at no charge.  The consumer said that his model was similar to the one in the recall and suggested that they take the grill back.  The consumer believes that another rubber hose will eventually present the same problem.  The consumer told the rep. that he could send the hose, but unless it is metal, he has not confidence in the grill and will not use it again.

The consumer was given a confirmation # 34475436.

The consumer believes that the recall needs to be expanded to include other rubber hoses on these grills.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a potential gas leak due to a melted hose, posing a significant risk of fire or explosion.

incident_description:
I purchased an outdoor fireplace manufactured by Garden treasures.  It was the Garden Treasures Living  Cast Iron Chiminea.  During assembly the leg became [de]tached because it was only spot welded in 3 points.  I was concerned that had I assembled and used the product the legs could have become detached during use.  This is especially a concern with this model since it is top heavy.  Once the spot weld detach, the unit could easily fall over.

Quite dangerous scenario and very glad the design failure presented itself during assembly.  I returned the product to Lowes and informed them of the product defect as well.

You can find a picture of this product at this url:  http://www.lowes.com/pd_291623-63094-SRCH06D_0__?productId=4764069
justification: The product's design flaw, spot-welded legs, poses a high likelihood of detachment during use, potentially causing the unit to fall over and leading to an incident.

incident_description: I was spraying off my deck with the hose and it developed a bubble at the neck of the hose. About the same time I discovered this it burst and I was soaked with water. I threw the hose down on the ground and walked down the steps to turn off the water. Then I started to itch. I looked at my arms. They were both covered in hives. I went inside and removed my wet clothes. I was covered in hives where my clothes had touched me.
justification: The incident resulted in an allergic reaction causing hives, which is considered an injury.

incident_description:
2013 Weber genesis gas grill knobs turn on too easily when putting cover on grill causing gas leak. There is little resistance to turn the knob like on other gas grills or stoves.  I store my grill near an air intake vent for my furnace room, so when the gas is accidentally turned on, the gas leaks into my basement near the furnace creating a potentially dangerous situation.

I try to remember to turn the gas off on the grill after each grilling session, but on three occasions have forgotten and smelled gas in my basement soon thereafter.  I'm afraid one of these times the gas will ignite.  I have seen  other reports online about this and weber customer service just recommends remembering to turn the gas off at the source each time.  Seems like some sort of recall to make the knobs harder to turn is in order.

incident_description:
On 07/10/2013 I purchased Stater Bros Brand 3lb bag of Light the bag charcoal for a family vacation.  On 07/12/2013 we were on a beach in Lake Havasu getting ready to bbq using the [REDACTED] BBQ pit,  I put the entire bag in the pit unopened like the instructions indicated and lit the bag with a long lighter  the bag emploded and fire flashed back and burned both of my hands on top of my fingers I ran away from it and a family went over to light the BBQ not realizing how bad I was burned and lit the bag again and the bag againg emploded and flashed back on him.

incident_description: I purchased the "Jetboil-Zip Cooking System" last year. I used it successfully 3 times. Last month, the stove malfunctioned on my 4th attempt. I was in the Adirondacks backpacking with friends. I was relying on the Jetboil stove to heat water. After setting up the stove and attempting to light it, the flames shot out around the stove. Fire was coming directly from the fuel canister and encircling the stove in a tall fire. I was afraid that the fuel canister was going to explode and catch our tent, or our faces, on fire, or worse - start a forest fire. We got the stove detached from the fuel canister using a stick and our boots and doused everything with water. It was horrible. The stove had malfunctioned, though it previously worked, leading me to believe that there is a material in the stove that cannot stand up to heat and use, therefore allowing it to malfunction over time.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant risk of injury or property damage due to the stove's malfunction and subsequent fire.

I returned the unit to my local Home Depot and bought a different brand.

This was the replacement unit. Is it too defective in, perhaps, a different way?!

 It was an alarming experience.

Thank you and.... May the Gov't shut down end soon!
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I bought a backyard fire pit from Christmas Tree Shop a few weeks ago.  It is made by Nantucket Distributing Company.  It is an iron frame that a round pinkish colored faux brick facade sits in and then the bowl that the fire goes in sits in the facade.

We intended to use it just for small fires, the roasting marshmallow kind.  And also clearing out some small branches that have accumulated over the summer.

I started the fire and put some branches, small logs, and a cardboard box in the bowl.  Everything seemed fine until I heard this huge 'POP' sound.  At first I thought my husband might have put a log on too and the wood had a knot in it, since that's a noise I have heard in the past when burning knotted wood.  

Didn't really think much about it until a few minutes later when another huge 'POP' sent a piece of the fiberglass facade whizzing past my face and half way across the yard.  I stood there in shock since I had just bought this, it was our first fire in the darn thing and now it was exploding all over my yard.  Pieces of the facade began flying everywhere and the noise it made sounded like I had bullets in my fire pit!

I don't know how a fire pit can be sold that explodes upon actually using it for what it is intended.  I am so grateful that my 3 year old was not in the yard with me at the time of all this.  If she would have gotten hurt from this I don't know what I would have done.

I called the store I bought it from and the manager said that he would tell his manager about it and so on, but I can't take the chance that he doesn't.  I have to tell everyone I can think of about this because it is incredibly dangerous and I couldn't handle it if a child were to get injured by this.  

I don't have any item numbers or anything like that, we recycled the box and contents after we put together the fire pit.  But if you need any further information, please let me know and I will do my best to obtain it for you.
justification: The fire pit exploded upon use, sending debris across the yard, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I have a John Deere 1026R Subcompact Tractor.  The hydraulic front end loader will malfunction.  When you manipulate the joystick to curl the bucket up, it will drop (tilt) forward several inches before curling back up. This is a safety issue as anything in the front end loader bucket can and will drop out causing possible injury and/or damage.  

John Deere's first solution is to tell everyone to operate their tractors as almost full throttle to stop this from happening, but yet they have redesigned the hydraulic control valve to fix the issue.

They refuse to fix everyones tractor, it apparently lies with the dealer you have.  If you are fortunate enough to have a good dealer, they will fix the problem, if not, they won't.  

This is a widespread problem as evidenced by the number of posts on-line.  Just google "John Deere FBS".  Those of us that have the problem have taken to calling it "Floopy Bucket Syndrome  (FBS)".

Also if you google "DTAC92992" it will show you from John Deere, that they acknolwedge the issue and have re-engineered the parts, but are gettin them to fix it is next to impossible.

The date in the "Incident Date" field is just a date, this is a constant on going problem.

Please help.
justification: The malfunctioning front end loader poses a high risk of injury due to objects falling out of the bucket.

When contacted Poulan stated they had no recalls.  I had not even told them the model yet.  When I mentioned the model - same answer. When I mentioned I was a safety engineer and concerned that someone will get hurt from the condition and was considering a call to the CPSC -  they noted that they were replacing the hand wheel with the conventional two nut system.  This recognition of a hazard and correction was not offered up front.  That is my concern for that is negligence. They then went on to note they would not replace without a receipt.

As a safety professional and long time user of many saw types and brands this is a dangerous condition for the user will tend to continue using the saw well after the loose chain is observed.  When the chain does come loose it flies off the bar when moving.  That fact that they are not forthcoming with the hazard and correction in not acceptable to me.

[REDACTED] CSP
justification: The poorly designed tightener causes the chain to consistently come off the blade, posing a high risk of injury to the user.

incident_description: The knobs on our gas barbeque turn on so easily that putting the barbeque cover over the grill can turn the gas on.  Most gas grills require pushing the knobs in before they will turn on, howver ours turn on with almost imperceptible depression of the knob.  Several times, we have discovered the gas on, hours and even days after using the grill when we smelled the gas.  I have contacted the maufacturer.  Their response is that the gas should be turned off at the tank after each use.  While this may be true, I don't think many people turn the gas off at the tank each time they use their barbeque. incident_description:
The product in question is a Traeger Little Tex Elite wood pellet grill.  This unit's firing cycle and subsequent cooking temperature is controlled by a simple digital that controls the operation of the wood pellet feed auger which delivers the pellets to the combustion chamber.  One setting of the thermostat is "smoke" which is time-based, in default, the auger operates delivering wood pellets for 15 seconds out of 90.  This setting is practically useless as the fire goes out.  If the restart procedure is executed, the unit can burn internally very aggressively and unexpectedly as the accumulation of unburnt wood pellets begins to burn.

Typically when the unit is operated in in non "smoke" or temperature cook mode, the thermostat will try to control the firing cycle via cooking chamber temperature and not by a set time cycle.  Today, the unit while operating in temperature cook mode unexpectedly went out.  I noted the the pellet hopper was empty and subsequently refilled it and executed the restart procedure as published by the manufacturer.  I checked on it after approximately 20 minutes only to find very heavy smoke and flames issuing from the unit.  I foolishly opened the lid at this point to find the interior of the unit engulfed in flames and a temperature reading of 521 degrees F on the thermostat readout.  Fortunately there were no combustible surfaces within three feet at the time of the incident save for some garden plants.  I believe that given the quantity of fire present and it's intensity that this unit which has no provision to shut the induced draft fan off in the case of fire constitutes a fire hazard.
justification: The grill's unexpected fire hazard, despite being operated in temperature cook mode and having no combustible surfaces nearby, indicates a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: WHEELS FALL OFF PUSH LAWNMOWER: I purchased, about three years ago, a Sears Craftsman lawn mower, model number 247.388140, and serial number 1c310861122.  The purchase was made at the Sears retail location in West Mifflin, Pennsylvania.  The product warranty had expired prior to the safety issue.  >>>In June of 2013, while operating the lawn mower normally, the right front height adjuster failed causing the right front wheel to separate from the lawn mower.  The failed part was ordered from Sears/Craftsman at a cost of about $17.00 and replaced.  >>>Within about four hours of operation after replacement of the right front height adjuster, the left front height adjuster failed in exactly the same way causing the left front wheel to separate from the mower chassis.   I BELIEVE THIS MAY BE A SERIOUS SAFETY HAZARD THAT COULD RESULT IN A POSSIBLE SEVERE INJURY.  When informed of this situation, Sears Customer Service personnel displayed little concern.  Perhaps the CPSC would be able to request parts orders of the replacement parts to ascertain whether replacement parts of the type that failed are being ordered with inordinate frequency, thus indicating an inordinate failure rate for this part.
justification: Potential for severe injury due to wheel separation, as demonstrated by the rapid failure of both front wheels within a short period of operation.

incident_description:
The lawn mower built up pressure in the plastic gas tank. The consumer said when the fuel would get low (less than 1/2 a tank); more pressure would build up in the tank.  The consumer would loosen the gas cap and could hear the pressure release.

The consumer has owned the mower for 3- 4 years and he has 102 hours of use on it.

The consumer cut his neighbors grass and sensed something wrong with the mower.  He turned the mower off and went to the rear to inspect it.  The gas cap literally blew off the tank and the metal valve cover caught fire, when fuel spilled on it from the cap blowing off of it.  The consumer had a rag in his pocket and he tried to put the flames out, but they kept re-igniting.  Some of the hair on the consumer's right arm was singed (no medical attention needed).  Within 7 - 8 seconds, the entire motor was engulfed in flames.  The consumer said that the motor and all of the plastic on the mower burned up and melted.  This included the mower's seat and the plastic controls on it.  The mower was a total loss.

The consumer's wife called 911 and the fire department responded.  In the mean time, the neighbor's son and the consumer attempted to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher and they were somewhat successful.  However, the fire department arrived and completely extinguished the fire.

The consumer believes that there was a 7 gallon fuel tank on the mower.  He did not have any additional fuel with him and the gas was limited to what was in the tank at the time of the incident.  The consumer said that they plastic tank is on the rear right hand portion of the mower.  The tank fits on a metal tray, which heats up and in turn, heats up the fuel.  As there is less fuel in the tank, the remaining fuel can heat to higher temperature.  The consumer noted that over time, the measurement decals on the mower either melted off or detached as a result of this heat.  [REDACTED], another person who used the mower prior to this incident also noticed the pressure that built up in the fuel tank.

The local sheriff also came out and filed a report on this incident.

The consumer paid approximately $12,500.00 for the mower.

(6/2013)  The consumer called the retailer; 2901 NW. Hwy 24; Topeka, KS  6618; Tel:  785-267-9200 (alt. tell:  888-273-9990) and they arranged for the mower to be picked up.  The retailer is a Farm Implement Store.  The consumer worked with [REDACTED] (retailer's rep.), when he purchased it.  The retailer contacted the mfr. and they sent one of their rep's ([REDACTED]) out to look at the mower.  

Mr. [REDACTED] arrived at the dealer and looked at the mower with the consumer and the dealer's rep. present.  Mr. [REDACTED] asked where the gas cap was.  The consumer told him what happened.  The consumer told him that the gas cap had burned up in the fire.

NOTE:  The consumer mentioned that he had replaced the gas cap on 1 or 2 prior occasions.  He said that the dealer provide replacement caps, because they thought that the cap may not have been venting properly.  

Mr. [REDACTED] ended up telling the consumer to turn this matter over to his home owner's insurance. 

The consumer contacted his insurance (State Farm), but they concluded that since the incident did not occur on the consumer's property, that they were no liable.  The consumer note that he had been with his insurance company 30+ years.

The consumer called Mr. [REDACTED], but prior to that, the consumer's wife contacted their agent.  The agent worked on this claim further and the insurance company reversed their decision and gave the consumer $10,200.00 for it.

The consumer called Mr. [REDACTED] and upgraded to a diesel mower by this same manufacturer ($14,383.40).

The consumer called Mr.[REDACTED] and said that his insurance company should not have to cover the entire cost of the replacement mower.  Mr. [REDACTED] called the retailer and the consumer was given a $300.00 discount on the purchase of the replacement mower.  

NOTE:  The consumer said that the mfr. should have covered the entire cost of replacing the mower.
justification: Injury occurred due to the gas cap blowing off and catching fire, singeing the consumer's arm hair.
