incident_description:
The consumer says he used the product once per month.  He says that a month ago he was mowing the lawn.  After 15-20 minutes it cut off, started smoking and caught on fire.  

He was near his truck and grabbed the fire extinguisher to put it out mostly but also had to pour water on it.  Smoke was coming out from the front of the engine.  

He contacted the manufacturer who apologized for the inconvenience.  They offered no further assistance.  He called his local John Deere Service dept who told him this was the second complaint they had heard of this season of a mower catching on fire.  

The consumer is not sure if the other complaint was on a similar model.  A local shop replaced a carburetor, and the fuel line that goes through it but they were not sure why the unit caught on fire.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of the mower catching fire poses a significant risk, as evidenced by the second similar complaint this season.

incident_description: I purchased a Webber Outdoor Grill and severely burned my hand when grabbing the handle to lift the cover while cooking.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe burn, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood of occurrence is possible (3) as it could happen due to user error or lack of caution while handling hot grill parts.

incident_description:
The consumer says he was cutting his grass when the shoot that disperses the grass goes flying off.  He placed the mounting is rusted, the mower deck was split and one of the blades was exposed.  

He says that he contacted the retailer/manufacturer who told him to buy a new mower.  The consumer is shocked by how rusted the unit is in such a short period of time.  He says that the deck disenegrated from rust while he was using it and could have amputated his foot.
justification: Exposed blade from a disintegrating mower deck due to rust could have caused severe injury, such as amputation.

incident_description:
The consumer says that on August 10th she was having a barbecue.  She turned on the gas and then the ignitor.  Within a few seconds she heard a loud "boom" and the grill portion flew up and hit her in the arm.  She says that their was no reason for this to happen.  

She turned it off immediately and has not used it since.  She then got a recall notice sent directly from the retailer.  The consumer says the "boom" was so loud that neighbors came to her asking if she was ok.  She has a mark on her elbow from where she was hit.  One neighbor saw the grill fly up when this happened
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, and the consumer's account suggests it was not a one-off event given the recall notice and neighbors' witness.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while his friend was using the riding lawn mower to mow the lawn within a few mins flames erupted from the exhaust pipe.  The carburetor had leaked onto the exhaust pipe which ignited the fire.  He used a fire extinguisher to contain the flames.  This incident caused his friend to receive 1st degree burns to his back.  First aid was administered to the wound. No medical attention was received. 

8/2013 The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed to take it to an authorized dealer and to make a claim on his insurance.  He took the unit to a dealer and was advised that he needed proof of purchase for them to assist him.

The product is not involved in a recall.

He is concerned that this lawn mower is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st degree burns, and while the exact cause is known, it's possible for similar issues to occur again.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the pocket water hose drips water which should not happen.  She was watering her garden and the hose exploded with water to her face, if the pressure of the water was on high it could have caused injury to her eyes.

She stated that she contacted the retailer about the incident and he advised that he would replaced it.

There are no recalls related to this product.

The caller feels that this hose is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: While no injury occurred, the potential for eye injury exists if the water pressure is high.

incident_description: Grill was being used normally when suddenly it burst into flames from the hose leading from the propane tank to the grill housing.
justification: The grill bursting into flames indicates an incident, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description: I have a perfect flame gas grill and the burner is defective. When I was grilling one of the burners blew out and created a large flame. The model number is 2518sl.
justification: The defective burner caused a large flame, posing a fire hazard but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting a safety incident involving his chain saw purchased April 30th, 2010 that presented no problems at all until July 24th 2013 he was using it to cut firewood and the sprocket shattered but remained inside of unit. 

This incident happened during a time that it was in use and if the sprocket pieces had flown out as projectiles they could have injured the user or bystanders seriously.           

Caller contacted the manufacturer August 5th, 2012 but could only obtain information that it is not under recall.

There are no injuries to be reported,
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potentially dangerous projectile hazard.

incident_description: We fired up our Weber E-310 to preheat it before cooking chicken breasts.  Roughly five minutes later, I went out to check on the grill and found the area under the control board full of flames.  I was able to quickly reach under and get the main propane valve shut off.  The controls, hoses, etc are burned beyond repair.  The grill is shot.  Scary considering the grill sat on a new Cedar deck attached to the house.  Another minute or two and we would have had a serious fire to wrestle.   Is there a recall?  I see this is a repeated problem reported.  Next steps?
justification: The grill fire could have easily spread to the attached cedar deck and house, posing a significant risk.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had used the mower for about 15 minutes. The consumer stated that normally he leaves the mower outside to cool off before putting it in the garage. This time, the consumer put the mower in the garage directly after use. After few minutes the consumer went to move the mower out of the garage.

When the consumer went to the garage, he saw flames shooting out from under the hood of the mower. The consumer stated that the flames were really close to the gas tank. The consumer extinguished the fire with a fire extinguisher.

The consumer stated that the dust from the fire extinguisher damaged the automatic switch to open the garage door. The consumer had to manually open the garage door.
The consumer contacted the garage door technicians and they informed him that the switch stopped working because of the dust from the extinguisher.

Consumer burned his thumb trying to extinguish the fire.

The consumer has not contacted the manf but he intends to.

This model is not included in the recall.

The consumer is not reporting any property damages.
justification: Consumer suffered a burn while attempting to extinguish the fire, resulting in an injury.

incident_description:
I have a Honda walk behind mower model HRX2172HXA (serial number MAGA-1575405).  I have owned this mower for several years.  This mower has developed a problem with the carburetor.  

It has started letting gas to flow out the air filter housing even when the mower is shut off.  It has progressively gotten worse.  At one point, it filled my entire garage with gas fumes.  My wife came in one evening and noted that the garage smelled of gas.  When I went out the fumes were over powering.  I was afraid to use the garage door opener as I thought the garage door opener motor might cause a spark.  With the amount of gas fumes in the garage, there would have been an explosion or at least a fire.  It was a dangerous situation.

I attempted to correct the problem by ordering a new carburetor from Plano Power Equipment in Plano, TX.  The new carburetor looked exactly like the old carburetor.  I installed it and within the month, it was leaking gasoline out the air filter hosing.  This indicates to me that they have a design or manufacturing defect in these carburetors.  

This evening while I was using the mower I shut it down for about 10 minutes.  When I went back to it, gasoline was already pouring out of the air filter housing.  It has reached the point that I have to use the fuel line shut off valve whenever the mower is shutoff.

I have an older model HRX217 at our rental house and I have never had this issue with that mower.  The only time I have to use the fuel line shut off valve on this mower is when I am storing it for winter.  I looked at the carburetor on this mower and it is a different design than the one on the problem mower.
justification: Gas fumes filled the garage, posing a high risk of fire or explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Craftsman WeedWacker Gas Trimmer (Item #07171102000) on October 2, 2012 on sale.  It was put into storage and not used for the first time until the following Spring, May 2013.  Since then I've used it only three times.  Each time in attempting to trim light, dry grass in my yard, the trimmer line would fray and deteriorate so that it would have to be replaced at least once during each use.  Also, the trimmer head and shaft would get so hot as to scald my skin if they were touched.  I had to wait for it to cool down before replacing the trimmer line.  The trimmer end cap would continually come loose and fall off while trimming, also.  And while cutting, the engine would repeatedly stall if I released the throttle lever to an idle position.  It would run extremely roughly while cutting.  The gas used was freshly purchased and mixed properly with recommended oil.
justification: Repeated skin scalding and engine stalling pose a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
was using a new black and decker cordless hedge trimmer 24" 36 volt lithium ion battery and reached in behind the guard instead of in front, where it is safe, to grab the handle, because the guard is way too small in width. it doesn't even go as wide as the motor or handle, and is too close to the handle to prevent what I had done anyway.

Just seems that the guard is pretty much useless. got lucky and only mangled my finger "pads" (index, middle and ring fingers on my left hand) instead of cutting them off, because I was reaching for the bottom part of the handle and my fingers were parallel to the blades. Ended up with about 10 stitches in my ring finger and about 30 stitches in my middle finger. index finger was cut, but no stitches.

NEEDS WIDER GUARD!

Thanks,

[REDACTED]
justification: Inadequate guard size led to severe injury, with fingers requiring stitches.

incident_description: Purchased a new Char-Broil Gas Grill in mid July.  Had difficulty connecting the gas nozzle to the LP gas tank.  After 30+minutes finally thought had it connected without obvious leak but ensure turn gas off at tank after every use and check for leaks when turn it on.  On Thursday, 22 AUG turned gas on at tank and immediately heard hissing sound and smelled gas.  Turned gas off and tried to tighten but nozzle was on as far as would go . Tried turning on and hissing was diminished but still present.  Turned off again.  There is an obvious problem with the design of the nozzle, it is incapable of making a secure connection to the LP gas tank leading to a very hazardous condition if not noticed by the consumer.  I've never seen an LP nozzle this difficult to connect.
justification: The difficulty in connecting the gas nozzle to the tank and the subsequent gas leak pose a high likelihood of incident, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was attempting to turn on my Patio Bistro gas grill to cook dinner.  I followed the directions that were printed in the user manual.  I turned on the gas and then turned the knob to ignition.  After hearing a few clicks, the flame wasn't turning on so I turned the knob back to the off position and turned off the gas.  I then turned the gas back on and turned the knob to ignition again.  This time, I leaned over to peek inside the grill to see if the flame was on and instantly, there was an explosion that burned my eyebrows and the front of my hair.  I had glasses on at the time so my eyes were not hurt.
justification: Injury occurred due to the explosion, which was likely caused by a gas leak, as the flame didn't ignite initially.

incident_description: I was using my Char-Broil ÃÂGas Patio BistroÃÂ Grill. I turned it on to the 'click-click-click" ignition sound and I heard the gas ignite. I shut the lid and walked away to let the grill heat up. When I returned a few minutes later to check the grill and put on my chicken if it was hot. I smelled gas. I went to turn the grill off immediately and quickly. In turning off the grill, you have to scroll the knob past the ignition portion of the switch. As the knob went past this section, the grill exploded and blew the top off of the grill. As this happened. I felt a significant impact of the blast against my chest. The hair on both of my arms and some of my facial hair and hair on my head was singed. While some of my skin was red and mildly burned like a sun burn, I did not sustain any severe burns. I could feel the impact on my chest from the blast for about 2 hours.
justification: The grill exploded due to a design flaw requiring the knob to pass the ignition point to turn off, leading to severe injury.

incident_description: We grilled hamburgers, and when they were finished, we closed the lid to let the grease burn off while we took the burgers inside. When we came back out, a flame was coming out of the far left knob, near the gas hose. We shut the gas off at the tank and the flame went out, but not before the knob melted.
justification: The incident involved a flame coming out of the grill, which could have led to property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The handles on Weber Charcoal Grills either absorb or conduct heat and become too hot to handle. This issue is the
result of a design flaw in the grill top. Formerly these handles were made of wood which did not create a safety
hazard. However, because of the need to label these handles with county of origin (this is what the customer service
representative reported) they are now made of a different material which becomes too hot to handle with ones
hands. This issue is not random or inconsistent but happens whenever these grills are used.
My experience result in three burned fingers and a dropped grill cover causing minor product damage.

These handles are not merely warm but too hot to handle causing burns.

After speaking with the customer service representative I was told to use a glove or pot holder in the future.

This issue is easy to resolve with a handle that does not absorb the heat from the grill. In fact such a handle did exist
when they were made of wood.

11 August 2013
[REDACTED]

[REDACTED]
V .P. of Customer Service
Weber Stephen Products, LLC
90 West Hillcrest Blvd.
Schaumburg, 11. 60195

Dear [REDACTED]:

I was referred to you by one of your on-line phone customer service representatives.
Last evening, while using my recently purchased, One-Touch Silver charcoal grill 22 Yz"
(serial number AU purchased at the Green Thumbers in Davenport Iowa on 5.11.13), I
lifted the lid to remove the meat and burned my hand. Three fingers were burned as I
tried to escape the heat from the handle. The lid was dropped causing a minor amount of
damage to the lid.

It is clear that this handle conducts heat or absorbs heat to a level that cannot be tolerated
by your customers.

The purpose of this letter is to call your attention to this very serious design flaw and to
correct the issue. I did a search of the internet and this issue is common among your
customers. It is absolutely amazing to me that a company like Weber that manufactures
products that get hot, would design a handle that conducts or absorbs intolerable levels of
heat.

I spoke to two customer service representatives. The first representative indicated that I
should wear a glove or use a pot holder. This hardly seems like an appropriate design
solution. The second service representative indicated that this has been a known issue for
some time. She added that 5 or 6 years ago Weber discontinued the use of wood handles
as there was a country of origin issue related to the labeling of the handles.

I can only conclude that you have cut corners to save on product costs putting your
customers at risk. From my perspective it is unthinkable that a manufacturer in good
conscience could allow this known product defect to exist. These grills are not highly
engineered products - a simple solution is available. The risk of injury is not random but
rather it is known and expected! When injuries can be significant and the cost of fixing
the problem insignificant, the solution seems obvious.

I look forward to your response.

Very truly yours,
[REDACTED]

CC:
[REDACTED], General Council & Secretary to the Board of Managers
Weber-Stepen Products
200 East Daniels Road
Palatine, IL. 60067
justification: The grill handles become too hot to handle, causing burns, which is not a rare occurrence as evidenced by the customer's experience and the company's knowledge of the issue.

incident_description: I just wrote you a lengthy note thru Char-Broil "contact us" option. Then I noticed the recall catagory. and my model # 12601558 was on it. Here is what I wrote them explaining my unfortunate incident. ........My roomate got this grill as a gift and the infrared emitter grill is dangerous! I was lighting the grill and it exploded in my face. You can't see if there is a flame and the type of grill makes the gas trapped and in only seconds the gas builds and when igniting, it exploded. The grill actually blew up over 3 inches high and slammed back down making flames burst out from the front because the front of the grill lifted more aiming flames directly onto my face and hair. The worst is I happen to inhale from the shock and the flames burnt deep into my nose...VERY PAINFUL!!! I have pictures of my nose with 2nd degree burns and it set my hair on fire. The pain was the worst pain I have ever felt. I suffered severly for over 3 weeks during the healing process. It could have been so much worse but my hair was damp from the pool, Lucky for both of us! It effected my job and my appearance along with the pain left me depressed and unable face people, it was quite awful looking. I notice you no longer have that grill on any of your products now. I want to know how Char-Broil wants to handle this. I am a victim of a faulty product of yours and hope you will take this serious as I do and I will take further action if Char-Broil fails to address this serious situation. I would like to send the pictures so you can see what your product did to me. I am sure Char-Broil is a upstanding company and will take care of this in a professional fashion. I look forward to hearing back as soon as possible! Regretfully [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in severe second-degree burns and potential disfigurement, and the likelihood of such a dangerous design flaw is high given the product's recall and the user's detailed account.

incident_description:
I purchased the "Pocket Hose" at Home Depot a few months ago. On Saturday, 17 Aug 13,  I was watering and noticed that the outside material started to crack and fray -- before I could get the water source turned off, the inside 'hose' exploded -- fortunately only dousing me with water. I went on line and found that this is a regular occurrence with this hose. Should you not do something about that; perhaps recalling them as safety hazards? What if it had exploded at the spray nozzle connecting point - that could have done significant damage to a body part -- perhaps even an eye!!!

She found online that this is a regular occurrence with this hose.  Injury ha
justification: The incident resulted in no physical injury, but the hose's tendency to explode is well-documented and likely to happen again.

incident_description: I purchased a fire pit/basket from Meijer a few months ago. I recently used the product for the first time and was shocked at how dangerous it was. Fire spewed out of the sides of the basket in whatever direction the wind was blowing.
justification: Fire spewing from the sides of the basket poses a risk of property damage or injury, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I have the Char Broil Patio Bistro gas grill that you issued a recall on yesterday.  I think you really need to get these off the market completely and here is why.

Several times I have started my grill thinking it was lit only to come out later and find that is isn't ignited and the grill is full of raw unlit propane.  DANGEROUS!

Also, the gas knob is easy to turn on by mistake.  We keep our under a cover and one day I came out, took the cover off and the knob was not quite off and gas had built up under the cover.  Static electricity made the raw gas flash!  I could have been hurt pretty bad had the gas been on for several days.

I'm 57 years old and have been using gas grills since I was a kid and this is without a doubt the most dangerous gas grill I have ever owned.  PLEASE do a total recall of this poorly designed product before someone gets seriously hurt.

Thanks

[REDACTED]
justification: The grill's design flaws, such as the easy-to-turn-on knob and lack of ignition, pose a high likelihood of incidents involving unlit propane buildup.

incident_description: We have had 2 separate instances.  The first incident blew open the cover and burnt the hair on my sons arm.  He was standing next to the grill and it exploded with no cause.  The second incident happened this week with my husband and burnt the hair on his arm.  We made the immediate decision to throw the grill away and replace it with a [REDACTED] grill.
justification: Both incidents resulted in burns, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
The burner flame goes out and then reignites when I turn the control knob to off. 
There was a small explosion and the grate flew up. This happened 4 times.
justification: Multiple incidents of the burner flame reigniting and causing an explosion, though no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was cooking hotdogs on the grill.  The burner went out.  When I turned end knob to off the grill flared up singing the hair off my arms. I was not hurt nothing was damaged. My husband saw it and was worried. I never though to report it, I assumed this was user error.
justification: Although no injuries or damages occurred, the incident involved an unexpected and potentially dangerous flare-up, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
grill would not ignite,  as I was turning it off, it ignighted  the gas had settled in the cover and the grill flamed up with a big bang and full of flames. then went out.
hair on arm singed and face felt the extreme heat
justification: Injury occurred due to flames from the grill singeing hair on the arm, indicating a possible reoccurrence.

incident_description: Last May 2012 right after recieving our grill, it exploded in my face. It burnt half my hair, one eyebrow, and eyelashes on one eye. I checked all hook-ups and everything was normal. My husband had it happen to him twice since then, but was not injured. I checked online to see if anyone else had this problem, but there wasn't any information.
justification: The incident resulted in significant burns to the individual's face, including hair, eyebrow, and eyelashes, classifying it as an injury event. The lack of online reports suggests it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: After turning on the gas and igniting with the ignitor I thought the grill was on.  However, it seemed to have gone out.  I turned the knob back to "off" and when I did the gas ignited and burned my eyebrows, eyelashes, some of my hair and left a burning sensation on my entire face for many hours.
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected gas ignition when turning the knob to 'off'.

incident_description:
My product issue has been during normal use.  As I'm warming up my gas grill, or even during normal cooking, I have the control knobs turned to high.  When I go to turn the flames down from high the plastic control knobs are so hot that I have received 1st degree burns on my fingers.  This has happened to me on several occasions and has also happened to guests I have had over helping me cook on the grill. This Depends on the amount of time I have allowed the grill to warm up or the amount of time the food is cooking on high heat. There is also a "clean" feature on this grill that leaves the burners on for a lengthy period of time which also causes the knobs to get dangerously hot enough to cause burns. This has happened on several occasions and can longer use my product because of this HUGE liability of injury that this product has caused to me and my family.

In doing research I have found that the new model released in the last year has a design change that appears to remedy the issue I am currently having.  The knobs on my grill are very close to the grill surface and heat exit of lid therefore causing them to get to an extremely unsafe temperature.  The new model has these knobs moved significantly lower and further out from the grill/lid surface.  This appears to be a resolution to the safety condition I am experiencing.
justification: The grill's design allows control knobs to reach dangerously high temperatures, causing first-degree burns, which is a significant injury.

incident_description:
The caller stated that hose blew up in a balloon form and exploded in her face while she was watering her garden.  She did not receive any injuries but she is concerned that if a child was present there could have been injuries.

The consumer called the customer service number (973-287-5160) (date unknown). She was told that she would receive a return receipt by three different people. The consumer stated that she never received the receipt.

incident_description: I purchased a Kubota zero turn mower model ZG127s. On delivery there were bolts missing and broken off. the dealer was quick to offer replacement bolts. The bolts are cheap and are "cast" instead of grade A. On Sunday, 8/4/13 while mowing the lawn, the main bolt broke that controls the right steering. This resulted in an accident causing injury. This cheap cast bolt should not have been used in the manufacturing process. I took photos of the broken bolt and accident. When the bolt broke, I lost the ability to steer and control the speed resulting in a crash.

incident_description:

This incident could have caused seriously injury.

The caller attempted to contact the manufacturer but was unsuccessful.

Too much gas caused lid to flip open with a fire burst, which then broke our window. Brinkmann refuses to contact me via email or phone. Their customer service is non-exsistent. BBB and other website have many complaints as well.

incident_description: While cooking on a Weber Spirit grill it caught on fire and burned up the lines to the control panel on the right side and melted the control knobs.  The only way to stop it was to turn off the propane tank, which luckily I was able to do.  The grill is at least 4 to 5 years old but we have always taken care of it and cleaned it.  I would like to re-build it with new parts but have not found replacement parts online.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
The caller stated that gas grill out-take from the regulator is leaking.  He noticed this when he changed the propane tank and checked for leaks.  The leak is right at the junction of the hose and the regulator, he feels that there is a faulty seal on the regulator.

7/8/13  He contacted the manufacturer and he was informed that they had not receive any complaints on these regulators.

The regulator was not related to any recalls.

The caller feels that this regualtor is unsafe and should be reported.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
The grill manufacturer had sent a replacement regulator after I complained to them. I
installed the new unit, but unfortunately I discarded the defective regulator. I did however
retain a photograph of the defective unit. Please note that the red arrow in the photograph
points to where the leak was noted (i.e. on the right side of the white tape where the
connection goes from the tank into the regulator).
justification: Although no injury has occurred, the gas leak poses a significant risk of fire or explosion, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I purchased a "Pocket Hose" at a local store, set it up at an outdoor spigot, and used it for roughly a month and a half.  Three days ago, as I used the hose to water my garden, it exploded. A piece of the hose's internal clear, flexible plastic structure flew out of the hose and across the yard, (luckily) narrowly missing hitting my dog.  It occurred to me that this might be a problem for others, and a danger to not only users but also to anyone in the vicinity.  Given the nature of a hose, and its closeness to the ground, I am especially concerned for children and pets; although the velocity of the explosion was such that the piece of the internal hose could have flown anywhere.  The outer hose structure simply separated.  It looked as if the force of the exploding hose tore it apart, none of it was missing.
justification: The hose exploded, narrowly missing the user's dog, and could have caused injury if someone had been in its path.

incident_description:
This incident is concerning the Master Forge 5-Burner Gas Grill, model # L3218 sold by Lowes Home Improvement between September 2009 and November 2009, manufactured by the Sagittarius Sporting Goods of China. This first recall was "fixed" by using a longer regulator hose.

My second incident occurred approximately 4 years after the first .  The first incident was resolved by replacing the regulator hose with longer hose.

I was having problems with the grill to come up to temperature and noticed the flame from the burners were low.  Decided maybe the burners were clogged with spider webs or something.  Removed all the burners and cleaned out the bottom (which is rotting away and becoming another hazard).  Reassembled everything and turned on the grill.  

The temperature didn't come up.  So, this time I was going to attack the valve regulator as perhaps good ol spidey took shelter there as well.  Removing the regulator hose first, I noticed the end that goes to the valve regulators (the rubber part) was slightly melted.  

This is why my flame was low it was constricted from a melt down from a burner that was too hot as a result from poor construction of the unit. Albeit it was 4 years however, this "first fix" did not fix at all.  It seems there is a space (3/4") between the bottom (dripping area) of the grill and the area that the valve regulators go through into the burner (firebox) section. 

This space is only visible when lying on you back to replace the hose (if one's not injured by now) and not visible at all from viewing down.

I'm fairly handy when it comes to replacing the hose however, this is a race to see whether or not one does get injured by a unit that's still working, or one that haven't rusted out yet in 4 years.  My simple solution would be to have a thicker base for the firebox, and extend the connector for the regulator hose down and away from the flame source with a metal gas line.

Your original recall site was:

http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2010/Sagittarius-Sporting-Goods-Recalls-Gas-Grills-Sold-at-Lowes-Stores-Due-to-Fire-and-Burn-Hazards/

I've seen the original recall report and decided to add to this units' demise.  Never again for the imports.
justification: Potential for injury is high due to the melted regulator hose and the space between the grill's bottom and the valve regulators, which could cause a fire hazard.

incident_description:
On May 6, 2013 I took possession of a new Arien's 30" cut riding lawn mower. It performed fine for about 11 weeks but then the neutral gear would not stay locked. With motor running, neutralgear caused the mower to go forward. I contacted Home Depot and they gave me a work order for the mower to be picked up and taken to Home Depot's designated repair facility. July 18th,Thursday, the repair man came to pick up the mower. I directed him to my utility building, he started the mower, put it in reverse gear to back it out and it went forward.Now this is a small space and if he had not acted quickly it would have possibly taken out the wall of my

incident_description:
Submitted to Saferproducts.gov 16 Jul 2013

I originally purchased our mower in Indiana, on 14 Oct 2008 (nearly the end of the mowing season).  At that time our property was less than 1/5th acre. In Dec 2012 we moved to Ocala, Fl. and now have nearly an acre.  We also now have a 52" riding mower for the majority of work, and this mower is very lightly used in some small spaces around bushes and such. 

I have had nothing but problems with this mower since purchase. The latest problem (&last straw for this junk) was a catastrophic fuel leak which occurred 07-15-2013. The fuel tank appears to be designed as a two piece tank with a seam seperating the upper and lower halves.  

I used the mower 2 weeks ago with no incident, cleaned it up and put it away.  So after it sitting for two weeks with an empty tank I pulled it out of the garage. I then filled the tank and within 10 seconds discovered it was now leaking massively all along the seam on the side that faces the engine.

This incident involves the Toro 22" Recycler Lawn mower, Model 20067, Ser# 280031200
This mower uses the Briggs & Stratton (B&S) Engine Model 126T05, Type -0933-B-1, Code -07072756 and has the fuel tank is identified from original parts manual Ref# 972, PN 699374

This is clearly NOT limited to this mower model!!!!

Apparently Toro and B&S still haven't learned their lessons with this tank design.  Search Toro 20071 or 20073 fuel leak and you will see what I mean.  I don't believe Toro is 100% responsible but they continue to use this engine/design.  Apparently this tank is interchangeable to other B&S engines.  You can also search "699374 fuel leak" and find numerous complaints.  This has clearly been an ongoing problem since before my particular mower design.  The actions Toro and B&S have taken since 2007 have been insufficient this needs government intervention or a Class Action lawsuit before someone dies.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the catastrophic fuel leak poses a significant fire hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (severity level 2) with a high likelihood (4) of occurrence based on numerous similar complaints.

incident_description:
My Weber Spirit 210 grill caught on fire two weeks ago, 6/28/2013. It was not a grease fire. The fire was under the control knob area and the flames were coming out of the right rear area where the gas line enters. My father had been using the grill at our house the week before and mentioned he was worried about flames from the back.   I opened up the Weber after that, took out the grate, flavorizer bars (they are both new this year) and looked around for any debris, etc.  I also had cleaned the grease pan and ensured nothing was in there.

I had lit the grill and was playing with our dog for a minute.  As it was still coming up to temperature, I went in side for ~5 mins, when I came out flamers were coming out of the back right area of the grill (under the control knob table and the back knob had already started to melt.  I quickly reached under, avoiding the flames and turned off the gas at the tank. The flames went out in the grill when the gas was shut off, but one of the knobs was actually on fire. Fortunately, I saw the fire before it burned through the gas supply hose. The fire burned the control knobs, the ignition wiring and it appears to have scorched the gas supply hose from the gas fuel tank. 

I contacted Weber and they asked me to send photos, which I have done. I am concerned that this is a safety issue that could result in a home fire, or possibly an explosion if other consumers experience the same issue.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire could have spread and caused property damage, making it an incident.

incident_description:
I purchased a CharBroil Patio Bistro TRU-Infrared Gas Grill (Model 126015 Series) from The Home Depot online that was delivered to my home on/about June 6, 2013. Upon opening the packing box and before assembling the unit, I noticed that the valve was not correctly positioned inside the burner tube (where the valve coming from the gas supply meets the aerated burner tube which then leads into the kettle)  I carefully but firmly repositioned the two parts into the correct position.  There is no hard connecting point here, just a matter of positioning the two gas lines to ensure proper gas flow.  THIS IS NOT COVERED IN THE ASSEMBLY GUIDE OR THE GRILLING GUIDE THAT CAME WITH THE PRODUCT, HOWEVER, AND IS ONLY MENTIONED IN THE PRODUCT GUIDE UNDER THE SECTION ON "CLEANING THE BURNER ASSEMBLY" ON PAGE 9.  THE CONSUMER SHOULD BE EXPRESSLY WARNED TO CHECK THIS PARTICULAR VALVE/BURNER TUBE ASSEMBLY EACH TIME THE GRILL IS USED AND SHOULD BE WARNED OF THE DISTINCT POSSIBILITY OF A SEVERE AND INTENSE FIRE.

 Problem 1:  An inexperienced assembler would not necessarily notice that the valve was not positioned correctly into the burner tube while unpacking the unit from the original box which was exactly the situation I faced.  I suspect the proper alignment was dislodged during routine handling and shipping.  That misalignment can produce a serious fire hazard WHICH I LEARNED THE HARD WAY SHORTLY AFTERWARD (see next paragraph).

 

After first assembling the grill per the Assembly Guide and connecting a new 20# propane tank, I used the grill on 3 or 4 occasions during the remainder of June without any problems.  The assembly worked perfectly and the grill lived up to the good reviews we had read.
However, on July 4th, I gently moved the grill approximately one foot (the grill is equipped with wheels for the express purpose of moving it) to make room for other items on our rear deck and prepared for a family cookout.  UNBEKNOWNST TO ME, the valve/burner tube "fitting" described above became dislodged.  I started the grill with the electronic igniter and brought the grill up to cooking temperature per the instructions .  I left the grill for appromixately 2-3 minutes to bring food from the kitchen to the deck to cook.  As I was loading my first food items, I realized that an intense fireball, approximately 6 inches in diameter, was roaring directly under the heat control unit and coming from valve/burner tube assembly area.  The fire had already severely damaged the control assembly, had burned through the igniter wires, and was rapidly devouring the gas supply line from the propane tank.    I first grabbed the burner controller which had already warped from the heat and was "frozen" in place (i.e., useless at this point) and then immediately reached underneath the fireball to turn off the gas from the tank (praying that the fire wouldn't reach the propane tank itself).  The grill and fully charged propane tank were less than 15 feet from the back door to my home and family during this episode.

 Needless to say, the grill is now ruined.  The gas feeder hose from the tank, the entire control assembly,and the igniter assembly are completely burned and unusable.  I do not trust this grill and will not have it near my family in the future.

 Problem 2:  Even an experienced person may not know how to control or extinguish a fire that can start so easily and was caused simply by moving the grill one foot and inadvertantly jostling a critical mating of gas lines (again there is no hard connection; the two lines are simply nestled together).    The engineering of this connection should be examined and changed.  Clear warnings of possible fire based on my very real expereince should be provided to the consumer.



I have contacted the Arlington County, Virginia, Fire Department/Fire Prevention Unit and am copying their representative on this email.  I am also submitting a copy of this communciation and reporting this incident to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission  U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission using their online reporting system (the action being taken here). 


I have asked The Home Depot to have a Customer Service Representative contact me to discuss how best to return my burned out yet "still new" grill.  I am equally concerned that other consumers be made aware of this dangerous situation which in my case became a real incident even when I followed all published safety procedures.  I will henceforth check the valve/burner supply connection before each use with any grill that I purchase and use in the future.

 

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and could have caused injury, given the proximity of the grill to the home and family.

On Saturday, July 6, 2013 we used our new weber grill for only the 4th time since purchase from Lowes in Egg Harbor Twsp, NJ on May 25, 2013.  

We turned it on, the automatic igniter lit and we let it warm up for about 2 minutes.
Upon putting 2 steaks on the grill, the entire grill became engulfed in flames.
The fire was shooting out from under the grill where the b ase of the burners were located and where the propane tank was stored.  Meanwhile  the steaks were located on the grill and the fire shot out the sides of the grill......it was not a grease fire.

The fire began burning a coating of metal material from inside the grill which emitted billowing gray smoke for at least 5 minutes. It was noxious.

It billowed into the neighborhood and made me sick.   A friend ran forward and turned off the propane using the knob located on the front. I thought the grill was going to explode on my deck and kill us.My husband said the temperature gauge was at the manimum of 600 degrees. It could have been hotter.

After the supply to the propane was shut off, the grey smoke continued to billow out.

Upon cooling, I noticed the inside of the grill which was supposed to be stainless steel was turned a medium brown color which did not rub off like soot.

I read tonight online that the grill grates are coated with something to promote flavor.Whatever that was it is completely burned off.

I was really scared and have owned a grill for 40 years. This type of incident has never happened.

The design of the grill is such that there is no bottom to the housing...essentially the housing consists of 2 sides and a lid which you pull shut   With no iron or other metal barrier between the propane tank and the burners directly above - the grill looks like a fire hazard. There are 3 removable teepe shaped metal parts which are to be cleaned periodically located directly under the burners. These were covered black.

Again the material burning and billowing out gray smoke was not grease from new steaks just put on.

Thank you for listening. 
[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the severe fire and billowing smoke pose a significant risk, making this a level 2 incident with a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The main blade bolt sheared off my lawn mower this morning and the blade came loose while I was mowing my lawn. How exciting.  Even though I was not struck by the flying blade, I am quite glad I always wear steel-toe boots when mowing.

Looks like my MTD lawn mower (model 11A-549Q755 (2008)) had a defective "blade adapter" - the cast iron part above the blade which allows mounting the blade to the motor shaft. 

The blade adapter is missing a big chunk out of one side - from the discoloration, the chunk was missing when it was originally installed. This appears to be an original casting defect - when the part was cast, it cracked and this part came off. The defective blade adapter was installed anyway instead of rejected. This missing chunk looks to be very important for securing the blade to the shaft. Without a properly functioning adapter, much more force is imparted on the blade bolt itself. It was inevitable that the bolt would eventually shear.

The assembly is such that this defect is not visible when the mower is assembled, or even during normal blade removal/replacement.

Fortunately, I was not hurt in this incident. However, mower blades detaching at full speed represent a real hazard.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm due to the blade detaching at full speed.

incident_description:

incident_description:

I have had this problem on this grill on two occasions.  

With a mild breeze coming in from the backside of the unit the controls on the front panel get hot enough to burn the fingers, hot enough to melt the knobs and trim and the electric igniter gets so hot that it has exploded.  The explosion is the result of the battery inside overheating.  The explosion cause the parts of the igniter to be shot directly into the face of the operator.

I replaced these parts once but the problem reoccurred.  I just spoke to the manufacturer and their response is to not use the grill in the presence of wind.  This is an outdoor device and there is always the possibility of a breeze outdoors.  I have another similar grill from another manufacturer that does not have this problem since it incorporates a simple heat shield between the burners and the controls.

incident_description:
My 9 year old granddaughter, while using the hose to water plants, was struck violently by the hose on her upper
left arm when the hose separated at its terminal end at the junction with the plastic threaded connector (See
photos). The action was so violent that the severed end or the threaded connector cut the skin in two places and
caused whelps and bruises on the skin in 5 places (See photos). She was using the hose normally under my
supervision at the time. She immediately screamed in pain. As she refused to move her arm and concerned about a
sprain or torn ligament, I called her father, a physician, requesting he observe her injuries. He purchased pain
medication in child dosage strength and gave it to her. He also recommended ice packs and a topical anti-bacterial
ointment with pain relief ingredients.
The hose was being used as intended and normal for a water hose. Our water service is provided by a municipal
water supply, not self regulated by a private well. Our water pressure is considered good or very good, but not
unsafe. The hose had been stored loosely coiled on the porch in the shade immediately prior to use.
Any reasonable person, after reviewing the facts of this incident, would be concerned about similar injuries or the
real potential for eye injury if the hose was used at or above face level, as is done while watering hanging baskets or
washing windows. To quate my granddaughter, "They should stop selling those things!".
justification: The incident resulted in visible injuries and pain, warranting medical attention.

incident_description: On June 27, 2013, I opened the lid of my Fiesta outdoor gas barbecue/grill, lit it, and closed the lid to allow it to preheat. I have done this numerous times since purchasing it two months earlier. However, this time, when I returned five minutes later, I grabbed the handle to open the lid and instead the handle came off in my hand. The plastic on the handle melted at the two ends that attach to the grill lid. Additionally, there was melted plastic on the screws that are supposed to hold the handle in place.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the handle coming off and plastic melting indicates a malfunction, making it possible but not likely to happen again.

incident_description:
I'd like to alert you to a defective and potentially dangerous product. 

I purchased a very expensive ($3,000+) Capital Cooking Outdoor Grill. Several times the igniters have burnt out and even the plastic coating on the electrical wires leading to them have been totally burnt off due to inadequate insulation between the grills themselves and the igniters. The igniters have been replaced twice but the company refuses to correct the problem. The danger comes from the fact that gas does not ignite and there is the real potential for an explosion. Furthermore the knobs at the front of the grill become so hot that they cannot be touched without an insulated glove and in fact I have burned my fingers twice.

I have had several discussions with the president of the company however his response is that the grill must have a surround built around it. I have owned a few other far less expensive grills and never had this problem. I though you should know so that you can test this make yourself and alert your readers to this deficiency and danger.
justification: The grill's inadequate insulation and overheating knobs have caused burns, posing a high likelihood of severe injury or explosion.

incident_description:
In mid-May, I was making steaks on my new Jenn-Air gas barbecue. I put the steaks on and walked back into the house to check on the rice. When I returned, literally minutes later, the patio was full of smoke and there were flames shooting out of the barbecue.

I went to shut off the gas burners, but they had become so hot you couldn't touch them without a hot pad. Worse, the controls inside them had apparently melted -- the nobs spun like [REDACTED]'s head in [REDACTED]. 

Fortunately, I have my gas shut-off valve right next to the barbecue, so I didn't have to call the fire department. But it was tense.

Still, I would have thought it was some weird anomaly if the company had responded differently when I called to report the problem. Instead, when I told them the barbecue had imploded, they started asking questions: How much ventilation is it getting?  Can you send photos of how the BBQ is set up -- from every side? etc.... 

When I asked what was up, they said: Well, if its not well ventilated, the heat can go down through the back and out the front....burning through the mechanism. In other words, this has happened before. So I started searching for complaints about this BBQ. I couldn't find the exact model number, but this struck me as interesting, since the second review came so close to what happened to me: http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/home-garden/lawn-garden/gas-grills/gas-grill-ratings/models/overview/jenn-air-720-0709-sams-club-99030943.htm
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved significant property damage and could have escalated due to the malfunctioning controls.

incident_description:

 began leaking gas. incident_description:
June 3, 2013: 

 I was preparing lawn equipment prior to using it.  This incident occurred while plugging in and securing the power cord in the B & D GH3000 trimmer. The unit has a handle to use during operation.  

The additional handle is where the power cord is inserted and secured in cord retainer, both housed in the same area as the trigger switch. I was in the process of inserting cord and securing it in the cord retainer. As I attempted to push the electrical cord into the cord retainer, the cord bumped the trigger switch and activated the trimmer. 

It is not possible to secure the cord in cord retainer without using two hands. One to hold the handle and one to pull cord through. It is not possible to insert cord into handle and pull back in order for it to secure in cord retainer.  One hand needs to hold handle while other hand needs to secure cord to cord retainer.

The trigger switch should not have been housed in the same area as cord retainer.  There is not enough room to effectively attach cord without hitting the trigger with a hand or the electrical cord.

Upon activation, the trimmer seriously damaged my foot.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury (foot damage) and the likelihood of it happening again is high due to the poor design of the trimmer.

incident_description: I was cleaning up my grill. After removing the plates and the drip catcher, I saw some oil (grilled salmon with olive oil) had spilled on my counter. I ran my dish cloth underneath the grill and my right ring finger made contact with a plastic piece under the grill that has an opening. The edges of the plastic are sharp and I cut my knuckle. The cut is approximately 1/8 of an inch deep and it was hard to get the bleeding to stop due to being on the knuckle.
justification: Injury occurred due to sharp edges of plastic piece under the grill, which is a possible scenario during grill cleaning.

incident_description:
The consumer says that when she lit the grill the burners shot up flames rapid and went out.  She says that the burners are burned to a crisp.  She says that she originally thought that the propane may have been set to high but was not the case.  

The consumer says that her product is experiencing the same thing as listed in the recall for this brand (Release #08-359).  She has the same model listed, but the date code is not.  When contacting Lowe's she was told they were not aware and had not heard anything about it.  

The consumer also said that she is never able to reach the manufacturer at the number listed in the recall.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a rapid flame-up and potential equipment damage, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description:
After filling the weedwacker with the proper gas/oil mix, I started it and began using.  Within 3-5 minutes, I noticed gas running out the back of the product and the engine was smoking where the gas hit the hot parts of the engine.  I immediately turned it off and noticed that the gas tank was empty.  The next day I examined the product and found that the plastic fuel lines had disintegrated into pieces the size of grains of sand and rice, leaving the two hole where they had been now open to the engine assembly. 

Contacting Sears about this, I was informed that the product was out of warranty (purchased 11/2010 and used only four times) and thus I could send it in for repair (60-80% of new product) or buy parts and repair it myself.  I assured them that the product had been stored properly with gas in the tank and that there must be a design or materials flaw.  They said sorry the product was out of warranty.

Clearly, I will be buying another brand replacement product, but given the danger of fire or even explosion, I felt I should report this since Sears did not either know or deem it important.
justification: Potential fire or explosion hazard due to fuel line disintegration, though no immediate injury reported.

incident_description:

Today I was watering my garden using a standard hand sprayer and the hose exploded within a 1.5 feet of the sprayer.  The explosion caused injurty to both of my legs.  The injuries didn't require medical attention but they're very painful.
  My grandchildren (4 and 6 years of age) like to help me water the garden.  They could have been severely injured if it had happened to them.
justification: The hose exploded causing injuries, though not severe, and could have been catastrophic if grandchildren were involved.

I am still able to use the left side of the grill but the left side is destroyed.  I am know trying to decide if I want to replace the parts on the left side or buy a new grill. incident_description:
PRODUCT:  Weber Charcoal Grill with glass filled nylon handle on lid.
While the instructions (fine print) instruct one to use a mitt, I think reasonable person would assume that the handle provides some insulating value.  It does not.  I touched it lightly and dropped the lid but burned my fingertips.  If someone gripped it tightly without a mitt (seemingly impossible based on space limitations), a serious burn would be the result.  In the past, the metal handles were covered with wood.  I don't believe the average consumer is going to realize that the glass filled nylon handles are heat conductors.

incident_description:
I purchased a used Craftsman Cultivator garden tiller.  When I asked to have the unit started, it ran ok, but was leaking gasoline from under the fuel tank.  I purchased it anyway, thinking that it was probably a fuel line issue that could be replaced easily.

When I removed the air cleaner, I found that the carburetor had a small "L" shaped plastic connector that the gas line connected to from the fuel tank.  The plastic connector was cracked and leaking gas.

I talked to eight SearsÃÂs representatives, a [REDACTED] representative, which by the way was an error by the Sears contact directing me incorrectly, the Company that bought Tecumseh, who manufactured the 2cycle engine (Certified Parts Corp), a distributor in Arkansas (Carswell) that sells Tecumseh engine parts to the open market and a wholesale supplier of Tecumseh parts in Wisconsin.

In talking to all of these representatives, I finally discovered that sometime between 2008 and 2013, either Sears or Tecumseh or both, discovered the engineering flaw in the plastic fuel line connection and reengineered the carburetor with a brass tube, eliminating the plastic connector, to connect the fuel line from the gas tank.

Sears stated that there had not been a recall and since I was the second owner, they would do nothing to provide a replace carburetor with the new brass tube connection, even though it is a dangerous safety issue.  I could purchase a replacement carburetor for $61.00 plus shipping if I wanted to correct the problem.

The model number of the Craftsman Cultivator is Model #536.292522 with a manufacturing date of 2008.  The original carburetor is listed in the owner manual as Part #640231.  The plastic connector is not available as a single purchase.  You have to purchase the entire carburetor which is now Part #640231A.  Please note that the reengineered carburetor has the same part number except the number now contains an "A" which indicates a modification to the original unit.

By not letting previous owners know about the risk of a fire from leaking gasoline or possibly exploding of the gas tank, it puts anyone who purchased one of these units from Sears a risk of serious burns or death.
justification: The cracked plastic fuel line connector poses a high risk of fire or explosion, potentially leading to serious burns or death.

incident_description:
On the morning of 04/18/13, we found one of our cats in critical condition near our fish pond (about 160 gallons). In
addition to obvious pain and little ability to move, we noticed his front legs were soaking wet. We took him to a vet (Monte
Vista Vet Clinic in Turlock, CA}. The vet examined the cat, told us that evidence on his tongue indicated electrocution and
that he should be euthanized because his organs were shutting down. We had him euthanized. Upon returning home, I
took a voltmeter and stuck one probe in the pond water and one in the surrounding dirt and read 1 volt. The voltage
disappeared when the pump was unplugged and no voltage was read when a different pump was substituted for the
apparently faulty pump. My suspicion is that the pump had a wiring issue and the cat while drinking water slipped and his
paws touched the case resulting somehow in a circuit that electrocuted him. I have contacted the pump company
(Danner or Pondmaster) and their response has basically been that a warning is present on the pump that it needs to be
unplugged before it is touched and it needed to be plugged into a ground fault receptacle. It was plugged into a ground
fault receptacle and to me this is unsatisfactory anyway as some people are not going to heed warnings like this. The
wiring in the pump should not be cabable of failing. I have included the series of e-mails with this attachment.
justification: Cat's death due to electrocution from a faulty pump, which could have been prevented with better product design.

incident_description:
My concerns are in regard to the Char-Broil Gas Patio Bistro, model #12601558. 

I would categorize two safety concerns with this bbq. The first is the cooking grill. It is a stainless steel accordian/fan type design with small perforated holes. While it's not completely solid it is enough that it traps propane underneath it if the flame goes out and the knob on the bbq is still on. You also can't see enough through the grill to see if the flame/element is lit which is also tricky when trying to ensure that it's lit or not. 
The second concern is the design of the controls on the knob. To turn off the gas flow into the bbq with its knob, you have to go by the ignition setting. So what has happened to me on 3 different occasions is that I'm pre-heating the grill, I go out and see/feel that it's not heating, so I turn the knob off, and it just hits the ignitor enough to explode the trapped propane. While I've been fortunate not to have been burned, I have lost some facial and forearm hair. When this happens it also projects the cooking grill from the bbq.
justification: The incident has caused injury, with hair loss reported, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the repeated incidents.
