The top cover is plastic and heat of exhaust will also destroy it, defeating the safety of the hand guard that is attached.
For information, this muffler is sold as a replacement for several models and also for some Husqvarna chain saws.
justification: The defective muffler design could cause the plastic top cover to melt, potentially leading to burns or injuries.

incident_description:
Caller and his wife had cooked a variety of meats on Sunday, April 7th, 2013 then sat down to eat after turning the burners and the gas line off.
They had been sitting down for approximately five minutes when they looked at the grill and saw thick black smoke coming from what seemed to be everywhere from under the lid.
Caller opened the grill top, observed that the grill itself was on fire with metal dripping into the drip pan.
He rushed downstairs to turn off valve from that location because all was already turned off a the grill location.
He opened the doors below the grill to air out and this assisted with the extinguishing of the fire.

The grill is melted under the grilling service at the "flavor bars" (upside down V) where they meet the grill.

Consumer contacted the manufacturer Monday, April 8th, 2013, he spoke with Customer Service Representative [REDACTED] who offered to send replacement parts but caller advised her that he didn't believe this would resolve the problem.
[REDACTED] transferred the information to her supervisor, [REDACTED] who contacted the consumer after viewing pictures that he sent to [REDACTED] and advised him that she could tell by the pictures that he had not cleaned the grill appropriately and that the fire was basically his fault.
His response to this was that the grill shouldn't have melted and it wasn't what was in the grill that was on fire but the grill itself.
He cleans the grill each time before he cooks again and he and his wife grill fairly often.
There were no injuries
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: Discovered a sump pump in our basement last evening around 9 pm on fire at the switch mechanism.  Reported it to the manufacturer via email and phone. Finally reached them on the phone and they were rude and hung up.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a fire, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
(04/01/2013) The consumer stated that he assembled the cart. During the assembly he became very dizzy and nauseated by the the smell coming from the plastic that the product is made out of . He stated that it is a very strong chemical smell. He took the product outside. The consumer stated that he remained dizzy for hours. He stated that it took him about five hours to come back to earth. He stated that he did not seek medical help. He was home alone so it only affected him.

The consumer stated that he will make another attempt to get in touch with the manufacturer.
justification: The consumer experienced discomfort but no injury, and the likelihood of such an incident occurring again is possible given the product's strong chemical smell.

incident_description: On Nov. 21, 2012 Consumer was using an electric Sears brand leaf blower (purchased Oct. 6, 2012) believed to be 12 AMP ELECTRIC BLOWER/MULCHER WITH METAL IMPELLER, Model No. 138.74899. (The brand was not [REDACTED].) As Consumer started to move blower from right hand to her left, the blower motor sound suddenly changed and was described as starting to "slip" or "skip." Almost immediately (with the blower about two inches from her left hand, while still held in her right hand), the shield shattered and seriously injured Consumer's left hand. The injury required eleven stitches to the middle and ring fingers. The injury was described in the orthopedic hand surgeon's notes as "Crush laceration of left middle and ring pulp tissues with nail plates intact."
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring stitches, but not death, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the age of the product and its usage.

incident_description:
A window mounted pellet stove being utilized in a home failed, causing a fire that damaged the house and resulted in one adult female occupant sustaining smoke inhalation. The woman was alerted to the fire when smoke alarms activated and she then called the fire department. Firefighters quickly extinguished the flames and the damaged pellet stove was left in place. The occupant was transported to a local hospital, treated, and released.  

Maine State Fire Marshal's Case #: [REDACTED]. The SFM report is pending and photographs of the incident scene were taken.
justification: Injury occurred due to smoke inhalation, but not life-threatening; occurrence likelihood is possible given the use of a pellet stove and potential for fire.

incident_description:
The caller stated that he owns the snowblower for 2 years, however, about 2 weeks ago it started leaking gas from the carburetor.  (3/25/13) He contacted the manufacturer who informed him to take it to a local dealer.  The dealer advised him that the blower was out of warranty and that his model was not part of a recall.  The cost of repairs would be at his own expense.

The caller feels that he is experiencing problems as Release #11-207.  Hazard: The carburetors on both products develop fuel leaks and can ignite when exposed to an ignition source, posing a fire or burn hazard.
justification: While no incident has occurred yet, the potential for a fire hazard exists due to the fuel leak, making it possible but not certain.

incident_description:
I pulled out my Ryobi [weed trimmer] to use this spring.  Filled it with gas and tried to start it.
After 3 pulls the thing caught fire!
Lucky I was outside and near a hose after inspecting it I noticed the fuel lines used are not of fuel grade quality. 
I had to purchase a new fuel take to replace the lines and inspecting the old and new tanks neither are very safe, there are just holes drilled into the tank for the fuel lines to come out. No seal and they can leak fuel at any givin time.
After getting it running and cutting weeds I smelled gas and it caught fire again this time the fuel primer bulb cracked leaking gas on the hor cylinder head causing fire.
The primer bulb does not appear to be of fuel grade material either and to replace it Ryobi says I have to buy a brand new carb.
justification: The incident occurred twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: WEEDEATER ONE RIDING MOWER-MODEL WE261- THE STEERING SPINDLE BREAKS SHORTLY AFTER BEING OPERATED REPEATEDLY CAUSING THE RIDER TO BE UNABLE TO STEER. BRAKES ARE FAILING REPEATEDLY AND TRANSMISSIONS ARE FAILING REPEATEDLY. THIS IS THE WORST ENGINEERED AND UNSAFEST RIDING MOWER ON THE MARKET. ALL OF THE ABOVE HAS HAPPENED TO ME OVER THE PAST 2 YEARS. IF YOU SEARCH ONLINE YOU WILL FIND THIS IS HAPPENING TO VERY MANY OWNERS. WEEDEATER (HUSQVARNA) HAS DONE NOTHING TO IMPROVE THESE SAFETY ISSUES. ACTION NEEDS TO BE TAKEN TO FORCE A RECALL.
justification: Repeated failures of steering, brakes, and transmissions pose a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her husband was using his 22 tons vertical horizontal log splitter and did not noticed that there was a bolt sticking out approximately 1 inch. The consumer stated that it was one of the bolts that held the wedge to the cylinder. The consumer stated that the bolt was describe as a ÃÂ½ inch by 3 1/4 inch GR5 hex Cap bolt, with a lock washer and ÃÂ½ inch hex nut. The consumer stated that his fingers become stuck when the wedge came down and it mashed the left thumb between the bolt and the log. 

The consumer stated that he mashed his left thumb and experienced one large laceration. The consumer stated that her husband was seen by a medical professional, but did not have to be admitted to the hospital. The consumer stated that stated that he had approximately 6 stitches on his thumb. The consumer stated that the doctor placed him on anti-biotic and wrapped his thumb. The consumer stated that he visited the hand specialist on April 1, 2013 has a follow up on Monday April 8, 2013. 

The consumer stated that she believes that this product was poorly designed and any consumers can amputate their fingers. 

The consumer stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report. 

The consumer believes this product should be investigated do to the safety hazard that it poses to the consumers.
justification: Injury occurred due to a design flaw, and the likelihood of similar incidents is high given the product's widespread use.

incident_description:
We purchased a new 21-hp Craftsman riding lawn tractor from sears.  THe first time I started the engine and put it into gear, there was a terrible grating sound coming from the rear axle.  After driving the tractor 25 feet and parking it in my garage I turned off the engine and lifted up the seat to see if I could spot an obvious problem.  I found that the box which holds the battery in place had broken.  the box, and the battery were now resting on top of a pully/fan above the rear axle.

When I pulled the battery out, I found that the bottom of the battery was all wet.  The pully/fan that the battery was resting on had rubbed through the plastic box and the wall of the battery.  My hands were covered with battery acid.  This resulted in a minor chemical burn with itching and redness on my hands.

This product needs to be redesigned with a more durable battery retention system and the battery needs to be relocated to a spot where if the retention system fails, the battery will not fall onto moving parts.
justification: Injury occurred due to battery acid exposure when the battery retention system failed, making the likelihood of a similar incident high.

incident_description: We bought 2 identical patio heaters thru Home Depot several months ago. We used them in late fall of 2012 right after purchase and then decided to use again in early spring of 2013. The gas regulator (model AZF), part # 1124 began spewing gas with hissing sound. We turned them off. The patio heaters did not ignite via pilot and we decided not to continue trying since it did not sound safe. The model of the patio Heater is HSS-A-SS, manufactured by Jiangsu Gardensun Furnace Company, LTD; made in China. We searched for that part and found out that there was a recall on it but associated wit the Stok grills; they use the same gas regulator. We need 2 new gas regulators that are safe to use because we want to continue using our patio gas heaters.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the gas regulator spewing gas poses a significant fire hazard.

incident_description:
I got a George Foreman  360 Electric Nonstick Round-Shaped Grill with 5 Interchangeable Grill Plates as a gift but the first time I tried to use it, the hot plates came flying off when I opened it. This grill has interchangeable plates which attach on the top and bottom. These are heavy, metal plates, but they don't secure properly. I saw many complaints of the same problem on amazon as these grills are still for sale. I got mine in 2010, but I haven't used it and since it was a gift I couldn't return it.

Here are the amazon reviews: http://www.amazon.com/George-Foreman-GRP106QPGR-Round-Shaped-Interchangeable/product-reviews/B001G8Y3R6/ref=pr_all_summary_cm_cr_acr_txt?ie=UTF8&showViewpoints=1
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction where hot plates flew off, posing a risk of injury, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an OSH brand pump sprayer that was made by the Hudson Company. I phoned the Hudson company yesterday (1-800-977-7293) to say that I have twice been sprayed in the face with [REDACTED] because the pump design makes it all too easy to allow the tank pressure to escape from the top of the unit. The rep I spoke with said it is a "good" unit and that I must not be securing the top tightly enough. I assured her that I had, but she continued to insist it was something I was doing incorrectly. She told me I could take the sprayer back to OSH for a refund, but I feel this design problem is serious enough that someone should look into it.

The product is the "OSH 2 in 1 Garden & Deck Premium Sprayer" Model number 23481.

The instructions say not to use the sprayer with your face or body over the pump, but there is no way to pressurize the pump unless you are. I have used many different pump brads over many, many years and have never had this problem. I am hoping someone can test this product to see if I just bought a lemon, or if there is something wrong with the overall design - which I believe to be the case. To tighten the pump, you turn it clockwise, but then to engage the pump, you have to turn it counter-clockwise. If you turn it just a fraction too far, however, you release the pressure in the tank and the liquid in the tank comes up in your face.

 I'm not going to return this unit to OSH until I hear from you.
justification: The user has experienced two incidents of being sprayed in the face, indicating a likely design flaw.

incident_description: Gas regulator on my Stok Quatro grill last pressure to grill and was leaking causing a slight back flash (fire) under grill.  As soon as leaking fuel burned (1 sec burst) the fire was out, however the regulator continued to give low pressure to the grill and leaked.  I turned the gas bottle off and the regulator off and when opened up it continued to leak.  When I went to Home Depot to buy a new regulator I found that there is a recall,  I have called the manufacture today and they want to pick up this regulator by FedEx next Thursday and when they receive it will ship a new one.  I would have much rather just been able to buy one and noted the recall issue.
justification: While the initial fire was brief and caused no injury, the recurring leak poses a significant risk of future incidents.

incident_description:
No injuries sustained.  I was mowing my lawn with a troy-bilt lawn tractor when all of a sudden it caught fire.  The wind was blowing very strong and before I could get a shovel to try and put the fire out it had grown stronger and had caught my lawn on fire.  I had to call 911 to get assistance to put the fire out.  The mower was a total loss and the yard was burnt.

Troy-bilt lawn tractor
model:  288804
serial number:  3912611483
I had purchase the mower new and had used it 3 summers.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) on the severity scale. The occurrence likelihood is rated 'Possible' (Level 3) as lawn mower fires, while rare, can happen due to various reasons such as mechanical failure or, as in this case, strong winds.

incident_description: Upon opening my garage to use my car I smelled a strong gas odor. After investigating I found gas leaking from the carburetor or my Toro CCR3650 snowblower. I removed the cover to inspect the leak and found a plastic carburetor the was leaking from the bowl area. I know that Toro has a recall going on for a different model but I believe this is the same issue on the model I have. I know that the replacement carburetor is not available and has a metal carburetor listed as a replacement. If indeed it is a design defect then I believe Toro should provide a new carburetor. As right now my snowblower is unusable unless I pay $125 for the replacement metal carburetor. Luckily I did not run the snowblower and found the leak first. The model number for my snowblower is 38518 and the serial number is 260005252. After searching for fuel leaks on the internet I have found many complaints for this carburetor with the needle valve design being prone to sticking open causing a fuel leak.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a significant gas leak, posing a high risk of fire or explosion.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she and her husband were experiencing low heart rates and low blood pressure. The consumer stated that they both went to the doctors and they could not find the reason why they were experiencing low heart rates. The consumer stated that after visiting the doctorÃÂs several times she started to discuss her health with her neighbor   and found that she was experiencing the same symptoms. 

The consumer stated that they were discussing what they had in common in their homes and found that they both used insects and rodent control electrical devices. She stated that they decided to remove them from their home and found that after 5 days there symptoms had decrease and their heart rates were back to normal. 

The consumer stated that she believes that the electrical current that these products send across the home affects the health of the people living in the home. The consumer stated that she believes these products should be investigated do to the safety hazard that this products pose to the consumer. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and was waiting for a response.
justification: Potential health impact, as evidenced by multiple individuals experiencing similar symptoms.

incident_description:
Consumer was in his garage and began to smell a gas odor. He checked his vehicles but did not see any leaks. He then saw his snow blower which was laying on the ground drip gas. The snow blower drained out about 1/4 of a gallon of gas and left an 8 inch" drip spot on the ground. 
The snow blower has only been used about a total of 4 times. 

The consumer placed an oil pan under the snow blower to catch the gas. The tank for the snow blower is now empty but the oil pan is still under the blower for safety measures. 

3/6/2013- Consumer contacted the manufacturer via email but has not spoken with anyone as of yet. He intends on contacting them today via telephone. 
Consumer has not contacted the retailer and does not intend on doing so. 

There are no injuries or damages to report.
justification: No injuries or damages reported, but potential for future incidents due to snow blower gas leak.

incident_description: (01/04/2013) The consumer stated that she tried to unplug the unit to plug it into another outlet. She stated that she could not remove it. She stated that she felt the marble tile wall around the outlet, as well as the outlet itself. It felt warm to the touch. The consumer cut the power for the outlet at the circuit breaker. The consumer called her electrician but it was late in the day. She left a message. She called back early Saturday morning (01/05/2013)/. The electrician was there within 20 minutes. The electrician had to cut the wires to remove the unit. He cut the plate out of the wall. The metal prong had melted into the plastic of the outlet. The unit had been plugged into this outlet for about seven or eight months.  The electrician checked to see if there any burn damage in the electrician box for the outlet. There was no damage. The electrician had to cut the electrical wire where it had burned.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident could have led to injury due to the outlet overheating and melting.

incident_description: I own a Weber 310 natural gas grill. Several times when I put the Weber grill cover back on the unit, it bumps the burner knobs and turns the gas on. This has happened three times since owning the grill. This last time it was on for over 24 hours. It's winter and I just happened to go out back where the grill is and got a strong odor of gas. I called Weber and they said it is not a manufacturing defect. While it not be a defect, it certainly is a safety problem. The knobs turn very easy. There is no locked position. My past grill, it was required to push down to unlock and then turn. These just turn and once the cover is on there is no way to tell if the burners are on. Weber says to turn off my natural gas supply to the grill when it's not in use. While this is the fix to stay safe, it is not practical.
justification: The grill's burner knobs can be easily turned on by the cover, posing a high likelihood of gas leaks, as evidenced by the incident occurring three times.

incident_description: I noticed a smell of gas in the bed of my pickup and discovered gas was dripping from my chain saw.
justification: Gas dripping from the chainsaw poses a risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: REDI SET GO COOKER OVERHEATED AND MELTED THE TIMER KNOB ON THE FIRST UNIT. REPLACEMENT UNIT SENT AND IT ALSO OVERHEATED WHEN THE TIMER QUIT WORKING. IF LEFT UNATTENDED IT WILL MOST LIKELY CATCH FIRE.
justification: Overheating incidents occurred twice consecutively, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and potential fire if unattended.

incident_description:
This is a report on a Streamlight TwinTask 2L. 

Wednesday night, January 23, 2013 I took it with me on a walk and it was not working right.  The next morning (yesterday) I changed the 2 lithium batteries because they tested below 2 volts.  I had 3 fresh [REDACTED] batteries & tested them before inserting them, 1 was under 3v, the other 2 were good & I put the good ones in the light.

This is a 3 stage light ÃÂ switch on once to get bright setting, click again & get that bulb + 3 LEDs or again & LEDs only. The first 2 stages are what quit working; the LEDs worked.  When I tested the batteries I thought the LEDs might have required less power thus they kept working.  But as the bright bulb didnÃÂt light when I replaced the batteries I figured that the bright bulb could have burned out ÃÂ or that the switch was bad. 
  
I brought the light w/new batteries to the office, put it on my desk. Late afternoon I checked it again, LEDs would only come on very faintly (indicating to me that something had drained the batteries since I installed them).  I went to StreamlightÃÂs website. Saw that this light is discontinued, but I sent an email about having it tested/repaired/replaced. 

About 30-45 minutes later I was on the phone at my desk when it went "bam" and shot a 12" flame out the switch hole and kept burning like a flame thrower.  Though the flame shrunk within seconds several papers on my desk were then on fire.  I grabbed the light by the strap, thank goodness for the strap because the light was extremely hot - and took it out the front door where it continued to flame for a couple of minutes. 

I have probably 6-10 lights with these types of batteries. IÃÂve gone through probably 50 batteries of this brand over maybe 6-8 years. I donÃÂt mix batteries as they warn. I have had no problem with any other light. IÃÂm suspicious about the switch or circuits in this one ÃÂ which of course, are now cooked! This is the only light IÃÂve had until now that had a 3 stage switch, the rest were on/off or brief burst. 

I have contacted Streamlight, they have requested the flashlight be sent in for forensic testing.  They say it is a battery problem, that they are aware of these problems, but the problems are always battery, not flashlight related.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns and property damage, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the product's defect and the user's repeated exposure to it.

incident_description: while riding my Troy-built Riding lawnmower model " Colt XP" the solenoid shorted out on the metal strap holing down the gas tank..... melting the gas tank and sparking the fuel to catch fire....... diagnosed by the city fire chief/ fire inspector.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such an event to occur, it's not common.

incident_description: My Snow thrower caught fire after I refilled the gas tank, and pumped the gas tank to prime the carburetor.
justification: While rare, gas fires can occur during refueling and priming, posing a potential hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I was using the Troy chipper/shredder model 24A-424G766 to chip up branches from just felled trees.I walked around to pick up some more branches when I heard a big bang and the chipper came to an abrupt stop.How could this happen when their was nothing in the chute.I tried to pull start it  but it would not turn over. Then I preceded to take it apart to find out what was wrong. What I found out was the chipper ate its self. The pins that hold the fails in place had moved out releasing the fails to fly out. After checking similar machines, the model that I used did not have the saftey clips in place that lock the fail pins in place.I did find two of the fails that where expelled from the machine in the chipped pile. The dealer said the machine was off warranty and would not repair. The parts cost was to be about $800. After talking to the manufacturing company and them looking at the pictures he said it was a maintenance issue. Their is no mention in the manual for this.This model does not list the safety clips, only a latter model. I believe their should of been a recall for this machine to install the safety clips. Those fails flying out are very dangerous and could kill some one.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in severe injury or death if the expelled fan blades had struck someone.

incident_description:
An explosion occurred in the kitchen of a restaurant at this location and resulted in burns to the person operating the equipment that exploded. The device that exploded was a portable camp type stove which is NOT approved for use in a commercial setting such as this restaurant and is designed for personal outdoor use only. A Fire Inspector will be performing a follow up to ensure this practice is discontinued at this location. The device is identified on the front as "Greatland" and the label on the rear identifies it as Athens Brands, Inc. Model Number 01579 Rated 7280 BTU!HR with a date of manufacture of 040224. The gas cylinder in the appliance suffered catastrophic failure at the seam at the top of the can and blew the cover off the device. 

A 38 year-old male sustained 1st degree burns to his head, chest, and arms.
justification: Injury occurred due to unapproved equipment usage, making it a possible event.

incident_description: Toro snowblower model 38515 started leaking gas from the carburator.  According to the local dealer, it needs a new carburator but they are having trouble getting one because this is apparently a common issue with this particular snowblower.  From what I can tell, Toro has issued recalls on this model snowblower but not our serial number (290004563) for this fuel leaking problem.  The bad news is that the thing leaks even if it is not running.  Almost all the gas in the tank leaked out over a weekend on non use.
justification: Gas leak, even when not in use, poses a significant fire hazard.

incident_description:
(9/2011) Caller stated that the while he was placing air in the wheel barrow tire, it exploded in his hands and caused him to receive a broken left thumb, numbness in both hands, constant ear ache and headaches.  The explosion threw him against the wall, the plastic rim when it exploded projected all over and he received lacerations to his left hand (swollen). He sought medical attention approximately 4 days later.  This incident has caused him a medical bill of over $6000.

(9/2011) He contacted the manufacturer and he was referred to their insurance company (Zurich) and his claim was denied.

The caller stated that the tire is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: Injury occurred due to tire explosion, likelihood is possible given the nature of the incident and the caller's actions.

incident_description:
Purchased a new Ariens Sno Tek 24E Snow Thrower in November. Only used it twice. The second time the engine wouldn't turn off, even after pulling the key out, flicking off the "stop" button, and turning off the fuel cutoff switch. Engine continued to run a full 15 minutes or so. Had this been an emergency, would not have been able to stop engine. This poses a serious risk. When I looked up the possible cause online, I saw that others had reported the same problem, apprently caused by a loose ground wire. No way for an average consumer to fix this. 

Called Ariens headquarters. They told me this was a frequent problem and would fix under warranty. So why no recall, if it's a defect that could potentially cause injury?
justification: The engine's inability to shut off poses a significant risk, especially in emergency situations, and the frequency of this issue reported by others indicates a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I was given a Garden Dump Cart as a gift. This item requires assemble. Upon opening the box the odor was so strong as to cause me to open the door in the garage to get fresh air. The odor was coming from all the packaging,the instruction book as well the box itself.  The odor gave new a headache,as well irritated my eyes. The odor remains in my garage the day after assemble.  I'am concerned as to the negative inpack to me as well other consumers from what ever chemical is in the packaging of this product.
justification: The incident resulted in immediate physical discomfort (headache, eye irritation) and potential long-term health risks from chemical exposure.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a 23 horsepower riding lawnmower on August 23rd, 2005 and had no problems with it at all until August 2012 when she had been cutting grass for around fifteen minutes then saw flames approximately one foot high coming from the back of the lawnmower.
She jumped off of the lawnmower and turned it off.

She yelled for her son who came with a neighbor and the two of them extinguished the flames.

Consumer contacted manufacturer August 2012 and was advised that the lawnmower was not under warranty and that they weren't going to assist her because it is 7-8 years old.

The consumer states that because it is 7-8 years old, cost over nine thousand dollars, she has seen other lawnmowers recalled for this same safety issue.
She is asking that her lawnmower be considered for recall with repair at manufacturer expense.

No injuries being reported

UPDATE: Consumer would like to add that the mower was for her home only- that is why she feels it should have lasted longer.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a significant fire from a lawnmower, posing a potential risk.

incident_description:
I have a owned Sears Propane Gas Grill Model 122.16643900 for about 3 years.  The peg's in the back ledge of the firebox, which hold the burners and diffusers in place have rusted away.  
This causes an unsafe condition as it allows the burners to pull out of the connections in the front of the grill wherein the gas enters the burners.
Have had to stop using because the burners have pulled out and allowed fire with going into the burners
justification: Burners pulling out and allowing fire into the grill poses a high risk of property damage, but no direct injury was mentioned.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that gas was leaking out of the carburetor, of the snow blower. Consumer has previously had problems with the engine powering on the snow blower. Gas had to be drained out of the tank for safety. Consumer is unsure of the size of the gas tank. The gas leaked onto the ground of the driveway. The leak is described as a fast and steady dripping leak. 

The snow blower will not power on and start at all; the snow blower has an automatic electric starter that is not working. The snow blower has not been used since early 1/12. 

Toro stated it was out of the warranty and his model is not included.

Dealer stated they would need authorization from mfr before any services could be conducted.
justification: Gas leak posed a fire hazard but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I bought a Professional Chargriller made in China.
The first time I used it we detected a gas leak. It turned out that the Regulator was defective.
In a haste to cook the food, I went down and bought a new one and put it on and it worked fine for a couple years. The first time it overheated due to chicken grease, it melted the internal lines inbetween the 3 burners. I did not turn the main tank off but, turned off the three burner knobs in the front. incident_description:
Our home has an Ecoteck (Ravelli) Pellet stove.  The model name is "Monica".  The pellet stove was operating normally when the power failed.  After the power returned, the stove's display indicated ÃÂBlack ÃÂ OutÃÂ.  The instruction manual solution for this message is ÃÂPress the OFF button and repeat switching ON the stoveÃÂ.  After doing this, the display indicated "Final Cleaning" which is the message normally displayed while it is in its shutdown phase.  After stove shut off, I restarted it and checked it a few minutes later.  The stove interior was filled with smoke & fire, smoke was seeping from the seams of the flue inside the house and smoke was billowing outside the house from the flue.  There was also a detonation of combustible gases in the flue which blew the bottom cover off the flue at the base of the stove.  I opened the stove door and used a fire extinguisher to put the fire out.  The fire pot was entirely filled with pellets, which apparently led to the runaway fire.  I called 911 and had the fire department make sure everything was ok.

Later investigation showed that the power failure created a failure mode in which the stove's electronic controller continuously loads pellets in the fire pot leading to a dangerous runaway fire condition in the stove's interior.  The intensity of the resulting fire is beyond the design limit of the stove and could easily have led to a structural fire in the home had I not contained it.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant fire, causing smoke damage and potentially structural damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:

The consumer turned the unit off and flipped the hood off, he took his shirt off and placed underneath the engine to stop the flames.  He believes that the gas line broke.  

Within a couple of minutes the entire unit was in flames and there were flames up to three feet tall.  The flames reached the battery, a couple of minutes later the battery exploded.  There was another explosion after that.  The only thing left of the tractor is the motor  in the flame.  There is a large burn spot about 6 ft in diameter in the yard.

The house and deck caught on fire, my husband was able to disconnect the propane tank before it exploded also.  We were able to get the BBQ grill off the deck and dragged it out to the driveway were it continued to burn, putting water on it made the flames brighter and it was difficult to put out.  We are very upset our house smells like smoke inside, we had to tear our our melted and burned vinyl siding to see if there was a fire underneath and our our brand new freshly painted deck now has burn holes. Not to mention we now had no dinner.  After the fire was out I called Lowes - [REDACTED] at store # 1559, said that it was not their responsibility after one year.  I told her that I had talked to my son who lives in another state and he told me that they had a lot of recalls on that brand.  She said they were still not responsible and gave me the number to the manufacturer.

incident_description:
As I was operating the snow throw through appx 8-10 inches of snow near the edge of the sidewalk, I noticed the chute bouncing around more than normal. As I continued to throw the snow with the machine, the snow discharge chute completely came off of the chute base and landed on the sidewalk as the machine continued to throw snow for a short time until I disabled the auger. 
Upon inspection, I noticed that the plastic chute base (the part that holds the chute to the machine) was completely cracked through/broken on appx 75% of its three shoulders (see photos). The single bolt holding the chute to the base worked its way out of the chute base hole it was designed to be placed in, but remained in the chute itself. I believe this was due to the normal pressure of snow being ejected from the chute. It seems the bolt rose up and out of the hole it was designed to be placed in due to being unsecured with a nut. The repeated pulsating pressure/stress on the plastic chute base shoulders (and no nut to hold the bolt securely in place) was too much for the plastic chute base to handle, it cracked, and subsequent pulsation of snow discharge quickly lifted it up and off of the base.
**The dangerous aspect is that the instruction manual "Assembly Instructions" directs the consumer to "Attach the chute to the snow output port using the bolt and washer (Fig. 3)." There is NO mention of affixing a nut to the bolt in the instructions! Later that night I read through the manual again and came across an exploded parts diagram in the back of the manual that reveals a nut beneath the bolt. 
Any consumer who wishes to be protected by the Warranty Coverage understands that one must do what is asked in the "Assembly Instructions" to have Warranty protection. For this reason, I believe it likely that other consumers also followed the faulty assembly instructions and are likely to encounter the same hazardous situation (chute coming completely off in full operation) after several uses. In my case, appx 10 since purchase.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the chute completely detaching during operation poses a significant risk of injury, and the faulty assembly instructions increase the likelihood of this incident recurring among other users.

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they did not provide any assistance. 

The consumer believes this product should be investigated due to the safety hazard that it poses to the consumer.

incident_description: I purchased a Bradley BTIS1 Smoker as a gift in November 2011. We used the smoker twice last summer. The second time we used it, it went up in flames. Had we not been outside when our smoker caught on fire, we could've lost more than just the smoker.

incident_description:
I have been using the GrandTurbo BBQ (from Barbeques Galore) for approximately 3 years and have had occasional problems with the barbecue knobs becoming too hot to touch and ultimately melting to the point that they slide off.
Also during that time, I have seen the stainless steel cooking grids slowly loose their structural integrity resulting in them "peeling" apart, and getting steel in the food. 
Early on in my ownership of the grill, the company that installed the grill replaced my control knobs.  Most recently, I have contact the manufacturer about replacing them again (the installation company is no longer in business), in addition to addressing the issue of the cooking grids.
However, my email exchange with them have only resulted in a position that I need to purchase replacement parts (even though the product has a lifetime warranty).  At first, I thought this was just a warranty issue.  Then I realized that I have been tolerating a product that is supposed to be used for cooking, but can result the food being injected with steel from the grids and knobs that are melting or too hot to turn off.... and that is a safety concern.
justification: The incident involves potential ingestion of steel particles from the grids and knobs, posing a significant risk of injury.

incident_description:

After the grill cooled off, it seems to operate correctly, though we are nervous using it now.

incident_description:

By the first of August I had to return it due to several of the crossover channels just fell off. In December the replacement grill did the exact same thing. This is a very serious safety issue. Model  810-2545-W

incident_description:

There were particles all over his body, face, some content got in his eyes, he was able to wash it off.  He stated that he received minor bruises around his left eye.

11/26/12 The manufacturer was contacted and he was offered a replacement bag which he declined because he feels that the incident will re-occur.  He feels that the manufacturer is aware of the safety hazard of this product.

Under incident details:  Consumer insisted that the replacement bag not be the same model bag.  Consumer informed Black & Decker customer service that he wanted the bag that is used on the LH 5000 model which has a slide bas VS zipper closure.  They verified that bag used on the LH5000 model would in fact fit the consumer's LH4500 machine.  Consumer received LH5000 model bag via UPS on 30 Nov 2012.  It is obviously a much more sturdy design than a zipper closure.
justification: Minor injury (bruises) occurred due to zipper malfunction, and the consumer's insistence on a different bag model suggests a recurring issue.

incident_description:
A new 6 1/2 HP Gasoline Engine (212cc) Predator Brand ([REDACTED]) was purchased from Harbor Freight approximately 1 year ago as a replacement for a tiller.  The engine was left in the box for several months and later filled with oil and started with a small amount of gasoline in the metal tank.  Recently I filled the tank with gasoline, restarted it, let it run for a while 30-40- minutes and shut it down.   I later found moisture on the exterior of the gas tank and thinking it was condensation, wiped it dry.  On a later date I discovered the same thing and discovered it was gasoline, leaking, weeping, seeping from a seam that holds the upper and lower portions of the tank together.
The seam is "crimped" metal and the gasoline appears to be coming from the upper portion of the tank.  IT IS UNSAFE TO USE.
I have talked to two Managers at the Fayetteville, NC Harbor Freight Store (1/23/2013 and 1/27/2013) and their only concern was, it is out of warranty and your problem.

I reminded them that the issue was not a warranty, but a safety issue, as in unsafe to use as sold and should be recalled.

An undamaged gasoline tank should be designed and manufactured to outlast the normal expected life of the engine which can be 10 plus years.
justification: Gasoline leak from the tank poses a fire hazard, although no injuries have been reported yet.

Im sure there are other people out there doing this same thing trying to get their tire back on the plastic rim, not knowing how violent of an explosion awaits them.

incident_description: In early December, 2012, I purchased an outdoor patio heater from Costco online. The product is Costco Item # 514537.  The heater is manufactured by Fire Sense Model # 60688.  The product requires some assembly.  I believe the product has a serious design flaw that could result in a fire hazard. The unit was designed so that the purchaser does not have the ability to test the upper hose (where it connects to the igniter and on/off switch for gas leaks. The owner's manual diagram shows that the hose is accessible through a hole in the housing and should be tested for leaks. The actual design is such that there is no testing hole and the entire unit must be dissembled, placed on the ground and tested and then reassembled. This is not practical.  The part of the unit where the hose connects comes already assembled and is very difficult to take apart.  I did in fact experience a gas leak but was fortunate enough to detect it before I experienced a fire or explosion.  I attempted to post a review of the product on the Costco web site describing my issue but Costco chose not to post it. I returned the product to Costco without a problem. I called the manufacturer customer service line.  They told me that they would have to replace the entire burner/valve portion of the heater but that they did not have any in stock and wouldn't for over a month as other customers have experienced similar issues.    I expect that most customers who purchase this product will not test the hose coupling for leaks as it is not accessible and they will not take the time to disassemble the unit.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the design flaw allowing gas leaks poses a high likelihood of incident.

incident_description:
Kenmore Gas Grill purchased from Sears
Item# 07116156000 
Mfr. Model# S3218ANB
My model is the following:
Model #:  148.16156210
Serial #:  ANB0008703

Previously seared a steak or two using the side burner (it is a sear-type burner).

Recently decided to sear a steak and when I lit the sear burner a large amount of flames were venting out of the air gap at the front of the burner.  Flames where striking the wiring and instrumentation on the front panel of the sear burner.  The controls and wiring were exposed to flames.  If left unattended the flames would have started the wiring and controls on fire.  The flames occurred regardless of the burner intensity (at the lowest setting the flames continued to be directed toward the instruments and wiring).

I shutdown the sear burner after about 2 minutes of operation.  I re-lit the sear burner after 1 to 2 minutes and the sear burner was operating as expected.  There appeared to be clogging of the burner element from a previous searing of steak.

After the incident occurred I have been careful to allow the sear burner to burn off any grease or fat on the sear element and the issue ***appears*** to not occur.

This is a product defect that should be addressed as it has a possibility of causing a fire.
justification: Flames venting from the burner posed a risk of igniting the exposed wiring and controls, which could have led to a fire.

incident_description:
I was grilling during the month of September 2012 in my backyard when my grill caught fire. I tried to turn the gas off but it was to no avail the fire spreaded so fast to the propane tank that there was no time to turn the knob to the propane tank off. Before you knew it the gas line, hose and the tank started to ignite. Luckily the tank was not full and the grill was far away from the house and the door to the propane tank contained the fire.

The propane tank burned for 15 to 20 minutes. I managed to keep the temperature from the propane tank down by spraying it with water from my garden hose.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (severity level 2). The likelihood of such an event occurring is 'possible' (level 3) given the common use of propane grills and the potential for gas leaks.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a new John Deere Model D100 (6/2012) and the unit has an issue with clutch engagement which does not allow for safe starts on inclines and provides jerky starts on flat surfaces.  The clutch and brake are operated by a single foot control, pressed down, it engages the brake and as you lift off it engages the clutch.  The pedal has about 8" of travel and the clutch engagement is at the very end (last 1/4 to 1/2) of the pedals travel therefore it cannot be engaged smoothly before the brake releases, when engaged it slams into gear!  When the clutch does engage it causes the front wheels to lift off the ground learching the operator backward nearly tipping the unit end over end.  This condition existed at the time of purchase and as instructed by the ownerÃÂs manual I contacted the local JD service center and they speculated it was an adjustment issue and that it would take 2-3 weeks for them to repair.  At the end of the mowing season I brought the unit in for the adjustment at which point they took it apart and informed me that the D100 could not be adjusted and that JD had no fix for the unit.  JD official response is there is no defect and the unit operates correctly.  Since contacting JD I have located similar complaints on the internet.  See link below.

http://reviews.deere.com/1507-en_au/D100EGX/johndeere-d100-lawn-tractor-reviews/reviews.htm
justification: The severe clutch engagement issue could cause loss of control and potential injury, as demonstrated by the front wheels lifting off the ground and the operator being thrown back.

incident_description: I ran the TORO Power Clear 421QE, empty of one tank and filled the tank full again to run later that afternoon.  When I went to the garage I could smell gasoline and there was some on the floor. When I went to start the snowblower it would not start.  I checked the tank it was empty. incident_description: I have the Troy-Bilt 4-cycle gas trimmer. The shaft comes loose at the attachment and the attachment can come off and injury someone.

I've used this snowthrower less than 10 times, and it's now unusable and dangerous to my family.
