incident_description: I placed three AAA batteries into a headlight/headlamp/flashlight that I bought from Target. It was labeled as Item #CORE-HL made by PerfectSense in China. It shows it is distributed by Core Distribution, Inc. Minneapolis, MN 55401. Also on the tag is DPCI #234-08-0038. The sku is 898140000833. After I placed the three batteries inside the battery "pack" and put it inside the body of the headlight, it immediately began to smoke. I pulled out the battery pack, check the polarity on the batteries and found them to be correct. I then removed and reinserted them and the batter pack warmed up to the point where it was almost hot enough to burn me. I removed the batteries again and I am returning the product to the Target store.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a product malfunction that could have led to injury, making it an incident with potential severity.

incident_description:
IÃÂm writing to inform you of an uncontained engine failure I experienced three weeks ago. While mowing, the engine lost power followed by an explosion where the connecting rod sheared and exited the right side of the engine case. In addition to the liberated piece of connecting rod, three pieces of engine case also became airborne. Following the incident, my greatest concern was not the engine failure itself but the fact that the engine failure was uncontained. Fortunately, no injuries occurred but I consider this incident to be a significant safety risk. 

Thank you for your attention in this matter.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the uncontained engine failure resulted in debris becoming airborne, posing a significant safety risk.

incident_description: I was using the Perfect Flame gas grill to make dinner for my family. There are 4 knobs across the front pf the grill, the knob 2nd from the left sounded as if the propane was getting low so I shut the knob off and just continued making the burgers. When I was done I left two of the burners on low so I could burn off the cheese, as I have done this many times before and then cleaned the grill with the brush. My daughter said the grill was on fire and I walked out the door and lifted the lid and sprayed a little water on it and the flame at first went down but then it came back even bigger, and thats when I realized the flame wasn't in the grill it was on fire underneath the grill. I could not turn off one of the knobs because the fire was shooting a flame out. I looked down under it so I could shut the gas off but that's where I realized the grill was on fire from the line of the grill to the propane tank. I kept a steady stream of water on it as I had just called for my husband to come quick and he just instructed me to keep the water spraying and he stuck his hand in where the fire was to shut off the propane. The whole right side of the grill is charred and melted.
justification: Injury occurred when the user attempted to extinguish the fire under the grill, which was fueled by a gas leak from the propane tank.

incident_description:
The consumer says that in late 2011 the battery to his lawn mower failed.  He contacted the manufacturer who replaced the battery.  The consumer says that in July 2012 he used it once again and it started smoking, battery acid was leaking from it, and almost caught on fire.  He unplugged the unit and it took about a day or so for it to cool off.    The consumer says he contacted the manufacturer after the incident in July 2012 and they replaced the battery once again.

Now it is going through this cycle when he turns it on.  He says it does not turn on and it does not take a charge anymore.  He tried to plug the battery into the lawn mower and nothing is happening.  This time there was not the presence of battery acid, smoke or heat.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to battery acid leakage and smoke, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Purchased Master Forge Stainless Steel Portable Gas Grill Model # GR4039-014247 from Lowes in Amarillo Texas. Regulator freezes up when using full 16 oz porpane cylinder. Regulator continues to freeze and flames spewes and flames then go out. This continues until cylinder is approximately 1/2 capacity.  Lowes replaced regulator. Problem continues with new regulator.  Master Forge product is inferior and dangerous.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the recurring issue of the grill's regulator freezing and causing flames to spew and then go out poses a significant fire hazard.

incident_description:
I've had this blower for many years, but when it broke I just put it away....  just now found out it was a recall item from TORO..
..   was using the blower in a normal way that I had been for several years.... moving leaves around in the yard in preparation for picking them up and putting them on my compost pile..  when all of a sudden the thing made a loud noise, began shaking uncontrollably and hurt my wrist before I could switch it off....   I looked inside and saw that the rotating turbine wheel had broken.... obviously out of balance for a wheel that spins so fast.... this was the cause of the vibration.  the broken part fell out of the opening after I pulled the nozzle off to look inside.  one large plastic piece and several small plastic pieces.
justification: Injury occurred due to the broken turbine wheel causing the blower to shake uncontrollably, and the likelihood is high as the incident happened during normal use.

incident_description: I have a Craftsman lawn mower (manufactured by Huskvarna) that started to melt the plastic shroud over the drive-belt system.  The shroud is located right under the muffler and I believe is too close.  My concern is that this could be a fire hazard.  Sears has replaced the shroud but I am concerned that it will happen again.  The Model# is 917370660 and Serial # is 090811M022572.  We purchased this last year but I think it was a leftover model.  Thank you.
justification: While no injury has occurred, the melting of the plastic shroud poses a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible future consequences.

incident_description:
The consumer says that his grandson was cutting grass at the church.  His sister noticed the unit was smoking.  He jumped off the lawnmower when it started blazing up around both sides and it blew up.  His grandson was not inujured.

The consumr says it burned the wheels and the tire off of it.  All the plastic was also melted.
justification: Although the lawnmower caught fire and was severely damaged, no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while they were asleep they were awaken by an explosion in the garage.  She discovered that the snow thrower rim had exploded which caused damages to her motor cycle and the roof of the car.

The caller feels that she experienced similar problems of Release #07-003.

The snow thrower model number matched the numbers listed on the recall.

The manufacturer was contacted through email on 10/15/12.  There was no response as yet.

The caller feels that this snow thrower is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: No injuries were reported, but significant property damage occurred, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' with a 'possible' likelihood of occurrence due to the recall history.

incident_description:
During the first day of use of the Home depot Rock Forge Maul with fiberglass handle the plastic sealing material at the top of the axe disintegrated when using the maul to strike a wedge when splitting wood.  This product has a integral design flaw where normal axes would provide increased friction as the steel head tries to move outward from a wooden handle with a wedge driven into it.

The Rock Forge maul friction that keeps the unit together decreases as the force of the head moves away from the position it started in.  The major concern with this product is that it has been seen that separation occurs with no visible signs of damage.  Fortunately in this instance no injuries resulted, however it was very obvious that a near miss with the head separated could result in serious injury/death if the head flew into ones leg.
justification: The incident involved a near miss with the potential for serious injury or death if the head had separated and struck the user's leg.

incident_description:
U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission
Attn: Reports
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814

Customer Service Center
Lowe's Companies, Inc.
1000 Lowe's Boulevard
Mooresville, NC 28117

Garden Treasures 11000 BTU Tabletop
Liquid Propane Patio Heater
Item #: 48221 I Model #: HPS-C-PC
I bought one of these from Lowes and after several months it quit.

I called three different times 888-775-1330 and the first time, they had me disassemble
the top portion to expose the pilot and use compressed air to blow it out.

The next day they had me disassemble it and expose the copper tube & orfice and blow
them out.

When I lit it, flames came out the lower section of the burner box at the top of the
extension tube.

I called a third time and the tech started into another fiasco and I told him, hell this is a
relative new unit and I don't want to be doing a bench repair on a product you should be
fixing or standing behind.

I bet there is a recall on it or there should be.

When I worked on it the third time I discovered that there was a main burner tube
connection that apparently is a slip fit and was most of the way out.

This is not safe and I refuse to go another hour on it.

Lowes should not be selling these unless they take responsibility.

My unit is serial number 20110710674 Model HPS-C-PC.

Your website had one purchaser state: "it just shut down all gas went off including the
pilot light. Thinking it may be a problem with the mechanism I called Lowes, the
manager told me it may be a bad thermo-coupler, to bring it in for an exchange. I did.
The new one has the exact same issue! I called the support number on the
instruction/warantee book they are AWESOME by the way. Come to find out, this is a
known issue with these heaters!

NOW WHY IS IT THAT LOWES SELLS THIS AND HAS "QUESTIONS
PROBLEMS MISSING PARTS ETC. CALL 1-888-775-1330"?

Maybe I should have done what that guy did and call Lowes, but I did not; I invested
three days of my life trying to fix a propane driven appliance that could become a bomb.
What do you want to do about this or should I turn this over to a consumer regulatory
body for a safety check?

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to a faulty connection, which could lead to injuries.

incident_description:
Product- Toro Power Clear 180 Snow Blower  Purchased 11/12/2009
              Model - 38272 Ser# - 310000821

Incident description - Continuing problem with fuel leaks.

Actions taken - 11/24/2010 Dealer replaced leaking Carburetor under warranty.
                         11/23/2011 Dealer replaced leaking Carburetor under warranty
                         10/18/2012 Owner rebuilt leaking Carburetor replacing needle valve.
                         10/18/2012 Owner drained fuel system and replaced old fuel with new fuel.
                         10/18/2012 Owner added MIX-I-GO to fuel to protect from ethanol problems.
                         11/20/2012 Carburetor started leaking again.

Comments -      It is obvious that the made in China Carburetor was not designed for US fuel and that the problem it has not been corrected. It is just as dangerous as it was in 2009.  If the needle valve was replaced with one with a metal tip rather than a rubber one the problem probably be corrected although this might require a more precision product.  I think that Toro should be required to fix this dangerous product!

Toro-                Toro's solution to this problem drain the gas from the unit when not in use and hope that snow falls are not more than a month apart.
justification: Fuel leaks are recurring despite multiple attempts at repair, posing a fire hazard.

incident_description:
I checked my Troybilt 20 HP Kohler 42 inch cut riding lawnmower.  It had 1/2 tank of gas.  I took it out to blow the leaves off my driveway.  About 1/3 way down the driveway fire flames shout up out of the mower.I turned the ignition off and got off, but now before it burned my arm. The wind was blowing fiercely and blew the flames into the woods.  The mower flamed to hotly I couldn't get by it to call the fire department so a neighbor called it for me. Seven neighbors came to help and four firemen came from the Sissonville Fire department.  They finally got it put out after it burned about 1 acre.

I called Troybilt and asked them to replace the mower and pay for my shrubs and the hole in my driveway. They said they could not pay because it caught fire because the muffler was in a place that caught leaves and grass on fire and the manual said not to run over tall grass or leaves when the motor is warm.

If the muffler does this, shouldn't it be put in another place or shouldn't the mower be recalled.They said they had gotten many complaints of this happening
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident caused significant property damage.

incident_description:
While mowing my lawn, the side wall of the combustion chamber blew out ~1.5" irregularly shaped hole in three peice.  The peices projected about 4ft and bounced off a retaining wall directly in front of them.  The mower had oil, was recently cleaned and the blade had been sharpened.  I had been mowing for approximately 10 minutes just before it happened, and was bagging the clippings at that time.  

The failed mower is a Toro GTS 6.5, Model #20016, Serial #220618424.

Prior to this event, I had noticed the first few times I used the mower this past spring it was choking increasingly while the recycle or mulch door closed and the mower was therefore forced to mulch all the grass clippings.  With the drought I was able to go without mowing June thru August.  Since the mulch or recycle mode was causing problems I started bagging clippings and used the mower 4-6 times without choking while bagging.  I have a standard 1/3 acre suburban lawn if that helps this appraisal any.  Using the self-propelled mode going uphill didn't seem to impact the choking.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant equipment failure with debris projection, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Carburetor leaks. Matches symptoms in Health Canada Release #11-207.
justification: Carburetor leaks pose a potential fire hazard, as indicated by Health Canada's release #11-207, but typically do not result in injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The consumer says when he was operating the bagger, the mower blades pushed the leaves into the bagger.  He says the blades continued to turn as he was bagging leaves.  He says that the power take off shaft is disengaged which is supposed to make the blades stop.    He says that the blades were not running at full speed which is deceptive.  He was not injured because he did not put his hands in the wrong spot.  

He says when he opened the top of the bagger, he noticed that there was still air pushing into the bagger.  Thats what indicated to him that the blades were still turning.   


He contacted the manufacturer who said that they would fix the mower at no charge since ti si under warranty due to it being only 15 months old.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a malfunction that could have led to injury, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description:
Defective propane gas regulator model RA329 manufactured by Ningbo Wanan, China. Product was included in the purchase of a Grillrite brand outdoor gas barbeque grill. Regulator functioned well several times before failing. On or about the 7th use, the regulator failed upon ignition of grill. Uncontrolled flames shot out from regulator where it connects to the propane tank.  I was able to access the main valve at the 20-lb propane cylinder to shut-off gas flow.  Fortunately there was no explosion and no injuries occurred.  Just lucky I guess.

The second occurrance was on 11/01/12 but this time I hear the propane gas escaping from the connection where the regulator meets the propane tank.  I was able to shut it off and disconnect the regulator unit.  This was a replacement that I purchased but made by the same company, in Ningbo Wanan, China.  

something needs to be done to stop this company from exporting defective regulator units before someone gets killed in an explosion.  I am surprised that the agency has not stopped the import of this product as I am not the only one who has reported the same problem.

Minor injury (burns to hand) ocurred as user tried to  Replacement of regulator with a different brand/model resolved issue.
justification: Injury occurred due to defective regulator, and likelihood of recurrence is high given multiple incidents with the same product.

incident_description:
I own a Homelite Leaf Blower Model UT08076S?N HT2750457? [see picture] and had an issue last weekend doing fall cleanup at my fathers house. When operating the leaf blower, the tote strap while loose got tangled into the blower air intake shattering some fins off the impeller. [See pictures attached] My wrist was hit by one of the impellers like shrapnel. My wrist recovered with just a minor scratch.

I took off the impeller cover to untangle the strap and continue to operate the unit but the vibration was so bad I had to stop. See the attached photos for any questions.
justification: While the incident resulted in a minor injury, it could have been more severe.

incident_description: We were tailgating after the Clemson vs Maryland football game.  We were packing up to leave  after cooking burgers on the O Grill 3000.  I let the grill cool off for about 20 to 30 minutes before starting to pack it up.  I have never had any problems with this grill, until I started unscrewing the 1 pound [REDACTED] gas cannister.  After unscrewing the cannister a piece regulator stayed attached to the cannister causing the propane to escape from the canniste.  The propane continued to escape from the cannister and there was not stopping it.  I removed the propane tank away from the area and away from any harm.  Very lucky no one was hurt, but could have been a disaster if the tank caught on fire.  The next morning I decided to look up replacement parts for my grill when I found out it was recalled back in January.  I had no clue it was recalled.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the propane leak posed a significant fire risk, classifying it as an incident.

incident_description: I was using a Black & Decker LH4500 Leaf Hog to vacuum leaves when a heard a loud "bang" and was knocked to the ground by an impact on my right leg.  When I was able to get up I discovered that the cast aluminum impeller in the unit had come apart.  The largest fragment was embedded in the units housing while a smaller fragment (about 2" X 2 1/2") had gone through the housing and hit me in the leg.  I was wearing very heavy work pants but still experienced broken skin in a "check mark" shape on the right leg about 4" above the knee.  The area around the point of impact (about the size of my hand) started to swell and bruise.  Now (5 days later) some swelling persists, the bruising has become deeper, and I still experience some discomfort with every step.  I was very fortunate to have been hit in the leg and be wearing heaving pants.  Had this fragment hit me in the face, neck, ankle, or knee, it could resulted in a significant injury or even death.  I have been in contact with Black and Decker and am providing the unit for engineering analysis.  As a former engineer I consider the unit unsafe (refusing B&D's offer to provide a replacement) because of the relatively brittle properties of cast aluminum, its use in a corrosive environment under cyclic loads (with the potential for fatigue failure), and a plastic case that is obviously incapable for containing such a failure.
justification: Injury occurred due to cast aluminum impeller failure, with a small fragment penetrating heavy work pants and causing broken skin, swelling, and bruising.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Halloween mini projection light from Five Below (distributed by :Atico International USA, Inc. ). On Halloween night upon placing the batteries into the light and turning it on it immediately began to get hot and the back end of the light melted. Luckily I was still holding it when this happened and not my 5 year old son whom the light was purchased for. I was not injured other than my hand turning a little red, but if a child had been holding it there was the potential for burning. I still have the light and accessories should you need photos or the light itself to investigate the matter. I have also sent emails to both Five Below and to Atico International.
justification: Although no serious injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in burns if a child had been using the product.

incident_description: Toro Model 38282,  S/N 311019462.  Toro Power Clear 180 Snow Thrower.  Relate to July 14, 2010 CPSC Release #10-299.  My unit is also leaking fuel in the same manner as descriped in release 10-299.  Called Toro to check if my unit is part of the recal and was told it was not.  Last fall, the unit leaked 1/2 tank of gas onto the flor of the garrage.  This posed a severe potential for fire.  I checked the unit today and found it is leaking gass uncontrollably from the carburator.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to uncontrollable gas leakage from the carburetor, as previously experienced.

incident_description: While trying to start up my snow blower for the first time this season, gasoline started to leak from the carburetor area.  I had gasoline over my hands, clothing, and had a large pooled area of gas on the ground.
justification: Gasoline leakage poses a fire hazard but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
TEC - Char-Broil Gril - Model Number - 463268407 - 

The heads of the bolts are falling off the TEC Infrared Burners.  They are coming off due to the heat generated by the burners themselves.  The bolts fall onto the top of the TEC Burner. This is causing movement in the burners themselves.  Making matters worse, the burners themselves are flaking apart allowing gas to come up in bursts.  The burners will go from working fine, to having a rapid popping noise as the gas escapes from the burner in small bursts, then a flash explosion on the grill surface will shoot a flame approximately 1'x1' across the top of the burner.  The burner then blows out with the gas still flowing.  The burner must be then shut off and relit.  It will go back to working fine, then popping, then explosion, and blowing out.

I thought this was normal until I read the other filed complaint and spoke with where I purchased the grill.
justification: The incident, while causing property damage, has not resulted in any injuries as per the description.

incident_description:
I was putting fresh gas in my Toro Snowblower for the winter season. I filled the tank that was 
empty with fresh new Non- Ethonol gas on Sat 10/20/2012 in my garage. I left the house and return 
home on Sunday morning to a strong odor of GAS. I left the garage door open & aired out the garage 
B/4 I left to go away for Sunday 10/21/2012. I returned home on Monday morning and open the garage 
door to the same gas odor & now it had penetrated into my homes Living Area. I moved the Snowblower 
out into the driveway to start the engine. It started and ran for
about 3 minutes and then stopped running.  I open the gas tank and it was empty, all of the Gas had 
leaked out of the machine onto the garage floor. This is a Safety of Healthy issue for me and my 
family to inhale gas odors & have
the risk of a Fire. So far all I have gotten is the run around from Toro .
This is a bad Model. I have done everything that the owners books has said, run the gas out at the 
end of the Season. Taken the advice of the Toro dealer to put in the Star Tron Gasoline Treatment. 
The machine is 2 years old and I afraid to continue using. Yesterday 10/22/2012 I spoke to Toro 
Customer Service and they wouldn't confirm
anything in writing that they would cover the expense of the repair. All they kept saying was were 
sorry.
I'm surprised that no one is sick from the gas fumes and we didn't hae a fire. We start the car in the garage.
justification: Potential for injury due to gas fumes, but no reported injuries.

incident_description: the grill fell apart just 2 years old leaking gas , second problem first was valve leaked the day I purchased it  they replaced it order#[REDACTED]. My house could of burnt down twice now because of this product.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a gas leak, posing a high risk of fire and property damage.

incident_description: I baited and set traps and placed them in my utility room where I seen evidence of mice.  I left the utility room and before long (from several minutes to an hour) heard a strange noise.  Upon investigating I discovered that the traps had come apart and pieces of the traps were scattered around the area where traps had been left.  If I had still been holding the trap in my hand and leaning over to put trap on floor I could have sustained an eye injury.
justification: The incident involved a potential eye injury, and the traps coming apart suggests a high likelihood of this happening again.

incident_description: I baited and set traps and placed them in my utility room where I had seen evidence of mice.  I left the utility room and before long (from several minutes to an hour) heard a strange noise.  Upon investigating I discovered that the traps had come apart and pieces of the traps were scattered around the area where traps had been left.  If I had still been holding the trap in my hand and leaning over to put trap on floor I could have sustained an eye injury.
justification: While unlikely, the traps could have malfunctioned while being handled, posing a potential injury risk.

incident_description: I have a Poulan PP4620AVX chainsaw with the tool-free adjusting system for the chain.  It does not work correctly and the chain has flown off the bar and injured me.  Poulan is aware of the defect and offers updated replacement parts to correct the issue to SOME people, but I was denied replacement parts because I could not locate my original receipt for the saw.  A quick search online shows that many others are experiencing the same problems.  This is a dangerous product due to an unresolved defect and I feel that a third party should get involved.
justification: Injury occurred due to a known defect in the chainsaw, and the likelihood is high given the widespread issue and Poulan's awareness.

incident_description:
During normal use according to the instructions that came with the Weber 7416 Chimney Starter, its handle caught on fire and melted.  I contacted Weber on October 21 and October 22, but heard back only on October 24th after a third email to Weber on October 23, 2012 stating that I contacted the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.

* used [REDACTED] [REDACTED] brand unused natural wood charcoal
* chimney starter was full
* no lighting aids were used including no lighter fluid or lighting cubes
* chimney starter was in the center of the uncovered Weber barbeque sash show on the packaging, which I can scan and email to you
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burnt handle) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the common use of charcoal and chimney starters.

incident_description: Homelite backpack blower with existing recall on fuel tank.  Model # UT08580A.  Fuel tank is leaking gas a the middle screw connect area.  Appears to be a recalled item with this exact problem.
justification: Leaking fuel poses a fire hazard, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
9/24/2012) The caller stated that her husband had just purchased a chainsaw. He took the saw out into the woods the same day of purchase to use it. Approximately 1 hour later, the bar, chain and cover for the assembly all detached from the saw in 3 parts. The consumer did not sustain any injuries due to the incident.
 
The manufacturer was contacted and report was filed and they were informed that forward the information would be forwarded to their corporate office.

The consumer took the chainsaw back to the retailer and received a refund.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction but resulted in no injuries, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as it's possible but not certain that such a malfunction could occur.

incident_description: I purchased a 2012 Cub Cadet Model LTX 1050 lawn mower this past Spring.  In May 2012the right side tie rod end came off, and the mower almost overturned on a slope. Today the left side tie rod came loose, again causing loss of steering control. There appears to be a defective design, as the tie rod clamps to a smooth shaft. There is no cotter pin, safety wire, or even a lock nut used to ensure the nut securing the tie rod does not loosen, allowing the tie rod to come off. If this had happened a few minutes earlier, I would have overturned into a ditch.
justification: The incident occurred twice in the same mower, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Hello,
This grill has been recalled. No one ever contacted me from BBQtec, the manufacturer or the vendor Lowes.
It started on fire last week and almost burned down our deck. Fortunately I was on the deck visiting with my wife. It is a very dangerous product and the company needs to be forced to at least contact the customers of the product. Yes, I did register my grill with them. I have the registration paperwork as proof.
When it caught fire the heat plates were also damaged. When I called I was told they were not covered in the recall only the burners were recalled. I said if I continue to use it, it would cause a fire and burn the deck down and possible my house. He said ÃÂwell maybe you will be killed so you cant sue us thenÃÂ I was appalled. He kept on this line of conversation and I asked to speak with a manager. Of course he said he was the manager. The call took place on 9 28 2012 at about 1:00pm Central Time.
This company should not be allowed to sell product in the USA.
[REDACTED]
Here is a copy of what I sent to the customer service department after we spoke.
My grill was recalled. It started on fire. The parts you have supplied are not sufficient to make the grill safe again. The Tents must be provided in the recall. Your customer service rep told me if i wanted to kill myself go right ahead, then I wouldnt be able to sue the company. I AM APPALLED AND YOU SHOULD BE AS WELL. I phoned Lowes and im quite sure you will never ever sell them another grill. Nor should you. I have a copy of this notification. If this grill should catch fire again and cause injury you will be sued. [REDACTED]
justification: The grill has already caused a fire, and the manufacturer's negligence in not providing necessary replacement parts increases the likelihood of another incident.

incident_description: Commercial SeriesÃÂ 500 Three-burner Infrared I had previously filed a complaint with your dept this is the third grill that keeps catching on fire
justification: The grill has caught fire multiple times, indicating a high likelihood of reoccurrence.

incident_description: On April 1, 2012 I purchased a Jenn-Air 720-0709 from a large membership only club and brought it home an assembled it as per the directions.  I used the grill on a regular basis, as per the directions away from my house at least 24."  on July 30th, I turned on my BBQ pit to cook some chicken.  I checked on it twice to ensure it was heating properly.  I returned outside with the chicken and it was completely engulfed in flames.  Fire was shooting out of the back vents and all around it.  I was able to extinguish the fire and my home.  I contacted the manufacture and asked them to repair my home.  After months of delays, an investigator came out to look at my house.  Their lawyers refuse to consider this a defect, but I have come across number other reports of the same incidents taking place on consumer reports and such.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
I recently purchased the Round Fire Pit (SKU: 2595032, Model: DS-4724) from my local Menards, and have found it to be both a highly inferior as well as downright dangerous product.

I realize that this is an inexpensive firepit ($49), but I do not think I have unrealistic expectations even given the price level.

The first issue was assembling the firepit, which was no easy task give the incredible poor craftsmanship, which left many screw holes un-punched, and dimensions that were not to-spec, making things much snugger fit than they should have been.  After assembling the unit, we placed a grill cover over it to protect it from the elements and to prevent rust. A week later, we decided to have our first fire in it.  We took the grill cover off, and placed three small logs in, and got a fire going. Just about the time that the fire had caught, one of the legs snapped off. In one week this pitiful excuse for a firepit had rusted through its leg, spilling flaming logs and hot ash everywhere. Honestly, I cannot believe how horribly irresponsible and negligent Menards has acted in selling such a poorly made and dangerous product, all in the name of making an easy buck.
justification: The fire pit's leg snapped off within a week of use, causing flaming logs and hot ash to spill, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: Flashlight is a clamshell design with the power switch in the cover. When the case is opened, bright light can shine in your eyes. The first time I used this light I did not know it would be so bright and damaged photo receptors in my eye.  Neither the device nor packaging contain warnings about potential eye damage.
justification: The incident resulted in eye damage, hence severity level 3. The lack of warnings and the unexpected brightness make it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
I have a John Deere backpack blower - Model BP6LE. It is a rebranded Kawasaki backpack blower with the TK65 67cc motor. The Kawasaki had issues with the gas tank leaking and creating a fire hazard and a recall for Kawasaki was issued. My backpack blower also has the same problem of a leaking fuel tank, causing a very dangerous and unsafe situation. 

I called John Deere - and they responded that since there was no recall in place for the BP65LE, that I was out of luck. Even though the blower is nothing more than a rebranded Kawasaki blower - which has been recalled along with other rebranded blowers such as those by [REDACTED] - John Deere would not offer to fix or rectify the issue.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to fuel tank leak, posing a significant risk to users.

incident_description: The riding lawn mower's fuel tank developed stress fractures at the mold injection point and leaked fuel in my garage over night. My entire house smelled of gasoline for a week. The fuel tank and the mower have never been subjected to harsh temperatures and has always been kept in my garage.
justification: Fuel leak in garage, no injuries reported, but potential for fire hazard.

incident_description: After using the electric smoker for the first time, I went to clean it. The metal chips box and drip pan were soaking in the large laundry room sink.  I picked up the washing drip pan and the sharp metal edge cut the side of my left index finger.  It started bleeding, but not real bad.  I put a little pressure on it with a paper towel and then continued to wash the remaining pieces in the sink.  The sink water was soapy and as I put my hand into the water to grab the metal chips box, my hand slipped and the front edge of my right middle finger fell against the side of the box. The metal edges are so sharp, they are like a razor.  My finger was cut down to the bone and the pain was excruciating.  The bleeding would not stop.  I rendered my own first aid, cleaning the wound and wrapping it up tight with bandages. The wound, over one-half inch long, continued to bleed for 3 days.   As I am making out this report, my finger is swollen, continues to throb and is wrapped on a splint.  I may have to seek professional medical attention.  This product has many very sharp razor edges around the chip box and inside of the cabinets which your fingers and hands are supposed to touch.  I returned the product to Lowes who stated they will send to the manufacturer.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury, with the finger cut down to the bone and continuous bleeding for three days, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: While grilling a large 3 foot flame began shooting out from underneath the grill. The flame made it very difficult to reach the propane tank shut off valve. The flame grew bigger very rapidly and it was very fortunate i was able to reach the shut off valve without being burned. Upon further inspection after the tank was shut off, the gas line (hose) was burned at the point where it connects to the grill's regulator valve. The uncontrollable flame burned a hole a few inches down the hose before the gas could be shut off. I called the Aussie support number and was told there was nothing they could do but offer to SELL me replacement parts because the grill was not under its one year warranty. (I purchased the grill roughly 18 months ago.) If this is flaw in craftsmanship while being assembled (this hose came from the factory connected) or flawed materials this represents a HUGE fire safety concern.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the rapid growth of the flame posed a significant risk, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
Sir:

The enclosed information is a result of us using Consumer Reports information.

Materials enclosed is self-explanatory. It is unsafe to operate, I had followed the instructions and three times of collected gas firing-last time burned the hair on my right arm off up to the elbow.

Read the information and notes...... I have had it adios

Sincerely,


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a severe burn, and the product's instructions failed to prevent this, indicating a high likelihood of similar occurrences.

incident_description:
I purchased a clamshell grill model SL1577A from DoughPro in Perris CA. It was duly delivered. We plugged it in and set the operating parameters, but did not put it into use immediately.
On June 23 of this year we experienced a power failure at our place of business. We closed the business and went home. Later my wife had occasion to return to the place of business. Power had been restored and the place full of smoke. The source of the smoke was the mentioned grill - I had left some papers on the grill surface. Checking it the following day I determined that the grill would activate whenever power was connected and run up to its pre-programmed temperature, in this case 450 degrees. I initially thought that the unit had possibly been damaged by a power spike and consulted with the manufacturer on Monday June 25. To my astonishment, the company confirmed that the appliance was working correctly since it was programmed to respond as it did. I told them that it was an unacceptable fire hazard, and that I would not be using the appliance. They agreed to send me a revised chipset. I have rechecked the unit different times and its response is allways the same. Disconnect the power - plug it back in and the unit heats to its programmed values. Any power interruption has the same effect. 
Two months later I again spoke with the same person and she indicated that she would need to speak with a supervisor before taking any action - she had apparently done nothing. Two subsequent voicemail messages went unanswered. 
My next course of action was to contact INTERTEK, the testing agency. Their concerns involve client privacy issues, and informed me that they may not be able to inform me of their investigative findings. 
Meanwhile I will not be using this product until its safety deficiencies are addressed. 
I am, of course, aware that many users of this appliance are likely unaware of this hazard and solicit the assistance of your office in facilitating a solutiom to this problem.

[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the grill's automatic activation upon power restoration poses a significant fire risk, making it likely to cause property damage or injuries in the future.

incident_description: Was using me electric leaf blower the other day when I smelled a burning smell. I noticed there was a bit of smoke coming by the plug in area where my 100 ft. outdoor extension cord was plugged in. I turned the blower off and noticed that the plug in was now melted as well as my extension cord end was melted as well. I inspected the cord and could find no other problems with it, ie. cuts or abrasions that would cause the cord to short out. This is the second time that this has happened to me with virtually the same model and brand of leaf blower. This model is a MTD Yard-Man model #YMESV1300 my previous model was a Ryobi (made by MTD) model #RESV1300. The Ryobi melted the plug on my extension cord so bad that I could not unplug the plug from the extension cord. This time when I smelled the burning smell I unplugged it in time to prevent this from happening. However the damage has been done to both the blower and the cord, rendering them both useless. The right side of the plug in on the blower appears to be the burnt side. Since this has happened to me twice with the the exact same product, I searched the government recall site to see if there was a recall on this product, but could not find one. I feel that there should be as I can't believe that I am the only one that this has happened to and this product is still available for sale.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (both the blower and extension cord were rendered useless), and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the same issue happened with a previous model from the same manufacturer.

incident_description: Toro Ultra Blower/Vacuum power cord melted to extension.  This was the second Toro Ultra Blower/Vacuum we have had this happen too.  The first was replaced and we purchased a new extension cord.  We have taken the current one to the Toro authorized dealer today and they have mailed it away for a replacement.
justification: Although this is the second occurrence, it's not yet a frequent issue, and no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
Toro snowblower #38282 leaked gasoline in my garage and could have burned my house down.
Model #38282 was previously recalled on July 24,2010 by CPSC.
Prtoduct returned to dealer 3/19/2012.
After many calls dealer said Toro refused to cover warranty due to corrosion in carburator.
This is exact reason for previous recall due to fire hazard- release #10-299.
This product is unsafe and dangerous and still being sold.
I purchased product 1/31/2011 from Countryside Lawn in Tinley Park.
Toro should recall and replace.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to a recalled product, which could have led to property damage or injury.

incident_description: The grill was heated and hamburgers were being cooked. We lifted the lid by the handle and removed the burgers. While the lid was lifted the heavy plate fell out of it's space and landed on the countertop. We reattached the plate which took about 20 minutes and made sure it was secure. The second attempt to use it was not successful- the grill plate became detached a second time.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the grill plate falling out twice indicates a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Homelite, the Yard Broom, SH2025UB24RA 10-98, EM08552-01, Mod# UT08074B, S/NHT2801669.
The unit gas tank is leaking  when gas level is higher than the fuel lines causing skin irritation and gas soaked clothing creating a fire hazard. The serial # is within the range listed by [REDACTED] for a safety recall but Homelite hot line stated today that the model # above was not a part of the recall though there are very similar model #s. Gas leaks rapidly from the tank fuel lines creating an extreme fire hazard. If it had not been noticed and use discontinued of the tool, I or one of my children would have been exposed to this defect. Gas tanks like this should not leak especially when the tank is upright and the blower is placed level on a driveway. I did not notice the wetness of the gas on my sleeve until after I had started the blower. The leak starts whenever the fuel level is at the level of the fuel lines either when filled or when the blower is tilted to a position in which the fuel level reaches the lines
justification: The gas leak could have caused skin irritation and created a fire hazard, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description:
Char-Broil Patio Bistro Gas Grill

I purchased the above model grill from Amazon on May 23, 2012. Yesterday I had an incident while using the grill. After the grill was lit and warming up, for some reason the flame went out. I noticed this because after about 5 minutes, the grill was cold. I went to turn off the gas and the explosion that resulted could have seriously injured me. I firmly believe had the cover been closed, which is what I normally do when warming up the grill, it is probable that a serious perhaps even a fatal injury could have occurred. 

The grill has a design defect that must be corrected. Until this defect is corrected, the grill should be removed from the market. I am certain others must have experienced this problem.

The design defect is as follows:
When you turn on the grill using the control knob, the first position you come to is the igniter. This ignites the gas. The problem and defect is that if for any reason the flames goes off,  gas continues to flow into the grill. When you go to turn off the gas, you must pass the same igniter position to turn the gas off. This ignites any accumulated gas causing a potential life threatening situation.
I believe this grill should be removed from the market.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident's potential for serious harm is high due to the grill's design defect.

incident_description:
Husqvarna model gth27v48ls lawn tractor. Main fuel line can contact drive belt for mower section resulting in damaged fuel line and severe fuel leak onto top of mower unit. Any spark and mower could catch fire and/or explode. I'm lucky to be alive right now. I have photos if you wish. It is likely that this problem exists with any Husqvarna riding mower that has the fuel tank under the driver's seat.

This is similar to 10-748.   It would appear that, two years later, Husqvarna is NOT repairing the defect and is continuing to sell product with this potentially deadly flaw.  Perhaps it's time for a mandatory recall?
justification: Potential for severe injury due to fuel leak and spark ignition, given the widespread nature of the issue across Husqvarna riding mowers.

incident_description:
(05/15/2012) The consumer was riding on lawnmower and her shoelace caught on the left side of the mower. There are nubs on the top of the deck. These nubs are used to attach the garden hose.
When her shoelace got caught the consumer stated she fell down on her knees. Her knee was not bruised but it keeps popping and cracking.

06/15/20120) The consumer got on the lawnmower to go over and fed her daughter's animals. She had a pair of bellbottom pants. The pant leg got caught on the left side of the lawnmower. 

The consumer considers this to be a safety hazard because of the placement of the nubs.

The consumer stated that there should be some type of cover over the nubs.
justification: The incident occurred twice with different clothing items, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
No injury occurred except to running into a house and fence.  The steering on my WeedEater One riding lawn mower failed due to a bad design in the steering column.  While mowing forward I went to turn and the steering wheel turned but the front wheels did not, and before I could stop I ran into the side of the house.  Backed up and got the machine lined up to start mowing again in a straight line towards the fence and when I got where I needed to turn it started to turn and then again the steering wheel turned and the wheels did not resulting in a collision with the fence.  I had to get it into my shed where I took the thing apart by removing the steering wheel and the steering adaptor and there I found the problem.  The steering adaptor is made of some sort of plastic and has molded teeth on it and they where all rounded out along with the flats where the steering shaft goes through the center of the steering adaptor.  I know this to be a big problem as I went on-line and there is many complaints about this lawn mower and the steering is a serious safety issue.
I did not find where WeedEater has sent out any safety notice or offered any fix for this problem.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage, and the likelihood of a recurrence is high due to the widespread design flaw.

incident_description: We have a master forge grill that is less than a year old and there was a small fire and the tube that connects the gas tank to the grill dissolved.  I have seen other recalls from the past with this brand but when i tried to get lowes to fix the problem they said my grill wasnt in that recall.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a fire and a malfunctioning gas connection, making it an incident with potential for injury.

incident_description: I have owned a George Forman Grilling Machine for a little over a year.  I like it a lot, until this morning when I woke to a house full of smoke, I thought the house was on fire.  I like, many don't unplug these Grills Model GRP4EWS.  the lights stay on but not the heat, well there were no lights on and it was turning the plates red.  I noticed when turning it over to get this info it looks like the grease has somehow leaked into the bottom part, not sure how this could happen.   This maybe the problum.
justification: The incident caused significant smoke but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the common practice of leaving the grill plugged in.

incident_description: A few nights prior, I had used my Coleman Roadtrip grill to cook some burgers.  Tuesday, I turned on the grill to preheat for a couple of steaks.  After a few minutes of preheat on high temp, I opened the grill to discover the aluminum grill grate had melted.  From reading other reports on the internet, it appears that grease fires can reach temps above aluminum's melting point.  The potential of molten metal in a cooking environment is a serious safety concern.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the melting of the grill grate poses a significant safety risk due to the potential for molten metal in a cooking environment.

incident_description:
The tractor has a transmission that is totally sealed and cannot be maintained.   Five feet down the driveway he noticed no resistance.  He said the brake, is more of a parking brake which did nothing.  He says it was continually gaining speed, got down to the bottom of the hill.  

He could not see from one direction and was headed towards the street. His only path would have been over the street and an embankment and over a creek bed.  He decided to bail out.  He received a rash on both arms, both legs his backs, hands and feet.  He received says the unit failed without any warning.  It failed and is a total design flaw.  He ways the wheels should have locked up and not free wheel
justification: The tractor's transmission failure, lack of functional brakes, and the operator's inability to control the vehicle resulted in injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer says the fuel tank developed a stress crack.  Consequently the fuel leaks out posing a fire hazard.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer yesterday who said that his model is not on recall.  They only offered to sell the customer another tank.  

The consumer says he removed the tank and replaced it with another tank from the same brand lawnmower but a different model.  He says that this tank is now also leaking in the same place.  

The consumer is upset with the company who wont own up to there responsiblity.  He says there are 25-30 online reports of the same thing happening to other customers.  

UPDATE: There is a current recall in effect for leaking fuel tanks on Lawnboy Silver Pro and Gold Pro Series walk behind 21" mowers with the following model numbers- 10247, 10252, 10323, 10324, 10424, 10550, and 10552.  why not expand it to all models which use the same fuel tanks? My mower is a Lawnboy, model #10525, and Lawnboy refuses to acknowledge responsibility.
justification: Multiple reports of fuel tank leaks, posing a fire hazard, and no recall expansion despite using the same fuel tanks.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she turned on the grill it immediately went up in flames.  Her husband unscrewed the propane because they could not shut it off any other way.  

She contacted the manufacturer on July 9th and sent them pictures.  The consumer says that they offered her a refund in exchange for the product.  This was the first time she tried the grill.

The consumer says that they followed all the instruction to her knowledge.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the immediate and intense flames indicate a significant hazard, making it a level 2 severity incident.

incident_description: This report is relates to the Husqvarna model 125B Leaf blower. After running the product for some time, it was turned off normally using the switch. Later, upon attempting to restart the blower, I noticed that gas was spewing out of the fuel line. I called Husqvarna customer support the next day to find out about a remedy and communicate the safety concern of a fire igniting because of the fuel hitting the hot engine. The gentleman at Husqvarna said this fuel line issue was a common problem caused by ethanol in fuel and there was nothing the company would do besides suggest that the customer find a way to get the unit repaired. It seems the manufacturer should take a more proactive view of this type of safety issue. Even providing a few inches of alcohol resistant tubing would seem to address the problem.
justification: Fuel spewing from the line could potentially cause a fire, posing a risk of injury.

incident_description: My wife was using Sears Hedge Trimmer, Model #900.79442.  She got a severe laceration (requiring stitches) on her left index finger.  As she was placing the trimmer on a ledge, she released the trigger.  The trimmer did not turn off and her left finger got too close to the blade.  She did NOT have the trimmer set for continuous run.  Both the trigger and the lock are VERY sticky and I could make the trimmer do the same thing.  The trimmer is stored indoors and is used for light-duty work.  We haved owned it for approx 2yrs.
justification: The severity level is 3 due to the injury requiring stitches, and the occurrence likelihood is 4 as the sticky trigger and lock mechanism made it likely to happen again.

incident_description:
I installed the Dayton Delux Dual Float Controller model 1APP4 to control a sump pump in my crawl space.  It worked fine for 2 years.  One week ago, I smelled buring plastic in my basement.  I could find the source of the smell at first.  Last place that I looked was in the crawl space and saw that the 2X6 that I mounted the float controller to was burned and the plastic on the housing for the float controller was burned and melted.

This failure could have started a fire and burned down my house!
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description:
Caller is visiting brother who has a composite decking outside.
Caller has cerebral palsy (mild C.P.) and walks with a crutch.

She was walking on brother's deck and almost slipped but caught herself.  Consumer's nephew caught her by the left arm if he was not there Consumer would have fallen back on her head and back.  Consumer told this to lady who was taking the report over the phone.  This would have caused a huge risk of injury a serious physical harm to Consumer.

She is reporting this deck because she believes it to be unsafe, stating that a deck is made for walking and if you can't walk on it without slipping on it then it is not safe.

She and her brother contacted the manufacturer with a previous incident on this same deck and does intend to contact them again.

Caller states that In a previous incident last year around Springtime one of CPSC's  Inspectors came out to check the deck out and almost slipped himself but nothing has been changed.
November 10, 2011 the same inspector took a piece of the decking for testing, he doesn't believe it was actually tested and was advised to create another report if anyone slipped on the decking again.

First Report #20110726-F220D-1193563 filed by Mr. [REDACTED]; this report has all the information CPSC needs.  Consumer lives in Florida.  Second Report # 20120813-471B5-1265957 filed by Ms. [REDACTED].

Incident location: Brother's house on a visit to Long Island.

Injury information:  (Consumer twisted her ankle (right) that was it).  Consumer strongly stated this over the phone to the lady over the phone.  This is the second incident that happened to Consumer.  The first was during the Thanksgiving holiday season last year.
justification: The consumer's mild cerebral palsy and use of a crutch increase the likelihood of slips, and the previous incident involving a CPSC inspector supports this.

incident_description:
The caller stated that gas/charcoal grill controlled knobs had melted due overheating.  The grill was in use for approximately 30 mins and then he noticed that one of the knobs had fallen off, the other knob had melted as well.   The grill was turned off to prevent further damages.

5/30/12  The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that there might have been a blockage in the burner tube and that that he should try to clean the  tube.  However, this was not the problem, the grill was being for the third time.
7/24/12 The manufacturer sent out some knobs but the sizes were incorrect.
 The caller feels that the grill is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The grill's knobs melting and falling off due to overheating poses a high likelihood of injury or property damage, despite no immediate harm reported.

incident_description:
An employee was starting a Stihl MS-290 chain saw. Once the saw was started the employee revved the engine twice and the saw exploded in the area of the fuel tank catching the saw on fire and the employees left leg (and chaps) on fire. The employee threw the chain saw to the ground and started rolling to put out the fire on his leg. He was assisted by another employee in the area and the fire dept. and medical services were called for assistance.

The employee was wearing the proper PPE (gloves, chaps, safety glasses, hearing protection). 

After the incident was over the chain saw was inspected by the employees co-workers and the safety department. 

The Stihl web site was researched and found that there was a "Fuel Cap" recall but the chain saw was not listed in the recall. The recall stated that the caps being replaced would have a molded letter "D" or lower on it and the new caps would have a "E" or higher on it. The caps on the saw involved in the incident (and one other saw of the same model) both had the letter "D" on the inside of the cap.

The Stihl phone number for the fuel cap recall was called and they were informed of the incident that had occurred with the saw and that a fuel cap with the letter "D" was on the saw at the time of the incident.

The Stihl representative stated that there were caps on other pieces of equipment that were similar to the recalled caps and that the cap could be replaced at no charge if the cap was taken to a local distributor.

Our concern was that there is a possibility that there are still defective caps on their equipment and that there could possibly be more incidents / injuries because of these caps.
justification: Employee suffered burn injuries due to a defective fuel cap, which is likely still present in other equipment.

incident_description:
In May of 2012, I was driving my kubota BX2230 to a neighbors house about 600 feet down the road.

I noticed a very dangerous "slop" in the steering, but thought the tractor steering was just being very sensitive on a paved surface.
I didn't think much else of the problem until this past week.

Around September 10th, I again noticed "slop" in the steering, this time on grass.  After some investigation, it appears that the steering has stopped responding if you turn the steering wheel slightly, or slowly.  This "slop" occurs all the time while maintaining a straight line.

Sharp motion appears to temporarily restore steering, but it requires a short, sharp motion to steer.

I have an extremely sharp incline in my back yard which I cannot mow now.

Luckily, I was not hurt, but if the steering on these tractors has a design flaw that will cause many people to experience steering failure, people could be hurt badly.

There is quite a bit of information at:
http://www.ssbtractor.com/wwwboard/view_all.cgi?bd=kubota&msg=8684

There needs to be a recall of all Kubota tractors with this faulty steering setup, and a safety replacement for all tractors experiencing the problem, with a NEW, properly engineered steering cylinder.

Please do call with any questions.  [REDACTED]
justification: Potential for serious injury due to steering failure, as evidenced by the user's experience and online forum discussions.

incident_description: Had Perfect Flame GAC3615 since 2007.  Worked fine, no issues, hardly used.  Kept BBQ clean and covered in a garage.  We started to use more in 2012, and on 9/16/12 the unit burst into flames.  Wrote down the customer service information, looked online to find grill had been recalled. We were unaware of the recall.   Will return to Lowes as soon as possible with printout from web site.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the grill bursting into flames is a significant incident, and the likelihood of it happening again, given the recall, is possible.

incident_description:
In May 2012, we purchased a Webber (Genesis E320) from Home Depot. We soon noticed that the ÃÂgrease trayÃÂ which is supposed to direct away the grease into the waste container, has a few design flaws. 
1. The Grease Tray was not properly directing the grease away and into the waste container; causing the grease to remain in the tray.
2. Grease Tray was located too close to the heat source; causing the grease to burn and make gross smelling smoke.

We had to manually clean the grease tray after each use since the grease was not led to the waste container.

On Wednesday September 12, we grilled 2 T-bone steaks. The meat had some fat and the drips were creating some smoke. I opened the BBQ to check the meat and suddenly the whole BBQ went on "FIRE"!!! I am pregnant (on a high risk pregnancy) and I was totally shocked and scared. I turned off all the keys and shut the door and turned to run inside to inform my husband. But as I turned I caught into a chair and fell on the ground. My 7 year old daughter just opened the door and called for help. My husband helped me move away and got the fire extinguisher and turned off the fire. Although he also burned the palm of his hand as the handle was too hot and the fire was everywhere.

We are totally frustrated to be sold an ÃÂunsafeÃÂ product which has a fire safety issues. We would like to get our money back and also an investigation be issued on the safety of this product and a possible "RECALL".
justification: Injury occurred (burn on husband's hand) and the incident was likely to happen due to design flaws and improper grease management.

incident_description:
I BOUGHT A MASTER FORGE GRILL GD 4825 AT LOWES ON 3/26/2012 .... .I WAS GRILLING AND THE RUBBER HOSE
THAT GOES FROM THE TANK TO THE BURNER BOX MELTED AND BURNT THE GRILL FRONT, Bottom ,SIDE AND LID.
IT ALSO BURNT MY DECK RAILINGS BEFORE I COULD GET IT PUT OUT. IT COULD OF BEEN A LOT WORST. I CALLED
THERE CUSTOMER SERVICE DEPT. 1-800-963-0211AND THEY STATED THEY COULD ONLY GIVE ME THE HOSE
REPLACEMENT PART.
I DO NOT WANT A REPLACEMENT PART I WANT MY MONEY BACK. ALSO ,MASTER FORGE HAS ANOTHER RECALL
FOR THE SAME PROBLEM (model # L3218 -SOLD BETWEEN SEPR 2009 - NOV 2009 ). WHY ARE THEY STILL ALLOWED
TO MAKE THESE PARTS .... .ITS PROBLEY BECAUSE ITS CHINA.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant property damage (burnt grill and deck railings), indicating a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had charcoal grill and a small camp fire on. The consumer stated that he also had a camping propane gas stove that was located on top of the picnic table. The consumer stated that he went to screw the can of propane on the tube that connects to the stove. The consumer stated that in the process of screwing the propane can the tube that connects to the stove came apart from the metal that screws to the can. 

The consumer started that gas was being splatter everywhere. The consumer stated that he unscrew the top of the propane can to stop it from splattering. 

The consumers stated that they could have exploded or cause a fire due to the fact that they had fires around the area. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that in 30 years they had not received any reports of this incident happened. The consumer stated that the representative asked him to call back next week for further assistance.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved a significant gas leak near open flames, posing a high risk of fire or explosion.

incident_description:
Master Forge Grill GR4039-014247
Grill would not  light.  The igniter electrode is at the end of a u-tube burner.  The gas enters at the center of the U, far from the igniter. An inordinant amount of gas fills the grill before ignition is possible.  I didn't try to ignite as the gas was strong.

There was no C- or E-clip on on the valve assembly.  It slipped out of the grill.  Fortunately it wasn't lit.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in a fire or explosion due to excessive gas buildup, making it an incident with potential for injury.

incident_description:
(08/06/2012) 
The consumer stated that the repair technician came out because the consumer could not turn the burner off.  The technician looked at the burner and decided that he could not turn it off either. 

The consumer stated that the technician said he would order need to order a gas valve (serial W10177101). The technician stated that the valve would arrive 08/9/2012. 

The consumer stated that when the part did not arrive at his home, he call the repair service and discovered that the part was back-ordered. The consumer stated that he then called LoweÃÂs and discovered that no one had this particular part. 

The consumer stated that he is concerned because the only way that the stove can be used is by turning the gas supply on and off. 

The consumer stated when he called the manufacturer, they considered it a safety issue and a technician was sent immediately to his home.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a safety issue with a gas stove, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2). The likelihood is 'Possible' (3) as the part was back-ordered and the consumer had to manually control the gas supply.

incident_description: Today, (8/23) I was blowing my porch when the blower short circuited causing a large hole in my left leg, bruising the skin and flesh. This injury is very painful. I was wearing rubber soles on a wooden porch. This should not have happened. I believe you should notify dealers of this defect. I contacted Lowes as directed by the Base Exchange (Moody AFB, Valdosta, GA) where the puchase was made. On second look, it appears that something came loose and came through the housing hitting my cutting my leg causing a lot of pain and blood.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, but the likelihood of occurrence is not high due to the specific circumstances.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his friend was using his new gas trimmer for approximately 2 hours. The consumer stated that when his friend finished his faced was burnt and that he did not burnt his eyes because he had glasses on. 

The consumer stated that he noticed that the reason why his face was burnt was because the exhaust system was located in a way where the heat was released towards the operator. 

The consumer stated that his friend used a burn ointment to treat the burns on his face. 

The consumer stated that his friend did not have to go to the emergency room. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and filed a complaint. 

The consumer believes this product should be investigated due to the burn hazard that it poses to the consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the face, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and the design flaw causing this is likely to recur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: My brand new grill caught my deck handrail on fire.  This grill was placed in the same location as my old grill on my deck.  The heat that came out the backside of the grill was unbelievable.  Luckily the handrail was just smoldering when I went to check on the steaks and I was able to put it out with a garden hose.  I went back to their manual and it states that the grill needs a minimum clearance of 36" from combustible constructions to the sides and back of the grill.  How many people have over a 3' clearance?  This is like an open flame hanging over a propane tank.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have escalated to a more severe level given the grill's proximity to combustible materials.

incident_description:
On March 24, 2012, I purchased a Weber Spirit E-210 gas grill for $399.00 (before tax) at the Home Depot store located [REDACTED] Fort Worth, TX 76137 [REDACTED]. In addition, on the same date, I purchased a propane tank pre-loaded with propane gas at the same Home Depot for 43.92 (before tax).  I also purchased a long-handled grill brush (9.99 before tax) and a 4-piece BBQ tool set (9.97 before tax).

I used the gas grill on several occasions between the date of purchase and September 9, 2012, and never noticed any problems or had any issues with the grill.  However, when I went out to grill two hamburger patties and one link of [REDACTED] sausage on Sunday, September 9, 2012, I heated the grill up and cleaned the grates as I normally do.  Once the grill had been pre-heated (about 5 minutes), I placed the food on the grates.  I sat out by the grill as I was cooking because I always turn the meat over after it has cooked 6 minutes on the first side.  After my food had been on the grill for 5 minutes, I started hearing this ÃÂwhooshingÃÂ sound and jumped up to see what was happening.  I went over to the grill and noticed flames were coming out the sides of the cooking area.  I was going to open the lid to the grill to alleviate the flames, when I noticed flames were also within the bottom cabinet area (where the propane tank sits).  I would have attempted to turn the propane tank off; however there were too many flames within the cabinet area to stick my hand in there.  As these few seconds went by, I suddenly heard a loud popping sound, like a firecracker.  At that point, it was very clear to me that the grill was about to explode.  So I ran into the house and called 911.  While I was on the phone with 911 within by kitchen, I heard a loud boom.  ThatÃÂs when the first explosion took place.  So I ran out to my front yard to get as far as away from the grill as possible while I was on the phone with the fire department.  At that time, I heard a second loud boom while I was on the phone with 911 and told the fire department to hurry.  I was fairly certain that the back part of home was going to catch fire from the explosions, but thankfully that did not happen.
I was not injured.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard with two explosions, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Purchased a LED flashlight at Home Depot. The flashlight is a 50 LED model made by a company called DEFIANT. The UPC on the package is 2090994039. It is made in China. I inserted the batteries into the flashing as directed (4 AA that were included) and tried to turn the flashlight on. When the flashlight didn't work, I took the batteries out and was burned on two fingers by two of the batteries that were obviously shorting out in the battery carrier. I tried to insert the batteries several more times with the same results. It is fortunate that I removed the batteries or they may have exploded. I will be returning the flashlight to Home Depot in the next couple of days.
justification: The flashlight's battery carrier shorted out, causing burns, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Purchased a Master Forge 2-burner gas grill Model MFA350CNP at Lowe's in July 2011. Just noticed a gas leak from regulator (Chant AZF 1049 model) This regulator was the main factor in a recall of [REDACTED] gas grills but I haven't seen a recall of Master Forge models with this regulator.
If the grill were used with this leak, it would almost certainly cause a fire and or explosion with no way to mitigate until it burned or blew itself out. the leak (regulator) is right next to the QCC coupling nut at the tank valve.
I will be contacting the manufacturer for relief but the recall / warning initiated for [REDACTED] grills should be expanded to include all grills with this Chant series / date code regulator.
Grill has been kept covered and is otherwise in great shape.
justification: Gas leak from regulator poses high risk of fire or explosion, but no injuries reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the drive shaft housing which is the only connector between motor assembly and gear box assembly ripped in two allowing for the motor to flop around on the top. 

 The consumer says this would allow gas and oil allowing to spoil over a hot muffler. 

 The consumer contacted the retailer who said there is no recall.  there are other several parts (plastic and foam) that is in the way so you cannot really see whats happening unless thoroughly inspected.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to leaked gas and oil coming into contact with a hot muffler, but no immediate injury reported.

incident_description: The connection between a Weber Platinum propane BBQ grill and a 20 pound propane tank failed. I have had 2 such failures this year. In each case the black plastic threaded connector, the nut that connects the supply hose to the tank, failed by cracking apart. I suspect a thermal expansion mismatch between the plastic and the brass parts on the tank. The BBQ is outside, mostly shaded and the connection is in the shade, but subject to daily temperature fluctuations. If you do not notice the crack and turn the tank on propane will leak out creating a fire hazard.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the propane leak poses a significant fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Purchased new in June this year.  Cub Cadet Garden Tractor Model GTX2100.  It had 31 hours the first time the hood melted off.  It got a second hood and heat shield modification.  It melted the hood off again.  It is now getting its third hood installed (under warranty) and they've stated they will Not refund my money.  It emits an unpleasant odor from the engine bay while mowing, and disfigures the hood horribly. The oil drain line that rests beside the engine is also melting.
justification: The incident has occurred twice despite modifications, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

Luckily it tripped the breaker and we caught it in time before any major damage happened.  Lowes replaced the light for us and we haven't had any trouble since.
