incident_description: An extension spring on the deck keeps breaking (two within 3 months) which shuts off the mower deck while in motion. The piece of metal off the spring comes off the deck and is hit by the mower blades which sends flying to who knows where. I took my mower to the Cub Cadet Dealer and they said this is a reoccurring problem with these mowers and Cub Cadet has done nothing to make a better quality spring. This mower is a year old and has been under warranty, but this is a defect in the manufacturing which creates a safety hazard for anyone or anything who is near the mower when the spring breaks. The cub cadet part number is 732-04229	 Extension Spring, .75 x 6.02.
justification: The recurring issue of the extension spring breaking poses a high likelihood of incident, as it has happened twice in three months, and the dealer confirms it's a reoccurring problem.

incident_description:
I have a Perfect Flame gas grill I purchased from Lowes about 3 years ago model #276964L. For the past year, all the burners have been corroding and we get uneven gas flow. I have tried cleaning all and trying to get it to work again. When we do, it usually erupts in a big "poof" of a fireball. We have learned how to light it (the electronic spark stopped working after 6 months so we have to thorw matches at it or use an extended lighter with the lid mostly closed. On several occasions we have ended up with signed arm hairs and other less than helpful side effects. I only recently learned that the company who imported these [REDACTED] was forced to recall many models. Mine is not one of them. I have tried to replace the burners themselves but these are held in place by thick iron bars welded into the frame and thus making it impossible to change. 

I suspect these are the VERY SAME BURNERS used in the recalled units. Lowes gave me the 800 number for the main company  who imported this and they stated my model was not under the forced recall so I am out of luck. They gave me another number to complain but all that was buck passing back to Lowes who was the retailer of this [REDACTED] unsafe product. I do not mind changing burners but the design makes it impossible here. I have disconnected the propane tank from this thing but wish to force another investigation into this company purposely selling dangerous products and knowingly doing so. PLEASE HELP!!!
justification: The grill's design makes it difficult to replace faulty burners, leading to frequent fireballs and potential burns.

incident_description: I purchased a Jenn-Air Gas Grill Model Jenn-Air 720-0709 sold at Sam's Club.  After four months of use, we stopped using the product due to the propensity of the unit to catch on fire even under controlled conditions.  We experienced two serious fires.  After the first incident, I inspected the unit for debri, leaks, or any other defect and found none.  However, I did noticed while attempting to clean the unit, that the design of this unit has two layered grease pans at the bottom of the firebox.  The layered pans are fix welded to the unit and spaced in between about 1/2" with the top one having a center drain sloping toward the center in which drippings fall to the next layer.  We believe the root cause of the fires is the design of these two layers.  The concentration of the right amount of drippings, heat, contiguous fire source, and spacing of the drip prans appears to be condition leading to these two fire events.  During both incidents, flames and black smoke occurred.  The flames spread to throughout the unit shooting out from behind, on front of the control knobs, and under the firebox.  The biggest concern for safety was the risk associated with flames reaching the hose and propane tank underneath considering that we were not able to control the fire after turning off the valves.  We were required to use a fire extinguisher to put out the fire.
justification: The grill's design, with layered grease pans, led to two serious fire incidents, posing a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The Weber Genesis S-330 was purchased new from Lowe's in West Windsor NJ. It was delivered on 08/30 and setup as per instructions in the manual.
The regulator leaked as soon as the propane gas tank was opened. Lowe's was informed the same day and the grill was replaced on 09/01 at around 9 AM. This one did not leak after original installation and passed the soap-solution test.
At 6 PM on 9/1 the grill was put to use. After about 30 minutes, the regulator attached to the propane cylinder caught fire, with the fire engulfing the interior of the grill cabinet. The thermal nut did not shut off. The flame kept on increasing for about 6-8 seconds during the time it took to access the grill, get the protection and shut off the tank tap.

Melted plastic is still stuck to the cloth used to shut off the valve and the hand suffered scalds with burnt hair. The regulator periphery has melted.

Hopefully this will be investigated.
justification: Injury occurred due to fire from leaking regulator, despite replacement and initial testing.

incident_description: trimmer/edger emmited smoke and burning odor from motor housing

incident_description:
Ryobi 48V Self Propelled Battery Powered Lawn Mower model: RY14110

While I was out traveling, [REDACTED] called me and said there was a sulfur smell throughout the lower floor of the house to the point she and our children couldn't stay in the house because they were having trouble breathing. I had her call Atlanta Gas and Light to come out and check for any gas leaks. What AGL found with their detection meters, instead, was that the lawnmower was giving off toxic levels of gasses (can't remember which) and trace amounts of carbon monoxide (not enough CO to set off our carbon monoxide alarm). Unplugging and moving the mower outside almost immediately caused the levels to drop. I have since moved it back inside but haven't plugged it back in. Without it plugged in, it is not emitting any odor. So I suspect the battery and/or charging circuitry is problematic up in some way.

I am about to call Ryobi to get the lawnmower fixed or replaced, so don't have any more information on the nature of the issue.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident caused significant discomfort and temporary evacuation, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
O Turn Lawn mower purchased at Beards Outdoor Power Equipment 6159 West Highway146 in Crest wood, KY 1(502) 241-7222 around May 5th, 2006 for the price of $6325.99,  
The mower presently has 156 hours of use on it.

Blades are continuously coming loose and seat are separated from the metal frame.

He had the blades sharpened about 2007 at the Beards Simplicity Repair Facility where he purchased it and that is when the blades began coming loose.

[REDACTED] who is manager at same repair facility (Beards) advised caller that there was nothing they could do about the seat.                                                                                    

He has tightened blades with a impact gun which tightens tighter than recommended torque but they still come loose.  The factory bolt is too long.  It needs a washer or be made with a shorter bolt so the blades stay tight to torque against the blade.

 

Lawn mower seat began coming loose around 2009 just after the warranty ran out.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
He is reporting this lawn mower as a safety risk due to the ability of the blades to come out if he did not notice looseness and could injure someone and he could also fall out of the seat as it became completely loose from its frame.

He has not been able to contact the manufacturer because he states that they can only be contacted via email and he doesn't know anything about that.

 Consumer also had to replace fuel solonoid oil. In 2008 the dealer called rep about the seat and said they would not fix it.  I believe this to be a big safety citation approx. 120 hours when incident occurred.
justification: Loose blades could cause injury, and a completely loose seat could lead to falls, both likely to occur given the history of the issues.

incident_description: My grandson was using a model 749 John Deere Lawn Tractor Mower.  On this model when you back up you have  to pull up the pto control switch to prevent the mower blades shutting off.  Because the blades shut off with any pressure on the reverse pedal the tendency is to pull up the pto switch while still moving forward.  My grandson apparently did this but because of the proximity of the cruise control switch which is immediately adjacent he accidentally engaged the cruise control.  He was approaching a 6 foot drop off and in an attempt to stop he stepped on the reverse pedal, the forward and reverse of the equipment is controlled by pedals.  However the cruise control cannot be disengaged this way and he went over the 6 foot wall sustaining a concussion and various injuries.  Luckily he is doing fine with no ongoing problems.  While I realize that the machine was operated in a manner not consistent with the manual I have concerns with the design because I believe the manner in which the machine is likely to be used this senario could repeat.  I feel it was poor design to place the cruise control and the pto switch adjacent such that it is relatively easy to pull up both simultaneously.  I also think a natural reaction to stop forward motion is to hit reverse and am concerned that this does not disengage the cruise control.  I have reported this incident to John Deere and they have stated they will look into the issues but thought it best I also report here.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries, and the design flaw increases the likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description:
Purchased a LEHR string trimmer (under Sears Craftsman name brand)

After approx. 2 years of use, the high pressure (Pre Pressure regulator) propane line failed causing propane gas to escape violently creating a fire , explosive, and general safety hazard.

Attempting to order a replacement part I found this part on backorder. 

Also there are numerous other complaints found via a simple google search of a simple failure.


Seen in link below

https://www.google.com/search?q=%22lehr%22+propane+leak&sugexp=chrome,mod=15&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8

Finally, when the repair part arrived it came with specific replacement instructions indicative that this was a systemic problem  and not an isolated event.

The severity of a failure of this nature combined with the high frequency of it happening makes this a high risk tool.
justification: The incident resulted in a fire and safety hazard, but no injuries were reported, and the likelihood of occurrence is high due to numerous complaints and systemic issues.

incident_description: Two wall mounted exterior lanterns which had fire/shortage causing circuit breaker trip, smoke and electric fire smell.  Occurred when lights were turned on.   They were on same switch but issue occurred on each lantern separately (March 2012 and August 2012).  First incident homeowner wasn't home when incident occurred but appeared as if there had been a fire in the lantern.  Second incident occurred with direct observation of smoke (no flames).

incident_description:
On June 30th, 2012 the caller turned his grill on, cooked food for party then turned valves off.

Did not notice right away that the heat just kept rising, after about five minutes later he saw heat coming from grill, went to it and viewed thermometer which was reading over 500 degrees.

He looked underneath and saw that the rubber hose was in flames and leaking propane.

He then shut the valve off to the propane also, the flames then extinguished but caller took the hose and sprayed the entire grill down with water.

July 5th, 2012 He contacted the manufacturer via phone and email, spoke with female named [REDACTED] who told him this grill is not on warranty, not on recall so they could not help him other than to sell him the replacement parts needed to repair grill.

He discovered through this contact that the rubber hose on his grill is now replaced with a flexible metal hose.

He states that he is an engineer and that if the rubber hose was replaced by metal hose then it has been replaced due to an issue of some sort with this product.

Caller would like the public notified of the danger, his grill repaired or replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to a leaking propane hose, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Brand new weed wacker Hitachi model # CG 22EAB(SLP) serial # J100659. While using weed wacker after 1/2 hr of use smell of burning plastic came from housing. Shut off unit and observed that the area of the housing containing the engine where the shaft enters had melted resulting in a circular crack around the shaft.  I brought the unit to the certified Hitachi repair shop where it remains. My concern is as a result of the plastic melting could the shaft have come lose, could the unit have caught fire.

incident_description:
Our weber grill (spirit) caught on fire. The fire destroyed the control knobs and the lines from the propane gas to the control knobs. Thankfully, we saw the fire and immediately took the propane gas away and contained the fire.  The grill was turned off but the propane gas was not. We are not sure what caused the fire but it could have been out of control if we were not in the immediate area to douse the fire. We only had the grill for two years and used it at least an average of two times during the summer months. 

Thank you.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Husqvarna 455 rancher chainsaw, 20 inch bar and chain, approximately 5 years old,  during routine use with brand new husqvarna chain.

While cutting, chain departed bar, unbroken, was ejected rearward, struck crankcase of chainsaw, punctured gasoline reservoir, approximately 3/16 to 1/4 inch diameter  hole, with resultant gas pouring out of running, hot, chainsaw.

Chance of fire, explosion, and injury or death is significant in this circumstance.

I telephoned consumer support line at husqvarna, spoke with [redacted] on 20 august at 1930 hours.  He took no name or contact info.  Suggested I might return to store where I purchased it to "see if they would do something," or take it to a local dealer, presumably for repair.  I indicated during my initial contact with him that it was not a warranty claim nor request for repair location, but a concern about safety about which I hoped the company would be concerned, perhaps wish to see the saw, etc.  When I reiterated that he suggested I send a letter to the "corporate office," and provided their mailing address.  I asked if there was a department or person to whom to address it, and he said "safety.". I will write such a letter but have little confidence in their interest in a fire/explosion hazard based on their representative's lack of enthusiasm to record any details, ask if I was injured, get a call back number, or offer to pass along my concern.

[redacted]
justification: The chainsaw's chain departing the bar and puncturing the gasoline reservoir poses a significant risk of fire or explosion, but no injuries were reported.

He says this cannot be seen normally.  He only noticed after thorough inspection.  He feels that there needs to be a recall on this product. incident_description: We were using the side burner on our grill to do a seafood boil.  The gas hose melted at the connection to the burner and caught on fire.  The hose was shooting propane & fire on our wood deck.  Luckily we were standing near it and could shut off the valve on the gas tank.  No one was injured.  2 months later, our friend with the same grill had the same thing happen to him.

incident_description:
Was mowing with 2009 Cub Cadet Model SLTX 1054 when steering failed. The failed steering almost caused a serious accident which could have resulted in the mower going into a large pond. I disassembled the steering assembly to find a flange made of oilite material that had 'ovaled' out due to absence of lubrication causing the pinion gear to lose contact with the steering gear. Teeth were damaged on steering gear which resulted in steering lock-up and inability to turn mower to the left. When attempts were made to turn to left, a popping noise was heard which was caused by the gear slipping. Flange has no lubrication point/access and dirty conditions would prevent this type of fitting from being an acceptable application for it's intended purpose.

This is a serious safety hazard since control of the lawn mower is prudent for safe operation. I have found research that shows Cub Cadet is aware of this issue and most dealers stock parts to repair it. Parts are NOT redesigned and the same flawed parts that one buys for repair will fail again because flange is not a sealed bearing in a housing which would prevent this from occurring.

Pictures of failed parts are available if needed.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have resulted in a serious accident, making it a significant safety hazard.

incident_description:
When I went to start my 4 month old Toro gasoline string trimmer, gasoline leaked all over the trimmer creating a very hazardous situation. I called the Toro support number and was directed to call the local repair facility (Lake Small Engine Repair, [REDACTED], Somerset, NJ 08873 - [REDACTED]. I was informed by the repair facility that fuel problems are usually not covered by the 3 year warranty that came with the trimmer & that I would have to give them $25 before they would even look at the machine. I explained to them that a rubber fuel hose broke off. They stated that this was a common occurrence and that the replacement part they used was not made from rubber, and was better able to resist the oil-gasoline fuel mixture.
No injuries resulted from this incident, but much of the trimmer's engine was covered in gasoline.
I ended up replacing the fuel line myself. The replacement line was not rubber (it is either plastic or some type of poly material), and was designed for fuel being used in small engines. The cost of the line was $4.76.
justification: Gasoline leakage created a hazardous situation but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: An 11 month old baby was placed in a wagon. A "Coleman 4D Quick Pump" was also in the wagon. The air pump contained 4 D-size batteries. The baby began to cry and the parents initially were unsure what provoked the crying. When they picked up the baby, they discovered that potassium chloride from the alkaline batteries had leaked and was burning the baby's posterior thigh. The baby's diaper also absorbed the battery fluid.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the baby due to battery fluid leakage, making it a 'possible' occurrence given the presence of batteries in the wagon.

incident_description:
While on recent camping trip I was cooking breakfast when the regulator on my camping stove started to have flames come out of the side  I quickly shut it off at stove and blew flames out then disconnected the regulator. My first thoughts was that I might have cross threaded the small propane bottle so I reinstalled the bottle and heard the gas escapeing out of the regulator top.  I Quickly removed bottle. after I got home I decided to recheck to see if it was something minor that caused problem I found after disensembling unit that it has a rubber O shaped washer that sit on top of a (valve stem type device ) the rubber washer had a hole in it so that is where the gas leaked pass.

I have contacted the company to see if they knew of such a problem, I'am sill getting information back but thought if I had this happen what could happen to some other family it could cause a big fire or even explode if not caught quickly.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a gas leak which could have led to a fire or explosion if not promptly addressed.

incident_description: I own a Sears Lawn Tractor (model 917.272672). On the metal mower deck there is a plastic mulcher cover (part 136420) over an opening that allows the mower to be a mulcher or throw the grass to the side. This plastic mulcher cover covers a large opening directly over the mower baldes which protects the rider from the sharp spinning mower blades and objects that might be thrown up by the blades. The mower deck itself is thick steel to provide protection from the blades and thrown objects. The original mulcher cover on my lawn tractor was damaged and needed replacement. I ordered the replacement part from Sears. The replacement part they sent to me is not the same as the original part and does not fit properly....the rear rubber strap that holds the cover is way too short. The mulcher cover has protrusions on the bottom to fit into holes in the steel mower deck which my mower does not have. It has a small hole in the top of the cover that allows grass and potentially small objects to be thrown at the rider. I have talked with Sears and they insist this is the correct replacment part. It is not the correct part and leads to a poorly fitting mulcher cover. If this cover comes off, it puts the user at great risk of stepping into the moving mower blades or having objects thrown at the user off the mower blades. Sears has refused to do anything to correct this hazard which likely impacts many users of their lawn tractors.
justification: The improperly fitting mulcher cover increases the likelihood of the cover coming off, exposing the user to spinning blades or thrown objects, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description:
We have been purchasing the Utilitech #0042122 75w Landscape Light with Sensor for several years now from Lowe's and have been very satisfied.  All we have to do is change the halogen bulb when it burns out.  Earlier this year on April 23, 2012 we purchased 6 more at Lowe's.  So far 3 of them have exploded and the last one took out our GFI plug so we had to have someone replace it.  The glass shatters and unit is dead.  Lowe's has been refunding our money and we told them the problem, but we also wrote to the company Cooper Lighting to tell them that this batch of lights is bad and dangerous.  The number on the box bottom of the bad box is 625-1494.  The good batch is 625-0226.  The bad batch has a CAution: Risk of Fire other numbers on the box are 0212 IC50030301229574.  The old box had no caution. The new box is 7 inches high and the old box was 11 1/2 inches high. We asked where we can get the old batch of lights.  We said we know why the new box has "risk of fire" and the old box did not have that caution.  We told them these lights are dangerous and we are going to contact our state attorney general.  We know Cooper Lighting is not in Michigan, but the Lowe's stores that carry these lights are.

We have one more light from this batch never used in a box. But we don't know if it will explode or not.

 

Date of purchase April 23, 2012

Dates of returns July 5, 2012, July 31, 2012, August 4, 2012 - had new gfi plug installed

 

 

Cooper Lighting

1121 Highway 74 South

Peachtree City, GA 30269

770-486-4800

Contact Cooper Lighting
justification: Lights have exploded, causing injury (shattered glass) and property damage (GFI plug replacement).

incident_description: The steering gear on my MTD Yard Machine lawn tractor has broken twice now.  This reaults in a loss of steering ability while using the mower creating a hazard for the operator as well as anyone in the path of the mower.  The mower is used only at my vacation home and has seen very little use for its age.  I would estimate that it has accumulated only 50-75 hours of use.  The steering gear that fails appears to be constructed by stamping sheet steel and the pinion gear that interacts with it is a solid metal piece.  Both times the gear has failed now, the same pattern has occurred.  First one tooth fails or breaks and the rest of the teeth then break off one at time in rather rapid succession resulting in the total loss of control of the direction of travel.  The lawn tractor is model #13A1762F729 and the gear that has failed is listed as Part #617-04024A.  The serial # of my unit is 1E317B30413.  The 1st failure was approximately August 2010 and the second this week - August 2012.
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the repeated failure of the steering gear poses a high likelihood of an incident, as it could lead to loss of control and potential injury.

incident_description: The grill's regulator leaked and caught fire and the product is only about one year old, so I think that the regulator might contain a defect that poses a fire and explosion hazard. The incident occurred on August 11, 2012 and we were all at a family reunion when it occurred. My uncle was cooking on it and then all of a sudden the grill stopped working correctly. When another person tried to fix it, it caught fire. There were no injuries, however.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire hazard due to a regulator defect, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: While my wife was cutting our lawn the Craftsman lawn mower engine exploded shooting pieces of hot metal, as large as 3", out the right side of the mower.  If these hot metal pieces had ejected to the rear, my wife could have been seriously injured if not burned by the hot metal
justification: The incident involved an engine explosion with hot metal pieces, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Master Forge Grill model #L3218. Purchased at Lowes on September 13, 2010.
Grill catches on fire when using low-med heat settings!  Flames were coming out all sides of grill from the grill top to down under the burners.  All that was cooking at the time was about 12 chicken wings!  Husband was able to disconnet propane tank or else we would have had a totally different outcome.  There was also a smell of melting plastic.  This grill came with the hose regulator clamp that was the issue of previous recall notice.  This problem is definatly something different. After this happened to us this evening, i was able to find several over posts online of people having the same issue. After reading that we were not the only ones, I thought I better report this problem.  For us it happened very quickly, wings were almost done cooking so my husband came into the kitchen to get a plate, he walked back out the door and started yelling that the grill was on fire!  It happened in less than a minutes time.  While we think our garage door may have melted some (have to see in daylight tomorrow) it could have been a lot worse if my husband wasn't able to disconnet that propane tank!
Thank you for your time on this issue.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and multiple online reports indicate a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: We have a Kubota BX 2230 Tractor for home use, lawn mowing and light hauling and often the steering goes out.  Sometimes it works fine and then all of a sudden you can turn the steering while over and over and no reaction from the tires.  We have had it in to our local Kubota dealer in [REDACTED] and they said it was probably due to an issue with the hydraulic system we were having.  It's worse since we got it back.
justification: Steering failure is recurring and unpredictable, posing a significant risk of accidents.

incident_description:
I have owned a Char-Broil Commercial Series infrared grill for almost 3 years, so it is beyond the 2 year warranty.  Recently when removing the grill grates, emitter surfaces and flame tamers for cleaning I noted that the firebox flange which supports the flame tamers had corroded sufficiently to become detached from the firebox itself as the welds attaching it were completely destroyed.  This allowed the flame tamers to drop closer to the burners which I believed might create a safety hazard.  In June I reported this to Char-Broil through an on-line chat at their website and the technician I chatted with agreed that it may make the grill less safe.  He offered to sell a replacement firebox but could not tell me whether the firebox had been revised to prevent this problem from recurring 2ÃÂ½ years from now.  He also suggested calling customer service directly as he could not do anything but sell the parts.

Today I spoke with their customer support and confirmed that purchasing an entire firebox is the only option I have.  I also confirmed that there had been no design or material improvements to suggest that the replacement box would last any longer than the original.  The customer service rep did seem concerned whether I was using the grill at a temperature too high, suggesting that high temperatures may be at issue here.  I responded that the maximum temperature capability of the grill would be determined by the orifice diameter that Char-Broil provided in the natural gas conversion kit and that I could find nothing in the literature provided with the grill that even hinted that using the grill on high would present a problem of any sort.  Since the grill is an infrared model, much is made of the benefits of searing the meat.  Further, the four temperature gauges on the front of the grill stopped working the first year I owned it.
justification: Potential safety hazard due to corrosion leading to detachment of firebox flange, but no reported injuries or incidents yet.

I had the Master Forge Grill, MFA350CNP, for less than a year and used it on a regular basis.  I turned it on to heat prior to grilling.  About five minutes later I noticed a fire in the area by the tank by the regulator.  Because it was a decent fire and it was dealing with propane, I called the fire department and they put it out.

I noticed on the Internet that there has been a problem with the regulator, maybe leaking gas.  I have worked with Lowe's to return the grill (manager was helpful) but I'm trying to understand more about the grill and other issues as I have seen some incidents reported on the Internet.  

Because Master Forge grills are made in China, they do not have a headquarters here in the U.S.A. The # that is inside the door to the grill is the parts department and appears to authorize RMAs to Lowe's -- they are not Master Forge.  

You call Lowe's Corp Office, they have you work with the local store, then local store sends you to the parts #.  With this being a Lowe's brand, my initial thought is Lowe's corporate would be handling this situation.  

I had to replace some siding because of the heat from the fire was very intense.  My concern is there could be a global issue with this grill.  Lowe's is still selling it.  I'm thinking their thought is since the regulator has been replaced in future grills, it is ok to sell.

I did learn I do need to return that information card so in case there is an issue, the company can contact me regarding recalls.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, posing a high likelihood of future occurrences given the reported regulator issues.

incident_description:
This complaint is about a safety issue with a Sears Kenmore Outdoor LP Gas Grill.  It concerns the gas coupling/regulator assembly that appears to be OEM from GLOBAL ILLIDA.  Note: This part may be commonly used on many makes and models of gas grills that are sold by many different companies under different names. 

The gas coupling/regulator assembly "blew apart" under pressure after it was attached to the LP Gas Tank OPD and the valve was opened.  The failure was not instantaneous.  It "blew apart" after the valve was opened and the system was under pressure for a few seconds.  The black plastic gas coupling thread assembly remained attached to the LP Gas Tank OPD valve and the regulator assembly broke away and was forcefully ejected from the OPD valve.  I did not notice anything wrong with the unit before using it.  It was last used the weekend of June 23rd.  The unit is stored indoors and wheeled outside and connected to the LP tank prior to each use, usually on the weekends.

The regulator just missed hitting my face.  I had been bent over to open the tank valve and was returning to an upright position.  My hand was removed from the valve and I was starting to stand back up.  The coupler/regulator assembly  "blew apart" approximately two seconds after opening the valve.  There was a loud popping sound as the assembly failed and the regulator was ejected.  Since the regulator remained attached to the flexible rubber gas line, it whipped in an arc and I dodged back and out of the way.  No one was injured.

I contacted Sears Kenmore to report the failure and request repair/replacement of the part.  They refused citing the fact that the product was purchased on 6/2/2011 and it was now 6/29/2012.  The product is covered by a one year full warranty and five year limited warranty on the burners.  I was requesting a courtesy repair since the failure occurred so closely to the one year anniversary.  The product was purchased on 6/2/2011, but was assembled later and placed in service approximately 6/11/2011. 

I attempted to report the safety defect to Sears Kenmore, but was given "the runaround". Seven different 800 phone numbers were provided and all were contacted.  Finally, a Sears/Kenmore customer solution representative took my information and promised to forward it to her supervisor.  I requested that someone from Sears/Kenmore call me back to follow up to report the safety defect of this gas coupling/regulator assembly.

Model: 415.16128010
S/N:  G550011104016135

The part that failed appears to be manufactured by "GLOBAL" or "GLOBAL ILLIDA" and has this information imprinted on it:
On Coupler:  GLOBAL ILLIDA 80GK Adapter for  LP-GAS YS900A
On Regulater: GLOBAL Low Pressure LP-Gas Regulator Listed 9T82

I would like to be reimbursed for the cost to repair or replace the grill.

Thank you.  
[redacted]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm, hence a severity level of 2.

I grilled bacon in the grill and the dip cups melted and hot grease spilled all over the counter and dripped on the floor. incident_description: A year ago my children purchased a Poulan Pro 25cc gas powered tree trimmer at home depot as a gift for me. They also purchased a weed wacker attachment for me. I have used the saw attachment with it's long pole 3 or 4 times. The unit has a shoulder strap to assist with holding the saw while working overhead-last week I was trimming tree branches overhead while on a 4 foot ladder. incident_description:
Bought a Char-broil grill model 463620411 yesterday. Did everything as said but when I went to open the lid the handle was so hot it burnt my hand. Be aware this handle gets extremely hot. I notified the company about the issue and this is what their response was. 

Thank you for contacting Char-Broil.

We would be happy to look into this issue for you if you could please give us a call at 1-800-241-7548 and reference your case number [REDACTED] any of our Grilling Experts will be happy to assist you with any questions or problems you may be having. One of our Grilling Experts can be reached Monday through Friday 8am to 6pm EST and Saturdays from 10am-3pm EST.

Unfortunately, I do not show we have a substitute material for your unit.  Due to the elements that the grill are exposed to, the handle has the ability to become hot.  We will be happy to discuss the issue with you though, if you would like.

We look forward to assisting you.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
Char-Broil. Specialist
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the likelihood of this happening again is high given the manufacturer's acknowledgment that the handle can become extremely hot.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed that when hill towards one side the engine would start to run roughly. Also that the fuel would move to one side of the tractor and cause the engine to misfire.

The manufacturer was contacted on many occasions since 2006. Each time they advised him that they have a fix for the problem, but he would have to cover the expense.  

The consumer feels the company should pay for repairs and he should not have to come out of pocket. 

The consumer feels that the tractor is safety hazard because if the engine dies he would get stranded.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the engine misfiring and fuel shifting pose a significant risk of the tractor breaking down, potentially stranding the consumer.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kuuma Stow and Go Grill from West Marine on 9 July 2009.  I was not aware until 12 July 2012 that there had been a recall of this product: Release #10-196.  I have had an occasional problem with flame that seemed to back out from the lit grill towards the control knob.  When that happened, I tried to make tighten the gas connections and that seem to help enough to allow time to cook a hamburger or piece of chicken.  We only use the grill 4 or 5 times a year in the summers aboard our sailboat, so it has not been a major issue until yesterday, 11 July 2012.  Upon lighting the grill, which was attached to the cockpit aft rail on our boat, I turned away briefly to pick the food I was about to cook, when the entire side of the grill where the propane tank is attached burst into flame.  The fire quickly engulfed the entire side of the grill where the propane tank is attached and melted the plastic gas control knob, so I could not twist the control knob with my hand without being burned.  I feared that the propane tank would "cook off" in an explosion, but was able to finally get the gas shut off by using a pair of cooking tongs.  I believe I and my wife were in grave danger of having our boat catch fire, since the flames would have quickly heated the cloth Sunbrella bimini top.
Last night I went on line to report this to the CPSC and discovered that the item had already been subject to a voluntary recall.  I do not remember seeing anything about this recall from either Eastwind Industries, or West Marine.
This was a life threatening incident and more aggressive action should be taken against this product.
justification: Potential for severe burns and boat fire due to grill's faulty design and lack of safety features.

incident_description: I purchased a deck from a local contractor in June 2007 for approximately $14,000.00  I chose the recommended Trex compost wood/plastic material because it was supposed to be virtually maintenence free. The literature stated that it was guaranteed to not warp, bow, splint, fade, spit, crack or be affected by insects. It never needed staining and only to be cleaned with a wood/ compost cleaner and a hose. Power washings not recommended. I noticed the deck was starting to fade and it was not the beautiful  "saddle" color it was originally. This was about a year later. I also noticed mold and mildew, so I purchased the cleaning material that Trex recommended. It did not clean off the mold, but lightened it and the faded the deck even more. I noticed that the boards were starting to get wider, and the mold and mildew worse. This has been a process of me contacting the contractor, and Trex. Last spring, I finally got the contractor to come out and look at the deck. By this time it was bowing, splinting, cracking, warping and part of the steps are pulling away.The deck had a 5 year warranty on it from the contractor. The contractor offered to replace 8 boards, and said it was not his installation but, the material itself and I would have to take it up with Trex. I did. Trex sent someone out and I received a standard from letter stating that it was the workmanship, not the material. They claimed that the boards were not installed at the correct measurements. They offered to refund me the price of 25 boards( installation not included) and a kit to clean the deck. I refused and took it up with the MD State Attorney Generals Office by filing a complaint. Trex refused mediation stating that they tried to settle the problem with me already and it was not the material, but the installation. I had 2 other independent contractors inspect the deck and verify that it was not the installation, but again the material that was defective.  I have a letter from the one contractor stating that not only is the deck, damaged, an eyesore, but a safety hazard also.I have researched claims about Trex and they have been in at least one class action suit where they lost. They also claimed in that suit that it was the installation, not the material that caused the problem's. That is their blanket excuse. I have contacted private attorneys, and can not afford to go that route. I have also inquired into Small Claims Court in Maryland, but there is no guarantee I will be reimbursed (the maximum $5000.00) by Trex,even if I would win. I don't know where else to turn. Thanks!
justification: The incident resulted in property damage and safety hazards, but no physical injuries.

incident_description: During the process of turning on the gas barbecue, fire was seen coming from the tubing (that connects the natural gas outlet to the burner) at a point involving the tubing itself.  To put it simply, fire was seen involving the tubing and not the burner where the fire is intended to be found and used for barbecuing.  The fire flared up quickly and we were able to shut off the gas before it got any worse.  When we inspected the situation, we found the tubing to now be melted.  The Southern California Gas Company was contacted and after their inspection, indicated to us that they had to shut off the gas feeding to the barbecue and "red tagged" the barbecue indicating that it was unsafe for any further barbecue use.
justification: Fire involved the gas tubing, not the burner, and was quickly extinguished with no injuries reported.

incident_description:
We received the Target Home Collection fire pit/bowl style named Pagoda as a wedding gift in July 2011.  Within a year, and one use, the bottom is very rusted, mainly where the flames were in the one use. 

Other concerns that we have with this product include: when the wind blows (strong wind or not) the top flies off the structure. The last gust of wind that we had, the top (which is square) stuck in our wood privacy fence before falling to the ground. The mesh sides fall easily as well. 

We used the fire pit for the first time in March 2012. We only had the fire going for 30 minutes or less. I think we burned 3 sticks of wood from the rick we purchased. Tonight (7/15/2012) when we moved the fire pit to clean our deck, we noticed that the boards under the fire pit were charred. 

This product seriously needs to be reviewed and potentially removed from the market as these issues can destroy property or a life.
justification: The fire pit's design flaws, such as the top flying off in wind and the bottom rusting quickly, pose a high likelihood of causing property damage or injury.

incident_description:
I have a Jenn-air stainless steel propane gas grill. 
Model number 720-0336
Serial no# 720VIIJC0336-022635A

The propane burner ignitor system constructed of what is suppose to be stainless steel is defect and deteriates to the point that the gas permeates the whole bottom of the cooking chamber and then when  it reaches a flame or spark ignites in a fire ball which can cause facial or extremity burns to the operator if they are not aware of the defect. I have repeatedly contacted the manufacture NexGrill of California about the defect and they acknowledge the issue but state they have no fix available. I'm not sure how long it takes for the defect to occur but, my grill is only a few years old and just out of warranty. I have enlisted the help of the store where I purchased the grill LOWES and they no longer carry the brand and have not been able to get the manufacturer to repair or replace the device. 

This defect has been present for over a year and the  last flare up incident occurred on the 4th of July 2012. I have now stopped using the grill. The grill was a $800 investment which is now not safe.
justification: The grill's defective ignitor system can cause gas leaks leading to fireballs, posing a high risk of facial or extremity burns to the operator.

incident_description:
The consumer says she grabbed the handle of the grill and it burned all her fingers.  She says the handle was burning hot.  The consumer says the grill was only on for about 15 minutes.  She continued using it until she was done.  She says she had to use an oven mit to open the grill.

The consumer sent an email to the manufacturer today explaining what happened.  She says the handle is made of steel.
justification: The consumer suffered burns on her fingers, indicating an injury (severity level 3), and the likelihood is high as she continued using the grill despite the hot handle.

incident_description: Purchased a new Max Fire gas grill from Home Depot, May 22, 2012.  Leak tested it and used it 3 times.  Fourth time the hose connection caught fire at the gas tank, where the regulator connects to the tank.  I could have been seriously injured or lost the house if I didn't have a fire extinguisher handy.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire could have caused serious harm or property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the gas tank was replaced.  There was a leak discovered in the regulator.  He could hear it, feel and smell it.  The consumer says he is fortunate that the unit did not explode.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him they could not do anything since the unit had not been recalled.  The consumer was told that they did not have the replacement part for it anyway.  They offered to sell him a new grill.

The part number is recalled under Release # 03-196.  The model number is not included in the recall.  The consumer says that he cannot determine the date code on the regulator.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the gas leak poses a significant risk of explosion, making it an incident with a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I recently learned of an injury that I would like added to the files regarding injuries incurred with 2-wheel rollout carts.  [REDACTED], was injured with his cart, manufactured by Rehrig Pacific Company, Los Angeles, CA.

[REDACTED] stated that "it was probably my own dumb fault as I was trying to do too many things at once."  [REDACTED] went on to explain that he wasn't sure as to how it happened but that he was both emptying grass clippings into the cart and attempting to move it, when he suddenly was pulled to the ground and thrown inside the cart (also reported by his wife, [REDACTED]).  Apparently [REDACTED] head hit the blunt edge of the cart as he suffered a facial laceration across the forehead, for which he received 8 stitches at a hospital instant-care facility.
justification: Injury occurred due to operator error while multitasking, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description: I was sitting at home supervising my 4 year old son as he was enjoying using the banzai geyser blast sprionkler. After an hour of continues use of the sprinkler I saw that the hose had came detached from the sprinkler unit that it was feeding water to. So immediatly I went to see that the condition was good enough for me to reattach the sprinkler to the hose again because my son was disappointed and wanted to continue to use it . I visually inspected the area that the hose came detached from to see why it came apart i noticed at that moment that there was a trace of a small amount of glue around the opening of the unit and the spout that it was attached to. I also inspected the spout along with the ring with the washer ring which flew off when the hose came apart from the whole unit and found that these were the only parts that came apart and that the rest of the sprinkler was not damged in any way.. As a result of my inspection I decided to put the sprinkler away for the day cause I knew that it was not safe to use since it had small parts that came detached. Honestly, I instantly though to myself after inspecting  that it was a ridiculous idea for the company to use such little amount of glue for such a large sprinkler that is suppose to withstand a lot of water pressure. please take these facts into consideration.
justification: The sprinkler detached due to insufficient glue, posing a potential injury risk to the child, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Craftsman Lawn Tractor online from sears.com on 4-6-12. The unit was delivered to my home on 4-13-12. During a pre-start up inspection of the unit, I found that the 2 mandrel pulley guards were missing. I contacted sears.com regarding the missing guards and was informed that the unit is being sold without the guards. I also checked the illustrated parts breakdown for the machine and it does not show the guards as a factory installed part. I am of the opinion that operating the Lawn Tractor without the guards in place is safety hazard and could possibly cause personal injury to the operator. Guards around mandrel pulleys are normally installed on all Lawn and Garden Tractors regardless of the manufacture. This prevents the possibility of loose clothing, feet and hands  from being caught between  the drive belt and the mandrel pulley. I fail to understand why sears.com would market this model of machine without guards, but  include the guards on the other machines listed in their 2011 Customer Buying Guide for Riding Equipment. It appears to me that if it is mandated by sears.com to include the required guards for all the other Riding Equipment they market, the unit I purchased should have the required guards installed on it.  Note - ANSI B71.1-2003 SAFETY STANDARDS FOR RIDING MOWERS states in part:  Do not operate machine without the entire grass catcher, discharge guard, or other safety devices in place and working. In the interest of personal safety, I am requesting that sears.com management issue a voluntary recall to install the required guards on all Lawn Tractors (Model No. 917.288562) marketed and sold in the U.S.A.
justification: The missing mandrel pulley guards pose a high likelihood of injury, as they protect against clothing, feet, or hands being caught between the drive belt and the pulley.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased a weed eater mower that she purchased and she is stating that it does not work properly. The consumer stated that she believes that this product poses a safety hazard to the consumer. 

The consumer stated that every time she tries to mow her lawn the weed eater gets stuck. The consumer stated that she has to stick her fingers where the blades are located to get the weed eater to work again. 

The consumer believes this poses a laceration hazard and the product should be investigated. 

The consumer stated that she spoke to the manufacturer and they referred her to the retailer.
justification: The consumer's actions of sticking her fingers near the blades to unclog the weed eater pose a high risk of laceration.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he has been using the weed eater for approximately a year. The consumer stated that he noticed 12/15/2012 that the plastic gas tank (part# 308675021) was leaking. The consumer stated that he continued using the weed eater even though gas has been leaking out of the tank while in use. 

The consumer stated that on 06/21/2012 he decided to order the part and that he would replace it. The consumer stated that when he contacted the manufacturer to order part and they stated that they had the orders of the part backed up to almost 500 parts that were requested. 

The consumer stated that he has not been injured. 

The consumer stated that this was a fire hazard and he believes this product should be investigated.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the gas leak poses a fire hazard, making it an incident.

incident_description: Homeowner was cooking with propane grill and had a fire that extended to the hose and regulator causing a fire and small explosion per homeowner. Upon arrival the fire was out. There was fire damage to a sliding screen door and paint and stucco no extension into the structure.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the fire extended to the hose and regulator, causing a small explosion, thus severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 as propane grill fires, while possible, are not common.

incident_description:
The consumer says the unit has a plastic fuel tank on the body and has developed a crack.  he says that it leaks fuel.  The tank holds two and a half gallons and he noticed it only had a gallon and a half in it and pretty much all leaked out on the garage floor.

He got home on 5-25 and noticed an awful smell of leaking gas that he had to ventilate throughout his home.  The lawn tractor stays in an attached garage in his home.  

He says the tractor is not heavily used.  He feels this is clearly a fire hazard. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said they never heard of it.  He spoke to them on 5-29-2012.  They offered no assistance.  The machine is currently in a local lawn mower shop. 

The consumer has seen many online reports of the same thing happening to other consumers.
justification: Fuel leak from cracked tank poses a fire hazard, though no injuries reported yet.

incident_description:
Caller's address is a second address where he lives 6 months out of the year and also works various repair projects for those living around him.

He returned to this address in April 2012 to find that his neighbor/friend had left a push mower on his deck.  The model has handle stubs that push into blade area for storage.

Plastic molding fits at back of deck w/two 18" long handle stubs, the U shaped handle portion bolts to the stubs.

The problem being reported with this option is that the caller's neighbor/friend had purchased one of these mowers, the seller didn't put the screws/stubs in when assembling mower.

The first few times the purchaser used the mower it worked well but when he took it out of the garage maybe the fourth time, the handle began going down into the cutting area because the screws/stubs were not in place.

Caller and his neighbor/friend are satisfied with retailers reaction to problem because the mower was replaced with a different design/model and those remaining in stock were removed.

Caller states that if CPSC will send In Field representative he would be happy to accompany that person to display and discuss the safety issue. 

Caller contacted the manufacturer around June 12th, 2012, doesn't know the name of the person he spoke with. 
He believes that the female in parts department avoided his safety issues and questions.

He is reporting that this is a very dangerous design that needs to be revised.  
When handle approaches a moving blade and chances that a piece could become sliced off then it could fly out and injure the user or those near the mower.

He would request that production of this design be ceased immediately and the mower become recalled.

I have talked to [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and [REDACTED] in addition to the local Home Depot.  These mowers are shipped in boxes with the handle stubs locked in the bottom position with the locking screws.  They all stated that they had problems with people trying to start the units with the handles in the down position.  They had not realized what could happen if the handle were allowed to enter the blade area when the units are running.  [REDACTED] also makes these units under [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] Brand names plus other possible Brand Names.
justification: The mower's design flaw, where the handle can enter the blade area when not secured, poses a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: Cooking burgers on new gas grill. Burgers were flaming a bit and when I opened the lid, I realized you have to open with your arm directly over cooking area. Did not get burned, but seems it would be very easy to. Handle is on front of lid. Would be safer on the side.
justification: The grill's lid design places users at risk of burns when opening it, making an injury likely.

incident_description: I purchased a Weed eater One rear engine riding lawn mower in March 2011 and have had many issues with it. The major one I consider to be a safety concern involves the brake cable breaking under normal use. I had just picked up my Weed eater One from an authorized repair center and the first time using it I went to apply the brake and noticed that the pedal went all the way down and the mower would not stop. I had to jump off the moving mower to get it to stop. I returned to the repair shop and over heard comments in the nature of "another broken brake cable" and doing a small amount of research online noticed that others have had similar issues.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the potential for serious harm was high due to the brake cable breaking under normal use.

incident_description: I have had my Homelite chain saw, Model #UT10947-A, SN # AF0990887 to an authorized dealer due to the saw not accelerating properly, and seeing there was a recall on some other models for chain brake problems.  He said he could not work on it without Homelite's authorization or a receipt of purchase.  After I tore apart the chain brake assembly and ran the saw without the chain brake, it accelerated the way it should.  The chain brake is in the "on" position at all times and does not allow the chain to turn, or the engine to accelerate.  It also causes the saw to generate immense amounts of heat and will smoke.  I feel this is a fire hazard, especially in dry wooded areas where this saw would be used.  I know I can use the saw without the brake, but for safety's sake, I would rather have it available.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to excessive heat and smoke generated by the malfunctioning chain brake, which could lead to property damage or injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a riding lawmower for my husband as ours was getting up in age and this one with model number #247288810, seerial number #1C231B40023. Purchased on June 1, 2011 and delivered a week later. Due to the rains in St. Louis, MO he did not use the mower and then the rear bagger fell off, the seat shifts and almost fell off. the bagger came off in one trying to mow the law on 18 occasions. technicans came out and he did not know what to do. Whey would you place a bumjer on the rear bagger. When we comparied our two lawn mowers, what a difference. This needs help as the mechanical items on it do not work. then our sone-in-law tried, it and fell off, what if he were killed on it. I then had our engineer a medical degreed individual with a BS and a Masters and h said the same things, the rear bagger is not properly affixed to the mower and needs correction. He even idnicated to us that we have a leom and I tried over a rear to have it
worked on and each time the service gusy did not know what to do. they have no knowledge of engineering, etc. So here we have a dude and cannot use it. Kindly recall this item for checks on it before someone has a serious accident on it, possibly dead.
Thanks.

[Additional information from the submitter:]
Also, regardless if there is one or several complaints, all should be legally taken as such.  When an individual falls off and the bagger falls off each time utilized, there is a mfg issue.
justification: Multiple incidents of the rear bagger falling off and individuals nearly falling off the mower, with potential for serious injury.

incident_description: I was going to use my weber grill and smelled gas.  I found there wasa hole in the hose which connected to the gas tank.  It must have been gnawed at by a squirrel or other animal.  Thank goodness I noticed this as it could have exploded!  Weber needs to protect the hose with a hard cover.  I spoke with them and they said a cover is available but it does not come with the grill.  I highly recommend that the hose should with a hard cover on it.
justification: Potential gas leak due to animal damage could have caused an explosion, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I own a Perfect Flame gas grill (Model Number 720-0335) which was purchased in 2007.  Yesterday afternoon, while cooking chicken, the cooking chamber caught on fire, which persisted despite the burners being turned off.  The entire chamber was burning and melted much of the metal to include the dials.  We later identified that the fire had burned through the hose connecting the tank, which is a significant explosion hazard.  The fire hazard, itself, is a concern as is the potential for explosion.  We had to use a fire extinguisher to stop the burning.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant fire hazard and potential explosion risk.

incident_description: lp gas line ruptured and started a fire that damaged my grill, my siding, and ac unit
justification: Although there was a fire, no injuries were reported, hence severity level 2. The incident's occurrence is possible given the nature of LP gas lines.

incident_description: I purchased a new John Deere lawn mower model number LA105 for $1,499 in June 2008. I was driving the mower on an incline in my yard when the brake seal started leaking, which caused transmission fluid to seep on to the brake disc, which caused the brakes to fail. Luckily, I'm an experienced operator and was able to divert an accident - a less experienced operator may not have been so lucky. I went to a local JD dealer to find out what is needed to correct the braking problem, they said there is a seal rebuild kit available for ($550) or a new transmission for ($650) The mower only has 45 hrs on it, it has always been parked in my garage and has been well taken care of. I called John Deere expecting there would be a recall for this seal; I was very surprised to find out they "don't" and that they are unwilling to offer assistance to remedy the situation. I believe JD is being very irresponsible for not standing behind this very unsafe design.
justification: Brakes failed due to design flaw, posing high risk to operators, especially less experienced ones.

incident_description: Weed eater 20v cordless string trimmer model lt 20v does not have trigger lock.  I picked it up by the handle and suddenly received four slashes to my lower leg.  It caused my leg lo bleed a lot.  Most power tools i have owned all have safty locks for the triggers.  I do not want to see this happen to other people.
justification: The lack of a trigger lock on the weed eater led to an unintentional start, causing injury, which is likely to happen again due to the design flaw.

incident_description:
The plastic gas tank of the weed wacker leaks gas from the seam.  Of you [REDACTED] roybi gas tank leak you will find that this is a common problem which is obviously a safety hazard.   The model is 890r, the serial number is 012045716 and the ppn # is 41BD890A034.

The unit has never been damaged.  The tank simply leaks at a seam because it is defective.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the gas leak poses a significant fire hazard, making it an incident.

incident_description: Homelite BP250 Backpack Blower, UT 08017E, serial number HP2301242, leaks gasoline during normal use.  Have not experienced a fire, but gasoline leaked onto clothes, creating irritation of skin.  The fact that it did not ignite is considered pure luck.  I have recently seen the recall of UT numbers 08017F and 08017G, but it appears the same problem exists with UT 08017E.
justification: Skin irritation occurred due to gasoline leak, and the lack of ignition is purely luck, indicating a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: My son was mowing with our Cub Cadet LT 1042 riding mower.  He used the mower for about 10 minutes - and then came in for a glass of water.  He turned the mower off prior to coming inside.  When he went back outside, the front of the mower was engulfed in flames.  We put the fire out with water.  The entire hood was melted.  It appeared the fire was more focused on the left side of the mower as you looked at it.  The hood was completely melted - and also involved the forward part of the steering wheel.  It did not involve the mowing deck or the rear gas tank.  The oil was checked prior to starting the mower and the mower deck was free of all debris.  I have noted on the internet that this is not an isolated event with this brand of mower, and that recalls for fires involving other models have already been issued.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the severe fire caused significant damage to the mower, indicating a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: This is a recurring problem that has existed since this product was installed at my house in June of 2011.  I had a replacement solid core cellular PVC decking material installed on my dock that is manufactured by Gossen Corporation of Milwaukee, WI and trades under the product name of "Passport Deck & Porch".  The manufacturer claims through their local representative dealer/installer and within their product brochure to be foot friendly and I was told I could walk on it barefooted.  However, the reality is that in direct sunlight, the temperature of this material is so hot that you get burns to your skin if it comes in contact with the material when the sun is on the product.  So far the dealer and manufacturer have told me that I must have overly sensitive feet and that they have had no other complaints from their customers.  The previous product that had been on my deck did not get hot like this; and I have since tested some other competitive products that do not get this excessively hot.  This product is so hot that my dog will not walk on it when the sun is out as it burns the pads on her feet.  So far the manufacturer refuses to acknowledge that there is any problem with their product, have suggested my deck is an anomaly, yet they refuse to come out and stand on their decking material as I have challenged them to do and have refused to make me whole on the $15,600 cost of this very dangerous product that they are selling for home decks, pools and dock applications.  I am wondering if there is anyway the CPSC can independently test this material and provide any recourse for me and also issue warnings to other potential consumers of the danger of this material.  My second complaint about the product is that despite their claims that "you don't have to worry about slipping..." I have found that in fact it is very slippery when wet even from the dew in the morning let alone other sources of water.
justification: The material's extreme heat causes burns to bare feet and paws, leading to injuries.

incident_description:
We own a Perfect Flame model SLG2006B outdoor gas grill.  When I went to buy the grill, I went for an upper level grill, liked all the features and design of this particular grill and have been fairly happy with it until about 1 1/2 years ago, it caught on fire while we were cooking on it.  Thankfully we had a fire extinguisher in the house to put it out.

Thinking that it was just too much marinade on the tenderloin and aluminum foil that aided in it catching on fire, I took the unit apart, cleaned it, replaced 1 bad burner, replaced the burner covers and put it back into action.  Then, on Fathers Day, my daughter went out to start warming up the grill.  Again, it caught on fire, this time with no food on it at all.  The thermostat registered over 800 degrees.  This time, I used the dogs watering bucket that happened to be sitting on the deck to drown out the flames.  (Getting a little tired of having to put out flames and clean this grill!)
So, I called the company today, read off the grill numbers, asked if she wanted me to read her the serial numbers - she said, that's not necessary.  We will send you new burners, you just pay for the shipping.  How much is the shipping, I asked?  29.95.  Really - from the reviews that I have been watching and finding on the internet - they want to charge another $30.00 to send you replacement parts b/c they have defective ones?  

Come on... This is a grill with propane and flames.  They are really lucky that the grill did not catch totally on fire, burn up, burn up my deck, explode the propane and wipe out my family and house.  And their response is, we will ship you new burners for $30.00?
I just went out and tested my grill.  2 burners are cracked, a 3rd now not working, the flames got so hot that it is now causing the controller on the left hand side  to not release, therefore keeping the ignition flame going until you pull the controller back.  The racks are now rusted out b/c of the heat and all of my coverings are shot.  Oh, but I could just pay another 12.95 for each heat plate.

So, in order for me to get this grill back up and running - 4 free burners, but $30.00 in shipping, 4 heat shields at 12.95 each = $51.80, the grill racks - over $100, new burner for left hand side control unit - would guess anywhere from $25-$45.  So, for about $225 - $250 I could correct this issue, get my grill back up and running - and possibly use it again.  HMMMMM.  Why would I trust that this would fix the problem and not catch on fire again?  

I am just so thankful that nobody got hurt during either one of these fires and that my house is still in tact.  Also, that my wife and I have been around during BOTH of these episodes.  What would have happened if one of my kids decided to grill something - even though they are young teens - I would have lost everything, house and family included.  And the companies response is... we will give you the burners, but you have to pay for the shipping.  Sorry, but that just [REDACTED}me off - It should be, hey, we are glad that everyone is o.k.   We had a recall on those units, we will be more than happy to either replace your grill with another one that we have or if you would rather continue to use that grill, we will make it right.  

What ever happened to a company doing the right thing?  After 2 fires, I would rather recycle that grill in the scrap yard and get what I can out of it before I buy any more parts for it.  

Here's a recommendation - [REDACTED].  That's Right!  They know how to make grills that don't catch on fire and burn up!
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the grill catching fire twice in a short period poses a high likelihood of severe injury or property damage.

incident_description:
Caller's wife started grill to preheat, turned, walked approximately fifteen feet away to pick up the hamburgers when a fire ball approximately 8 - 10 inches high and 8 to 10 inches around  shot out from the dial (valve)

Caller's wife called for him and he came to her and shut the main propane tank dial.  Did not work as it was on fire.  Consumer Added: Valve/Knob burned--stainless steel grill face and hood had heat damage from the fire.  Thank God that we were able to REACT QUICKLY!

He went online to find parts for this grill and discovered many of them on recall.

His grill however is not on recall.

He contacted the retailer where he purchased the grill and was provided with the phone number for CPSC Hotline .
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant fireball, indicating a high-risk situation.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on June 10th, 2012 the left and right shelves of his grill became extremely hot after 15 minutes of use.

The consumer touched the right side shelf of the grill and burned his hand. 

He did not received medical treatment.
The consumer applied ice to hand to calm the redness and swelling.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer on June 11th, 2012 and they advised him that there was no issue with the grills. 

The consumer took the unit back to the store and received a refund.

He contacted the manufacturer a second time on June 11th, 2012 to inform them that he had returned the product. 
They will review the issue and get back with him.
justification: Consumer suffered a burn injury, but no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express that her gas grill was engulfed in flames after a short time. The consumer was preparing steaks on the grill for roughly two minutes and had the burners on the grill set to medium-high, before she noticed the grill was engulfed in flames. Frantically, the consumer attempted to put out the flames by pouring dirt on it. The consumer also used a fire extinguisher but the flames would not go out completely. The consumer called her son in law who lives close by and he arrived to her home in 5 minutes. 

Her son in law was able to finally extinguish the flames by pouring dirt on the grill and using the fire extinguisher. The consumer's son in law was able to remove the propane tank from the grill. The consumer was able to take the grill off her porch and away from her home before the damage could spread. The consumer stated that the grill is completely unusable and burned. The consumer has not called the fire department or her home insurance company. The consumer has not called the firm or the retailer. The consumer was not harmed or injured.
justification: Although the incident resulted in significant property damage, no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his lawn tractor as the consumer was on the tractor when a fire started in the engine. The consumer was on the tractor for roughly 90 minutes before the incident. The consumer put out the fire by pouring water on it. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. The consumer was suggest that the mower is no longer usable. The consumer has not called the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer was mowing the lawn in his backyard at the time. The consumer called the retailer and was informed that his model was not recalled. The consumer has not called the firm as of yet.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident of a fire starting in the engine is serious and could have been catastrophic if not quickly extinguished.

incident_description: No one was injured when a window mounted wood pellet stove heater caught fire while in use in the window frame of a single family residence. The resulting fire was extinguished but casued an estimated $45,000 in damages.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the significant property damage ($45,000) warrants a severity level of 2. The likelihood of this occurrence is possible, given the potential hazards of wood pellet stoves.

incident_description:
Perfect flame Stainless Steel NG Gas Grill Model 730-0335

Main Stainless Steel burners created fire and hazard when ignited to use grill.  Grill manufacturer "Nexgrill Industries".  This could have been a tragic incident and house could have caught on fire if not for some quick thinking.  This grill is unsafe to use and should be recalled.
justification: The grill's main burners ignited unexpectedly, posing a significant fire hazard and potential property damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
In the fall of 2011 I purchased a new gas valve for my barbecue grill. It worked satisfactorily until it was put away for
the winter. In the spring the valve leaked gas. Since I did not save the sales invoice, I was told there was nothing
which could be done for me. I purchased a new valve this spring. When I installed the new valve it leaked immediately.
The barbecue grill gas valves were supplied by the:
Onward Manufacturing Company
585 Kumpf Drive
Waterloo, Ontario, Canada N2V 1 K3
tel.: 519-885-1390 toll free 1-800-265-2150
I have talked to the Onward Mfg. Co. several times and even sent them photographs of the faulty valve.
The valve in question is PIN 10440-T20 (see photocopy of sales invoice).
I have offered to return the most recent defective valve to them and they do not want to examine It.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of gas leakage poses a potential hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description:
0 Turn Mower purchased June 2010.

Wheel lug nuts have come off tire and tire would have come off while he was riding on it if he had not noticed it when he had.

The only reason he noticed that the lug nuts had come off is due to his stopping the mower while cutting grass to pick up some trash and at that time he noticed that the wheel was sitting crooked.

The rim is "walled out" and damaged to the point that nuts cannot be screwed back onto the studs.

Dealers have informed him that the tires on this particular 0 Turn Mower are mounted at the manufacturers and not at the dealers location.

Caller confirms that if the tire had come off while he was mowing a hill it could have thrown the mower off balance causing it to potentially turn over and possibly on top of him.

He would like the public notified of this danger and repair at manufacturer expense stating that he could question if he had ever had to replace a tire (which he hasn't)  but this is from the factory and should not come off this way.

He also would like the nuts on the other wheels checked.

He has only 44 hours use with this mower.



He has not contacted the manufacturer, however the mower is at a repair station, they are contacting the manufacturer.

He will enter serial number at a later date.
justification: Potential injury due to mower imbalance and tip-over if tire had detached while mowing a hill.

incident_description: two toro rake and vac have caught fire where the extension cord connects
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not a frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer was using the lawn mower when the left side gas tank caught on fire.  He jumped off of it, but it burned up the seat.  The lawn mower did not have much fuel in it so the fire burned out on its own.  It did burn up the other gas tank before going out.  

The consumer says he was riding the lawn mower for ten to fifteen minutes before the incident occurred. He contacted the manufacturer via email who told him that nothing has been recalled and is no longer under warranty.  

He bought the mower with 171 hours on it and it caught on fire at 216 hours.  

He saw an online report of one consumer needing the fuel lines replaced.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident resulted in property damage (burnt seat and gas tanks).
