incident_description: My parents bought this for me as a christmas gift from the sears outlet. I had the grill not even 7 months and used it about 23 times before it had a major issue. Today I lit the grill so it could preheat to cook chicken breasts. Went in side the house to get the chicken breasts and when locally I came back out pretty quick. The left burner stopped working and started a fire in between the control knob and the interior grill. The other three burners were still burning. I went to turn the knob to shut it off and it fell off from the plastic being burnt. I quickly turned the propane tank off and watched as the front left section stayed lit and burned for another 5 minutes. Thank god I did not wait longer than 5 mintues to come back out with the chicken, the grill probally would have caught the tank on fire or something else. I called sears and they said that there were no recalls and since it was bought from the outlet basically there is nothing they will do even if it is unsafe. Do not buy this grill and if you have it you better keep an eye on it and not leave it for any amount of time if you value your life. MFG #720-0670A   MODEL# 122.16641901  SERIAL NUMBER# 720CWIJ0670A-055773B.
justification: The grill caught fire while in use, posing a significant risk, and the incident could have escalated to a more severe level if not promptly addressed.

incident_description: A newly installed RMV2.5G30 pump was started for the first time.  Less than 10 seconds after initial start, the center high pressure plug catastrophically failed sending the top half of the metal plug flying into the air.  The plug narrowly missed injuring the operator.  The pump continued to eject high pressure water out of the failed plug hole until the pump was shut down.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident involved a high-pressure component failure, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2). The likelihood is 'Possible' (3) as it occurred during initial startup, suggesting potential manufacturing or installation issues.

incident_description: The grill was being used to cook meat and during cooking, the grill caught fire in the upper & lower chambers. The fire was shooting out of the back & sides of the grill. The fire needed to be put out with a fire extinguisher & water and was very close to being an emergency situation because we had trouble putting out the fire. There were no injuries or damage to home, but the grill is most likely ruined.
justification: Although the incident resulted in no injuries or property damage, the severity level is 2 as it was an incident with potential for harm.

incident_description: Model YTH20K46 Husqvarna Lawn Tractor (purchased about June 2008) - plastic gas tank developed large stress fractures at top and bottom of tank where it was ejected from the mold-injection manufacture.  The fuel began leaking while the machine was being operated but I did not know it.  The remaining tank of fuel leaked into my garage and fumes eventually infiltrated my home; the dog was in the garage too, although he did not die.  Tractor requires either repair or replacement.  Definitely a fire hazard.
justification: Fuel leak from the lawn tractor caused a potential fire hazard in the garage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
While in use, the trimmer end of a Troy Built Stringed Trimmer fell off of the shaft. Due to the high rotational velocity of the loose assembly, the assembly was propelled backwards, hitting the operators foot.

It appears that a single screw (parts list item # 19) came loose due to the wear/stretching of a hole in the trimmer shaft (parts list item # 16). Part # 16 is damaged but intact and parts #17-#35 detached from the trimmer.

I contacted the manufacturers "Level 1 tech support" (they do not have a level 2) to ask if they have seen this issue before and I also asked who I needed to speak with in order to report a potential safety issue. I was advised that they do not accept safety complaints from the consumer and I should take the parts to an authorized dealer for repair.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the operator's foot, and the likelihood of this happening again is high given the worn-out part and lack of manufacturer's response to safety issues.

incident_description:
BBQ Burned.  I saw this already on your site, but wanted to report another incident.
BBQ Name - Perfect Flame.  Purchased at [REDACTED] 
Model Number - GAC3615

Incident occured last year on Father's Day.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the occurrence was possible as it happened in the past.

incident_description: I have A Honda Harmony Model# HRB215HXA self propelled mower. The deck is made out of a plastic called Xenoy...supposed to be darn near  indestructible..i started it yesterday and about 25% of the deck holding the engine fell off along with one of the bolts. after stopping it and turning it on it's side, i found the remaining bolts had cracks on the frame they went thru...i called Honda USA and asked if they had any reports of similar problems and the man said only on mowers were someone hit an object which bent the crankshaft which caused excessive vibration..  this was my personal mower and only i used it and i never hit no object, as a matter of fact i babied this thing, it never sit outside one night,,motor starts on first or second pull every time...but this could have been a major catastrophe.....
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have resulted in serious harm if the mower had been in use when the deck fell off.

incident_description:
Weber Spirit E210 Gas Grill - Model #4411411 - S/N  DE6182604

Homeowner was preparing to use grill and heard a hissing sound coming from the valve connection to the propane tank.  She tightened it and the hissing worsened.  She then loosened it a little and it stopped.  She lit the grill and shortly afterword the hissing started again.  She once again went to adjust the connection and upon doing so the leaking gas ignited.  The homeowner received 1st degree burns to her arm and her hair was burned.  

The fire investigation determined that a faulty valve connection from the grill to the propane tank was a result of the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in the homeowner receiving first-degree burns, classifying it as an 'Injury' (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the issue was persistent and ultimately led to ignition.

incident_description:
Black & Decker HT512 22-Inch 3.8 amp Dual Action Electric Hedge Trimmer

I believe these hedge trimmers may be a few years old, but they still appear to be brand new as they have only been used occasionally and have been stored indoors. I'm trying to hunt down the receipt to see when I bought them and if they are covered by warranty, but in the meanwhile I feel this is worthy of reporting to the CPSC as it is extremely dangerous. 

The switch sticks in the on position and the only way to turn them off is by unplugging them.

In addition to the danger of the trimmers not being able to be turned off, merely trying to unplug electric trimmers while they are running is scary.
justification: The hedge trimmers' switch malfunctioning and inability to turn off without unplugging poses a high likelihood of injury due to the risk of electric shock.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sportsman's Grill Model: GR4039-014943  at Sam's Club (#6649) in Worcester MA on April 5, 2012

I have used it a total of less than 7 hours.

After pre-heating the grill for a small roast in early June 2012, I lifted the top and it detached and fell to the ground.  The grill temperature at this time was about 500 deg F.

Upon examination after cooling, I found that the  rivets (they look to be aluminum) that hold the backplate to the body had melted and broken.

incident_description:
Charbroil Grill bolts to the Lid bent in and gave way. The lid fell off on the left side as I was grilling and i tried to catch the lid so it wouldn't completely fall off; as a result, the fire box and lid was damaged.

I called Charbroil and tried to explain what happened and they required me to pay shipping for the lid and its hardware, i was told by my boyfriend to call back because i didn't explain that the part where the lid attaches was damaged and that will need to be replaced. Charbroil rep then stated, I would have to send pictures in order for them to send out the fire box and I would also have to pay shipping for that as well.

I explained to the representative, that the grill was purchased around the end of Feb beginning of March and this should not happen. I shouldn't have to pay shipping for a product that has manufacturing issues or is defective. 

My grill has a cover and is only a few months old. I had my granddaughter outside in the yard with me and this could have caused injury to myself as well as her , if the lid would have fell off completely and if i did not have good reflex's.

The screws need to be recalled because this should just happen and I don't want someone to get injured if it could be a quick fix of replacing the screw and bolts.
justification: The grill lid falling off could have caused injury to the individual or their granddaughter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We bought a 2-burner Master Forge #MFA350CNP Gas Grill last May 18, 2011 at our local LoweÃÂs. incident_description:
Troy-Bilt TB320BV 
Blower/Vacuum
serial number:1J219DF6509

I bought this leaf blower 3 years ago and while I was using it for the 3rd time this year I suddenly realized I was soaked with gasoline. A fuel line or something must have broke and I was sprayed with gasoline. All of my lower body was covered with fuel. I looked but could not see any broken lines or other damage although I did not take it apart. When I phoned Troy-Bilt to see if there were any recalls I was asked if I drained the blower before I put it away for the winter. When I informed the customer service rep that I always drain all my tools and run them dry prior to storing them away for the winter she then informed me that the new gasoline today contains ethanol that eats away or compromise the fuel lines and that is probably what happened. She recommended a local authorized service shop that could repair it for me. I'm wondering if others are experiencing this problem? If they know that is happening maybe they should change the materials of the fuel lines and use another composition that stands up to the ethanol. It is very dangerous to suddenly be doused with gasoline.
justification: User was soaked with gasoline, posing a significant burn risk.

incident_description: Grilling outdoors on normal day several hamburgers when flames erupted and the grill caught fire burnt up the hoses knobs, lid and ruined the grill. Fire had to be extinguished and grill is not usable now!
justification: Although there was an incident with significant property damage, no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Toro Brand 11" electric [weed trimmer], model number 51347 and Is about 2 1/2 years old and is only used once a week at best.  I have the proper gauge and length of outside rated power cord.  I have taken good care of it and it was in outstanding condition.  When I was weed [trimming] a few days ago, it began to start to run slower until it stopped and caught on fire at the end where the motor was located with flames coming out near where the string rotates.  

I sent an email to Toro and in return was sent a basic form type response.  I will not buy any other Toro products because I do not feel they care about safety following this issue and their lack of meaningful response.  

Just want to make sure that no one else gets hurt by this product.  

Please let me know if it is OK to throw this away or not.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a fire, posing a potential hazard.

incident_description:
Yesterday I had my engine mounting bolts loosen up while mowing my yard, 3 of them fell out which displaced the engine.  This displacement sheered my muffler attachment, sent sparks flying due to the drive pulley being damaged by rubbing against the belt guide which eventually got sheared off as well.
I don't know of any periodic maintenance that specifically tells one to check the torque of the engine mounting bolts.  I had an incident with a bolt two years ago that sheared off that was holding the blade on while the blade was in motion on the same lawn mower.  Don't know if I got a bad batch of bolts, or if things weren't torqued to specs, but I've never had things like this happen to a lawn mower before. 
My lawn mower was bought new in 2004.  It is a John Deere LT160.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant damage to the lawn mower, making it unusable until repaired.

incident_description:
Caller purchased smoker on October 10th, 2011 and used it the first few days after purchase t cook ribs.
He realized that the smoker was steadily building heat while set at a specific temperature and took this first smoker and exchange it on10/17/2011.
The retailer provided Caller with an exchange.
He took the replacement smoker home and began using it.
He used the replacement smoker possibly 8 times, however then he had been cooking ribs in the smoker in April 19th, 2012, turned the smoker off but didn't unplug it.
He came out to put the dog out around six hours later and realized that the smoker, although turned off was running strong at around 300 degrees.
He unplugged the smoker and sat it to the side to cool off.
Caller has not used the smoker since then but has plugged it in to test whether this incident would be repeated and it has.
He received payment from the retailer as refund, he has no financial request but would request that the public be notified of the fire danger this grill has.
justification: The smoker continued to heat up even after being turned off, posing a fire risk and potential injury.

incident_description:
Like many others that purchased the Perfect Flame Double Lid Four Burner Gas, model GAC3615, we also experienced this product burst into flame and engulf the entire cooking chamber exactly as described by the other complaints, with flame involving both interior and exterior surfaces. In our circumstance this dangerous event has now occurred three times. This grill is manufactured by Lucas Innovation Inc., of China, distributed by BBQTEK Enterprise, Inc. and sold exclusively by Lowes is apparently incredibly dangerous. 

At first it was presumed a cooking error had been committed, however after the third occurrence where our home almost caught fire, we became suspect and discovered this model grill is subject to a partial recall due this specific issue. Lowes was incredibly helpful once we discovered the recall however BBQTEK refused to honor or acknowledge the recall of their product unless it could be specifically identified as being a part of a particular manufacturerÃÂs serial number string and date code. Due to cleaning efforts and weathering the label on our particular grill was worn and torn so only the model number is identifiable. This complaint has been added since apparently the entire product line is deficient not only part of it as in the present recall. We encourage any one that has purchased this model grill to file a complaint to expand the recall to the entire product line.
justification: The incident has occurred multiple times, with the most recent event nearly causing a house fire.

incident_description: We purchased a Black and Decker 18" 36v cordless lawnmower, CM1836, less than a year ago. We have slightly less than average use for living in the Northeast. About two weeks ago, the kill switch arm stopped working abruptly. This is a potentially dangerous situation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning safety feature (kill switch) which, if not addressed, could potentially lead to injury.

incident_description:
On Saturday, May 1, 2010 I was using my Great Dane Riding Mower, RZ6125KAE 03. Serial #4552198. The cap on the hydraulic oil reservoir melted causing the hot oil in the tank to spew out  burning my back and my leg. It ruined the shirt and pair of long pants that I was wearing while mowing. I have pictures of the burns and the shirt.

Prior to this, I had to buy replacement caps, on two separate occasions, for the hydraulic oil reservoir. They had melted, oil had leaked and the caps no longer fit. An employee at the store, Jacobi Sales, Inc told me that he had the same problem with the fluid leak and melting caps.

Jacobi's manufactured a special metal cap but the tank continues to leak. They are picking the mower up again to try to find an answer to the problem. The hydraulic system had to be rebuilt and the hydraulics have been a constant problem since I bought this mower new from Jacobi's. The staff, especially [REDACTED], have been very helpful and courteous yet I have spent in excess of $2,500.00 in repairs mostly because of the hydraulic system.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the user's back and leg, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as the issue has occurred multiple times, with the user and an employee experiencing melted caps and leaks.

incident_description: Fiesta Blue Ember Natural Gas Grill model FG50069-U701 Serial# 08K053633 caught fire. Was not advised of original recall. Found the recall when looking for parts.
justification: The grill caught fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was mowing the lawn and while mowing the lawn the blade hit a rock. The rock shot out of the back of the lawn mower and the safety guard did not stop  the rock. The rock then hit my shin and cut the skin of my shin down to the bone requiring me to get 10 stitches
justification: The injury occurred due to a projectile from the lawn mower, which was not effectively stopped by the safety guard.

incident_description: I was called out to investigate a propane grill fire.  Fire was determined to be accidental in nature with fire starting near propane cylinder and most likely from a leak in the hose from the cylinder to the burner.  Grill was a "Member's Mark" brand model #720-0691A.  Owner believed grill to be only a few years old and was operating normal prior to fire.  Propane cylinder was DOT 4BA 240 M4875 and was last filled at Agland Inc, w/o incident.  Owner did not have internet service and asked that I file the report for them.  I informed the owner to keep the grill and propane cylinder for several weeks in case they were contacted by CPSC.  Owner's name is [REDACTED].
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a propane grill fire, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: While cooking on a Fiesta Blue Ember Model FG50069 gas grill I experienced an extensive house fire after the gas line failed and erupted in flame.  I have discovered afterward the recalls and had not been notified about them either from Home Depot (the retailer purchased from) or Keesung Manufacturing Co. Ltd. and Unisplendor Corp., of China (manufacturer).  The initial estimate of damages to my residence are in excess of $10,000.
justification: The incident resulted in extensive property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the known recalls and lack of notification.

incident_description: Our grill caught on fire while cooking with it.
justification: While cooking, the grill caught fire, causing an incident but no injury.

incident_description: New batteries were inserted in a Black Diamond Gemini head lamp.  Even though lamp was off, battery pack began heating up, enough to melt the plastic backing.  The batteries were quickly removed.  Three new batteries were inserted.  Same result.
justification: The incident occurred twice with the same batteries and lamp, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: craftsman lawn mower model 917.388620 is unsafe. The bag system is poorly designed so the bag falls off repeatedly while mowing. This creates a trip hazzard as the bag falls off directly in front of where you are walking. the brackets that hold the bag onto the mower are not long enough causing the bag to fall off constantly. I have contacted sears numerous times but get no response or fix.
justification: The poorly designed bag system falling off repeatedly poses a high likelihood of causing a trip incident.

incident_description: I own a little-used Husqvarna 125L grass trimmer, which was purchased from Lowes in 2007  and while attempting to start it recently and ended up with gas splashed all over my hands.  The cause immediately became evident when inspecting  the special molded fuel pickup lines which were completely rotted and had leaked gas while attempting the starts up.  I contacted Husqvarna after noting a similar CPSC recall on anther trimmer model and was told that the 125L is not part of the recall program.  I was instructed to to repair the unit out of warranty and have it inspected by a dealer.  This unit has been used less than a dozen or so times since it's purchase and should not have failed in such a dangerous way.  It's clear that the materials being used are substandard (it's made in China) and result in a risk of skin contamination and other hazards.  Pressure needs to be applied to Husqvarna to improve the safety and quality of these products.  It was also one of the more expensive units on the market and one would most certainly expect better quality.
justification: Gas splashed on hands, no injury reported but potential skin contamination hazard.

incident_description:
While trying to start my Ryobi Touch Start Model RY29550 electric start gasoline powered string trimmer, the fuel line crumbled spilling fuel down the engine and on to my hands.  Fortunately this was a cold start and not a restart while trimming, so nothing caught fire.  

It is still an extreme fire risk as the fuel line material is damaged by the fuel and could fail even while the engine is hot and running.  The fuel line material should be changed to something not effected by gasoline or ethanol blends to prevent fire risks.
justification: Although no injury occurred this time, the fuel line's susceptibility to gasoline poses a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: The steering went out on our BX2200.  This happens anytime the tractor gets warm.  The dealer has had the tractor 3 times and not fixed it.  We had a very close call with it in December, 2011.  We were going down a hill when the steering went out.  This caused the tractor to crash into a tree, bending the bucket and breaking the supports on the bucket.  Luckily no one was injured.
justification: The incident has occurred before and the dealer's inability to fix it increases the likelihood of it happening again, potentially causing an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his father purchased a lawn tractor and they noticed that the gas tank is deteriorating. The consumer stated that his father noticed multiple cracks on the gas tank and he patched them to prevent a leakage. The consumer stated that it is a 4 gallons gas tank and is located underneath the seat. 

The consumer does not have specific details, but he stated that he believes that these cracks have not been cause by any incidents. The consumer did not notice any other damages on the lawn tractor.

The consumer stated that his father was not injured. 

The consumer stated that the manufacturer advised him to contact CPSC and to visit their website to file a complaint.
justification: Although no immediate harm was reported, the deteriorating gas tank poses a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible future consequences.

incident_description: Using this electric trimmer and switched hands to pull a branch out of the bush. Trigger released but blade kept running. Hit my hand against blade while pulling on the branch. Trimmre lacerated two fingers on my right hand. Blade did not stop for several seconds when trigger is off. Needs a brake for instant stop. Had to go to Emergency and get stitches in fingers. Not sure yet of outcome.
justification: Injury occurred due to the trimmer's blade continuing to run after the trigger was released, increasing the likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Incident Description
Sears Craftsman Mower (Model 536.270280) fuel tank started to leak gas on floor of garage. Gas tank part number is 7601040. I first noticed that garage smelled of gas, but it took me two days to see a puddle of gas on the floor of the garage under the mower. I removed and drained gas tank and filled it with water to check for leaks. Leak appears to be coming from the hole where Bolt (no. 23) holds tank to mower frame.
I am wondering if this is related to other Murray manufactured mower fuel tank leaks reported in the news.
justification: No injuries reported, but potential for fire hazard due to gas leak.

incident_description: Installed a patriot landscape post solar light and when nigh hit realized the light was not working.  So I looked and realized that the tab on the battery was not pulled so that the battery would contact the product.  To pull this tab off you have to take the cap off of the top by twisting it.  I tried and it would come off so then I thought I would go try the other one since I have 2 of them (they come in sets of two).  than one twisted off easier.  Then I went back to the first one and tried again that when it cut my hand open in three places.  Two where just minor and no blood but the third was in between my fingers and that one started to bleed and has a pretty good cut.  I had to bandage and apple pressure for it to stop.  I went back and looked at the light and realized that the top of it was razor sharp, which can not be safe at all.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, with a cut between the fingers that bled and required bandaging.

incident_description: my gas grill is less than 3 years old  Brinkmann 810-9520s and when I ignite the burner the flame sounds real strong and is shooting a rushing flame high above the grill and i only have the ignition buner on I have never seen anything like this in over 50 years of my life. It seems like the gas is coming out very rapidly and out of control turned off the maon gas tank valve and the rushing flame burned out .I know some manically uninclined person would not know what to do and it could explode and kill someone or burn their house down. please can we get this kind of garbage off the market
justification: The rapid, uncontrolled gas emission and high flame could lead to a fire or explosion, posing a significant risk to life and property.

incident_description:
Once repair completed [REDACTED], caller lit his grill then within one minute he heard a sound similar to that of gas escaping.
He went to the grill, tried to tighten the fitting but couldn't tighten it anymore.

He turned valve off on propane tank.

[REDACTED].

He said that if he had not remained nearby there could have been a fire with damage.

He would like these grills inspected by investigators before something more serious happens.
justification: Potential for fire and property damage was high, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I have Coleman Gas Grill 5600. the information on the back production plate:  Model 9990-646 SN# 139467.

Monday May 28, 2012. We invited few friends over for memorial day. the grill has to separate compartment, each has two burners. I turned the four burns on to heat the grill. then after 15 minutes, I put on my steak on one side and chicken on the other side, closed the cover for the grill.  in few minutes i was ready to jump in the pull, i was standing with the grill behind me. I heard scream from my brothers and guests that flames are shouting out of the grill, back side. My shorts wear on fire.  I jumped in the water as my brother ran to turn the gas off. I was OK, not burned
The grilling stopped, and we waited for the girl to cool off. Once it did, we took the top grill screen of on the right compartment.  We removed the bottom try and seen both burners in has been split broak about two inch from the back, when that happened, the bottom end of the burner dropped down and ws open for the gas to flow to the back of the girl and have the flames shouting out. What was crazy, that both burners that are made of heavy steel, wear clear-cut broke in the same area same time.

Today,  I called Coleman and talked with customer support.  I advised the first operator of what happened, and asked her if there is an safety issue with the unit or known recalls, she said now, at first she told me that I need to replace the burners, then with me pushing the safety issue she offered to send me replacement for the burners. I offered to send the burners back for analysis; she said that was not important. She never asked me about the information that is on the unit sticker, like the model number and the serial number.  Needles to call I did not feel satisfied tht Coleman cares about the safety of it customers and what happened to me could happen again with some else.
After finishing the call, I get on your website and researched outstanding issues for the Coleman 5600 Grill and found there si a recall for the gas regulator assembly.   
I called back to Coleman, the second operator was more concerned, I explained the issue and inquired about the gas regulator assembly recall. She said that was in 2005, meaning I need not worry about it. [REDACTED] say I was not assure that my  grill unite assembly is safe.  As far as the broken burners, first she offered to replace them.  When I raised the safety issue and other customers, she put me on hold , then told me that they want to pick up the unite and if I have the box for it, I said of course no, she put me back on hold.  When she came back on line, she said someone would call me.  I was not given tracking number, when I asked for one, I was giving tracking number:  [REDACTED]
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to broken burners, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was using the lawn mower according to the instruction.  While cutting the lawn sideways uphill, he noticed that the gas was pouring out of the air cleaner onto the the motor.  There is no warning about this that it can tilt and cause a hazardous condition.

5/7/12  The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised not to use the lawn mower uphill  anymore because this incident would occur.


The consumer stated that this lawn mower has a faulty design with the gas being unable to stay without pouring out when going uphill.  He is concerned of the safety hazard it poses.
justification: The incident occurred due to a design flaw, making it likely to happen again if not addressed.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he purchased a used riding lawn mower and used it for the first time 05/02/2012. The consumer stated that while in used the lawn mower ran out of gas. The gas tank is located in the front under the hood and behind the engine. The consumer stated that when he went to fill the gas tank, he realized that it has a crack. He stated that it seemed as though the gas tank is deteriorating. 

The consumer stated that he will replace the gas tank. The consumer was not injured. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they did not assist him effectively. He stated that they kept asking him about his warranty and it seemed that the representative did not understand his request.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have led to one if the consumer had not noticed the gas tank crack in time.

incident_description:
The context of the the following report is based on a post-recall, repair-kit retrofitted Charmglow grill:

As many grill owners know, recalls are important to follow and heed. Having purchase a Charmglow Home Depot Grill in 2005, we learned about a recall and received the retrofit kit after incident #1.

Incident #1 After lighting the grill last year, we noticed the smell of propane within minutes. The igniter had burned through the hose. We immediately found a recall on CPSC and notified the manufacturer. We installed the retrofit kit.

Incident #2 Two months after retro fit install, we were grilling happily on our patio- we had 7 guests and a two year old waiting for burgers and steak. Instead, we heard a whoosh and saw flames licking our from the interior of the grill. After running for safety, we called the FD and waited across the street for the inevitable propane explosion. Thankfully, one of our guests was able to extinguish the fire. What we have now is a charred patio area , frayed nerves and questions about the 'repair' kit, along with overall negligible consumer confidence in the manufacturer.
justification: Although the grill was retrofitted after the first incident, a second incident occurred, indicating a possible issue with the repair kit.

incident_description:
The caller bought a Troy Bilt Bronco and while mowing his lawn at normal speeds it sped out of control and he was unable to control it. 
On 9/21/2011 the mower had over turned and fell on his right leg. The caller had received lacerations to his right leg and had went to hospital to receive stitches. The caller was not admitted to the hospital but was treated and sent home. He received treatment at Angel Community Hospital in Franklin, N.C. 
After the incident the mower was taken to Lowes Mower company and they advised him that they would repair the mower. The caller was unknown about the exact repairs that were performed on the mower. The company had kept the mower for 12 to 13 days and was brought back to the caller.
On 12/5/2011 the incident had re occurred. 
The manufacturer was contacted approximately 12/5/2011 and recently and they did not offer any assistance.
The caller feels that the lawn mower is a safety hazard that should be reported. 

[The following are additional notes from the submitter.]
Your report is only one of three I reported about my Troy Bilt Bronco riding mower: a) speeded totally out of control, b) returned repaired mower - fails to run, and c) repaired mower breaks down.  

Finally, while cutting lawn for the first time (after two trips to repair shop) mower suddenly started to stall; cutting blade disconnected, caused mower to speed up out of control!  Brakes were of no use!  Had to cut off ignition to save having mower turning over.

I tried to contact Troy Bilt Co.  Was told could only handle warranty service - "sorry".  Only wanted to give Troy Bilt "a heads up" of possible trouble in clutch-speed control.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring medical treatment, and the likelihood of recurrence is high given the manufacturer's lack of assistance and the caller's repeated experiences.

incident_description: On 28 May 2012, had a fire from the regulator on a charmglow grill, 720-0396, model number. Extinguished the fire unknown damage to grill.
justification: Fire occurred but was extinguished with unknown damage, no injuries reported.

incident_description:
I live in Olathe, Kansas. My house was built in 2008, and we moved in in 2009. In late March, my 13 year-old daughter stepped through a board on our deck (the board broke simultaneously in two places between the supporting beams). She was not seriously injured, with minor abrasions to the leg that went through the deck board. The decking product is Weatherbest composite decking, a recalled product from Louisiana Pacific. I obviously had no idea the decking material was deteriorating (or subject to a recall) until the incident happened. 

We filed a claim with LP. They immediately sent out a company to install plywood over the deck (they used scrap pressed board, very unsightly, and it's warping, so it's a trip hazard). That was approximately 6 weeks ago. We can't use our deck, during the best outdoor weather of the year. They told us the next step was for an inspector to show up. We keep calling the inspector, but can never get a firm date for her to show up. I'm frustrated, and in the process of retaining an attorney.
justification: Injury occurred due to recalled decking material, and likelihood of similar incidents is high given the widespread use of the same product.

incident_description:
We have a new Sears Craftsmen Riding Lawn Mower. Bougt new on 3-10-12
The ignition/key switch does not work properly. The key starts it okay but the mower does not shut off when the key is turned off and the key pulled out. You have to hit the ignition switch several times and then it will shut down. In addition, the seat safety switch does not work. If the mower is running and you get off, even if the blades are engaged, the mower stays running. Additionally, the back up safety does not work.
justification: Multiple safety features (ignition switch, seat safety switch, backup safety) are malfunctioning, posing a risk of injury.

incident_description: I have a Master Forge L3218 gas grill. While grilling the grill started fire from the main gas line connected to the burner controls that leads back to the propane tank. Was fortunate to be able to shut off the gas to the tank and put out with fire extinguisher.  Once the fire was extinguished, propane tank, removed, and the grill cooled down I was able to evaluate that extent of the damage.  All the main gas lines were destroyed (even for the side burner), the light switch was melted on the inside and no longer works, and 3 of the control valves (1 rotesorie infrared control) as visible heat dame and will need to be replaced.  There is one other gas connection under the grill between the3rd and 4th control valves that was melted off that I am not sure what it is for. So today is Memorial Day and I am stuck not being able to grill out and enjoy the holiday. I also now have to see if the grill and be repaired and the gas lines changed out to a commercial grade hose or piping or if I will have to purchase another grill. Up to this point I loved this grill, just very glad that no one was hurt other than pride.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: Cub Cadet Zero Turn Mower caught fire while mowing. 2nd degree burns to left leg and 3rd degree burns to both hands
justification: Injuries sustained (2nd and 3rd degree burns) warrant a severity level of 3, and the likelihood of such an event occurring is possible, hence a likelihood of 3.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that last fall he stored his riding lawn mower, with a full tank of gas. The consumer stated that on 4/16/2012 he went to turn it on and the motor would not move. After several tries the consumer used jumper cables to connect it to the lawn mowers battery, to boost battery power on the lawn mower. 
The consumer stated that while using the jumper cables the wires that connect to the starter of the lawn mowers motor were burning hot and were emitting smoke. The consumer stopped and let the motor cool for approximately 15 minutes. The consumer stated that he tried it again and used the jumper cables to try to turn on the motor. He stated that it would turn but it was still not working properly. After several tries by using the jumper cables the motor started to turn over.  After a few more tries it started to run.  However at a low speed and running real rough.  It emitted a big cloud of smoke. 

The consumer stated that the motor was running and emitting smoke. The consumer came out from the shed where he kept the mower because he could not see with all the smoke. The consumer stated that he left the motor running for approximately 5-7 minutes and smoke was coming out of the shed. He stated that after these 5-7 minutes the motor started to function properly and the smoke dissipated rapidly. 

The consumer unhooked the jumper cables of the mower and left the mower running for approximately 3-4 minutes. He stated that he walked back in the shed and he took the mower out and cut the entire yard that approximately took 45 minutes.

The consumer stated that the lawn mower ran out of gas after using the lawn mower. He stated that it is unusual, because it usually does not take that a whole tank. The consumer stated that he went to fill the gas tank, when he opened the hood in the front he realized that there was gas all over the bottom area of the motor and the bottom frame.  The tank holds 1.5 gal.

The consumer stated that he filled the gas tank, turned it on for approximately 1-2 minutes to make sure it was running properly.  The consumer stated that he sprayed off a mixture of soap to the areas that were covered with gasoline and oil. He washed the lawn mower to remove all of the gasoline and oil. 

The consumer let the mower sit for a couple of days and on 05/04/2012 he turned on the lawn mower and the motor would not turn. The consumer stated that he looked inside and the gas tank was down to a quart of gasoline left inside. The consumer stated that the gas tank was leaking and he was unsure from where or where it was going. 

The consumer unscrewed the spark plug and over a quart of gasoline pour over the engine and the ground. The consumer stated that he tried to turn on the engine and it sprayed gas everywhere out of the spark plug hole. 

The consumer stated that after analyzing the lawn mower the consumer realized that gasoline was leaking into the engine. The consumer stated that he unplugged the plug from the oil tank and at least 2 quarts of oil and gas mixture was released into an oil pan that the consumer placed underneath the mower. 

If the spark plug wire was close enough to the lawn mower frame or any metal to cause a spark, it would of cause a massive fire or explosion.
The consumer believes that this matter should be investigated.  The carburetor float valve was stuck "open".
justification: Potential for severe injury due to gasoline leak and spark, as evidenced by the consumer's description of gas pouring out of the spark plug hole and the risk of a spark igniting the gas.

incident_description: Purchased a Brinkmann 5 Burner Gas Grill with Smoker 2 weeks ago.  Have used all of the features 4 or 5 times and this morning, put a brisket in the smoker at 250 degrees and went to the store.  When I got home (hour and a half), the grill had exploded and the entire grill was burnt to pieces.  No plastic was left, the gas lines were all disintegrated, the doors had burst open and were dented, the propane tank had blow the gas line and fitting off and was covered in white residue.  I am very lucky I wasn't standing in front of the grill or even worse, glad my three year old wasn't outside nearby.
justification: The grill's explosion and destruction, despite no injuries, indicates a high likelihood of occurrence given the recent usage and similar actions.

incident_description:
2007  Lawnmower purchased April 2007_ Roto Blade Control in the handle snapped in half due to metal fatigue while the caller was using it.

He contacted the manufacturer on April 2, 2012 and was advised only that product is an out of warranty item.
He then contacted the retailer who stated that incident is from normal wear and tear.

Caller states that this is a safety issue because the Roto Blade Control in the handle controls the blade and if broken there is no control of the blade that could cut/injure user or bystanders.

He is requesting to be reimbursed $55.00 for repair at manufacturer expense because he does not view this incident as from normal wear and tear or as a normal occurrence.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the broken handle poses a potential safety hazard, making it an incident with possible reoccurrence.

incident_description: The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his walk behind mower, as the bag behind the engine of the lawn mower feel off the mower and caused him to trip to the ground. The consumer stated that he was  mowing the lawn on normal dry conditions. The consumer stated that he was not injured after the tumble and the product is not broken or damaged; the bag seemingly just fell off. The consumer stated that he called the retailer today and was referred to the firm. The consumer called the firm and was not able to speak to anyone.
justification: The bag falling off the mower caused the consumer to trip, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was cutting wood with the chain saw for approximately 10 minutes. When I released the trigger it would not go back to idle setting. It would run at high speed causing the chain to keep moving.  I pushed the stop button but it would not stop.  I had to pull the choke lever out to make it flood itself out and stop.  I have had it serviced 5 times for the same problem.The consumer believes that this chain saw is posing a laceration hazard that needs to be investigated.
justification: The chain saw's failure to idle and stop poses a high likelihood of laceration injury.

incident_description: Handle and clutch design is extremely dangerous.  A cap nut is used on the bail clutch control, which has very sharp edges.  It is easy to pinch your hand between the bail clutch lever and handlebar when engaging the clutch.  I got a deep cut on my knuckle through my work gloves the first time I used it.  Had I not been wearing gloves, this would have cut to the bone, requiring stitches.
justification: The sharp edges of the cap nut on the bail clutch control pose a high likelihood of injury, as demonstrated by the incident where the user cut their knuckle.

incident_description:
Electronic Rat Trap, Model M240, Victor Brand, Distributed by Woodstream. 

I received a serious shock while attempting to put (4) "c" batteries in a newly purchased Electronic Rat Trap designed to electrocute a rat.  I could not tell if unit switch was in on or off position because I do not understand universal symbols for ON or OFF.  I looked all over package for an explanation of universal on/off symbols but there is no information.  Also there was no product insert sheet inside the box.  I decided to attempt putting batteries in while being really careful as I did not know if unit switch was in the ON or OFF position.  

I removed the battery compartment cover.  Battery compartment reveals space for 4 batteries inside a plastic track.  The sides of the plastic track are bent in really tight and you have to force first the positive ground battery in one side of track, then hold the negative side of battery against the spring and force battery down into track.  This is very difficult to do because of the plastic sides of the track also pushing in and blocking easy insertion of the batteries.  So you are dealing with tight battery track at same time as forcing tight batteries end to end.

Got the first two batteries in.  Started attempting to get second two batteries in. Got the first one while pushing out on the plastic track and down on the battery.  

While attempting to get the 4th battery in I had to again force the plastic track out and attempt to force the 4th battery against the large firm spring and down into the track behind the already installed 3rd battery.  It was at this point that my hand slipped and my fingers touched something (i presume it was the inside electrocution plate that is meant kill the rat. I got a serious shock and the product flew out of my hands onto the floor.  

This product is seriously dangerous.  It says all over it that it can kill small animals other than rats. It warns of electromagnetic waves and possible damage to pacemakers. It tells to be sure to remove the batteries when loading bait and yet there is none of the following:

1. No product sheet to explain in various languages how to tell if the unit is on or off before loading. This information is probably available on the internet but should be plainly available on the package as not everyone has the internet and the consumer should not have to search for this information. 
 
2. No warning to be sure not to let your hand slip and touch the plates while trying to load the difficult battery assembly.

3.  No temporary cover over the openings where the rat goes in that could be used to shield from this accidental shock when hand slipped while trying to load the tight, difficult battery compartment.

In my opinion this product should be recalled for serious lack of safety considerations and incomplete safety warnings and preventative measures.

It would be a simple matter to put a snap on plastic cover on each end of the until to be removed after loading the batteries.

It would be a simple matter to include an explanation of the on/off symbols in plain English, Spanish etc.

Furthermore, when I reported this to the manufacturer the customer service rep said that the only complaints they had were that the unit won't work if the peanut butter falls on the back metal plate. 
The only instruction on baiting says "Insert a small amount of peanut butter through the bottom hole on back of trap". It does not say anything about making sure the peanut butter does not run onto or fall onto the back plate. If I had gotten to the point of putting the peanut butter in  I would have figured  I was suppose to put the peanut butter through the hole and ONTO the back plate.   I guess we are suppose to figure out for ourselves that we are to poke the peanut butter through the hole and make it stick to the inside of the back vertical plate some how.  Additionally the picture shows about a teaspoon of peanut butter. If your peanut butter is the natural kind it most certainly would run onto the back plate.  It says to remove the batteries before baiting. I could find no where on the box that it says not to let the peanut butter touch the bottom plate.  I can imagine it is real easy for the peanut butter to fall while trying to put these difficult batteries back in the unit after inserting the peanut butter. 

Dangerous Unit! Should be redesigned so that children cannot put their hand inside or a small kitten could not put their paw inside trying to get at the peanut butter or play with the dead rat. Should include more detailed safety and use instructions.  Battery compartment should be made easier to load batteries.
justification: User received a serious shock, which could have led to injury.

incident_description: The consumer says she was having a cookout.  All of a sudden the ignitor was making noise and flames shot out up to 5 ft.  A fire marshall came who said the ignitor was faulty.  A technician sent by the retailer who said that the grill caught fire caused by gas leak from joint side burner and regulator.  The consumer says that everything inside the grill was completely burned.  The fire dept put the fire out.  Nothing else was damaged beyond the grill and no one was injured.  The consumer said that the unit caught fire after 10-15 minutes of the grill being on.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (severity level 2). The likelihood is 'possible' (3) as it resulted from a combination of a faulty ignitor and a gas leak.

incident_description: I received 1st degree burns when I lifted the lid on a hot Weber One-Touch Gold 22.5" grill.  I have used this type of grill for decades with no problems.  The older design of this product used wooden inserts on the handle.  These never got hot to the touch.  The new design uses plastic instead of wood.  The plastic gets VERY hot.  I emailed Weber about this several days ago.  I have not heard from them.
justification: The incident resulted in a 1st degree burn, indicating an injury, and the likelihood is possible given the change in design and the user's long-term experience with the product.

incident_description: I have two riding mowers, one is a Scotts by John Deere and the other is a [REDACTED] Both of these mowers have a Briggs and Stratton 20 horse power OHV INTEK motor. I purchased the [REDACTED] unit used and had it cleaned and tuned up before using it. The unit ran great for approximately half a season before the rod broke and shot out of the side of the crank case. I priced a replacement motor and found it to be more expensive that buying another mower. So I then purchased the Scotts mower lightly used I knew the previous owner and he had only used it for less than a half hour. I have put around ten hours on the mower and today the same thing happened the piston connecting rod broke shooting out of the side of the crank case and sending a piece of crank case shrapnel flying. I have serious concerns about this line of Briggs and stratton engines as I have been researching them and this seems to be a EXTREMELY common issue.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (mower destruction) but no injuries, and the likelihood is high given the repeated occurrence with the same engine type.

incident_description:
My Perfect Flame Barbeque grill went up in flames.  While preheating, flames started going very high out of the unit and soon the fire was out of control.  The wires and the gas line were completely engulfed by the fire.  Thankfully my patio is made of cement and we had a calm day with no wind.  That doesn't happen very often in central Oklahoma.  A strong south wind would have caused untold troubles with a fire that size.

In January 2010, I received replacement burners and lid and replaced those parts as part of a recall.  My model number is SLG2008A.  It was difficult to replace the burners, since the bolts that held the original burners were completely void of any heads to put a screwdriver on.  Apparently the replacement parts only lasted about as long as the original parts did.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the fire was out of control and could have easily spread if not for the calm weather and cement patio.

incident_description: Repeated flare ups when starting grill.  Burned self.  Gas line on grill also started on fire within a couple minutes after starting grill.
justification: Repeated flare-ups and subsequent burns indicate a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: I have a John Deere LX188 approx 1996 model year. The fuel pump went out causing fuel to leak out the weep hole at the bottom of the pump directly on the HOT muffler below.  I feel this is a hazard as the fuel could of easily ignited and burned the mower, garage and possibly the person riding it, as my internet searches indicated has already happened to other people.  I called John Deere customer service and they are reluctant to offer a recall but they must have realized the dangers because the replacement pump comes with a hose to direct the fuel away from the muffler.
justification: Fuel leak directly onto hot muffler poses high risk of ignition and fire, as evidenced by similar incidents reported online.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was riding his garden tractor for approximately 45 minutes and the seat shifted completely to the left side. The consumer immediately turned off the tractor and got off. The front of the seat is located on hinge for support. The consumer stated that the metal sheet underneath the hinge (8 inch bar) was cracked. The consumer stated that this is very a serious hazard because if these metal parts break they could damage the gas tank that is directly position underneath the seat. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that they could not assist him because the garden tractor is out of warranty.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the cracked metal sheet poses a potential hazard to the gas tank, making it an incident.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the Lawn mower seat safety switch is malfunctioning which cause the unit to operate unsafely, it will quit working or kill the motor while still operating, thus he is not able to control it.  The first time the dealer told me to move the seat forward, that women had trouble with the seat.  The consumer stated that when the mower was examined a year later the issue was not addressed to his satisfaction. 

In the fall of 2010 or Spring of 2011, the consumer took it a  service dealer who advised that he install a seat belt and a ROPS Bar, which would not resolve the problem of the faulty safety switch.  The consumer has not contacted the manufacturer since.

The consumer is concerned that this lawn mower is a safety hazard and could cause an accident resulting in serious injuries or fatality and that he cannot legally bypass the safety kill switch.
justification: The malfunctioning safety switch poses a high risk of injury or fatality due to loss of control while operating.

incident_description:
I have a Weber Genesis grill and was using it a few days ago (5/5/2012).  The fuel hose caught on fire which melted the rubber hose.  A hole erupted on the hose that then spewed propane out until I was able to shut it off.  Upon investigation, I determined that Weber incorrectly assembled the hose.  The rubber hose from the propane tank is connected to what they call a bulkhead.  From the bulkhead a metal flex tube is connected to route the fuel to the grill and side burner.  On this bulkhead they inserted the rubber hose where the metal one should have been.  The rubber hose touched the hot grill tray which caused the fire.

I was fortunate, this could have been much worse.

Repeated calls and e-mails to Weber have not been positive.  They refuse to accept responsibility which is why I am reporting this issue.  I am concerned that there may be other grills with the same issue.

Regards,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incorrect assembly of the fuel hose led to a fire, which could have been more severe if not caught in time.

incident_description:
I purchased a Master Forge Outdoor Gas Grill, Model # L3218, Serial # L32001245.
Two weekends ago, I turned it on to pre-heat, went into the house, and moments later ran back outside when I saw flames engulfing the right side of the grill. I reached through the flames and shut off the burners, but I could hear the gas continuing to flow and the flames did not subside. I opened the front doors and saw the gas hose, still attached to the gas tank, but not the grill, flopping around on fire. I reached inside, released the tank restraining band, slid the tank rack out of the grill and shut the tank valve off. Fortunately I was not injured and only had my arm hair singed. The resulting damage to my grill however has rendered it completely useless and irrepairable.

While attempting to find out information on the company to file a complaint, I discovered that the Consumer Product Safety Commission in cooperation with Sagittarius Sporting Goods of China have announced a safety recall on the Master Forge 5-Burner Gas Grill, model #L3218 sold by Lowes Home Improvement between September 2009 and November 2009 because of a known problem where the rubber gas line may come in contact with the Grill's firebox causing it to melt, leading to a fire. I never received any such notice.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, and the likelihood of a similar incident happening again is high due to the known design flaw.

incident_description: Lock button does not stop the trimmer when trigger is released
justification: The trimmer continues to operate after the trigger is released, posing a potential injury risk.

incident_description: Toro Lawn Mower leaks gas through the air filter when not running. Model 20330 with Briggs 6.5 HP engine. Serial number 290018687
justification: Gas leak from the air filter, though not running, poses a potential fire hazard and environmental risk, but no immediate injury threat.

incident_description: My Perfect Flame SLG Series Gas Grill caught on fire (a very substantial and dangerous fire that melted/deformed the metal components of the lid, burners, and side shelving and melted the propane gas line). This occurred AFTER I had already performed the steps outlined in the recall Release # 10-043 to address this potential problem. Despite installing the "improved" parts, a very dangerous fire occurred that destroyed my grill.
justification: The grill caught fire despite the user following recall instructions, indicating a possible design flaw.

incident_description:
Garden Treasures 39" firepit  #0085452 - we were attaching the LEG SUPPORT ASSEMBLY to the legs and the welds holding the support together came apart.  This welded piece is the support for the entire firepit.  If the welds came apart during use, the legs holding the pit in the air would not be braced and could fall and cause serious injury and/or burn the surface it is sitting on. 
LEG SUPPORT ASSEMBLY consists of 4 pieces and is welded together at each connection.
justification: Weld failure on the leg support assembly could lead to the firepit collapsing, causing injury.

incident_description:
A battery operated portable lantern, turned on only one time, had the inside battery casing melt. Along with the outer jackets of the batteries split and become separate from the core. 
The only name on the product is "Utilitech". 
It was purchases at Lowes. 
I have saved all the batteries and still have the lantern.
This was purchased as a christmas gift to be used in case of a power failure and has been sitting unused since the battery installation.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have caused a fire or property damage, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: Repeated failure of corrigated aluminum supply line to distribution manifold. Tubing develops hole in supply line leaking LP gas out the right side of unit creating flash fire situation. This is second failure as tube has been replaced for same defect.
justification: Repeated failure indicates a high likelihood of recurrence, and while no injuries were reported, the potential for flash fire poses a significant risk.

incident_description: toro lawn mower model 20199 purchased on 4/3/12. mowed grass 2 times went to work come home my house is full of gas fumes.took back to the dealer said they fixed the gas dripping from the carb.took it home mowed the grass put it back in the garage. went to work come home house is full of gas fumes .  i called toro to tell them they said take back to the dealer.i started looking at reviews on my computer to see this is happening to alot of people just not me this is a danger.home depo reviews alone have 2 commets of gas coming out of the carb.this is a new lawn mower out and this needs to be looked at fast this mower is a timemaster 30 inch
justification: Gas fumes filled the house twice, indicating a recurring issue with the carburetor.

incident_description:
After mowing the yard, I returned the riding mower to the pole barn.  Within 5 minutes as I was returning to the house I heard a hugh explosion and ran to the barn to see what had happened.
The Cub Cadet riding mower was a ball of flames.  Although I had a fire extinguisher at hand, I was only able to use the nearby hose to water down the surrounding area until the flames slowed down to where I was able to extinguish the lawn mower.  The mower was the cause and was the so engulfed in flames that there was no mistaking it was the source of the explosion.

   All surrounding objects were either burnt crisp or had melted from the heat.  The roof of the barn is very elevated so there was fortunately no structural damage done.

   No injuries occurred (thankfully I was not still on it), however, there was a lot of damage and destruction done in the surrounding area.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident caused significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I purchased a water powered back up sump pump. It was manufactured by Zoeller Pumps 3649 Cane Run Road, Louisville, KY.  It was installed on May 30th 2011. When Huricane Iren Hit New Jersey Aug 28th 2011 we lost power. The new back up pump failed to turn on and when i turned it on manually it did not pump. This was all verified by the installer a few days latter.  The basement took on water, which caused damage to the finished basement. 
When I spoke to the manufacture they stated to turm it into my home owners or sue them. This could let to great personell injury whith eletricity and water mising,not to mention the chance of mold now growing in my basement.

[REDACTED] from the manufacture told me they have had other pumps fail and mentioned 3 that failed and caused $70,000  of damage. He also sited that the stopped shipping the pump. I feel had they done a product recall for know quality problems my basement would not had taken on water, and this dangerous situation would had been avoided. I aslo spoke with [REDACTED] and he rudely told me the same thing sue them. No effort was made on their part to eith pay for my dames or replace the pump. I requested that the come here and see for them selfes that the pump does not work and they refused.
This is a dangerous product out on the market and the manufacture is aware of quailty issues. Please force a recall before someone gets electracuted or has sever mold issues. This company is not being responsible for their known product failures.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident resulted in property damage and created a potential health hazard due to mold growth.

incident_description: We have owned a Perfect Flame Grill for approximately 3 years.  Model # SLG2006C purchased at Lowe's in Chino Hills CA.  The unit was used 2-3 times a month [maybe] and performed normally.  Recently, when being used the unit caught on fire and burned severely the cabinet, knobs valves all bar b que accessories in the drawer.  The unit is a complete loss.
justification: The grill caught fire, causing significant damage but no injuries, indicating a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
We purchased a Master Forge Grill from Lowes, Model #MFA350cnp, less than a year ago.  The Regulator and Hose Model AZF Date Code 1050 is leaking.

While searching for a replacement, I noticed a similar problem with another grill manufacturer using the same part from China with a recall already initiated:




[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the grill's regulator and hose leaking poses a fire hazard, making it likely that an incident could occur.

incident_description: Was cooking on my gas grill and the flames were about 2 feet high when I opened the cover I shut the gas off quickly and shut the lid the insides of the grill are all gone nothing left just rust
justification: Flames reaching 2 feet high pose a risk of property damage, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description:
This Spring when I had finished mowing my lawn, I placed the mower in the garage.   The next morning I awoke to the strong smell of gasoline permeating throughout my home.  I discovered 
the source of the smell was my Poulan lawn mower.  All of the remaining gasoline in it's tank had leaked out onto my garage floor.  In trying to determine the cause, I discovered that anytime the mower is shut off, the gasoline leaks from the carburetor.  The defective carburetor is on a Kohler
engine, (model # XT173-0084).  Upon researching the mower on the internet, I found countless individuals having the same problem.  Any gasoline left in the tank leaks freely from the carburetor.  I also learned from the Internet other people were told to install a fuel shut-off valve to
prevent the gasoline from reaching the carborator when it is shut off, however that does not really solve the problem.This to me is just a band-aid and does not solve the problem with the defective carborator.  Also I was told that rebuilding the carborator did not solve the problem either.  
I contacted Kohler and was told to call a local repair facility.  When I explained the problem to them
(QC Power Equipment Inc. Davenport, IA) they were familiar with the problem but had no solutions.
They told me that they would contact the Kohler representative and get back with me.  Since I was not contacted in 2 weeks, I called QC Power again and was told they had not heard from Kohler.  I have continued to call QC Power and still they have not had a phone call from Kohler.  I am greatly inconvienced by not being able to use my mower which I have had for only one year but also I don't want my home or anyone else's to burn down as this is definitely a fire hazard.  I am requesting the CPSC look into this situation that could result in a senseless loss of life.
justification: Gasoline leak from the defective carburetor poses a significant fire hazard, though no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: Purchased a BRINKMAN LP gas patio grill at Home Depot; the grill is labeled PORTICO COLLECTION and is model # 810-3260-S.  I took the unit home and assembled per the instructions and connected LP gas tank.  Started grill to grill fish in a basket.  Waited for grill to warm up with temperature set at medium low.  I was ready to place fish on grill and reached with one hand to grab the grill handle on the front to open the grill top.  The grill was so hot I dropped the handle as it was too hot to hold.  I received minor burns on two fingers.  This grill also was found to have very sharp edges on the sides of grill top.  I believe that this product represents a potential hazard and is improperly designed/manufactured.  I am returning product to Home Depot and advising them of potential issues.  If a small child were to walk by this grill while it was turned on and reached to grab the grill handle, I believe that they could suffer burns to their fingers/hands.  The grill shipping box indicates that it is "DESIGN CERTIFIED"; i am not sure if this is a industry ceretification or simply a play on words.  This product is dangerous and hazardous.
justification: The grill's handle became dangerously hot, causing minor burns, and its sharp edges pose a risk of injury, especially to children.

incident_description:
The Perfect Flame gas grill gas burners all began to significantly deteriorate over the course of three years of ownership/usage, with holes in the burner tubes that were approximately 3-4 inches in length and 1/2 to 3/4 in. in height.  This problem was seen in other Perfect Flame models that were the subject of a recall by the company; however, this product was not.  

The deterioration of all four burners allows large quantities of gas to escape unregulated, leading to large flames and the potential for fires inside the grill and outside.  On several occasions, the bottom of the grill would catch fire.  The flames on two of the four burners, when gas was left on medium, would rise approximately 6 inches to 1 ft. above the surface of the grill.

As was previously mentioned, the grill is approximately 3-4 years old.  It has been kept covered the entire time of ownership.

The Perfect Flame grill was subject to prior recalls, with the SLG model being recalled for similar reasons (November 18, 2009, Release #10-043).  The GAC, which I own, was subject to a recall for different reasons, although my date code (LO) is outside of the recall range.
justification: The grill's significant deterioration and unregulated gas leaks pose a high likelihood of causing fires, although no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Power switch on Black & Decker hedge trimmer (HT020) does not turn off when released. Switch was stuck in on position when power cord was attached. In use when turned on switch stays in on position and can not be easily disengaged.
justification: The incident resulted in an inability to turn off the hedge trimmer, posing a potential hazard but no immediate injury.

incident_description: Earthwise cordless lawn mower model #60120.  Two year old mower.  Fully charged battery would not start mower.  Then on the fourth attempt the ignition switch box started smoking.  There was no physical damage to the ignition switch box.
justification: While no injury occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to the smoking ignition switch box, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Friday, March 16, 2012 caller purchased T-Con Mouse Trap, set it up in his kitchen then after approximately an hour he heard a "snap", went to kitchen.

No mouse in trap

Bottom piece is round, 4" in diameter, Spindle in center comes up about 2", then a plastic top that goes over the spindle.

Somehow the axle from the bottom part snapped and a quarter inch of the plastic shot up and caller found it a couple inches away from the rest of the trap.

Model# 0261071

He is reporting as a safety hazard because if a curious child had been trying to see how it worked or got close to it for any reason could have lost an eye or been injured in another way when the plastic hit him or her.

He believes that the plastic should be much tougher.

UPDATE FROM SUBMITTER: A quarter inch of the vertical axle was found a couple of inches away but that was only half of the piece that had broken off. When the piece broke off it split vertically and a second piece was found on 31 March 2012 across the kitchen in a wicker basket on the opposite counter that is used to hold bags of onions. That second half was imbedded in the weave of the wicker and at first I thought it was a black spot on the wicker. I was able to pry it out. That piece had traveled more than 52 inches and I do not know how high above the counter the apex of the arc was.
justification: The incident involved a projectile (plastic piece) that could cause serious injury, specifically to children, making it a high likelihood event.

incident_description:
on 05/02/2012 at approx. 1930 hrs. My wife had just finished using our BBQ, she went inside sat down the plate of food turned around and our BBQ was fully engulfed in flames. My wife got water on the fire and the fire exploded into small balls of fire. Thanks to the two dads that live across the street who used fire extinguishers and my wife on the water hose the fire was contained and only minor damaged was done to our deck. After I got home from work I checked the internet for recalls and found a recall on our BBQ which we bought in 2009. The BBQ is as follows:

Perfect Flame
Model: GAC3615
serial # 022151
Date Code: KZ
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire that could have escalated, making it an Incident with potential for injury.

incident_description:
Leaking gas tank from the Honda Harmony II lawn mower may cause fire hazard:
I picked up the lawn mower after tune up at a local shop on April 6, 2012. During transit, I smelled gasoline
smell in the car and I opened all the windows. At home, during lawn mowing the smell continued so I stopped
and checked the lawn mower. It took me a while to figure out that the gas was leaking from the lawn mower's
gas tank. I took the lawn mower back for service and they confirmed that the leak was indeed from the gas
ank. I left lawn mower for the replacement of the gas tank. They ordered a new gas tank and a new Honda
gas tank was installed and I picked up the lawn mower on April 13, 2012.
Please note that this lawn mower has 50-100 hours of usage due to my illness.
There were no injuries.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the gas leak posed a fire hazard, making it an incident.

incident_description: I purchased a pair of "Hedge Shear" from Dollar General.  The first time I went to use them on my rose bushes the handles bent together as you applied pressure to the handles.  The handles close in on your thumbs.  I had bruises on both thumbs.  I was only trimming very small rose bushes.  As I checked the handles, you could see the metal between the handle grips and the blade will bend with very little effort, which would be very dangerous if I had been using them on a branch of tree.
justification: The handles bent inwards, putting pressure on the thumbs and causing bruises, indicating a potential for serious injury.

incident_description:
I have a John Deere L-108 Riding Mower.  I see from other reports on this site that there have been numerous reports of gas tank leaking/failure.

I checked with my local John Deere Dealer, Georgetown Farm Supply in Georgetown, Texas and they would not cover the repair to have the tank replaced.  I expressed my dissatisfaction with them and have contacted the manufacturer, John Deere through their website to seek a refund.  I had a battery replaced and the cost of this and the tank repair was $232, of which $45 was for a new battery.

As noted in other complaints about this product, the leaking gas tank exposed me to hazard in that I keep the mower in an enclosed shed, which filled with gasoline vapors from the leaking tank.  Thankfully, there was no explosion.  But in routine operation, the mower leaked gas from the tank onto the lower part of the chassis and the mower deck.  A spark could have easily caused an explosion, which in turn could be lethal or fatal.


Deer should have recalled this product and made good on the repair.  They did not.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the gas leak posed a significant fire hazard, making it an incident with high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer notices that when he releases the trigger the chain saw continues to operate. The consumer states that he has to press the chain brake to stop it from operating.

The amount of time the chain saw was in use was not provided. 

The consumer noticed a recall (see release #81-024) where the hazard was with the saw's "on/off" switch may fail to function properly. The consumer has not used the saw since noticing the failure.

He attempted to contact the firm but was not able to get through. He plans to contact an authorize dealer for further assistance. Consumer added that he is unable to find a dealer that will cover the repair.
justification: The incident did not result in injury, but the potential for injury is high due to the malfunctioning 'on/off' switch.

incident_description: My husband and I own a Craftsman  20HP 42" lawn tractor model #917.287070 which we purchased at the  Ellsworth,Maine Sears store on 5/29/12. It has a Briggs and Stratton motor model #31P977-0575-E1. My husband went out today to start it up  and upon starting it blew the side of the motor out of it. I am talking pieces of metal exploded and landed on the ground. This could have been serious if someone especially a child was around the area.
