incident_description:
Opened the Jeep 12 LED multi purpose tripod flashlight and inserted the 3-AAA as instructed.  First set of batteries did not work so removed the battery pack and the pack was hot to the touch.  Inserted a second set of fresh AAA batteries and they did not work so took out the second set and this set was extremely touch almost burning my palm when I held the pack.  Obviously a short in the pack causing the batteries to heat up.

Contacted the manufacturer via email (no response) and phone (twice).  The CSR on the phone was unhelpful and unable to assist beyond the scripted conversation due to limited english.  Offered to return the product for their examination but not a part of their script so the went into an infinite loop regarding waiting 5 minutes and reinserting another set of batteries turning it on for xx minutes turning it off, waiting xx minutes then turning it back on and it should work.  Great, in the mean time it'll probably catch on fire.  

Company needs CSRs that can speak the native language of the consumer they are conversing with to enable effective communication.
justification: Potential for severe burns due to overheating battery pack.

incident_description: I ordered a refurbished grass trimmer, manufactor by MTDR and sold by The Outdoor Store. P.O. Box 600 Brown's Summit, NC 27214  The weeder shoots out oil out of the airfilter compartment. Thus creating a bio-hazard and possible fire.
justification: The incident involves a potential bio-hazard and fire risk, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: echo ea-410 earth auger, used for drilling holes to plant flowers, fence posts. When in use the exhaust gases from the motor blow directly in the face of the operator. It is a design problem.

incident_description:
I purchased  a Toro e-cycler electric lawn mower last summer.  For the past two weeks, the automatic shutoff safety feature has failed to work.  I let go of the handle, and the lawn mower continues to run at normal speed.  I actually have to pry the handle over to get this machine to shut down.

Inasmuch as Toro has made it clear to me that they will not stand behind their product with respect to past complaints, I feel it now necessary to report this condition to you for handling.

[REDACTED]

incident_description: We have a Toro Snow Blower, Model 38282, which we purchased in November of 2009. We used it through the winter of 2010 and the first part of 2011. incident_description: Parking break failed on 5 day old Husqvarna Riding Mower YTH22V42. Parking break will not engage and the mower will not stay in a stationary position. incident_description: Black and Decker 12in electric grass trimmer and edger was purchased at Lowes 4/22 to edge a small yard.  Used the product for 20 minutes and product started billowing smoke (no fire) and then stopped working.  Product was returned to store for refund.
justification: Although no fire occurred, the product emitting smoke and ceasing to function after brief use indicates a potential safety issue and likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Brinkman 4 Burner Gas LP Grill has caught huge fires 3 Times. I was burned the first fire. 
I clean out the bottom every time and it still catches fire. Now it will not even light.
I need to buy new burners for inside due to the fires had to be put out with baking soda. I could not find the new burners as an option on th Brinkman.net web site for my grill. I wonder if there are issues with this. This is a year and half old.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that when he would ride the lawn mower down hill it would freewill, having him loose control of the mower. When he would press the breaks they would lock and would be no traction.  When the tractor lost control he steer it until the tractor stopped.

He took the mower to the dealer and have them repair the mower. They replace the transmission and he no longer has the problem.

incident_description: Using the smoker on med/high heat went to go check on it about an hour into use. found flames coming out from under the unit. Turned off fuel source and found the gas hose had melted causing fire.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not likely to occur frequently due to the need for a combination of high heat and neglect.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury (partial foot amputation) and the occurrence likelihood is considered possible due to the safety switch malfunction.

incident_description:
Possible fire or explosion hazard - gas tank leak on Toro 22" Recycler Mower, model 20073, serial # 270055479, build date is likely in 2006.  Engine model is a Tecumseh LV195XA Serial# 363089E.  Tecumseh was bought out by the company Certified Parts.  New Fuel Tank part number is 37947. 

I purchased this mower new and within a few years, the gas tank developed a leak at the seam on the the middle back of the tank.  The tank is attached directly to the back of the engine.  I attribute this problem to a faulty gas tank design.  The leaking gas can cause fumes to build up in a homeowners garage which can lead to an explosion, or can lead to a fire while in operation.

I see many complaints on the web for the same issue.  There are several types of mowers with these engines that have the leaky gas tanks.  A recall was put in for some models but not all.  

A few references are:
http://www.saferproducts.gove/ViewIncident/1176399
http://www.craftkb.com/Uwe/Forum.aspx/metalworking/4696/fixing-gas-tank-on-lawn-mower
http://www.abbysguide.com/ope/discussions/38607-0-1.html
justification: The gas tank leak poses a high likelihood of an incident (fire or explosion) due to the accumulation of fumes in the garage or during operation, as evidenced by numerous online complaints and a partial recall.

incident_description:
On the day of the incident, consumer plugged an extension cord into a power outlet, inside the house, and then uncoiled the cord as he carried it to a location near the gate.  He returned to the house and got the hedge trimmer and carried it to the gate.  He placed the trimmer onto the concrete then took the trimmer's power cord in his left hand and the extension cord in his right hand.  The consumer believed that the lock button was in the off position and that the trimmer was off, but the lock button and trigger were in the locked on position. He plugged the trimmer's power cord into the extension cord and the trimmer suddenly and unexpectedly became energized. 
The consumer raised his right hand to protect his face from the reciprocating blade, the blade contacted his hand, and he was injured.
The trimmer blades are sharp and as such create a cutting hazard. 
Black and Decker's instructions and warnings were inadequate because they provide confusing information. In a diagram in their Instruction Manual for the hedge trimmer Black and Decker identifies the trigger and the lock button and do not refer to a "switch".
Black and Decker should have placed the warning on a label that was right on the power cord, near the plug. A warning in such a location would be located where the user's attention was focused, when he was in danger of encountering the hazard.
justification: Injury occurred due to user error compounded by inadequate warnings on the product.

The blade adaptor on my Sears Model 917.385270   625 Series   Briggs and Stratton   22" side discharge mower split into tow pieces and one of the pieces was ejected between my legs into the gargae refrigerator. If this broken part has hit me in the leg I feel that I would have sustained a serious injury.

I purchased a repacement part at a Sears Repair Center and noticed that the  broken part - #420097 - was replaced by # 418373.  The new part appears to be made of a "heavier" metal than the original part.

I do not believe that the blade was over torqued and the mower had not hit any rocks or obstacles the day before to cause thsi fracturing of the blade adaptor.
justification: The incident involved a sharp object (blade adaptor) being ejected at high speed, posing a high likelihood of serious injury if it had struck the user.

incident_description:
My Toro Power Clear 180 snowblower  S/N 310005757 has leaked gas since new. 

It went into the shop  for repair on 2/14/10  It leaked right away and went into the shop again 3/2/10. It was noted that a carburetor was replaced. (This was before the recall). It again leaked and went in for repairs 1/8/12.  The dealer told me that it would relieve a new carburetor because the one replaced 1/8/12 was also defective.

It does not appear that Toro replaced the carburetor on 1/8, and Toro refuses to respond if the machine has been fixed or not.
justification: The repeated gas leaks and lack of resolution despite multiple repairs indicate a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description:
While tilling garden releasing the the on/off bar did not disengage transmission. I was in a bad spot, the tiller trapped me in the fence, pushed me in to and through fence, boot became trapped in fence, slammed the ground hard enough my head bounced. Fortunately the tiller became hung in the fence otherwise it would have run over me due to my boot being caught in fence.

After speaking to the people who do my small engine repairs they informed me that the belt that had failed was also responsible for disengaging the transmission. Until the incident the machine had performed flawlessly. They also informed me that if a pulley failed the same could happen.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, and the likelihood is high given the machine's flawless performance until the incident and the belt's dual responsibility.

incident_description:
I bought a brand new Kenmore 3 burner grill.
I lit the grill for the first time and kept the lid closed for 5-10 minutes.
When i went to open the lid, the lid was extremelly hot. the handle of the lid is made out of metal.
I had to shut the grill off and wait 5 minutes for it cool before lifting the lid of the BBQ.
I called Sears and they said use a mitten and that other have complained.

The product is not well designed and will cause a burn when touched.
justification: The grill's metal handle can cause burns when touched after use, as demonstrated by the user's experience and confirmed by Sears' acknowledgment of similar complaints.

incident_description: We have a Bond GAC3615 grill that recently had a small fire on the inside and the right lid was damaged.  The rest of the grill seemed fine, so I went online to try to find a replacement lid.  I then came across the recall of the Perfect flame GAC3516 grill and it appears to be the same exact grill, but has the Perfect Flame lable instead of BOND.  So, I went to look at the information written on our grill.  Our serial # is 001297...which is a serial number that is included in the Perfect Flame grill recall.  So, it appears that Bond is selling the same exact grill that Perfect Flame was selling, but I can't find a recall for the Bond Grill.  Maybe it hasn't been discovered that this is the same exact grill?
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident of a small fire inside the grill indicates a potential hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description: I use my grill that I bought at lowes in May of 2008 regularly.  The description is as follows;Perfect Flame Double Lid Four Burner Gas Grills, model number GAC 3615 Serial number 050627.  Since purchasing the grill, small flames are continuosly catching inside the grill which I thought were normal as the flames were not extremely big, I tought it was greese and fat falling from the items I was cooking, however, on 2 occasions, the grill completely caught fire and I had to throw water on it quickly.  Had I not been around it, the damages could of been significant as the flames were everywhere.  Again, I may of been naive but did not report it as I thought debris from old food was the cause, until I went on the lowes website and saw that my grill's model number was recalled.  Initially and incredibely,  when I visited the store, the manager refused to do anything about it as they said my serial number did not match the parameters of the recall.  I then called the lowes customer service to explain my situation, they said the store should of accepted my grill, that is where we stand now.  I am not sure if they will take it back, but regardless, I wanted to let you know, the exact description of the recall is what happened to me in and it was preety scary.
justification: The grill caught fire twice, and could have caused significant damage if not attended to.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,
I"m writing in regards to some trouble we recently had with our Blue Ember Fiesta grill. In Wisconsin the grilling season is just beginning so I attempted to use our grill this weekend. Shortly after preheating, I noticed an irregular amount of smoke in the back yard. Smoke was coming our from the grill cover and bottom doors. I was going to lift the cover but could see flames so I left it closed and turned off the burners. I pulled it to the middle of the yard and left it to cool. I had our kitchen fire extinguisher ready but didn't deploy it. I was worried about opening the cover if I didn't have too to use the extinguisher. 
When it stopped smoking I looked it over. The inside was completely charred and black. The once nice clean stainless steel is now stained black and full of greasy grime. Half of the grease pan seems to have crumbled into pieces and is just gone. The remaining half is still hanging from the guide rail but is extremely brittle. My 20lb LP tanks is full of grime and the entire bottom storage areas is disgusting. It's like the hot grease caught fire and splattered all over.
 
After doing some research, I noticed this was not the only incident like this and found there's a recall on my particular grill. I would like to make some arrangements to correct the issues I'm having. I purchased this grill because of the stainless steel features, reasonable price, and ratings in consumer reports but after this issue I'm deeply concerned about the product.
 
Respectfully,
[redacted] 
Blue Ember Fiesta Gas Grill
Model-FG50069-U401
Serial #- 07013900
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a fire pit sold through Walmart, imported by Dewan & Sons and manufactured in India. The problem I am having is the threading on the grating handle is only about a ÃÂ¼ inch total. This was not long enough to clear the support and grating and then fasten with a nut securely. The threading stripped and the handle popped off while the lid was being lifted off the fire pit resulting in the lid falling into the fire and casting burning material outwards at people standing around the pit.  I contacted the Importer and manufacturing contacts and was told they know of the issue and donÃÂt care about the safety concern, that they donÃÂt plan on changing the design and will continue to sell an unsafe product that will likely result in injury to all users including children standing around the fire pits making smores.
The site where the item can be found is here:
http://www.walmart.com/ip/Better-Homes-and-Gardens-Oil-Rubbed-Brass-Urn-Fire-Pit/17235792
The Importer/Manufacturers site is here:
http://dewansons.com
From talking with the manufacturer I believe this is an issue with most if not all of their fire pits currently for sale in the U.S. and they stated they are insured up to 5 million in losses per incident so they would rather continue making faulty dangerous products then have to make design changes that would cost them money.
justification: The stripped threading and handle popping off could easily cause burns or other injuries, and the manufacturer's indifference to the issue increases the likelihood of such incidents.

incident_description:
I am writing to you about a serious accident that occurred using a vertical smoker. The smoker was a gift years ago and I have used it quite often. 
It is Landmann / Great Outdoors Smoky Mountain Model #A033141, Serial #531000468, 25,000 BTU/hr vertical smoker, 16ÃÂx 24ÃÂx 45ÃÂ. 
The accident occurred on February 5, 2012, when the propane flame went out and I went to open the door to the smoker to check the beef brisket I was preparing. The chamber had filled with gas, and a spark from the wood chip box inside the smoker ignited the gas before I could open the door. The latched door to the smoker exploded into me, and caused some serious damage. I was rushed to the hospital ER where I was given 12 stitches, a CAT scan and a few weeks of rehabilitation. The hair was burned off of my eyelids, eyebrows, and singed the left side of my head. 
I am 6ÃÂ 3ÃÂ tall and weigh 220 lbs, and I fully believe that the blast could have killed a child. Doing some research online, I have found several recall notices for vertical smokers due to safety issues with these types of regulators (gas shut off after flame goes out). 
Thank you for your attention to this serious issue. I want to prevent this from happening to someone else if possible, especially a child.
justification: Injury occurred due to gas accumulation and ignition, and similar incidents have been reported online.

incident_description:
Brinkmann Gas Grill Model number 810-9425-W, serial# TBC-9425W.

My wife was grilling when the grill caught on fire. The knobs/valves and hoses were all engulfed in flames. Black smoke poured out and was sucked into out home. Luckily my wife was able to get my infant son out of the house, and turn off the gas supply before the fire reached the propane tank.. All the hoses and valves are now burned and melted. Luckily no injuries, just some black smoke damage inside our house.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire and smoke event, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I had a UniFlame gas grill that is about 2.5 years old. The unit was well kept and in good working order. Model GBC976W

While grilling out, I left the grill unattended for 12 minutes. When I came back out I noticed that the grill brush that was 3 inches from the grill was melted. I then looked at the grill temp gage and notice it was complete spiked passed the temp of 750 degrees. The control knobs would not work to turn off the gas flow. I then attempted to turn the gas off at the tank. The tank valve was very hot and I was able to turn of the gas flow.

I reported the issue to Uniflame. They told me that the unit was out of the warranty period.
They wanted me to pay almost $100 to replace what they think might be a problem. My concern is since the unit could not have been turned off by the control knobs and the tank was very hot the safety feature should have turn the gas flow off. However since the unit was well over 750 degrees, I'm worried other might not be so lucky.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the grill's failure to shut off gas flow at high temperatures poses a significant risk of injury or property damage in future use.

incident_description: I purchased a Primus Express Lander VF Lightweight Compact Stove and took it out to my picnic table to try it out.  I followed the priming warmup procedures:  I opened the fuel valve a few seconds, closed it, then lit the fuel in the warm up cup.  The fuel ignited as it should but did not warm up the stove sufficiently for it to run propperly.  When I repeated the warm up procedure as instructed, fuel leaked out of a fitting oon the fuel line, ran down the line to my picnic table and when I ignited the fuel it caught my picnic table on fire.  I was trying out the stove in the dark since that is often the conditions under which I would use it so I was unaware of the fuel lleak when I lit the stove.  I do not have the serial number etc. because I returned the stove to the seller.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in property damage (picnic table on fire). The likelihood of this occurring is possible, as the fuel leak was not immediately visible in the dark.

incident_description: Lawn mover cuts off then will not start(intermittant)without a number of tries, final starts sometimes, then sparks. Burned from one of the sparks.
justification: Injury likely due to lawn mower spark, occurrence is possible based on intermittent starting issues.

incident_description: The gas regulator on my Char-Broil "Red Urban Infrared Grill" (Model # 463250210) failed.  When I opened the valve on the propane tank, gas started leaking out very rapidly.  I turned off the tank, disconnected the coupler, re-connected the coupler, and the same thing happened (I was checking to make sure that the coupler was connected properly).  The grill was purchased in June of 2010.  The original regulator (Char-Broil part number G352-3500-W1) was defective straight out of the box (same issue of gas leaking when the tank valve was opened).  Char-Broil sent a replacement part, which has now failed less than 2 years later.  The failure of this part allows propane to leak out very rapidly.  If the grill was on when this happened, there would be a serious risk of fire or an explosion.
justification: Rapid gas leakage could cause a fire or explosion if the grill was on.

incident_description:
I was in the process of cleaning the main burners and noticed that the small brackets that hold the rear end of the main burners in place have severe rust.  In trying to remove the burner, one of the brackets crumbled into flakes.  A second bracket is almost as bad- have not checked the other two. The burner is supposed to be screwed into these brackets.  At this point there no way to secure a screw into these brackets or what is left of them.  Un-noticed, a burner could fall in the back yet still be attached at the valve, leaving at an angle.  This is probably a severe safety hazzard.  I contacted the manufacture who was unconcerned and claimed to not have heard of any rust problems.

Product Info:
Charmglow BBQ Grill (Gas)
Model: 720-0536
Purchased: April 2009
When not in use this grill remains covered.
justification: Rust has weakened brackets, increasing likelihood of a burner falling and causing injury.

incident_description:
the return cycle,  on the control valve,  does not release automatically and continues
to build pressure until manually released.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the potential for damage was high due to the buildup of pressure, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description: On Saturday, Mar 10, 2012, Char-Broil Barbecue Model No. 463268008 knob caught on fire. The plastic knobs are highly flammable and when the knob caught on fire, my husband happened to look over and see it flaming high and melting onto our deck. If he had not seen it immediately, the deck would have likely caught fire and possibly burned the house. We spoke to representatives of Char-Broil who refused to take responsibility even though we told them we would be reporting this issue to the Consumer Product Safety Commission. My husband suggested the problem could be resolved by placing a metal washer on the shaft behind the knob so that the heat or flame cannot get to the plastic knob.  Another solution would be to make the knobs out of metal or some other non-flammable material.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire that could have spread to the house, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' level 2 severity.

incident_description:
I was attempting to fill my walk behind lawn mower, using a partially full Blitz 5CXG 5 gallon gas container. I inserted the filling tube in the mower tank opening, pushed down on the trigger to let gas flow and the pressure in the container shot gasoline onto my face and into my eyes.
After recovering from the incident, I looked at the signage on the container, and did find a sticker that I honestly had never noticed before on the front of the container, facing away from any one using the container, that detailed that you should release the pressure before each use. 
I believe such information should be placed in a more obvious site on the container, for instance on the top by the handle. And I would suggest that it not be a sticker but stamped into the container.
This is obviously a dangerous product the way that it is sold right now. And from the other similar incidents that I have found detailed on this site and elsewhere, I would hope that this company shows some concern and responsibility and at the very least moves the signage to the top of the container where it will be noticed by the user.
justification: Gasoline shot onto face and into eyes, causing potential serious injury.

incident_description: Deteriorated burners on our Perfect Flame model 720-0522 grill similar to other recalled models from the same manufacturer have created a fire and burn hazard.  The flame burns in only certain areas due to the deterioration of the burners creating areas where the grill gets extremely hot.
justification: The deterioration of burners can lead to uneven heat distribution, creating hot spots that pose a fire and burn hazard.

incident_description:
On June 10, 2011 I was trying to remove a Shakepeare Heavy Duty Brush Cutter tool from my weed trimmer to add a washer for proper fit, when one of the 3 blades swiveled and cut my right thumb to the bone. This was my first use of the brush cutter.

I contacted the company and suggested they add cheap plastic blade guards to all 3 blades that could be removed before use. This would be a cheap way to protect consumer fingers and hands while installing or removing the brush cutter. The brush cutter is designed for "no tool" installation and removal but is seriously dangerous to get off the weed trimmer because of the grip and torque needed for removal. The instruction documents provided even show an hand with no gloves trying to remove the cutter from a trimmer.

Jarden Corporation never responded to my suggestion for plastic blade covers but did respond to my demand for damages. Civil litigation is pending.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (cut to the bone) and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the design of the tool and lack of safety measures.

incident_description: Cooking with gas grill JENN-AIR Model 730-0727 using rotisserie attachment.  Grease from chicken feel into drip pan heat from grill ignited the grease which heated wires for igniter's.  The wires melted and shorted out.
justification: Grease ignited and caused a short circuit, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:

incident_description: gasoline drips out of  snow thrower carberator.  It is a Toro model 38282 serial number 311021252.  I have the same problem with miy Toro lawn mower.  I can not put either in the garage for fear of it catching on fire
justification: Gasoline dripping from the snow thrower's carburetor poses a fire risk, especially when stored in an enclosed space like a garage.

incident_description: PerfectFlame Model GAC3615 four burner LP gas grill purchased early 2008 at Lowes. While pre-heating the grill on outdoor patio, went inside to kitchen for food. Upon return, grill was in flames -- shooting out the side. 'melted' the interior coating and weakened all internal parts in the cook box. Was able to turn off grill by knobs and fire went out on its own. Originally assumed I overheated it during the pre-heat cycle and abandoned grill use for a while. In trying to find replacement parts today discovered the grill KX 021139 serial number was part of a huge recall -- found info on cpsc.gov. Have never even used the side cook area. Afraid to do so now. Have stopped using it and will try to get refund from Lowes. Thanks.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire, causing substantial damage to the grill.

incident_description:
Though it otherwise functions normally, my Toro CCR 2450 Snowthrower leaks gasoline while at rest.  The manufacturer, Toro, refused to offer any assistance other than to say, the obvious, "take it to a repair shop".  

I wouldn't recommend placing a device leaking gasoline into an enclosed space such as an automobile as Toro did with me.
justification: Though no immediate injury is reported, the potential for fire or explosion exists if the gasoline leaks into an enclosed space like a car.

incident_description: gas leaks from the carburetor after the engine is shut off posing a fire or explosion hazard..
justification: Gas leaks from the carburetor after engine shutoff pose a potential fire hazard, but no injuries are typically expected.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a very serious safety issue with my JOHN DEERE model 125 lawn tractor. I purchased my tractor on April 3,2006 ( id# GX0125A012933 ).
 After only 55 hours of service, I sent it to my dealer for regular maintenance service ( 11/08/2011). Among the many problems found, they discovered that the GAS TANK WAS LEAKING AT THE SEAM AND LEAKING FUEL ONTO THE MOWER DECK ( copy of report available ).I was informed that this problem was not covered by the warranty.
I did not have the repair done because I thought they were mistaken because I had just washed the unit and I believed it was just water. I checked it a few weeks later, and smelled a strong odor of gasoline and a POOL OF FUEL ON THE MOWER DECK. Because the tractor is stored in my garage, which is under my home, this is an EXTREMELY DANGEROUS CONDITION.
I have written to John Deere, but at this time, I have not heard anything.
If you need any further information, I can be reached at [REDACTED].
justification: Fuel leak onto mower deck in a garage, under a residence, poses a high likelihood of fire or explosion.

incident_description: I have had this Trimmer for approx 18 months and just after the warranty ran out the fuel hoses that go into the gas tank disintegrated and caused a fuel leak. I replaced the tank assembly and in less than six months later the same thing happened. When I noticed the fuel leaking after filling the tank I poured the fuel back into my gasoline container and the hoses were so disintegrated the fuel filter inside fell out of the tank. When I called Homelite they advised me it was due to using gas with ethanol and there was nothing they could do for me. This inferior hose being used by Homelite is a fire hazard, I was lucky I noticed the leak before starting the unit or the might have been a fire. There are very few gas stations that do not have ethanol in their fuels.
justification: Fuel hoses disintegrated twice in less than 18 months, posing a fire risk.

incident_description:
I purchased a Toro Power Clear 180 snowblower on 1/4/10.  I notified Toro on 2/21/10 and again on 3/14/10 to tell them that I could smell a gasoline leak from my snowblower (their case numbers are [REDACTED] respectively).  In addition to the smell, I was very concerned about the fire hazard because I keep my snowblower in an attached garage directly beneath the bedroom area of my house.
While I was on vacation in February 2010 a major leak developed and all the gasoline in the snowblower's fuel tank leaked out.  If there had been any kind of spark, it would have set my house on fire.
I finally received a letter from Toro in July 2010 telling me that Toro was "voluntarily" recalling my snowblower in cooperation with the CPSC.  I took my snowblower to an authorized dealer and had the recommended repairs made.  The dealer told me that they changed the carburetor needle valve.
On 2/23/11 I awoke to the  strong smell of gasoline fumes in my house.  The Toro snowblower had leaked again and flooded my garage with gasoline!
I took the snowblower back to the dealer who made the initial repairs.  I am awaiting his recommendation.
I feel strongly that this snowblower presents a major fire hazard and should be replaced or fixed properly by Toro.  Simply changing the carburetor needle valve is not a sufficient repair.
Others may be unaware of this problem and be exposed to a major fire hazard.
justification: The incident has already occurred twice, with a significant potential for property damage and injury.

incident_description: Purchased a Sear Craftsman Riding Lawn Mower and from the first day the rear bagger kept coming off.  My son who is an engineer claimed it was a lemon as he looked at it and said it was unsafe due to the clips that were holding up a heavy rear bagger.  My son-in-law fell off of it when the rar bagger got loose and myelf, it was unstable and again, the rear bagger kept coming off.  We only used it four time and it has only 7 miles on it.  We purchased this item in March, 2011 and we have been arguing with Sears to get a refund for this lemon and unsafe product. They sent their technican and he did not even know anything about rear baggers.  It is a joke with this folks come out.  I have been a homeowner for over 40 years and had a [REDACTED] and never had a problem.  Decided to try this one, and it was a lemon from day one and a failure.  They did send me clips and after our son reviewed them, he would not place them on the rear bagger due to it being now a defectie riding lawn mower.  We sent them back to them.  They will never admit to the faults of this mower.  All I want is my money back and as a business they should honor their policies of satifaction to the customer.  They have an outlet store and I at first purchased a used one and ralized after completing my research, that it was defective and the rear bagger was torn.  I requested my money back and they did not honro.  they have many items at their Outlet stores from customers who have returned items.  So Sears needs to stop lying about good customer service and return my mones now.  I will never use this mower because it is dangerous to me and my son-in-law.  that is why Sears is failing because they have never provided great customer satisfaction and given out excellent products to their customers.  Kindly contact them and see what kind of story they will give out as they usually have their specialist who are not llicensed engineers or have no backgrou9nd in the design and engineering factors of the mower.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (son-in-law fell off) due to the unstable and unsafe condition of the mower caused by the rear bagger coming loose.

incident_description: Toro Power Clear 180 Snowthrower Model 38272, S/N 311006471 purchased 1-15-1011. Walked into garage 2-25-2012 mid afternoon & smelled gasoline. Found a 3 foot diameter puddle of gas under the carburetor area and fuel dripping on the floor at a good rate.
justification: Fuel leak could lead to fire or explosion, posing a significant risk.

incident_description: I purchased a box of 2 Hudson Eliminator garden sprayers 1 gallon from Mendards in Indiana. Both of the sprayers burst on the side after I filled them with a liquid both were less then a yer old
justification: Both sprayers burst, causing no injury but leading to property damage.

incident_description: I purchased a new Toro Ultra Blower, Model 51599, Serial # 311384699.   I was having trouble getting it to stay on, as the connection to the internal plug was making poor contact.  The second time I used it, the blower stopped, started to smolder and smoke started coming out of the plug, with the plug showing signs that it was beginning to melt.  This item was made in Mexico it says on the piece.  Obviously it was not put together properly and poses both a fire hazard as well as a danger to the user.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (smoldering, melting plug) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the poor assembly and electrical issue.

incident_description:
The summer of 2011 the caller was cutting his lawn with his compact tractor when he turned the wheel and it would turn but if he turned it over and over it would move a bit.

This has happened since the summer of 2011 for approximately 50 times with each incident lasting possibly 5 minutes before it begins working properly again.

Caller states that he hydraulic cylinder seal on piston does not seal, it is bypassing.
This seal was revised with tractors manufactured around 2006

Caller would like his tractor successfully repaired at manufacturer expense or at least have the cylinder provided for him to install at manufacturer expense.
He states that steering going out is a sever safety issue and that it needs to be recalled before someone is seriously injured.
justification: Though no injuries have been reported, the recurring steering issue poses a high likelihood of causing an incident with potential injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer says when he bought the unit, he opened it up and started using it.  He turned it to the side and noticed gasoline was all over his hands and on the chain saw.  The gas cap was not tightening up.  He contacted the retailer who would send him a replacement gas cap.  He received the new cap that was working fine.  This occurred in August 2009.  He says he was going to use the chain saw this weekend.  He noticed that the gas cap is not tightening up again.  He says it seems to be expanding.  He contacted the retailer again who told him they have not heard of any problems.  The consumer feels that the retailer was well aware of this problem when he brought it to their attention in 2009.  


UPDATE: 

Consumer called Sears Parts and was told he would have to buy a new cap since this was out of the 90 day warranty.  He bought new one at $12 plus change. 2/6/12  
New gas cap has been modified from original one and replacement cap sent in 2009.  New cap has 1/8" or more lip on bottom of cap that makes it fight tight
justification: Although no injury has been reported, the recurring issue with the gas cap poses a potential fire hazard, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
My Weber gas grill caught fire and burned both it and the surrounding area.  The fire occurred after I used it.  I then turned off the three valves but a few minutes later a fire occurred in the venturii tubes.  It burned up the side of the grill plus burned surrounding items and part of a tree trunk.  We put it out with a garden hose.  

The grill was relatively new and was purchased in assembled condition.
justification: The grill fire caused property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible for such incidents to occur, it's not likely given the grill's new condition.

incident_description:
Greetings:

About two weeks ago my Black and Decker Leaf Hog leaf blower/mulcher caught on fire while I was using it. The rear area of the motor was in flames and the plastic housing partially melted. I was not harmed and there was no property damage. There is nothing wrong with the electrical system in my home, as I have used other outdoor appliances and equipment before and after this incident.

incident_description:
I purchased a new Weber model S310 gas grill and assembled it per the included instructions. During the first several uses I would find that the burner control knobs would come on while doing other tasks. Example grilling for two people and only turning on and starting just one burner and while cooking I would find that one or both of the other burners on and not lit. Also I would find the burner control knobs on while installing or removing the weather protective cover.
I now have to double and triple check that the burner control knobs are turned off whenever I am doing any tasks on or around the grill and make sure that the propane is turned off and stays that way until it is to be used and continue checking them while it is in use.
I called Weber Customer Service and was told that there is nothing wrong with the shutoff mechanisims.  
I also went to several stores that sell Weber Gas Grills and looked at 50 different 310 Grills and found that 40 of them operated the same as mine and the burner control knobs would not lock in the off position, but the other 10 would lock and there would be no inadverent unlocking of them.
When checking other models of Weber grills I found that they do have very positive locking of their burner controls and there is no inadvertant unlocking possible.
So I find that this style of grill is inherently UNSAFE and the potential for an explosion and or fire is very high. I beleive that the the burner control mechanisims should be recalled and replaced, before someone is injured.
justification: The grill's burner control knobs can turn on unintentionally, posing a high likelihood of an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
On June 4th, 2011, my wife and I purchased a Ryobi self propelled cordless electric lawn mower from HomeDepot.com. The lawn mower had received great reviews on the website up until that point and we were interested in a more ÃÂgreenÃÂ option than a traditional gas mower. The mower was functional and we were satisfied with our purchase until August 2011.

One afternoon in August, I smelled a chemical smell in the garage. I investigated the smell and figured out it was coming from the lawn mower. The battery was hot, all of its lights were on, and it was covered in a clear fluid that we later determined to be battery acid. After unplugging the mower and waiting until the next morning, my wife called the customer service department at Ryobi. They stated that there had been a problem with the battery chargers and a new charger had been remanufactured. They assured us that a replacement battery and battery charger would be delivered within 3 weeks. 

Fast forward to January 2012, we have not received anything from Ryobi. 

Last night I decided to take a look at homedepot.com to see if any other customers had a similar problem. When I looked up the lawn mower, there were at least 20 other customers with the EXACT same story as us. Battery overcharged, leaked battery acid, called Ryobi, were assured theyÃÂd get a replacement, and no battery was ever replaced. Clearly RyobiÃÂs product is defective.  

In summary, weÃÂve lost almost $400 on a mower that doesnÃÂt work, and quite possibly is a fire hazard. The battery acid leaked onto our garage floor, which was a safety hazard for me, my pets, and the environment. 

Even with the slew of negative reviews on HomeDepot.com, the store continues to sell the product. What is most questionable is that both my wife and I attempted to leave poor product reviews on the HomeDepot.com site, and they rejected both of our reviews because we included the fact that Ryobi had been terrible to deal with. If they rejected our reviews, how many other customers have had this same issue but could not be heard because HomeDepot.com is rejecting reviews from unsatisfied customers, thus keeping the rating for the product high? In addition, RyobiÃÂs issued no recalls and thereÃÂs A LOT of people left with broken lawnmowers and tons of frustration. How much longer will they sell the product before someone is injured?
justification: Multiple customers experienced the same battery overcharging issue, leading to battery acid leaks and potential fire hazards.

incident_description: In the spring of 2011, I purchased a Ryobi walk behind battery operated electric lawn mower from Home DepotÃÂs online store. After using it to maintain my lawn during the summer, I placed the mower into storage and moved the battery pack to my basement to keep it in a temperature stable environment for the winter. On the afternoon of Jan 29, 2012, I brought the battery from my basement to the garage in order to charge it in an effort to maintain the battery packÃÂs life. The charging was performed by the original charger that came with the mower and has worked normally in the past. On the morning of Jan 31, I awoke to the smell of what I believe was hydrogen sulfide gas in the house. After a quick search, I discovered the red charge light was still illuminated on the battery charger and battery pack was the source of the gas. After beginning ventilation of the house, I carried the battery pack outdoors and noticed it leaking acid. The battery charger had been connected for approximately 40 hours and during this time, failed to automatically shut off as it is designed to do when the battery had fully charged. The failure of the charger to discontinue operation at the appropriate charge level created a highly dangerous situation which could have resulted in fire, explosion, or the poisoning of my family had I not found and removed the device. I believe a properly designed and manufactured charger would not have failed in this fashion and created such a dangerous situation.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a hazardous gas leak and potential fire/explosion risk, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
This is in regard to a Bradley BTIS1 Original Fully Automatic 4-Rack Outdoor Food Smoker 

Nearly caught my house on fire with this product, and please do note I am not alone, especially lately - check out the customer photos, reviews and their dates on the Amazon.com website: http://www.amazon.com/Bradley-BTIS1-Original-Automatic-Smoker/dp/B000FK2DNM/ref=cm_cr-mr-title

 Either this product is too difficult to use safely for most consumers, or I had a defective unit. I really believe it was the latter, but if it's the former, you're going to have a hard time keeping this product clean enough to be safe.

I bought this smoker in July (five months ago) and used the product according to directions. On the fifth use, it inexplicably overheated, melting the door seal. There was no fire that time.  I contacted Bradley.  Bradley sent out a replacement door seal, saying that the only way this can happen is if you improperly keep the vent closed, but they'd help me this time. I hadn't kept the vent closed, and said I was concerned it was a defective unit and a fire hazard. They continued to assert it must have been a closed vent. I crossed my fingers I had just not noticed my error.

It took me nearly 2 hours to replace the door seal, a dirty job that made me swear to myself I'd maintain the smoker perfectly so there would be no potential of user error going forward. Every single time I removed every single removable part and steel wool clean it. I wiped down the sides each time, and removed any obvious grease.

On about the fifth use after replacement of the door seal, my wife looked out the window just in time - the whole thing was ON FIRE. I unplugged it, doused the fire with water, and finished the turkey breast (not a greasy pork roast mind you, a turkey breast) in the oven.

I called up Bradley immediately, assuming the fire was proof I had a defective unit that would be quickly replaced. I figure, hey, they had a record of the first incident, so it shouldn't be much of a fuss. Ahem - no.  It would have to be reviewed.  I was asked to send in photos of the charred remains of the smoker.

After a week of chasing, I finally got to talk to [REDACTED], who is in charge of "fire incidents." I explained the situation, the previous problem, my exact experience and use of it, and he somehow determined, based only on AFTER photos of the charred remains of the unit that had been doused with water, that it was because of user error - that I hadn't cleaned the smoker thoroughly enough, and too much grease is why it caught fire. Then he offered me a "deep discount" that he didn't actually reveal.

I tried to engage him in simple logic. If you're saying this unit, that has caught fire, is NOT DEFECTIVE, and I'm saying that I've used this as responsibly as possible, what you are saying is either A) I am lying to you about how I maintained the product or B) that this product carries a very reasonable risk of a fire starting through normal customer use.

[REDACTED] didn't really want to say "A" but he essentially did when he refused to acknowledge the possibility of a defective unit. He said the chances of a defect were "slim to zero," explaining to me about how the components are each inspected before assembly. When I raised the possibility that it had been improperly assembled or perhaps my unit was otherwise defective, and offered to provide the unit to him somehow, he said there was no reason to do so. When I noted that I noticed others on Amazon were also having this issue, he literally laughed and said every product on Amazon has negative reviews from a few people.

This was pretty insulting given the time that I had invested in contacting the company to avoid a repeat of the overheating incident, and my earnest belief that I had used this product right and it was a defective unit. But at that point I realized that any company that would rather call a customer a liar than acknowledge the possibility that it could make a manufacturing error, was not worth a minute more of my time - other than helping assure other people aren't in my exact situation.

I wish I had taken others' warnings seriously on the Amazon website and not written them off as being posted by careless people who didn't bother taking care of the unit properly.

Consumers need to know that this product has the potential to catch fire, even if used very responsibly - and even if you are as careful as I was. I'm not some random Internet troll or someone in desperate need of a refund - I'm a regular suburban father who wouldn't bother submitting this if it were merely a product that stopped working.   This is about starting fires.
justification: The incident resulted in a house fire, but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of occurrence is high given the repeated incidents and user's careful maintenance.

What do I do? Prior to bringing the unit into the repair shop the last time I wrote to Toro expressing my dissatisfaction, not with the overall performance but the constant leaking gas and the failur of the repair parts to do the trick. I even provided them the name of the repair shop.  They wrote back  via e-mail dated July 23, 2011, giving me case # [REDACTED], stating I had to work with the repair shop. In April, 2010 I had received a recall notice from Toro about this problem.  Well, they don't know how to fix it and I'm at the end of my patience. I fear for the safety of my wife and me, wondering when will a spark ignite the leaking gas while in the garage or as I'm operating it. 

Help, I've got a lemon of a snow thrower and the snow season is upon us.

[REDACTED]
justification: The recurring gas leak poses a high risk of injury due to potential ignition by a spark.

incident_description:
This involves the Thomas the Tank Engine Flashlight with siren whistle and morse code button.
The flashlight stopped working, and we assumed the batteries had run down.

 A few minutes later, my son cried out. He'd picked up the flashlight again, and it had grown extremely hot. I touched it quickly and nearly got burnt. 

It was definitly hot enough to be very dangerous to anyone, let alone a small child.
justification: The flashlight overheating to a dangerous temperature, posing a high risk of injury, especially to a child.

incident_description:
Consumer sated that while working on the snow blower for a customer, the plastic composite rim exploded while he was putting air in the tire.  This incident caused him to receive severe injuries to his right hand.

Consumer was taken to the hospital (Winchester Urgent care) Wilmington Ma. by a coworker, he received 6 stitches in three of fingers on his right hand, his right thumb was fractured and had lacerations to his knuckle and fingers.  He received treatment and was released, but had to return twice for medical care due to infection.

Consumer is concerned that this product is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries, including stitches and a fractured thumb, but no death, making it a level 3 severity. The likelihood is 'possible' given the consumer's account and the nature of the product.

incident_description: while preparing to grill some steaks, I started my "perfect flame" grill, model # SLG2008A. while waiting for grill to reach cooking temp (350*), grill started blazing out of control. I could not reach the bottle to turn the gas off, so I grabbed my water hose and doused the flames enough so I could reach the gas knob without getting burned, and turned the gas off. I still had to douse the grill with the water hose to extinguish the fire. The fire burned all the paint off the grill and burned the gas hose in half. It also burned the flame covers above the burners. If I had not been close when this happened, my whole house could have burned to the ground since the grill was under my covered porch.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity. The likelihood is rated 3 as it could have escalated to a catastrophic event if not promptly addressed.

incident_description:
I was preparing to start my snowthrower, and I noticed gasoline leaking out all over my garage floor.  To avoid a fire in my garage, I immediately pulled the machine out to the driveway.  Upon inspection, I noticed that the plastic fuel tank is cracked.  This creates a potential for fire and injury.

The fuel tank is fused/molded to the plastic shroud that covers the top of the machine.  A crack developed where the tank & shroud meet.  This appears to be a common probelm, as Toro recognized this hazard and issued a recall (release #06-224, 8/3/2006).  However, the recall only appled to their 20" & 24" snowthrowers.  The model I have is a 16" size, but the fuel tank/shroud design is very similar to the recalled models.  I'm not sure why the smaller size was not included in the recall as it also appears to have the same defect.
justification: Potential for injury due to cracked fuel tank, as evidenced by similar recalled models.

incident_description: The consumer says the unit stopped working.  He says it was on for about 4 hours before the incident.  Upon inspection he discovered the connector to the heating element was burned in two.  The consumer says he noticed melted plastic and uninsulated wire that could come in contact with metal posing a fire or shock hazard.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who was very unhelpful and said it was not replaceable.  They told him it is no longer being made.  The consumer says that it is not the element but the wiring and connector to the element that is bad.  The consumer says that if he didn't open it up, he wouldn't have noticed it.  He says that is the real danger. The unit was used approximately 12 times before the failure.
justification: The incident involved a fire or shock hazard due to exposed wiring, posing a high likelihood of injury if not discovered.

incident_description:
I have already filed a case [REDACTED]

We bought a Sears grill in 2009 my husband was using it and the grill knob melted off and flames shot from it. Sears responded to my complaint by giving me a number to call. I have already done that. They said they could send a tech out to look at it but it was going to cost over 100$ after talking with many managers they sent one out for free. Upon arrival the tech said he has seen this problem many times. He said because the knobs aren't enclosed on the inside well spiders get in it and build a web. Then when you turn it on all the stuff in the web catches on fire melts the knob and fire shoots from the hole. We are lucky my husband wasn't standing directly in front of the grill but off to the side or he would have been badly burned. Again we have the fire shooting out on video. 

Sears is aware of this problem. They do not have the interior of their knobs closed off well allowing spiders and bugs to build nests that are flamable.  It is apparently a common problem with this grill. They have done nothing to fix it nor have they done anything to warn people of this potential hazard!
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to a design flaw in the grill, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: I turned on my Brinkmann 9 LED Spotlight (Item 809-1201-S) and it was blinking and going out a lot so I open it up and tried to pull out the battery compartment but I burnt my hand from the heat of the shorting out parts and dropped the compartment.  I was able to reach down and find it in the dark but it was still quite hot and you could smell the burnt plastic.  I later took it inside but the stench of the melted plastic was so nauseating after 10 minutes that I had to put it in the garage.  I find it a bit difficult to believe that such a sever short could not occur without there being a design flaw in this spotlight. I also notice that a previous set of new batteries had die with only minutes of use the night before.  I now suspect the same short may have cause this to happen as well only more slowly but I can not be certain.  However, it's completely clear that so much heat could not have been created in mere seconds (about half a minute) without a sever arching occurring within the spotlight.
justification: Injury occurred due to severe short-circuiting, and the likelihood of such an event is high given the repeated battery issues.

incident_description:
Brand- Streamlight
Make- Strion
Serial number- 253603

My daughter took the above flashlight with her when she took a nap on 12/4/2011.  Shortly after falling asleep, she woke up because the flashlight caused first and second degree burns on her left hand and left arm. Her dad realized after comforting her that it was the flashlight that caused the burns.  He tried handling the flashlight to turn it off, but was not able to do so without using a blanket as the flashlight was too hot to touch without burning him.  

A call has been placed to Streamlight,  but have not had a response as of this morning at 9:25am central time zone.
justification: The flashlight caused second-degree burns, indicating severity level 3, and the likelihood is high given the direct contact and heat generated.

incident_description:
Yesterday my 10-year son was blowing up balloons in the house with the Pumponator.  He was sitting down, holding the base of the Pumponator against his thigh as he pumped it up.  It exploded suddenly, with an incredibly loud bang (I thought a cabinet or bookshelf had somehow been knocked over.)  It sent shards of plastic through the room.  One shard hit his thigh and cut his skin through his fleece pants, and the force of the explosion left a huge bruise on his thigh.  

The label on the product said it was not for use by kids under 8 (my son is 10).  It does not say anything on the label about over-pressurization and the possibility of the plastic bottle exploding suddenly.  It does not say how many times the pump should be depressed, or give any warnings about too much pressure. The toy is not that old (about 15 months old), and was not left outside or in the sun (which could have caused the plastic to degrade and weaken.)
justification: The toy's sudden explosion caused a cut on the child's thigh, resulting in injury.

incident_description:
Craftsman Riding Lawnmower caught fire 10/24/2011 while caller's husband was riding on it and cutting grass.

Caller smelled burning, got off of lawnmower, opened hood and saw flames about a foot to a foot & a half high, grabbed hose and sprayed to extinguish.

Fire was confined under the hood.

Caller does not know DOM.

Some melting of plastic around the engine area.

Caller would request repair at manufacturer expense.
justification: Fire was contained and no injuries were reported, but the incident could have escalated.

incident_description:
Caller purchased 18" snow blower November 2010 but did not use until January 2010 then after use placed it in his garage for storage until next use.

He took it back out of garage in February 2011 because there was a heavy smell of gasoline and noticed that the gas was leaking out of the new snow blower just underneath the carburator.

He took to Toro Master Service Center in [REDACTED] in March 2011 but they declined repair stating that they do not service snow blowers in March & advised him to bring it back during the September/October time frame.

Caller took the snow blower back to the service center around the 11th of October 2011, received a call today October 20th, 2011 iinforming him that the carburator was corroded and needed to be replaced.

Caller would like public to be made aware of the danger with this snow blower and would like for the repair to be at manufacturer expense due to the problem being the same problem as with recalled snow throwers in release# 10-299..
justification: Potential injury due to gasoline leak, though no incident reported yet.

incident_description: plastic fuel tank on Craftsman riding lawn  mower has six cracks leaking fuel
justification: Cracks in fuel tank pose a fire risk, but no immediate injury or death reported.

incident_description:
Purchased a Club Cadet RZT 42 on 9/3/2011.  When I got home with the machine, while unloading it from the trailor, and at an incline, the machine began smoking profusely and continued to do so for a little while after it was unloaded.  It also began to sputter(want to kill).  The first time I used it to mow the lawn, it would begin to smoke and want to kill whenever cutting on any slight incline.  I used it twice to mow my lawn and had the same problem both times.  33 days after purchasing this machine, I contacted a service center for Club Cadet.  Lemann's Farm Supply in Donaldsonville, LA  kept the machine for 3 weeks, trying to repair the faulty parts manufactured by Club Cadet/Kohler. This is what the repair report states: Tech found the motor was lacking power and using oil. Tech found the head gasket was leaking compression and there was oil coming in from the breather. Tech replaced the head gasket.  He also found the reed valve was bent.  Tech replaced the reed valve.  When tech pulled the spark plug wire from the spark plug, he found the wire in the ignition module was broken. The module was replaced.  The mower was then returned to me.  The next day while mowing the lawn, the machine started to run rough and sputter, during which the extreme back pressure caused the dipstick/top to fly off of the engine about 4 ft away, causing oil to spew all over the mower and me.  This happened twice and I had to stop. I brought the mower back to Lemann's for further examination/repair.  The following are the service notes for the second repair visit:  Tech contacted Cub Cadet Technician and was advised to follow instructions on service bulletin #309 ? Tech removed the PTO, drive pulley, engine and oil pan, as per bulletin.  Tech installed breather kit.  Tech re-installed oil pan, engine, drive pulley and PTO.  Tech operated mower at an incline and the mower performed normal.  After getting the machine back the second time, I had trouble starting the machine and a tech came to adjust the choke. 
During my visit to Lemann's, I noticed many Club Cadet mowers in for repairs.  I believe Cub Cadet/Kohler are manufacturing sub standard equipment and parts, with these machines being sold at large retail stores like Lowe's and Tractor Supply, etc., and which are dangerous to the consumer and of poor quality.  I have found this with [REDACTED]mowers also.  I did contact Club Cadet yesterday, 11/29/2011( Ref # [REDACTED]) with my complaints and requested my money back for this mower, which is obviously a lemon. They informed me that they cannot refund my money.  After research, I found out that there are no lemon laws in place for lawn mowers.  I also found that Cub Cadet lists service providers according to where the machine was purchased.  If purchased from a Cub Cadet dealer, then they will service the machine.  If the machine was purchased from Lowe's or Tractor Supply Co, then the service providers were individuals with small businesses. Never have i been so disappointed in a product.
justification: Multiple incidents of oil spewing and engine failure, with potential for injury.

incident_description:
While trying to use the  walk behind snow blower near a side garage door of his drive way in reverse it lunged knocking him to fall off of it and got him pinned by the levers . He could not get near the safety levers to enable the blower from moving. 

He had to roll on the ground in order to free himself and prevent getting caught by the blades.

He was able to free himself from being cut by the blades by getting a hold of the handle t  the snow blower.

He received bruising to his left hand and took himself to Montevideo Hospital in Montevideo MN where x rays were taken and various test were ran. 

He was also released with instructions to follow up with his Primary Care Physician. His follow up appointment was on 11/25/2011 where his doctor advised him to not to return to work and limit the use of his left hand.


He has not contacted the retailer or firm but plans to do so.  The snow blower has not  been used since the incident occurred and was not damaged.
justification: Injury occurred due to the snow blower's unexpected movement, which could have been prevented with better safety features or user training.

incident_description:
I bought a Toro Model #38585 Serial #280002680 in 2008.  It worked fine over the 2008-2009 winter.  The following year, (2009-2010) I try to start it and find it leaks gas out of the carburetor; so I take it apart and find one end of the float spring has been pinched between the bowl gasket and its mating surface; it was an easy fix and took care of the leak.

For the 2010-2011 winter I had a similar gas leak from somewhere in the carburetor.  I bought a rebuild kit, installed it and that took care of the the leak last year.  Now its the winter of 2011-2012 and I find that the carburetor is leaking all over again.  What gives?  Toro has recalled many models that are the same as mine, except newer.  I bought a 421Q from the first two years when Toro was buying Snow King engines from Tecumseh.  Tecumseh is apparently no longer in business.

Is there a recall on my snowblower?  Have others had sll the same carburetor leaking that I have had to deal with?
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the recurring gas leaks from the carburetor pose a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description: The inside of the grill lid melted, caused a small fire inside the grill. The grill is now useless as the melted lining dripped throughout the grill.  The fumes made us nauseous.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while grill fires can occur, they are not common.

incident_description:
I was using my Ridgid 2 in one shop vac and the blower wheel detatched from the housing made a loud noise sparked, and chards of metal flew out through the exhaust and it felt like pin needles, super small splinter sice metal peices stuck in my hand, I did get them out ok but ouch. This also scared the heck out of me. I went on the Web to see what it could be and found the below recall on this exact unit however with a lower seriel number. I have Seriel number 08042   R 2594.   Model WD16650 I feel this should be expanded to include the machines with my seriel number range as its the same issue. 

The recalled units have the model number and a serial number from 04104C through 04114C
