incident_description:
I have purchased a Poulan Pro model PP4218AV chainsaw.  After some use, the gas cap is extremely difficult to screw in or out, in fact, I need to use pliers to do it.  I called Poulan/Husqvarna customer service, and was told that the problem is that the ethanol used in gasoline causes the plastic screw threads to expand, thus creating the issue with the cap.

Their solution is to "put the cap in the sun, or other heat source, such as a light bulb, to dry out the cap", thus shrinking the threads so that they will work.  Presumably, a consumer will have to do this frequently, as the problem is only temporarily fixed.  

I personally believe their response is unbelievably poor, as it does not solve the problem.  But more importantly, I can envision some consumer applying a heat source that should not be used near gasoline, such a a lighter or blow torch to dry the cap.  Obviously, this could be a catastrophic event for the person.
justification: Consumer may use inappropriate heat sources like a lighter or blowtorch to fix the cap, leading to potential burns or fire.

incident_description: Turned on gas cooktop and experienced an explosion that blew off the controls and burner diffusers
justification: The explosion caused property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
While I was blowing leaves in my backyard, a burning smell began to come from the electric Toro Ultra Blower/Vacuum (fully adjustable speed) that I was using.  I turned the blower knob to the off position, and set it down on our concrete porch.  

As I was going to unplug the cord, the blower burst into flames from the inside top of the motor housing.  I ran to turn on the garden hose and dowse the fire.  It was very difficult to put it out, and thick, black smoke billowed from the blower continuously.  The circuit breaker (GFCI) tripped and shut off the electricity to the unit.  The result can be seen in the pictures that I've emailed previously.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire and smoke, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Sears Craftsman Riding Lawn Mower, front wheels, rims & tires have been replaced 3 times due to disintegration inside caller believes because the middle of rim is plastic & falling apart.

The first time this happened was approximately 3 months after purchase, the second time was sometime this year and then again 2011.  (caller does not have exact dates)

Caller traveled until recently and used this home as a vacation home from January through April then returned North from May through December when a lawn care individual would take care of his yard using his own tools.

75yrs old caller contacted manufacturer the fourth time 10/21/2011 and was told that he must pay this time.  Caller advised that they have been replaced three times, Manufacturer told him that he had to pay this fourth time, caller stated problem is a manufacturers defect, he said that representative of manufacturer agreed with him and provided phone number to contact CPSC advising that he call to report.

Caller is reporting as a severe hazard and would like public to be made aware.

Caller would like to have these tractors recalled and the manufacture replace the tires, rims etc with more durable product before someone is injured severely.
justification: The incident has occurred multiple times, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence, and while no injuries have been reported yet, the disintegrating rims pose a significant risk of causing an incident with potential injuries.

incident_description:
Caller's Cordless Electric Lawnmower would not hold a charge after a short term of ownership, she contacted the manufacturer sometime around August 2011 who sent her a new charger, however lawnmower still would not hold charge.

Caller took to authorized lawnmower repair shop she thinks in late September and was told, then shown by [REDACTED]  who is the only technician that the battery was burned, distorted and had white acid marks showing on it.

Caller said it didn't appear burned to her but appeared to be bulging out and distorted.

Repair technician advised her to leave battery at the shop to be disposed of because it could damage her car.  She agreed & left it there.

Repair tech speculation was that the first charger that came with purchase of the lawnmower could have been faulty, caused an overload and caused the battery to become burned.

Caller contacted manufacturer today, November 7. 2011.    [REDACTED]  has escalated within their company.

They advised her to provide the pictures in her possession of the burnt battery.

Caller reporting lawnmower to alert the public.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a potentially hazardous battery that could have caused harm if not properly disposed of.

incident_description: I purchased a Black and Decker Grass Hog XP trimmer a few years ago. The trimmer hasn't worked properly this summer, the string is let out too soon and jams the machine. I noticed on their site some of there trimmers were on recall because the cap would fly off and become a projectile. My trimmer was not on recall. I wrote Black and Decker and they sent me a new automatic feed part and new spools of string because they said I might be using the wrong string or restringing it improperly. After installing the part according to their directions, and installing a new spool, the string  was release too soon and parts of the strings became the projectiles. Within two minutes all the string was gone.  I was struck and bruised in my arm through a light coat. I was also struck in the leg and foot, which stung immensely, even though wearing heavy pants and shoes.  I contacted Black and Decker again about how dangerous this machine had become and what would happen if one of these projectile hit someone in the face? They said they had tried a solution and there was nothing they could do. I feel after spending $80 for this trimmer it had become a very dangerous machine and they had some responsibility here. I will not use this again or let anybody use it. It is not a safe product, and I am out an expensive trimmer.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries, including bruising and stinging, despite the user wearing protective clothing.

incident_description: carburetor leaks gasoline
justification: Gasoline leaks pose a fire risk, but typically do not cause immediate injuries.

incident_description: Gas from toro 22 in recycler lawn mower model 20071 was leaking from the seam of the back of fuel tank. It was unnoticed until I was trying to start the engine. Fortunately, the gas did not catch fire.
justification: Gas leak could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
In 2003 my nose was broken while transferring my Yardy yard-waste cart to the street for curbside pick-up.  I am uncertain exactly how it happened, but I was rolling it across a relatively flat area of the lawn, perhaps striking a partially exposed tree root or a grass divot.  In any event the Yardy tipped and the edge of the lid struck me squarely across the nose, causing immediate heavy bleeding.  We have subsequently moved and no longer reside at the location of the accident. To my knowledge the unit is still in use at the address where the accident occurred.

My wife took me to the Emergency Room where I was informed I had a 'clean' nose fracture and no setting of the bone would be required; they said it would heal on its own.  I recall the X-ray Tech telling me, "You're not the first one of these that I've seen!"

My nose healed, but I was later informed I now had a deviated septum.  Progressively I found my right nostril closing when I slept on my left side, causing severely restricted airflow thru the right nostril.  It got to the point where I went to an ENT specialist and he performed surgery to correct the deviated septum on 3/29/2011.  It is now early Novemnber of 2011 and I have scheduled another appointment with the specialist, as the right nostril is again causing restricted airflow.  

Prior to the Yardy incident, I never experienced breathing problems through my nose.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken nose and subsequent deviated septum, requiring surgery, despite occurring in a seemingly low-risk activity.

incident_description: The product did not retain its power connection securely during usage, resulting in intermittent arcing (and intermittent operation) due to the loose connection, which lead to a buildup of carbon on one prong of the connection, overheating, and an eventual electrical fire.
justification: The intermittent arcing and overheating indicate a high likelihood of recurrence, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his gas powered tiller is a potential fire hazard as there appears to be a leak where the fuel tank is and fears that the gas leaking into a hot engine may flare up, resulting in a fire hazard. The consumer stated that he has not had any injuries sustained by the product but stated that he did inhale some of the fumes. Luckily, he has not suffered any adverse effects. The consumer stated that the product was on for an unknown amount of time before he noticed the leak.

The consumer called the retailer today for the first time about his difficulties with the product and was informed that there have been no reports or recalls on his product. The retailer offered no additional assistance and referred him to the CPSC. The consumer has yet to call the firm. The consumer stated that the product appears to show no structural damage or charring. 

The consumer stated that the product did not damage anything else in his home. The consumer opted to not call the fire department at the time of the incident. The consumer stated that he had to buy a new fuel cap last summer after it split. Last summer at the time he did notice a slow leak but just opted to replace it. Again, he cannot recall exactly when it started leaking. The consumer would describe the leak as a slow leak.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the potential for a fire hazard due to a fuel leak makes this an incident.

incident_description:
This is a resubmittal of a report I started a few minutes ago as it was accidentally submitted before completion.

We own a Poulan Pro lawn tractor, Model #PPR2042ST, Serial #020702D010378, Mfr. ID #PPR20425TA.  The plastic gas tank on the lawn tractor failed at the horizontal seam, allowing gasoline to leak into the engine compartment.  The seam failure is not visible and can only be detected by the odor of gasoline and watching the gas tank after filling more than half full (allowing the gasoline level to rise above the seam line) and observing the tank to see the gas flow out around the seam.  This is a potential fire hazard; fortunately we noticed the problem and replaced the tank before a dangerous situation occurred.  We do not know how long this problem existed with gas tank before it was detected.  We found recalls on the Poulan Pro gas tanks from the 2000-2001 time period, but these recalls were for gas tanks that cracked, not where the seam failed.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to gas leak, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: after starting and then shutting it off TORO Snowblower model 38282 leaked gas from under carburater. It poured out, emptying the whole tank onto my driveway. Could have easily caught fire but didn't. I found a recall from Toro for it. The TORO dealer sold me the recalled unit unfixed AFTER the recall had been issued. The snowblower is now fixed per the recall.
justification: Gas leak from recalled snowblower could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
The incident relates to a new Weber natural gas grill purchased in the spring of 2011. In the ~20 times that we have used the grill and then put the cover back on (which came with the product), on 3 occasions, we have gone to our driveway/out back on the deck only to smell a strong odor of natural gas. Upon further investigation, we have figured out that the gas on the grill was turned on by the cover.. in other words, the amount of pressure needed to move the control knob to open the gas was so minimal, that replacing the cover over the grill was enough to turn it on. We are so lucky that someone did not walk back there with a cigarette, as we would have significant property damage and worse.. the potential for someone to get very hurt! As a Weber grill owner previously (last one we had for 10 years), not once did this happen on our old model!! That said, I am very sad to share the actual correspondence from Weber (below)... who first claims that they recommend that you shut off the gas after each use (although this warning/recommendation is NOT in the owner's guide), and the secondly, advises me "to be more careful". Very disappointing for a clear safety issue for their product, and one that clearly was not the same on prior models (where the same event did not occur) Actual correspondence with Weber Customer Service provided below : From: [REDACTED] To: support@weberstephen.com Subject: RE: Ticket: [REDACTED] Re: Weber Genesis E-310 - safety hazard Date: Mon, 14 Nov 2011 06:19:54 -0500 You see, this is very interesting to me being as we just replaced our old Weber of 10+ years with this one. On that one, there was more pressure required to turn the gas on with the control knobs, and not once in 10+ years did putting on the cover EVER turn on a knob. Seems to me that you did have a design that was different. In addition, in my previous email, I asked for the page # on the owner's guide that gives this warning. I read through the 20+ warnings and did not come across it. Please advise. Thanks for putting the blame on the consumer, surely not the customer service or concern I would expect from Weber. In an effort to prevent others from putting their life and property in jeopardy, I will be pursuing this with CPSC with fervor. incident_description: I purchased 3 Ozark Trail Mini LED Camp Lanterns at Walmart.  Tonight when the wind picked up we put batteries in the units.  The power never went out and about an hour after placing the batteries we smelled something burning.  My 14 year old said why is the plastic glass part all cloudy. incident_description: When I start my lawn mower it runs for about 5 minutes then gas begins to drip out the mower, dripping from the bottom of the carborator.  I took it to a small engine repair and he replaced the carborator.  I got the lawn mower back and the same thing happened. incident_description:
I purchased an emergency light stick made by Life+Gear at Home Depot.  This product is listed as for ages 3+, but frankly is not safe at any age.  The product is a flash light with a polypropelene end that lights up in one of 3 colors for emergency use, and has a whistle included.  While the overall product is great, when you take the cap off of the whistle, it has a sharp end that would severly injur a child or adult if they slipped with it in their mouth.  As soon as I saw it, I cut the sharp point off, rounded the edges, then gave it to my grandson who is 3 1/2.  The very virst thing he did was uncover the whistle and insert about 2 inches of the device in his mouth!

While the product is very good, the end needs to be rounded before someone is hurt.
justification: The sharp end of the whistle poses a high likelihood of injury, especially given the product's intended use for young children.

incident_description:
I purchase a Kenmore Grill at end of season in 09. I did not use the grill until 2010. It worked well a few times that summer however one day the knob to the far left got extemely hot and melted. I replace. the knob thinking it was something I had done only for it to have happened again this time burning my fingers.

I called Sears and  they offered to send repair with a flat rate of $65.00 just to evaluate the problem. I declined as  I think the design is somehow flawed and it will end up costing me more than I made for the defective unsafe grill
justification: The grill's design flaw caused burns, indicating a high likelihood of reoccurrence.

incident_description: In October of 2010, I purchased an Earthquake model 9070300 chipper/shreader from Tractor Supply in Westfield, Indiana.  After two or three hours of use of shreading leaves, the Briggs & Stratton engine caught fire.  The fire was between the muffler and the chipper housing.  The fire was due to about a handful or two of leafs falling next to the muffler. The fire actually damaged the fuel line or gas tank, gas ended up pouring out the bottom.  I was amazed that there was not an explosion.  I believe the cause of the fire is that the muffler heat shield gets too hot, it gets hot enough to vaporize water.  I believe there is a design flaw with the heat shield that it does not have an insulating gasket between the heat shield and the muffler, as a result the heat shield ends up getting as hot as the muffler does.  The B&S engine diagram does not show any insulating gasket, so the engine was not missing it.  I contacted B&S and they had me fill out a fire report and about a month later they basically told me they were not at fault, to contact my insurance company for the loss, and that I was at fault due to not cleaning the chipper after eight hours of use, which is a dumb statement for them to make since I repeatily informed them that the unit was only used for two to three hours.  I complained to Tractor Supply and they ended up swapping my fire damaged unit for a new one, in which I have modified, I put a screen shield a few inches above the heat shield to prevent any leafs from touching the heat shield.  The leaf feeder opening is directly above the heat shield.  I just recently learned of this website which is why I am reporting this so late, with my leafs falling off my trees it reminded me of the issue.  I feel that I am lucky that my wife and I did not end up being burned or killed from an exploding gas tank and noticed that this model of chipper/shreader is still being sold.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a fire and potential explosion, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Our condo association purchased 14 LP Gas barbecue grills for our complex.  I used two of them for the first time on Saturday, October 29, 2011.  The grills are put out by Modern Home Products (MPH) and the model of the grill is WNK4.  These grills can heat to an internal temperature of close to 500 degrees.  The handle to these covers is metal without any insolation of any type on it and it is attached directly to the cover so the heat of the cover is transferred to the handle and when you go to lift the handle, you burn your hand as I did that night.
justification: The grill's metal handle, directly attached to the hot cover, caused a burn injury, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
The LA Water Board is forwarding a complaint we recieved.  The complaint is as follows: "I'm writing this letter to express my concerns arising out of a consumer complaint lodged with a company doing business in California. The company Alpine Corporation of 4901 Zambrano St., Commerce, CA 90040, markets a product that was advertised as safe for aquatic life (?fish safe?) but was so highly toxic that in the course of less than 12 hours it killed all the fish in a 10,000 gallon pond after a short (10 min) exposure. 

My repeated attempts to deal with the company on this matter have been ignored and I must conclude that they have taken no steps to protect either the public or the environment from this toxic material. It is clear to protect the public and the environment this material should have been immediately withdrawn from the market and recalled but no such action was taken. I believe this material continues to pose a threat to the environment until it is recalled and safely and properly disposed of.
As such I wish to lodge a formal complaint with your department in the hopes that you are able to conduct an investigation and determine and Alpine Corporation is not currently selling, distributing or warehousing materials that may be harmful to the environment, aquatic life and people.

The product in question is a blue polyvinyl chloride lay flat hose (2 inch diameter) for use in low-pressure applications such as pumping water from a water garden or quite upon. I purchased the hose for use in the annual cleaning and water change of the 10,000 gallon Koi pond. Upon removing the hose from the packaging I noticed a faint plastic smell which became considerably stronger with exposure to the atmosphere. The chemical order became so strong that after 10 to 15 minutes of use I remove the hose from the pond and discontinued its use. Approximately 8 to 10 feet of the 50 foot hose was submerged in the pond for less than 15 minutes. The water in the pond at the time of the exposure was reduced to approximately 100 gallons and was diluted with approximately 10,000 gallons of additional fresh water. 
By the 12 hour point all of the fish in the pond had died. The pond contained 17 large mature Koi fish and several frogs that had been through several previous water changes of this type without a single loss. 

More than 12 hours after unwrapping the product the chemical smell the hose emitted was very pungent and could be smelled from over 30 feet away. Even with the hose wrapped tightly inside two Hefty garbage bags the odor emitted by the hose was strong enough to induce nausea and caused our German Shepherd to vomit repeatedly. When returned to the pond store the hose was tested by submerging them in a large tank containing healthy fish resulting in the death of all of those fish as well.

Although I only handled the hose for a short period of time my hands became numb and tingly and remained so for the next few days these symptoms persisted for several days after exposure.
In the aftermath of this event and made inquiries to determine the producer of the product and was given the name of Alpine Corporation. I then contacted [REDACTED]  president of Alpine Corporation via e-mail to make you aware of my concerns with the safety of his product. After receiving no response from Alpine I followed up my e-mails with several phone calls and spoke to the manager of their customer service department. Despite these efforts Alpine's management made no effort to return my e-mails or phone calls and continue to advertise the product on their website as being "fish safe" for several months.

I am unaware of any efforts on the part of Alpine to either recall this dangerous product or make notifications to the appropriate consumer and environmental protection departments of the states concerned. Given the cavalier attitude with which my concerns are being treated and the fact that Alpine never sought the return of the product I believe they merely ignored the toxic nature of their product in the hopes that the problem with simply go away with the sale and distribution of the product..

As an outcome of this complaint I am hopeful that the California Department of environmental protection will investigate this matter to ensure that Alpine Corporation has taken the steps necessary to safeguard the safety of the people of California as well as the environment. These include notifying all customers and distributors of the product of the potential danger associated with the product and the notification of the US EPA and the corresponding state agencies of all states to which the product was exported."
justification: All fish in the pond died within 12 hours of exposure to the hose, indicating a high likelihood of severe impact if similar incidents occur.

incident_description:
I am a mechanic at Filoli Center, a property of the National Trust for Historic Preservation (www.filoli.org) and would like to bring to you attention my safety concerns regarding Little Wonder Electric Hedge Trimmers manufactured by Little Wonder a division of Schiller-Pfeiffer Inc. Filoli Center has used several different Little Wonder electric hedgers models since the early 1980's to maintain our public gardens. Our experience has shown the current model to be far less reliable than previous  models. We pay $300 U.S. for each model 3010 and put a maximum of 50-70 hours a year on each unit. Three of the new units have failed in such a way that a shower of sparks is emitted from the motor area. Initially, when I  bench tested a  malfunctioning unit it produced a quantity of sparks sufficient to burn several holes through a synthetic fleece jacket I was wearing. 
This first sparking incident occurred In March of 2009. On 4/01/09 I spoke with a female individual by the name of [redacted] with Little Wonder at phone number [redacted] and explained my problem and expressed my concern with the brand new Little Wonder electric hedger model 3010-00-01 serial number 1050015400 that sparked and caught fire after 5-6 second run time out of the  box. I show us as having purchased two hedger units model 3010-00-01 serial numbers 1070023039 and 1070023040 on 2/27/08. Unit ending serial number **3039 failed 10/09/08 and was replaced under warranty with unit serial 1080011425. Unit ending in serial **3040 failed 9/26/08 and was replaced under warranty with serial 1080011424. My recall of the reason for the units failure was electrical / electronics related.
More recently on 8/10/10 we purchased two more units model 3010-00-01 serial numbers 1090011415 and 1090011416. Unit 1090011415 failed late July 2011 due to the excessive sparks being emitted from the motor and the loud abnormal bear box noise. The unit was replaced with moderate difficulty and delay with a new hedger serial 1110064530 on 9/07/11. The local repair shop indicated the shaft running through the armature in the motor was bent and the California Distributor Golden Eagle Distributing in Rocklin, CA. was not going to cover the repair under warranty. Eventually the unit was covered under warranty. Our usage consists of finely hedging established boxwood and english laurel hedges that only requires the cutting of leaves and some stems rarely exceeding 0.125 inches in diameter. Little Wonder markets the hedger as being rated to cut any type of hedge or shrub that does not exceed 0.500 inches in diameter. Yesterday( 10/06/11), another Little Wonder hedger was brought to Filoli's in house mechanical repair shop by a horticulturalist with the sparking and grinding problem. It is the other unit purchased last 8/10/10 serial 1090011416. I believe the division Little Wonder of Schiller-Pfeiffer is marketing  product with a serious defect and needs to investigate the quality of materials used in the construction of all the electric hedger models that have the defective motors.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the frequent sparking incidents pose a significant risk of injury, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: I purchased a Ferris 5100 Zero-Turn Mower approximately 5 years ago.  During this time, I have experienced multiple events where the suspension bolts on the mower sever while using the mower, thus causing the steering mechanisms to fail while using the mower.  This failure could result in serious injury up to and including a fatality.  I have reported this issue to Briggs and Stratton (Parent of Ferris).  They have recognized this engineering failure and have developed a fix for this issue.  Unfortunately I have experienced multiple repair events that have been quite costly.  Ferris agreed to pay for the parts but refused to pay for the labor.  This labor charge is much higher than the parts.  I feel that a Product Recall should be considered to ensure that all 5100's are repaired so that a mechanal failure would prevent a serious injury to the consumer.  I have filed complaints with the State of GA and State of WI.  Both states requested a review by Briggs.  I have not received any response from the company (over 60 day) since my first complaint.  In my mind they are ignoring a huge safety issue that needs immediate resolution.  I am attaching the vaious communications I have had with this company.
justification: The incident involves a recurring mechanical failure that could lead to serious injury, as evidenced by multiple reports.

incident_description: Craftsman Gas Lawn Mower has had a variety of problems, since purchased new, at the Sears store in Slidell, Louisiana.  The latest incident involves the plastic fuel tank, on the mower, that failed at the seam of the tank, and has been leaking gasoline all over the (hot) engine housing.  My 20 year old son was fortunate that it didn't explode, or flame up, when it was noticed.  We brought it to the store, and they agreed this plastic tank should have not failed in less than 2 years of minimal use, but they were not willing to order me the replacement tank (which i was told was less than 50 bucks). I called their recall unit, at Sears, also, and they also agreed it should not have failed so soon, but also was unwilling to replace the part.  Then, I contacted national customer service, and got a form letter response.

incident_description: I was using a Weedeater lawnmower.  I tipped over when the rear wheel ran over a brick.  It completely flipped over on it's side but did not shut off.  The engine kept running and the blade stayed engaged and continued to turn.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the potential for harm was high due to the blade remaining engaged.

incident_description:
My John Deere L-111 Riding lawn tractor was parked in my garage and had not been used in over a week. During the overnite period of June 21, to the morning of June 22, 2011  my garage 
filled with gasoline vapors to the point that it was unbearable to enter the garage. Had the hot water heater in my garage been a gas type instead of electric my house would have been destroyed by the explosion and ensuing fireball, possibly killing me, my wife and our two children. 
After carefully opening the garage doors manually so as not to create a spark I let the garage air out which took one and a half hours. When it was safe to reenter the garage I traced the gasoline 
vapors to the John Deere. Upon closer examination I could see that the gasoline was leaking out of the lower right side seam of the fuel tank and creating a large puddle under the machine. As well as 
filling the garage with a very large volume of vapors.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident could have led to a catastrophic explosion and fire if the water heater was gas-powered.

incident_description:
Purchased brand new 2011 Husqvarna Garden Tractor ( Model# GTH27V48LS) from Husqvarna dealer 10/1/2011.

Used for the first time 10/7/2011 and this is when the following occured.
Received with a a full tank of gasoline ( 4 gal.) After mowing for apoprox. one (1) hour, machine quit
running. OUT OF GAS !! Couldn't believe it used up so much gas in 1 hour. Re-filled tank and then decided to look under machine to see how much gas was in the translucent plastic tank. Gas was
pouring out of the fuel line--no way to stop it. Immediately hosed everything off with water.Anyone
smoking or a spark near this would have been disasterous!!
I observed visually that the affected fuel line was not only too long, but it had never been tied up out of the way of moving steel parts (namely when the mower deck was raised to a higher position, the 
rubber fuel line became pinched between pieces of steel) and ruptured.
Called the dealer : S&D Power Sports,Inc. 708 Manitou Rd., Hilton, NY 14468   (585-366-4800)
They came right out, confirmed what I observed regarding the fuel line and said they would contact Husqvarna concerning this dangerous flaw in the machine.(Note:S&D promptly returned the repaired machine to me within 2 hrs.)
This needs to be addressed as I since discovered that Husqvarna did have a recall in 2010 for that
model year Garden Tractors FOR THE VERY SAME PROBLEM !!!
Also, if you look back to year 2006, Husqvarna recalled 174,000 tractors for fire hazard problems.
I personally sent a review to Husavarna regarding the danger of the leaking fuel line and they sent me an e-mail telling me that my review was NOT ACCEPTABLE !!

The New York State Attorney's Office would also be interested in this matter.

Please look into this before someone gets hurt,or worse.  Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have led to a fire hazard, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is 'possible' as the issue was present in previous models and was not addressed despite a recall.

incident_description:
I have a Cub Cadet model 1040 lawn tractor. Manufacture date is 5/ 2011. While riding the mower, somthing underneath the mower snapped or broke and I was not able to stop the mower. The brakes and gas pedal were stuck and would not operate. I did notice a lond gold colored pin on the left side of the mower frame that appeared to be loose. Trying to start the unit afterward was not succesful since you have to have the brake pedal fully depressed prior to starting. Both the brake and the gas pedal would not go down further then half way. 
This is a MAJOR defect in the design of this unit.

incident_description: The seat on the riding mower inadvertently comes unlatched and moves when going forward or changing from forward to reverse. incident_description: On July 23, 2011 I purchased a CharBroil RED 4-burner infrared grill.  Within two months of purchase, the labels for the settings of the burner began to peel off. incident_description:

incident_description:
We have a Weedeater Rotary Lawn Mower Model 96134000602, purchased at Wal-Mart in May 2008.

On October 17, 2011 I was attempting to start this mower in my driveway.  When I got it started, it began to vibrate violently and was actually trying to spin in a circle.  I let go of the handle which allowed the engine to shut off.  I had no idea what was happening.  I then noticed holes in my siding on the outside of the garage (photos attached).  As I was trying to figure out what happened, I saw two pieces of metal in our garden approximatley 6 feet to the right of the holes in the siding.  I retrived the pieces of metal and realized it was a blade from the mower and the blade had sheared in two (see photos)!  

These blades are supposed to be made of metal tempered so that they will not break, but will only bend.  Upon further investigation I discovered that the blades had actually put a hole THROUGH the garage wall and caused a hole on the INSIDE of the garage wall as well (see attached photo).  

I am thankful to be alive and I am EXTREMELY fortunate that I was not killed or seriously injured when this happened.  

This product is a real danger to consumers who should be made aware of this risk.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
justification: The mower blade shearing and causing damage to the garage wall, with potential for serious injury, warrants a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that a plastic flashlight projecting Halloween images is a potential burn hazard. The product comes with no instructions, no warning and no batteries. The consumer attempted to place a battery into the flashlight and within 5 seconds the battery casing became very hot, within 15 seconds the plastic casing began to blister and melt. The consumer placed it in her sink and watched it blister and smoke. The consumer powered off the toy at the switch using a pot holder and the smoking subsided. The consumer stated that it took 30 minutes to allow the product to cool. 

After the product cooled down the consumer opened the battery compartment and found that her batteries melted and had battery acid over her hand. The consumer called the media and will inspect the product. The consumer called the firm yesterday and left a message. The firm called her back the same day told that they would have the product recalled. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. 

The consumer stated that the product has not caused damage to her home. The consumer was burned to her right hand on her inner palm but not any substantial burns. The consumer has called the fire department after the incident took place. The product takes AA batteries and does not indicate on the packaging to what ages the product is intended.
justification: Consumer suffered minor burns, and the product's design and lack of warnings pose a high likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description: I bought a Dora the Explorer Flashlight for my granddaughter .  It is made by Imperial Toy LLC.  It was on for a very short duration.  We used C Cell Duracell Batteries and the flashlight go so hot it melted the batteries inside the flashlight.
justification: The flashlight overheating and melting batteries poses a high likelihood of injury due to potential chemical burns or shrapnel.

incident_description: model # 917.276410, 18.5 HP, 42" electric start 6 speed transaxle mower...we have owned this mower for only 5 years, and now are replacing the lift link assembly for the 3rd time, 1 time under warranty, 2 times at our expense, and the lift lever assembly and groove pin are now broke and will have to be repaired. This mower has a suspension deck and the lift links are very thin rods and it appears that the poor design does not have the strength to hold the deck without the rods snapping. incident_description: In August of 2010 our homeownerÃÂs association ([REDACTED])  in Lisle, IL purchased  a quantity of 33 Ardmore 8992-61 PL outdoor light fixtures manufactured by Minka Lavery . We experienced a high failure rate of the photocells in the units. Per my request, the manufacturer warrantied the photocells and shipped redesigned replacement units to us in September of this year (2011). Upon having our electrician replace the defective photocells it was discovered that five (5) of the original photocells (16%) had shorted out, melting their enclosures and arcing inside the fixture. Fortunately we have these installed on fieldstone exteriors, but had they been on a wooden structure, or arced into the electrical box inside the wall, the structures could have easily caught fire. While the fixures ceased to operate properly (either staying completely on or completely off 24/7), they failed to trip any circuit breakers and the electrical current remained live on shorted out and exposed wiring. This was a definite electrocution hazard for anyone who might have needed to change a bulb. In my opinion, this is more than a photocell defect; this should be a product recall issue. I suspect Minka is aware of this problem or they would not have redesigned the photocells and warrantied their replacements. They have blamed the occurrences on our installation process, which did not follow their instructions. I am further concerned by their responses being more geared toward legal statements of liability than consumer safety. While they sent one of their distributors on property to inspect the situation, he was more concerned about how they were installed (to place blame) than on the actual failures. He was offered to take a defective (melted) photocell back to the manufacturer for inspection and declined. I am completely convinced that the original photocells present a fire or electrocution hazard and should be tested and/or recalled. I have all of the original photocells (both melted ones and still functional ones) and would be happy to provide them to your agency or a third party for evaluation and testing.
justification: Shorts in the photocells could have caused fires or electrocution, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
[REDACTED]
								[REDACTED]
								20 SEP 11
The Toro Company
8111 Lyndale Avenue South
Bloomington, Minnesota 55420

				Re: SAFETY REPORT
				      Part ejection from lawn mower
				      No injury from this incident	

Dear Toro Company

	I like my Toro self-propelled walk-behind lawnmower Model 20066, serial 280037564, but it surprised me earlier this month when it forcefully ejected the plastic trailing shield that is mounted horizontally at the lower back edge of the deck, and usually drags along, protecting my boots, shins and toes from objects slung backward by the rotating mower blade.  

FACTS

This happened just as I was making a 180-degree turn to start another row of cutting, which involves a sharp turn and sometimes a little backward motion of the mower to line up for the next row of cutting.  While the mower continued to run, there was a loud bang sound, a perceptible sudden movement of the mower handle, as if the blade had hit something solid, and the entire trailing shield shot out about two feet to the front (fortunately for me) of the mower.  I was startled, but not hurt in any way.

I stopped the mower to check for damage, and noted a hole (with adhering flap of plastic)  in the plastic disk of the mowerÃÂs right front wheel, with the flap signaling that the impact had been from the inside of the wheel.

The plastic trailing shield bears two numbers debossed or stamped into both sides of the black plastic part: 114-1585 near one end, and J0108 near the other end. I cannot be sure whether the second and fourth characters are the numeral 0 or the letter O.   The shield, which seemed normal and in good condition prior to this mowing, has been sliced by something, causing a roughly V-shaped cut, straight on one leg of the V, but puckered and curly on the other.  The shieldÃÂs straight bar, which fits into the holes at either side of the back of the mower deck supporting it in place, and allowing it to rotate on the horizontal axis to stay in touch with the grass, is now slightly bent and scraped, but is not completely cut.

I had adjusted all the wheels on the mower that day to the cutting height just below the center option.  In your manual, this corresponds to a nominal cutting height of 2 3/8 inches (60 mm).  I estimate that the top 1 1/2 inches of the blades of the dry grass was being cut at the time, and the mower was running at normal speed, without lugging, and before I had started pushing forward on the handle that engages the self-propelled feature. 

I have retained the trailing shield, which either you or CPSC may examine and test at your convenience, if you bring me a replacement for it.  My contact information is at the end of this letter.

SPECULATION
I think that the trailing shield jammed and dug its usually-trailing edge in the grass as I pulled the lawn mower slightly backward, which caused the flexible shield and its rod to bow toward the front of the lawnmower, enough to allow one end of the shield to pop out of the retaining holes in the deck, and that end of the shield was free to flip a short way into the rotating mower blade, which pierced it, slung it forward with enough force for one end of the shieldÃÂs rod to poke a hole-with-a-flap in the right front wheel, but the momentum of the shield was enough to carry it forward of the mower.

CONCERN
This is likely to happen with other mowers that include this shield, and the ejection may not always be to the front.  I was not hurt, but someone else may be hurt, either by the ejected shield, or (if they rolled over it with the mower running) parts of the shield if the blade caught it and chopped it up and threw it out.

SUGGESTION
Consider mounting a trailing shield in a different way, to prevent the possibility of it being bowed out of the side holes in the deck.  Perhaps a piano-type hinge, with multiple support points.  Consider shaping the trailing shield a different way, to reduce the possibility of it catching and jamming in the grass if the mower is momentarily pulled backward as is frequently necessary in lawn cutting.  Consider a fabric trailing shield (ballistic nylon?).

If you are willing to replace this shield, please do so within the next two weeks.  If you have further questions, or want to examine the lawn mower and the shield, please let me know within the next two weeks.


							Sincerely,

							[REDACTED]

mailing address above
[REDACTED]
cc: Consumer Product Safety Commission
justification: Although no injury occurred, the forceful ejection of the trailing shield poses a potential hazard for future users.

- Manufacturer (printed on package): TechLite Lumen Master, CREE XPE L.E.D., Imported by Costco Wholesale Corporation, Seattle, WA
- Also printed on package: ITM./ART.564808

The package contained three LED flashlights and a total of 9 Duracell AAA batteries (99543760 Expiration March 2017) (3 batteries for each of the 3 flashlights). The package was securely sealed (plastic 'bubble' and cardboard) and showed no signs of tampering or having been opened.

Carefully following the included printed directions I placed each battery correctly as shown both on the printed directions and the guide labeling on the battery holder in each of the 3 flashlights and assembled the flashlights completely following all printed directions.

On two of the three flashlights I tested their operation and found no problems. On the third I noticed the outside metal body of the flashlight seemed warm. I carefully opened this flashlight and took out the battery holder which was extremely hot to the touch and quickly removed one of the batteries. While the battery holderÃÂs metal parts were still very warm they began to cool down immediately. I again carefully, following the printed directions and the guide labeling on the battery holder, removed and correctly replaced all batteries and as soon as the third and last battery was put into the battery holder the metal parts and the batteries themselves began to heat up instantly to an extremely high temperature. Again I quickly removed the batteries and the assembly began to cool down.

SN:  079681
Model #: BB10769A

On September 4, 2011 I lit the grill (all three burners), preheated it, and put all burners on "Low".  I placed six large chicken quarters on the grill and left it for 20 minutes.  When I returned, I noted a small amount smoke and assumed the grease from the chicken skin had caught fire.  When I reached the grill, I noted the temperature gauge was pinned at at the end of the scale--the scale stopped at 800 degrees F.  My first impression was that I had left it on high, but the knobs were all on low.  

I opened the grill and the chicken was charred, and an aluminum serving plate that I was preheating had melted and curled over the edge of the upper warming rack (I checked later and it appears aluminum melts at about 1250 degrees).  I tried to turn off the grill, but the first knob spun freely--apparently melted.  I reached to turn off the gas at the tank, but heat too intense.  I then got a rag to use as a hotpad and turned off the tank.  There was no evidence of a grease fire when I opened the grill, but each of the three burners was burning brightly.

The only explanation I have is that the pressure regulator of the grill failed, causing the extreme overheating.  Had I not intervened I feel sure there would have been a fire and/or explosion.  I received two second degree burns to my right hand, each about 1/2 inch in diameter.  Actually I feel very lucky and blessed that no worse injuries were sustained.

The grill has always been stored indoors.
justification: Severe burns sustained due to grill overheating, likely caused by a failed pressure regulator.

incident_description:
Over this past weekend, I experienced a flash grease fire while grilling on my Weber Genesis Grill.  I am wondering if there has been a recall on this particular grill.  I am concerned as it appears there are several dangerous design flaws.  The design of the drip tray allows for food scraps to fall into the drip tray and over time grease collects on the food scraps rather than running down the drip tray to the left side aluminum drip pan as intended.  While grilling, grease dripped down onto the burners, catching fire, and transferring that fire to the drip tray.  In an instant the tray was on fire, and it was so intense I had to back away from the grill before I could remove the food on the grill.  The food on the grill fed the flames, which at this point was so hot inside the lower cabinet that it melted the plastic grommets around the door handles.  Toxic plastic fumes billowed from the grill.  This fire was right next to the propane tank, which you will see in the attached photos got hot enough to blacken the tank.  It was by the grace of God that the tank did not explode.  
 
I am not an engineer, however I have been grilling for many years.  Several things stand out to me.  First, the grease tray appears to be too close to the burners.  The grease tray itself should pitch to the center of the tray, not the side.  This would create a shorter distance for grease to travel to reach the aluminum grease pan. The doors should not have plastic components within close proximity to the heat source.  Being an enclosed space below the grill allows for heat build-up in a flash fire, creating a risk of exploding the propane tank.  
 
This is my four gas grill, and first grease fire.  I have had one other Weber grill, an [REDACTED] grill, and others.  I purposefully selected this grill after reading reviews and receiving personal recommendations of Weber Genesis users.  It was purchased for me as a Christmas gift this year.  I recognize now that the grease tray should be cleaned frequently, however, I never regularly cleaned the grease tray on past grills, and I suspect that most people are like me and do not clean the grease tray frequently.  
 
My concern is that someone will be seriously injured or could die from a propane explosion if they experience what I experienced this weekend
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but had the potential for severe burns or even death due to the proximity of the fire to the propane tank.

There is NO information on the package, or the paperwork or the unit as to any company information or contact information.  There is no information found on the internet regarding this company.  I am concerned about this product.  I had a unit in my toddlers room when I noticed a smell of plastic burning.  I honestly can't believe that a product is sold in the US and allegedly "UL listed" without any way to contact anyone regarding this product.

incident_description:
I have a Perfect Flame Barbeque Gill with Sear Chamber, Model E3520-LPG, Serial E15033608.  I attempted to use the Searing chamber 3 times in a row to see what was wrong.  It was never used before.  When I turn it on the gas backs out of the searing element and fire ignites at the gas switch used to turn it on.  Flames pop out all around and under the unit.   I looked at the unit and all connections are good, no leaking gas etc.  The design of the unit is very dangerous someone could get killed.  I'm concerned I took it apart 3 times to find a problem and it is definitely a design flaw.  When I purchased this from Lowes I spent $650.00 for it and feel ripped off.  I found numerous complaints on line and on the RipOffReport.com

UPDATE:  West Side Grill came out on September 13, 2011 and gave my grill a complete going over.  They tested every part  of the grill.  What they found was that the gas "orifice" that led to the sear burner had a spiders nest hiding inside.  This caused gas to back up and create my unsafe condition.  They used a tiny little cork screw brush and pulled it out.  Clearly this is a situation that had nothing to do the way the grill was built.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident could have caused serious harm due to the design flaw, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description: While cutting grass with my Troy-Bilt riding mower, "RZT Series Tractor - Mustang ZT50", one of the three blades separated (broke) about 1/3 of the way from the end. I was unable to find the part of the blade that separated as it apparently was slung away. I asked via email if Troy-Bilt wanted the blade to inspect it. Their response was only if there was a warranty issue, not the failure.

incident_description:
In August of 2006, we purchased a Jenn-Air outdoor gas grill from Lowe's. (Model # 720-0165.)   We tried to go to Lowe's to speak to someone, but they claim that they no longer sell Jenn-Air or any parts associated with Jenn-Air.  The only person who uses the grill is my husband.  It is used only during the summer months, and he takes very good care of it. We have become increasingly concerned each time  we use it, that there is something very wrong with it and that someone will get hurt by it. The outside of the grill is way hotter than it should be.  We don't let our children or any visitors walk anywhere near it!  My husband can barely lift the handle without getting severely burned.  Heat seems to be shooting toward the front of the grill.  The ignitor buttons no longer seem to be working.  

This appliance has been cared for meticulously by my husband...there is no way that this is normal wear and tear.  When not in use, it is always covered.  Also, my husband is a person who is a certified installer of high-end appliances such as [REDACTED], so I have confidence that he knows what he is talking about when he says that this gas grill is defective and/or made with sub-par dangerous  materials!

We are not generally people who file complaints , but when one clearly sees that something is wrong, action must be taken to correct it before someone gets hurt!  We use it with extreme caution, but I am sure there are others who don't know the dangers of it.
justification: The grill's excessive heat and malfunctioning ignitors pose a high risk of severe burns, making an injury likely.

incident_description:

A second light exhibited similar problems just recently and I realized that all of the lights were shorting out. IÃÂve since replaced all of these with another product.
 
Notice how the central stem that supports the 3 bulbs at the base. The issue seems to be inadequate shielding of the wires, or sub-standard insulation on the wires that run through the tube.  On two of the lights IÃÂve actually had the central stem melt and a hole burned in the tube.  The other lights all showed varying degrees of burning, melting or overheating. incident_description:
I have a John Deere series L108 riding lawn tractor. I have a problem with the fuel tank leaking gasoline.  This is an extreme safety issue as it could cause fire and potenially cause serious, if not death,  to the operator.  
I have talked a John Deere customer service supervisor and was told to take the mower to a John Deere service center to determine the exact cause of the leaking fuel.  It was then confirmed that the fuel tank was indeed leaking and needed to be replaced. This same service center indicated that they have replaced several other fuel tanks on John Deere mowers this year.
However, the service representative said there was no product recall at this time and would not pay for the repair because the mower is about six years old.  To that I say:
1.  The fuel tank is not a normal replacement item like a spark plug, therefore it should not need replacing during the life of the mower.  The motor should fail before the gas tank.
2. The fuel tank is made of molded plastic composed of several pieces.  Therefore, the design is flawed because the engineers knew or should have known that composing the tank of several pieces instead of a single tank with no seams would lead to potential leaks. And due to the importance of safety it should have had a better, safer design.
3. The lawn mower is about six years old but has had excellent care. When not in use, it have been stored in the basement of my home, so it has never been exposed to any extreme weather conditions.  Also the gas tank was not punctured in anyway, it is well enclosed in the body of the mower surrounded by metal.
The incident number give by John Deere is [REDACTED].  The person I spoke with is [REDACTED].  Her telephone number is [REDACTED].

Thank you for looking into this matter.  I looked forward to hearing from you
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the potential for serious harm or death due to fuel tank leaks makes this a high likelihood incident.

It has resulted in several near fires when stopped  on dry leaves, and has produced extensive damage to turf and grass when the mower slows it's speed to go from one direction to the opposite direction.
justification: The downward-facing exhaust system poses a high risk of fire when operating on dry leaves, as evidenced by previous near-fire incidents.

incident_description: I was at a friend's home and we were on her deck.  She had a fire pot and it was lit.  As the gel burned down and was almost out, she poured more gel into the pot.  As she did this the fire followed the fuel into the bottle and the gel shot out as fireballs all over her deck.  I was hit by some of the gel.  My left foot was on fire but I was able to remove my shoe quickly and only received a monor burn on my left foot.  My right ankle was on fire.  I stood up and moved to an area where I could stop, drop and roll.  However, this did not extinguish the fire.  My husband found a patio pillow and hit the burning area with it until the flames were extinguished.  I suffered 2nd and 3rd degree burns on my right ankle.  Two weeks after the incident I was hospitalized with heart issues.  This ended up being a vagus nerve reaction to the burn.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries (2nd and 3rd degree burns) and subsequent hospitalization, but did not result in death.

incident_description:
Consumer believes his Toro snow blower is unsafe and a fire hazard.  While his snow blower is not recalled, it is having the same problems listed in recall release 11-207. In the winter, the consumer started it a few times just to make sure it was running properly, even when he didnÃÂt intend to use it, and then stored it in his garage. I have been told that, although my grill sustained extensive damage, the company will only replace parts, which I consider unacceptable due to continued safety concerns with the company.

incident_description:
I was in charge of grilling hamburgers at my church this evening. The grill the church had set up was a "Bakers & Chefs" model with eight (8) burners and two (2) propane tanks. Upon further investigation, it appears this model is called "Main Event" and is produced by a parent company called Grand Hall.

I followed the instructions on the grill to start it up. I have worked with many grills, both charcoal and gas, and had no difficulty getting the burners to ignite. Once I had waited for the grill to warm up, I placed the burgers on the grill. As they were cooking, huge flames jumped up through the grill grates. Many were over a foot tall. I was afraid to go in and flip or remove my burgers for fear of being burned. They seemed to occur regardless of where the dial was set--I had it set to "low" the entire time on one burner and this happened (the same thing happened when "high" was selected).

Eventually, I caught a break and managed to flip one of the burgers. When it was set down on the griddle, the huge flames began again. Most of them occurred right around the burger, but others jumped up in seemingly random locations.

I had to turn all the burners off and wait for the grill to cool down to safely remove my burgers, which were inedible.

While I understand flames are an inevitable part of any grilling experience, the amount and intensity of flames even on the lowest heat setting were unacceptable to me. I have been grilling since I was in my early teens and this is the first time I've ever been scared to place a tool on the grilling surface in fear of burning my arm or hand.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the intense and unpredictable flames posed a significant risk of burns, classifying it as an incident.

I saw the recalls on this grill when looking for replacement parts and wanted to notify you of this problem.  I have an LX date for the grill so it is not in the other recalls.

He did not have feeling in his pinky finger the whole time.  

Consumer also mentioned the product is on recall Release #07-078.
justification: Consumer sustained injuries (lacerations) due to the explosion of the air pump, but no fatalities were reported.

incident_description:
After noticing the gel from the fire pot was out he refilled it with the alcohol gel. Then a flame entered the bottle and caused it to explode and flew in every direction. The fire pot (also known as a Napa candle) was near a deck where it burned a hole threw a cushion of the patio furniture and umbrella, and his American flag.  The finish on the deck was destroyed (the location near where the where the fire pot was set). 

 It got into one personÃÂs eyes (but was not on fire) and the victim receive severed burns to the abdomen, thighs and right hand. He immediately fell to the ground and rolled to put the fire out but when that did not help he then jumped into his Coi pond and that extinguished the flames. He was then taken to the University of North Carolina were he was kept in the Burn Unit for two days. He was diagnosed with having Superficial second degree burns. He had various skin grafts and was treated for the burns. 

The retailer was contacted on 5/24/2011 or 5/25/2011 to inform him of his injuries associated with the product. He discarded of the product and has not contacted the firm.  The product is a fancy styled vase and the center is a stainless still little tub and that is what you pour the gel into.  It is manufactured and sold by Napa Home and Garden Inc.

He indicated that it is a great product but the concerns with it are if you refill the gel while the fire pot is still hot it could pose as a potential fire hazard. So itÃÂs safe to refill the gel when the fire pot in cool and not in use.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns and required hospitalization, and the likelihood of such an event occurring again is high if the product is not used correctly.

incident_description:
I was using a pesticide / sprayer combination to spray some trees in my yard.  When I tried to turn the sprayer off, the nozzle / valve combination came off in my hand and the pesticide sprayed uncontrollably, some spraying back on myself. 

Fortunately, my wife was near the faucet and was able to turn off the water supply and stop the spray.

The nozzle/valve combination seems to be poorly designed to pop off so easily, allowing an uncontrollable release of the sprayer contents.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have been severe due to the uncontrollable pesticide spray, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description:

Defect/Problem = Installer failed to install in accordance with Manufacturer's Safety Instructions (NEC 110.3(B) Installation and Use.). It was a non-compliant installation, and was missing safety equipment.  This gate operator is at our city Public Yard Waste and Installer should have installed Safety Contact Edges on both sides of Electric Operator, this Model is the same as the one that Killed the 11year old girl in Toledo last year by pulling her in between the gate and the electric operator a 5.25 inch space, if the two required contact safety edges had been in place the gate is designed to STOP AND REVERSE 2 to 6 INCHES.
How and When Discovered = While visiting our local city's Public Yard Waste to dump our yard waste, I have installed these units for over 30 years and the city pays no attention to my complaints of at least 9 safety violation (NEC, OSHA, MIOSHA, UL325, ASTMf2200, Manufacturer's Safety Installation Instructions, to name a few.

Type of Hazard = other
Other Hazard = NEC, Manufacturer's Safety Installation Instructions violations

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that her Kenmore gas grill caught flames yesterday while it was being operated outside on her deck. The product is solely a grill. The grill was on for about 10 minutes until flames came out of the handles to turn on the grill and the interface is now burned. The consumer called the retailer today and spoke with [REDACTED] at the number posted on the grill and was transferred to another woman who offered to send out a technician at the consumer's expense. When the consumer asked if there was anything else that could be done about the incident, the representative subsequently gave her the number to the CPSC. The consumer stated that the structure of her home is not damaged. The consumer also stated the fire was put out with a dry rag. At the time the consumer chose not to call the fire department. Thankfully, no one was injured during the incident. The consumer was also informed by the retailer that her grill is not on recall. As of now, the consumer has not yet called the firm. The consumer felt it was imperative to report this incident to the CPSC.

incident_description: BBQ grill started on fire.  User was bbq'ing hamburgers.  The lid was down and the grill was smoking so the user lifted the lid and flames shot out the front of the grill.  The user dumped a 5 gallon bucket of water on the grill to put out the fire.  The knobs burnt off and the siding on the house was burnt.  The food was not even burnt!

incident_description:
Left side transmission on my Cub Cadet RZT 50 lawn mower, looses power and will neither pull or go into reversr after only ten or fifteen minutes running time.  The right side performs well.

After many attempts to fix the problem, I learned the manufacture Hydro-Gear knew about the problem being caused by poor design of the transmission.  I ham in the process of replacing the transmission with a new one at a cost of over $750.00.

The belts were replaced the belt on two occasion. The most recent incident was on 6/29/2010 he went to purchase another belt and make sure the store manager [REDACTED] was aware of the incident he experienced. The tractor has only been used for a total of 10 hours.

His safety concern is that if he was to get off the tractor and the belt snaps it could possibly cut off his ankle.

incident_description:
Purchased McCulloch Gas Backpack Blower, Model BL30, S/N 0809003258 at Sears 11/26/2010.  Used only 6 times, but have had multiple issues that are safety related.  First, and continuing problem is the gas cap fails after prolonged exposure (weeks?) to gas/fuel mixture in the tank.  The threads no longer seal and the cap won't stay tight.  Mfg explained that there is an additive in the gasoline that is causing the cap to fail.  I have 3 different caps furnished by the mfg that leak.  The last time I asked them for a new tank, but in trying to replace the tank, the torx screws holding the blower frame to the engine were stuck on so tight that the substandard torx heads stripped.  I did not accomplish the tank replacement, gave up, and reassembled the blower.  It still works correctly since I once again replaced the gas cap.  I now have 3 non-function gas caps and fully expect the new one to fail the next time I go to use the blower after it is exposed to the fuel mix.

My second complaint is that one of the rubber isolator bolts devulcanized from the metal, leaving the motor separating from the backpack and just flapping.  I asked for multiple replacements since the bolts appear substandard as well.
justification: Although no injuries have been reported, the repeated failure of the gas cap and the devulcanization of the rubber isolator bolts pose a significant safety risk, making it likely that an incident will occur.

incident_description: Leaf Blower muffler guard is too close to muffler or muffler runs too hot. When held in my left hand at waist level it burnt a hole in my pants.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (burn hole in pants) and the likelihood is high as it occurred while the tool was in use and at waist level.

incident_description: The Trex decking that I had installed is failing--flaking, peeling, etc.  This in turn is going to cause structural instability.  Trex has offered to send a few boards, but I feel they should replace the decks to ensure structural stability.  Despite their warranty, they are unwilling to step up and take care of their faulty product.

incident_description:
I have recently bought a Chargriller outdoor BBQ grill and have noticed the unpainted interior shell is coated to prevent corrosion. I reviewed the manual and online data to verify what the coating is. It is stated by Chargriller that the coating is "vegetable based." That is the only detail available. I contacted Chargriller by email and inquired about the coating. They simply restated it was "vegetable based."

The reason I contacted Chargriller, and now sp.gov, is that I feel this coating MAY NOT  be vegetable based and may possibly be a toxic corrosion inhibiter instead. 2 reasons lead me to believe this:

1. While serving in the Navy, I worked on jet aircraft where we used toxic petroleum-based anti-corrosion coatings on almost all engine parts, fittings, and compartments. MSDS sheets I reviewed at the time stated the coatings were indeed quite toxic if ingested. The coating on the Chargriller has the exact same appearance, consistancy, and odor as the anti-corrosin coating I worked with in the Navy.

2. While working on my motorcycle, I recently used a rust-preventative spray made by [REDACTED]. This spray, which is also nasty if inhaled, ingested, or even has prolonged skin exposure, also has the same color, consistancy, and odor as the previously mentioned toxic anti-corrosion coatings as I used in the navy.

You cannot mistake the odor that these anti-corrosion coating give off. It's an acrid, skunk-like strong odor that gives you a headache very quickly. I have recontacted Chargriller for MSDS information on the coating they are using and I have not been contacted back. If Chargriller is, indeed, using a toxic coating, they are seriously endangering the health of consumers who use their grills. The basic research I have done on my own has shown that the compounds contained in anti-corrosion coatings can cause neurological damage, lung damage, and cancer in minute quantities. I would like to request that Chargriller be made to divulge the detailed nature of their grill coating and disclose any MSDS if available.

Thank you for your time
[REDACTED]
justification: Potential exposure to toxic chemicals could cause injury, and the likelihood is high given the consumer's experience and lack of response from the manufacturer.

incident_description:

Consumer stated that the cord is too close to the carburetor which causes this incident.  Due to his blood being on the unit he stated that it is now a bio-hazard. Consumer stated that he administered first aid to his wound.

Consumer feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be reported.

incident_description:
The other evening, I fired up the Weber Gas Grill and got it warmed up.  I turned the heat down once I had preheated it to burn off the crusty things.  I put on an ear of corn wrapped in foil to reheat it, and went inside.  Looking out the kitchen window as I was preparing to return with some other food stuffs, I notices some flames at the end of the grill where the propane tank is and the burner controls are located.  I thought perhaps there was some greasy stuff still on the grill still flaring up.

As I got closer, things did not look right.  I looked up  under the burner control panel and discovered that the all three burner controls were in flames.  They have plastic assemblies that were burning and dripping hot plastic.  Somewhat foolishly, I tried to dodge the dripping flaming hot plastic to shut off the propane tank.  I did get some flesh burned off a finger from the molten plastic in my pursuit.  I eventually got the cylinder off, and slowly the burner controls died down and I blew them out.  The controls below are a total loss and the burner knobs are trashed from melting by the heat below.

So from one perspective, no harm (less one burn), no foul as everything was contained.  However having a devious mind, the thought occurred to me that many folks have units like this sitting on a wooden deck.  The dripping plastic is like flaming tar balls and is burning all the way to the ground.  The splat will continue to burn on the surface it hits.  Potentially things could get real ugly.  We had stone and sand below our unit, so the supplemental fuel source was not a big deal.
justification: Injury occurred due to molten plastic from burning controls, and likelihood is high as this could happen again with improper grill maintenance.

incident_description: My 2007 Cub Cadet lawn tractor burst into flames.  The plastic couling burned rapidly catching the seat and wiring on fire as well.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while it's possible, it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description: We own a Perfect Flame Model SLG-2007B gas grill. On July 12, 2011, we were cooking chicken on the grill when we noticed more smoke than normal coming from the grill. We saw that the entire side of the lid was on fire. The METAL lid. The flame was bright white from burning so hot. It was literally melting away. It only took a minute or two before the entire side of the lid was gone. I had time to turn off the burners and remove the tank. Thankfully, the grill was on our patio made of brick. This would have been a different story if it were located on a wood deck. There were white hot pieces of melted metal falling to the patio.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the severe fire and melting of the grill lid indicate a significant incident (severity level 2). The occurrence is possible but not frequent, given the unusual intensity of the fire (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Property owner was attempting to start his recently purchased gas-powered weed trimmer when it caught fire, resulting in minor burns to his hands and arms
