justification: Although an incident occurred (grill fire), no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
User was cutting grass on an established lawn with the push power mower. Without notice the mower suddenly made a several loud noises as if it had struck a foreign object on the ground. Before shutting down, it appeared to eject an unknown object from beneath the mower, but nothing was immediately found. The female operator did observe blade damage as well as a damaged component in the blade area that had contacted the blade, but did not understand exactly what or how it had occurred. The mower was parked until I came to inspect it several days later.
Upon inspection I discovered that the mower was designed to allow the lower handle section to extend through holes in the deck. The lower handle bracket assembly is made of a composite material rather than metal. The adjusting/retaining wingnut appears to thread into the composite material rather than metal. In this case, the right wingnut had backed out which allowed the lower handle assemly to slide directly into the blade path. Correspondingly approx. 3 inches of the lower  tubelor handle section had been cut off and ejected. A search later located the part across the street in another yard where it came to rest in the driveway next to the foundation. Further inspection indicated the left wingnut would not tighten securely, suggesting the threads into the composite material were compormised. It appears to be a very poor and unsafe design by allowing the handle assembly to extend directly through the deck and into the area of blade operation. THe 3 inch steel projectile could have caused serious injury to operator or to by standers.
justification: The mower's design flaw allowed the handle to enter the blade path, ejecting a steel projectile, posing a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
I have a Thermos bbq grill that has aluminum legs and sits in the floor or a table (about 2 feet high).  It has a red body about 15 inches square with fake coals, a gas burner and rack, and a red lid.  The propane bottle (about the size of a quart jar) screws onto the round control that has a knob that springs up (for off) and down (for on) and gives Off/ignition position/hi/med/low   settings.  
I hooked up the bbq and lit the burner with a long match.  A few minutes later, the flame was coming from the outside connection where the knob was.  It appeared to be coming from the narrow tube where the (regulator?) slid into the tube going to the bbq.    I blew out the flame and managed to turn the gas off.  It scared me quite a bit.

I did not use the bbq for a few years until yesterday (7/2/2011), I decided to try the bbq again, but a friend put a rubber o-ring between the parts to block the escaping gas.    I lit the bbq and 10 minutes later put the steaks on.  A few minutes later, I went to turn the steaks and found the bbq in flames right near the gas bottle again.  It was so bad the fire burned right through the plastic handle on the lid.  I could not turn the gas off to where the switch popped up to the off position, but managed to turn it to where the flame was out (using long handled bbq tongs).  Every few minutes it would flare up, but my friend was using my fire extinguisher on it and this would extinguish the flame for a few minutes,  We managed to unscrew the gas bottle from the bbq with oven mits, but the controls to the bbq - like the handle- were melted or burned beyond use.

A very strange thing was discovered.  My friend pulled the regulator? off the bbq after the bottle was unscrewed from it.  He poked into the tube where the gas flows into the bbq grill and was pulling strawlike material out (excelsior).  How this got there is quite a mystery, but obviously was there when the unit was purchased.  The excelsior was blocking the flow of gas somewhat, and the gas was escaping  (and flaming) through two small holes in the tube near the regulator.   I kept the excelsior and regulator and bbq for inspection if necessary.

I am trying to locate any other instances of a THERMOS bbq doing this and whether there is a recall or refund for the product.  (The steaks were cooked okay!)
Thank you.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire risk, with flames reaching the gas bottle and melting the grill's controls.

incident_description: I recently turned my grill on to let it heat up. I turned my back to continue to prepare dinner, all of the sudden i noticed back smoke billowing out of the grill. When I opened the grill flames were shooting out of it uncontolably. Soon the whole unit was up in flames. I quickly pulled out my garden hose to exstinguish the fire. Thick black smoke filled the air, a passer by stoped to see if my house was on fire. It was a scary experiance to say the least.
justification: The grill fire was uncontrolled and produced thick black smoke, indicating a significant incident but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
I recntly purchased a Poulan Model PP4218AVX. My saw was stored in my non airconditioned Garage in Central Florida. I attempted to use the saw on 18 June, 2011. Temperature in my garage was about 100 Deg F. I was not able to unscrew the gas-cap from the saw. Using pliers I finally got it off. After filling the tank, I screwed the cap back in as far as I could (The threads on the cap and on the tank were not stripped.) I used both hands to do this. After using the chain saw for about 10 minutes, I noticed that there was gasoline running down the front of my trousers. It was coming from the not completly seated gas cap. The problem turns out to be a thermal expansion problem of the Plastic gas cap and possibly of the gas tank itself. I solved it by putting my gas cap in the freezer for about 90 minutes. I was then able to screw the cap fully in. I spoke with Poulan about this problem and they stated that they were very much aware of it. My contact was a MS.
[REDACTED] who said she was with the Escalation of Complaints Department. She spoke with someone else while I was on the phone with her. Her suggestion was that they would send me an extra gas cap which I could store in my refrigerator while not in use. I would then rotate the two gas caps between the saw and the refrigerator. I stated that, for me, this was not a suitable fix. I asked for a full refund of the purchase price. This they refused.
justification: While no injuries occurred, the incident could have led to property damage or injury due to gasoline leakage.

incident_description: the grill caught on fire. Upon investigation, the support on the u shaped stainless steel burners had fallen off opening a large hole in the burner. All 3 burners have the same problem.

incident_description: I recently Purchased an outdoor gas grill. Charbroil Model# 463440109. The 3rd time I used it approxamatly 46 days after purchase, I lit the grill and discover that ther was not much flame. I checked the LP tank to see if it was full, and noticed that Lp gas was leaking out of the regulator valve conection. This valve and hose has never been tampered with, or damaged in any way. Inside the lid of the grill is stamped "magnesium alloy", which explains the white flame.  The heat damaged the wall near the grill, but it is okay.  The controls were on medium.  I have used this grill many times before with no hint of anything like this.

incident_description:
Gas lines failed on weed trimmer (Poulan FL26) due to break down in the gas line fittings dissolving in gasoline.  This is a fire and explosion hazard that could result in serious injury or death to the user if this occurs during operation or filling of gas tank.  

Upon examination of the 3 part gas line system (2 lines that pass through the gas tank, 2 double male fittings inside the tank, two sleeves to retain the fittings), it was noted that the sleeves dissolved and failed.  

Solution:  Recall of all Poulan weed trimmers with this design to repair this problem.  A redesigned gas tank with two nibs extending outward from the tank eliminating the fittings inside the tank.  These could be similar to commonly used designs that have flared ends to secure the gas lines.
justification: The dissolved gas line fittings pose a high risk of fire or explosion, likely leading to serious injury.

incident_description: I bought a new Husqvarna Model #RZ4623 zero turn riding mower on 3/19/2011 from Lowe's in Hamilton, Ohio  45013.  Ever since new it has left burned (dead) grass under the muffler if I am sitting still with the motor running for aproximately 5-10 seconds.  It has started a grass fire once just recently.  I am afraid this could start a bad fire if the mower is stopped and left running.  I have to stop several times during mowing to remove objects in my way, this is a normal routine.  I have not seen anything happen like this with any other mower.  The muffler should be repositioned or have a more efficient shield.  Thank You
justification: The mower's design flaw, leaving the muffler exposed, has already caused a grass fire and poses a high likelihood of starting a more severe fire if left running while stopped.

incident_description:
Product:  Sears Craftsman Lawn Tractor; Model No. 917.28924(4);  Serial 090310A036368

Injury sustained:  Two occasions with sand and/or dirt thrown up into face and into eyes

Problem is that the riding lawn mower has an inadequate deflector shield over the mower blade.  When on perfectly level ground, the shield usually performs correctly.  If you are on a slight slope or encounter slightly rough terrain, the shield bends so that it no longer covers all of the blade area.  This allows rocks, dirt, and sand to be thrown into the face of the driver.

In addition to the sand and dirt, the mower threw up a large nail last week.  Luckily the nail penetrated the heavy vinyl deflector shield.  If it had been a few inches in a different direction it might have been thrown up into the face or chin of the driver.  The force behind the nail would be enough to puncture the skull of a human or penetrate the area under the jaw.  It would have been more than sufficient to blind someone if struck in the eye.

I contacted the Sears warranty line.  They told me that it was not a warranty issue and they could not help me.  I am capable of modifying the deflector on my own lawnmower so that it is no longer a safety hazard.  However, I am concerned that someone who is unaware of the problem could be  seriously injured or blinded.
justification: The inadequate deflector shield allows debris and projectiles to be thrown into the driver's face, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description:

The third year     -  It ran good at first, but acted like the previous year.
The fourth year   -  It ran good again, but soon seemed like it had 1/2 the horsepower -- same as other years.
This snowthrower is used by me only in Dec. and Jan. as we go south for Feb. and Mar.  I also run the gas out in early spring.  We have gone south for 13 years.  Very few hours on snowthrower.
This is like recall for the Toro 1800 -- ?  Toro's other snowthrower being recalled.
justification: Gas leak in the garage poses a fire hazard, though no immediate injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I was cutting my front lawn with the Toro Recycler 22" self-propelled mower.  After fifteen minutes or so I noticed white smoke wafting up from the back of the engine.  The mower deck on the back left side appeared wet.

I immediately shut off the mower.  When I looked at the mower, I noted that the gas tank itself was very wet from about halfway down.  I pushed the mower to a spot in the yard away from the house and sidewalks and let it cool down thoroughly.  It first appeared that there was about a three-inch long crack in the plastic gas tank.  I took off the top cover of the mower, removed and drained the gas tank.  Upon closer examination I found the tank to be cracked/split clear across the width at a spot about a half inch above the seam in the tank, at an area where the tank bends 90 degrees.   

It seems to be an obvious defect in the manufacture of the plastic tank.  My concern, of course, is that someone may have a similar problem and not notice it before the gasoline ignites.
justification: Potential for fire hazard due to gas leak from cracked tank, but no injury reported.

incident_description: I have a Power Clear 180 and I still have the leaking gas problem.  I received the recall and brought it to the dealer for repair.  When I got it back, it leaked gas immediately.  Took it back and they replaced the carburetor.  Checked a few weeks ago, and it is leaking gas again.  Not sure why Toro is not doing more to correct this problem.  In my opinion, this is a major safety problem.

incident_description: We own a perfect flame grill model SLG2008A and my husband recently started to examine the grill for another reason and noticed that the heating tubes had burned and rusted so bad that they could not even be removed to be replaced and that the grill was unsafe to cook on and would need to be thrown out. This is when I saw recall information about another model and other complaints about this manufacturer of grill and was encouraged to report my issue as it could have turned into a dangerous situation if not caught in time for us.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the grill's unsafe condition posed a potential risk, making it an incident.

incident_description: My forhead was cut on the top left door to the charcoal access area between assembly steps.  Since I was following instructions the door handle / latch was not yet assembled which is one of the last steps.  This left the top left door hanging down horizontal in frontfront of the grill.  When I repositioned in front of the grill my head came on contact with the door causing a 4.5cm laceration to the forhead.  This required immediate medical attention including 8 stitches.  The door appeared to be stamped stainless steel and was extremely sharp around all edges.  It did not appear that the door had any post processing to eliminate the sharp edges from manufacturing.  This will be a safety concern during all normal usage when the door is down.  I currently have the door covered and will not be able to use that portion on the grill.

incident_description:
Defective welds on Kubota Tractor Loader with potential safety hazards.
Model/Serial Number of Loader: LA 681/sn 12135
Description of problem:
While doing routine service on my tractor and loader I discovered a number of cracks in the loader left hand side frame around the boom assembly pivot pin and a developing crack in the same area on the right hand side frame. In addition the weld is cracked and part of the frame broken where the left boom cylinder attaches to the boom assembly.
This loader is capable of lifting 1499 pounds to a height of 102 inches. Had these defects not been discovered there was the potential for the either the side frame or boom assembly to break or collapse under load endangering the safety of the operator.
I have lubricated the loader every ten hours of less as instructed by the Kubota operatorÃÂs manual. The manual does not list a recommendation of checking the loader welds for breaks or defects. Either the Kubota dealer or myself have serviced the tractor and loader within the time frame recommended by Kubota. Service records are available. The tractor and loader have not been used commercially and in fact have been used almost exclusively by me for property maintenance. The tractor and loader have a total of 900 hours since new in 1999.
An online check of defective welds on Kubota Loaders found an identical problem to mine.
A check at the local welding shop found that a Kubota tractor loader had been re-welded there with the same problem.
Discussions with Kubota service personnel have not been satisfactory which is why I am reporting this safety hazard to the CPSC. I asked Kubota for service bulletins on this loader and they tell me there are none.
The attached photos show the defects:
justification: The loader's defective welds could cause the boom assembly or side frame to break or collapse under load, posing a high likelihood of an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
This is a copy of an email sent to Weber regarding a fire hazzard with a Genesis grill.
FIRE HAZZARD

Weber Genesis Gas Grill
s/n DI1656236
purchase date 06/29/07

To Whom It May Concern,

At least early last year I had noticed a large burn mark on the left side frame panel and although I was not happy about the appearance I thought it came about because of the heat from the grill.
When I started to use the grill this year, flames started to come up outside the grill between the left side of the grill box and outside burner of the left side of the grill and therefore I shut it down immediately.
Upon inspection, I found two holes in the left side of the grill box and contacted your customer service department.  After providing a description of the problem they asked me to inspect the burner tubes and the crossover pipe.
The conclusion made was that there was a defect in the weld holding the middle tube causing it to come loose and burn a hole in the side of the grill.
The offer was made to replace the parts which I appreciate, but taking the entire grill apart is not a job for a layman.  
In addition, I feel that this is a dangerous condition precipitated by a poor design or weld which could have resulted in bodily injury.  
I was told that there was not a recall on this product which I will investigate further, and if there is not, I will try to initiate one.  I find it difficult to believe that this was a fluke and other consumers could be exposed to possible injury.
This is not my first Weber Grill and my other grill is at least twice the age and is still in very good condition.  I feel that offering parts to correct a dangerous situation and not offering the labor or a replacement is just a token gesture at best.
I have forwarded you the pictures you requested and will also forward the contents of this email to the CSPS.

On March 6, 2007, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission released a memo, Release #07-122, regarding a recall  on Weber Gas Grills and a Fire Hazard on a number of grills including the one which I own, model Genesis S-320 3780001.

incident_description: After a camping trip last fall, I retrieved my Optimus Nova stove, fuel can and pump from my camping bin and noticed a strong smell of gas in the container.  I did not actually use the stove at that time.  Last week, I got out my stove to fry fish and when I began to pressurize the fuel tank with the pump, I noticed a significant gas leak from the shut off valve on the pump.  The leaking fuel was sufficient to create a decent sized puddle where I was setting up the stove.  When I took the valve apart there were just remnants of an O-ring in the valve.  I tried replacing the O-ring with one from a hardware store, but it did not work and the leak continued.  The stove is completely unsafe to operate with this gas leak.  I did not get hurt, but did have a large amount of gas leak on my hands and clothing.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the significant gas leak posed a high risk of ignition and explosion, making it a serious incident.

incident_description:
I purchased a SPECTRACIDE 1 gal garden sprayer last fall from a local big box store. I have used it approx. 50 - 75 times.  On June 12, 2011 as I was pumping it, the sprayer hose came off where it connects to the tank.  Because the tank was under pressure, the contents (insecticide) came out at the hose connection point and went into my eyes, mouth and nose, covered my face in an instant.  After flushing my eyes, showering and changing clothes, I reattached the hose according to the mfgr. instructions, repressurized the sprayer and the hose came off again. This hose connection point is poorly designed, making this product potentially dangerous, even when mfg. instructions are followed.
Although I was wearing gloves, I did not have eye protection on at the time of pressurization because there was no expectation of a component failure.  I don't believe there was any mfg. warning to wear eye protection while pressurizing the tank.  There is no compression fitting for the hose at the tank connection.  The screw down fitting is insufficient. If there had been a more caustic solution in the sprayer I probably would not be able to see to write this.
justification: Injury occurred due to unexpected hose disconnection under pressure, and likelihood is high as no warning or safety measures were provided.

incident_description: I have a Char-Broil COMMERCIAL SERIES LP/PROPANE powered outdoor grill. I grilled beef (Hamburger) on the grill at 600ÃÂº for approximately (24) twenty-four minutes. When I determined that the beef was cooked properly, I closed both of the knob type valves that are fixed on the front of the grill to the closed position,  I opened the bottom storage door to close off the LP/PROPANE valve. Successfully closing off the the ignition source of fuel to the grill and burners, I pulled the beef off of the grate and closed the Stainless looking lid to the closed position and at that point visually the fire was completely extinguished from a visual perspective as well as I could tell.  I walked away from the grill appliance, went inside for approximately (2-3) two or three minutes when I looked outside and the grill appliance was blowing off a mix of dark gray smoke pouring out of the entire upper end of the fire-box with the lid still closed.  I checked the valves a second time making sure that all fuel sources had been completely closed off and they are closed. At this point the grill is on fire.  My next step was to contain the fire as effectively as possible, as I noticed that the thin perforated grate and the upper grill insert that sits inside of the thin perforated grate had caught on fire, I also noticed that the fire was burning below the thin perforated grate as well as burning on the top of the cooking surface.  I successfully extinguished the fire with wet kitchen towels, I used up (4) four towels to put the fire out.  The next day I uncovered the grill to take a look inside. What I found was that the run-off (fat) from the beef as it cooked had built up and baked itself to the thin perforated grate and the insert.  It appears visually like charcoal build up on the cooking surface of this type of grill cooking surface.  The cleaning history on this appliance is it gets the thin perforated grates and inserts pulled out every third time I cook on the grill. In total there are (4) pieces that get cleaned on the cooking surface.  This type of cooking surface gets a visual build up on the grate after (2-3) two or three uses.  I have used this appliance for about (13) months now and this is the first time that the entire firebox and grate had caught on fire after closing off all the fuel sources.  I also notice that on the top of the grate/cooking surface the the words PATENT PENDING are visible.  The good news is that that fire is out and we did not need the Snorkle truck. It was an incident that had serious potential to cause injuries and damages.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire that could have easily escalated, posing a high potential for injury.

incident_description:
Toro snowblower power clear 180 model 38282 serial 311000799
The snowblower is leaking gas.  The 2010 model year was recalled for this problem.  My unit is a 2011 model year and is not included in the recall but has the same issue.
justification: Although not recalled, the 2011 model has the same gas leak issue as the 2010 model, making an incident possible.

incident_description:
My John Deere L-110 Riding lawn tractor was parked in my garage and had not been used in over a week. During the overnite period of May 15, to the morning of May 16, 2011 my three car garage
filled with gasoline vapors to the point that it was unbearable to enter the garage. Had the hot water heater in my garage been a gas type instead of electric my house would have been destroyed by the explosion and ensuing fireball, possibly killing me, my wife and our two children.
 After carefully opening the garage doors manually so as not to create a spark I let the garage air out which took one and a half hours. When it was safe to reenter the garage I traced the gasoline 
vapors to the John Deere. Upon closer examination I could see that the gasoline was leaking out of the lower right side seam of the fuel tank and creating a large puddle under the machine. As well as
filling the garage with a very large volume of vapors.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident could have led to a catastrophic explosion and fire if the water heater was gas-powered.

incident_description:
"Perfect Flame"  Grill Model 720-0335 

I bought this nice looking grill in June 2007.  I used it for about a year and it started giving me problems.  I started having burner issues with it and the grill started burning all of our food.  It was hard to regulate the flame size and keep it at a consistant height. It would not do this all of the time, but about 30% of the time. Sometimes the flames would get REALLY big while cooking on the grill and the flames were hard to contain. I have had a few small fires on the grill that have scared me a little.  I have 3 small kids that I would not even let get near me while cooking because I was scared of what might happen unexpectantly. Now, I am afraid to even use the grill because of the potential fire threat. The last few times I used it a few months ago, if I have one side on and I go to turn on the other side on, the flames in all the burners go from and inch or two down to about 2 cm. The grill won't heat up and cook food properly. The burners were cleaned out and the grill is totally clean.  I am afraid to use it anymore because it might explode or something. So.....I have a nice grill that I paid over $600 dollars for a grill that is a major fire hazard.  It is a death box just looking for a place for an accident to happen. I would like my money refunded! 


The grill was always cleaned after several uses to get rid of food and grime so it would not catch fire. This grill should be recalled and consumers refunded in full. They can even come pick mine up and have it back. NEVER will I buy another one of these grills.
justification: The grill's inconsistent flame size and uncontrollable fires pose a high likelihood of property damage or injury.

incident_description: My Stihl FS 55 weed trimer has a fuel leak at the top of the fuel tank at the rubber grommet. The rubber grommet contains the fuel line and is press-fit into the top of the tank. Gas leaks from the machine making it dangerous and unusable.
justification: Fuel leak poses a fire hazard, making the machine dangerous but unlikely to cause physical injury.

incident_description:
Purchased Husqvarna Rear Wheeled Self Propelled Mower model HU800HW Honda Engine at $399.00 plus tax on or about May 13, 2011.

Returned the mower one week later because the rear wheel were locking, mower could not be pulled backwards, could not be turned.  You were actually stuck and had to shut mower down, lift up the mower and turn around.

I returned the mower to Peerless Power Equipment New Fairfield, Ct., they were shocked to find the mower did this and said no one has had this experience, and they had no idea what could be wrong because it was a brand new machine.  We, both my self and Peerless discovered that the rubber safety flap would get caught up under the rear wheel and lock the wheels completely.  Peerless said the only fix would be to "cut off" half of the rear safety flap.  I didn't want to do this, however, Husqvarna said that is the only way to be able to use it until a "fix" was found.

I hesitantly did what they recommended, the flap was cut in half - I picked up the mower several days later - used it two days ago - June 2nd - the machine is doing the exact same this.  

The balance of the safety flap is getting caught under the rear wheels jamming the the machine.

I contacted Husqvarna left a message for a [REDACTED] (no response) I tried to fax Husqvarna [REDACTED] the fax does not work; I called the customers service department, faxed them a letter never heard from them.

Peerless Power Equipment is getting the mower back today June 10th - I am hoping to get a full refund of $423.95 - this is a very dangerous machine and Husqvarna is not responding.
justification: The incident involved a recurring issue with the mower's safety flap getting caught under the rear wheels, causing the machine to jam and become inoperable.

incident_description: The consumer says the manufacturer sent him an aftermarket part.  He says the universal part fits.  The previous part had no holes.  The one that the manufacturer sent him has holes all around which makes gas leak by the gas valve.  He says the burner itself is not supposed to have any holes to the rear of it, althought this one does and is making gas come out by the body of the valve.  Consumer says he is afraid of using the grill because it may cause a fire.  Consumer says he is having a very hard time trying to contact the manufacturer.
justification: Potential gas leaks due to incorrect aftermarket parts could lead to a fire, posing a significant risk.

incident_description:
I was attempting to light my Sonoma 27" Platinum Edition grill. When doing so, I noticed flames coming from the center control valve, instead of the burner. The other two valves light the burners as they should.

I removed the main burner & valve assembly (part # 40275101) to see if tightening the screws holding the valve to the manifold in place would solve the problem. It did not.

I contacted kaylamillwood@sureheat.com and explained the dangerous situation. I also attached pictures showing the valve on fire. I asked for them to send me a replacement valve & manifold assembly for no charge, as this was a very hazardous condition. Her response was, and I quote:
"I do apologize sir for your inconveniences that you are having with our product."

They want to charge me $60 plus shipping & handling for replacing the very dangerous part of their Sonoma grill.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a dangerous fire from the grill's valve, posing a risk of property damage or injury.

incident_description: I started the grill with 2 of the 5 burners set to high to warm it up. After 6-7 minutes the temp gauge on the lid showed it was ready at the 350-400 degree range. I put two pork chops on the grill and set a timer for 6 minutes before i was ready to flip them.  When the timer went off, my wife went to flip them.  When she raised the lid to the grill, she was given a third degree burn to her left thumb.  Of the 2 burners that were on, one of the knobs had been melted off of the face of the grill body (laying on the patio ground), and the other one was melted but not yet had fallen off.  The front face of the grill and the lower edge of the grill lid are completely black from the burn.  The food was not the issue; when my wife yelled to me that the grill was melting I ran over and moved the food to the side and it was not on fire.  The next step i took was to open the doors underneath and shut off the supply of propane to the grill.  We took pictures of the grill that evening.  Our grill is only a few years old.  We bought it brand new at Sears in Greeley, Colorado.  It has five main burners, one rear infrared burner, and one side warming burner. The model number is 141.16235 and it is rated at 84000 btu total.  The serial number is SU3P009193 with a lot number RS0706.
justification: The grill overheated rapidly due to two burners being set to high, leading to a third-degree burn on the wife's thumb.

incident_description:
Sears Craftsman Mower (Model 536.270280) fuel tank started to leak gas on floor of garage.  Gas tank part number is 7601040.    I first noticed that garage smelled of gas, but it took me two days to see a puddle of gas on the floor of the garage under the mower.  I removed and drained gas tank and filled it with water to check for leaks.  Leak appears to be coming from the hole where Bolt (no. 23) holds tank to mower frame.  
I am wondering if this is related to other Murray manufactured mower fuel tank leaks reported in the news.
justification: No injuries reported, but potential for fire hazard due to gas leak.

incident_description:
I own a Honda Push Mower, Model HRX217HXA, and having serial number MAGA 1045663. I was using the mower to cut the lawn on this date. (I am not that mechanically knowledgeable regarding the mechanics of and the internal workings of the mower parts.) The affected parts of the product, I believe are called the recoil assembly parts. These are the parts that have the pull rope that emanates from the mower that a person would use to pull start the mower. After each pull the rope would retract.

I was operating the mower at the time of the incident and it had been running for approximately 15 minutes at the time of occurrence. 

Suddenly, and without warning, the recoil area of the mower shattered on the inside the mower. This is the top most part of the mower; it has a protective type shroud over this area with horizontal slits about a 1/4 wide. The recoil part that shattered are a type of plastic / composite / or fiberglass.

When the recoil area shattered, it sent the shattered pieces of black / charcoal plastic out through the slits. Unfortunately, most pieces seemed to be directed toward me, the operator. As this occurred, the recoil rope itself, got sucked into the mower's recoil area. As the rope got sucked in, it sheared the rope apart, leaving the pull handle and part of the rope outside the mower. There is a larger piece of shattered black / charcoal stuck in the slits, as it got caught in the same as it was projecting out of this area. A white plastic piece, looks like a small part in its entirety, is also stuck in the slits of the mower, on the side toward the operator.

There was no warning sound associated with the incident. The sound that occurred when this happened was comparable to running a lawn mower over small gravel, as it was the sound of things being chopped ground up, or could be comparable to using a blender to chop ice, nuts or coffee beans. In this case, it was the rotating area in and about the recoil area that was being ground up, upon itself.

At first I thought I had run over something with the mower, because of the sound, and the fact that I got hit with something on my shirt, my eyeglasses and my forehead. I was initially startled, and turned abruptly by the bombardment of objects, which were later determined to be the black / charcoal plastic pieces. I regained my composure and then shut the engine off as fast as i could.

I did sustain a cut on my forehead from one of the projecting plastic pieces and a scratch on my glasses. This was in the same immediate area. It appears that the glasses sustained the brunt of the impact of a projectile, then it sort of glanced off the lens, into my forehead, in the exposed skin area, just under the brim of my hat.

I did collect all the broken pieces, I could find, from the grassy area. Some were found approximately 15 feet from the mower. I did photograph the mower and pieces, and the injury on my forehead. I have not disturbed anything with the mower, since the incident. I did contact Honda Power Equipment by phone, and they advised that there was no recall on this type of problem, and that they were sorry that my mower was not under warranty.

I advised that I was not contacting them about a Warranty Issue, and the call taker,[REDACTED], advised that he would escalate the issue and have [REDACTED], contact me, but it could be up to three days from now. [REDACTED],  subsequently contacted and does want me to take the mower to an authorized Honda Power Equipment Servicing Dealer for Inspection.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the operator, with a cut on the forehead, but no death or serious injury.

incident_description: I HAVE A CUB CADET RZT50 ZERO TURN RIDING MOWER,WHICH I PURCHASED 4/24/090. HAVE NOT HAD ANY PROBLEMS UNTIL TODAY. WHEN STARTING TO MOW, YOU HAVE TO PUSH THE CONTROL ARMS FORWARD TO GO FORWARD AND BACK TO BACKWARD. THIS ALSO IS YOU STEERING CONTROL. THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE CONTROLS DO NOT RESPOND AND THE MACHINE EITHER WILL NOT WANT TO GO AT ALL OR YOU ARE UNABLE TO PROPERLY CONTROL THE STEERING AS YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO. THIS UNIT HAS ONLY 126 OPERATING HOURS OF USE SINCE I PURCHASED IT NEW, HAS BEEN SERVICES AT REGULAR INTERVALS AND MAINTAINED PROPERLY, AS WELL AS BEING KEPT INSIDE WHILE NOT IN USE. WITH THE STEERING AND CONTROL NOT WORKING PROPERLY, THIS COULD CREATE A VERY DANGEROUS SITUATION FOR THE OPERATOR OR ANY ONE WHO MAY BE STANDING NEAR THE MACHINE, DUE TO NOT BEING ABLE TO CONTROL THE OPERATION OF THE UNIT. HAVE CONTACTED THE MANUFACTURER, AND AM HOPING TO GET SOME RESULTS THROUGH WARRANTY, BUT NOT SURE IF THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED.
justification: Although no injury has occurred yet, the malfunctioning controls pose a high risk of injury or accident, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
While using a Stihl FS75 weedeater over the past 2 yrs  , I have burnt my right arm several times on the engine cover  covering the muffler.
Each time the the burn is about the size of a m&m to about the size of a dime.
Also I have been weedeating on a hill side and after 30min or more..
I just sent Stihl a email concerning this same problem... asking them if have had any complaints or a correction to this problem.
justification: Repeated burns on the arm, with sizes ranging from a small to a dime, indicate an injury has occurred.

incident_description:
We had Progreen arifical turf R69F dog turf installed in our yard in April 2100.
Prior to installing the turf we asked numerous questions including if the turf got hot.
We were told it gets warm, slightly warmer than natural grass. But never hot enough
to cause a problem or prevent usage.
A few weeks later  when the temperature started to warm up so did the turf.
Not hot but very warm. I placed a call to the company and was told to give it a little drink of
water and it would cool off. I questioned if it was going to get so hot we couldn' t use  it and 
was assured it would not.
Memorial weekend the temps hit the 80's and the turf was to hot to walk on for us or our 
dog. It does cool for a brief peroid after watering but then heats back up.
As the temperature continues to climb so does the turfs temperature.
This is truly a safety issue for pets and people. There was no warning in the literature 
nor were we told it is not safe for sunny areas. Now several thousand dollars later 
I am worried if my dog or relatives will sustain a burn from this.
justification: The turf's high temperature, reaching unsafe levels in warm weather, poses a risk of burns to both people and pets.

incident_description: I purchased a precise fit 17 cu foot steel dump cart from Lowes home improvement stores in Killingly CT.  After a week, both tires had dry rot cracks and would not hold air.  I called for a replacement set.  They sent me a replacement set.  Both wheels have dents from the tire mounting process.  When using I had a tire blow out which caused the trailer to flip and the lawn tractor to wheel up on me.  Upon checking, both of the new tires are cracked and dry rotted.  This has been stored under an enclosed garage and not exposed to the sun.
justification: Tire blowout caused trailer flip, leading to potential injury.

incident_description: I used a new Sears Craftsman lawnmower model #37455 for the first time on June 2, 2011.  After using it for approximately 90 minutes in which it functioned normally, the engine made a loud pop, the oil was shaken loose, oil sprayed all over the mower deck, and smoke poured out of the engine.  No injuries were sustained.
justification: While no injuries were sustained, the incident resulted in significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
My Snapper Pro S150X Commercial Zero Turn Lawn Mower burst into flames, with me sitting on it. I had turned around to go in reverse and the flames were right in my face, directly behind the seat. I had been on it less than 5 minutes.I jumped off immediately, realizing that it was full of gasoline. I ran to the house to call 911, the fire department came. There was no warning at all. It was a well taken care of, immaculate machine, documented by the dealer.We paid $7000.00 for it and had it not quite 3 years . I loved that machine (I called it the Mighty Mowing Machine) and never allowed anyone to use it but me. My husband kept it clean for me. I have no idea why I didn't burn up with it. Had I not turned around at that precise moment, I would have caught on fire. When I ran to the house, I turned around to look at it and the seat was enveloped in flames. This was a major malfunction with dangerous consequences for consumers. The cause should be investigated. The mower was picked up by our dealer who has talked to Snapper/Briggs & Stratton over 50 times to discuss the situation with them. SnapperPro/Briggs & Stratton seem to think that they have no product responsibility. The engine was Kawasaki. I looked on your web-site to see if there had been a re-call that I was not made aware of, and there doesn't seem to be. Our purchase was well documented and had there been a re-call, Snapper would not have had any problem notifying us.
My husband and I are just sick about this and think it very important that consumers are made aware of the danger we experienced with this product.
We asked Snapper if they had sent a representative to investigate the cause of the fire.  They said they  had not. Apparently, they don't want to know the cause.
justification: The incident resulted in potential severe injury, with flames directly in the user's face, and the likelihood of such a sudden and severe malfunction is high.

incident_description: The decals that indicates the different cooking tempeatures and the warning for hot surfaces just peels off because the panel is right on the heating area. After just 5 uses I can't tell any settings. The decals are a thin plastic layer that simply fall of in pieces. This are the indicators for all knobs and the warning for hot surfaces.
justification: The incident is likely to occur again due to the poor design and material of the decals, leading to a loss of functionality but no immediate injury.

incident_description:
I bought a Perfect Flame SLG2007A from Lowe's a few years ago.  A few weeks ago, the grill caught on fire and flames shot out the hole on the right side.  The flames melted the plastic/molding on the right side of the lid and it is bubbled.  The paint on the inside of the lid also peeled from the 800+ degree temperatures.  It appears that the burners have deteriorated, but they still work.  The flames burn much higher than they should.  I just determined that there was a product recall and you indicated that you would still like incidents reported.

I turned the grill on and left it unattended for five minutes while I went upstairs.  I came back down and the flames were shooting out the right side of the grill.  The temperature gauge was at the maxumum.  I threw water on the flames to get the fire out.  There was also some bright glowing material that continued to glow after I put water on it.  I put some more water on it and it stopped glowing.  No injuries.
justification: The grill's burners deteriorated, leading to uncontrolled flames and potential injury.

incident_description: I was grilling and my grill caught fire.  It caught fire so quickly that it burned the gas line and started burning.  It burned the gas line, the ignitor, the hoses and the handles before we could turn off the gas, it almost caught our back porch on fire in the process. I visited Lowe's today and the salesman told me about the recall on Perfect Flame Grills that we were not yet aware of.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the rapid spread of the fire and potential damage to the back porch warrant a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Char-Broil Grill MOdel 463212511

During assembly, a razor-sharp edge on one of parts sliced deeply into the interthenar region (flexible area between fingers) between my thumb and first finger of the left hand.  I had been reading the instructions - no warning of such surfaces or need to wear gloves.

I've stopped the bleeding but as a surgeon, I'm out of commission for a while.

I'd strongly suggest a 'black box' warning that there are sharp surfaces and that gloves should be worn.  As most people do not read the instruction manual before they start unpacking items (all I was doing was unpacking the box), the black box warning must be on the top of the box that the grill comes in.

The injury is fairly significant.  It's in a very challenging location.  Strongly recommend contact with the manufacturer to remedy this.

I've notified the manufacturer at their web site and Target Stores where it was purchased as well.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the lack of warning about sharp edges and the common practice of not reading instructions before assembly.

incident_description:
Toro 180 powerclear snow blower purchased Nov 2010 at a local Home Depot started leaking a large amount of fuel while sitting unused. Serial # is outside of range in previous recall but unit appears to have exact same problem as noted in recall. It appears that published serial number range may not include all affected units. This is a serious fire hazard.

Model # 38282
Serial #311022272
justification: Potential fire hazard due to fuel leak, with likelihood of recurrence high given the unit's serial number is outside the previously recalled range.

incident_description: When preparing my Defender mosquito magnet for storage, I attempted to use the quick-clear valve with a CO2 cylinder.  It malfunctioned, releasing CO2 as I tried to assemble it.  I tried a second time, thinking the cylinder was defective.  The result was the same, so I put the mosquito magnet away for the winter without clearing the fuel line.  When I went to the website to purchase a new quick-clear valve this spring, I discovered the recall.  I was not injured, only startled by the sudden release of the CO2.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a malfunctioning product, making it an incident.

incident_description:
I just noticed a recall of the Stihl backpack blowers.  I have one of these, Model BR550.  On at least 2 occasions, I filled the unit with gasoline, replaced the fuel cap which seemed to go on oddly but looked tight.  After starting the unit and putting it up on my back, I felt gasoline spilling down my leg.  As an emergency physician myself, I decided on the second event to quit using the unit and took it to the local dealer and complained.  He acted like he knew there was a problem and immediately replaced the gas cap.  This was last fall.  This seems to have corrected the problem.

I am thankful that this is being recalled before someone gets badly burned by this defect; however, Stihl should have a MANDATORY recall of these products.  If any questions, give me a call.

[REDACTED]
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the potential for burns due to gasoline leakage is high, as evidenced by the user's experience.

incident_description: My safety concern is with the Toro 22 inch Recycler Mower (Model 20067). The seam around the gas tank leaks alot. You can only put about a quarter tank of gas in order to avoid it leaking. My concern that this could be a serious safety hazard. We have only had the mower since July 2009.
justification: Leaking gas poses a fire hazard, and limiting gas capacity reduces the mower's usability.

incident_description:
On April 29, 2011 I purchased a H. D. Hudson 27912 Pumpless Sprayer (http://www.hdhudson.com/product-search/product-details/?id=43) from Menards in Long Grove, IL. On May 1, 2011 I filled my Hudson 27912 with Ortho Weed B Gon MAX - Weed Killer For Lawns Concentrate (http://www.scotts.com/smg/catalog/productTemplate.jsp?proId=prod70196&itemId=cat50064) then I filled and pressurized the sprayer using a garage hose exactly as in the instruction manual (see URL below for the manual). When the tank was full I removed the hose quick disconnect from the tank and was sprayer with the high pressure solution of  Ortho Weed B Gon MAX and water from inside the sprayer. The Ortho Weed B Gon MAX and water solution was released because the check ball was missing from the fill nipple connector. After being sprayer with the contents of the sprayer I took a thorough shower and flushed my eyes. After investigating the active ingredients Ortho Weed B Gon MAX I don't think there will be any long-term consequences of being sprayer but I could have been using a more caustic or poisonous herbicide/pesticide. My fear is that many of these sprayers could have been manufactured incorrectly and others could be sprayed with poisonous chemicals.

http://www.hdhudson.com/components/com_catalog/documents/product-instructions/product-instructions-4d751ce82de12.pdf
justification: The incident resulted in potential exposure to harmful chemicals, but no immediate injuries were reported.

incident_description: Consumer reports gas grill does not ignite per manufacturer's instructions & believe's the unit is unsafe.  Consumer had to try the igniter 15-20 times instead of the 2 times per manufacturer instruction in order for the unit to ignite resulting in a gas buildup.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident of a gas grill not igniting as intended and requiring multiple attempts, leading to a gas buildup, is concerning and could potentially escalate to a more severe incident.

incident_description: The burners on the grill are pealing apart at the rear of the grill. This appears to be the same issue other, already recalled models have had.
justification: The grill's burners peeling apart is an incident that could potentially cause a fire, but no injuries or deaths have been reported yet.

incident_description: The consumer says he was cooking when the unit got so hot he couldnt go near it.  Consumer says it burned his hand and his neck.  Consumer says the knobs were no hot they are welded open and he could not turn them off.  The consumer says the manufacturer sent an inspector to view the unit.  The manufacturer told him his grill was dirty and did not offer any assistance.  Consumer has same product as Release #06-174.  He says the manufacturer has pictures of unit and documents of incident.
justification: Consumer suffered burns on hand and neck, indicating a severe injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high as the consumer was able to replicate the issue and the manufacturer's inspector confirmed the unit's condition.

incident_description: Motor Impellor broke on a Sears Craftsman electric blower, Model nmber 138.748270, Sears part number 100-9068. When I tried to order a new part, Sears parts told me that they could not sell the part as it had been recalled by the vendor, Toro. Checking your site, the Sears website and Toro's website, I can find no notice of recall or alert to the public of the danger this part could produce. Sears exchanged my blower for a new one.
justification: Although no injury was reported, the incident could have caused harm due to the impellor breaking, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
(5/1/11)  The consumer is filing the report on behalf of her adult son, who actually owns the grill.

The grill had been in use for approximately 5 - 10 minutes, when it caught fire.

The son noticed that the front portion of the grill was hotter than it normally is.  The consumer noticed that flames began to emit from 2 of the control knobs.  There are 6 knobs in all.  The son turned the propane tank "off" and removed it from underneath the grill.  It took a few minutes for the flames to extinguish themselves.  Some of the control knobs melted as a result of this fire.

The front of the grill also became discolored as a result of this incident.  There were no injuries.  Damage was limited to the grill itself.

The son paid $650.00 for the grill at the time that it was purchased.

Same day, the consumer and her son went to the retailer about this matter. The retailer's rep. told the consumer that they were not aware of this problem happening before with their brand of grills.  The rep. looked up the parts that would need to be replaced and it would cost around $300.00 to replace these parts.  The consumer said that they were not interested in spending that amount of money on the grill.  The retailer's rep. did not offer anything else to the consumers.
justification: Although the grill caught fire, there were no injuries, hence severity level 2.

incident_description: I have a 2005 Cub Cadet RZT 50 (180 hrs) riding mower with independent hydrstatic transmissions. The transmissions over heat and loose power. Three incidences: First-I was cutting near my pond and the left transmission failed, which nearly sent me down the hill and into the pond.  Second-I was cutting near the road and the right transmission lost power, which sent me out into the road. Luckily, my neighbor was coming home and moved over considerably or I would have slammed into his [REDACTED] truck.  Third-I was cutting near my childrens playset while my son was up in the structure and the left transmission failed, which sent me into the play set and scared us both.  We are so lucky that the playset is built out of 4x4's and treated wood and I anchored it into the ground to keep it from tipping over when they swing.
justification: Multiple near-miss incidents with potential for serious injury, despite no actual injuries occurring.

incident_description: Plastic gas tank on lawn mower cracks leaking gasoline
justification: Gasoline leak poses a fire hazard but no immediate injury risk.

incident_description:
Caller was mowing his land today and when he came to a stop, disengaged blade and started to step off but then noticed that the dicharge chute was missing. 
His foot was within possibley an inch or two from stepping in hole with spinning blade.
He pulled his foot back up and got off mower on the opposite side.
Caller states that some of his grandchildren cut his grass with this mower sometimes to mow his yard and if this had happened while they were on the mower they may not have noticed the problem that had occurred while mowing.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a near-miss with a spinning blade, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Gas grill is repeatedly hard to ignite using built-in electronic ignition.  Once the grill does light up, it usually generates a small fireball.  Upon further inspection, all four burners were found to be cracked and allowing one large flame to be generated at the end of the burner.
justification: Repeated ignition issues and large flames pose a high risk of property damage or injury.

incident_description:
I was grilling and my grill caught on fire.  The lid caught fire, the coating started to melt, the coating caught fire and it melted part of the framing on the grill.

I have tried to contact Lowes as well as Perfect Flame and I am not getting anything but problems.

I have provided them with 21 pictures of the grill.

The burner has a hole in it and this appears to be what caused the fire to start with.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, and while grill fires are possible, they are not common.

incident_description: Bird Brain fire pot was used for first time with bird brain fire pot fire gel.  Gel was placed in steel container in ceramic decorative pot and lit in accordance with instructions.  Pot was placed in middle of a table on back patio which was 40 or more inches wide and 31 inches deep.  Consumer seated next to table with dog laying at feet.  Gel was burning for some time before it exploded.  Consumer was spared, but dog was struck, and caught fire.  Table caught fire and gel landing on concrete patio burned for up to 15 minutes.  Dog ran and caught some grass and plants on fire in yard.  Entered house and ignited some of interior before being caught and fire extinguished.  Fire Department responded and reported.  Dog in critical condition with 3rd degree burns over 35% of body at UC Davis Veterinary Hospital, Davis, California.  Bills approaching $12,000.
justification: Dog suffered severe burns (35% of body) and is in critical condition, despite consumer's careful use of the product.

incident_description:
Ride on mower purchased Summer of 2005, no problems until Summer of 2008.
Summer of 2008 anything caught in clipping catcher would fly out catching are whether it was on or not.
Seat should be engaged when sitting on seat and disengage when getting off but it wasn't working thereby posing a safety hazard to rider and anyone nearby.

Summer of 2010 ride one lawnmower would no longer turn on with key, caller repaired ingnition in this case.
Summer of 2010 the hoses that go from the fuel pump to the gas tank were leaking, caller's husband repaired these.

Safety issue posed is constant repair of small issues that could present themselves as hazards.

Caller has noted that many do not have the capacity to repair and could be in danger if any of these issues were to go unnoticed or not repaired and would like this lawnmower replaced or repaired at either retailer or manufacturer expense.
justification: The recurring issues with the lawnmower, such as the seat not disengaging and fuel hoses leaking, pose a high likelihood of incidents leading to injuries.

incident_description:
Failure of a Weber Genesis E-320
I am writing to notify you of a serious problem I experienced with my Weber Genesis E-320 on April 16, 2011.
 
The lower left side of the grill melted! 
 
I donÃÂt really know how to explain what happened, except to say that the aluminum casing has a very large hole in it, and that there are dried puddles of aluminum in the bottom of my grill. This causes me great concern as aluminum has a melting point of over 1200 degrees Fahrenheit.  How can a grill get that hot? How can this be safe?

incident_description: Homelite backpack blower was leaking gasoline.  We contacted the company last year about this and they did not tell us there was a recall.  We went to use it this season and once again when my husband has it on his back it leaked gasoline all over his clothes.  After calling the company a second time we were told to take it in for repairs but were still never informed that this was a recall.  I learned myself it was a recall when doing research online.  It ruined the clothes he was wearing.  We were unable to get the gasoline smell out.
justification: The incident occurred twice, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

Consumer feels that the tank on the lawnmower is a potential fire hazard and should be reported.

Carburetor leak just like other recalled products

justification: Gasoline leak poses a significant fire risk, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We purchased a Perfect Flame propane grill, Model Number GAC-3615, from Lowes in the summer of 2008. The grill has always been kept clean and covered, but I noticed that the burners were beginning to deteriorate and it was beginning to heat unevenly. On Monday, 5/9/11, we lit the grill to pre-heat it. Within 5 minutes smoke was pouring from under the lid of the grill and flames were coming from the back of the lid at least 18 inches above the lid. We immediately turned off the burners, and a neighbor with a fire extinguisher ran over and helped put out the fire before it could spread to our deck and/or house. Upon inspection afterward, it actually appears that the lining of the cooking chamber and lid may have been burning, and metal from both has peeled away from the intense heat while the fire was burning. I contacted Lowe's and have been offered a replacement grill.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire that could have spread to the deck or house, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
Kobalt Hatchet - purchased at Lowe's April 23, 2011.
Used hatchet immediately after purchase to chop shrub roots.  After 30-40 swings the head detached from the handle and landed several feet away.  Fortunately I was not struck and no one else was nearby.
justification: The hatchet head detaching after use, though not causing injury, indicates a potential manufacturing defect, making it possible for such an incident to occur again.

incident_description:
Homelite UT10518  46cc Chainsaw   manf date  03/01/08

Using this saw for about the 3rd time, it has seen very little use.  Today when using the saw, it worked ok for a few minutes then I turned it off,  upon restart the fast idle would run at almost full power,  attempted to adjust the fast idle screw to no avail,  no change at all to the idle speed with any of the adjustments I made. Also when running at this fast idle  the power off switch will not power off the saw,  I have to use the choke to kill it.  Very unsafe!!!!   Again this saw has seen very little use!  What can be done about this?   I reviewed the Internet and have notice a number of other people having the same issue with their Homelite saws with the same model number.  Due to the safety issues (racing idle and power off switch), sounds like a recall should be made.
justification: The saw's fast idle running at almost full power and the power off switch not working pose a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: Drain panel rusted through with holes that allow hot grease to drip onto the ground and fuel tank. Also the heat diffusers at the top of the burners are starting to rust through, this will cause flare ups. This grill is only 2 years old. Sears Kenmore Model #146.16222010
justification: Rust holes in the drain panel and heat diffusers pose a high likelihood of grease fires and flare-ups, potentially leading to property damage and injuries.

incident_description: Gas tank leaking.  Sears/Craftsman Garden Tractor model 917.275010, purchased 4/02.  No previous problems, but when put into operation for the 2011 season,  gas immediately started to leak out of the tank.  Have not taken the tractor apart to get to the tank yet to determine the location of the leak, but it is on the right side of the tank.  The tank is located beneath the seat, in the rear of the tractor.  The leak is profuse, rendering the tractor unusable.

incident_description: cub cadet zero turn lawnmower, caught on fire due to electrical problem, minor burn to left hand.
justification: Injury occurred due to electrical fire, but not life-threatening.

incident_description:
I purchased a Toro 22in Recycler Lawn Mower, Model no. 20331, in May 2009. I used the mower for the summer and into October. I then stored the mower for the winter following explicitly the instructions on page 15 of the Operator's Manual "Preparing the Mower for Storage." This included using fuel stabilizer for the last refueling and running the mower until the engine stops from running out of fuel. I also disconnected the spark plug wire, removed the spark plug and added oil as specified. The mower was then stored in a cool, clean, dry place.
On the first use in spring, 2010, as I filled the tank with gasoline, it ran straight through the fuel tank and carburetor and onto the deck of the mower. All of the fuel immediately ran out and over the mower deck and onto the ground.
As the mower was still under warranty, I contacted my retailer and was directed to an authorized repair shop. The repair needed was a new carburetor. It now works fine.
I had no idea what had caused this to happen. Then last week I heard about the recall of the Toro snowblowers and lawnmowers due to carburetor leaks and fuel spills affecting units manufactured between September 2009 and March 2011. Visiting the CPSC web site, I read release #11-207 dated April 26, 2011 and learned that the recall for the exact same issue I experienced does not include my mower. The recall is for Model no. 20323 (mine is 20331) and a 20in mower (mine is 22in). Is the same defective carburetor used on other models, including mine?
justification: Although no injury occurred, the fuel spill posed a potential fire hazard, making it an incident with a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
On 27 April 2011 I purchased a "2-pack mini engine flashlight set" at the Home Depot store here in Tehachapi, CA 93561, where I live, at 21208 Mountain Drive.  My name is [redacted], a mature adult male.  The two flashlights feature very bright LED bulbs (that is not the problem), and the package directions require opening the flashlight and removing a cardboard tab which prevents accidentally turning on the flashlight.  I noticed immediately that the front end of the flashlight features seven machined grooves in the aluminum housing, and the edges are sharp.  But how sharp I did not realize until I had opened the flashlight and removed the tab, and closed the flashlight again.  Then I saw that it had inflicted a slice across the tip of my left forefinger; there was blood on my hand, the flashlight and the table.  As I write this, late on 3 May, the finger is still sore, and I have to keep a bandaid on it to protect the wound.  It may seem slight, but the probability of being cut by use of this flashlight is EXTREMELY high.  
The flashlights are manufactured in China, and distributed in the U.S. by Iron Bridge Tools, Inc.
624 S. Military Trail, Deerfield Beach, FL 33442 Tel (954) 596 8712
justification: The sharp edges of the flashlight caused an injury, and the design flaw increases the likelihood of this happening again.

incident_description:
After having the ride on mower for approxiametly 13 months he began to notice that there was a crack on the gasoline tank and when there was atleast half a tank of gasoline in the tank the gasoline would leak out.

One occassion after attempting to start the mower he noticed that it would not start he then looked down at the gas tank and it was leaking gasoline. He noticed that the tank had several cracks on it and since he was hosing the mower down very regularly water had leaked into the gasoline tank.

The gas tank is located underneath the seat  where there is a little opening so that you can see how much gasoline is in the 

He had an appointment with the retailer to have the gasoline tank repaired 3/2011 and no one has showed up to make the repairs. He still currently uses  the mower but he only puts half a gallon of gasoline in the tank.
justification: Gasoline leaks pose a fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description: The consumer says that the fuel tank in the lawn mower leaks.  Consumer says the unit poses a fire hazard because the fuel tank cracks and is defective.  Consumer contacted the manufacturer and they told him it is not under warranty and there is nothing they can do.  The consumer said the retailer notified him that its not the their responsibility to notify anyone of a recall if they didnt purchase an extended warranty.  Consumer wants to know where the tank was made.

incident_description:
Hello, I bought a wood chipper from an online retailer - GudCraftOnline - through an Amazon link.

Retailer: www.GudCraftOnline.com

I've only used it twice and the second time a piece of metal popped out inside of it while it was running, causing major damage to the chipper and blades, and riking my life in the process.

I tried to get the manufacturer's information from GudCraftOnline but they responded with the following:
--------------
Date: Fri, 15 Apr 2011 12:57:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Warranty on Wood Chipper 
From: [REDACTED]
To: [REDACTED]
No sorry, we do not provide manufacture information. Sorry.
--------------

This incident as it was very dangerous, and could have ended up badly had the metal pieces escaped from the entry point into the chipper.  Luckily they hit the insides, and then I turned the chipper off.  But in that short time they made big dents on all sides on the chipper popped the whole metal plates off one another...  Had the piece of metal been flung by the blade in the direction of the opening, it would have hit me straight in the face/head and at the speed it was being spun, I'm certain it could have caused my death. If you see the pictures of the piece of metal and what became of it and of the wood chipper, you'll understand.

http://www.gudcraftonline.com/SearchResults.asp?Cat=31
justification: Metal debris was propelled at high speed, causing significant damage and posing a high risk of serious injury or death.

incident_description:
While attempting to brake while in the higher gear range the brake pedal, which had shifted position, would not push down when foot pressure was applied.  It is a design flaw.  You have to reposition your foot and push up and forward to pass the center point and then down.

In the lower gear range the pedal does not reposition itself, or not as radically and a normal foot position and pressure activates the brake system.

Having to apply foot pressure in the two different styles creates a hazard.  

The Sears riding mower  model is 247.288811.  It is a 2011 model.  Sears has been notified.
justification: The design flaw in the brake pedal increases the likelihood of an incident, but the incident described resulted in no injury.

incident_description:
Back on November 15,2010 I took my Stinger Electronic Insect killer down to clean it before putting it up for the winter. Since this model UVB45 has a device on it that will make it come on when it get dark and turn it off when it get light, I wanted to see why it was staying on all the time.

I opened the top up and discovered that their is a small circuit board directly below the light that stays on all the time and the one that detects when it gets dark enough for the unit to come on.

The main current comes into this circuit board, their is nothing to waterproof this board. My board is rusted and when I look on the box I discovered that this bug killer has a warranty of 3 years.

I put the unit back together and sent an e-mail to the company that made it,Kaz and received an e-mail stating that since I opened it, it vodes the warranty and that the unit is not waterproof and can only withstand light rain, that they are not waterproof and during heavy rain, they should be removed to a dry place.


There is nothing on my circuit to protect the circuit board, nothing to even keep the moisture out. and since their is a shock hazard when it get wet, I feel the thing is unsafe.

This unit came from Wal-mart and was made by Kaz Inc., Southborough , MA
justification: The insect killer's lack of waterproofing and shock hazard during heavy rain poses a high likelihood of an incident, although no injuries were reported.

I have a Toro Recycler mower, model #20037, which has the exact same problem.  Fuel leaks from the carburetors when I fill the tank with gas.

Related to the recent Toro reclass on Power Clear Snowblower:

The failed carburetors caused a spill of about 2 gallons of fuel all over my garage and driveway.  I took it for repairs to a Toro retailer, and claimed to have fixed it. John Deere Riding Lawn Tractor Model GXL 100a  ID# 181580. Estimated hours in use 400

incident_description: One month ago I purchased a Craftsman YT4000 Lawn Tractor. For the most part I'm happy with the product. But I've noticed that the backs of the spokes are hollow and uncomfortable when turning the tractor. Today I was dismounting to open the gate to my backyard when my finger became caught in one of the open spaces under the steering wheel spokes. Somehow my finger got stuck but I kept going. I tore a chunk out of my index finger and thought for a few moments that I'd broken it. I called Sears to find out of a safer steering wheel was available. Not only is no replacement available but no one seemed interested in correcting what I consider to be a hazard.

incident_description: We purchased a Nickelodeon SpongeBob Squarepants Projector flashlight from our local Wal-mart in Albuquerque, NM. We gave this to our grandson inside of his Easter basket. We installed two new Duracell Coppertop "C" batteries in flashlight. He played with it for about 15 minutes or so, and it would no longer light up. Thinking possibly the batteries were bad we changed them out again. The light still would not work. We placed the light to the side to be returned to Wal-mart at a later date. Approximately a hour and a half later I went to move the light, as it was in my way, and discovered that the plastic case was extremely hot to the touch. I picked up light and there was a burn mark where the light had been setting on the table. I opened the light to remove the batteries and discovered that they had exploded inside the plastic flashlight tube. It was leaking battery fluid throughout the flashlight and was seeping out of the light in several different places. I did document this with photos for future reference. I have no doubt, that if we had not been home, a serious fire could have ensued.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a potential fire hazard due to battery explosion, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:

Called the dealer on 3/29/11 and they picked it up and it is still in their possession.

incident_description:
My husband was digging out a shrub in our backyard with a 1 year old YardWorks brand shovel.  As he was pushing down on the shovel to lift the small shrub out of the hole the shovel snapped in half and hit him in the face.  He was fortunate that his teeth, nose, eyes were okay.  He had a laceration that went all the way through his lower lip.  We called 911 and went to the emergency room where required 15 stitches.  

I am just concerned about this shovel since it wasn't old (we had it for only one year).  Also, he wasn't misusing the shovel or exerting an unusual amount of force.  He had dug around the shrub and loosened it to the point that it simply needed to be propped out of the hole.  

We still have the shovel and can take a picture of it if needed.

I hope this was an isolated incident but I also don't want this to happen to anyone else.  Thank you.
justification: The shovel snapped unexpectedly, causing an injury that required stitches, but no serious facial damage.

incident_description:
On 4/9/11, I started the grill without incident.  Turned knob on tank to allow gas flow, opened lid, turned bottom burner dial which controls front burner on, pushed ignite button.  Font burner ignited normally, and I turned the back dial to ignite the back burner, which also lit normally.  
Closed lid to allow grill to preheat.  Returned after about 10 minutes to place chicken breast (placed on tin foil) on grill.  Didn't notice anything abnormal.  Close lid.
Returned after 7 minutes to turn chicken.  Smelled a "hot" smell, didn't notice anything abnormal, and assumed it was something burning off the grill grates.  Turned my chicken, went back into the house.
Returned after 7 more minutes to retrieve the chicken.  "Hot" smell was stronger.  Looked down at controls to see that front burner dial, as well as igniter button, were both melted. Looked underneath to see a flame burning under those controls.
Immediately turned the back burner knob off, turned knob to stop gas flow from tank, blew out flame, and opened the lid.  Flame was out. I disconnected the hose attaching the tank with the grill. I watched it for a few minutes to be sure the flame would not ignite, and then left the grill.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to melted controls and an underlying flame, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
I was preheating a month old Master Forge grill, model SH3118B, and noticed low heat even though the 3 main burners were on high, there wasn't much flame or heat. The grill had been used several times before and had functioned satisfactorily.  Suspecting low fuel in the LP cylinder I turned off the grill to replaced the cylinder. Removing the original cylinder, I noted that it was heavy and should have had plenty of fuel, but I replaced the cylinder anyway.
  The second cylinder did not change the operation of the grill, the flame was still low and not producing much heat.  I knelt down and opened the front cabinet of the grill.  Suspecting a regulator or hose issue at this point I quickly looked at the regulator to see if it was possibly venting fuel, and reached to move the hose that goes from the regulator to the grill to see if it was kinked.  I was planing to immediately turn off the grill if any discrepancies were noticed but I didn't get a chance.  As I reached into the compartment and moved the hose, the upper right area of the lower cylinder storage compartment erupted in flames.
  Fire quickly engulfed the compartment, LP cylinder, and the front of the grill.  I started to go inside for an extinguisher or welding gloves to protect me against the flames ,but the flames grew and I was afraid that they would ignite a nearby umbrella and then my deck/house.
  The flames and heat grew inside the compartment and I was hesitant to try to turn off the tank because the tank valve handle was extremely hot at this point.  Expecting that the excess flow valve on the tank would shut off the gas flow if the tank was disconnected, I removed my outer shirt and wrapped it around my hand and arm.  Reaching for the quick connector on the tank, I unscrewed the grill to tank connection, sustaining 2nd degree burns on my right arm.
  At this point the tank valve apparently failed and the tank caught on fire from the unrestricted LP exiting the valve.  Due to extreme heat and flames, and burns I had already sustained, I threw the burning tank off of my deck into the yard.
  While attempting to control the burning tank away from the house I sustained further 1st and 2nd degree burns to my face, forehead, and arms requiring treatment in the ER.
justification: Injury occurred due to flames erupting from the grill compartment, causing second-degree burns.

incident_description: I purchased a Lowe's Portfolio brand "Oval Deck Light" model #0048398.The pictures on the box show the light mounted on a deck upright. After opening the box, I found a label on the light and a note in the instructions that the light was "for ceiling use only." The Lighting Departmment manager at the Lowe's I bought the light from advised me that if I installed the light as pictured on the box, it probably would catch on fire.
