justification: The broken safety trigger could cause the unit to turn on unexpectedly, posing a risk of injury.

incident_description: I have a self propelled Cub Cadet lawnmower Model # 12AE18JA056, Serial # 1C278K30360 which is approximately four years old now.  Last July (product was only three years old then), while mowing my yard, a bolt sheared that connects the self propel wire to the drive.  Literally sheared - clean and in half. Thankfully, I had pants on so when it came back it did not cut my legs.  Sure jerked my shoulders tho when all of a sudden I was trying to push the thing with no self propel.  I contacted Cub Cadet about fixing it since it was obviously a product flaw and posed a hazard; I offered to send in photosbut they didn't want them.  The Customer Care agent told me he knew exactly what part I was talking about just by my description (sure makes me think they have had other issues) but refused to do anything because I could not provide my purchase receipt altho I knew it had been bought at Home Depot.

incident_description: The gas cap on a Poulan Pro PP3516AVX chainsaw swelled and became stuck in the tank opening. A great deal of force was required to remove the cap of the tank which still contained some fuel. Once open, the cap cannot be replaced exposing the fuel and fumes to the hot motor and creating a spill hazard. I contacted the company and they did not offer a repair or suggestion other than to buy a replacement cap. The repair shop informed me that they are selling a large number of the caps for the same reason. The replacement cap, at $8.95 apiece, lasted for two tanks of fuel before repeating the problem. The repair shop suggested that the ethanol in the fuel causes the plastic to deform and there are no caps currently available in another material.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but caused a spill hazard, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' scenario.

incident_description:
I have owned a Chapin Mfg. model 20000 (one gallon) sprayer for one year. In that time i have used it about eight times.

Yesterday i pulled it out to spray Roundup weed/vegetation killer. I had one gallon of mix in the sprayer and had sprayed weeds for about 10 minutes and used about 1/3 of the mixture. The pressure was running low(i normally dont run the thing at a very high pressure because im just spraying weeds at my feet) and i bent over the sprayer to pump the handle....the sprayer suddenly released pressure around the collar of the handle...basically exploding upward and sending about 12-16 ounces of weed/vegetation killer up into my face,
neck and shirt and pants. The sprayer will no longer pressurize. i figured i had the pressure at about 75% when it exploded. 

I havent suffered any short term affects from the weed killer but im concerned that other people with this sprayer could end up being injured, possibly blinded by a similar event. I was fortunate enough to have closed my eyes when the Roundup Weed/Vegetation Killer mixture hit me. 

I can understand CHEAP sprayers...they dont get used very often....but i cant understand DANGEROUS sprayers. I have been using sprayers for many years and never encountered a problem like this. This is a DANGEROUS SPRAYER.
justification: The sprayer suddenly released pressure, causing a significant amount of weed killer to be expelled, which could lead to serious injuries, including eye damage or chemical burns.

incident_description:
This tractor body has cracked and rusted around the seat bolts after only 500 hours of use. New Holland Agriculture has offerred that they have an option to reinforce the issue as they are aware of it. This part needs to be welded on. The metal itself is defective and has corroded under the seat which has created a potential life threatening issue if the seat collapses from further metal decay. The metal was clearly not designed to hold the weight of the driver.

Tractor Model New Holland #TZ24DA

Purchased and garaged since 8/2004.

Purchased from New Holland Dealer: Theros Equipment in Sterling, VA
justification: The severe corrosion and cracking of the tractor body poses a high risk of the seat collapsing, potentially leading to driver injury.

incident_description:
I have a Toro Power Clear 180 Snowthrower Model #38282.  I purchased it from Home Depot on November 2, 2010.  When not in use, it was stored in my garage.  I began noticing an odor of gasoline in the garage after it was used.  The odor dissapated in a few hours.  As it seemed that there would be no need to use it for this year, I intended to prepare the snowthrower to be stored until next winter as per the directions in the Toro manual.  Approximately one week ago, the odor of gasoline got stronger and stronger, until it got to the point that it completely permiated the garage.  There also were puddles of gasoline on the floor.  The gasoline was removed and the odor stopped.  The leakage of gas seemed to be coming from around the carburetor.

I, then, went online to Toro's website and found that this model had been recalled.  I was advised that the recall was for 2010 models and that mine was a 2011.  What matters, here, that there is still a problem with gas leaking from the carburetor no matter whick model year it is.
justification: Gasoline leakage from the snowthrower, though not causing injury, poses a significant fire hazard, as evidenced by the strong odor and puddles of gasoline.

incident_description: When shutting down the lawn mower by releasing the handle, the blade continued to spin for an estimated 10-20 revolutions. On inspection, it was found that the outer wound sheath on the operator presence cable had broken, causing the inner cable to fray and jam. The break was located behind a cover on the handle, and ajacent to a mounting bracket that is part of the cable assembly.
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries, but the potential for injury was high due to the unexpected blade spin.

incident_description: Toro recycler lawn mower, model 20073.   These mowers and also other models with the same fuel tanks develope fuel leaks at the seam on the tanks.   These are attached direct to the back of the engine.   This could be a potential fire or explosive hazard with the fuel leaking.  I have just put on my fourth tank in 3 years with the mower.  Toro never would answer or pay for the tanks.   I see many complaints on the web for the same issue.
justification: Fuel leaks are common and could lead to an incident, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
Two outdoor Chandeliers (Product 15409 OZ) were supplied by Kichler Lighting with a switch that was wired to short circuit when the switch was closed (i.e., switched into the ON position).

The product had been installed per the directions. 

What was Observed:
When power was supplied to the light fixture, the light turned on.  When the toggle switch on the chandelier was pulled (to turn the light off), the circuit would short out and pop the circuit breaker.
 
What was Actually Happening:  
1) When power was supplied to the light fixture, the light turned on. (the toggle switch just happened to be in the open position (i.e., OFF position)).
2) When the toggle switch on the chandelier was pulled (to turn the light off), the toggle switch was closed causing a short circuit because the toggle switch was wired in parallel with the lights instead of in series with the lights.
justification: The incident caused a short circuit and tripped the circuit breaker, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: A stadium light pole manufactured by the Whitco Company collapsed at a St. Louis, Missouri area sports stadium. These light poles are the subject of an existing recall, release #10-295.   Our engineering firm (Briem Engineering) was contacted for examination of the remaining seven Whitco poles.  A kink near the base was found in one and this pole was removed.  Of the six remaining poles, three were found to have cracks at the junction of the pole to the base.  The cracks were similar to the photos supplied with the recall notice.  The remaining three poles were less heavily loaded (supported fewer lights) and no cracks were found.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a structural failure of multiple light poles, posing a significant risk to public safety.

incident_description: Perfect Flame 5 burner gas grill Lowes# 271573 Model 720-0522 propane - burners corroded out and caused large flames in rear of grill. Flame burns only to rear of grill
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to corroded burners, making it possible for it to occur again.

incident_description: I own a Blue Ember gas grill.  The grease pan has completely eroded and fallen apart.  When I went online to search for replacement parts, I found the website informing consumers about a recall for just this situation.  That is the first I had heard.  I was fortunate enough to catch this situation before a serious fire.  The model and serial number of my grill match the recall list.  I have called and sent an email to the company, but have not received a reply.  I am writing this report so that it is on file in case I do not get any satisfaction in receiving replacement parts.
justification: Although no incident occurred, the grill's grease pan erosion poses a high likelihood of fire, hence a severity level of 2.

incident_description: Char Broil grill model number 463420507 This grill has a problem.  The far left had burner developed a fault that resulted in a jet of flame coming out from behind of the burner control knob.  The result was a melting of the knob and smoke damage to the stainless steel face and top.  I also received  a small burn on my fingers as a result of trying to turn the burner off with the knob.  I was not aware of the knob being that hot as I was more concerned about the fire coming out of the front of the grill.  I have not used the grill.
justification: Injury occurred due to the unexpected flame and heat from the faulty burner knob.

incident_description:
My child was playing with a new Dora the Explorer "Explorer" Flashlight, and within a few minutes the bulb went out ~ and when we notived a funny smell. We took the flashlight away, and the area near the bulb felt hot. We took the flashlight apart, and the batteries were very hot (too hot to touch). The bulb area appeared to be melted, and the connection between the flashlight and the batteries was also very hot.

The flashlight was made by Nikelodeon.
justification: Potential for burns due to overheating batteries and melted bulb area, but no injuries reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the chain bar comes loose and the chain slides off.  It has  tool-less chain adjuster/tightener and does not tighten the bar properly.   Consumer says he has had the chain replaced and that he follows all directions.  Consumer says something causes the bar to come loose.  He says he tightens the bar as much as he can without breaking it, but it still comes loose.  Consumer says he contacted manufacturer and they told him they have not heard anything like that before.and that it is not on recall.  Consumer feels there is a hazrd that the chain could slide off and strike him.
justification: The consumer's repeated experience of the chain bar coming loose despite his efforts and the manufacturer's lack of awareness suggest a high likelihood of recurrence, posing a potential injury risk.

incident_description:
The gas tank on the tractor, located underneath the seat, is leaking gas. Consumer removed the cover over the fuel tank to make a temporary repair. There was a crack of approx. 3.5 inches in the top right hand of the tank (front) just above the seam line.  Consumer concludes that this was a defective tank or was not properly supported.  Nothing can reach the tank unless the seat cover is removed.

He contacted the retailer and was advised that there was no recall involving his model number. He indicates that he plasn on contacting the firm and will get the unit repaired.
justification: Although no injury occurred, the incident involved a hazardous gas leak, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Level 2) with a 'Possible' (Level 3) likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I was riding a Dixie Chopper LT2200-34, mowing a lawn, and the tractor caught fire, near the right side of the gas tank. I owned the mower for 5 years, and had been complaining to the manufacturer of excessive heat. The manufacturer replaced the heat shield, but the excessive heat issue was not fixed. I believe there is a design defect that the excessive heat from the engine causes it to catch fire. I am not the only one to complain about the Dixie Chopper catching fire:
1. Custodian at the [REDACTED] , was engulfed in flames while mowing on a Dixie Chopper. Passersby helped extinguish the flames and he was taken to the hospital where he later died. On another tv news report, a witness said that fuel was spraying out of the mower onto the victim and he was trying to shut it off. They also reported that it was a Dixie. http://www.wthr.com/Global/story.asp?S=12430999
2. Dixie Chopper had a recall for the fuel tank unit-when cap gets put on it cracks the seam open and/or seals tear. The rivet line has a weak spot causing bottom to split making the fuel dump out bottom. Even replacement part had flaws. One guy went to his garage and smelled fuel and he pulled the over head door open to let in light and while he was looking for leak he heard a click(hot water heater kicked on)he got out but had burns to his legs and back and had to have house rebuilt.http://www.lawnsite.com/archive/index.php/t-316447.html
3. Dixie almost caught fire=   Was mowing this afternoon and all of a sudden the mower starts to die, pulled throttle back (why I don't know) and the motor regained rpms. Did it again a few seconds later and I saw smoke coming from between my feet. The hot post on the battery finally rubbed a hole in the protective cover and shorted to the panel my feet rest on. I lifted it and it stopped. My question is what to do with this, is there a fix from the factory on this. It is a flatlander and is an 05 or 06 model, only has 350 hours on it. http://www.lawnforums.com/showthread.php?10889-Dixie-almost-caught-fire]
justification: The incident resulted in injuries and there is a history of similar incidents involving Dixie Chopper mowers, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: using DR wood chipper and the main flywheel with cutting blades inside broke in half ejecting half of it out of the machine approx. 10# sharp chunk of metal . the safety guards on this machine were not able to contain the broken cutting blade. I called dr it appears this is a metal fatigue issue and they have changed their flywheel (cutter wheel) design but there are 1000's of these in use and potentionally could be dangerous or even fatal to the operator. I have pictures
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the potential danger is high due to thousands of similar machines in use.

incident_description: I have a perfect flame grill model number SLG2006B that on April 3, 2011 caught on fire.  I was grilling burgers and the flame started getting out of control so I cut the gas off and turned the burners off and the flames would not stop shooting up.  They were going as high as the lid when the lid was open.  I got burnt on my arm not severe when trying to put water on it to get it out.  I ran out of water so I ran to the hose and put more water in a container to try to put out the fire and finally got it out.  I thought it was also going to catch my hair on fire.  I thought maybe because I had not cleaned it yet this year is why this happened so I started to clean it out and noticed one of the burners had actually busted and another had rusted of the back part of the wall.  I started looking for parts on the internet is how I found out there was a recall on this item.
justification: Injury occurred due to flames reaching high levels, and the likelihood of a similar incident is high given the grill's condition and the recall notice.

incident_description: I have a black and decker electric weed trimmer, model gh600, type4.  I bought this about 2 years ago, but have used it infrequently.  A few days ago I was cleaning my yard when there was an electrical short in the handle and it started to catch on fire. I have not taken the handle apart because I wanted to contact the manufacturer first and get their response but I can send pictures which clearly show the handle started to melt at the base of the electrical socket.  I believe the problem is that the socket is defective and poorly designed because often times the cord does not stay fastened to the handle.  Continuous refitting of the cord to the handle has probably broken the electrical prong inside the handle which caused the short.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burnt weed trimmer) but no injuries, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible due to the frequent cord detachment issue.

incident_description:
I had purchased a Princess flashlight for my granddaughter from Big Lots. It contained plastic coverings that went over the lens and showed different shapes. The flashlight used two AA battery.
My granddaughter had been playing with it all day. When she began crying complaining of pain in her hand, the flahlight had melted and burned her hand she is 3 years old.
justification: The flashlight melted and burned the child's hand, resulting in an injury.

incident_description:
In September of 09 I purhased a Mater Forge Gas grill from Lowe's . On Monday of this week I went outside opened the propane and lit the grill to warm it up.I  walked inside to grab the food and when I came back out the grill was on fire. After grabbing my fire extinguisher and putting out the fire I examined the grill to find that the hose that feedss the burners from the tank had melted and after further inspection it would appear that the line had been in contact with the bottom of the burner tray. 

Fortunately no one was hurt and the damage was limited to the hand rail around my deck and the control/ignitor wires are now cooked.
justification: Although no one was injured, the incident resulted in property damage, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' with a 'Possible' likelihood of occurrence due to the grill's design flaw.

incident_description: Blue Ember Grill, Model: FG50069, Serial #: 07000680.  My grill caught fire this past Thursday with my entire family gathered around it for a family reunion. My problem is different than the recall I see from CPSC. My problem is with the grease pan. It feels like it is engaged when you slide it into position but it really is not until you pick up the edge toward you, slide it forward another inch and set it down over a locking mechanism (my directions never mention this). If not, the grease will run down into the storage area below the grill. They have a space to store an ice bucket. This bucket is apparently made of a volatile plastic. While grilling I smelled plastic, threw open the door and had a burning bucket with flames licking the propane tank. It melted through to the patio and up into the knobs. I was able to put the fire out with an extinguisher.
justification: Although no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant fire hazard due to a design flaw in the grease pan and volatile materials used in the grill's storage area.

incident_description:
Saturday, April 2, 2011


On Friday, March 25th I purchased a "Grow Flavor" Windowsill Herb at Home Depot.  The manufacturer  of the product is "Ferry-Morse" and their website is www.ferry-morse.com.  Contents included: a cedar wooden planter with a drainage liner, 4 Biodegradable Pots that look like plastic, 4 Jiffy Quick Soil Mix Pellets, and four packets of seeds.      

The next day, Saturday, I mixed the soil pellets with warm water as directed and let it set a few minutes. Then I put the soil in each of the four pots, loosened it and added the seeds. As indicated, I put it out of direct sunlight.

On Sunday night I heard a very loud cracking sound, like a platter falling to the floor and breaking.
I looked around and couldn't see anything that would cause that sound.

The following evening, Monday, while on the phone, I heard that loud sound again, went looking around and saw nothing.  I went back to the phone and a few minutes later, it happened again.  By then I was frightened as I feared that someone was in the house and I live alone.  My friend heard it through the phone and asked what that was.

Later that night while upstairs I heard the sound again coming from downstairs.  So I went down and looked all over when I looked at the planter, I saw that three of the pots had shattered.  The pieces are very sharp and someone could easily cut themselves on them.  The next morning I removed the soil and seeds and transplanted them in something else.  The fourth pot was still intact and I put it on the kitchen counter.

Later in the day, sure enough, the pot on the kitchen counter shattered while just sitting there.  

All I could think of was that if a toddler was here and these pots were within reach, it is very possible he would investigate and possibly put a piece in his mouth, not to mention that anyone else could cut themselves if they weren't careful.

I wrote to the company on Wednesday and received a return e-mail offering to replace the product if I still had the receipt.  I was appalled that they did not even consider the injuries that could occur.  I asked them to escalate my e-mail to someone who could made the decision to recall this product.

I don't expect to hear back from them so I decided to write to you to see if you can help get this product off the market.

Thank you for you attention to this matter. 

 [REDACTED]
justification: Sharp shards from shattered pots pose a high likelihood of injury, especially to children.

incident_description: I purchased a Perfect Flame gas grill from Lowe's.  I read in Consumer Reports that there was a recall on these grills because the burners were defective.  This was exactly what happened to mine.  The burner cracked on one end and all the gas shoots out that end, creating one big flame and not one that is spread along the burner.  I looked on the list that was provided on which models were covered, and mine was not listed.  It's model # GSC3318, manufacturing data code IZ, and serial number IZ12562.  This is not right and I have the duel burner model.
justification: Although no injury was reported, the defective burner poses a significant fire risk, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: No accident or injury has occurred with the use of the defective lawn mower deck. The intent of the report is to document the manufacture and sale of a defective product. The Craftsman replacement mower deck was manufactured in that the cutting blades are out of line. Not only does this cause poor grass cutting it prevents correct height adjustments which may lead to contact with the ground which in turn may cause damage to the blade or hard objects to be discharged.
justification: Although no incident has occurred yet, the defective mower deck poses a high possibility of causing an incident due to its misaligned blades.

incident_description: I have had my Honda HRC216HXA commercial lawnmower since July 2008, frame serial number MAKA-1062862.  This year I noticed that the transmission drive clutch lever was not returning when released, i.e.  the lawnmower would continue on cutting and propelling without any hands on the drive clutch lever.
justification: The lawnmower's drive clutch lever not returning when released could lead to loss of control, potentially causing an incident but unlikely to result in injury.

incident_description: On May 25, 2010 we turned our Perfect Flame SLG2008A on low to heat it up for burgers.  It warmed fine.  My husband put on the meat and left it outside for about three minutes while he was retrieving a plate.  When he came back outside, he noticed flames coming out of the sides and the entire stainless steel lid was brown and the inset thermometer was pegged high.  He shut off the LP gas at the tank. He opened the lid to find the paint entirely melted/peeled off of the inside of the grill.  Once it cooled, I inspected the insides, which showed the three burners had ruptured towards the rear of the grill (the side not directly attached to the LP gas header).  Also, the grating/grill was destroyed and the lid was severely damaged.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: I was using my Makita blower for 2 hours off and on prior to the accident. After I had started the blower there was a load boom and the blower caught fire and burned both my arms, right side and partial face. I have reported this to Makita Corp in California and they referred me to the Legal Department. The product is Makita Handheld Blower Model #BHX2500.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns on the user's arms and face, indicating a high severity level. The fact that the blower caught fire and caused injury suggests that such incidents are likely to occur again, given the same conditions.

incident_description:
I have a Sears non powered garden tool, Bypass Pruner 7183716.  It is almost impossible to cut a thick branch (close to  the 1" cutting capacity) without getting a very severe pinching of the palm of the hand between the two hand grips.

The tool is hand pruner that operates with a scissor like action by squeezing the opposing handles using one hand.When there is pressure applied to the handles to cut through a thick branch, upon complete cut through,  space between the hand grips is reduced very rapidly . The result is a  the users palm is pinched between the grips.
justification: The tool's design causes the user's palm to be pinched between the grips upon complete cut through of a thick branch, leading to injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Potting Mix made by Miracle Gro. The name is Organic Choice. Proof of Purchase: VID-EPT 11/10             0 71645 29785 8 

I took this home to start planting some of my vegetable seeds. I opened the bag and put the soil in a big bowl so that me and my Granddaughter could scoop it out with a spoon into the pots. I found a nail in the soil.

My concerns is that someone might get hurt if they just stick their hands in the bag, It is a rather big nail and rusty.

I contacted Walmart and told them what I found and the Manager said he will take care of it. I am not sure what it is that he would do, I feel he needs to take it off the shelf.

I contact Scott Miracle Gro and the following is how they responded:
Thank you for contacting us concerning Scotts products. As always, it is our goal to make sure that our customers are completely satisfied with our products and services.
I apologize for the nail that you have found in your Miracle-Gro Organic Choice Potting Mix, REDACTED. I would like to assure you that Miracle-Gro makes every effort during manufacturing to ensure our products stay as pure as possible. Please rest assured that I will forward your information on to our Quality Assurance Department so they can investigate this matter and look for ways to make sure this does not happen again.
Again, thank you for taking the time to let us know of your concerns. Please do not hesitate to contact us if we can be of any additional help to you.

REDACTED

I do not know if they are going to pull this off the shelves as well. I feel this product should be recalled because of the danger of getting hurt and a bad infection from it.

Thank you for your help!
REDACTED
justification: A rusty nail found in the potting mix poses a high likelihood of injury to consumers.

incident_description:
Hello,
 
On March 25, 2009, I purchased a Signet 90 Series Grill with 50K BTU, 10K BTU Side Burner and Rear Rotisserie Burner -LP Gas manufactured by Onward Manufacturing Company (585 Kumpf Drive, Waterloo, Ontario, Canada N2V1K3  519-885-1390/N.America# 1-800-265-2150) from a U.S. distributor of their products, AMROYAL (info@amroyal.com), order #35623.
 
This grill has proven to be a fire hazard.  I have had to extinguish out of control flames on at least three occasions, to prevent the unit from burning the house down, as I keep the grill on a back screened in porch.
 
I contacted your customer service, and I was told that there was a safety recall on the grill requiring a new part (no cost) which they sent.  When the part arrived, I found that it was a part that was already installed in the grill, as I had received it with the new grill when it first arrived.  The problem is the design.  The top/lid extends about 2" beyond the bottom half of the grill in the back, allowing air to fuel flames inside the grill since the lid, as with most grills, cannot be closed to seal off oxygen during flare-ups due to the approximate 2" gap described.  It also allows for debris to fall from the inside of the lid onto the floor behind the grill.
 
The heat, during the dangerous flare-ups is so great that the aluminum lid melts, dripping flaming/molten aluminum onto the floor behind the grill, as you know, from a Consumer Report study brough to your attention a few years ago.

That Consumer Report, still found on-line states in part:

"Recalled Broil King Signet 90 grill might still pose risk, even with fix"
  
"A retrofit kit to fix a problematic gas grill might still leave some owners at risk, our follow-up tests show."

The kit is a stainless-steel baffle that is placed inside at the bottom of the firebox on the Broil King Signet 90 986784LP (Rating available to subscribers). We judged that grill Not Acceptable in the June 2008 issue of Consumer Reports after the firebox deformed and melted in our tests.

Working with the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) and Health Canada, Onward Manufacturing of Canada voluntarily recalled the grill on May 5, 2008, included the kit with new models, and began sending the kit free of charge to consumers who already owned the grill.

We installed the kit on two Signet 90 986784LP grills we bought after the recall and had no problems. But after we installed the kit on a grill we had bought before the recall, our flare-up tests with fatty steaks deformed the firebox"
 
I now own a grill that I paid $649.95 for on March 25, 2009 that is worthless to me, as it is a fire hazard.
 
I  requested a credit toward the purchase of a new grill, from the manufacturer and from AM Royal that sold me the grill, but I have received no response.  
 
On all occasions, had I not had in my possession a large ABC fire extinguisher, I doubt that I could have extinguished the flames to avoid a major house fire.  This grill is dangerous, and all models (still the same design and still being sold, even on Amazon.com) should be recalled and a credit of some kind issued toward the purchase of a new grill.
 
I appreciate your assistance!

[REDACTED]
justification: The grill's design allows for dangerous flare-ups and melted aluminum dripping, posing a high likelihood of house fire.

incident_description:
I have (had) a fiesta Blue Ember BBQ grill, model # FG50069. This grill currently recalled, caught fire and destroyed the grill. This fire had the potential of becoming extremely dangerous with loss of limb & property however I was able to extinquish the fire with minimal losses. The flames were shooting, propelled  by the propane tank/hose 3 plus feet in a forward and upward direction.
I have contacted the manufacturer but so far there has been little action or satisfactory results
justification: The grill's recall was ignored, leading to a fire that could have caused serious injury or property damage, but was luckily contained.

incident_description: Scaffolding collapsed due to the securing pins not engaging fully, I was treated for a broken forearm at Via Christi Hospital in Wichita Kansas.  Total cost of the broken arm was more than $19,000.00 to the hospital & Doctor. The scaffolding was made by Buffalo Tools Corp. & sold by Tractor Supply in Wichita Kansas.
justification: Injury occurred due to scaffolding collapse caused by improperly engaged securing pins.

incident_description: Power unit for garden lights, hanging on the outside wall of my house, got so hot that it melted the plastic housing for the unit....in my mind, could have started a house fire.
justification: While no injury or fire occurred, the incident could have led to a house fire due to the overheating power unit.

incident_description: My outdoor lampost lantern fills up with water when it rains and I am afraid of electrical shock. I am afraid to use it.  All the lampost lanterns in our neighborhood were replaced a year or so ago and many of them have the same problem.  The association that had them installed said they have had complaints, however they are no longer under warranty by the manufacturer.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the potential for electrical shock exists, making it an incident with possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Homelite Chainsaws with the plastic bar adjustment and locks allow the chair bar to move when motor is running at cutting speeds. The movement of the bar allows the chain to come loose from the bar at high speeds with no control until it hits something and stops. 
The plastic lock for the bar will not stay locked allowing the bar to move which allows the chain to fly off the bar when running at cutting speeds. 

The model I have is Homelite UT10580A  18 in but the same locking unit is used on most models.
justification: The design flaw allows the chain to fly off the bar at high speeds, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
I received two (2) Xpress RediSet GO electric grills (two grill for price of one sale) for roommate's Christmas gift. When we used the FIRST of the two grills ONLY YWICE; within 2wks of gift, the outside enamel paint started popping off red paint shards onto our counter. Called Xpress RediSet GO number (800-357-9213) for replacement grill, BUT BEFORE the replacement came the SECOND original grill did the same popping hazard. Two out of two grills showed overheating defects. I refused to try this third replacement grill so I called Xpress RediSet GO again but for a full refund... they refused. Then I remembered I bought Xpress' Extended Warranty and called them back and ONLY THEN did they agree to refund.

Both times the cooking was less than 12 minutes (some recipes called for greater cook times), you can see the grill's top cover changing to a darker cover THEN the popping would occur. The product does not appear to have adequate insulation between the elements and outside covers. I deem this product both fire and electrical hazardous. MADE IN CHINA.

My opinion is the other consumers who did not buy the Extended Warranty were bilked their money because they would be refused any refund back and since I havent received my refund yet may still be in the same boat. PLEASE CHECK INTO THIS BEFORE SOMEONE IS HURT or a fire is started!
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to overheating defects in two out of two grills, posing a high likelihood of injury or property damage.

incident_description: I was using my newly purchased Sears Dual Stage snowthrower (model C950-52943-0 13.5 T.P. 27 inch) for the first time.  After about 15 min. of use I went to disengage the clutch to stop the machine by letting up on the spring loaded clutch control lever, the lever came up to the disengaged position but the machine did not stop.  I pulled the emergency stop key to shut off the engine.  I never did get it out of gear.  Sears came and picked it up and delivered a new machine. No one was injured and no property was damaged.
justification: Although no injuries or property damage occurred, the incident involved a malfunction that could have led to loss of control, warranting a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
A number of years ago (approximately 3) I purchased a Perfect Flame Grill model 720-0522 from Lowe's.  Although I have notice a large number of these recalled, this model was not.

Last night I went to just perform some regular cleaning and found that 2 of the burners had rusted through causing a 4 inch long (approximate) piece of the top half of the burner to fall off.  Further, a third burner will suffer the same problem short and the 4th and 5th burners are not looking good either.

I attempted to remove the burners to measure for replacement and found that the screws holding them down are seized.  

Ultimately, the above does not really constitute a safety hazard (although the two broken burners produce some pretty long flames out the broken parts) but upon working with it last night I did notice that at one point all 5 burners were creating about an 18" long flame out of the ignition port and the gas was completely bypassing the burners.  I had NOT made any changes to the grill, simply removed the grates and heat tents to get at the burners.  I did reinstall all of the above mentioned parts and still experienced at random the extremely long (18" plus) flames from the ignition port of each burner.

I have now discontinued use of this product and have contacted Lowe's who have been extremely helpful and accommodating in resolving this however my concern stems from the uncontrolled flames coming from the ignition ports on each burner.  Personally, I am too concerned for the safety of the unit to continue using it and will be replacing it.  Although I can not attest to whether or not the two failed burners have contributed to the problem I am seeing now, the failed burners in and of themselves in such a short life span could post a risk as well.
justification: Long flames from ignition ports pose a fire hazard, and the grill's rapid deterioration suggests potential future incidents.

incident_description:
I purchased Char-Broil Red grill on 4/25/10 from a local Home Depot.  I also bought a protective cover for the grill to protect it from the weather.  The cover is never been off the grill except to actually use the grill.  The labeling on the main control panel began coming off almost immediately.  Within three months it was almost unreadable and now it is almost completely gone.  This not only is very unsightly for a grill I just paid $400.00 for but it is extremely dangerous.  I cannot allow anyone to start he grill or adjust it because you cannot read the settings.  If the grill is accidently turned on, and you would not know because there is no indication in the control panel, and then started the grill would explode from gas that would gather in the box. 

I contacted the Char-Broil company and asked to have the panel replaced.  The informed me that it was strictly a cosmetic problem and was not covered by the warranty.  I sent them photos and explained that it was a safety issue as well as a cosmetic issue.  They refused the claim.  They did offer to sell me a new one.
justification: While no injuries have been reported, the potential for an accident due to unreadable controls makes an incident likely.

incident_description: I was using a MS361 chainsaw that had received a recall notice from STIHL and had the necessary repairs completed at R.H.McCrary. I was operating said chainsaw on Wednesday, March 2, 2011 at about 11:10am when the throttle trigger stuck as a I was removing the chainsaw blade from the trunk of a tree I was in the process of cutting. The chain kept its high turning speed instead of reducing to idle speed and the result of this caused the blade to "jump-back". I attempted to throw my leg out of the path of the blade but was not quick enough. The chain knicked my left leg just below my kneecap. I was taken to the ER where I recieved stitches to sew up two separate lacerations. I have photo documentation of the wound from before stitches were applied and from after the lacerations were stitched. I am not a first-time chainsaw user and have used multiple types of chainsaws and multiple brands while working for my mother's firewood and tree clearing business.
justification: The injury occurred despite the user's experience and the repaired recall notice, making it a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
The Brinkmann 4 burner gas grill's hose which connects to the LP cylinder sticks out of the front of the grill by 4 to 5 inches and there are very tight bend radii on the hose if one attempts to connect it to the LP cylinder. After assembly I checked the Home Deopt display model and had an empty tank attached and associates also agreed the design is not correct.

Model # 810-9410-S

Purchased March 2011
justification: The grill's design flaws increase the risk of a gas leak, potentially leading to an incident.

incident_description:
On New YearÃÂs Eve 2011, I  used my five person George Foreman Grill at home to make dinner.  My mother, brother, and I used the grill to grill steaks.  We grilled them individually for safety  and to lock in the taste.  After letting it cool for a good hour while eating, my mother asked me to bring the grill from the counter to the sink to clean it.  The grill sat unplugged and was not hot. I picked it up and after approximately two seconds of it being  in my hands the ribbed metal grill lid slammed shut.  It closed on both of my thumbs with such force that I felt it had taken them clean off.  I was instructed to run them under hot water because my family believed that the grill  had burned me.  They were unable to understand my complaint due to the excessive screaming and crying that followed.  After it was discovered that I had no burns I was given an ice pack and was told to sit down and relax for a little bit. 

While I was sitting at our dining room table my mom had to throw the grill  away; not because it hurt me but because it broke.  When it slammed on my thumbs, the metal lid crushed with such force that the clamps that held it in place snapped  apart and the lid broke in half while my thumbs were still in it.  I sat for five minutes before I asked to go the emergency  room. Before we left I examined my thumbs and found a deep green/ purple blood blister had already formed under my right thumb nail.  The time between the lid closing on them and the blister formation was less then ten minutes.  By the time we arrived at the emergency room I was still screaming and crying from the pain. 

 I was seen right away  I had I two nurses, three x-ray technicians, and a doctor all attempt to move my thumbs but they were so injured from the weight of the metal lid that they would not move.  They remained locked in a bent position and were unable to straighten.  I had to have two separate sets of x-rays taken due to the excessive swelling and immobility.  In the x-ray room I had a technician examine a shot and asked me, ÃÂdamn, what did you say you did again?ÃÂ

The x-rays revealed that I had fractured my  left thumb in two places and crushed the bones and all the veins in my right.  I was given three pain killers, two prescriptions, and my  hands were wrapped with a splint all the way past my wrist. I was also instructed to meet with an orthopedic surgeon on Monday January 3rd to see what they thought.   The orthopedist rewrapped my wrists with new splints that now go all the way to my elbow to limit mobility.   I was also given two more prescriptions to assist  with the pain. In addition, I have also had an MRI on my right hand because it is believed that I have severe muscle and tissue damage. 

The results of my MRI  revealed that I had contusions consistent with my pain, tissue and muscle damage.  I have been seen by a different Orthopedic Surgeon as I was displeased with my initial Orthopedist.  My new doctor gave me yet another series of x-rays which revealed that my bones have healed. However, I am still suffering from muscle and tissue damage.  The doctor gave me two new prescriptions for medication and a prescription for occupational therapy three days a week for a month.  I have been attending therapy two days a week and have a received copies of my at home therapy regime.  Over the course of the four weeks that I have been attending these therapy sessions I have received two Edema Compression Gloves to help minimize the swelling, an air cast for my left hand and  Comfort Cool Therapeutic hand splints for both hands.  The air cast was worn 24 hours a days for a week and now is only to be worn at bed.  The hand splints are to be worn during the day.  At my therapy sessions I routinely have my hands cast in Paraffin, use putty, Digi- Flex Hand/ Finger Exercisers, Cando Wed Finger Flexion, Extension, and Wrist Exercisers, and various other exercises. At this point, I still have nerve damage in both thumbs to the point where everything I touch feels like sandpaper.  I still have difficulty extending and straightening both thumbs.

Due to this injury I have had to miss three full weeks of work, which is a bigger deal then just missing out on wages ( I am part-time  and paid hourly  and am not paid for  sick time).  I work at a middle school with autistic children as a support aid.   These children  rely  on my presence to assist them throughout the day.  I help them with taking  notes, homework, exams, and basic social interaction.  Approximately 90% of job is documentation, I also dictate for a few students who struggle with writing.  Unfortunately this injury has significantly impacted my ability to do my job.  My hands cramp up after just a few words and my handwriting is illegible.  

I have tried to contact the company directly and have sent two letters and both have gone unanswered!
justification: Injury occurred due to defective product design, likelihood is possible given the product's widespread use.

incident_description:
I have investigated two accidents now involving Bad Boy zero turn mowers. One of these accidents involved a consumer and one involved an older gentleman that mowed yards. In both instances the accidents were the result of the mowers running over and onto the victims.
I have inspected both mowers and they do not meet the requirements of the ANSI B71 standards to:
ANSI B71.4-2004 indicates in Section 4.5.8 "Operator-presence controls" and specifically paragraph 4.5.8.1 "Ride-on units and ride-on turf tractors" that:
"A means shall be provided that automatically stops or disengages the traction drive when the operator leaves the normal operator position."
The forseeability of this type of accident is demonstrated by the Appendix to ANSI B71.4 which indicates with respect to paragraph 4.5.8.1 that:
"The requirement for a traction drive Operator Presence Control (OPC) is intended to address run-over type accidents associated with machine movement when the operator leaves the normal operator position. This requirement does not allow the machine traction drive to be operational when the operator is out of the normal operator position."
The design of both machines, unlike many other manufacturers, does not require the travel control levers to be in neutral and the park brake applied before the operator can dismount. This allows a travel lever to be contacted and moved from neutral as the operator dismounts or is getting off the mower such that it moves in a fast turn and can knock the operator down and run up on them.
justification: Both incidents resulted in injuries, with victims being run over by mowers that failed to meet ANSI B71 standards for operator presence controls.

incident_description:
I am a Certified Fire Investigator with the ATF and recently investigated a fatal fire that was caused by the ignition of potting soil (specifically Miracle Gro potting soil).  The container was plastic, half-filled with dried out potting soil on a covered balconey, sitting adjacent to wood siding and below a window.  Aided by wind, cigarettes that had been discarded in the container ignited the potting soil and the plastic container, which then spread to the siding and into the adjacent apartment.  This fire spread throughout a 12 unit apartment building and resulted in the death of an occupant who was not able to escape in time.  

I have been a fire investigator since 2007 and have encountered multiple fires caused by the ignition of structures after dried out potting soil or peat moss was ignited when cigarettes were discarded within plant containers.  In talking to victims, everyday average people, and even other fire investigators, this fire causation is not widely known.  The publication Fire Findings did a study on this phenomenon in its Spring 2009 issue, Vol. 17, No. 2.  

I believe that lives could be saved and millions of dollars of fire damages could be avoided every year if warning labels were present on bags of potting soil, peat moss, and other similar soil amendments.  The general public is not aware of the fire hazards associated with these products and needs to be educated about the dangers.
justification: The incident resulted in a fatality, hence severity level 4.
